title: PTI Fact Check: Fake X post in name of Kapil Sibal claiming 'he will commit suicide before construction of Ram temple' shared on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a purported X post from Kapil Sibal is doing the rounds on social media, in which the former Congress leader and MP allegedly claims that he will "commit suicide" before the construction of Ram Temple in Ayodhya. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that screenshot of a fake tweet was shared on social media. The screenshot is going viral on social media ahead of the idol consecration ceremony of Ram Temple in UP's Ayodhya, an issue that has dominated the political and electoral landscape for long. Claim The Desk received on WhatsApp no. (+91-8130503759) an X post carrying screenshot a purported X post from Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal, with a request to verify its veracity. The alleged X post by Sibal in 2020 stated that he will "commit suicide before the construction of Ram Temple". Here is the link and archive link to the December 24 X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk looked for similar claims on social media and came across another X post, carrying another screenshot of another purported X post by Sibal, making the same claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted an advanced search using time filters on Sibal's X account, but could not find any such X post made on July 20, 2020, neither in English nor Hindi. In the next step, the Desk tried searching for archives from 2020 on Wayback Machine, to check whether any such X post was made and later deleted. However, we could not find any such archived post. Here is the link to the archived version of Sibal's account from August 3, 2020. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk, however, found a recent post made by Sibal in which he dismissed the claim made in the viral posts. "The following fake Twitter post is being circulated. This only shows the level to which our political discourse has been reduced to," the former Congress leader wrote in his X post on December 24, which carried the one of the same screenshots as shared in the viral posts. Here is the link to Sibal's X post , and below is a screenshot of the same: In another post, Sibal stated that the Hindi version of the claim was also fake. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On closely observing the viral X posts, the Desk noticed some discrepancies in the purported X post shared in the screenshot. Here's what we noticed: 1. The account name was incorrect with uncapitalised initial alphabets. 2. The 'PM' was written in an incorrect manner, and so was the year in the date mentioned. Below is a combination image, comparing the viral post with an original post shared by Sibal on the same date: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake post was shared on social media in the name of Sibal.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, the woman dancing to Bhojpuri song in this video is not BJP MLA Shreyasi Singh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 02 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a woman singing and dancing to a Bhojpuri song in the front seat of a car, claiming that she was Shreyasi Singh, BJP MLA from Jamui, Bihar. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video of a Bhojpuri actress was shared on social claim with a false claim. Claim An X user shared, on December 25, 2023, a video of a woman singing and dancing to a Bhojpuri song while seated in the front seat of a car. The user claimed that the woman was Shreyasi Singh, BJP MLA from Bihar's Jamui. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across another X post carrying the same video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted an advanced Google search with the keyword "MLA Shreyasi Singh viral video". The search led us to a news report by Prabhat Khabar related to the same video. The report identified the woman in the video as Bhojpuri actress Yamini Singh and stated that Shreyasi Singh approached the police regarding the matter. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "I am always conscious of my responsibilities and work. I have nothing to do with such things. Social media and other sites that make such ridiculous videos viral should be banned, and my office has lodged an FIR. Further, it is the responsibility of the police to ensure that appropriate action is taken against such people in this case," the report quotes MLA Shreyasi Singh as saying. During our search, we also came across a YouTube video on January 6, 2023, which carried the byte of a Bihar Police official stating that the matter was being investigated. Here is the link to the YouTube channel , and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk came through an Instagram post shared on November 26, 2022. This post carried the same video which a fan of Yamini Singh shared. Here is the link to the post , and below is its screenshot: We also found that Yamini Singh commented on the post. Below is a screenshot of the same: In the subsequent investigation, the Desk scanned the official Instagram account of Yamini Singh and found a post dated November 25, 2022, in which she is seen wearing the same outfit as in the viral video. In this video, she can be seen dancing and enjoying a Bhojpuri song with four other people. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: This post was also shared by 'pankajbihari789', tagging Yamini Singh in it, like the one being shared recently on social media. The Desk also contacted Shreyasi Singh and Yamini Singh for their comments on the viral video. The story will be updated as and when responses are received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Bhojpuri actress Yamini Singh was falsely shared as recently on social media in the name of BJP MLA Shreyasi Singh.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Italian PM Georgia Meloni did not share her beach photo on X after PM Modi's recent post on Lakshwadeep; fake screenshot shared in her name on social media
content: New Delhi, Jan 7 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A screenshot of a purported X (formerly Twitter) post by Italian PM Georgia Meloni is doing the rounds on social media. The users claimed that the photo was posted by Meloni shortly after Indian PM Narendra Modi shared some pictures of him walking along the beach and trying snorkelling during his recent visit to the Lakshwadeep Islands. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated photo of Meloni was used to create a fake X post, which was shared on social media with a false claim. The fake screenshot comes amid the internet buzzing with '#Melodi' memes around the camaraderie between PM Modi and his Italian counterpart following the G20 Summit held in India in September 2023. Claim An X user shared on January 5 a post which carried a screenshot of a purported X post by Italian PM Georgia Meloni, which included a photo of her walking along the beach. The caption of the alleged post read: "I have suddenly started loving beaches. IYKYK". The post also carried a combination image, carrying a screenshot of the purported X post by Meloni alongside PM Modi's X post on his Lakshwadeep trip, dated January 4. The user claimed Meloni shared the post just half an hour after PM Modi's X post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the screenshot through Google Lens and found another X user shared it with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning social media platforms, the Desk found an Instagram post shared on January 4 which carried the same photo. Here is the link and archive link to the post, which has garnered over 41K likes, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next step, the Desk scanned the official X handle of Italian PM Georgia Meloni ( ) but could not find any such post she shared. The Desk then checked the account's activity of Social Blade, a social media analytics website. Here's what we found: The data showed that Meloni shared two posts on January. The posts can be seen here and here . Below are the screenshots of the two posts: While scanning the X handle, the Desk also noticed that all the posts shared by Meloni were in Italian, whereas the one shown in the screenshot was in English. The Desk then ran Meloni's photo, shared in the screenshot, through Google Reverse Image Search to identify its source. The search results led to an article published on a Romanian website named Digi24 in September 2022. According to the article, which carried the viral photo along with several others, the pics were from Meloni's vacation before the general elections in Italy back then. Here is the link to the article and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a screenshot of a fake X post with a false claim was shared on social media in the name of the Italian PM.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Congress didn't release QR code with Sonia Gandhi's photo for its 'Pay For Desh' donation drive; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 10 (PTI Fact Check): The Congress launched its 'Donate for Desh' crowdfunding campaign in December 2023. Related to this campaign, a photo of a purported QR code with party leader Sonia Gandhi's image is widely shared online. Many users sharing this photo on X claimed that Congress sought donations in Sonia Gandhi's name. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a fake QR code with false claims was shared on social media. Claim An X user shared a photo of a purported QR code with Sonia Gandhi's image, which read: "PayForDesh". "*कल तक जो डिजिटल इंडिया का मजाक उड़ा रहे थे* *वही लोग आज डिजिटल तरीके से भीख मांग रहे हैं," read the X post shared on December 28. An English translation of the post read: "Those who were making fun of Digital India till yesterday* *The same people are begging digitally today." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo of the QR code through Google Lens, and on scanning the search results, we came across another X post shared on December 25, carrying the same image with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted an advanced Google search with the keyword "Congress Pay For Desh campaign" and came across a PTI report published on December 16, 2023. Here is the link to the report titled – 'Congress launches crowdfunding campaign, seeks help of common people to build country'. On further scanning the search results, we found an X post shared by the official handle of Congress on December 28. The post carried an image of a QR code with Congress' election symbol, the hand. An English translation of the Hindi post read: "Important Notice Today, on the foundation day of the Indian National Congress, a barcode has been installed on the back of the chairs in the Maharally in Nagpur. By scanning that barcode, you can donate ₹138, ₹1,380, ₹13,800, ₹1,38,000, or more to the Indian National Congress". Here is the link to the X post , and below is a screenshot of the same: On scanning the QR code given in the post, it redirected to the website donateinc.net, with an option to donate. Below is a screenshot of the page: We further scanned Congress' X and other social media platforms, along with its official website, but couldn't find the photo of any QR code with the image of Sonia Gandhi. The Desk then checked the QR code shared in the viral social media posts, which could not be scanned. On closely watching the viral photo, we found a logo of 'memebhaimbbs'. Here is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Congress did not release any QR code with Sonia Gandhi for its 'Pay For Desh' crowdfunding campaign.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video of Bollywood actor Hrithik Roshan falsely linked to India-Maldives row; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): An X user shared a video of Bollywood actor Hrithik Roshan claiming that he announced the cancellation of his Maldives tour following the boycott calls back in India amid the recent row between the two countries. In its investigation, the Desk found that the actor's video from last year was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. The video being shared on social media dates back to November 2023 when Roshan announced the cancellation of The Stars on Fire Kuala Lumpur Bollywood concert, which was scheduled to be held in Malaysia on December 1, 2023. Claim An X user shared a video of Hrithik on January 9 and used the 'Boycott Maldives' hashtag, insinuating that the actor cancelled his Maldives tour amid the recent diplomatic row between the island nation and India. "Thanks and appreciate Hrithik Roshan ji for such a fantastic decision. This is literally mine a lot for our country. May lord jagannath bless you a lot Jay jagannath (Sic)," read the X post with over 120K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk listened to the video and found that the actor was cancelling his trip to Malaysia, a Southeast Asian country, not Maldives, a South Asian country and archipelagic state. "Dear people of Malaysia, I eagerly looked forward to being with all of you for the Stars On Fire Tour. However, considering the current challenges and out of deep respect for the well-being of the people in Malaysia, we have all made the decision to cancel this tour. My prayers and thoughts are with you all. Lastly, I would like to thank Heart-Art Productions and our crew members along with our promoters Dembi Productions and Yess Boss Group for working towards putting this show together. Thank you, and stay safe ((Sic)," the actor says in the video. In the subsequent investigation step, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across an Instagram post by Heart-Art Productions on November 30, 2023. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Conducting a customised Google search, the Desk found that several Malaysia-based news outlets reported the cancellation of Roshan's concert in Malaysia. Here is the link to one such report by Malay Mail , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Star also carried the news on December 4. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted another customised Google search to check whether Roshan made any remarks or issued any statement on the row between the two countries, but couldn't find anything. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Hrithik's old and unrelated video was falsely linked to the India-Maldives diplomatic row and shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake Alert! Digitally altered video of PM Modi shared on social media with fake claims; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): An Instagram user shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi purportedly speaking on love at a public rally. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the PM's public address video was digitally altered, and an audio in his voice, created using artificial intelligence, was superimposed on it. The Desk also found that the speech of the superimposed audio was of Bageshwar Dham's Dhirendra Krishna Shastri. The viral video comes in the backdrop of the #Melodi memes around the camaraderie between PM Modi and his Italian counterpart following the G20 Summit held in India in September 2023. Claim An Instagram user shared a video of PM Modi on January 24, where he talks about love and prayers. The user captioned the video, "True words. " Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the video closely and noticed that the audio was not in sync with the lip movement. The same result was seen when we broke the audio into keyframes using Adobe Premier Pro. The Desk then ran the video through an InVid Tool search and found a few keyframes. When running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an October 2019 report by News18 Hindi, which carried a photo of PM Modi, similar to the viral video. Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the photo to the viral video: As can be seen in the combination image, the PM's background and outfit are identical, indicating that the viral video is indeed an old video. On further scanning the Google Lens search results, the Desk found another report by a website named Indiagk.net, dating back to February 2019, which carried the same image of PM Modi. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the photo carried in the article to the viral video keyframe: It was thus concluded that an old video was digitally altered and shared as recent on social media. In the subsequent investigation stage, the Desk used Adobe Premier Pro to break the audio into keyframes. Subsequently, it came across a YouTube Shorts video of Bageshwar Dham's Dhirendra Krishna Shastri. We found the audio superimposed in the viral video was taken from that video. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video of PM Modi with superimposed audio was shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of railway track-laying machine is not from India; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 1 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X user shared a video of a railway track-laying machine laying concrete sleepers and claimed it was from India. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found an old and unrelated video from Malaysia with a false claim that was recently shared on social media. Claim An X user shared on January 27 a video of a railway track-laying machine laying concrete sleepers and claimed that it was from India. "ये हैं आज के भारत की टेक्नोलॉजी। जिसे विगत 60 वर्षों में सरकार लांच नहीं कर सकी क्योंकि भारत की जनता के टैक्स का पैसा स्विस बैंक में जमा किया जा रहा था।," read the post, with over 150K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the video closely and noticed that the railway track laying machine had written 'China Communications Construction'. The Desk then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an X post shared on January 9, 2024. The post carried the same video as the one shared in the viral post. "Malaysia's East Coast Railway began laying tracks," read the post's caption, shared by a handle named Sharing Travel. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the Google Lens search results, the Desk came across the same video shared on the Chinese video-sharing platform 'ixigua' on January 7. The video description mentioned the video's location as a 'track-laying site of the East-Malaysian Railway…' Here's the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Upon further scanning the search results, we found a video news report shared by AP's official YouTube channel on December 16, 2023. The video showed the same track-laying machine as the viral video. The caption of the news report read: "China-backed Malaysian railway gets on track". "Malaysia's King Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah officiated the start of the track-laying process of the ECRL or East Coast Rail Link in his home state of Pahang," read a part of the description. Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from Malaysia was falsely labelled as one from India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video falsely linked to recent Mira Road violence in Mumbai; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Jan 31 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X user shared a video in which several men can be seen behind bars and a police officer thrashing some men with a stick and linked it to the recent violence that broke out in Mumbai's Mira Road area. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video was falsely linked to the recent violent incident. Members of two communities clashed during a vehicle rally organised in Naya Nagar of Mira Road on January 21, a day before the consecration of Lord Ram's idol in the Ayodhya temple. Claim An X user shared on January 26 a video of several men behind bars and a policeman thrashing some men with a stick. The user posted the video with a hashtag suggesting that it was related to the recent clashes in Mumbai's Mira Road area. "The police are looking after guests. Such treatment is essential for all paper tigers who create No Go Zones. West Bengal also needs this medicine. #MiraRoad," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across another X post carrying the same video and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk came across a report by Dainik Jagran, published in June 2022, which carried an image of men behind bars, similar to the viral video. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the photo carried in the news report to one of the keyframes of the viral video: On running another keyframe through Google Lens, the Desk came across an X post by BJP MLA Dr Shalabh Mani Tripathi, shared in June 2022. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the viral video keyframe to the video shared by the BJP leader: The Desk came across a report by The Week, shared on June 12, 2022, a day after Tripathi shared the video on X. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: "Uttar Pradesh BJP MLA Shalabh Mani Tripathi kicked up a row on Saturday when he shared a video of a few alleged rioters being thrashed by police in what appeared to be a police station," read a portion of the report. "While the MLA did not mention details of the police station in which the incident took place, media reports said it was a station in Saharanpur where protests were held following Friday prayers against the remarks on prophet Muhammad by BJP's now-sacked two functionaries," it read further. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old, unrelated video was falsely linked to the recent violence incident in Mumbai's Mira Road area.

author: Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Faking Death for Awareness? A Dangerous Gamble with Public Trust, a Misguided Path and a Call for Responsible Reporting
content: New Delhi, Feb 3 ( Pratyush Ranjan , PTI Fact Check ): Celebrity deaths often send shockwaves through society, grabbing headlines and igniting social media firestorms. But what if that death was a fabrication, a carefully crafted hoax, designed to raise awareness for a cause? This was the ethical tightrope walked, and even a line of trust crossed, by Poonam Pandey who recently faked her death to shine the spotlight on cervical cancer. While the cause itself is undoubtedly worthy of attention, the method employed raises concerns about the dangers of misinformation and the responsibility of news outlets in our information age. Pratyush Ranjan, the head of PTI's Fact Check service, elaborates on the pitfalls, and the lessons for the media, from the charade surrounding Pandey over the last couple of days. The Allure of Shock Value There's no denying the attention-grabbing power of a celebrity death hoax. It's a splashy headline, a social media wildfire, and a guaranteed conversation starter. But this virality comes at a cost. It erodes trust in legitimate news sources, blurs the lines between truth and fiction, and trivialises the real issue it seeks to address. The Perilous Path of Misinformation Misinformation, like a virus, spreads quickly and can have devastating consequences. It can stoke fear, ignite panic, and ultimately hinder genuine progress on critical issues like healthcare. When celebrities resort to such tactics with their massive platforms, they risk normalising the use of misinformation, making it harder to discern truth from fiction in an already information-saturated world. The Responsibility of News Outlets: Death reported without verified information In this age of instant news and the pressure to be the first to break a story, news outlets must exercise due diligence. Verifying sources, cross-checking information, and avoiding sensationalised headlines are essential for responsible journalism. By amplifying an unverified death hoax, news outlets not only contribute to the spread of misinformation but also risk damaging their credibility and the public's trust in legitimate news sources. Respect Genuine Awareness Programmes Employing fabricated narratives undermines the credibility of genuine public health campaigns. When the line between truth and fiction blurs, audiences become desensitised to critical messages, making them less likely to engage with authentic awareness efforts. This can have real-world consequences, discouraging individuals from seeking essential preventive measures like vaccinations or cancer screenings. Finding Better Ways to Raise Awareness There are countless effective ways to raise awareness about important issues like cervical cancer. Educational campaigns, public service announcements, and partnerships with healthcare organisations can all significantly drive positive change. While less flashy, these methods are far more ethical and sustainable in the long run. A Call to Action Both celebrities and news outlets must prioritise truth and responsible communication. Celebrities must recognise the immense power they wield and use it ethically. News outlets must uphold their journalistic integrity and act as gatekeepers, ensuring the information they disseminate is accurate and verifiable. By working together, they can create a media landscape where awareness is raised through truth, not trickery. Actual progress is built on trust and transparency, not sensationalised hoaxes. Let's choose the path of responsible communication and work towards a future where awareness campaigns rely on facts, not fabrications. Proper awareness stems from honest and responsible communication, not fabricated narratives and manipulative tactics. Let's commit to building a society where truth prevails, and public health initiatives prioritise genuine engagement over misleading theatrics.

title: PTI Fact Check: Viral claim about Class 9 book adding a chapter on 'dating and relationships' wrongly attributed to CBSE; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 4 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users and media outlets recently shared two screenshots, which they claimed were snapshots of chapters on dating and relationships from CBSE value education books of Class 9. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the book in which the chapter was included was wrongly attributed to the CBSE. The screenshots were shared on social media with a false claim. NCERT is a publishing organisation that publishes books for CBSE schools. Most CBSE-affiliated schools use NCERT textbooks, which cover all the syllabus of CBSE subjects. Claim An X user shared on February 2 a post which carried two screenshots of chapters on dating and relationships and claimed that they were from CBSE Class 9 textbooks. "CBSE class 9 books reached about Dating?? NCERT Books When we think about why kids are attracted to Western Culture, here is the answer. What is this? " Read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first conducted a customised Google search to check the claim's veracity and found a clarification issued by the CBSE in an X post. The education board stated that the book, whose screenshots were going viral, was wrongly attributed to them. "A section of media is wrongly attributing a book to be a publication of CBSE containing objectionable material on dating and relationships, according to the reports. This is baseless and incorrect. The contents of the chapter, which are going viral on social media, are, in fact, from a book titled A Guide to Self Awareness and Empowerment, written by Gagan Deep Kaur and published by G. Ram Books (P) Ltd. Educational Publishers. The CBSE neither publishes any books nor recommends books of any private publishers," read the notification issued by the CBSE. Here is the link to the X post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a queue from the CBSE's X post, the Desk conducted another customised Google search with the keywords "G Ram Books Pvt Ltd" and came across the publishing house's website . Subsequently, we spoke to Tency Mangal, the publication's executive director. Their viral screenshots were from a chapter of their book on mental health. "It is my company's book and is not at all related to CBSE. It is a book about mental health, and dating and relationships are just a small chapter in it, much later in the series, in the 9th grade. We have an entire series from Class 1 till 10," Tency told PTI. She also shared an X post by her publishing house on February 2, expressing gratitude for the "positive response that our chapter on Dating & Relationships has garnered on social media". Here is the link and archive link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also reached out to CBSE via email for its response to the viral screenshots. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a book was falsely attributed to CBSE and its screenshots were shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Rahul Gandhi offering biscuit to a dog shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Feb 6 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Many X users affiliated with the BJP shared a video of Rahul Gandhi, claiming that it showed the Congress leader offering the same biscuit to a party worker that a dog refused. The PTI Fact Check, in its investigation, found that the man in the video was the dog's owner, not a party worker, and the Congress leader 'gave the biscuit to him to feed him later'. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Rahul Gandhi is currently leading the Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra, which started in Manipur on January 14 and is scheduled to culminate in Mumbai on March 30. Claim An X user – Karnataka's Deputy Leader of Opposition Arvind Bellad – shared a 14-second video of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and claimed that it showed him first offering a biscuit to a dog and then offering that same biscuit to a party worker after the dog refused to eat it. "Here's a glimpse of Rahul Gandhi's 'Mohabat ki Dukhan'! He offered the same biscuit to a party worker that a dog refused! Imagine how those who treat their party workers this way would treat the country's people if they were to ever come into power!" read the post, dated February 6. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across two other X posts by BJP leaders – Amit Malviya and Shehzad Poonawalla, who shared the same video with the same claim. The posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found an X post by activist Tehseen Poonawalla, which was a quoted post on the X post by his estranged brother Shehzad. The post, which carried the same video of Rahul Gandhi, stated that the man to whom the Congress leader offered the biscuit was the dog's owner, not a party worker. He also insinuated from the post that Gandhi gave him the biscuit because dogs often feed only from their owner's hand. "Shehzad, this is the full video. Shri Rahul Gandhi ji gives the biscuit to the dog parent who feeds his dog! Our mom- feeds Hatchi and Moon Poonawalla with her hand. My mother-in-law feeds Miyake and Koko with her hands. Moreover our mom has adopted a handsome Indie called Sheru at Jamat Khanna (her mosque), and she feeds him too. Dogs sometimes look to their pet parent to feed them.. but Alas.." read the post. Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords. It came across an X post by PTI, in which Rahul Gandhi responded to a media query on the claims made by the BJP and said that the man was the dog's owner and not a party worker. Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the post's comment section, a user shared a video of the said dog owner. Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found a PTI report on Rahul Gandhi's reaction, carried by The Print website. The report's headline read: "'Offered biscuit to the dog owner to feed it': Rahul Gandhi on viral video". The Desk also contacted the party for a reaction to the viral video. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of Rahul Gandhi was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of tractor running over policeman is not related to the ongoing farmers' protest
content: New Delhi, Feb 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): An X user shared a video of a policeman getting stuck under the wheels of a tractor and shared it with hashtags suggesting that it was related to the ongoing farmers' protest at the Punjab-Haryana Shambhu border. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video from Punjab was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. Hundreds of farmers are staying at the Punjab-Haryana Shambhu border after being stopped from marching to Delhi to protest against the central government over their unfulfilled demands. Claim An X user shared on February 13 a video of a policeman being stuck under the wheels of a tractor and used hashtags suggesting that it was related to the ongoing farmers' protest at the Punjab-Haryana Shambhu border. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk divided the video shared on social media into several keyframes using the InVid Tool Search. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across another X post, which carried the video with a similar post. Here is the link and archive link to the post with over 135K views, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post shared by a journalist named Gagandeep Singh in August 2023. The post, which carried the same video as shared in the recent social media posts, read: "A clash between farmers and the Punjab Police occurred in Sangrur's village Longowal as they were heading towards Chandigarh to participate in a protest. During the clash, one farmer lost his leg as he came under a tractor trolley tyre & he lost his life during treatment. At the same time, one policeman got severely injured. #Sangrur #FarmersProtest #Punjab." Here is the link and archive link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a Google search to look for more information regarding the video. It came across a report by The Indian Express, which carried a screenshot of the same video. The title of the news report, published on August 22, 2023, read: "What farmers want: dams, flood water harvesting, better drainage system on highways". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The report stated that the incident took place during clashes between farmers and the police in Sangrur, which broke out when farmers were protesting against the detention of several farm union leaders ahead of their Chandigarh rally. Upon further scanning the search results, we found an X post by Sangrur Police, which carried the same video. "Reg unfortunate death of a protester today at Longowal, it is clarified that as per witnesses & videos, the deceased was overrun by a rashly driven tractor trolley by protesters, which also severely injured a police inspector who narrowly escaped from getting crushed. Our condolences," read the post dated August 21, 2023. Here is the link to the X post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to the ongoing farmers' protest.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video from Rahul Gandhi's public speech in UP's Amethi digitally altered and shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 04 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, in which he can be heard saying that those chanting 'Bharat Mata ki Jai' and 'Jai Shree Ram' will die of hunger. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found an old video from Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra in UP's Amethi was digitally altered and clipped portions of the speech were combined and shared on social media to make the false claim. Rahul Gandhi is currently leading the Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra, which started from Manipur on January 14 and is scheduled to culminate in Mumbai later this month. Claim An X user on March 2 shared a video of Rahul Gandhi, in which the Congress leader can be heard saying that those chanting slogans of 'Bharat Mata ki Jai' and 'Jai Shree Ram' will die of hunger. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk noticed that the video was originally shared by an X handle named Megh Updates on February 26. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of Congress, on February 19, 2024. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: We watched the full video and found that it included the portions from the viral video. Below is a combination image, showing the same: The description of the video stated that it was from the public address by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and leader Rahul Gandhi during the Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra in Amethi, Uttar Pradesh. We found that clips from timestamps 26:22 to 26:29, and 26:59 to 27:10, were clipped and combined to make the video, which was shared on social media. Hence, the context of his comments was missing in the viral video. Originally, Rahul Gandhi made these statements while criticising the Central Government on the issue of unemployment. In this video Rahul Gandhi can be heard saying "In the inauguration ceremony of the Ram Temple, did you see a Dalit, did you see a farmer? The President of India was not allowed inside, did you see a farmer or labourer? You have seen Adani, you have seen Ambani, you have seen Amitabh Bachchan, your Hindustan does not exist. Your job is to say, 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' and 'Jai Shri Ram'. Their (Adani and Ambani) job is to count money, their job is to fly in a private plane, their job is to have fun, your job is to look here and there, look there brother, Pakistan, look there brother Amitabh Bachchan has performed a new dance, keep doing it brother, keep doing it… do as much as you want, have fun, everyone will die of hunger, everyone will die of hunger, everyone's time will come, no one will be left… everyone will die of hunger." Subsequently, the desk concluded that a digitally altered video was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of policeman assaulting woman on the street falsely linked to violence in West Bengal's Sandeshkhali; Details inside
content: New Delhi, March 5 (Anushka Pandey / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video purportedly showing a policeman assaulting a woman on the street, and claimed that it was from the violence-struck area of Sandeshkhali in West Bengal. The user also claimed that the police was acting at the behest of TMC leader Shajahan Sheikh, the prime accused in the case of alleged systematic assault on women in the region. In its investigation, the Desk found that an old and unrelated video from West Bengal's Badurai was shared on social media as recently with a false claim. The Sandeshkhali region, located on the fringes of the Sunderbans, has been engulfed in turmoil for over a month due to accusations against TMC leader Shajahan Sheikh and his cohorts of sexual abuse and land usurpation. Claim An X user shared on March 1 a video of a policeman assaulting a woman on the street, and claimed that the incident took place in West Bengal's Sandeshkhali. "देखो पश्चिम बंगाल के "हैवानों" को। बहन बेटियों को पुलिस और शेख के गुंडे कैसे पीट रहे हैं, ताकि वह डरकर आवाज ना उठायें... 😭 शाहजहां जैसा रेपिस्ट पुलिस सुरक्षा में सीना तानकर चलता है, और पीड़ित महिलाओं पर लाठियां बरस रही हैं।" read with post with over 145.6K Views. An English translation of the post read: "Look at the "brutes" of West Bengal. How the police and Sheikh's goons are beating sisters and daughters, so that they do not raise their voice out of fear... A rapist like Shajahan walks with his chest raised under police protection, and the victim women are being beaten with sticks." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk divided the video shared on social media into several keyframes using the InVid Tool Search. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video has been posted on Youtube with several different accounts. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) to two such YouTube videos. On further scanning the Google Lens results, we came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of Hindustan Times, on April 22, 2020. The Desk watched the video and found that this was an extended version of the video, which was shared on social media in the name of Sandeshkhali. The description of the video news report stated that the incident was reported in West Bengal's Baduria region, allegedly over improper distribution of ration during the COVID-induced lockdown. "A scuffle broke between police and locals in West Bengal's Baduria region on Wednesday. The clash allegedly erupted over the improper distribution of ration in the area. Police allege locals are blocking the road in the area. Police personnel were seen beating up locals while the locals pelted stones at the police. This comes as the country is under lockdown till May 3 in view of Covid-19," read the description of the YouTube video. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the video report, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a report by The Indian Express, reporting about the incident. The title of the news report, published on April 22, 2020, read: "West Bengal: Locals and policemen clash over allegation of irregularities in ration distribution". Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the desk concluded that an old and unrelated video was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to the Sandeshkhali incident.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Chitra Tripathi predicting INDIA bloc's victory in 2024 Lok Sabha polls is digitally altered; Details inside
content: New Delhi, March 6 (Anushka Pandey / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video featuring renowned TV news anchor Chitra Tripathi, purportedly making predictions about the INDIA bloc leading against the BLP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally altered video of Tripathi was shared on social media to make the false claim. The INDIA bloc is an alliance of anti-BJP parties coming together to unitedly contest the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls. Claim An X user shared on March 4 a video of Aaj Tak news anchor Chitra Tripathi, who can purportedly be heard predicting INDIA bloc leading against the NDA in the run-up to the Lok Sabha elections. "यें सच्चाई कैसे निकल रही है?लगता है बीजेपी ने हार के डर से इनका पेमेंट रोक दिया है।इस लिए सच्चाई मुंह से निकल रही है? क्या यह सच है की NDA हार रही है?@iamAKstalin की वाल से कॉपी। #INDIAAlliance #GandhiMaidan #AnantRadhikaWedding #TejashwiYadav #RahulGandhi" An English translation of the post read: "How is this truth coming out? It seems that BJP has stopped their payment due to fear of defeat. Is this why the truth is coming out of your mouth? Is it true that NDA is losing?Copy from @iamAKstalin's wall. #INDIAAlliance #GandhiMaidan #AnantRadhikaWedding #TejashwiYadav #RahulGandhi" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the viral video and noticed a lip-sync issue in it. We then divided the viral video into several keyframes using the InVid Tool Search. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an X post, carrying the same video and claim. Notably, this video was posted by a user who goes by the name 'A K Stalin', who was mentioned in the post above. Here is the link and archive link to the post with more than 1 million views, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post, which quote tweeted the above-mentioned post, calling it 'fake AI generated' video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and found a YouTube video posted from the official handle of Congress on July 19, 2023. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the 1:29-minute video and noticed that the audio was same as the viral video. Even the screengrabs used in the viral video were taken from this video. Below is one such example: The Desk then further scanned the search results and came across a YouTube video, uploaded by the official handle of Aaj Tak on July 21 last year, which was of Chitra Tripathi's TV debate show 'Dangal'. The Desk watched the 10:18-minute video and noticed that Tripathi was wearing the same outfit as the viral video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: In the video, she responded to a panelist's allegations that the channel had not covered ethnic violence in Manipur. On watching the video closely, the Desk noticed several similarities from 2:08 minutes. During its research, the Desk found that the survey mentioned in the viral video and the video shared by the Congress was conducted by News24 on July 18, 2023. Here is the link to the X post by News24 and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted Chitra Tripathi, for her response on the viral video. While demanding stringent action against those spreading fake news, Tripathi shared two of her X posts related to the viral video. In the first X post, she called out a user for sharing the edited video created using AI and demanded strict action against those doing so. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the second X post, she quote tweeted the post by the user 'AK Stalin' and called for action against those spreading fake news. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of the news anchor was digitally altered and audio was superimposed in it to make the false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this photo doesn't show the crowd at INDIA bloc's Patna rally; old photo edited and shared as recent on social media
content: New Delhi, March 7 (Anushka Pandey / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo of massive crowd at a public rally, which he claimed was at the iconic Gandhi Maidan in Patna on March 3, when INDIA bloc leaders including Congress' Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, and Samajwadi Party's Akhilesh Yadav converged for the Jan Vishwas Maharally. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old image was photoshopped and shared as recent on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user shared on March 3 a photo of massive crowd and claimed that it gathered at the iconic Gandhi Maidan in Patna, when several leaders of INDIA bloc gathered for the Jan Vishwas Maharally. "Tsunami of crowd at the iconic Gandhi Maidan in Patna. Over 12 lakh people joined the historic rally today," read the post with over 480K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk found that the user shared an 'Update' in thread post, where she shared another photo of crowd at a public gathering and wrote: "Seems like this is an old photo. But this is today's picture. The same massive crowd." The Desk then ran the photo, shared in the viral post, through Google Lens and came across an X post shared by RJD chief Lalu Yadav in August 2017. The post, which carried the same photo as shared in the viral post, read: "No "Face" will stand in front of Lalu's "Base". Come & Count as much as u can in Gandhi Maidan, Patna #DeshBachao." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the photo shared on social media with the one shared by Yadav in August 2017. The Desk then went through the comment section of the X post, and found several users calling out the photo as 'photoshopped'. One of the users shared a photo, and wrote: "लालू भक्त ये देखो भीड़ .. फोटोशॉप ऐसे भी तो कर सकते थे !! लालू इसे कहते है मोदी का चक्रवाव." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, another user shared a photo, seemingly from the same gathering, which showed lesser people as compared to what the viral image showed. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comapring the viral photo with the one shared by the X user (as mentioned above): In the next part of investigation, the Desk further scanned the Google Lens search results of the viral photo and came across the same image, carried by The Financial Express in a photo gallery dated August 27, 2017. "Unprecedented gathering at BJP Bhagao, Desh Bachao rally at Gandhi Maidan of Patna? Lalu shares pics," read the headline of the article. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: However, the description of the photo mentioned that "there are several tweets doing the rounds claiming that the image tweeted by RJD chief Lalu was Photoshopped". Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a news report by Jansatta, shared on August 27, 2017. The report carried the image, same as the one shared by an X user as mentioned above, which showed a smaller gathering than what was shown in the recent image viral on social media. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the above-mentioned photo with the one viral on social media: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated photo was edited and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Viral post of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif about India's CAA falsely shared; Details inside
content: New Delhi March 13 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a screenshot of a purported X post by Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, in which he announced a Citizenship (Amendment) Act in the country, to counter "Indian government's undemocratic and communal CAA". The further post suggested Sharif announcing that Indian Muslims "who feel persecuted in India" would get Pakistani citizenship. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a fake screenshot was shared on social media with a false claim. The rules for implementation of the contentious Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) 2019 were notified on March 11, paving the way for granting citizenship to undocumented non-Muslim migrants from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Afghanistan. Claim An X user shared a screenshot of a purported X post by Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif, which mentioned about him introducing a Citizenship Amendment Act in the country, to counter India's CAA. The post read: "Wow #ShehbazSharif, What a #Masterstroke. Good news for those Indian Muslims who are not happy in India. Now they can go #Pakistan easily. #CAARules #CAA #CitizenshipAmendmentAct #stockmarketcrash." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran a screenshot through Google Lens, and came across an X post, carrying the same claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the X handle of Shehbaz Sharif but couldn't find any such post, as suggested in the viral social post. We found that the latest by Pakistan PM, shared on March 10, expressed gratitude towards the President of Maldives, HE Dr Mohamed Muizzu, for extending congratulations on his appointment as the Prime Minister of Pakistan. During further investigation, the Desk tracked the activity of Sharif's X handle on Social Blade, to ascertain if any post was shared and later deleted. There were no reports about Sharif making a remark about granting Pakistani citizenship to Indian Muslims. Here is the link and a screenshot of the results found on Social Blade. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot shared on social media in the name of Pakistan PM was fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake notification on appointment of two new Election Commissioners shared on social media
content: New Delhi, March 15 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a screenshot of a purported gazette notification of the Government of India related to the appointment of two Election Commissioners. The post mentioned the names of the newly elected commissioners as retired IAS officers Dr. Rajesh Kumar Gupta and Priyansh Sharma. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a fake screenshot was shared on social media with false claim. Former IAS officers Gyanesh Kumar and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu were on Thursday (March 14) appointed as election commissioners, ahead of the announcement of the Lok Sabha polls. Claim An X user shared a screenshot of gazette notification of the Government of India related to the appointment of two Election Commissioners, namely retired IAS Dr Rajesh Kumar Gupta and IAS Priyansh Sharma. The post read, "New Delhi: Government of India notifies appointment of two new election commissioners to the Election Commission of India." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and came across an X post, carrying the same claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the official website and social media handles of the Election Commission of India, but did not find any information related to the claim. Taking the investigation further, the Desk also visited the official website of the Government of India, and found that no such notification was issued by the government regarding the appointment of the new Election Commissioner. Here is the link to the website. During our search, we came across a PTI news report carried by The Print, dated March 14. The headline of the report read: "Ex-bureaucrats Gyanesh Kumar, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu appointed election commissioners". We then conducted a customised Google search and found a PIB release on Gyanesh Kumar and Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu assuming charge as Election Commissioners in the Election Commission of India. Here is the link to the release and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake screenshot was shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Election Commission didn't skip journalist's question; clipped video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 18 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video claiming that it showed the Election Commission skipping questions on PM Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah. The video was shared on social media on March 16 - the day when the ECI announced the schedule for the Lok Sabha polls and Assembly elections in four states. During its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped portion from ECI's press conference was shared on social media with a false claim. On March 16, Chief Election Commissioner Rajiv Kumar, along with Election Commissioners Gyanesh Kumar and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu, announced the schedule for the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls, and the Assembly polls in four states. Claim An X user shared a video, claiming that it showed the Election Commission skipping a journalist's question regarding the violation of Model Code of Conduct, and if unbiased action will be taken against leaders of ruling party and the opposition. The post with over 18K views reads: "SHOCKING Arrogance -The spineless and coward @ECISVEEP skips the valid Questions. -Do you think Elections will be free & fair under these puppets. -They even afraid to deny such non baised approach. -BJP is using Religion & Children Consistently. -Share max to Xpose ECI." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk divided the video shared on social media into several keyframes using the InVid Tool Search. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video was posted on X by several other users. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) to two such X posts. On further scanning the Google Lens search results, we came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of Election Commission of India, on March 16, 2024. The Desk watched the video and found that it was an extended version of the viral video. Here is the link to the video of ECI press conference and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and found that the video shared on social media was taken from 1:00:48 timestamp. The journalist introduces herself as Ashlin Mathew from the National Herald and the asks the question. However, on further watching the video, we noticed that the Chief Election Commissioner did answer her question at 1:10:22 timestamp . Responding to the query by the journalist, the Chief Election Commissioner says: "Wherever there will be a case of violation against anyone, no matter how renowned the politician may be, we will take action against him or her". We also found that the Election Commission was taking up media queries in groups of five questions and answering them.

title: PTI Fact Check: France denies sending 2,000 troops to Ukraine, as claimed in news reports; Details inside
content: New Delhi, March 21 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a Hindi news report is being widely shared on social media, with the claim that France is ready to send 2,000 troops to war-torn Ukraine. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claim made in the news report and several social media posts was false. Claim A user received on PTI Fact Check Desk's WhatsApp number (+91-8130503759) screenshot of a purported Hindi news report, which claimed that France is preparing to send its 2,000 troops to Ukraine. The news report attributed the claim to the Russian Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR) chief Sergei Naryshkin. Below is the screenshot received on WhatsApp: Investigation The Desk searched the headline of the purported news report on Google and found that it was published by TV9 Hindi on Mar 20, 2024. Here is the link and archive link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk found an X post, shared on March 19, which made a similar claim. The post read' "1/3 Russia's foreign intelligence chief Sergey Naryshkin: "According to information coming to the Russian SVR, a [French] contingent to be sent to Ukraine is already being prepared. Initially, it will include around 2,000 troops" following with 2 more tweets regarding the same claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came a report by The Moscow Times, published on March 19, whose headline read: "Russian Spy Chief Claims France Planning to Send 2K Soldiers to Ukraine." Here is the link and archive link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the websites and social media handles of French authorities, to look for an official confirmation on the claim made in the news reports and social media posts. We came across an X post shared from the official handle of France's Ministry of Armed Forces Ministère des Armées 🇫🇷 (@Armees_Gouv), which refuted the claim made in the reports. The post read, "The information released by Sergei Naryshkin, director of the Russian Foreign Intelligence Service, is another example of Russia's systematic use of mass disinformation," the post's caption read. We call for utmost vigilance to prevent any instrumentalization through this type of campaign.'' Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot related to the same: We also conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords, and came across a report by Reuters, as per which, France categorically refuted the claim made by the Russian spy chief. Here is the link to the report titled 'France calls Russian spy chief remarks 'irresponsible' provocation'. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in news reports and on social media was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Serum Institute didn't donate Rs 52 crore to BJP via electoral bonds; Details inside
content: New Delhi, March 23 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a graphic to claim that the Serum Institute of India (SII) donated Rs 52 crore to BJP via electoral bonds. In its investigation, the PTI fact Check Desk found that the donation was made through Prudent Electoral Trust, and not electoral bonds. The graphic was shared on social media with a false claim. The Centre's electoral bond scheme was scrapped by the Supreme Court last month. On March 15, the apex court further directed the SBI to disclose all 'conceivable' details available with it regarding electoral bonds, including the alphanumeric number corresponding to each bond. Claim An X user shared a graphic claiming that the Serum Institute of India donated Rs 52 crore to BJP through electoral bonds. "Serum Institute of India donated 50 crores to BJP via electoral bonds. Serum Institute was the main company with which govt procured the vaccine. Connect the dots.#ElectoralBond" read the post with over 45K views. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot related to the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and came across multiple X accounts posting the same screenshot with similar claims. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) of two such X posts. Below are the screenshots of the same: The Desk found that the above-mentioned social media posts made two claims – first, that the SII donated Rs 52 crore to the BJP via electoral bonds; and second, that no other institute except SII was allowed to manufacture the COVID-19 vaccines in India. For the first claim, the Desk further scrutinised the details present in the screenshot credited to Reuters, which stated, "Money which companies gave to Prudent Electoral Trust was disbursed to the BJP almost immediately." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a keyword search and came across a report from Reuters, dated March 14. The title of the report read: "Obscure trust links India's top businesses with Modi's election war chest." Here is the link to the report: "The Prudent Electoral Trust has raised $272 million since its creation in 2013, funneling roughly 75% of that to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party. The trust's donations to the BJP total 10 times as much as the $20.6 million it issued to the opposition Congress party, the records show," read a section of the report. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted research on the ECI website and found the details of the contributions received by the Prudent Electoral Trust during the financial year 2022-23. The data showed that the SII donated a total of Rs 50 crore and 25 lakh to the trust in three instalments of Rs 40 crore, Rs 10 crore and Rs 25 lakh in August 2022. Below is a screenshot showing the same: The Desk further checked that the BJP received a cheque of the same amount on August 18, 2022. Below is a screenshot of the same: Here we would like you to know the difference between an electoral bond and electoral trust. According to a report by Association of Democratic Reforms (ADR), electoral trust is set up by companies with the sole objective to distribute the contributions received by it from other Companies and individuals to the political parties. The concept of 'Electoral Trust' was introduced by the then Congress government in the year 2013. The trusts were required to contribute 95 percent of their total income to eligible political parties. The information related to the contribution and details of the companies were available on the website of Election Commission. On the other hand, 'Electoral Bond' was introduced by the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government in 2018. Electoral bonds are interest-free instruments available for purchase from authorised State Bank of India (SBI) branches by both companies and individuals. These bonds do not require the donor's identity or other details, ensuring anonymity. Political parties are required to encash these bonds within a designated time frame. Here is the link for report by Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR). We also found an article by The Indian Express, published on March 22, whose headline read: "Electoral bonds: Serum Institute, Nippon Steel among electoral trust donors which didn't take bond route." "While many companies that donated to parties using electoral bonds also used the electoral trust route, there are some among the top 10 donors through trusts over the past five years, including COVID-19 vaccine-maker Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd, Hyderabad-based electronics manufacturer Medha Servo Drives and ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel, who did not opt for the bonds that gave anonymity," read a section of the report. Moving to the second claim, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and found that according to a Lok Sabha response in July 2021, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) authorised several COVID-19 vaccines for restricted emergency use, including Moderna and SPUTNIK-V, among others. During further examination an additional CDSCO list, revealed that besides Serum Institute's Covishield, Bharat Biotech's Covaxin along with 16 others received approval for manufacturing, sale, or distribution within India. Here is screenshot of the report from CDSCO, India's national regulatory body for cosmetics, pharmaceuticals and medical devices. Of these seven COVID-19 vaccines allowed for usage, only Covishield was manufactured by the SII. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a graphic on prudent electoral trust donations was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, CJI DY Chandrachud did not walk away during the hearing on electoral bonds; clipped video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 24 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud is being widely shared on social media, with the claim that he "walked away" while Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta was presenting his arguments during the hearing on electoral bonds case. Towards the end of the video, the CJI appeared to be getting up from his chair. That's when the video ended abruptly. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. The viral video was taken from the Supreme Court hearing on March 18 when it directed SBI to make public the alphanumeric numbers of electoral bonds. Tushar Mehta was representing the central government in the case. Claim An X user shared on March 18 a quote tweeted a video of CJI DY Chandrachud and claimed that he "walked away" while Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta was presenting the arguments in the electoral bonds case. "How can the #CJI behave in this manner? SG is presenting his arguments before him and without adjourning, he and other judges simply walked away..This is gross humiliation and insult to the Govt of India..All the judges including the CJI Chandrachud, should be hauled up and, forced to resign by the President of India.Totally mannerless and ARTOGANT this man Chandrachud is..He and other judges are taking vengeance against the Govt of India..I will be shortly post a thread listing reasons, behind this attitude of judges.." read the post with over 1.5 million views Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot related to the same: Investigation Starting the investigation the desk noticed that the video was shared by an X handle named iMac_too on March 18. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On scanning social media platforms for similar claims, we found that a Facebook user had shared the same video with a similar claim on March 19. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: During further investigation, the Desk found that the original video was shared by an X handle named Law Today, which was further picked up by social media users to share with the viral claim. The user wrote, "WATCH: "Witch-hunting has started on some other level now... Petitioners have starting giving press interviews deliberately to embarrass the court. It is a non-level playing field. We can't rebut them. There is a barrage of social media posts now that are intended to cause embarrassment. Any kind of posts are being made!" says Solicitor General CJI responds "We are only concerned with compliance of our judgment. As judges, we decide according to the Constitution. We are governed by the rule of law. We are also the subject of commentary on the social media and the press, but as a Court, our shoulders are broad enough". "My job is to inform you that there is something else that is playing out... something that neither did the Supreme Court intended, nor the Electoral Bonds scheme intended" says Solicitor General." with over 392k views. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is the screenshot below of the same: The Desk then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of the Supreme Court of India, on March 18, 2024. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: We watched the full video and found that it included the portions from the viral video. Below is a combination image, showing the same: The description of the video stated that it was from the hearing at the Supreme Court of India - Court 1. On watching the video, we found that the viral clip was taken from 23-minute timestamp . At 27 minutes and 4 seconds timestamp, the CJI can be seen talking to his colleagues and adjusting his seating position. This is the point where the video shared by Law Today abruptly ended. However, on watching the complete video, the Desk found that the CJI did not get up from his chair, and was seated during the entire hearing. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with specific keywords and came across a PTI story carried by The Print on March 23. The headline of the story read: "Was trolled for changing seating position, says CJI while highlighting stress management". In the report, the CJI, speaking after inaugurating the 21st Biennial State Level Conference of Judicial Officers, stated that recalled a recent incident of him facing 'trolling' and 'vicious abuse' for adjusting his seating position, during a hearing due to a discomfort. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, the man in this viral video is not removing AAP hoarding; old video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, March 29 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video with the claim that it showed a person removing poster of Aam Aadmi Party from a roadside pole while BJP flags were left intact. The user also questioned if the Election Commission of India was abiding by the rules of Model Code of Conduct. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video from Rajasthan was shared as recent with a false claim. The Model Code of Conduct came into force on March 16, following the announcement of schedule for the Lok Sabha polls by the Election Commission of India. Claim An X user shared on March 25 a video, which showed a man removing a poster from a roadside pole. The user claimed that the man was removing Aam Aadmi Party poster while the BJP flag was not removed. The post read, "आचार संहिता का पालन करता निष्पक्ष चुनाव आयोग भाजपा का झंडा लहरा रहा है उसे नही उतारा जा रहा है और आम आदमी पार्टी का होर्डिंग उतारा जा रहा है।क्या चुनाव आयोग भी भाजपा के हाथों बिक गया है?? @ECISVEEP" An English translation to the post read: "Fair Election Commission follows the Model Code of Conduct. The BJP flag is flying but it is not being taken down and the hoardings of Aam Aadmi Party are being taken down. Has the Election Commission also been sold to the hands of BJP?? @ECISVEEP." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk divided the viral video into several keyframes using the InVid Tool Search. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was posted on X with multiple accounts. The posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The desk then watched the video carefully and noticed that '@NSUIRajasthanOfficial' was written on the video. Below is a screenshot showing the same: Taking a cue from this, the desk started scanning the social media handles of Rajasthan NSUI. During investigation, we found a viral video on the official Instagram handle of Rajasthan NSUI. Along with this video uploaded on January 14, the caption read: "Bhajanlal government was so scared by the arrival of NSUI State President Shri Vinod Jakhar ji in Jaipur that it ordered to collect the posters early in the morning. Bhajanlal Sharma ji removes posters like this, puts up barricades and pushes police forward, trying to scare but they should know that our leader Shri Rahul Gandhi ji always says one thing "Don't be afraid" Babbar Sher, every worker of NSUI. We will not be intimidated by these actions, we will continue to fight against injustice." Here is the link and archive link of the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then went through other posts shared from the handle and found the contact number of Vinod Jakhar, the NSUI State President of Rajasthan. Jakhar told PTI that the video in question dated back to January 13. Further, Jakhar told PTI Fact Check Desk, "When I became the state president of NSUI in January this year, there was a lot of enthusiasm among the workers about my visit to Jaipur for the first time and they had put up banners and posters at various places to welcome me. But all the posters were removed by the Municipal Corporation. These were NSUI posters and have no connection with the Aam Aadmi Party." Subsequently the Desk concluded that the viral video neither showed poster of AAP being removed, nor did the incident take place after the Model Code of Conduct came into force.

title: PTI Fact Check: Three-year-old video of TMC's Sujata Mondal being chased away by villagers shared on social media ahead of Lok Sabha polls
content: New Delhi, March 30 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta Fact Check Desk ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a woman being chased by a group of men with sticks and claimed that she was TMC's Lok Sabha candidate Sujata Mondal who was beaten by villagers in Arambagh for intimidating voters. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video of Mondal, dating back to the 2021 Assembly polls in West Bengal, was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.
