Mondal has been fielded by the TMC from Bishnupur Lok Sabha seat, where she will be facing competition from her estranged husband and MP Saumitra Khan, a BJP candidate. Claim An X user shared on March 23 a video which showed a woman being chased by a group of villagers with sticks. The user claimed that the woman was TMC's Lok Sabha candidate Sujata Mondal, who was beaten by villagers in Arambagh, allegedly for threatening the voters. The post with over 12,000 views read: "Sujata Khan, TMC candidate from Bishnupur, Bengal, was threatening voters of Arambagh to vote for TMC or face the consequences. Voters of Arambagh beat up Khan and other party workers and chased them away. The Hindus of Bengal are fighting back." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several X posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) of two such X posts: The Desk then watched the viral video closely and noticed the logo of 'Anandabazar Patrika' on the top right corner of the viral video. The desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a video report on YouTube, shared by the handle of Anandabazar Patrika, in April 2021. The Desk watched the video and found that this was an extended version of the video, being shared on social media recently. The description of the video news report stated that the incident was reported in the Arambagh area of Bishnupur, Bengal during the third phase of the assembly election in the state. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the video report, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a video report by The Times of India, about the incident. The title of the news report, published on April 6, 2021, read: "West Bengal polls: TMC candidate Sujata Mondal allegedly attacked in Arambagh". "TMC candidate Sujata Mondal was allegedly attacked in West Bengal's Arambagh constituency. The TMC said that the party will move the Election Commission. Mondal claimed that 'BJP workers targeted her'. On the other hand, the BJP activists blamed TMC for the same. Security forces moved there and they vacated the village," read the description of the video report by the Times of India Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: PM Modi didn't make any remarks against caste-based reservation; clipped video shared on social media
content: New Delhi, March 31 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi purportedly speaking against reservation in the Parliament. In its investigation, the Desk found that a selected portion of PM's recent speech in the Rajya Sabha was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. The viral video was a selected portion of PM Modi's Motion of Thanks to the President's Address in the Rajya Sabha, delivered on February 7 during the Budget Session. Claim An X user shared on March a video of PM Modi purportedly speaking against reservation to the backward class in his speech at the Parliament. The post with over 3,500 views read: "All Scheduled Caste, Tribe and Backward Class people should watch this video of Modi, their eyes will be opened. Modi is saying that by keeping people from these classes in government jobs, the standard of government work will fall! जागो भक्तों जागो! #NoVoteToBJP #GintiKaro." Here is the link and archive link to the post and screenshot related to the same: Investigation The Desk divided the video shared on social media into several keyframes using the InVid Tool Search. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video was posted on X by several other users with similar claims: Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) of two such X posts: On further scanning the search results, the Desk across a video on YouTube, uploaded from the official handle of PM Narendra Modi on February 7, 2024. The Desk watched the video and found that this was an extended version of the viral video. The description of the video stated that it was a Live from PM Modi's Rajya Sabha Speech during the Motion of Thanks on the President's Address during the Budget Session. "Prime Minister Narendra Modi replied to the Motion of Thanks on the President's address to Parliament in Rajya Sabha. Addressing the House, PM Modi said that the 75th Republic Day is a significant milestone in the nation's journey and the President during her address spoke about India's self-confidence. PM Modi underlined that in her address, the President expressed confidence about India's bright future and acknowledged the capability of the citizens of India," read the description of the YouTube video. Here is the link and screenshot of the same: While watching the 1:44-hour-long video, the Desk noticed that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 40 minutes and 20 seconds. On listening to the entire speech from the timestamp of 39:20 minutes, PM Modi can be seen reading a letter, which he stated was written by former PM Jawaharlal Nehru to the then CMs of states. In the letter, Nehru was quoted expressing his views against reservation in government jobs. While quoting Nehru in the letter, PM Modi said: "I remember Nehru ji more with respect these days. Once Nehru ji had written a letter and this letter was written to the Chief Ministers. I am reading the translation he had written.. this is a letter written by Prime Minister Nehru ji to the Chief Ministers of the country at that time. It is on record, I am reading the translation. I (Pandit Nehru) do not like any reservation… and especially not reservation in jobs. I am against any step which promotes inefficiency, which leads to second-rate standards. This is a letter written by Pandit Nehru to the Chief Ministers." After watching the full video, the Desk found that it included the portions from the viral video. Here is a combination image, showing the same: Taking a cue from the video, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a report by The Economics Times, reporting about the incident. The title of the news report, published on February 7, 2024, read: "Nehru didn't want reservation in jobs at all," says PM Modi in Rajya Sabha. Here is the link to the report : Subsequently, the desk concluded that a clipped video of PM Modi's speech in the Parliament was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this photo doesn't show the crowd at INDIA bloc's 'Loktantra Bachao' rally; old and unrelated photo shared as recent on social media
content: New Delhi, April 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo of a massive crowd, which he claimed gathered during the INDIA bloc's 'Loktantra Bachao' rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on March 31. In its investigation, the Desk found that a five-year-old photo was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. Organised by the Aam Aadmi Party in protest against the arrest of Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal by the Enforcement Directorate, the 'maha rally' on March 31 was attended by several opposition leaders, including Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, and PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti among others. Claim An X user on March 31, shared a photo of a massive crowd, claiming that it gathered at INDIA bloc' 'Loktantra Bachao' rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi on March 31. The post with over 221k views read, "BIG BREAKING Massive crowds today at the INDIA alliance rally at the Ramlila Maidan New Delhi.Godi Media won't show you these visuals." Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the photo, shared in the viral post, through Google Lens and came across multiple accounts sharing the same photo with similar claims. Here is the links( here and here ) and archive links( here and here ). On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an article by Peoples Democracy, shared on February 10, 2019. The report carried the same image as the one shared in viral social media posts. According to the report, in view of the Lok Sabha elections of 2019, a huge rally was organised under the leadership of Left parties on February 3, 2019 at the Brigade Parade Ground in Kolkata. In this rally, a resolution was taken to remove the Trinamool Congress government and the BJP-led NDA government from power. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk further scanned the Google Lens search results of the viral photo and came across another X post by Communist Party of India (Marxist), West Bengal State Committee carrying the same image dated June 10, 2020. The post read, "You can cut all the flowers but you cannot keep Spring from coming. A bird eye view of last year Birgade Rally at #Kolkata #LalSalaamComrade" Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same: The search results also led us to a news report by Hindustan Times, published on March 8, 2021. The report carried the same photo with the caption: "Brigade rally called by Left Front, Indian National Congress and Indian Secular Front (ISF) ahead of West Bengal Assembly Election in Kolkata. (Samir Jana/HT Photo)." Here is the link and screenshot of the report: Subsequently, the Desk managed to trace the online presence of the photo back to 2019 and also found that it has been reshared on social media multiple times over the years.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of women hurling abuses at BJP van falsely linked to upcoming Lok Sabha polls; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of women hurling abuses at an election van of the BJP and tearing its posters is being shared widely shared on the internet, with caption and hashtags insinuating that it is of a recent incident. In its investigation, the PTI fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video from Bihar's Muzaffarpur was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user on March 25 a video of women hurling at a BJP election campaigning van and tearing its posters. "BJP's trend beyond 400 have started coming #NoVoteToBJP," read the caption of the Facebook Shorts video, insinuating that it was a recent incident ahead of the Lok Sabha polls. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several videos on YouTube, which carried the same video with similar claims. Two such video can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk then watched the viral video closely and observed that women in the video were talking in Hindi. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a video on Facebook dated for October 25, 2020. Here is the link and archive link to the post, below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and found that this was an extended version of the viral video. We watched the full video and found that it included the portions from the viral video. Below is a combination image, showing the same: The caption of the video stated that the incident took place in the Kudhni area of Muzaffarpur, during the runup to the 2020 Bihar assembly elections. The caption of the video read, "मुज़फ़्फ़रपुर के कुढ़नी से BJP विधायक केदार प्रसाद गुप्ता की प्रचार गाड़ी एक गाँव में पहुँची तो महिलाओं ने इतनी गंदी-गंदी गालियाँ दीं कि आप कल्पना भी नहीं कर सकते। महिलाओं ने गाड़ी पर पोस्टर फाड़ डाले और गाड़ी को उलटा भागने पर मजबूर कर दिया। #ViralVideo" An English translation of the caption, "When the campaign vehicle of BJP MLA Kedar Prasad Gupta from Kudhni in Muzaffarpur reached a village, women abused him so much that you cannot even imagine. The women tore the posters on the car and forced the car to reverse. #ViralVideo" Taking a cue from the video report, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a video report by News Click, about the incident, which was published on October 21, 2020. The title of the news report, published on October 21,2020 read: "Bihar Elections: JD-U, BJP Leaders Face Protests by Angry Voters during Campaign". "In several villages, people have asked campaigning NDA candidates to 'go back' over issues of unemployment and development work," read the summary of the report. Here is the link and screenshot of the report: Another news report by Jansatta, published on October 25, 2020, also reported about the incident. Here is the link to the report . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video from Bihar's Muzaffarpur was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of PM Modi seated while President Droupadi Murmu stands shared with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi April 2, (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo, showing PM Modi sitting next to BJP stalwart LK Advani while President Droupadi Murmu standing next to them. The user shared the photo to insinuate that the latter was disrespected by the two leaders. In its investigation, the Desk found that a photo from the event was taken out of context and shared on social media with a misleading claim. On March 31, President Droupadi Murmu conferred Advani with the prestigious Bharat Ratna at the latter's residence. Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar and PM Modi were also present on the occasion. Claim An X user shared on March 31 a photo of PM Modi and former Deputy PM LK Advani seated, while President Draupadi Murmu remained standing. The user shared the photo to insinuate that the latter was disrespected by the two BJP leaders. Here is the link and archive link and screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral image through Google lens, and came across an X post with the same photo, shared by Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Priyanka Chaturvedi. Here is the link and archive link and below is screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the same photo was shared by TMC MP Jawhar Sircar on March 31. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and found a video on YouTube, shared from the official account of PM Modi, on March 31, 2024. The description of the video read, "LIVE: President confers Bharat Ratna on Shri LK Advani Ji in PM Modi's presence." Notably, this video was from the same event, from which a photo was shared in the viral social media posts. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Here is the link and screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the full video and found that President Droupadi Murmu stood up to confer the award to Advani, while she remained seated the rest of the time. While Murmu was giving the award to the veteran BJP leader, all others, including PM Modi, Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar and former Vice President M Venkaiah Naidu remained seated. Taking a cue from the video, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a report by The Mint. The report published a picture where President Murmu can be seen sitting adjacent to PM Modi and former deputy PM Lal Krishna Advani. Here is the link and screenshot of the same: The title of the news report, published on March 31, 2024, read: "PM Modi 'proud' to witness Bharat Ratna award ceremony for Lal Krishna Advani: 'He played pivotal role in…'". "President Droupadi Murmu on Sunday conferred the Bharat Ratna upon veteran Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Lal Krishna Advani. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar were present at Lal Krishna Advani's residence on the occasion. While acknowledging Lal Krishna Advani's pivotal role in shaping modern India, PM Modi said that he is proud of getting the chance to work with him." We then scanned the X handle of President of India and found a March 31 post, which carried four photos from the same event in two thread posts. Here is the link to the X post , and below are screenshots of the thread posts: One of these photos was the same as the one shared in the viral social media posts, while another photo showed the President seated alongside PM Modi and LK Advani. The event, which is traditionally held in the Rashtrapati Bhavan, was conducted at the residence of LK Advani, considering his age and health condition. Others who received the award were former Prime Ministers PV Narasimha Rao, Chaudhary Charan Singh, former Bihar CM Karpoori Thakur, and agrarian economist MS Swaminathan. They all were given the award posthumously. To further cross-check the claim made in the social media posts, we watched other videos from the event and noticed that only the President of India and the one receiving the award stood while others in the audience remained seated. Here is the link to the video where RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary receives the Bharat Ratna award for Chaudhary Charan Singh. Below are screenshots of the same: The Desk then further checked videos from other award events and noticed the same pattern where only the President and the awardees can be seen standing while others remain seated. Here is the link to the video from 2023 National Sports and Adventure Awards, and below are screenshots from the same: We then conducted a customised Google search to look for protocols at such events and came across an X post by Ashok Malik, the Press Secretary of President Ram Nath Kovind from 2017 to 2019. As per the post, Rashtrapati Bhavan adheres to various protocols. According to these protocols, during certain ceremonies, both the President and recipient stand, while other dignitaries such as the Vice-President and Prime Minister are seated. Exceptions are made for elderly or indisposed recipients who may remain seated. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo was taken out of context and shared on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Amit Shah shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 2 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : A video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah is being widely shared on social media, in which he can be heard saying that "the country should be divided into two parts – North India and South India". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video from Shah's interview to a news channel was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on March 20 a video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, in which he can be heard stating that the "country should be divided into two parts – North India and South India." Here is the link and archive link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk then divided the video shared on social media into several keyframes using the InVid Tool Search. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video was posted by several other users with similar claims: Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) of two such X posts: Further, the Desk noticed Amit Shah holding a mic with the logo of News18. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of 'CNN News18'. We watched the video and found that this was an extended version of the viral video. The description of the video stated that it was a Live from the Rising Bharat Summit 2024, organised by News18, that featured PM Modi, Amit Shah and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the Live, the Desk noticed that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 2:21:22 to 2:21:25. On listening to the entire conversation from 2 hours 40 minutes 40 seconds Amit Shah can be heard answering a question by the anchor about BJP's performance in South India. An English translation of the conversation between the anchor and Union Minister Amit Shah, "Amit Ji, let's discuss South India, where Modi Ji has focused extensively. In the past two to three months, Modi Ji has visited multiple times. You also hope that this time BJP's performance will be very good in South India. The first question is a senior Congress leader said that South India should be a separate country. First, I would like to know what you want to say about this.' In response, Amit Shah stated, "Well, the answer to this should be given by Rahul Ji. So far, the Congress has not condemned the statement made by that leader. The people of the country seem to believe that it is Congress policy to divide the country into two parts, South India, and North India. But Rahul Baba, don't worry, now the BJP is so powerful that the Congress won't be able to divide the country again. BJP will never allow the country to be divided. It cannot happen. What are you doing? You are talking about dividing the country into two to win elections" After watching the live session, the Desk found that it included the portions from the viral video. Here is a combination image, showing the same: In further investigation, the Desk scanned the official X handle of Shah and found that a video of the same event was shared by him. Here is the link and archive link and screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Shah was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of BJP's Ashwini Choubey crying at a press conference shared as recent on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 3 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of senior BJP leader Ashwini Choubey, with the claim that he broke into tears at a press conference for being denied Lok Sabha poll ticket from Buxar, Bihar. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check found that an old and unrelated video of Choubey was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The BJP on March 24 announced its candidates for 17 Lok Sabha seats in Bihar, dropping three sitting MPs, including Union Minister Ashwani Kumar Choubey. Choubey, who was elected from Buxar for the second consecutive term in 2019, has been replaced by Mithilesh Tiwari, a senior party leader and a former MLA. Claim An X user shared on March 28 a video of Union Minister Ashwini Choubey, and claimed that crying after being denied an election ticket from Buxar. "अश्विनी चौबे के एक एक आंसू का बदला लेगा ब्राह्मण समाज भाजपा ने अश्विनी चौबे का टिकट काटकर बिहार के सम्पूर्ण ब्राह्मण का अपमान किया है। ब्राह्मण समाज स्वाभिमानी समाज है वो ऐसी पार्टी को कभी वोट नहीं करेगी जिसने उसके प्रिय नेता को सार्वजनिक जगह पर रोने को मजबूर कर दिया हो।ब्रह्मण समाज अपने इस अपमान का बदला राजद को वोट करके लेगा ताकि भविष्य में भाजपा फिर किसी ब्राह्मण को रुलाने की गलती न करेगी।" read the post with over 90k views. An English translation of the post read: "Brahmin community will take revenge for every tear of Ashwini Choubey. BJP has insulted the entire Brahmin community of Bihar by cutting the ticket of Ashwini Choubey. Brahmin society is a self-respecting society, it will never vote for a party which has forced its favorite leader to cry in a public place. The Brahmin community will take revenge for this insult by voting for RJD so that in future the BJP will not make the mistake of making any Brahmin cry again." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video was posted by several other users with similar claims: Two such X posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The Desk the conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a video report on YouTube, shared by IndiaTV on January 16, 2023. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The description of the report read, "केंद्रीय मंत्री अश्विनी चौबे आज मीडिया के सामने फूट-फूटकर रोने लगे | किसी को कुछ भी समझ में नहीं आया कि आखिर हुआ क्या | लोग एक दूसरे को देखने लगे, मंत्री जी को हुआ क्या? किसी को समझ में नहीं आ रहा था अश्विनी चौबे पटना में थे | नीतीश सरकार के खिलाफ प्रेस कॉन्फ्रेंस कर रहे थे... तभी एक खबर उनको मिली खबर सुनकर अश्विनी चौबे खुद को संभाल नहीं पाए और रोने लगे, अश्विनी चौबे ने बाद में खुद बताया उनके रोने की वजह क्या थी" An English translation read, "Union Minister Ashwini Choubey started crying bitterly in front of the media today. No one understood what happened. People started looking at each other, what happened to the minister? No one was able to understand that Ashwini Chaubey was in Patna. Nitish was holding a press conference against the government... then he got the news. On hearing the news, Ashwini Choubey could not control herself and started crying, Ashwini Choubey herself later told what was the reason for her crying." Taking a cue from the video report, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a report by Hindustan Times, about the incident. The title of the news report, published on January 17, 2023, read: "Why Ashwini Choubey broke down during a press conference". According to the report, Ashwini Choubey could not control his tears at a press conference in Patna when he heard news of the demise of Parshuram Chaturvedi. Parshuram Chaturvedi accompanied Ashwini Choubey in the hunger strike and died due to cardiac arrest. Here is the link to the report : Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video was shared as recent on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This organisation supporting INDIA bloc in Lok Sabha polls is RSS namesake; social media posts shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi April 3 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a press conference under the banner of 'Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh', the BJP ideologue. A person addressing the press conference can be heard announcing his support to the opposition's INDIA bloc in the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that that the organisation in question in the viral video was not the real RSS, but was a new organisation floated with the same name. The social media post was shared with a misleading claim. The organisation mentioned in the name of 'Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh' was founded by an activist, named Janardan Moon, in 2017 whereas the RSS we all know of was founded in 1925 by Keshav Baliram Hedgewar. Claim An X user shared on April 1 a video of a press conference held under the banner of 'Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh' where the organisation announced its support to the INDIA bloc in the upcoming Lok Sabha polls. "RSS ने BJP का छोड़ा साथ ! कांग्रेस के विचारधारा का किया समर्थन , "प्रेस कांफ्रेंस" के मंच से "भाजपा" को हराने का किया एलान !! देशवासियों से अनुरोध हैं कि "मोदी भगाओ,देश बचाओ"," read the post with over 3,300 views. An English translation to the post, "RSS left BJP! Supported the ideology of Congress, announced to defeat "BJP" from the platform of "press conference"!!The countrymen are requested to -- "Drive out Modi, save the country" " Here is the link and archive link to the post, and screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several users who carried the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The Desk then watched the viral video closely and found that the logo and banner of the organisation seen in the video was completely different from that of the RSS. Below is a combination image, showing the same: Further, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and came across a video on YouTube, uploaded by a channel named 'AWAAZ INDIA TV' on April 3, 2024. The Desk watched the video and found that this was an extended version of the viral video. Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: The description of the video read: "जो लोग अचंभित हो रहे है की "RSS" ने INDIA गठबंधन को कैसे समर्थन दे दिया, उनके लिए बता दे कि देश में दो RSS हैं, एक Online REGISTERD है जिसने कांग्रेस को समर्थन दिया हैं, और दूसरा UNREGISTERD जिसके सरसंघचालक मोहन भागवत है, कृपया ध्यान रखें भ्रमित न हो जाए। Nagpur ፤ RSS given unconditional support to INDIA Alliance" An English translation of the description read: "For those who are wondering how RSS supported the INDIA alliance, let us tell you that there are two RSSs in the country, one is online REGISTERD which has supported Congress, and the other is UNREGISTERD whose Sarsanghchalak is Mohan Bhagwat. Please be careful not to get confused. Nagpur; RSS gave unconditional support to INDIA Alliance." Taking a cue from the video, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search and came across a report by National Herald, reporting about the incident. The title of the news report, published on August 13, 2023, read: "A new political RSS, four years old, takes on the old RSS, the cultural organisation." Here is the link to the report and screenshot of the report. During investigation, we found another report by Indian Express. According to this report published on March 31, 2024, a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) official filed a complaint against Janardan Moon with the Election Commission and Nagpur Police Commissioner on March 29. The report stated that in the press conference, Jarndon Moon misrepresented the facts and misled the people by saying that the RSS was supporting the Congress in the Lok Sabha elections. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by Organizer Weekly, the Mohan Bhagwat-led RSS mouthpiece. According to the post, "After cursing #RSS for more than 75 years, #Congress and INDI Alliance have come up with their own 'FAKE RSS' to confuse voters. A desperate attempt? #FakeRSS_Alert" Here is the link and archive link and screenshot of the post In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to Janardan Moon, the founder of the 'Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh', who held the press conference to announce his support to the INDIA bloc. "My organisation has nothing to do with the RSS led by Mohan Bhagwat, mine is a different RSS. The RSS has lodged a complaint against my organisation with the Election Commission of India. We have not only extended support to the Congress, but to the entire INDIA bloc," he told PTI. Moon also shared with the Desk the form of application for registration of a society, dated August 28, 2017. Below is a screenshot of the same: Moon also shared with us the subsequent the order by the Assistant Registrar of Society, Nagpur, dated December 8, 2021, which rejected the application of Moon seeking registration of the organisation. Below is a screenshot of the same: For further confirmation, the Desk contacted RSS' All India Co-Publicity Chief Narendra Thakur, who said: "We have no connection with the RSS (led by Janardan Moon). They are misusing the name of the RSS and trying to mislead people." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an organisation with the name 'Rashtriya Sayamsevak Sangh' was confused with the RSS, the leader of a large body of organisations called the Sangh Parivar.

title: PTI Fact Check: These photos of Virat Kohli's sand sculptures are AI-generated; Details inside
content: New Delhi April 4 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a combination image of four sand sculptures of cricketer Virat Kohli, which he claimed were made by the kid seen in the photos. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photos of sand sculptures were created through Artificial Intelligence (AI) and shared with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on March 31 a combination image of four sand sculptures of cricketer Virat Kohli, which he claimed were made by the kid seen in the photos. The post with over 730k read, "बच्चे की खूबसूरत कलाकारी, बना दी विराट कोहली की प्रतिमा #viratkohli#bestphotochallenge#BestPhotographyChallengeio#picturechallenge #photo#challenge#photographychallenge#photography#picture#picoftheday#photographer #photoshoot#photochallenge#PhotoEditingChallenge#ChallengeChallenge" An English translation of the post read: "Child's beautiful artwork, made a statue of Virat Kohli #viratkohli#bestphotochallenge#BestPhotographyChallengeio#picturechallenge #photo#challenge#photographychallenge#photography#picture#picoftheday#photographer #photoshoot#photochallenge#PhotoEditingChallenge#ChallengeChallenge" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google lens, and came across multiple posts with similar photos and claims. Two such X posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively: In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the comment section of the Facebook post and noticed that a user claimed the photos were AI-generated. On this comment, the user who shared the photo acknowledged the fact that they were generating using AI. Here is a screenshot of the comment. Taking a cue from this, the Desk further scanned Sharma's profile and found that apart from Virat Kohli, he had also shared pictures of sand sculptures of former Indian team captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni and several others with the same claim. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) along with the screenshots respectively: Taking the investigation further, the desk examined the picture with the help of an AI image detector tool HuggingFace.co. Here is the link to the website and screenshot of the result we found. During further investigation, the Desk found a video tutorial on how to create AI generated images. The video was uploaded by a YouTube channel 'Bk oll Tech'. According to the video these pictures can be easily created with the help of Bing AI tool. The description of the video read, "Viral Cricket Image Create | Virat Kohli Image Create | Bing AI image createExperience a rollercoaster of emotions in this heart-wrenching 3D-rendered proposal scene. Watch as a 20-year-old boy bravely kneels, clutching a red rose, to profess his love to an 18-year-old girl. But amidst the beauty of the garden backdrop, tears flow as the girl, adorned in a white lehenga, stands beside another boy wearing a hoodie with 'Name' printed on it. Join us in witnessing this poignant moment unfold, where love and heartbreak collide. Don't miss out on the raw emotions captured in this breathtaking visual narrative." Here is the link to the YouTube video , and below is a screenshot of the same: As can be seen in the screenshot above, this is the same kid as seen in the viral photos of Kohli's sand sculptures. According to the information received, the desk put the relevant prompt on the same tool and created a picture exactly like the viral picture, which can be seen here. The desk also tried to create pictures of other cricketers by putting different prompts on this tool, which can be seen here. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Virat Kohli's sand sculptures, as seen in the viral photo, were created with the help of an AI tool.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Bill Gates has not appointed Dolly Chaiwalla as Windows 12 brand ambassador; video with false claim shared on social media
content: New Delhi, April 5 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check) : A video is being widely shared on social media, claiming that Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates appointed internet sensation from Nagpur, Dolly Chaiwalla, as the brand ambassador of Windows 12. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that no such announcement was made by Microsoft or Gates. The video was shared on social media with false claim. The viral video comes in the backdrop of Bill Gates visiting the tea stall of Nagpur resident Sunil Patil, popularly known as Dolly Chaiwalla, during his visit to India in February 2024. Furthermore, while there have been a lot of speculations around Windows 12, the highly-awaited update for the Windows operating system is yet to be announced by the company. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 5 a video which claimed that Bill Gates appointed Dolly Chaiwalla as the brand ambassador of Windows 12. The video shows a photo of Bill Gates and Dolly Chaiwalla standing together along with Microsoft logo and text stating that the former has been appointed as the brand ambassador of Windows 12. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video was posted by several other users with similar claims: Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The Desk then scanned the website and social media handles of Microsoft, to check if the company made any such announcement, as claimed in the viral social media posts. However, we could not find anything related to Windows 12 or any mention of Dolly Chaiwalla. Here are the links to X , Facebook and Instagram handles of Microsoft. We also scanned the official website of Microsoft, but could neither find any mention of Windows 12 nor Dolly. Here is a link to the website . In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords, and came across an Instagram post a post related to the same claim, shared by a page named 'thebindutimes' on February 29. "Dolly Chaiwalla made brand ambassador for Windows 12 by Bill Gates after having tea at Dolly ki tapri" read the caption of the post with over 35,000 likes. Here is the link and archive link and screenshot of the post: On scanning the Instagram handle, the Desk found that it mentioned: 'India's most trusted SATIRE news source. All posts are done for Satire/Parody.' Here is the link for the Instagram profile and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the post was shared on February 29, soon after pictures of the meeting between Dolly Chaiwalla and Bill Gates emerged on the internet. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Bill Gates' photo with Dolly Chaiwala was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Centre hasn't announced 'Ek Parivar Ek Naukri' scheme; social media posts shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, April 5 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user recently shared a video, which claims that the central government has launched 'Ek Parivar, Ek Sarkari Naukri' (one family, one government job) scheme, under which lakhs of people will get government job without giving any exam. The video, claiming that only families with non-government jobs, will get the scheme's benefits, also explains how one can fill the form to apply for it. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the central government has not announced any such scheme. The social media post was shared with a misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 2 a video which claimed that the central government had launched 'Ek Parivar Ek Sarkari Naukri' (one family, one government job) scheme, under which lakhs of people will get government jobs without giving any exam. The video also explained the process to apply to get the benefit of the scheme. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google search to check if the central government launched any such scheme. We came across a Facebook post – a Reel – in which a person makes the same claim, further stating that the age limit for the scheme is 18 to 55 years and mentions different salary brackets, based on the educational qualification of the beneficiary. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across an article published by a website named 'PM Yojana Adda' on April 4, whose headline read: "Ek Parivar Ek Naukri Yojana 2024: अब हर घर में होगा सरकारी नौकरी, यहाँ जाने आवेदन कैसे करे!" Here is the link to the webpage and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the government websites but couldn't find any mention of any such scheme, as claimed in the viral posts. Click here and here to check the government websites. In the next part of investigation, the Desk logged on to the website 'Crypto Pur', mentioned in the viral post. We searched for the said article on 'Ek Parivar Ek Naukri' scheme. Here is the link to the said article and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk clicked on the 'form' hyperlink mentioned in the post, but it just redirected to the homepage of the website. We then conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a January 2019 news report by Amar Ujala, according to which, a similar scheme was announced by the Sikkim government back then. Here is the link to the report titled 'सिक्किम : हर परिवार को मिलेगी सरकारी नौकरी, लागू हुई 'एक परिवार-एक नौकरी' योजना'. We also found a report by India Today, dated Jan 13, 2019, whose headline read: "Sikkim launches 'One Family, One Job' scheme". Here is the link to the report . Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the central government had not launched any such scheme as claimed in the viral social media posts.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video from Haryana's Nuh shared as recent with false claim ahead of Eid; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 8 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a group of men warning people of social boycott if they employed any Muslim is being widely shared on social media. The video is being shared with hashtags insinuating that it is from a recent incident and warns people to watch it before going for Eid shopping. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated from Haryana's Nuh was shared as recent on social media with false claim. The video dates back to August 2023, following the communal violence that erupted in Haryana's Nuh which left at least seven people dead and several others injured. Claim A Facebook user shared a video of a group of men carrying a banner and warning shopkeepers of social boycott if they employed any Muslim. Using hashtag of Eid, the user insinuated that it was a recent incident and warned people to be careful when shopping for Eid-ul-Fitr. "ईद की शॉपिंग करने से पहले ये वीडियो जरूर देखें।वीडियो को ज्यादा से ज्यादा शेयर करें प्लीज ज्यादा से ज्यादा शेयर करें प्लीज#ईदमुबारक#eidulfitar#shopping#brand' read the post with over 91,000 views. An English translation to the post read, "Please watch this video before doing Eid shopping. Please share the video as much as possible. Please share as much as possible #EidMubarak#eidulfitar#shopping#brand." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across the same video posted on YouTube on April 2. Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: On watching the viral video closely, the Desk noticed that the banner mentioned "Nuh (Mewat)" and July 2023. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across an X post by journalist Rana Ayyub on August 9, 2023. The post carried an extended version of the viral video and the caption of the post read: "Muslims given an ultimatum in Haryana. Shopkeepers being asked to sack their Muslim employees or face boycott. Some of our well meaning friends will continue with the most neutral and nauseating whataboutery. Every day apartheid." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across a video report on YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of Al Jazeera English on August 10, 2023. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The description of the video read, "Far-right Hindus in India's Haryana state have launched a boycott to expel Muslims after a wave of communal violence that has led to the deaths of several people." Meanwhile, a report by Economic Times, published on August 12, 2023, quoted the Supreme Court observing that the alleged call for social and economic boycott of Muslim community was "unacceptable". The title of the news report read: "Call for boycott of Muslims unacceptable; hate speech needs to end: Supreme Court" Here is the link to the report: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking to the upcoming Eid festival.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Hardik Pandya has not joined BJP; social media post shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 8 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and cricketer Hardik Pandya sharing a dais, and claimed that the latter had joined the BJP. In the video, Shah can be heard announcing Pandya's name while the slug running on the video claims that the cricketer had joined the ruling party. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video from an event was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. On February 12, Shah inaugurated the Gandhinagar Lok Sabha Premier League, a cricket tournament for the people of Gandhinagar Lok Sabha constituency. The event was attended by Indian cricketer Hardik Pandya and Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel. The clipped video is being shared on social media ahead of the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls. Claim An Instagram user shared on February 20 a video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and cricketer Hardik Pandya sharing a dais, and claimed that the latter had joined the BJP. The video shows Shah announcing the name of Pandya while the text running on the video claims that the cricketer had joined the BJP. The Instagram post with over 1 million views read, "क्या लगता है" An English translation read,"What do you think?" Here is the link and archive link and screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a photo gallery by The Free Press Journal, which carried the pictures as shown in the viral video. The caption in the photo gallery, dated February 13, 2024, read: "Amit Shah inaugurates Gandhinagar Lok Sabha Premier League with Hardik Pandya." Here is the link to the photo gallery and below is the screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a video shared by the official handle of CMO Gujarat, dated for February 12, 2023. The description of the video read: "Union Home Minister Shri Amit Shah inaugurates Gandhinagar Lok Sabha Premier League." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk noticed that the viral video was clipped from the timestamps of 03:55 to 4:12 and 22:20 to 22:35. On listening to the Union Home Minister's speech from 21 minutes 40 seconds, he can be heard addressing the dignitaries on the stage. After watching the video, the Desk found that it included the portions from the viral video. Here is a combination image, showing the same: In further investigation, the Desk scanned the official X handle of Shah and found that he shared photos of the same event. "आज अहमदाबाद में गाँधीनगर लोकसभा प्रीमियर लीग (GLPL) का शुभारंभ किया। प्रधानमंत्री श्री @narendramodi जी के नेतृत्व में देशभर में 'सांसद खेलकुद स्पर्धा' का आयोजन किया जा रहा है और इसके तहत ही गाँधीनगर लोकसभा प्रीमियर लीग शुरू हुई है। मुझे विश्वास है कि गाँधीनगर लोकसभा की 7 विधानसभाओं के बीच खेला जाने वाला यह क्रिकेट टूर्नामेंट, क्षेत्र में खेल की संस्कृति और एक स्वस्थ जीवन शैली को बढ़ावा देने में उपयोगी साबित होगा।" read the caption with over 137k views. An English translation of the caption read, "Gandhinagar Lok Sabha Premier League (GLPL) launched in Ahmedabad today. Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, 'MP Sports Competition' is being organized across the country and under this, Gandhinagar Lok Sabha Premier League has been started. I am confident that this cricket tournament, played between the 7 assembly constituencies of Gandhinagar Lok Sabha, will prove useful in promoting the culture of sports and a healthy lifestyle in the region." Here is the link to the post and screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped portion of a cricket inauguration event was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of AAP MP Sanjay Singh shared as recent on social media with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Apr 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of AAP MP Sanjay Singh confronting police officials for allegedly manhandling a person is being widely shared on social media. The timing of the posts and the hashtags used along in them insinuate that the incident was a recent one, after the Supreme Court granted him bail in the excise policy case. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video dating back to 2021 was shared as recent with a misleading claim. Singh, after remaining lodged in Tihar Jail since October 2023, walked out of the prison on April 3, a day after the Supreme Court granted him bail in the excise policy-linked money laundering case. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 2 a video of AAP MP Sanjay Singh confronting a police official allegedly over the issue of manhandling a person. "Welcome back #SanjaySingh He knows how to deal with Modi's Police, CBI, ED #viral #viralreels #public #aamaadmiparty #arvindkejriwal #modi #ModiKaParivar #rahulgandhi #tejaswiyadav #akhileshyadav #uttarpradesh #yogiadityanath #reelit #reelindia #india #bjpexposed #bjp #instagram #instagood #sanjaysingh #viral #viralvideos," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a Facebook post, which carried the same video as the one shared in above mentioned post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning social media platforms, we found that the same video was shared by several social media users too around the same time. Three such X posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by Aam Aadmi Party – Uttar Pradesh's official account, shared on October 20, 2021. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: "तिरंगा यात्रा अवैध है, भारत में तिरंगा यात्रा नहीं निकालेंगे तो कहां निकालेंगे? #Tiranga_Virodhi_BJP," read the caption of the post. The video shows Singh arguing with the police official, reportedly after being denied permission for Tiranga Yatra in Varanasi. The Desk noticed that this video was from the same incident, from which a video was shared in the viral social media posts. Below is a combination image, comparing the two videos – one shared on social media recently and the other shared by AAP in 2021. We found another post by AAP from the same date, hitting out at the BJP over the subsequent arrest of Sanjay Singh after the party was denied permission for the rally in Varanasi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a video report by OneIndia Hindi, dated October 21, 2021. The title of the news report on YouTube read: "AAP MP Sanjay Singh लिए गए हिरासत में, बिना इजाजत निकालने जा रहे तिरंगा यात्रा | वनइंडिया हिंदी" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the video report and the viral video: We also found a report by Times of India, dated Oct 21, 2021, on the incident. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Sanjay Singh was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of man sleeping near leopards is not from India; 2019 video from South Africa shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 11 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man sleeping with leopards is being widely shared on social media, with the claim that it was from Pipleshwar Mahadev Temple located in Sirohi, Rajasthan, where leopards come at night and sleep near the priest. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video from a cheetah breeding centre in South Africa was shared as recent with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 10 a video of a man sleeping with leopards and claimed that it was from Pipleshwar Mahadev Temple in Sirohi, Rajasthan and the man in the video was the temple priest. The post read, "राजस्थान के सिरोही स्थीत पिपलेश्वर महादेव के मंदिर मे रात को चीते पुजारी के पास आकर सो जाते हे ۔۔भगवान् होने का ईससे अच्छा प्रमाण ओर क्या हो सकता हे ۔ " An English translation to the post read, "In the temple of Pipaleshwar Mahadev located in Sirohi, Rajasthan, leopards come and sleep near the priest at night. What could be a better proof of the existence of God than this?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other users with a similar claim. Two such Facebook posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found an 'X' post by one Parveen Kaswan, an Indian Forest Service officer, who had also shared the same video on June 10, 2020. "So what does a #cheetah prefers. Hard concrete or warm cloth. This one from an enclosure. All looks loveable though. VC Dolph C Volker," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the video report, the Desk conducted an advanced Google search with customised keywords and came across a video on YouTube uploaded by Dolph C. Volker on January 21, 2019. Here is the link to the YouTube video: The description of the video read: "I love when I know the answer to a question before it's asked. Do cheetahs prefer cold concrete or warm blankets and company?" "These captive cheetahs were bred and born at cheetah breeding centers in South Africa; one at Cheetah Experience. All are quite tame as they are groomed for the breeding program so when they have cubs, they can be monitored closely. An accepting and approachable mother allows that. There is a plan to release one of these cheetahs into a protected wild in the near future. "I was granted special permission to spend my nights with the three because I had watched them grow up and built up a relationship with them during past volunteering. It is natural for a family or friends of animals living together to share warmth. It is a survival behavior that is innate," it added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video from a cheetah breeding centre in South Africa was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to India.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 photo of IUML flags at Congress rally in Wayanad falsely shared as recent; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check): A photo showing an "ocean of green flags" at a roadshow is being widely shared on social media, with the claim that it is from the Congress' recent poll rally in Wayanad, the constituency of party leader Rahul Gandhi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo of Congress' rally with IUML in Wayanad was falsely shared as recent on social media, with a misleading claim. The photo went viral following the April 3 rally of Rahul Gandhi in Wayanad. The roadshow held in Kalpetta was attended by all major UDF partners, including key ally Indian Union Muslim League. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 9 a photo of an election rally, with the claim that it was from a Congress' roadshow, where there was an "ocean of green flags". The time of sharing the post insinuated that it was from the recent roadshow of Rahul Gandhi held in Wayanad on April 3. "Congress's road show, just see the ocean of green flags. No wonder their manifesto had everything about how to make India an IsIamic country...," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and came across an April 9 Instagram post by BJP leader Naveen Jindal, who shared the same photo with the caption: "केरल के वायनाड में आपका स्वागत है.." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the same photo was posted by several X users as well. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. We also found some users, insinuating that the green flags in the roadshow were that of Pakistan. One such post can be seen here , and its archived version can be viewed here : The search results further led the Desk to an article by The New Indian Express, published on April 5, 2019. The article carried the same viral photo as its feature image and its headline read: "You won't hear from me a word against CPI(M): Rahul Gandhi in Wayanad". Here is the link to the news report , and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption of the photo read: "AICC president Rahul Gandhi and general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra greeting party workers during the road show at Kalpetta after Rahul Gandhi filed his nomination papers in Wayanad on Thursday | A Sanesh". While it was clear that the viral photo was from the run-up to the 2019 Lok Sabha polls, the Desk further scanned the social media handles of Congress and found a post from April 3, the day Rahul Gandhi held a roadshow in Wayanad. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the photos of the two rallies – one held recently and the other held in April 2019. A stark difference can be noticed in the two photos above – the green flags, which are absent in the roadshow which was held recently. Taking a cue from this, we conducted an advanced Google search and came across a PTI report carried by The Print, which highlighted the same point, while also pointing out that the flags in the viral photo were those of Indian Union Muslim League (IUML), an ally of Congress in Kerala. Here is the link to the report. "Rahul Gandhi's roadshow here on Wednesday was visibly different from that of 2019 in the constituency when the green flags of ally IUML outnumbered the Congress's in the crowd. This time, the flags were conspicuous by their absence — even those of the sitting MP's party. The roadshow held in Kalpetta in Wayanad was attended by all major UDF partners, including key ally Indian Union Muslim League. UDF workers mostly displayed placards of Gandhi's image and his election symbol — the hand — to add colour to the campaign," read a section of the report. "At the height of the election campaign in 2019, senior BJP leader Amit Shah had criticised Gandhi for contesting from the constituency in Kerala, and remarked that during a procession in the area, it was difficult to discern whether it was India or Pakistan, alluding to the presence of IUML's green flags during the Congress leader's roadshow, a Congress source said," it added. Below is a combination image, which shows a clear difference between the logos of IUML and Pakistani flags: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old image from Congress' 2019 roadshow in Wayanad was falsely shared as recent on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show people attacking the car of BJP's Ashok Tanwar in Haryana's Sirsa
content: New Delhi, April 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video claiming that it showed BJP's Sirsa Lok Sabha candidate Ashok Tanwar's car was recently attacked by people while he was campaigning for the upcoming polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 11 a video, which showed some people pelting stones on a vehicle escorted by police vans, while cops tried to stop them. The caption of the post read: "He is Ashok Tanvar, BJP Candidate from Sirsa, Haryana. People, especially Farmers chasing him out who came to do election campaign. Abb Bolo Abb ki baar _____ Paar? #Elections2024 #SupremeCourt #ED #RRvsGT #EidAlFitr2024 #Patanjali." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an Instagram post, shared on April 11, which carried the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Two X (formerly Twitter) users also shared the same video. The posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk watched the video carefully and noticed the logos "Bharat News" and "PB News" at the top right corner. Taking a cue, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across an extended version of the viral video, shared by Pahredar Bharat News on July 11, 2021. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The title of the video read: "बड़ी खबर -भारी पड़ गया डिप्टी स्पीकर को सिरसा cdlu आना,किसानों ने तोड़ी रणबीर गंगवा की गाड़ी" An English translation of the title read: "Big news - Sirsa CDLU arrival proved costly for Deputy Speaker, farmers broke Ranbir Gangwa's car". On further scanning the search results, we found a report by The Hindu, dated July 15, 2021, which stated that the car of Gangwa was attacked by protesters in Haryana's Sirsa. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Mirror Now also published a video report on the incident, which included visuals from a different angle, which can be seen from 1:52 minutes timestamp. The title of the report read: "Haryana Deputy Speaker's car attacked in Sirsa, police disperse farmers & several detained". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across an April 11 report by The Tribune, where Tanwar disproved the viral video and accused the Congress and Aam Aadmi Party of spreading it. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video dating back to July 2021 was shared as recent, falsely linking it to BJP's Ashok Tanwar.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Kerala Govt didn't publish this textbook with communal claims; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A collage of two chapters with communal claims is being widely shared on social media, with the claim that the textbook which included these chapters was published by the Kerala government. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the textbook was published by the school chain - Peace International School - and was shared on social media with false claims. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 5 a photo of a collage of two chapters with communal claims and claimed that they were from a textbook published by the Kerala education board. The Instagram post with over 6000 likes read, "Very deep propaganda is going on in the state of Kerala.Such are textbooks children read in the schools run by Kerala Board. Shame." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and came across multiple Facebook posts with the same photo and similar claims. Two such Facebook posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. The same photo was also shared on X by several users. Here is the link and archive link to one such post with over 2 million views, and below is a screenshot of the same: While further scanning the search results, the Desk found a post from the official X handle of Minister for General Education and Labour of Kerala, V Sivankutty. The post with over 196.3K views read, "A complaint has been filed with the Kerala Director General of Police regarding the dissemination of false propaganda aimed at the Kerala Government, by the individual identified on X as 'Mr. Sinha'. The complaint urges legal intervention against the perpetrator." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning, the Desk found the official website of Kerala State Board 'Samagra' where all textbooks were available for download in multiple languages such as English, Malayalam, Kannada, and Tamil. Here is the link to the website . We scanned several textbooks on the website but couldn't find anyone with the said chapters, as mentioned in the collage. Meanwhile, the Desk noticed a reply on the minister's post, claiming that the chapters were from a textbook published by Peace International School, and not by Kerala Government. Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a report by Business Standard, dated for January 8, 2018. The title of the news report read, "Case registered against Kochi school for teaching objectionable contents." Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same: According to the report, a case was registered against the Peace International School in Kerala's Kochi for teaching objectionable content and for following a syllabus containing material violating existing Indian laws. The complaint was filed by The District Educational Officer in Ernakulam. The inquiries revealed that the textbooks in the school were aimed towards propagating ideas contradictory to the secular policies of the country to spread propaganda, against the policies of India. Another report by The News Minute, dated December 3, 2016, stated that the Kerala Police had arrested three publishers for "objectionable and communal content in school textbooks". "The Kochi city police arrested three Mumbai-based publishers on Friday, for printing textbooks with objectionable content that were part of the syllabi taught at the Peace International School in Ernakulam," read a section of the report. "The Peace School came under the radar of the authorities, following the missing cases of 21 persons from across Kerala, many of whom were in one way or the other connected to the school," read another portion of the report. Here is the link to the news report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the chapters, whose collage was shared on social media, were published in textbooks issued by the school chain named Peace International School, and not Kerala government.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi didn't push an old man during his Vellore rally; clipped video shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi April 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of PM Modi is being widely shared on social media with the claim that it shows him pushing an elderly man on the stage and not bothering to look back while he fell down. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the man fell on the stage after losing balance, and was not pushed by the PM. A clipped video was shared on social media with a false claim. The viral video was from PM Modi's election rally in Tamil Nadu's Vellore, held on April 10. Claim An Instagram user on April 11 shared a video of PM Modi, claiming that he pushed an old man on the stage and continued walking without bothering to look back as the man fell down. The post read, "मोदी जी को बुजुर्ग की उसके गिरने की कोई परवाह नहीं है।" An English translation read, "Modi ji doesn't care about the old man's fall." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other users with a similar claim. Two such Instagram posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a Live video shared by the official channel of Firstpost shared on April 10. The description of the video read, "PM Modi LIVE: PM Modi Addresses Public Meeting in Vellore, Tamil Nadu | India Elections 2024." Here is the link of the video and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the video contained the portion which was shared in the viral social media posts. Below is a combination image, showing the same: We then watched the entire 48:25-minute video and found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 48 minutes 02 seconds. The Desk observed that the PM addressed the crowd, and later after finishing his speech at the timestamp of 47 minutes, he greets people present on the dais. While greeting the members the old man can be seen on the stage where he loses his balance due to the crowd and falls down, following where others help him stand, and the PM leaves the stage. In further investigation, the Desk scanned the official X PM Modi and found pictures of the same event were shared by him. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The first photo shared by the PM shows the man who lost his balance and fell down on the stage. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of PM Modi's public rally was taken out of context and shared on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this photo of traffic discipline is not from UP's Bijnor; 2022 pic from Mizoram shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 15 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A user shared a photo of cars and two-wheelers queued up on one side of the road in an exemplary display of compliance of traffic rules, and claimed that it was from UP's Bijnor. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo from Mizoram was falsely shared as recent in the name of Bijnor. The compliance of traffic etiquettes by people in Mizoram have been lauded time and again on the internet. Viral pics and videos of people patiently waiting in their lanes, without honking or overtaking have often emerged on the internet. Claim A Facebook user on April 13 shared a photo of cars and two-wheelers queued up on one side of the road in an exemplary display of compliance of traffic rules, and claimed that the image was from Bijnor in Uttar Pradesh. The Facebook post with over 24,000 likes read, "ये अपने जिला बिजनौर की ख़ूबसूरती हे ट्रैफिक होने पर सब एक साइड में रुक जाते हे )बिजनोर वाले यूपी 20#bijnoriboys #sherkot #najibabad_city #afzalgarh #bijnori #Bijnor #Noorpur #Chandpur #seohara #dhampur" An English translation to the post read: "This is the beauty of our district Bijnor, when there is traffic, everyone stops on one side) Bijnor people UP 20. #bijnoriboys #sherkot #najibabad_city #afzalgarh #bijnori #Bijnor #Noorpur #Chandpur #seohara #dhampur" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot for the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and came across a Facebook post, with the same photo and a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The desk then observed the photo closely and noticed that the number plate of several vehicles started from 'MZ', an abbreviation for Mizoram. The desk further conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a post shared by Anand Mahindra, Chairman of Mahindra Group, on X (formerly Twitter) on March 1, 2022. He quote tweeted a user's post, which carried the same photo. The post with over 1,000 likes read: "What a terrific pic; Not even one vehicle straying over the road marker. Inspirational, with a strong message: it's up to US to improve the quality of our lives. Play by the rules… A big shoutout to Mizoram." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a report by Firstpost, dated March 2, 2022. The title of the news report read, "Commuters obeying traffic rules during jam win hearts, check viral picture here" Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a two-year-old photo from Mizoram was falsely shared on social media as recent in the name of UP's Bijnor.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Dainik Bhaskar didn't predict lead for INDIA bloc in pre-poll survey; fake screenshot viral on social media
content: New Delhi, April 15 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A purported newspaper clipping of Dainik Bhaskar is being widely shared on social media, with the claim that it shows the media house's joint survey with Nelson, predicting a lead for the INDIA alliance in 10 states in the upcoming Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Desk found that a fake clipping was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 13 a screenshot of a purported newspaper clipping of the Bhopal edition of Dainik Bhaskar, claiming that it predicted a lead for the INDIA alliance in 10 states, including Kerala, Karnataka, Telangana and Tamil Nadu, in its joint survey with Nelson ahead of the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls. "Dainik Bhaskar-Nelson Survey:- In 10 states INDIA alliance is leading & could cross 200 in these 10 states alone. Even in the Hindi heartland states, Modi's image is not enough to get votes for the BJP. NDA will find it tough to cross 180 this time as people of India have understood the real face of Modi & Gang," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that the same screenshot was shared by several Facebook users with similar claims. Two such Facebook users can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. We also found several X users sharing the same video with similar claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively: In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the April 13 e-paper edition of Dainik Bhaskar's Bhopal edition, but couldn't find any sch mention of the survey, mentioned in the viral social media posts. Here is the link to the April 13 edition of e-paper : The e-paper, however, carried an analytical article on the forthcoming polls, whose headline read: "उत्तर से पूर्व तक 'एनडीए' और दक्षिण में 'इंडिया' का दबदबा". Below is a screenshot of the same: Dainik Bhaskar had also shared the same on X on April 13. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found an X post, in which Dainik Bhaskar, termed the viral survey as "fake" and called for strict action against the "anti-social elements" who created it. "#FakeNews : यह सर्वे फेक है, जिसे कुछ असामाजिक तत्वों ने तैयार किया है... दैनिक भास्कर ऐसे किसी भी कंटेंट का दावा नहीं करता है... ऐसे लोगों पर सख्त कार्रवाई होनी चाहिए," read the caption of the April 13 X post. An English translation of the post read: "#FakeNews: This survey is fake, which has been prepared by some anti-social elements... Dainik Bhaskar does not claim any such content... Strict action should be taken against such people". Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: The publication's national editor LP Pant also responded to a now-deleted X post by journalist Paranjoy Guha Thakurta, who shared the same viral screenshot. (The archived post can be viewed here ).
