In his X post , Pant wrote: "महोदय, दैनिक भास्कर ने ऐसा कोई सर्वे नहीं करवाया है। भास्कर मास्टहेड का इस्तेमाल कर फर्जी सर्वे चलाया गया है। आपको भी शेयर करने से पहले इसकी प्रामाणिकता जांच लेनी चाहिए। दैनिक भास्कर आपकी इस पोस्ट पर कानूनी कार्रवाई करेगा।" An English translation of the post read: "Sir, Dainik Bhaskar has not conducted any such survey. Fake survey has been conducted using Bhaskar masthead. You should also check its authenticity before sharing. Dainik Bhaskar will take legal action against this post of yours." During our investigation, however, we came across a report by Dainik Bhaskar about is 'मेरा वोट, मेरी मर्जी' (My Vote, My Choice) survey, published on April 14. According to the survey, conducted on over 8 lakh respondents, 48 per cent of them said that they wanted to see PM Modi coming back for a third term while 37 per cent of the respondents noted unemployment as the biggest poll issue. Here is the link to the survey report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fabricated screenshot was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Aamir Khan didn't endorse any political party; edited video with AI voice clone shared on social media
content: New Delhi, April 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Bollywood actor Aamir Khan, in which he was heard talking about Rs 15 lakh in every Indian's bank account, and 'jumlas' (catchphrases). The video, because of its audio, gave an impression that Khan endorsed a political party during the run-up to the Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the actor's video dating back to 2014 was overlaid with fake voice cloning to make it look like Khan endorsed a political party. The social media posts carrying the edited video of Khan were shared with false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 16 a video featuring actor Aamir Khan, in which mentions about Rs 15 lakh in every Indian's bank account while cautioning people against 'jumlas' (catchphrases). Towards the end, the video features the Congress' party symbol with the text: 'Vote For Nyay, Vote For Congress'. The caption of the post read, "भारत के हर नागरिक लखपति है। क्योंकि सबके पास काम से कम 15 लाख तो होने ही चाहिए! क्या कहा आप ,, आपके अकाउंट में 15 लाख नहीं है। तो आपके 15 लाख गए कहां ??? तो ऐसे जुमलेबाजोंसे रहे सावधान। नहीं तो होगा तुम्हारा बड़ा नुकसान। #देशहित_में_जारी।" An English translation of the post read, "Every citizen of India is a millionaire. Because everyone must have at least Rs 15 lakh from work! What did you say, there is not 15 lakhs in your account? So where did your 15 lakhs go??? So beware of such catchphrases. Otherwise it will be a big loss for you. #देशहित_में_जारी #फ़िल्मफ़ेयर_अमीर_खान" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the viral video and noticed a lip-sync issue in it. We then ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an X post carrying the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link of the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Two such Facebook claims can be found here and here , the archive links for the posts can be viewed here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video from a channel Satyamev Jayate, shared on August 30, 2016. The title of the video read, "Sataymev Jayate Ep 4 Promo - Each Indian is entitled to one crore!." Here is the link of the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that Khan's outfit and the background in this video was the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos: The Desk listened to this 35-second video and noticed that the actor's statement differed from what it was in the viral video. He can be heard saying that all Indians are entitled to Rs 1 crore and does not make any political endorsements in the video. "Friends, if you think that India is a poor country then you are absolutely wrong, because every citizen here is a millionaire. Everyone should have at least one crore rupees…what did you say? You don't have this amount?…So where did your Rs 1 crore go? Know this Sunday at 11 am," read a rough English translation of what Khan said in the promo video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the official website of Satyamev Jayate and found that the above-mentioned video was the promo for Episode 4 of Season 2, titled 'Kings Every Day'. Below is a screenshot of the same: The IMDb website mentions that this episode was telecast on May 26, 2014. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also came across an X post by the official handle of Satyamev Jayate, which carried the YouTube link of the promo video, shared on March 23, 2014. Here is the link to the X post , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found a PTI report carried by The Telegraph Online on April 16, whose headline read: "Video of Aamir Khan warning against rhetoric is fake, he never endorsed any political party: Actor's spokesperson". Here is the link to the report . "Aamir Khan has never endorsed any political party in his 35-year career and the viral video of the Bollywood superstar is "fake" and alarming, his spokesperson said on Tuesday. According to Khan's spokesperson, the actor has reported the matter to authorities and filed an FIR with the Cyber Crime Cell of the Mumbai Police," read a portion of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake audio was superimposed on an old video using AI, to make it look like the actor endorsed a political party.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, AAP leader Atishi didn't apologise for chanting 'Jai Shri Ram' at Delhi school inaugural event; clipped video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi April 17, (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : A user shared a video of Delhi Education Minister and AAP leader Atishi's speech during a school inauguration event. The user further claimed that she chanted 'Jai Shri Ram' during her speech but later apologised after observing the crowd's reaction. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video from Atishi's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. On March 10, Atishi inaugurated a newly constructed Sarvodaya Girls Children School in Shriram Colony in Khajuri Khas area of Delhi. Claim On April 13, a Facebook user shared a video of AAP leader Atishi's speech during a school inauguration event. The user claimed that she chanted 'Jai Shri Ram' during her speech but later apologised after observing the crowd's reaction. The caption of the post read, "दिल्ला का शिक्षा मंत्रा आतिशा मारलना अपन क्षेत्र श्रा राम कॉलोनी के नये बने स्कूल में आई थी और वहां उसने जय श्री राम बोल दिया। उसे लगा होगा कि वो जगह श्रीराम कालोनी है तो यहाँ हिन्दू ज्यादा रहते होंगे, लेकिन यहाँ उसका उल्टा हो गया। तुरंत मुसलमान की भीड़ उठी और हंगामा करने लगी कि आपने जय श्री राम क्यों बोला ? फिर आतिशी मारलेना ने तुरंत माफी मांग ली कि मैं अब जय श्री राम नहीं बोलूंगी।" An English translation of the caption read: "Delhi's Education Minister Atisha Marlena had come to the newly built school in her area, Shri Ram Colony, and there she chanted Jai Shri Ram. She might have thought that if that place were Shri Ram Colony, more Hindus would live there, but it was the opposite here. Immediately, the crowd of Muslims got up and started creating a ruckus, asking why did you say Jai Shri Ram? Then Atishi Marlena immediately apologised that she would no longer say Jai Shri Ram." Here is the link and archive link , and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk uploaded the video to the InVid Tool so that the keyframes could be looked for. Further, scanning those keyframes through Google Lens, we found a Facebook post shared on April 12, which carried the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link , and below is the screenshot of the same: Two X (formerly Twitter) users also shared the same video. The posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a video shared by the official channel of the Directorate of Education, GNCT of Delhi, shared on March 9. The video description read: "Directorate of Education, GNCT of Delhi is going to organise a ceremony on the occasion of 'Inauguration of New School Building'. The Hon'ble Chief Minister of Delhi has kindly agreed to be the Chief Guest for the inauguration of the New School Building, and the Hon'ble Education Minister of Delhi will grace the occasion as Guest of Honour." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that Atishi's outfit and the background in this video were the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: While watching the entire 49:25-minute video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 41 minutes 40 seconds. The Desk observed that the AAP leader started her speech at the timestamp of 31 minutes 15 seconds. Then, during her speech, she addressed the members on the dais, and while addressing the crowd at the timestamp of 40 minutes 40 second, the AAP leader mistakenly said Khajuri Khas school. Reacting to Atishi's inadvertent mistake, the crowd raised objections when Municipal Councillor Mohammad Amil Malik approached to correct her, which can be seen at the timestamp of 41 minutes 20 seconds. While remedying her statement, the AAP leader apologised and said: "I would like to apologise to the residents of Shriram Colony; the school of Shriram Colony is where the children of Shriram Colony, Khajuri Khas, Karawal Nagar, and Sonia Vihar also study." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google. It came across a press release issued by the Aam Aadmi Party on March 9, 2024, indicating the inauguration of two magnificent in Shriram Colony, North East Delhi. The press release title read, "NEWLY BUILT SCHOOLS IN SHRIRAM COLONY HAVE WORLD-CLASS FACILITIES AND ARE BETTER THAN PRIVATE SCHOOLS—EDUCATION MINISTER ATISHI." Here is the link to the release, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Atishi's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This photo of Jashodaben challenging 'Modi ki Guarantee' is digitally altered; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 17 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have been recently sharing a photo of Jashodaben, holding a placard with the text 'he gave the first guarantee to me, rest you are wise enough.' In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo of Jashodaben was digitally altered and shared as recent on social media with false claim. 'Modi Ki Guarantee' is a term coined by PM Modi and is also the title of the BJP's manifesto for the upcoming Lok Sabha polls. The term has been repeatedly used by PM Modi and other BJP leaders during the campaigning to assure several benefits to the people, if the BJP-led NDA retains power. Claim A Facebook user on April 16 shared a photo of Jashodaben holding a placard with text 'सबसे पहली "गारंटी" उसने… मुझे दी थी! बाकी आप समझदार हो!' An English translation of the text on the placard read: "he gave the first guarantee to me, rest you are wise enough." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and came across multiple Instagram posts, with the same photo and a similar claim. The posts can be viewed( here , here and here ) and the archive links can be viewed ( here , here and here ) respectively. The Desk further conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Hindustan Times, published on February 11, 2016. The PTI report carried by Hindustan Times, which featured the a similar photo as the viral image, was titled, "PM Modi's wife files RTI, seeks details of his passport". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi's wife Jashodaben on Thursday filed an RTI application with Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Ahmedabad seeking details about the marriage- related documents Modi had submitted to get his passport when he was chief minister of Gujarat," read a portion of the report. The caption of the photo read: "Jashodaben was denied a passport last year in November because she failed to produce her marriage certificate. (AFP File Photo)." Below is a combination image, comparing the two photos: We also came across a report published by The Firstpost, published on November 26, 2014, which carried the same photo as the above-mentioned news report. The title of the report read, "Inconveniently yours: Why PM Modi can't ignore Jashodaben anymore". According to the report, Jashodaben raised concerns about her safety and asked for details regarding her security arrangements. She filed a Right to Information (RTI) application to the state government in Gujarat. Here is a link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a video uploaded by the official channel of NDTV, dated for November 25, 2014. The description of the video read, "In a small home in her village, Jashoda Chiman Modi is prepping for her daily visit to the local temple. When she heads out, she will be escorted by two security guards in civilian clothes carrying pistols. The 63-year-old retired school teacher filed an application yesterday seeking details of what sort of security she is entitled to as the wife of Prime Minister Narendra Modi." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old photo of Jashodaben was digitally altered and shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi didn't resign from Congress; video edited with AI-generated audio shared on social media
content: New Delhi, April 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a video of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reading out a statement off a sheet of paper in an office and announcing his resignation from the party in Hindi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of Gandhi filing his nomination for the forthcoming Lok Sabha polls was digitally altered with AI voice clone to make it look like he resigned from the Congress. The edited video was shared on social media with a false claim. The video was of Gandhi filing his nomination for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections from Wayanad, Kerala. Claim A Facebook user shared a video which showed Congress leader Rahul Gandhi reading out a statement in an office. Gandhi can be heard announcing his resignation from the Congress party. Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had also shared the video, while questioning whether it was genuine or edited. Two such Facebook posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be seen here and here , respectively: An X user also shared the same video, claiming that Rahul Gandhi had resigned from the Congress. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then watched the video closely, and heard Rahul Gandhi saying in Hindi: "I, Rahul Gandhi, am resigning from the Congress party. I can no longer pretend to be a Hindu for the sake of elections. After the 'Anyay Yatra', I released the 'Nyay Patra' as well, but Modi ji is sending all corrupts to jail. Under Modi's leadership, will send us corrupt people to jail, too, so I am going to my maternal grandfather's house in Italy." The Desk the continued to further scan the search results and came across an X post by AICC Secretary PV Mohan, which carried a photo, similar to the visuals shared in the viral social media posts. Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption of the post read: "Wayanad witnessed the historic gathering to see @RahulGandhi Ji who is fighting for the soul of India, file his nomination again from Waynad for the Loksabha election. I was dumbfounded by catching sight of the enthusiasm, endearment and encouragement of the crowd for Rahulji." Below is a combination image, comparing the photo with the visuals in the viral video: Taking a cue from the information shared in the X post by the Congress leader, the Desk conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and came across an X post, shared by Rahul Gandhi, in which he can be heard speaking in English while filing his nomination in Wayanad on April 3. Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the video, Rahul Gandhi can be heard saying: "I, Rahul Gandhi, having been nominated as a candidate to fill a seat in the House of the People, do solemnly affirm that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established and that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India." The official YouTube channel of Congress had also shared the same video on April 3. The title of the video read: "The video was titled 'Rahul Gandhi files nomination from Wayanad' ('राहुल गांधी से वायनाड से भरा नामांकन')." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded a video of Rahul Gandhi was digitally altered and was overlaid with an AI voice clone to make it sound like he announced his resignation from the party.

title: PTI Fact Check: Another video of Aamir Khan, with superimposed AI-generated voice, shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 18 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video of Bollywood actor Aamir Khan purportedly talking about two types of 'guarantees' given to the citizens – 'good and bad' – to claim that he endorsed Congress party's campaign for the forthcoming Lok Sabha elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the audio of a 10-year-old video of the actor was overlaid with a fake AI-generated audio to give an impression that Khan endorsed a political party. The digitally altered video was shared on social media with false claims. During the run-up to the Lok Sabha polls, the BJP and Congress have focused their respective campaigns around their manifestos - 'Modi Ki Guarantee' and 'Nyay Patra' – respectively. The social media posts carrying Khan's edited video are indicated towards the guarantees given by these two parties to the citizens. The Desk recently debunked a similar digitally altered video of Aamir Khan, which was shared on social media with the similar claim of endorsing a political party. The fact-check titled 'PTI Fact Check: No, Aamir Khan didn't endorse any political party; edited video with AI voice clone shared on social media' can be read here . Claim An Instagram user shared on April 15 a video of actor Aamir Khan talking about two types of guarantees given to the citizens for the upcoming Lok Sabha elections. The caption of the post read, "Aamir khan ne 2024 Election Ko le kar kya kaha, Ki Abki baar Congress ko vote do #news #aamirkhan #election #bollywood" Here is a link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Khan, in the video, can be heard saying, "There are two types of guarantees in these elections - good and bad. The bad news is that once again, 'jumle waade' (catchphrase promises) have been made to ruin your life. But the good news is that this time, there are '5 Nyay' (five justices) for your development." Moving forward, the video featured Congress party's logo with the text 'Vote for Nyay, Vote for Congress'. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the viral video and noticed a lip-sync issue in it. We then uploaded the viral video to the InVid Tool Search and received a few keyframes. Further, scanning those keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a Twitter post shared on April 15, which carried the same video. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the Google Lens search results, the Desk found that a similar video was uploaded on YouTube from the official channel of 'Satyamev Jayate', a chat show hosted by Aamir Khan, which was telecasted on Star Plus channel. Here is the link to the video titled, "Satyamev Jayate S1 | Episode 13 | The Idea of India | Liberty (Hindi)", which was published on August 30, 2016, and below is a screenshot of the same: The description of the video read: "Stay tuned to the new season of Satyamev Jayate, starting March 2, every Sunday, 11 AM onwards only on STAR Plus." The Desk noticed that Khan's outfit and the red glowing light at the bottom of the video was the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos: The Desk listened to this 40-second video and noticed that the actor's statement differed from what it was in the viral video. He can be heard saying that that he will be coming again for a new season with five episodes, which will be telecasted on Sundays. An English translation of what Khan said in the promo video, reads: "Friends I have two news for you, one is good and other is bad. The bad news is that I am coming back again to spoil your Sunday. But the good news is that I will only spoil your 5 Sundays….. only 5 Every Sunday of March". Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the official website of Satyamev Jayate and found that the above-mentioned video was the promo for Season 2, Episode 1, titled 'Fighting Rape'. Here is the link to the official website and below is a screenshot of the same The IMDb website , however, mentions that the first episode of Season 2 was telecast on March 5, 2014. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake AI-generated audio was superimposed on an old video, to make it look like the actor endorsed a political party.

title: PTI Fact Check: This photo of Smriti Irani holding a fish was not clicked during Navratri; pic shared on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, April 18 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a collage including two photos of Union Minister and BJP leader Smriti Irani – one of her holding a fish and the other in which she holds portrait of Goddess Durga. The claim accompanying the collage suggested that the picture of Irani holding fish was taken recently, during the holy festival of Chaitra Navratri. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo in question was from April 6 - before the nine-day festival of Navratri started. The photo was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Smriti, while campaigning BJP's North Chennai candidate RC Paul Kanagaraj on April 6, received the large fish as a gift from a local fisherman. Claim A Congress leader shared on April 15 a collage of two photos of Smriti Irani – one of her holding a large fish and the other in which she holds portrait of Goddess Durga. The user claimed the The caption to the post read, "नवरात्रि के पावन पर्व में एक हांथ में मछली एक हांथ में दुर्गा जी की फोटो!भाजपाई मित्रों क्या कहेंगें ?" An English translation to the post read, "On the holy festival of Navratri, a fish in one hand and a photo of Goddess Durga in the other! What will BJP friends say?" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens, and came across multiple posts with the same photo of Irani holding a fish, shared by several users. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) for the posts. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by The Times of India, published on April 7, 2024, which carried a similar photo. "INDIA hugging in Delhi, begging in Kerala, thugging in Tamil Nadu,' read the headline of the report. Here is the link and screenshot of the report: Below is a combination image, comparing the viral photo with the one carried in the news report: We also came across a photo gallery by a website named Social News XYZ, published on April 6, which carried a similar photo as the viral one. The title of the report read: "Chennai: Union Minister and BJP leader Smriti Irani greets supporters during an election campaign rally in support of the party's candidate from Chennai North constituency R. C. Paul Kanagaraj #Gallery". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption of the photo read: "Chennai: Union Minister and BJP leader Smriti Irani greets supporters during an election campaign rally in support of the party's candidate from Chennai North constituency R. C. Paul Kanagaraj ahead of Lok Sabha elections, in Chennai, Saturday, April 6, 2024.(IANS/R Parthibhan)." The Desk also scanned the official X handle of Smriti Irani and found pictures from the event shared by her. Here is the link and archive link of the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We then searched about Chaitra Navratri and found that the nine-day festival started on April 9 and concluded on April 17. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo was from before the start of Navratri, that was shared on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake Alert! No, actor Ranveer Singh did not oppose PM Modi; edited video with AI voice clone shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 19 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : A Facebook user shared a video of actor Ranveer Singh in which he can be purportedly heard saying Prime Minister Modi's purpose is to celebrate the sorrows of our lives. The actor was also heard criticising the prime minister for the country's 'surging inflation rate' and 'unemployment'. Because of its audio, the video gave the impression that the Bollywood actor tried to oppose the PM and endorse a particular political party during the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the actor's video was from April 16, when he visited the Kashi Vishwanath Temple in Varanasi. His video was overlaid with AI-generated voice cloning to make it look like Singh opposed PM Modi and endorsed a political party. The claim shared in the social media post was false. 'AI voice clone" refers to the creation of a digital replica of a person's voice using artificial intelligence technology. Claim A Facebook user shared a video of actor Ranveer Singh criticising PM Modi for the country's surging inflation rate and unemployment. Towards the end, the video features the Congress party symbol with the text: 'Vote For Nyay, Vote For Congress'. The caption of the post with 320k views read,"Vote for न्याय ,Vote for Congress" An English translation of the caption read, "Vote for Justice, Vote for Congress" Here is the link and archive link , and below is a screenshot of the same; Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the viral video and noticed a lip-sync issue. The Desk uploaded the video to the InVid Tool, so the keyframes could be looked for. Further, scanning those keyframes through Google Lens, we found multiple posts with the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and the archive links can be viewed here and here , respectively. Upon further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram reel shared on April 17 by a Jist page named Jist.News. The post's caption read, "Actor Ranveer Singh praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his work on improving public infrastructure and developing Varanasi, the country's oldest pilgrimage site. On Sunday, Ranveer and Bollywood actress Kriti Sanon were in Varanasi, where they walked the ramp as showstoppers for fashion designer Manish Malhotra's show." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk noticed that Singh's outfit and the background in this video were the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: The Desk listened to this video and noticed that the actor's statement differed from what it was in the viral video. He can be heard sharing his experience at the temple and also mentioned that PM Modi wanted to celebrate the rich culture and heritage. "Modi ji's vision was to celebrate our rich cultural heritage, history, and legacy. India is progressing toward modernity quickly, but we must never forget our roots and cultural heritage. That's why development with heritage is crucial; this is a blend of the past and the future." Read a rough English translation of what Khan said in the promo video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and found a report by Hindustan Times published on April 16. The report's title read, "Ranveer Singh, Kriti Sanon offer prayers in Varanasi; walk the ramp for Manish Malhotra. Watch" Here is a link , and below is a screenshot of the same Subsequently, the Desk concluded that fake audio was superimposed on an old video using AI to make it look like the actor endorsed a political party.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Asaduddin Owaisi's 2021 speech shared on social media with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi April 18, (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi delivering a speech is being widely shared on social media in a way to make it look like a communal speech. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped portion of an old video of Owaisi was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 13 a video of AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi delivering a speech, which seems like a communal speech. The caption of the post read, "Listen tell the end #jaishreeram #bjp #ramnavmispecial #ramnavami2024 #hanumanjanmotsav#hanumanji #reelitfeelit #tredingnow." Here in the link and archive link to the post with more than 1.2 lakh likes, and below is a screenshot of the same: An English translation of what Owaisi said in the video clip reads: "Yogi will not always be the Chief Minister. Modi will not always be the Prime Minister. Us, Muslims, are silent because of the time. We will not forget your injustices. Allah with destroy you with his power. Things will change with time. Who will save you?" Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such X posts can be viewed here and here , and the archive links can be found here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search and came across a Facebook Live on the official page of AIMIM, shared on December 12, 2021. The description of the video with 147k views read, "बैरिस्टर असदुद्दीन ओवैसी ने कानपूर में शोषित वंचित समाज सम्मलेन को संबोधित किया" An English translation to the post read, "Barrister Asaduddin Owaisi addressed the Shoshit Vanchit Samaj Sammelan in Kanpur." Here is a link to the Live and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the 44:58-minute video, the Desk found that the viral clip was taken from the timestamp of 40 minutes 18 seconds. At 39:14 seconds, Owaisi says (an English translation to his speech): "At Rasulabad Police Station in Kanpur, 80-year-old Mohammad Rafiq urinated upon and his beard pulled. This was done by SI Ganjendra Pal Singh." At 40:12 timestamp, Owaisi asks, "what problem do you have with our beard?" At 40:18 timestamp, he further says: "I want to tell this to those policemen…", which is followed by the clip being shared on social media. Thus, we understood that the part of the video, where he addresses the policemen involved in the alleged incident, was cropped out. In further investigation the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and came across a video report by India Today uploaded on December 24, 2021. The video carried in the report included the part where he can be clearly heard addressing the policemen. Also, the title of the video report read: "Asaduddin Owaisi's Shocking Rant To UP Cops At Kanpur Rally | Owaisi 'Hate' Speech" The description of the report read, "All India Majlis-E-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) chief Asaduddin Owaisi has stoked a controversy by openly threatening the Uttar Police. Addressing an election rally in poll-bound UP, Owaisi said, "I want to remind police officers that they need to know this fact that Yogi and PM Modi will not always be there...We Muslims are definitely compelled according to the times, but remember we are not going to forget your atrocities. We will remember your atrocities. Allah will destroy you with his power." "Things will change, then who will come to save you? Yogi will go to his Mutt and Modi to the mountains. Then who will come to save you," said Owaisi." Here is the link to the video news report and below is a screenshot of the same: A video report by Navbharat Times even compared the cropped video with the extended version to highlight the cropped-out part of the video. Here is the link to the video report , and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across an X post by Owaisi shared on December 24, 2021, in which he posted an extended version of the viral video, to clarify that he did not incite violence, but talked about police atrocities. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Owaisi was cropped and shared on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Anupam Kher and Akshay Kumar shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 19 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a collage of four photos featuring actor Anupam Kher. The fourth photo of him with actor Akshay Kumar carried the text claiming that the latter was his son. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the text on the photo made a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 12 a collage of four photos of actor Anupam Kher. The first two featured Kher, third of him with wife Kirron Kher, and the fourth one with Akshay Kumar with the text 'son'. The caption of the post with over 186k views read, "80 और 90 के दशक पर बॉलीवुड पर राज करने वाले एक्टर अनुपम खेर को कौन नहीं जानता उन्होंने अपने एक्टिंग से लाखों करोड़ों बना लिए हैं आज हम आपको अनुपम खेर के कुछ पुरानी तस्वीर दिखाएंगे। अक्षय कुमार को अनुपम खेर अपना बेटे के समान मानते हैं " An English translation of the caption read, "Who does not know actor Anupam Kher, who ruled Bollywood in the 80s and 90s? He has made lakhs of crores from his acting. Today we will show you some old pictures of Anupam Kher. Anupam Kher considers Akshay Kumar like his son." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and came across multiple Facebook posts, carrying the same photo and similar claim. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and archive links can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk further conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Hindustan Times, published on October 31, 2023. The title of the report read, "Anupam Kher pens birthday post for son Sikandar Kher, mentions Kirron Kher's wish: May you shave every alternate day" Here is a link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned Kher's official Instagram account and found the same picture shared by him. "Happy Birthday dearest Sikandar! You have grown to be a wonderful man! Confident, vulnerable, most of the time responsible, funnier of course and loving when you want! And a FANTASTIC actor! 😁😍 ! My wish for you - May God give you all the happiness in the world! May you have a long , healthy and peaceful life! May you shave every alternate day if not everyday and so on! Your mother's wish apart from all this - GET MARRIED! 😬! Love and prayers always! ❤️🙌🕉 @sikandarkher" read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk the conducted another advanced Google search, while looking for information on Akshay Kumar's family. The IMDb website mentioned: "Rajiv Hari "Akshay Kumar" Om Bhatia was born on September 09, 1967, in Amritsar, Punjab to Aruna Bhatia and Hari Om Bhatia". Here is the link to the IMDb page and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Kher's photo with actor Akshay Kumar claiming to be his son was shared with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Uma Bharti criticising PM Modi, when she was not in BJP, resurfaces on social media
content: New Delhi, April 20 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of senior BJP leader Uma Bharti is being widely shared on social media, in which she can be heard criticising PM Modi over the situation of Gujarat. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dates back to the time when Bharti was not part of the BJP and Narendra Modi was the CM of Gujarat. The video was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 16 a video of Uma Bharti in which she is heard criticising PM Modi over the situation of Gujarat. The caption of the post reads as 'vinash purush', as referred to by Uma Bharti for PM Modi in the video. Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned social media platforms and found that an Instagram user had shared a similar video on January 2. "Modi hai Vinash Kaari Purush; Uma Bharti!" read the caption of the post, with over 49k likes. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across an X post by senior lawyer Prashant Bhushan who shared the same video on January 17, 2024. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video – an extended version of the viral video – uploaded on July 27, 2011. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: ABP News' YouTube page also shared the same video on April 17, 2014, whose title read: "Uma Bharti calls Modi 'Vinaash Purush', Congress releases video". According to the description of the video, "Congress released a video clip in which senior BJP leader Uma Bharti was seen launching blistering attack at PM candidate of her party Narendra Modi." Here is the link to the video and screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, a Times of India report – published on April 17, 2014 – stated that the video clip released by the Congress was "reportedly shot shortly after Uma had quit the BJP to float her own political outfit by the name of Bharatiya Janshakti Party in 2006". "She rejoined the BJP in 2011," it added. Here is the link to the report , and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted an customised Google search with specific keywords and came across a report by NDTV, published on April 17, 2014. The headline of the report read: "Uma Bharti files complaint over CD release of her old Narendra Modi attack". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "BJP leader Uma Bharti has complained to the Election Commission after the Congress today released a three-year-old video clip in which she is heard describing Narendra Modi as a "vinash purush" or man of destruction," read a section of the report. "The Congress admits that the video is old, but says it demonstrates that there are "thousands" within the BJP who see their prime ministerial candidate as a dictator who makes false claims," read another part. The report also quoted Bharti stating that she made the remarks against Narendra Modi – the then BJP's prime ministerial candidate – when she was expelled from the party. "Even America has changed its mind about Modi," she quipped. Bharti had been expelled from BJP in 2005 after a public spat with veteran LK Advani, and had rejoined the saffron party in 2011. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Uma Bharti, when she was not part of the BJP, was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This opinion poll on Lok Sabha elections shared in the name of Axis My India is fake
content: New Delhi, April 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Some photos are being widely shared on social media lately, with the claim that they show results of an opinion poll survey conducted by Axis My India ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The alleged survey predicts a close contest between the BJP-led NDA and the opposition's INDIA bloc, with none of them touching the majority mark. The survey is in contrast to the other pre-poll surveys, which have predicted another landslide victory for the NDA this time. In its investigation, the Desk found that fake images were shared on social media in the name of Axis My India's pre-poll survey. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 19 a photo of a purported opinion poll survey in the name of polling agency Axis My India. The alleged survey on the 2024 Lok Sabha polls predicted a close contest between NDA and INDIA bloc, with none of touching the majority mark. The caption of the post read: "Big upset for BJP incoming! Axis My India predicts even share of seats for NDA and INDIA blocs. No saffron wave in Lok Sabha elections 2024!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first scanned social media platforms and found that multiple users had shared the photos of the purported survey, to claim that the BJP-led NDA will suffer a major setback and fall short of the majority mark in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. One such Facebook post can be seen here and its archived version can be seen here . Below is a screenshot of the post: The same photos were also widely shared on X (formerly Twitter). Two such X posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk tried looking for news reports on the alleged survey, but couldn't find any. We then scanned the official website of Axis My India, but could not find anything related to any opinion poll on the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The last surveys mentioned on the website were those of the Assembly polls in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Telangana and Chhattisgarh. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the X handle of Axis My India and found a post, where they shared a press release issued by the agency. "Reiterating the press release shared earlier," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post , and below is a screenshot of the same: "With regards to the upcoming 2024 Indian General Elections, certain opinion polls are being published using the name of Mr. Pradeep Gupta, Axis My India, since the past few days, which are completely false (misleading)," read the press release. "This is to inform you all that Axis My India never publishes any kind of pre-poll/opinion poll. We will publish exit polls only after the elections as per ECI guidelines, on June 1 at 6:30 pm," it added. Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the X handle of Pradeep Gupta, and the found the same press release that was issued on April 3. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake opinion poll on 2024 Lok Sabha elections went viral in the name of Axis My India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Akhilesh Yadav hitting out at Congress shared as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, April 21 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video of Samajwadi chief Akhilesh Yadav in which he can be heard, urging the public not to vote for Congress, while calling it as a 'chalu' (manipulative) party. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video of Yadav was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim. Yadav's Samajwadi Party is part of the INDIA bloc, an alliance of opposition parties led by the Congress, contesting against the NDA alliance in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 11 a video of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav in which he can be heard urging the public not to vote for Congress, calling it a manipulative party. The caption of the post read, "हे प्रभु ये क्या हो गया #bjp #inc #reels #reelsinstagram #trendingreels #boy #friends #picoftheday #funny #comedy" An English translation of the post read, "Oh Lord what has happened #bjp #inc #reels #reelsinstagram #trendingreels #boy #friends #picoftheday #funny #comedy" An English translation of the text on the video read: "Don't vote for Congress, it is a manipulative party". Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search, and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found multiple posts with the same video and similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. Two such X posts can be viewed here and here and archive links can be viewed here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Economic times on November 5, 2023. The description of the video – same as the one shared on social media – read, "Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday continued his spate of attacks on the Congress amid tension between the INDIA bloc partners over seat distribution in Madhya Pradesh, as he called the latter a "chalu" (cheat) party." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and found a report by The Times of India published on Nov 6, 2023. The title of the report read, "Congress 'chalu' party, don't vote for them: Akhilesh Yadav in Madhya Pradesh." According to the report, Samajwadi chief Akhilesh Yadav while addressing a rally in Madhya Pradesh called Congress a 'chalu' (cunning) party and accused it of betrayal as Congress denied seats to Yadav's party in Madhya Pradesh, saying the INDIA bloc was meant for national politics, not regional elections. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of Samajwadi chief was shared as recent on social media with false claims

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show panicked Israelis after missile attack by Iran; unrelated video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 21 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video with the claim that it showed Israelis panicking and fleeing to safety, following attack by Iran. In its investigation, the Desk found that an unrelated video was shared on social media with false claims. Iran launched hundreds of drones, ballistic missiles and cruise missiles that sought to overwhelm Israel's air defences in the April 13 attack — the first on Israel by a foreign power since Iraqi dictator Saddam Hussein launched Scud missiles at Israel in the 1991 Gulf War. However, Israeli air defences and fighter jets, backed by the US, the United Kingdom and neighbouring Jordan, shot down the vast majority of the incoming fire. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 14 a video, claiming that it showed Israelis panicking and running to safety following an attack by Iran. "The population of Israel is fleeing to bomb shelters. Explosions in the sky and on the ground can be heard throughout the country, media reports. Iran fired more than 200 missiles at Israel," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such Facebook posts can be viewed here and here , and the archive links can be found here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search and came across an X post by Shayan Sardarizadeh, a journalist with BBC, shared on April 14. The caption of the post with 1.3M read, "This video, posted by Jackson Hinkle and others and viewed nearly 5 million times, claims to show "Israelis panicking" as Iran's missiles and drones reach Israel. In fact, it shows Louis Tomlinson fans near Four Seasons Hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina last week; verified by @LGalrao." Here is the link and archive link of the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and found a report by Infobae, an Argentinian news outlet, published on 06 April 2024. The title of the report read, "Louis Tomlinson llegó a Argentina para empezar a palpitar su show en el mes de mayo" An English translation to the title read, "Louis Tomlinson arrived in Argentina to start performing his show in the month of May" According to the report, Louis Tomlinson was in Argentina to perform at The José Amalfitani Stadium. He stayed at the Four Seasons hotel during his tour and interacted with fans in the vicinity of the hotel. Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same Taking a cue from this, the Desk located Four Seasons Hotel Buenos Aires on Google Maps. Using the Street View, the Desk noticed the buildings and zebra crossing were the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: On further investigating, the Desk came across another X post shared by the official handle of Louis' team on April 8. The caption of the post read, "Meeting fans in Buenos Aires, Argentina. Louis will be back next month performing at Velez Sarsfield on his #FITFLatinAmerica tour. http://louist.lnk.to/FITFWT" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from Buenos Aires, Argentina, and not Israel.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Dhoni is not promoting any political party in this photo; 2020 pic shared as recent with false claims
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of former Indian skipper Mahendra Singh Dhoni showing an open palm and index finger. The users suggested that the cricketer was endorsing the electoral campaign of Congress with that gesture, since the party's symbol is a hand. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated photo dating back to 2020 was shared on social media with false claims. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 20 a photo of cricketer Mahendra Singh Dhoni showing his hand and index finger of the other hand and claimed the cricketer was supporting a particular political party for the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. The caption of the post with over 2,000 likes read: "आप किसी भी पार्टी को वोट दें लेकिन पार्टी का चुनाव चिन्ह दिखाना ज़रूरी है 💯" An English translation of the post read: "You can vote for any party but it is important to show the party's election symbol💯." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and came across multiple Instagram posts, carrying the same photo and similar claim. Two such Instagram posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive links can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk further conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another Instagram post shared by the official handle of Chennai Super Kings dated for October 5. The caption of the post read, "Nandri filled Thala Dharisanam as our Twitter fam becomes 6 Million Strong! #SixerOnTwitter #WhistlePodu #Yellove 🦁💛" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same Taking a cue from this, the Desk further conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by NDTV Sports, published on October 31, 2023. The title of the post read, "IPL 2020: MS Dhoni, Chennai Super Kings Celebrate Six Million Twitter Followers" Here is a link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same; Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated photo of Dhoni was shared as recent on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Allu Arjun didn't endorse any political party; 2022 video shared as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a video of South Indian actor Allu Arjun waving at people, and used a caption to insinuate that he was endorsing the Congress party amid the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video dating back to 2022 was shared as recent on social media with false claims. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 21 a video of South Indian actor Allu Arjun waving at people and claimed that the actor was campaigning for a political party. The caption of the post, with over 4500 likes, read: "Vote For Congress..." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool, and found a few keyframes. We then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found multiple social media users sharing the same video. Two such Instagram posts can be found here and here , and the archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The same video was also shared by several X users as well. Two such X posts can be viewed here and here , and their archives versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named Indian Journo on August 22, 2022. The description of the video read: "Allu Arjun is one of India's most famous actors. His film Pushpa: The Rise - Part 1 was a box officer superhit, and earned ₹300 crore worldwide. The Telugu actor was recently in New York, where he represented India at the India Day parade, one of the most well-known annual events organised by the Indian diaspora in the US. On Sunday, Allu shared videos from the event in New York, which celebrated the 75 years of India's independence." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk noticed that Arjun's outfit and the background in this video were the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and found a report by Hindustan Times published on August 22, 2022. The title of the report read, "Allu Arjun makes grand entry at India Day parade in New York: 'It was an honour'" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Allu Arjun was invited to represent the country as grand marshal at the annual India Day parade in New York. He was joined by his wife Sneha Reddy at the parade. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of Allu Arjun was shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show crowd at PM Modi's Rajasthan rally; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 23 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video of massive crowd, which they claimed had gathered for PM Modi's election rally in Rajasthan's Jalore. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. PM Modi addressed public rallies in Jalore and Banswara on April 21. Polling in both the Lok Sabha constituencies will be held in the second phase on April 26. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 22 a video of massive crowd, suggesting that it gathered for PM Modi's rallies in Jalore and Banswara. "Today there is rally of modi ji in Rajasthan's Jalore at 2 PM and Banswara at 4 PM. This is visual before rally. These visuals may give shivers to Congress. 10 lac people may attend this rally. Ashok Gehlot's son is Congress candidate from Jalore," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across another Facebook post, carrying the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, we found that the same video was shared by several users as well. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk then went through the comment sections of the X posts, and found several users claiming that it was a 2019 video. One such comment can be seen here and its archived versions can be seen here . Below is its screenshot: Another user claimed that the video dated back to 2019 and was of a Congress rally in Ramseen, Jalore. Here is the link and archive link to the comment and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across a Facebook post, which shared the same video on April 25, 2019. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption of the video read: "ये विडियो कही ओर का नही हमारे राजस्थान में जालोर जिले के रामसीन में Rahul Gandhi व Ashok Gehlot व Sachin Pilot की जालोर के लोकसभा कांग्रेस प्रत्याक्षी की जनसभा में उमड़ा जनसैलाब है..।।" An English translation of the caption read: "This video is not from anywhere else, in Rajasthan, there is a huge crowd in the public meeting of Lok Sabha Congress candidate of Rahul Gandhi, Ashok Gehlot and Sachin Pilot in Ramseen of Jalore district." Below is a combination image, comparing the viral video to the one found on Facebook from 2019. The Desk then took a cue from one of the comments highlighted above, in which a user shared a photo from the rally to claim that it was from 2019, we conducted another customised Google search and found a YouTube video, which was the same as the viral video. "रामसीन ( जालोर) कोग्रेस मिटिंग (date 25/04/2019)," read the title of the YouTube video, uploaded on April 26, 2019. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: We then conducted another Google search with specific keywords and found that Rahul Gandhi indeed held a rally in Jalore on April 25, 2019. Here is the link to a Facebook post by The Indian Express on the same. We also found a PTI report carried by Business Standard , on Rahul Gandhi's Jalore rally held on April 25, 2019. However, the Desk could not independently establish or confirm that the video was from that rally. But we were able to conclude that a video – at least five years old – was passed off as recent, falsely claiming that it showed crowd at PM's rally.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of man putting garland of shoes on a BJP leader shared as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, April 22 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of an elderly man putting a garland of shoes on a BJP candidate campaigning on the streets. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found an old video dating back to 2018 was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 12 a video of an elderly man putting a garland of shoes on a BJP leader while he was campaigning on the streets. The caption of the post read, "हिमाचल प्रदेश के बागी विधायकों का भी हाल कुछ ऐसा ही होने वाला है" Meanwhile, an English translation of the text appearing on video read: "BJP workers asking for votes. Rebel MLAs of Himachal Pradesh are going to meet a similar fate". Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and the archive links for the same can be viewed here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report by Amar Ujala, published on January 8, 2018. The description of the report read, "मध्यप्रदेश में नगर परिषद के अध्यक्ष पद के लिए वोट मांगने गए बीजेपी के उम्मीदवार को लोगों ने जूतों की माला पहला दी। लोगों ने जिस तरह से अचानक ये जूतों से माला पहनाई कि जनाब मना भी नहीं कर पाए। देखिए पूरा वीडियो।" An English translation of the report read, "In Madhya Pradesh, people gave garlands of shoes to the BJP candidate who went to seek votes for the post of Municipal Council President. The way people suddenly garlanded the shoes, the gentleman could not even refuse. Watch the full video." Here is a link and below is a screenshot of the same: The feature image of the report was same as the visuals of the viral video. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search on Google and found a report by NDTV, published on 08 January 2018. The title of the report read, "BJP Candidate Greeted With Garland Of Shoes In Madhya Pradesh." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident took place when Dinesh Sharma, the BJP candidate for Dhamnod civic election, was participating in door-to-door campaign to seek votes for his party. The man who made him wear the garland said he wanted to highlight the acute water problem in the region. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of crowd at PM's Kolkata rally shared as recent in the names of Jalpaiguri and Barmer
content: New Delhi, April 24 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a massive crowd gathered at PM Modi's public rally is being widely shared on social media with some users claiming that it was from West Bengal's Jalpaiguri while others claiming it to be from Rajasthan's Barmer. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video of PM's rally in Kolkata was shared on social media as recent with misleading claims. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 7 a video of a massive crowd gathered at PM Modi's public rally and claimed that it was from Jalpaiguri, West Bengal. The caption of the post read, "Modi wave in jalpaiguri #norenromodi #jalpaigurinews #siliguritimes #Modiji #BJP #Vairla" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, carrying the same video with a similar claim. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and archive links can be viewed here and here respectively: Several X (formerly Twitter) posts can be viewed here and here and archive links can be found here and here respectively. The caption of the post read: "PM @narendramodi at Brigade Parade ground Kolkata rally today." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the video shared by Sharma was from the same event, whose visuals were shared on social media. title: PTI Fact Check: Old photo of Congress booth agent falsely linked to first phase of 2024 Lok Sabha polls
content: New Delhi, April 24 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared photo of a man, seemingly a Congress booth worker, sleeping with his head on a table. The users shared the photo suggesting that it was related to the first phase of the ongoing Lok Sabha polls to insinuate a low voter turnout in favour of the Congress party. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo, dating back to at least 2019, was shared on social media with misleading claims. As many as 102 constituencies across 21 states went to polls in the first phase of the Lok Sabha elections on April 19. The photo in question went viral soon after the first phase polling. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 20 a photo of a man, seemingly a Congress booth worker, sleeping with his head on a table, and claimed that it was related to the first phase of polling in the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. The caption of the post read, "प्रथम चरण का "रुझान"आपके पास कोई तस्वीर है तो भेजो?" An English translation of the post read: "Trend" of the first phase. If you have any picture then please send it" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens, and came across multiple social media posts, carrying the same photo and similar claim. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another post, carrying the same photo on a Facebook shared by a page named 'Save Jammu'. The caption of the post, shared on April 11, 2019, read: "Somewhere in Gandhi Nagar segment today" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found an X (twitter) post with the same photo shared by Ashwin Ruparel on April Apr 11, 2019. The caption of the post read: "Congress worker outside poll booth, knowing results, in deep sleep". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In this image, the registration plate of a two-wheeler parked near the table was clearly visible. The number started with KA-20, which is the registration series for Udupi in Karnataka. Meanwhile, it is important to mention here that the polling for Lok Sabha elections in Karnataka will be held in the second and third phase on April 26 and May 7. The Desk could not independently establish when and where the photo was originally taken. However, since we were able to trace its digital footprint back to 2019, it can be concluded that it was falsely shared as recent.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of woman polling agent influencing voters falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha polls; Details inside

The caption of the post read,"ऐसे होगा 400 पार" An English translation of the caption read, "400 will be crossed like this" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such Facebook posts can be viewed here , here and here and the archive links for the same can be viewed here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another X post by Vinod Sharma, Political Editor at Hindustan Times, dated May 15, 2019. title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of man removing VVPAT slips from EVMs falsely shared as recent on social media
content: New Delhi, April 25 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : A Facebook user shared a video of some people purportedly removing Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) slips from an EVM machine and keeping them in a black envelope. The user claimed that the man in the video was stealing the slips from the EVM. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2022, and was shared as recent on social media with false claims. The Desk had debunked the same video last year when it was viral on social media during the runup to the Assembly polls in Karnataka The fact-check titled 'PTI Fact Check: Video of VVPAT slips removal shared on social media with false claim' can be read here . Claim An Instagram user shared on April 23 a video of a man removing Voter Verified Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) slips from an EVM machine and keeping them in a black envelope. The video was shared with the claim that the man was stealing the slips from the EVM machine. The caption of the post read, "EVM से पर्चियों की चोरी 😡😡😡 #viralvideos #reels #trending #instareels" An English translation of the caption read, "Theft of slips from EVM 😡😡😡 #viralvideos #reels #instareels" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively: Two such X posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk tried to understand the procedure followed at the polling booths, regarding the EVMs and VVPAT slips. On conducting a customised keyword search on Google using the keyword "Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961', we came across the official website of the Chief Electoral Officer, Rajasthan, where we found a downloadable PDF file. Here is the link to the file The Desk downloaded the PDF document and scrolled down to Section 94 of the election rules regarding the disposal of election papers.Section 94(b) of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, states that subject to any direction to the contrary given by the Election Commission or by a competent court or tribunal, election-related papers such as used and unused ballot papers, counterfoils of used ballot papers, marked copies of electoral rolls, and registers of voters shall be retained for one year. However, this rule does not explicitly mention VVPAT slips. Below are the relevant screenshots: Nonetheless, the video in the viral post does not show the destruction of VVPAT slips or any other election-related papers. Instead, it shows the removal of VVPAT slips from respective machines (which is part of the process stated by the ECI, as mentioned in the article below). The Desk noticed that Section 94(c) of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961, which addresses all other election papers not mentioned above (including VVPAT slips), states that they can be retained for a period as directed by the Election Commission unless the election petition/court case is Pending. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a Google Search with the keyword "removal of VVPAT slips, ECI", which led to a page on the Election Commission of India's official website. A link to download a copy of the rules about removing VVPAT slips after completing the counting of votes has been provided on the page. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the ECI's rules, the VVPAT paper slips shall be removed from the drop box of VVPAT and kept in a paper envelope made of thick black paper polling station-wise. Also, the VVPAT slips taken out from each machine must be kept in a separate envelope. Below is a screenshot highlighting the ECI's rules: This was the same process followed by the person in the viral video, wherein he removed the VVPAT slips from the machine, preserved them in an envelope of thick black paper, and sealed it later. While further scanning the Desk came across another Facebook post with a similar video shared on December 12, 2022. The caption of the post read, "બીજેપીના ઠેકાદરો બીજેપી કેવી રીતે જીતે છે એ જોઈ લો તમે તમારી આંખોથી આ ભાવનગર જીલ્લા નો છે" An English translation of the caption read, "See with your own eyes how BJP's contractors win. This is from Bhavnagar district." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same Even though the Desk could not trace the viral video to its source, it concluded that its digital footprints can be traced till 2022. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video, related to the process of removing VVPAT slips from the EVM machine and its preservation, was shared on social media as recent with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Kirori Lal Meena's statement shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, April 26 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Rajasthan minister Kirori Lal Meena in which he can be heard saying that if the BJP-led NDA government is able to secure 400 seats in the ongoing Lok Sabha Elections, it will remove reservation and also change the Constitution. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video of the minister's statement was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 25 shared a video of Rajasthan minister Kirori Lal Meena in which he can be heard saying that if the current government is able to secure 400 seats in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, it will remove reservation and also change the Constitution. The caption of the post read: "राजस्थान सरकार के मंत्री किरोड़ीलाल मीणा जी खुद कह रहे है की 400 करेंगे तो मोदी जी आरक्षण ख़त्म कर सविंधान को बदल देंगे" An English translation of the post read: "Rajasthan government minister Kirori Lal Meena ji himself is saying that if 400 are done then Modi ji will end the reservation and change the constitution." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. Further the Desk noticed a person holding a mic with the logo of 'First India News'. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of India First News on April 22. The description of the video read, "आरक्षण को लेकर Kirodi Lal Meena का बड़ा बयान | Loksabha Elections 2024 | Rajasthan Politics | BJP" An English translation of the description read, "Kirodi Lal Meena's big statement regarding reservation. Lok Sabha Elections 2024 | Rajasthan Politics BJP" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk found that it was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the original video with the one shared on social media: "The Congressmen have spread such an illusion that if Modiji crosses 400 seats, he will finish reservation and change the Constitution. This confusion is getting spread across the country. They want to take the votes of innocent people by misleading them. Modiji himself said in Barmer that even if Bhimrao Ambedkar comes on the earth, he cannot change the Constitution. And even Amit Shah has also said that there will be no tampering with reservation. I have come to give this assurance especially to the SC-ST brothers. He is also assured. He has assured that by pressing the lotus button on 26th, he will make Om Birla ji victorious and send him to the Parliament," reads a rough translation of what the minister said in the statement. In further investigation, the Desk scanned the official X handle of Kirori Lal Meena, in which he called out those sharing the clipped video. The caption of the post read, "प्रधानमंत्री श्री @narendramodi जी स्पष्ट कर चुके हैं कि खुद बाबा साहब अंबेडकर भी आ जाएं तो भी आरक्षण खत्म नहीं होगा। कुछ शरारती तत्व सोशल मीडिया पर मेरे अधूरे बयान को इसके उलट दावे के साथ शेयर कर रहे हैं। वे इससे बाज आएं अन्यथा मुझे कानूनी कार्रवाई के लिए बाध्य होना पड़ेगा।" An English translation of the post read," Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji has made it clear that even if Baba Saheb Ambedkar himself comes, reservation will not end. Some mischievous elements are sharing my incomplete statement on social media with the opposite claim. They should stop doing this otherwise I will be forced to take legal action." Here is the link and archive link and screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Kirori Lal Meena statement was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of AAP leader Atishi suggesting people of 'vote for goons' falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha polls
content: New Delhi, April 26 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Delhi Minister Atishi addressing a public meeting, in which she allegedly said that people should not hesitate in voting vote for goons or thugs to defeat the BJP. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video was shared on social media, falsely linking it to the ongoing Lok Sabha Elections. Claim A Facebook user on April 3 shared a video of Delhi Education Minister Atishi in which she can be heard speaking that in order to defeat BJP people should not hesitate in voting for goons or thugs. The caption of the post read, "#ShockingThe real face of Kejriwal's protégé Atishi Marlena who promised to fight against thugs and goons and change the system. Here she unhesitatingly asks people to close their eyes and vote for thugs and goons because BJP must be defeated at all cost."
