Here is the link and archive link and below is screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here, here and here and archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. Two such X posts can be viewed here and here and archive links can be viewed here and here respectively. Further the Desk noticed the logo of 'Okhla news' on the video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a YouTube video from the official channel of Okhla News uploaded on April 19, 2019. The description of the video read, "Atishi Merlena at Tikona Park: A dialogue with Atishi, AAP Lok Sabha candidate from East Delhi. The election is to be held soon. #atishi #aap #LSelections2019" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk found that it was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the original video with the one shared on social media: The Desk found that the viral video was clipped from 37:10 minutes timestamp. While addressing the people, Atishi mentioned that the country has faced a lot of difficulties such as demonetisation, GST, decline in economy and so on. "I think this election (2019) is not a normal election. The people must make sure that they are not only voting for 5 years but we are voting to save the future of our country. And we must make sure that from which part of the country we are voting from we must make sure that we must vote for that candidate or party that can defeat BJP. But we must keep in mind that there is no single party in the country that can defeat BJP single handedly. Every state has different parties that can defeat BJP. There is a phase of polling in UP today or tomorrow. In UP only the coalition of SP and BSP can defeat BJP. So if we were UP voters, what should we do, we should vote for the coalition no matter who is the candidate. I spoke to one of my known person from UP, he told me that the candidate from our area is a goon, so what should we do? I said blindly go and vote for the coalition because this is an election where we need to defeat the BJP." In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report published by Indian Express on April 28, 2019. The title of the report read, "Atishi draws flak for 'goons' remark, Singhvi says poor campaigning by BJP" Here is the link to the news report. Subsequently the Desk concluded that an old video of AAP leader Atishi was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking to the ongoing Lok Sabha polls.

title: PTI Fact Check: This viral screenshot of PM Modi's tweet is digitally edited; claim shared in social media post is fake
content: New Delhi, April 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported X (formerly Twitter) post by PM Modi, quoting him that people across the country voted for opposition's INDIA bloc in record numbers in the first phase of Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral screenshot claiming it was published from PM Modi's X handle was digitally edited. The claim shared in social media posts was fake. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 20 a screenshot of a purported X post by PM Modi, which quoted him stating that people voted for the opposition's INDIA bloc in record numbers in the first phase of Lok Sabha polls, which was held on April 19. The text on the screenshot read: "First phase, great response. Thank you to all those who have voted today. Getting EXCELLENT feedback from today's voting. It's clear that people across India are voting for INDIA in record numbers." Meanwhile, the caption of the post read, "Modi ji got the exit poll numbers, which suggest that people have voted against the NDA in record numbers all across the country. This election will be tough for the NDA." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, we found another Facebook post, carrying the same claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The same screenshot was shared on X as well. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across another X post, which carried a screenshot of an X post purportedly by PM Modi, similar to the one viral on social media. "First phase, great response! Thank you to all those who have voted today. Getting EXCELLENT feedback from today's voting. It's clear that people across India are voting for NDA in record numbers," read the text on the screenshot shared in the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the official X handle to search for the post in question. Here is the link to the X post by PM Modi shared on April 19, after the first phase polling concluded. Below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the viral screenshot to the original post and also highlights how "NDA" has been replaced with "INDIA" in the former. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a screenshot of an X post by PM Modi was digitally altered to make it look like he asked voters to vote for the opposition's INDIA alliance.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of former Congress leader Pramod Krishnam's 'remarks on caste-based reservation' shared as recent on social media with false claims
content: New Delhi, April 29 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of former Congress leader Pramod Krishnam, in which he was heard saying during a public meeting that 'India should be free from caste-based reservation system'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video dating back to 2023 was shared on social media with false claims. Krishnam, a former member of Priyanka Gandhi's team, was expelled from Congress for six years, citing 'indiscipline', and 'anti-party' statements in Feb this year. Claim A Facebook user on April 27 shared a video of Pramod Krishnam in which he can be heard saying that India should be free from caste-based reservation. The caption of the video read, "संविधान बदलने की बात सिर्फ़ बात नहीं है - यही इनका असली एजेंडा है। सुन लीजिए, मोदी जी के प्रिय भाजपा के यह नेता सरे आम आरक्षण समाप्त करने का प्रण दिलवा रहे हैं।" An English translation of the post read, "The talk of changing the Constitution is not just talk – this is their real agenda. Listen, these leaders of Modi ji's favorite BJP are making people promise to end reservation." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same; Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk uploaded the video in the InVid Tool and extracted several keyframes of the footage. Later, the Desk applied Google Reverse Image Search on one of the keyframes and found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and archive links can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. Two X posts can be viewed here and here , and archive links can be viewed here and here , respectively. Further, the Desk noticed the logo of 'BGT News' on the video. Taking this as a cue, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a Facebook video from the official page of BGT News uploaded on September 26, 2023. The caption of the post read, "मंच से आचार्य की सत्ता धारी को चुनौती ब्राह्मणों को धमकाने की कोशिश मत करना बोल कभी हमारे होते थे 7 मुख्यमंत्री" An English translation of the post read, "Acharya's challenge to those in power from the stage: Don't try to threaten Brahmins; say that once upon a time we had seven Chief Ministers." Here is the link and archive link , and below is the screenshot of the same While watching the video, the Desk found it was an extended version of the viral clip. Below is the combination image of the screenshots taken from both the original video with the one shared on social media: While further investigating the Desk scanned the official X handle of Acharya Pramod and came across a post where he gives a statement about the viral video. The caption of the video read, "आचार्य प्रमोद कृष्णम ने ताजा बयान जारी करके कहा है की वो आरक्षण के समर्थक हैं।आचार्य ने कहा की वो जातिवाद, भेदभाव और छुआछूत में विश्वास नहीं करते। उनके पुराने बयान को गलत संदर्भ में पेश किया जा रहा है।#AacharyaPramodKrishnam | @AcharyaPramodk" An English translation of the post read, "Acharya Pramod Krishnam has issued a latest statement saying that he is a supporter of reservation. Acharya said that he does not believe in casteism, discrimination and untouchability. His old statement is being presented in the wrong context" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same; The Desk has tried to contact Krishnam for his remarks on the viral video. We will update the copy as soon as we get his remarks. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Acharya Pramod was shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally edited screenshot of pre-poll survey aired by India Today channel in March this year falsely shared as recent on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, April 29, (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a purported screenshot of India Today's Mood of Nation survey predicting 52 seats to the BJP, 17 seats to Samajwadi Party and five seats to Congress in Uttar Pradesh in the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. The purported survey suggested losses for the BJP in the state, where it bagged 62 out of 80 Lok Sabha seats in the 2019 general elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found a that a digitally edited screenshot was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 17 a purported screenshot of a poll survey India Today, which predicted 52 seats for the BJP, 17 seats for Samajwadi Party and five seats for Congress in Uttar Pradesh respectively. The caption of the post read, "इंडिया टुडे ने उत्तर प्रदेश के अपने सर्वे में ~ सपा को 17 सीट दी है ~ कांग्रेस को 5 सीट दी है ~बसपा को 3 सीट दी है अभी देखते जाइये भाजपा यूपी में 20 सीटों से नीचे आ गई है ये जनता का सर्वे है….. Akhilesh Yadav Akhilesh Yadav जी धीरे धीरे ये आंकड़े और बदलेंगे.......गठबंधन अकेले यूपी में 50से 55 सीट जीतने जा रहा है...." An English translation to the post read, "India Today in its survey of Uttar Pradesh ~ SP has been given 17 seats ~ Congress has been given 5 seats ~BSP has been given 3 seats Now keep watching, BJP has come down to 20 seats in UP, this is the public survey….. Akhilesh Yadav Akhilesh Yadav ji Gradually these figures will change further...the alliance is going to win 50 to 55 seats in UP alone." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, we found another Facebook post, carrying the same screenshot and claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The screenshot was also shared widely on X (formerly Twitter). Three such X posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of India Today on March 20, 2024. The description of the video read, "Mood of the Nation: India Today Group's Mood of the Nation survey results from across the country is here. The Mood of the Nation poll results, one of India's leading opinion polls that has always given a definite picture of the voters' viewpoint, from Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, to eastern states in Bengal, Bihar, Maharashtra in the west, and Tamil Nadu and Kerala in the south, are here now." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk found the visuals at the timestamp of 1 hour 35 minutes looked similar to the screenshot shared in the viral posts. Below is a combination image, comparing the viral screenshot to the original survey by India Today: On further investigating, the Desk also came across an X post shared by the official handle of India Today anchor Rajdeep Sardesai on April 18 writing about the viral screenshot. The caption of the post read, "This is a fake graphic image and WhatsApp message that is doing the rounds. No such UP poll numbers have been shown on the channel." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered photo of India Today survey was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: These Congress' press releases declaring Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi as party candidates from Amethi and Raebareli are fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, May 1 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users have shared screenshot of a purported press release by the Congress, which mentions Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra as party's candidates for the prestigious Amethi and Raebareli constituencies respectively in the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. Meanwhile, several others have shared screenshot of another purported press release which mentioned Rahul as party's candidate from Raebareli and Priyanka from Amethi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the press releases shared in the name of Congress were fake. The party is yet to announce its candidates for the two high-profile seats in Uttar Pradesh. The alleged list of candidates by the Congress is being shared amid the party maintaining suspense over the names of its candidates for the two seats. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 30 a screenshot of a purported press release issued by the Congress, according to which Rahul Gandhi will contest the 2024 Lok Sabha polls from Amethi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra will contest from Raebareli. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the screenshot through Google Lens and found that several other Facebook users had shared it along with the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. Several X (formerly Twitter) users also shared the same screenshot with the same claim. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk also came across another Facebook post, carrying a screenshot of another purported press release by the Congress, which Rahul Gandhi as party's candidate from Raebareli and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra from Amethi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the social media handles (X and Facebook) of Congress, but could not find any such press release as mentioned in the viral social media posts. We, however, came across a list of four Lok Sabha candidates released by the party at 8:22 pm on April 30. The list included the names of Raj Babbar, Anand Sharma, Satpal Raizada and Bhushan Patil. Below is a screenshot of the post: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found a news report by Hindustan Times, published at 10:08 pm on April 30. The headline of the report read: "Cong fields Anand Sharma, Raj Babbar; suspense continues over Amethi, Rae Bareli". "The party, however, is yet to announce its candidates from Amethi and Rae Bareli. The last date of filing nominations for the two seats is on May 3. A senior leader who recently met Rahul Gandhi said, the latter only smiled when party leaders told him that the media's entire focus is on the possible Congress candidates in the two seats," read a section of the report. "Last week, the members of the Congress' Central Election Committee (CEC) unanimously supported a proposal moved by the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge Avinash Pandey to field former Congress chief Rahul Gandhi and general secretary Priyanka Gandhi from the two Gandhi family bastions, Amethi and Raebareli, said two members of the poll panel," it added. Here is the link to the report . Meanwhile, we came across another report by Economic Times, published on April 30, 2024, whose headline read: "Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi may not contest from Amethi and Rae Bareli: Report". Here is the link to the report . The Desk also found Congress leader Dr Vineet Punia who said that the purported screenshots were fake. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that fake screenshots were shared on social media in the name of Congress press releases.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of cow-laden trucks is not from Gujarat's Adani Ports; claim shared in social media posts is fake
content: New Delhi, April 30 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of trucks carrying cows, which they claimed were being supplied to Arab countries from a port owned by Adani Group in Gujarat. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video from Iraq and was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 29 a video of trucks loaded with cows and claimed that they were being supplied to Arab countries from a port in Gujarat, owned by the Adani Group. The caption of the post read: "Gujarat :- Thousands of cows are standing in trucks at Adani's port. To go to *Arab countries*... 😱😱😱 Which will be cut there... Where are the dead devotees?? Let me remind the donkeys that BJP has taken donations only from those doing beef business. Everything is a game of money. You are just there to raise slogans of "Jai Shri Ram". So devotees, say it loudly..." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes of the video. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such Facebook posts can be viewed here , here and here , and archive links can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the Desk came across a Facebook post carrying the same video dated for April 19. The caption of the post read, "الاستعداد لعيد الأضحى EGEG" An English translation of the post read, "Preparing for Eid Al Adha EGEG" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: While further scanning the Desk came across another Facebook post with the same video posted by Hamed ELhagary, a meat wholesaler from Ras El-Barr, Dumyat, Egypt. The caption of the post uploaded on April 19 read, "اللي نايم ع البضاعه ومستنى ترفع EGEGEG اول " An English translation to the post read: "Who is sleeping on the goods and waiting for the first 25,000 heads to be raised? EGEGEG" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned for similar looking ports across the area and came across a YouTube video by Al Mayadeen Channel on January 12,2023. The description of the video read," ميناء أم قصر في البصرة نافذة العراق الاقتصادية وإطلالته البحرية على المياه العميقة، يدخل عبره أكثر من 80% من بضائع السوق العراقية والسلطات تعمل لتطويره باستمرار لمواكبة ارتفاع حجم التجارة الخارجية. إعداد: صلاح الخزاعي" An English translation of the post read, "Umm Qasr Port in Basra is Iraq's economic window and its sea view of deep waters. More than 80% of the Iraqi market's goods enter through it, and the authorities are constantly working to develop it to keep pace with the increasing volume of foreign trade. Prepared by: Salah Al-Khuzaie" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the background and surrounding area was similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: The Desk also reached out to Adani Group via email seeking their response on the viral video. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently the Desk concluded the viral video is from Umm Qasr port and not from India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old 'cash for votes' video involving BJP leader falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha polls; shared on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, May 1, (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check) : Multiple social media users shared a video of a woman counting money from an envelope bearing the symbol of BJP along with photo and name of a party leader, and linked it to the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to at least November 2023, which was falsely linked to the ongoing general elections and shared with misleading claims. Claim An Instagram user shared on April 19 a video showing a woman counting money from an envelope bearing the symbol of BJP and with photo and name of a party leader. The caption of the post read, "#BJPHataoDeshBachao" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes of the video. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such Facebook posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. Two such X posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X (Twitter) post shared on November 16, 2023. The caption of the post read, "बीजेपी प्रत्याशी सुदेश राय के लोग रात में पैसे बांट रहे, वार्ड 13 सीहोर। भाजपा ख़रीदने और बेचने से आगे नहीं सोच सकती।" An English translation to the caption, "People of BJP candidate Sudesh Rai are distributing money at night, Ward 13, Sehore.BJP cannot think beyond buying and selling." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a video report on YouTube, uploaded by the official channel of Inh 24X7 uploaded on November 17, 2023. The description of the video, "INH, Sehore में पैसे बांटने का Video Viral | Collector ने लिया संज्ञान, लिफाफे में भाजपा प्रत्याशी का फोटो" An English translation to the description read: "Video of distribution of money in Sehore goes viral. Collector took cognizance, photo of BJP candidate in envelope" Here is the link for the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The video report included visuals same as those shared in the viral video. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to November 2023, from the runup to the Madhya Pradesh Assembly polls, was shared as recent on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Uddhav Thackeray at public rally in Maharashtra shared on social media with misleading claims
content: New Delhi, May 2 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and claimed that it showed him being interrupted by Congress workers while addressing in Maharashtra's Wardha. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video was shared on social media with misleading claims. The Thackeray's led faction of Shiv Sena and Congress, along with NCP (Sharad Pawar faction) are part of the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) alliance in Maharashtra. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 27 a video of Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray, being interrupted and denied to make a speech during a public rally, with claims of Congress workers hindering his speech in Maharashtra's Wardha. The caption of the post read, "What a fall!! Congress workers of Wardha denied Uddhav Thackeray to even make a speech in a rally. Let me speak for 5 min, pleads Uddhav" Here is the link and archive link and screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool and extracted several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Reverse Image Search, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and archive links can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the Desk came across a video on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of Zee 24 Taas on April 22. The description of the video read, "Wardha Uddhav Thackeray UNCUT | उद्धव ठाकरे यांचं वर्ध्यातील सभेतलं संपूर्ण भाषण पाहा" An English translation of the description read, "Wardha Uddhav Thackeray UNCUT | Watch full speech of Uddhav Thackeray in Wardhya Assembly" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The same video was uploaded by the official channel of ABP Majha on April 22. The title of the video read: "Uddhav Thackeray Wardha Speech : उद्धव ठाकरेंचा नितीन गडकरींवर पहिला वार, पाहा संपूर्ण भाषण". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk found that it was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the original video with the one shared on social media: The Desk found that the viral video was clipped from a 00:13-minute timestamp. The video began with Thackeray, speaking in Marathi, in which he could be heard saying that he would only be able to speak for five minutes as he had to leave for another event. However, later in the video, it can be seen that others on the stage insisted him to speak longer. Taking a cue from this the, Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a video report by the official Youtube channel by Saam TV uploaded on April 23. In the video, MVA candidate from Wardha Amar Kale can be seen addressing the rally while someone interrupts him and informs that Thackeray had a flight to catch for another event. The description of the video read, "महाविकास आघाडीच्या उमेदवारासाठी उद्धव ठाकरे यांनी सभा घेतली. वेळेअभावी त्यांन लवकर निघावं लागलं, पण एका कृतीने त्यांनी अनेकांची मनं जिंकली. | prd" An English translation of the description read, "Uddhav Thackeray held a meeting for Mahavikas Aghadi candidate. He had to leave early due to lack of time, but with one act he won the hearts of many" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Thakeray's public rally was taken out of context and shared on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi didn't say 'BJP can never make India strong'; digitally altered video shared on social media
content: New Delhi, May 3, (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of PM Modi addressing a rally, in which he is heard saying that "BJP can never make a strong India". In its investigation, PTI Fact Check Desk found a digitally altered video of PM Modi was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 26 a video of PM Modi addressing a rally in which he can be heard saying that BJP can never make a strong India. The caption of the post read, "मोदी कह रहा है भाजपा सरकार कभी भी भारत को मजबूत नहीं बना सकती देखतो नतीजा" An English translation of the caption read, "Modi is saying that BJP government can never make India strong, see the result" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same; Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes of the video. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found an X post carrying the same video with similar claim. Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same On further investigation, the Desk came across a Live on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of Narendra Modi on April 21. The description of the video read, "Campaigning for the 2024 Lok Sabha election has intensified, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the star campaigner for the NDA, amplifying his support for BJP candidates in Rajasthan. Talking to the people of Jalore, PM Modi announced that those who haven't yet secured a pakka house will be guaranteed by Modi. He mentioned that out of the 3 crore houses to be constructed, one belongs to you. Also, he urged people to inform the sisters of families yet to receive a permanent home that these houses will be allocated in their names." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from a 17:55-minute timestamp. The Desk noticed that while addressing the rally, PM Modi says that in the first phase of elections, half of Rajasthan has punished the Congress. At the timestamp of 17 minutes 50 seconds, he says, "Rajasthan is filled with nationalism and the people know that Congress can never make India strong." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised search and came across a report by India TV published on April 21. The title of the report read, "Congress can never make India strong, symbol of instability,' says PM Modi in Rajasthan" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of PM Modi's speech was digitally altered and shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of meat shop under Hindu temple is from Pakistan, not Kerala's Wayanad; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 2 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a purported meat shop, which they claimed was running under a Hindu temple in Kerala's Wayanad – the constituency of Congress MP Rahul Gandhi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the temple in the video was located in Ahmadpur Sial of Pakistan, and not India. The video was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user on May 1 shared a video of a what looked like a small shop under a temple like structure. The user claimed that it was a meat shop running under the Sita Ram Temple in Kerala's Wayanad. "Wake up Hindus, wake up, this is Sita Ram temple in Wayanad, Kerala, which has a chicken shop which has been inaugurated by Rahul Gandhi," read the text plate running on the video. The caption of the post read, "केरल के वायनाड में राहुल गांधी और प्रियंका वाड्राइन ने चार साल पहले हिंदुओं के बड़े मंदिर श्रीसीताराम मंदिर पर मुसलमानों का कब्जा रजिस्टर्ड करा दिया था 😡अब तो कांग्रेसी ब्राह्मण क्षत्रिय बहुत खुश हो चुके होंगे 😭😭सब लोग भाजपा को ही वोट दें 🙏@INCIndia @SupriyaShrinate" An English translation of the post read, ""In Wayanad, Kerala, Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Vadrine had registered the occupation of Muslims on the big Hindu temple Sri Sitaram Temple four years ago.Now the Congress Brahmin Kshatriyas must be very happy.Everyone should vote for BJP only." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes of the video. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. While further scanning the search results, Desk came across a video on YouTube uploaded by the official channel MyNation on December 16, 2023. The description of the video read: "The conversion of the Sita Ram temple into a chicken shop is being viewed as not merely an act of vandalism, but a clear violation of the right to freedom of religion and a blatant disregard for the cultural diversity that is an integral part of Pakistan's identity." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The temple shown in the video looked strikingly similar to the one shown in the viral video. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by the Hindi Post published on December 19, 2023. The title of the report read, "Historic Sita-Ram Temple converted into a chicken shop: Pakistan" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk located the Sita-Ram Temple of Ahmedpur Sial, Pakistan on Google Maps. Using the Street View, the Desk noticed the structure of the building was the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: In the next part of investigation, we conducted a separate Google search and found that there was no temple by the name Sita Ram Temple in Kerala's Wayanad. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of Pakistan's Punjab province was falsely shared in name of Kerala's Wayanad.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this shootout video captured on CCTV is old and not related to California gunfire incident and Goldy Brar; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 3, (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) Multiple social media users shared a video of a purported shootout on the street, claiming that it showed the murder of Canada-based gangster Goldy Brar in California. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video of a shootout in New Orleans was shared as recent on social media with false claims. The California Police has refuted the media reports of his killing, saying the person who was killed was not the gangster who was named in the Punjabi singer Sidhu Moose Wala murder case in India. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 2 a video of a shootout on the street, claiming that it showed the killing of gangster Goldy Brar in California. The caption of the post read: "Gangster Goldy brar Sidhu moose Wala murder Master mind shot Dead in California by rival Dalla lakhbhir gang #." (Sic) Here is the link and archive link , and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation To start the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across several videos with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and the archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of WDSU News on July 31, 2023. The description of the video reads, "Video shows two women shot on Industry Street after gunmen open fire." Here is the link and archive link , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the cars and background in this video were the same as in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by Nola published on August 1, 2023. The title of the report read: "WATCH: Footage shows 7th Ward shootout that wounded two women Sunday." According to the report, New Orleans Police were looking for the two shooters who were captured in a video of a 7th Ward shootout. The New Orleans Police Department stated that two women, ages 76 and 36, were wounded in the shooting. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning for reports on the Fresno shooting, the Desk came across a May 2 PTI report by The Print mentioning the same. The title of the report read, "Goldy Brar not the victim in Fresno shooting: Police in California." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. According to the report, the police in the US state of California dismissed reports that the victim of the shooting incident in Fresno city was Canada-based terrorist Satinderjit Singh alias Goldy Brar. The Fresno Police identified the man killed in an alley at Fairmont and Holt avenues as 37-year-old Xavier Gladney in a gang-related interpersonal dispute. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of a shootout in the US was shared on social media, falsely linking it with the Goldy Brar murder.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated photo of President Droupadi Murmu and PM Modi falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha polls; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 6 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a photo of President Droupadi Murmu and PM Modi, which shows the latter handing over a document to an official. The photo was shared with the claim that the President accompanied the PM, while he was filing his nominations for the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo of PM Modi accompanying Droupadi Murmu, when she filing nomination papers as NDA's presidential candidate back in June 2022, was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim. PM Modi will file his nomination papers from the Varanasi Lok Sabha seat on May 14. Elections in Varanasi will be held on June 1 in the seventh and last round of the general elections. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 5 shared a photo of President Droupadi Murmu and PM Modi, and claimed that the latter was accompanied by the President while he was filing nomination papers for the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. The caption of the post read: "राष्ट्रपती एका लोकसभा उमेदवाराचा फॉर्म भरायला जाऊ शकतात का ?देश गुलामीकडे वाटचाल करत आहे.संविधानाची ऐशी तैशी होत आहे.पहा आणि गप्प रहा 😷" An English translation to the post read: "Can the President go to fill the form of a Lok Sabha candidate? The country is moving towards slavery. This is how the constitution is getting ruined. Watch and keep quiet 😷" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the screenshot through Google Lens and found that several other Facebook users had shared the same photo with the same claim. Three such claims can be viewed here , here and here and the archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another Facebook post by the official account of Mid Day, carrying the same photo dating back to June 24, 2022. The caption of the post read: "PM Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, JP Nadda all senior leaders of BJP Rajnath Singh Amit Shah Yogi Adityanath Manohar Lal Khattar Shivraj Singh Chauhan at nomination filing of BJP Presidential Candidate Dropdi Murmu" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the social media handles (X and Facebook) of PM Modi and came across many other photos from the same event, shared by him on June 24, 2022. The caption of the post read: "Earlier today, accompanied leaders from different parties for the filing of nomination papers of Smt. Droupadi Murmu Ji." Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same: The Desk also came across a report by The Hindu published on June 24, 2022 whose headline read, "2022 Presidential election | Droupadi Murmu files nomination papers" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old photo of PM Modi, along with President Murmu was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Incident of electoral irregularity in 2021 Assam Assembly polls falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha elections; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 6 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users claimed that 171 EVM votes were cast in Assam's Dima Hasao while only 90 voters were there at the polling booth. The users further claimed that the Election Commission had suspended five officials in connection with the incident. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an incident that took place during the Assam Assembly polls in 2021 was falsely linked to the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 3 a photo of Election Commission of India building and claimed in the caption that 171 EVM votes were cast at a polling booth in Assam's Dima Hasao district, where only 90 voters were present. The caption of the post read, "#BREAKING : असम के दीमा हसाओ जिले में एक बूथ पर थे सिर्फ 90 मतदाता, लेकिन EVM में वोट पड़े 171, चुनाव आयोग के 5 अफसर सस्पेंड #ElectionCommission @ECISVEEP #AssamAssemblyPolls" An English translation of the post read: "There were only 90 voters at a booth in Dima Hasao district of Assam, but 171 votes were cast in EVM, 5 Election Commission officers suspended. #ElectionCommission @ECISVEEP #AssamAssemblyPolls" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the screenshot through Google Lens and found that several other Facebook users had shared it with the same claim. Three such claims can be viewed here, here and here and the archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. The Desk further conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by The Indian Express, published on April 5, 2021. The title of the report read: "Assam Assembly elections: 171 votes cast in Haflong booth that has 90 voters" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the booth was in the Haflong constituency, which went to the polls in the second phase of Assam Assembly elections on April 1, 2021. Haflong witnessed 74 per cent polling. As the incident came to light, the District Election Officer suspended five poll officials of the booth, set up at 107(A) Khotlir LP School, and proposed a repoll. On further scanning, the Desk came across a thread of posts on X (formerly Twitter) by the Chief Electoral Officer of Assam giving a clarification regarding the post. The caption of the post, dated May 3, 2024, read: "A false narrative has been circulated in the social media regarding 171 additional votes being polled in one of the polling station in Dima Hasao, district of Assam." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: "A false narrative has been circulated in the social media regarding 171 additional votes being polled in one of the polling station in Dima Hasao, district of Assam," read the X post. "The incident mentioned in the said post refers to one that had taken place in the assembly election of 2021.Re-poll was conducted in that particular polling station and disciplinary proceedings against the concerned officers was taken," the state chief electoral officer added in the thread post. Meanwhile, we noticed that Dima Hasao, which is part of the Autonomous District Lok Sabha constituency, went to polls in the first phase of Lok Sabha elections on April 26. But, we could not find any report on any election malpractice being reported from the district. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old incident dating back to Assembly polls in Assam in 2021 was shared as recent on social media with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Viral video claiming a temple in Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi turned into mosque is baseless; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 7,(Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of what looked like a religious place, and claimed that it was a temple that was encroached and converted into a mosque in Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi district. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk could not find any evidence cementing the claim that the Pottalpudur Mohaideen Andavar Dargah in Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi was a temple earlier. The video was shared on social media with a false communal twist. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 4 a video of what looked like a religious place, and claimed that it was a temple converted into a mosque in Tamil Nadu's Tenkasi district. The caption of post read: "Temple turned into a mosque in Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu" Meanwhile, the text plate running over the video read: "Temple turned into a mosque. This is the generations old Hindu temple in Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu, encroached and converted as mosque. Hindus, wake up. You know well who is the only person who can deal with such menace? to save you and your future generations. Ask your friends and family to vote wisely." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several of its keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archive posts can be viewed here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the posts which mentioned that the video actually shows "Pottalpudur Mohaideen Andavar Dargah, a notable religious site located in Tenkasi, Tirunelveli". The dargah is known for its construction, which is inspired by the Dravidian architecture. The dargah was constructed in the memory of Islamic scholar 'Mohideen Abdul Qadir Jilani' in the 17th century (1674 AD)." Here is the screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across an X post shared by the Fact Check Unit of the Government of Tamil Nadu on May 3, in which they termed the claim as 'fake news'. Here is the link to the X post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search and came across a video on YouTube, uploaded by a channel named Tourism Bell on July 2, 2013. The description of the video read: "Pottalputhur Dharga is a popular pilgrim centre not only to Islamic people but also to other religion people. Here every one can see that the dharga itself showing the all religionic architecture.I t is about 45 kms from Tirunelveli on Tirunelveli to Tenkasi via Ambasamudram.It was said that the Dharga built around the year 1674.Here there is a great belief that typical diseases who has not been cured by any kind of medicine has been cured who attended worshipp here...Welcome to this shrine to get prosperity." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the dargah shown in the 11-year-old YouTube video had striking similarities with the one shared in viral social media posts. Below are two combination images, comparing the visuals of the two videos at two different instances: In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted Tenkasi District Collector Thiru AK Kamal Kishore, who confirmed that the claim of a temple being encroached and turned into a mosque was fake. "The claim that temple turned into a mosque is fake. Pottalpudur Moideen Andavar Dargah is a place where people from all faith come and worship. It's a place of religious harmony," Kishor told PTI. During its investigation, the Desk also noticed that the viral claims were shared by right-wing affiliated social media handles, which claimed that a temple was recently turned into mosque. Notably, the state currently has a DMK government. However, the 11-year-old YouTube also mentions the religious place as a mosque, thereby further corroborating the fact that the video was shared with a false communal claim

title: PTI Fact Check: The social media post claiming Supreme Court granted interim bail to Arvind Kejriwal is false; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check) : Multiple social media users claimed that the Supreme Court granted interim bail till June 7 to Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal, who has been accused of money laundering in a case linked to the alleged Delhi excise scam. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that that the Supreme Court had not passed any order on the Delhi CM's plea on May 7, when the social media users shared the claim. The Supreme Court is hearing Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal's bail petition, who has been in judicial custody in Tihar Jail since his arrest on March 21. The AAP convenor has sought interim bail to enable him to campaign in the Lok Sabha elections. Claim A Facebook user claimed on May 7 that Supreme Court had granted interim bail to Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal till June 7. Here's the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched social media platforms and found that several users had shared the same claim on May 7, the day the Supreme Court was hearing the bail petition of Kejriwal. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search to look for any news reports on the matter. We found a PTI report carried by The Print on May 7, whose headline read: "Kejriwal fails to get immediate relief from SC in money laundering case." "A bench of Justices Sanjiv Khanna and Dipankar Datta, which reserved its order on grant of interim bail earlier during the day and said it will be pronounced at 2 p.m., rose without delivering its verdict," read a section of the report. Here is the link to the report: Meanwhile, a Hindustan Times article, reporting about the Supreme Court hearing, quoted the top court saying: "We may grant or we may not grant. But we must be open to you as neither side should be taken by surprise." Here is the link to the report: Another report by PTI, carried by Business Standard on May 7, quoted the Supreme Court saying that "it doesn't want Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal to discharge his official duties if he is released on interim bail" in the money laundering case linked to the alleged excise policy scam as it would lead to a conflict of interest. "Kejriwal failed to get any relief from the top court, with a two-judge bench rising without pronouncing an order granting him interim bail to enable him to campaign in the Lok Sabha elections," read a portion of the report. We further scanned news websites and channels, and came across a report by The Hindu, published on May 7, whose headline read: "Supreme Court defers order on Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal's interim bail plea." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claims made on social media on Kejriwal's interim bail were false.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi did not visit Ram Mandir in Ayodhya after filing Lok Sabha nomination from Raebareli; old video shared with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, May 7 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, claiming that he visited the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya after filing Lok Sabha nominations from UP's Raebareli, where the crowd mocked him with chants of 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Modi, Modi'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video of Rahul Gandhi's visit to Baidyanath Dham in Jharkhand's Deoghar during his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra was shared as recent on social media with misleading claims. The video was shared on social media soon after Rahul Gandhi, accompanied by Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, filed his nomination papers for the Lok Sabha elections from Raebareli on May 3. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 6 a video from a temple visit of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, with the claim that he was mocked by the crowd with chants of 'Jai Shri Ram' and 'Modi, Modi' when he visited the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, after filing his Lok Sabha nomination from Raebareli. The caption of the post read, "आज नामांकन दाखिल करने के बाद पप्पू फिर ब्राह्मण बन गया और अयोध्या चला गया! लोगों ने जय श्री राम और मोदी मोदी के नारे लगाकर उसका स्वागत किया..." An English translation to the caption read, "After filing nomination today, Pappu again became a Brahmin and went to Ayodhya! People welcomed him by raising slogans of Jai Shri Ram and Modi Modi..." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several of its keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by BJP leader Satya Kumar Yadav, who shared a video on February 3. The caption of the post read: "Gandhis think they can con Hindus every time with their age old tactics but now no more! The Hindus of our nation don't want to see the haters of #SanatanaDharma in our temples and as soon as @RahulGandhi reached Deogarh, he was welcomed with the slogans of "Rahul Gandhi go back". The real mood of the nation!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The video shared by the BJP looked visually similar to the one shared on social media. Below is a combination image comparing the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a video report by the Times of India published on Feb 03, 2024. The title of the report read: "Crowd raises 'Modi, Modi' chants as Rahul Gandhi visits Baba Baidyanath Dham in Jharkhand" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same; According to the report, Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Nyaya Yatra reached Jharkhand on February 02. The latter offered prayers at Baba Baidyanath Dham on the next day and as soon as Rahul Gandhi entered the famous Jyotirlinga in Jharkhand's Deoghar, loud sloganeering began. Public in large numbers raised 'Rahul Gandhi Zindabad' slogans, but suddenly it turned into 'Modi-Modi' chants. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video dated back to Rahul Gandhi's visit to Jharkhand's Deoghar in February during his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra.

title: PTI Fact Check: PTI logo falsely used in screenshot of alleged survey on Andhra Pradesh Assembly elections shared on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Some users shared a screenshot of a purported pre-poll survey on Andhra Pradesh Assembly elections, bearing the logo and watermark of Press Trust of India (PTI), on social media. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the PTI had never published such a pre-poll survey. The screenshot with the PTI Logo and the watermark shared on social media is fake. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 7 a screenshot of a purported pre-poll survey on Andhra Pradesh Assembly elections, which predicted a massive victory for the YSRCP. "YSRCP's victory mark in PTI survey," read the post's caption. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens and found several other users shared it. Two such posts on Facebook and Instagram can be seen here and here . The archived versions of the posts can be viewed here and here , respectively. The screenshot has also been widely shared on X. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the PTI website and other news websites but could not find any mention of any such pre-poll survey. The Desk then contacted PTI's Executive Editor G Sudhakar Nair, who refuted the screenshot as fake. "This is fake news. PTI has nothing to do with this screenshot. Someone has falsely used the PTI Logo on it," Nair told PTI Fact Check Desk. Hence, it was concluded that a fake screenshot of a pre-poll survey on Andhra Pradesh Assembly polls was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video, which falsely claimed 'proxy voting by Indian Army' for BJP, shared again during 2024 Lok Sabha polls; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 8, (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of some individuals confronting uniformed personnel, accusing them of proxy voting in favour of the BJP. The user claimed that the Indian Army personnel were "caught red-handed inside election booth for influencing voters to cast fake votes for BJP" during the third phase of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the same video was shared with the false claim in 2019. The same video with the same claim was shared on social media again during the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. Claim An X user shared on May 7 a video of some men confronting uniformed personnel, standing near what looked like an Indian Army vehicle. The user claimed that the Indian Army was indulging in proxy voting and influencing people to cast fake votes in favour of the BJP in the third phase of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. "BIG BREAKING The BJP is using the army to cast fake votes. INDIAN ARMY has been assigned to do ILLEGAL & FRAUDULENT work for the BJP. Caught RED handed inside the Election Booths to influence voters for FAKE Votes to the BJP," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across another X post carrying the same video with an identical claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The same video was also shared on Instagram with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to one such post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The video has also been widely shared on YouTube. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively: On further investigation of the search results, the Desk came across a quote tweet on the viral post, which claimed the video dated back to 2019 and stated that the Indian Army had complained back then. The user also shared a purported screenshot of a Times of India article which carried a letter by Lt General GS Sangha, whose headline read: "We won't be cowed down by propaganda". A second screenshot shared in the X post was of a purported police complaint lodged by the Indian Army at Sadar Police Station in Jabalpur against the men seen in the video. Here is the link and archive link to the comment, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google. It came across a report by the Times of India, published on May 3, 2019, whose headline read: "Gen comes out fighting for Army after viral video seeks to malign soldiers". Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, "The Army has reacted with outrage to a viral video clip where some soldiers, who had gone to cast their vote in a polling booth in Jabalpur, are accused of canvassing for a party." "The Army approached police on Thursday, alleging that goons tried to snatch voter IDs of soldiers and family members, obstructed them from casting a vote in Jabalpur Cantonment area, and circulated a video to malign the image of force," it added. "The video was taken during polling on April 29. The soldiers are seen trying their best not to get provoked as some men follow them around and accuse them of siding with a party," the report read further. During our investigation, we found a Facebook post shared on May 1, 2019, which carried the same video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On another keyword search on Google, the Desk came across a report by The New Indian Express, published on May 2, 2019. The report headline read: "Army officers claim miscreants obstructed them from casting votes in Madhya Pradesh, lodge complaint". Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: The report quoted a letter from the Indian Army about the incident. "On 29 April 2019, the day of voting for Parliamentary Elections, soldiers and their spouses of the Grenadiers Regimental Centre proceeded to cast their votes on a bona fide transport viz Army vehicle at Booth no 146, Swami Vivekananda Higher Secondary School, Katanga, Jabalpur. At booth no 146, when the soldiers of the Indian Army were in the process of exercising their right to vote, certain miscreants approached and snatched their voter identity cards by using criminal force and tried to obstruct them from casting their votes," read the letter dated May 1, 2019. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 2019 video was falsely shared as recent on social media, linking it to the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.

title: PTI Fact Check: This election-related advertisement featuring ''Amulya girl' is fake; Claim shared on social media is false
content: New Delhi, May 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a photo featuring the logo of dairy cooperative Amul, along with text in Hindi suggesting people to vote. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the advertisement shared in the name of Amul was fabricated. No such ad was made or shared by the company. Claim An X user shared on May 6 a graphic which carried the logo of Amul along with text in Hindi, whose translation read: "Vote or don't vote, take the right decision. Your vote is priceless." The caption of the post read: "Very topical, as always Jiyo Amul. The true taste of India" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the screenshot through Google Lens and found that a Facebook user had shared the same photo. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by former IPS officer Kiran Bedi, who shared the same graphic tagging the Election Commission and Amul, on May 5. The caption of the post read, "@ECISVEEP @Amul_Coop" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the official social media handles (Twitter and Facebook) of Amul and came across a post, giving a clarification on the viral post. The caption of the post read, "Issued in Public Interest by Amul" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fabricated graphic was shared in the nameof Amul on social media

title: PTI Fact Check: Reader's comment dating back to 2009 shared on social media as New York Times article on Indian elections with misleading claims
content: New Delhi, May 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared posts, quoting a purported article by the New York Times, that praised India and its elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the text shared as NYT article was in fact a comment on an article published by the organisation in 2009. This comment was shared as NYT article on social media with misleading claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 6 a post quoting a purported article by the New York Times, that praised India and its elections. The text (quoted as NYT article) was credited to one 'V Mitchell'. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched social media platforms with relevant keywords and found that several users had shared the same claim. Three such Facebook posts can be viewed here , here and here and archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. We also found an X post by former IPS officer Kiran Bedi, who shared the same text, claiming it was an article published by the NYT. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed one of the comments on the posts which mentioned that the article was not by 'V Mitchell' in New York Times, rather it was a comment on an article published in 2009. Here is a screenshot of the comment: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across an article published by The New York Times on April 14, 2009, written by Somini Sengupta. The title of the report read: "As Elections Near, Tightrope Awaits in India" Here is the link of the article: We read the article, and found that it had a lot of grammatical errors and did not include any part of the text that was shared on social media in the name of NYT article. However, on scanning the comment section of the post, we came across a comment with the same text as shared recently. Here is the link to the comment and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on the NYT website and in Google to know whether anyone with the name of V Mitchell has ever written any article or opinion piece on this website but we didn't find anything with the name of 'V Mitchell' either on NYT website or in Google search. This showed the name used in the viral social media post as the author is misleading and he just wrote a comment on an article, not the entire article as author. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a user comment was falsely claimed as an article by New York Times and shared on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Mayawati did not ask voters to vote for BJP; clipped video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 10 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a video of BSP president Mayawati addressing a rally in which she was heard saying that 'since PM Modi gave free ration, voters should be indebted to vote for him in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was a clipped version of Mayawati's recent speech, and it was shared on social media with misleading claims amid the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. Claim: An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on May 6 shared a video of BSP chief Mayawati, in which she can be heard appealing voters to vote for BJP since they were indebted towards PM Modi who gave them free ration. The caption of the post read: " *हिंदुओ से मायावती की अपील बीजेपी को वोट दे* और नरेन्द्र मोदी जी को जिताए।" An English translation of the caption read: "Mayawati appeals to Hindus to vote for BJP and make Narendra Modi win." Here is the link and archive link and a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through the InVid Tool search and extracted several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here, and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube Live video of Mayawati's speech, uploaded by the channel of News State on May 4. The title of the video read: "Mayawati Rally: Agra में बसपा अध्यक्ष मायावती ने जनसभा को किया संबोधित | BSP | Latest| Update" An English translation of the title read: "Mayawati Rally: BSP President Mayawati addressed the public meeting in Agra. BSP | Latest| update." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the video shared on social media. At 2:43 minutes, the BSP supremo can be heard giving the same statement, whose selected portion was shared in social media posts. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across another YouTube Live uploaded by the official channel of the Bahujan Samaj Party on 4 May 2024. The description of the video read: "LIVE - सुश्री बहन मायावती जी | Rally in Agra, Uttar Pradesh | Lok Sabha Election 2024". (this is not the description but the title) Please try to mention the description. An English translation of the description read, "LIVE - Ms Sister Mayawati ji | Rally in Agra, Uttar Pradesh | Lok Sabha Election 2024". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that it was the complete version of Mayawati's speech, whose clip was shared on social media. Below is a combination image, comparing the original video with the one shared on social media: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 26 minutes 14 seconds. "People of BJP and RSS are roaming around in villages with bags on their shoulders and what are they saying.. Shri Narendra Modi ji has given you free ration, so you have a lot of debt to Modi ji, so you have to repay this debt by voting for BJP..." During our investigation, we also came across a report by Hindustan Times published on May 4. The title of the report read: "Don't feel obligated to vote for any party, Maya tells ration beneficiaries" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Mayawati's speech was clipped and shared on social media with misleading claim. Muskan (Trainee from IIMC Delhi) supported the PTI Fact Check Desk in the investigation of the claim debunked above.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video of Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar talking about Islam is edited and shared with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video of Congress leader Kanhaiya Kumar in which he was heard praising Islam. The video was shared with the claim that Kumar urged people to embrace Islam. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally edited video made by combining different clips from his old speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claims. Kumar is contesting the 2024 Lok Sabha polls from North East Delhi constituency. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 2 a video of Kanhaiya Kumar, in which he is heard praising Islam, and claimed that he asked people to embrace the religion. "An undated video of Congress candidate Kanhaiya Kumar goes viral on social media where he can be seen demeaning Hindu religion and praising Islam and Allah for generosity. We all have not come here from Arab. We became Muslim because of preaching of peace and equality," read the caption shared along with the 35-second video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes of the video. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across two more Facebook posts carrying the same post with similar claims. The posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The video has also been widely shared on X. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post shared on February 3, 2020, which carried the same video. The caption of the post read: "Is he a Muslim? I thought he is a communist I.e. an atheist." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, we found that the same video of Kanhaiya Kumar was shared by film director Vivek Agnihotri. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across the full video uploaded on YouTube by 'One Channel' in August 2018. The caption of the video read: "Kanhaiya Kumar answered the questions of intellectuals of Muslim community in Nanded." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the full video and found that the viral video was clipped from 12:03 minutes timestamp, while leaving out the context at 11:50 minutes, where Kumar quotes a speech by Abul Kalam Azad made at the Jama Masjid. "Nation's first Education Minister Maulana Abul Kalam Azad made an argument at Jama Masjid that this nation belongs to all of us. We won't go somewhere, just because someone tells us to. Our blood and sweat is mixed with this nation's soil. Our ancestry is connected to this nation. All of us did not walk from Arab, we were brought up here...," Kumar says. This clip is combined with other parts of the video at 15:03 timestamp and 16:01 timestamp . At 16:01 minutes, Kumar says: "We will save ourselves, our community and the nation. Allah is very powerful, he will protect us." The latter part of this statement was combined with what Kumar said at 15:03 minutes. "If someone comes to you in the guise of a saviour of your community and says that he will protect your religion, give them a fitting reply and say – Allah is very powerful, he will protect us." Subsequently, the Desk found that selected portions of Kumar's 2018 speech were combined and taken out of context, and further shared on social media with misleading claims. The Desk then conducted another customised Google search to verify the second claim made in one of the social media posts that this was second time that Congress had fielded Kumar in Lok Sabha polls. We found that Kumar fought the 2019 Lok Sabha polls as a CPI candidate against BJP leader Giriraj Singh from Bihar's Begusarai and had lost. This time, he has been pitted by the Congress against BJP's Manoj Tiwari in North East Delhi seat.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video of Mallikarjun Kharge talking about 'redistribution of wealth' is edited and shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 11 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, in which is heard saying that Congress will redistribute citizen's wealth if voted to power in the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video of Kharge's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with misleading claim. In the runup to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the BJP and PM Modi have been targeting Congress over its promise to address the inequality of wealth and income in its manifesto. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 7 a video of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge in which he is heard saying that Congress will redistribute wealth to people having more children. The caption of the post read, "इनका मक़सद साफ़ है- गजवा ए हिन्द हिंदू को अब अपना भविष्य तय करना है।#VoteForDharma" An English translation to the caption read, "Their intention is clear - Gajwa e Hind Hindus have to decide their future now.#VoteForDharma" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same "Do you know what the Congress is doing? Congress people are entering your homes, breaking in your almirahs and distributing the money to people outside, giving it to the Muslims. Those who have more children, they will get more; what can I do if you don't have children," Kharge is hear saying in the video. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. Several X users also shared the same video. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a recorded Live video uploaded by the official YouTube channel of Congress on May 3. The description of the video read, "LIVE: Congress President Shri Mallikarjun Kharge addresses the public in Ahmedabad, Gujarat." Here is the link for the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the extended video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 32 minutes 29 seconds. The Desk observed at the timestamp of 31 minutes 50 seconds, Kharge talks about Congress manifesto and states, "In Hissedari Nyay, we (Congress) have talked about caste-based census, which will be conducted to know how many people are educated in each community, how many graduates are there, how much is the income, what is the per capita income; to see this, we are going to do a caste-based census." Further he adds, "So Modi Sahab immediately says 'you know what Congress people are doing? Congress people will enter your house, break your cupboards, take all your money and will distribute your money to others. They are distributing to Muslims, those who have more children will get more'. If you do not have kids, what can I do? But we are not going to redistribute. We are not taking away anything and giving it to others like this. Forgive me, but what Modi sir is saying is wrong. It is wrong for the society, wrong for the country, and wrong for all of us." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Mallikarjun Kharge's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false communal claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Kangana Ranaut's speech shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 12 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of actor and BJP's Lok Sabha candidate Kangana Ranaut saying that the crowd gathered only to see her and not vote for her, and claimed that she had accepted her defeat in the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video of Kangana's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 5 a video of actor and BJP leader Kangana Ranaut in which she was heard saying that the crowd gathered only to see her and not vote for her.
