The caption of the post read, "कंगना ने मानी हार, "भीड़ बोट नहीं देगी, सिर्फ देखने आती है" #VideoSocialMedia" An English translation of the post read: "Kangana accepted defeat, "The crowd will not give votes, they only come to watch" #VideoSocialMedia" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation: Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Punjab Kesari published on May 02. The description of the report read, "करसोग में विक्रमादित्य और प्रतिभा सिंह पर बरसीं कंगना, कहा-मैं मुंबई से आई कोई हुस्न परी नहीं हूं". An English translation of the description read, "Kangana lashed out at Vikramaditya and Pratibha Singh in Karsog, said- I am not a beauty angel from Mumbai". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk found that it was an extended version of the viral video. The viral video was clipped from a 00:10-minute timestamp. The Desk noticed that Kangana was reacting to Pratibha Singh's comment on her. "But his (Vikramaditya) mother Pratibha ji, whom I consider as my mother, yesterday said at a place that the crowd which gathers to see Kangana, will not vote for her. They only come to see what kind of object she is.. and what beautiful lady has been brought from Mumbai. They come to see the object only. I am not an object, I am a girl. I am also made of flesh and bone as you sisters," reads a rough translation of Kangana's speech. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by Hindustan Times published on May 03. The title of the report read, "Kangana fires another salvo at Vikramaditya Singh" The link to the report can be seen here and below is the screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Kangana Ranaut's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claim. Muskan (Trainee from IIMC Delhi) supported the PTI Fact Check Desk in the investigation of the claim debunked above

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Jharkhand Police did not seize truck full of cash and gold; AI-generated photo shared as real on social media
content: New Delhi, May 13 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of a truck loaded with cash and gold coins, claiming that it was seized by the Jharkhand Police during the ongoing 2024 Lok Sabha elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found an AI-generated image was shared on social media as real with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on April 30 a photo of a truck loaded with cash and gold, claiming that it was caught by the Jharkhand Police during the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the post read: "यह देख लो मित्रों इसी को कहते हैं कल पैसा जब मोदी जी छापा मारते हैं तो एड को बेईमान और फ्रॉड बोलते हैं राजनेता लोग जो चोरी करेगा वह जेल जाएगा जो भ्रष्टाचार करेगा अर्जित संपत्ति काम आएगा वह जेल जाएगा यह देख लीजिए गेहूं के ट्रक में नोटों का अंबार निकल रहा है यहां तक की कार्टन बॉक्स में भी नोट भरे हुए हैं इसीलिए बेईमान लोग चिल्लाते हैं कहते हैं कि हमने तो भ्रष्टाचार किया ही नहीं है दारू में यह झारखंड की पुलिस ने पकड़ा है." An English translation of the post read, "See this friends, this is what is called money tomorrow. When Modi ji conducts raids, politicians call advertising dishonest and fraud. The one who steals will go to jail. The one who commits corruption will go to jail. The one who will use his acquired property will go to jail. Look at the notes in the wheat truck. Even the carton boxes are full of currency notes, that is why dishonest people shout and say that we have not committed corruption in liquor, it has been caught by the Jharkhand police." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched social media platforms and found that several users had shared the same photo with a similar claim. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any news report mentioning any such recovery in the state. Had such a big seizure been made, it would have grabbed the headlines across news channels and websites. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk closely watched the viral photo and noticed several discrepancies, suggesting that it might be digitally created. Below are some combination images, highlighting the discrepancies in terms of distorted faces and bodies, and currency which doesn't like Indian. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the viral photo through AI-detection tool Hugging Face. Here's what we found: A similar result was seen when we ran the image through Hive, another AI detection tool. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral photo was AI-generated and was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of people breaking EVMs during Karnataka state elections falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha polls; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 13 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of some people breaking EVMs, which they claimed were being stolen away in a car belonging to the BJP. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that video linked to the 2023 Karnataka Assembly polls was shared as recent on social media with misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 2 a video of some people breaking EVMs on a street, and claimed that the car carrying the electronic voting machines belonged to BJP. The caption of the post read: "Evm, से लोकतंत्र खत्म है." An English translation of the caption read: "Evm, democracy is over." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes of the footage. The Desk then ran one of the keyframes through Google Lens and found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively: On further scanning, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of The Tribune on May 10, 2023. The description of the video read: "Karnataka Polls: People manhandle officer on election duty, damage ballot units in Vijayapura." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the viral video and the video report by The Tribune, dating back to May 2023. Below is a combination image, comparing the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Print published on May 10, 2023. The title of the report read: "23 arrested after poll official manhandled ballot units damaged in Karnataka village." Here is the link to the report: According to the report, the villagers stopped a section officer's vehicle carrying reserved EVMs for the Assembly elections and damaged two control and ballot units each and three VVPATs (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail). The police officials informed that the villagers came into action after hearing the rumour that the officials were changing the EVMs and VVPATs. In the next part of the investigation the Desk came across an X post carrying a press note by the official handle of Chief Electoral Officer, Karnataka dated for May 10, 2023. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same The press note confirmed that the officials who were taking the reserve EVMs and VVPATs from a strong room in Basavana Bagewadi constituency to Masabinal were attacked on the way and 24 people were arrested from the spot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video related to 2023 Karnataka Assembly polls was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to the ongoing Lok Sabha polls.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi didn't make vote appeal for AIMIM; digitally altered video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi in which he was heard saying that "people must vote for AIMIM in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video clip was digitally edited to make it look like the PM asked people to vote for AIMIM. In the original video the Prime Minister addressed people during his rally in Telangana and asked them to vote for the BJP. The edited video was shared on social media with the false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 12 a video of PM Modi addressing a rally, in which he can be heard saying that people must vote for AIMIM in the ongoing elections. The caption of the post read, "Modi ne Hyderabad me AIMIM ko kiya Support" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first watched the video clip and noticed several audio and visuals jumps in it. We then ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. Three such YouTube videos can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube Short uploaded by one 'NNC News' on May 11, 2024. The title of the video read: "BJP ko ich vote denge | Brs Nakko, Congress Nakko, Aimim Nakko | PM Modi speaking typical Hyderabadi" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk noticed that this was a similar video to the one shared on social media, except that here, PM Modi said: "Telangana says: Congress nakko, BRS nakko, MIM nakko, BJP koich vote denge, BJP ko jitayenge." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a recorded YouTube Live of PM Modi's Telangana rally uploaded by the official channel of Narendra Modi on May 10, 2024. The title of the video read: "PM Modi Live | Public meeting in Hyderabad, Telangana | Lok Sabha Election 2024." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that it was the complete version of the PM's speech, whose clip was shared on social media. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 12 minutes 50 seconds, and was edited in a way to make it look like PM sought votes for AIMIM. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by Deccan Chronicle published on May 10, 2024. The title of the report read: "PM Says Telangana People Are Saying Congress Nakko, BRS Nakko, BJP Jeeto" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video of PM Modi's speech was shared on social media with false claims

title: PTI Fact Check: No, people did not hurl shoes and slippers at Akhilesh Yadav during roadshow; video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 14 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav, and claimed that it showed people hurling shoes and slippers on him during a roadshow. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of supporters throwing garlands on Akhilesh Yadav during his recent roadshow in UP's Kannauj was shared on social media with false claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 8 a video of Akhilesh Yadav in a roadshow and claimed that it showed people throwing shoes and slippers at him. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes of the video. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across two more Instagram posts carrying the same video with similar claims. The posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The video has also been widely shared on X. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed that the post carried a text 'Live from Kannauj'. Taking a clue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report by NDTV published on Apr 27, 2024. The title of the report read: "Akhilesh Yadav Holds Mega Roadshow In Kannauj". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk carefully watched the video report and found that the crowd threw flowers and garlands towards Akhilesh Yadav, and not shoes and slippers. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Samajwadi Party on Apr 27, 2024. The description of the video read: "माननीय राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष श्री अखिलेश यादव जी का जनसंपर्क अभियान, रसूलाबाद, कन्नौज लोकसभा।" An English translation of the video read: "Public relations campaign of Honorable National President Shri Akhilesh Yadav, Rasulabad, Kannauj Lok Sabha." Here is the link below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any news report verifying the claim made in the viral social media posts. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of supporters throwing garlands towards Akhilesh Yadav was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat didn't say 'Sangh is against reservation'; clipped video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, in which he was heard saying 'people of the Sangh oppose reservation from within, but cannot say it openly'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found a clipped video of Bhagwat's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with misleading claims. In the runup to the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the Congress-led opposition has been targeting the BJP with its claim that if re-elected to power, it will scrap reservations for tribals, Dalits, and backward classes. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 14 a video of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat in which he was heard saying that people of the Sangh oppose reservation from within, but cannot say it openly. The caption of the post read: "हम संघ वाले अंदर-अंदर से आरक्षण का विरोध करते हैं, लेकिन बाहर आ के बोल नहीं सकते...!!!! :- संघ प्रमुख (मोहन भागवत) मोदी योगी अमित शाह बीजेपी के सारे नेता संघ के हैं क्या वह आरक्षण दें पाएंगे?" An English translation to the caption read: "We Sangh members oppose reservation from within, but cannot come out and speak...!!!! :- Sangh Chief (Mohan Bhagwat) Modi Yogi Amit Shah All BJP leaders belong to Sangh, will they be able to give reservation?" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The video has been widely shared on X too. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk came across an X post with a similar video uploaded by official handle of Bharat Samachar on April 28. The caption of the post read, "संविधान सम्मत सभी आरक्षण का समर्थन करते हैं।" आरएसएस प्रमुख मोहन भागवत ने हैदराबाद में संघ के कार्यक्रम में यह स्पष्टीकरण दिया है।" An English translation of the post read, "Everyone supports reservation as per the Constitution. RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has given this clarification at the Sangh's program in Hyderabad." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk found that it was an extended version of the viral video. The viral video was clipped from a 00:08-minute timestamp. The context was cropped out to make it look like the RSS chief spoke against reservation. "When I came here I heard about a video circulating on the internet, that people in the Sangh oppose reservation from within but cannot come out and speak. This is completely false. The Sangh has been supporting all reservations as per the Constitution since the beginning." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by Times Now published on May 28. The title of the report read: "Sangh Has Always Stood For Reservation As Per Constitution: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Trashes Viral Clip" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Bhagwat's speech was clipped and shared on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video doesn't show vandalism by farmers at Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini's rally venue; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 15 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a group of men vandalising a stage, and claimed that they were farmers who destroyed the stage set for a public rally of Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2021 from the then Haryana CM Manohar Lal Khattar's rally venue in Karnal, which was shared on social media as recent with misleading claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 13 a video, claiming that it showed farmers forcibly entering Haryana CM Nayab Saini rally and demolishing the stage amidst the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. The caption of the post read, "हरियाणा के मुख्यमंत्री नायब सिंग सैनी के पंडाल को किसान नो ने घुसकर तहसे नहस कर डाला। BJP सरकार " An English translation to the caption read: "Farmers entered the pandal of Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini and destroyed it. BJP government" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here, here and here , respectively: Two such X posts can be viewed here and here and archive versions can be viewed here and here respectively. Further the Desk noticed that the people in the viral video were wearing jackets and sweaters, suggesting that the video was from winters. Also, while going through the comment section, the Desk found a user mentioning that the video was from an old incident. Below is a screenshot of the same Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report by ABP NEWS uploaded on January 11, 2021. The description of the video read: "The Haryana police will be registering an FIR against 71 people for causing ruckus and ruining the programme of Chief Minister Manohar Lal Khattar.On Sunday, the farmers in Karnal protested against the Haryana Chief Minister Manohar Lal Khattar. The farmers were so angry that the Chief Minister could not hold jansabha in order to explain the benefits of three Farm laws. After this, Haryana Chief Minister Manohar Lal Khattar spoke during a press conference. He said, "These people have defamed the farmers because a farmer doesn't have such nature. A farmer can be less educated or simple but he's sensible." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the viral video and the video report by ABP News, dating back to May 2021. Below is a combination images, comparing the two videos: We also came across a news report by Times Now, dated January 10, 2021, which carried a video from the same incident. Below is a combination image, comparing it with the viral video: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search relating to the incident and came across a report by the Indian Express published on January 10, 2021. The title of the report read, "Haryana CM's event cancelled after protests turn violent at rally venue" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to 2021 was falsely shared as recent on social media with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Plastic perfume bottle in BJP's election kit in Mumbai misidentified as 'gold biscuit'; video shared on social media with false claims
content: New Delhi, May 16 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video showing a police official examining BJP's election campaign kit and claimed that the party distributed 'gold biscuits' to the voters in Mumbai's Ghatkopar. A voice in the background also referred to an object from the kit as 'gold biscuit'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that plastic perfume bottle was misidentified as gold biscuit. The video was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 12 a video of a police officer examining BJP's campaign kit and claimed that the party distributed 'gold biscuits' to the people in Ghatkopar, Mumbai. The caption of the post read: "Bags containing BJP poster, a banner & one GOLD biscuit inside every bag at GHATKOPAR, Mumbai." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of Zee News on May 12, 2024. The description of the video read: "A video of Ghatkopar Police Station in Mumbai is going viral. In this video, police and election officials are seen searching a car. BJP's election campaign material is visible in the video and it is being claimed that BJP is distributing gold biscuits. What is true? Watch this report" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the BJP's District Vice President from North Central Mumbai Ajay Badgujar stated that he was made to wait at the police station for hours and out of frustration referred to the plastic bottle as 'gold biscuit.' The leader further blamed the opposition for the incident saying that, "The gold biscuit that you are talking about. This is that plastic biscuit. This is not a biscuit but a perfume bottle, but the opposition has to make a mountain out of a molehill. So they are calling perfume bottles a gold biscuit." The Desk noticed the articles in the viral video were similar to the one in the news report. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search and came across a report published by the Deccan Herald on May 12, 2024. The title of the report read, "Lok Sabha Elections 2024 | No gold biscuit in poll kit, only 'plastic' perfume bottle: BJP leader on viral video" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk found that a plastic perfume bottle in BJP's election campaign kit was misidentified as 'gold biscuit' and was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Claim in Social media posts that 'PM served food with empty bucket and ladle' at Patna Sahib Gurudwara is false; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of PM Modi from his visit to the Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib Gurudwara in Bihar's Patna was shared on social media, with a claim that he was seen serving food to the people sitting in queue, but there were no food items in the plates, and the ladle and bucket carried by PM. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the PM actually served food to the people sitting in queue at the gurudwara, and the entire event was captured in a video, which was later aired by several news channels on the same day. The screenshot shared in multiple social media posts with the claim that the 'PM served no food' was absolutely false. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 14 a photo of PM Modi serving 'langar' at Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib Gurudwara in Bihar's Patna, and claimed that he wasn't actually serving food to the people sitting in queue, since he was carrying an empty ladle and bucket. The caption of the post read: "Pictures don't lie. The bucket? Empty. The serving spoon? Empty. The plate? Empty. The recipients? Grateful. The server? Smug and self-assured. The public? Applauding. Who else? Where else? Photographer?" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched social media platforms with relevant keywords and found that several users had shared the photo with the same claim. Two such Facebook posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively: Two X posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of Aaj Tak, which shared a video from the same event. The caption of the post, dated May 13 read: "प्रधानमंत्री @NarendraModi ने बिहार के पटना में, गुरुद्वारा पटना साहिब में लंगर सेवा दी। " An English translation to the post read: "Prime Minister @NarendraModi delivered langar seva at Gurdwara Patna Sahib, in Patna, Bihar." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed the viral photo was taken from the same langar service. Below is a combination of the two visuals. On watching the video, the Desk noticed that the PM can be seen placing food on the plates, which looks like 'kheer'. We also noticed that the viral screenshot was taken at 00:14 seconds timestamp. Below is a combination image, showing the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by NDTV, published on May 13, 2024. The title of the report read: "Watch: Wearing Turban, PM Modi Serves Langar At Historic Patna Gurdwara" Here is the link and below is the screenshots of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a screenshot of PM serving food at langar was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Claim in social media posts that 'PM accepted upside-down sketch of Rabindranath Tagore' is misleading; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 17 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, with the claim that PM Modi received an upside-down portrait of Rabindranath Tagore during a public rally in West Bengal's Barrackpore, insinuating that he disrespected the Nobel laureate. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video from the event was shared on social media with misleading claims. The part of the video where Tagore's sketch was straightened and PM Modi held the picture upright was omitted in the viral video. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 12 a video which showed PM Modi receiving an upside-down sketch of Rabindranath Tagore from BJP MLA Pawan Singh during a rally in West Bengal's Barrackpore. The caption of the post read: "Glaring visuals from PM @narendramodi's rally in Barrackpore today! The PM received an UPSIDE DOWN PORTRAIT of Kabiguru Rabindranath Tagore from Bhatpara BJP MLA Pawan Singh. এরা নাকি বাংলার হৃদয়ে জায়গা করতে চায়! " An English translation to the caption read, "Glaring visuals from PM @narendramodi's rally in Barrackpore today! The PM received an UPSIDE DOWN PORTRAIT of Kabiguru Rabindranath Tagore from Bhatpara BJP MLA Pawan Singh. They want to make a place in the heart of Bengal!" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The video was shared on X by several TMC leaders as well. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and archive versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of Narendra Modi on May 12. The title of the video read: "PM Modi Live | Public meeting in Barrackpore, West Bengal | Lok Sabha Election 2024". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that it was the full video from the public rally of PM in West Bengal's Barrackpore. We watched the video and found that the viral clip was taken from a 02:45-minute timestamp. In the video, PM can be seen standing as Pawan Singh inadvertently presents him an upside-down portrait of Tagore. Later, West Bengal BJP President Sukanta Majumdar noticed that the portrait is upside down and signals Pawan Singh to straighten it. The latter then straightens the portrait. Below is a combination image, showing the sequence of events in which the mistake is rectified by the BJP leaders on the stage: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by the Times of India published on May 13. The title of the report read, "Row over Tagore portrait gaffe by Bhatpara MLA" Here is the link to the news report and below is a screenshot: According to the report, Bhatpara MLA Pawan Singh gifted a portrait of Rabindranath Tagore to PM Modi. The portrait was upside down when he handed it over to Modi. BJP state president Sukanta Majumdar, who was present on the dais, noticed it and rectified it, but Pawan's mistake was captured by the cameras. Subsequently, the Desk found a selected portion from the video of PM Modi's rally in West Bengal's Barrackpore was shared on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, LK Advani didn't call Rahul Gandhi 'hero of Indian politics'; report shared by news outlet was false
content: New Delhi, May 20 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported Hindi newspaper article, which quoted BJP stalwart Lal Krishna Advani praising Congress leader Rahul Gandhi as the "hero of Indian politics". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk could not find any evidence substantiating the viral claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 11 a screenshot of a purported Hindi newspaper article, which quoted BJP stalwart Lal Krishna Advani praising Congress leader Rahul Gandhi as the "hero of Indian politics". The caption of the report read, "ये क्या कह गए ये क्या कह गए लाल कृष्ण आडवाणी जी " An English translation of the caption read, "What did they say, what did they say, Lal Krishna Advani ji" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched social media platforms with relevant keywords and found that several users had shared the same claim. Three such Instagram posts can be viewed here , here and here and archive links can be viewed here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed the masthead of the newspaper read 'Townhall Times'. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, which led to its official website. We tried looking up for the said article, and found that the report was deleted from the website. On further the search results, the Desk came across another similar report in Hindi, published by Avadh Bhumi on May 8. The title of the report read, "राहुल गांधी भारतीय राजनीति का नायक है: लालकृष्ण आडवाणी" An English translation to the title read, "Rahul Gandhi is the hero of Indian politics: LK Advani" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that almost all the articles on the website were written by Anil Shukla Madhukar. We then checked the 'Terms and Conditions' section of the website, which stated that the company provided services "in accordance with and subject to, prevailing laws of Netherlands". Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: Even the disclaimer section of the website stated: "All the information on this website – https://avadhbhumi.com/ – is published in good faith and for general information purpose only. avadhbhumi.com does not make any warranties about the completeness, reliability and accuracy of this information." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search to look for any other credible source to support the claim. We, however, found that Townhall Times had issued a clarification regarding the now-deleted article on May 11. The title of the report read: "राहुल गाँधी पर दिया गया लाल कृष्ण अडवाणी का ब्यान फैक्ट चेक में गलत निकला" An English translation to the title read, "Lal Krishna Advani's statement on Rahul Gandhi turns out to be false in fact check." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that LK Advani did not make any such comment on Rahul Gandhi.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of CM Yogi making remarks on reservations for Muslims shared on social media with false claims
content: New Delhi, May 20 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath, in which he was heard making remarks on reservation for Muslims and saying "go to Pakistan and beg there, don't burden India". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that selected parts of CM Yogi's speech at a public rally were combined and shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 17 a video of Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi in which he was heard making remarks on reservation for Muslims and saying 'go to Pakistan and beg there, don't burden India.' The caption of the post read, "Go to Pakistan and beg there, don't burden India; They say all the reservations should be given to Muslims," said Uttar Pradesh chief Minister Yogi Adityanath." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first watched the viral video and noticed a discrepancy in the visuals. We then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was shared on X as well. Three such X posts can be viewed here , here and here and archive versions can be found here , here and here respectively. While further scanning the Desk came across a Youtube video uploaded by the official channel of ABP Ganga on May 15. The description of the video read, "CM Yogi Mahoba Rally: महोबा में सीएम योगी ने एकदम बदल दिया पूरा माहौल | ABP GANGA" An English translation of the video read, "CM Yogi Mahoba Rally: CM Yogi completely changed the entire atmosphere in Mahoba. ABP GANGA" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk found that it was the complete version of the CM's speech, whose clip was shared on social media. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video the Desk noticed that the viral video was made by combining two different clips, taken from timestamps 11:55 minutes and 18:54 minutes. At the timestamp of 11:28 minutes, Adityanath can be heard saying: "Modi ji has lifted 25 crore people out of poverty, enabling them to lead a prosperous life. In the past 10 years, more people have been lifted out of poverty in our country than the entire population of Pakistan. You must be seeing the daily protests in Pakistan. People are fighting over a kilogram of flour. This kind of grabbing and snatching is happening in Pakistan. Tell those who are singing praises of Pakistan, if you love Pakistan so much, why are you becoming a burden on India? Go to Pakistan and beg there with a bowl." Further at the timestamp of 18:55 minutes, CM Yogi hits out at Congress and Samajwadi Party, saying: "Muslims should be given all the reservations. Where will our people from the backward class go?" These two separate remarks were combined to make it look like Adityanath made a communal remark. During our investigation, we also came across a report by ABP Live, published on May 15. The title of the report read, "'Go, Beg In Pakistan If...': Yogi Adityanath's Jibe At Opposition" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Uttar Pradesh Minister Yogi Adityanath lashed out at Congress and I.N.D.I.A bloc on Wednesday over their "love for Pakistan" and said that "those who are singing for Pakistan, ask them if they love Pakistan this much then why they are a burden on this country, go there and beg," read a portion of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that clipped sections of CM Yogi's speech were combined and shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of EVMs carried in a truck shared on social media with false claims; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 21 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video showing a group of men standing on a goods carrier and purportedly holding EVMs in their hands. The voice in the background, seemingly of the person recording the video, claims that the BJP was openly doing an 'EVM scam'. The timing of the social media post insinuated that the incident was related to the ongoing Lok Sabha elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video dating back to 2022 UP Assembly polls was shared as recent on social media with false claims. The video actually showed EVMs, which were marked for training of the counting officials back then. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 16 a video of some men standing on a goods carrier, purportedly holding EVMs in their hands. The background audio claimed that it was a scam by the BJP. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The video has been widely shared on X too. Three such posts can be seen here, here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the posts, which mentioned that the video was old. Here is a screenshot of the same Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of Oneindia News on March 9, 2022. The description of the video read: "The counting of votes for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections is set to begin on Thursday and yet again the EVM issue has been brought out. BJP's biggest opposition in UP, Samajwadi Party's chief, Akhilesh Yadav has accused and alleged that EVMs have been stolen from a counting centre in Varanasi district of Uttar Pradesh." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the viral video with the one shared on YouTube. On further investigating, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of the CEO Office, Uttar Pradesh carrying a press release giving clarification on the incident. The caption of the post, dated March 8, 2022 read: "उत्तर प्रदेश विधानसभा सामान्य निर्वाचन - 2022 जनपद वाराणसी में आज 8 मार्च 2022 को कुछ इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वोटिंग मशीनों को गाड़ी में ले जाने के संबंध में प्रेस विज्ञप्ति जारी...#ECI#AssemblyElections2022" An English translation of the caption read: "Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly General Election - 2022. Press release issued regarding carrying some electronic voting machines in a vehicle in Varanasi district today on 8 March 2022… #ECI#AssemblyElections2022" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the press release, the report sent by the officer found that the EVMs were marked for training of the counting officers in the district. The EVMs were taken from storage in a separate food warehouse to the training ground at UP College. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search and came across a report by the Times of India published on March 10, 2022. The title of the report read, "Uttar Pradesh elections: Row over EVMs ends after clearance of ECI officials." Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video from an incident dating back to 2022 UP Assembly polls was shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of wrestlers claiming they were stopped from watching IPL match shared as recent on social media with misleading claims
content: New Delhi, May 21 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Indian wrestlers Bajrang Punia, Sakshi Malik and Vinesh Phogat, in which they claim that they were stopped by the police from watching an IPL match at Delhi's Feroz Shah Kotla Ground (Arun Jaitley Cricket Stadium). In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to May 2023 from an incident during the 16th season of Indian Premier League. The video shared on social media as recent with misleading claims. A group of wrestlers led by Bajrang Punia, Sakshi Malik and Vinesh Phogat staged protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar from January 2023 to mid-June 2023, alleging sexual harassment female wrestlers by BJP MP and the then WFI president Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 16 a video of Indian wrestlers Bajrang Punia, Sakshi Malik and Vinesh Phogat claiming that they were stopped by the police from watching IPL match at Delhi's Feroz Shah Kotla Ground. The caption of the video read, "पहलवानों को दिल्ली में IPL देखने से रोका गया - पहलवान अब क्रिकेट के दर्शक भी नहीं हो सकते। - वो पहलवान जिन्होंने मोदी के प्रिय बृजभूषण शरण सिंह के - खिलाफ आवाज़ उठाई थी। - लाठियां खाई थीं। - यौन उत्पीड़न के खिलाफ संघर्ष छेड़ा था।" An English translation of the caption read, "Wrestlers stopped from watching IPL in Delhi - Wrestlers can no longer even be spectators of cricket. - The wrestler who had raised his voice against Modi's favorite Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. - Was beaten with sticks. - Wage a struggle against sexual harassment." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively: The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and the archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning Google Lens results, the Desk came across a Facebook post shared by the official page of DNA India Hindi on May 21, 2023. The caption of the post read: "पहलवानों को IPL मैच देखने से दिल्ली पुलिस ने रोका, बजरंग-विनेश-साक्षी का दावा #WrestlerProtest #IPL2023 #DNAOriginals" An English translation of the caption read, "Delhi Police stopped wrestlers from watching IPL match, claims Bajrang-Vinesh-Sakshi #WrestlerProtest #IPL2023 #DNAOriginals" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same video as the one being shared in social media posts, claiming it to be related to the ongoing IPL. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Indian Express published on May 21, 2023. The title of the report read: "Wrestlers claim they were denied entry at Feroz Shah Kotla for DC-CSK match; Delhi Police issues denial". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, "Indian wrestlers Bajrang Punia, Sakshi Malik and Vinesh Phogat along with several others had bought tickets for the Delhi Capitals vs Chennai Super Kings (CSK) match. Despite doing so, they were not allowed to enter the stadium. Reacting to the claims made by the wrestlers, a senior police official, as quoted in the report, said that 10-12 wrestlers had come to the stadium to watch the match, whereas only five of them had tickets. Those without tickets or passes were not allowed to enter and watch the match. Subsequently, the Desk found that an old video dating back to May 2023 was shared as recent on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Sonam Wangchuk's remarks on 'plebiscite' shared on social media with misleading claim; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, May 22 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users shared a video of climate activist Sonam Wangchuk claiming that he demanded a referendum for Kashmir. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected short part of Wangchuk's one of the recent interviews was taken out of context and shared on social media with misleading claim. Sonam Wangchuk, a renowned engineer and environmentalist, recently led a 21-day fast in sub-zero temperatures over his demands of statehood for Ladakh and its inclusion in the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution, among others. Claim A Facebook user shared a video on May 19 of Sonam Wangchuk claiming that he demanded a plebiscite for Kashmir. The video's caption read: "True colours of Magsaysay Award now coming out... Dubious Activist Sonam Wangchuk in Leh demanding a plebiscite for Kashmir. Now, he has become a separatist. The environmentalist was just a mask." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here , and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Twitter. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search with specific keywords and found the complete version of Wangchuk's interview, whose clip was shared on social media. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: While watching the 15:35-minute video, the Desk found the viral video clip from a 14:50-minute timestamp. In the extended video, Wangchuk discusses the Sixth Schedule and its importance. At the timestamp of 14:23 minutes, the interviewer asks Sonam about his views on the residents of Kargil who continue to associate strongly with Kashmir, to which he responds, "So this is what I was asking that people can have their views. But if it is of the whole region or population… then we will pray and work hard to ensure it happens. Be it any area in the world… it should be happy; people should be free to go where they want. So that's why you must have heard about referendums and plebiscites. So, if everyone thinks the same, why not in Kashmir?" It is worth mentioning here that representatives from the Leh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), which represent the social, political and religious groups of the two areas, have held a series of meetings with a high-powered committee of the Union home ministry over their demands for 6th Schedule implementation, statehood, job reservation, a separate public service commission for Ladakh and two parliamentary seats for Leh and Kargil. In the next part of its investigation, the Desk scanned Sonam Wangchuk's official social media handles (Twitter and Facebook) and came across a video in which he clarified the viral video. The caption of the post, dated May 20, 2024, read: "Sad to see my statement being twisted beyond recognition. But I can understand how the doctored version of my video could be misunderstood when taken out of its context. Please spread truth, not lies. Satyamev jayate" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report from The Week on May 20. The report's title was "Did not make any statement on Kashmir Sonam Wangchuk on claims he sought referendum." Here is the link to the report: According to the report, Sonam Wangchuk told PTI that his statement was twisted and he was quoted out of context. The activist stated that, "A politician from Kargil said Ladakh should be re-merged with Kashmir. I objected to that and said it was ok if this was his personal view, but if all people of Kargil feel this way, they can do that. But Ladakh will continue to be a UT. We are not interested in re-merging with Kashmir. That was the context. A small clip from that (interview) was shown in a way that appeared I was talking about Kashmir and giving an anti-national statement." Responding to a question on views expressed by some leaders in Kargil on re-merging with Jammu and Kashmir if statehood is not granted, Wangchuk had said, "It may be the personal opinion of some people. But if someone feels they want to return to J&K, the government can look at it." Subsequently, PTI reached out to Wangchuk for his reaction to the viral video. "It's sad when statements are twisted and small clips are circulated, whether with me or with Amit Shah ji, as happened recently. Twisting statements is not right. I have not said anything on Kashmir," he told PTI. Here is the link to the video of his response, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk found that a selected portion of Wangchuk's interview was taken out of context and shared on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this photo doesn't show Rahul Gandhi holding Chinese Constitution; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 23 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi holding a red book in his hand, which they claimed was the Chinese Constitution. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Gandhi held the coat pocket edition of the Constitution of India, and not the Chinese Constitution. The photo was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 17 a photo of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi holding a red book in his hand, which the user claimed was the Chinese Constitution. The caption of the post read, "भारत के संविधान की मूल प्रति का कवर नीला है।चीन के मूल संविधान का कवर लाल है।क्या राहुल के पास चीनी संविधान है? हमें इसकी पुष्टि करनी होगी। ये संविधान बचाना नही बल्कि बदलना चाहती है।" An English translation of the caption read, "The cover of the original copy of the Constitution of India is blue. The cover of the original copy of the Constitution of China is red. Does Rahul have the Chinese Constitution? We will have to confirm this. It does not want to save the Constitution but wants to change it." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk searched social media platforms with relevant keywords and found that several users had shared the photo with the same claim. Three such Facebook posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively: The photo was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and the archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an IANS report, carried by one AP7AM on May 5. The title of the report read: "This election being fought to protect Constitution, reservations: Rahul Gandhi" Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Rahul Gandhi reiterated BJP's allegations to change the Constitution and scrap the reservation while the INDIA bloc is trying to protect it. while displaying a pocket-size copy of the Constitution of India. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Rahul Gandhi on May 5. The description of the video read, "Lok Sabha 2024 Campaign | Public Meeting | Gadwal, Telangana" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two visuals: We then came across a PTI photo of Rahul Gandhi holding the same book, from his public rally in Delhi on May 22. Below is a screenshot of the same: As highlighted in the photo, it mentions 'Constitution of India' and 'EBC'. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across the website of Eastern Book Company (EBC) mentioning Coat Pocket Edition of The Constitution of India by Gopal Sankaranarayanan. The book resembled Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning, the Desk found that several leaders, including PM Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Madhya Pradesh Governor Mangubhai Chhaganbhai Patel had also received the same pocket-size Indian Constitution in the past. The Desk came across a report published by The Statesman. The title of the report read: "PM Modi meets President Ram Nath Kovind." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a photo of Rahul Gandhi holding a red-covered coat pocket edition of the Constitution of India shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of PM Modi talking about President Murmu is digitally altered; social media posts shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 23 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): A video of PM Modi purportedly making remarks on President Droupadi Murmu's skin colour is being widely shared on social media. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a cropped video of PM Modi was digitally altered and shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 15 a video of PM Modi, claiming that he made remarks on the skin colour of President Droupadi Murmu. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first watched the video clip and noticed several audio and visuals jumps in it. We then ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of BJP on May 8. The description of the video read: "LIVE:PM Shri Narendra Modi addresses public meeting in Warangal, Telangana | Lok Sabha Election 2024" Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that it was the complete version of the PM's speech, from which a clip was shared on social media. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 43 minutes 40 seconds, and was edited in a way to make it sound like the PM commented on the dark complexion of President Draupadi Murmu. In the extended video, PM says, "Today I got to know that the 'shehzada' (referring to Rahul Gandhi) has an uncle (Sam Pitroda) in America. This Prince's uncle is his philosopher and guide. And just like cricket has a third umpire these days, if there is a confusion they ask the third umpire, similarly if the prince has any confusion he takes advice from him." Adding to this, the PM says: "This prince's philosopher and guide uncle has revealed a big secret. He said that those who have black skin color, all of them are from Africa. That means all of you, he abused all the people of my country based on the skin color. Then I understood that seeing the color of the skin, he assumed that Draupadi Murmu is also from Africa and if her skin is black she should be defeated." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a PTI report carried by The Hindu, published on May 8, 2024. The title of the report read: "PM Modi slams Congress over Sam Pitroda's 'skin colour' remarks, hits out at Rahul Gandhi" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion from PM Modi's public rally was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming man attacked in video was Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann are false; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 24 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a mob attacking a man wearing turban, claiming that he was Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. In its investigation, the Desk found that the man in the video was one Amandeep Singh Boparai, president of an outfit named Yuva Jatt Sabha, who was attacked in Jammu in April this year. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 13 a video of a group of men attacking a man wearing turban and policemen struggling to save him. The user claimed that the man beaten up was Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. The caption of the post read: "देखो मुख्यमंत्री भगवत मान कि कैसे पिटाई हुई है!" An English translation of the caption read, "See how Chief Minister Bhagwat Mann has been beaten!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. Several X users also shared the video with the same claim. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video posted on Facebook by one JK Rozana News, on April 13, 2024. The caption of the post read, "Breaking Jammu - युवा जाट सभा की रैली मे हुआ हंगामा Amandeep Singh Boparai Page पर हुआ हमला @followers JK Rozana News" An English translation of the caption read, "Breaking Jammu - Uproar in Yuva Jat Sabha rally, Amandeep Singh Boparai Page attacked @followers JK Rozana News" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same video as the one shared on social media. Below is a combination image, showing the sequence of events from the same incident. Further, the Desk scanned the social media handles of Amandeep Singh Boparai (Twitter and Facebook) and came across another video posted by him, giving details about the incident. The caption of the Facebook livestream video, dated April 13, read: "It was Pre planned attack on Yuva Jatt Sabha Jammu Kashmir rally to create Hindu Sikh rift during elections. #yuvajattsabha #jammu" Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Punjab Kesari regarding the same incident. The title of the report read: "युवा जाट सभा:- पाकिस्तान की साज़िश पर युवा जाट सभा की रैली में हुआ हंगामा" An English translation to the post read, "Yuva Jat Sabha:- Ruckus in the rally of Yuva Jat Sabha over Pakistan's conspiracy" Here is the link and archive link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk found that the man getting attacked in the viral video was Amandeep Singh Boparai, the president of Yuva Jatt Sabha, and not Bhagwant Mann.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video falsely linked to Singapore Airlines turbulence incident; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 24 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed passengers panicking during the recent turbulence incident on a Singapore Airlines plane. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an unrelated video of turbulence on a Mallorca flight, dating back to August 2023, was shared as recent, falsely linking it to a recent incident. On May 21, a Singapore Airlines Boeing 777-312ER operating as Flight 321, flying a scheduled passenger flight from London Heathrow Airport to Singapore Changi Airport carrying 229 occupants on board, encountered severe turbulence over Myanmar, resulting in one death and seventy-one injuries. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 21 a video, claiming that it showed passengers panicking during the incident of turbulence in a London-Singapore airplane, which happened the same day. The caption of the post read: "Singapore Airlines cabin footage exposed## Singapore Airlines forced landing cabin stewardess nosebleeds and meals scattered all over the floor#] On the 21st local time, a Singapore Airlines passenger plane encountered severe turbulence on its way from Heathrow Airport in the United Kingdom to Changi Airport in Singapore. At 15:45, the flight was diverted to Bangkok Suvarnabhumi Airport. According to Thai media reports, the death toll on board has now risen to 2. # Singapore Airlines passenger plane deaths rise to 2# The passenger plane involved was a Boeing 777-300 passenger plane, 16 years old. #CreditToTheOwner" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by one 'KLTV 7' on August 29, 2023. The description of the video read: "A flight to Palma, Majorca was forced to land in Alicante, Spain after weather conditions caused extreme turbulence. Credit: @estelaorts / BON VOYAGED /TMX" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the two videos – one shared on social media and the other uploaded on YouTube. Below are two combination images, highlighting the same: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Independent on August 29, 2023. The title of the report read, "Passengers captured screaming as Mallorca flight experiences severe turbulence amid fierce winds" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the flight took off from Alicante and was expected to land in Mallorca, Spain. In the middle of the journey, the plane was hit with severe turbulence. One of the passengers on the plane described that after the flight took off, it experienced a slight shake, but gradually it got worse. As the situation worsened, the pilot landed in Alicante. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of turbulence in a Mallorca-bound flight was falsely linked to the recent incident on a Singapore Airline plane going from London to Singapore. In the next part of investigation, we tried to check the veracity of another video that was shared by one of the users. The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a report by NDTV published on May 21, 2024. The title of the report read, "Horror On Singapore Airlines Flight, Turbulence Kills British Passenger" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the visuals in the report were similar to the visuals of the viral video. Below is a combination of images, comparing the viral video to the visuals carried by the news report. This proved that the second video was genuine and it actually showed the aftermath of the recent turbulence on the Singapore Airlines plane.

title: Mallikarjun Kharge didn't say 'Congress is over'; Clipped video of his speech shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 25 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users shared a video of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge's election rally speech with a claim that he said -- "Congress is dead and you will not see Congress anywhere now" -- during his address. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a clipped video of Kharge's recent election rally speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with the misleading claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 14 a video of Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge in which he can be heard saying, "Congress is over, Congress is dead and you will not see Congress anywhere now." The caption of the video read, "अबकी बार कांग्रेस मुक्त सरकार# मल्लिकार्जुन खड़गे #मोदीकापरिवार #" An English translation of the caption read, "This time Congress free government # Mallikarjun Khadge #मोदीकापरिवार #" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk watched the video and noticed several audio and visuals jumps in it. We then ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and extracted several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Congress on May 3. The description of the video read: "LIVE: Congress President Shri Mallikarjun Kharge addresses the public in Ahmedabad, Gujarat." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that it was the complete version of Kharge's speech. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 14:38 minutes, which made it look like Kharge spoke against his own party. In the extended video, the party president says, "So I would like to say that the foundation of Congress party in Ahmedabad is very strong, nobody can remove it. And nobody can dare to finish it. Some people talk that Congress is finished, Congress is dead, and you will never see Congress anywhere. The leaders here talk about… " Adding to this, Kharge says, "I just want to ask this to the leaders that Ahmedabad is the holy place of Mahatma Gandhi but it is surprising that at this place people of such ideology are born who are planning to finish Gandhiji's ideologies…" Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a clipped video of Kharge's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi did not refer to one of 'Panj Pyare' as his 'uncle'; video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressing a public rally is being widely shared on social media, claiming he said that one of the 'Panj Pyare' of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the tenth and last human Sikh Guru, was his uncle. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that PM Modi didn't refer to the 'Panj Pyare' as his "uncle", but said that one of them was from Dwarka (referring to Bhai Mohkam Singh). A clipped video of PM's speech was shared on social media with false claim. The term 'Panj Pyare' refers to a collective name given to five men − Bhai Daya Singh, Bhai Dharam Singh, Bhai Himmat Singh, Bhai Mohkam Singh and Bhai Sahib Singh – by Guru Gobind Singh Ji during the historic and monumental assembly at Anandpur Sahib in the Punjab region of India on March 30, 1699. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 26 a video of PM Modi's public rally claimed that he referred to one of the 'Panj Pyare' of Guru Gobind Singh Ji as his uncle. "Narendra Modi has claimed out of the " Panch Pyare" of Guru Gobind Singh one of them was his uncle," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk started the investigation by scanning social media platforms for similar claims, and found that the same video was shared by several others Facebook users as well. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The same video was shared by several X users too with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running of the keyframes through Google Lens, we came across an X post, shared by Punjab BJP on May 23. We noticed that the video in the post was an extended version of the video shared on social media. "Fateh Rally: Huge enthusiasm among the public People's voice Punjab with Modi ji June 4 crossed 400," read an English translation of the caption in Punjabi. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We listened to the video and noticed PM Modi saying, "Leave about being Prime Minister, I am related to you by blood. One of the 'Panj Pyare' of Guru Gobind Singh Ji was from my Dwarka. I am related to you by blood." The Desk further scanned the search results and found that the full video of the PM's public rally in Patiala was uploaded on YouTube from the official channel of Narendra Modi on May 23. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and noticed that the viral video was clipped from 36:42 minutes timestamp, where PM can clearly be heard referring to one of the 'Panj Pyare' being from Dwarka (present-day Gujarat). Even in the viral video, the PM can be clearly heard saying that one of the 'Panj Pyare' was from Dwarka. Nowhere can be heard referring him as his "uncle". In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and found that Bhai Mohkam Singh – the fourth of the five 'Panj Pyare' of Guru Gobind Singh Ji was born in Dwarka on June 6, 1663. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected part of PM Modi's recent election rally speech in Punjab's Patiala was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Six-year-old video of Mohan Bhagwat praising Congress shared as recent on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, May 27 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat with a claim that he recently praised Congress for their contribution to India's freedom movement. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video clip shared in social media posts was a part of an old video dating back to 2018. A smaller part of video of his 2018 speech was shared as recent. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 22 shared a video of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat in which he can be heard praising Congress for their contribution to India's freedom movement. The caption of the post read, "Mohan Bhagwat Praises Congress party" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results the Desk came across a video on Facebook uploaded by the official page of The Indian Express on September 18, 2018. The caption of the post read: "RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat said that Congress' ideology played an instrumental role in bringing the people of this country on the path to freedom." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same video as the one shared on social media recently. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of NDTV on September 18, 2018. The description of the video read: "If an outreach was the aim, reach out it did. Mohan Bhagwat, chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh, opened a three-day conclave in Delhi today with a rare conciliatory tone for one of its harshest critics. "In the form of the Congress, a huge freedom movement fledged in the nation. It too gave birth to a number of all-sacrificing great personalities who continue to inspire us today. That movement managed to inspire ordinary people to join the freedom struggle. It had a huge hand in us achieving Independence," he said." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos, which shows that they are same. "In the form of the Congress, a huge freedom movement fledged in the nation. It too gave birth to a number of all-sacrificing great personalities who continue to inspire us today. That movement managed to inspire ordinary people to join the freedom struggle. It had a huge hand in us achieving Independence," said the RSS chief. Subsequently, the Desk found that an old video dating back to 2018 was shared as recent on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of crowd gathered at PM Modi's election rally falsely shared in name of Rahul Gandhi's rally; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 27 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of an aerial view of a crowd, which they claimed had gathered to attend Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's election rally. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from PM Modi's rally in Bihar's Maharajganj, which was held on May 21. It was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of an aerial view of a large gathering with a claim that the people had gathered to attend Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's rally. The caption of the post read, "ये जनसैलब देख कर मोदी जी को पता चल गया होगा कौन है राहुल ?" An English translation of the caption read: "Seeing this crowd, Modi Ji must have realized who Rahul is?" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and their archive versions can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning, the Desk came across another X post shared by the official handle of PM Modi on May 21, carrying the same video. The caption of the post read: "महाराजगंज में उमड़ा जनसैलाब बता रहा है कि बिहार में भाजपा-एनडीए को यहां के मेरे परिवारजनों का अभूतपूर्व आशीर्वाद मिल रहा है!" An English translation of the caption read: "The huge crowd in Maharajganj is telling that BJP-NDA in Bihar is getting unprecedented blessings from my family members here!" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report by TV9 Hindi published on May 21. The title of the report read, "बिहार:महाराजगंज में PM मोदी की रैली, उमड़ा जनसैलाब,मिला जबरदस्त जनसमर्थन" An English translation to the title read, "Bihar: PM Modi's rally in Maharajganj, crowd gathered, got tremendous public support."
