Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, PM Modi addressed rallies in Motihari and Maharajganj. A huge crowd gathered to listen to PM Modi. During the rally, the PM fiercely targeted the INDIA block and its allies. Subsequently, the Desk found that the video of crowd was from PM Modi's rally, and not Rahul Gandhi.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, the painting behind Rahul and Sonia Gandhi is not of Jesus Christ; photo shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 28 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): Multiple social media users shared a photo of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi taking a selfie with his mother Sonia Gandhi after having voted in the sixth phase of Lok Sabha polls, and claimed that there was a painting of Jesus Christ in his room, and not of any Hindu god. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the painting was not of Jesus Christ, but one titled 'Madonna Oriflamma' created by Russian painter Nicholas Roerich. The viral photo was shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 25 a photo of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Sonia Gandhi showing their inked fingers after casting their votes. The user further claimed that the leader had a painting of Jesus Christ and not of any Hindu god. The caption of the post read, "जनेऊधारी ब्राह्मण राहुल गांधी के कमरे में किसी हिंदू देवी देवता की नहीं बल्कि जीजस की तस्वीर है , बैक ग्राउंड देखें" An English translation to the caption read, "In the room of the sacred thread Brahmin Rahul Gandhi, there is a picture of Jesus and not of any Hindu deity, see the background." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran a screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several users had shared the same claim. Three such Facebook posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be viewed here , here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on X. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and their archive versions can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning, the Desk came across an X post by a handle named 'X Breaking News' which carried the same painting as in the viral post. The post was regarding clarification on the viral social posts, stating that the painting behind Rahul and Sonia Gandhi was not of Jesus Christ, but Nicholas Roerich's 'Madonna Oriflamma'. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a blog on a website, that featured the same painting. The title of the blog, published in August 2017, read: "Cozumel, One Circle, Three Red Dots" Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the painting in the viral photo and the one featured in the blog post. Below is a screenshot comparing the two photos: According to the post, the geometrical figure on the cloth-like thing held by the lady in the painting was the Banner of Peace. "The world peace flag is based on a design by Russian artist and mystic Nikolái Roerich, who proposed the red circle with three dots inside as an international symbol to mark museums, schools, and similar cultural landmarks to prevent destruction by aerial bombs (World War I era). The idea was similar to the large red cross marking hospitals and medical tents in war zones ... similarly to "prevent" bombing and strafing of helpless patients and medical personnel. William Dunning, 17 March 1998," read a section of the blogpost. Taking a cue from the blogpost, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across the official website of 'Nicholas Roerich Museum New York'. A blogpost on the website mentioned about the Banner of Peace, its origin and relevance. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the painting in the viral photo does not depict Jesus Christ.

title: PTI Fact Check: Fake video of Aaj Tak anchor Sudhir Chaudhary 'predicting AAP candidate's victory' in LS polls shared on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 28 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video that showed Aaj Tak anchor Sudhir Chaudhary predicting AAP candidate Mahabal Mishra's victory from West Delhi seat in the ongoing Lok Sabha polls. Meanwhile, the graphic of a purported exit poll displayed alongside predicted AAP's win in three out of seven seats in the national capital. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of Sudhir Chaudhary was digitally altered using his voice clone and was shared along with fake graphics on social media. Aaj Tak or TV Today Network have not released any exit polls for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections yet. Under Section 126A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, exit polls are regulated to ensure fair conduct. This section prohibits the conduct and dissemination of exit polls between the start of polling and half an hour after the last phase of voting concludes across all states. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 23 a video of Aaj Tak news anchor Sudhir Chaudhary, in which he can be heard predicting AAP's Lok Sabha candidate Mahabal Mishra's victory from West Delhi seat. Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the viral video and noticed a lip-sync issue in it. We then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such Facebook posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on X too. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Aaj Tak on May 16. The description of the video read: "लोकसभा चुनाव के बीच प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने आजतक से खास बातचीत की. इस दौरान उन्होंने कहा कि मैंने 100 दिन का एजेंडा प्लान कर लिया है. मैं इसमें 25 दिन और जोड़ना चाहता हूं. इसे पूरी तरह यूथ पर फोकस करूंगा कि आप मुझे आइडिया दीजिए. मुझे अपनी प्रायोरिटी बताइए, जिस पर मैं 25 दिन पूरी तरह से डेडिकेट करना चाहता हूं. उन्होंने कहा कि मैं 100 दिन को आगे बढ़ा रहा हूं, अब सवा सौ दिन के एजेंडे पर काम करूंगा." An English translation to the description read: "Amidst the Lok Sabha elections, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had a special conversation with Aaj Tak. During this he said that I have planned an agenda for 100 days. I want to add 25 more days to it. I will focus it completely on youth so you give me ideas. Tell me your priority on which I want to dedicate 25 days completely. He said that I am extending the 100 days, now I will work on the agenda of 125 days." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that striking similarities between the visuals of the YouTube video and the one shared on social media. Below is a combination image, comparing the two visuals: In the 8:42-hour video, Chaudhary can be heard talking about PM Narendra Modi's interview along with the details about AAP leader Swati Maliwal's assault case against Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal's personal secretary, Bibhav Kumar. Nowhere did Chaudhary talk about the Delhi exit poll survey at any point during the programme. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find out if any such report on any exit poll survey conducted by the channel. During our research, we also came across an X post from Election Commission of India's guidelines prohibiting the release of exit poll results until the conclusion of polling in the final phase, which will be at 6:30 p.m. on June 1. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video was made using voice clone of Sudhir Chaudhary and fake graphics.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Amit Shah claiming he spoke against 'Modi's guarantees' is edited; Claim shared in social media is false
content: New Delhi, May 29 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Many social media users shared a video of BJP leader and Union Minister Amit Shah with a claim that he spoke against 'Modi's guarantees, and said' "guarantee means nothing, they talk till elections, then forget everything." In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a small part of Shah's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 23 a video of Union Minister Amit Shah in which he can be heard saying, "that's why I say, guarantee means nothing, they talk till elections, then forget everything." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video of Amit Shah's interview to a news agency. The caption of the video read: "Amit Shah's full interview on PoK, NDA seat prediction, Mamata, Swati Maliwal-Kejriwal & more" Here is the link to the video: The Desk found that it was the complete version of Shah's speech. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 25:14 minutes, which made it look like Shah spoke against PM Modi's guarantees. In the extended video, Shah responds to a query on why he called Congress' guarantees 'Chinese.' To this, the Union Minister replied: "I went to Telangana recently, there I saw women waiting for their 12,000 rupees, farmers waiting for loan waiver of 2 lakh rupees. The young girls are waiting for their scooty which Rahul ji promised, he gave the guarantee and now people are looking for him. " The interviewer further asks, "Now the elections are over in the South, Rahul ji has come to the North." Adding to this Shah says, "He has come to the North but he used to go when there were elections in the South. So, that is why I say that his guarantees have no meaning, he talks about them till the elections and then forgets them." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Shah's speech was taken out of context shared on social media with false claim

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan did not post anything on Rahul Gandhi from his X handle recently; this viral screenshot is fake
content: New Delhi, May 29 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a purported X post by actor Shah Rukh Khan was shared by many social media users. "Congress leader Rahul Gandhi will be the next prime minister of India," read the alleged X post by the actor. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the screenshot shared on social media was imaginary and fake. The actor has not published anything recently on the Congress leader. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 25 a screenshot of a purported X post by Shah Rukh Khan, which claimed that Rahul Gandhi will be the next prime minister. The caption of the post read: "अबतो शाहरुख खान ने भी कहदिया राहुल गांधी ही प्रधानमंत्री बनेंगे...." An English translation to the caption read, "Now Shahrukh Khan also said Rahul Gandhi will become the Prime Minister...." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned social media platforms and found that several other users had shared the same screenshot with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to one such post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The screenshot was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be viewed here , here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any report regarding any such social media post. In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the official X handle of the actor but could not find any such post by him. As can be seen in the screenshot above, Khan shared only post in the month of May, in which he urged people of Maharashtra to exercise their franchise and cast vote in the state in the fifth phase of Lok Sabha polls held on May 20. The Desk also checked the account's activity log on Social Blade, a social media analytics website, and found that no post was deleted recently. Below is a screenshot showing the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake screenshot was shared on social media in the name of Shah Rukh Khan

title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake Alert! Digitally-altered video of Columbian model in swimwear shared on social media in name of actress Rashmika Mandanna; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 30 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) Social media users shared a video of a female model posing in red-colour swimwear near a waterfall claiming the woman in the footage was Indian actress Rashmika Mandanna. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman in the video was Colombian model named Daniela Villarreal. Her video was digitally altered to superimpose Rashmika Mandanna's face on it and share on social media with a false claim. The deepfake goes viral just six months after Mandanna fell prey to the deepfake technology, when her morphed video showing her in black shorts and a top with a plunging neckline went viral. Claim An Instagram user shared on May 17 a video of a woman wearing red bikini and posing near a waterfall and claimed that she was Indian actor Rashmika Mandanna. Here is the link and archive link of the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk noticed several discrepancies on the face and the eye of the actor. Below is a combination of screengrabs from the viral video, which highlight the same: The Desk also noticed several users questioning the authenticity of the video, and claiming that it was edited using AI technology. Below is a screenshot to one such comment: Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post with the same video posted by DANIELA VILLARREAL, a model and content creator, on April 19. The caption of the post read, "Nice place." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the two videos. Below is a combination image showing the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through Hive , a deepfake video detection tool. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a Colombian model's video was digitally altered and Rashmika's face was morphed on it to create the viral deepfake.

author: Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: This video of AAP leader Atishi announcing discontinuation of power subsidy scheme is old and edited; Details inside
content: New Delhi, May 30 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Delhi minister and AAP leader Atishi was shared on social media with a claim that she allegedly talked about AAP government's decision to cancel the power subsidy scheme in the national capital. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an edited version of an old video dating back to April 2023 was shared on social media with the false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 26 a video of Delhi Minister Atishi, in which she was heard saying that the AAP government had decided to cancel the power subsidy scheme in the national capital. Meanwhile, the text running on the video read that 'free electricity ends in Delhi'. The caption of the video read, "लो भाई उतर गया बुखार people who voted for freebies deserved this. Freebies are a sure recipe for economic disaster" An English translation of the caption read, "The fever is gone. People who voted for freebies deserved this. Freebies are a sure recipe for economic disaster." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: "The power subsidy for 46 lakh families in the national capital ends today, which means from tomorrow subsidized electricity bills will not be provided. Those previously receiving zero bills will see an increase, and those with 50 per cent subsidy will face higher bills," Atishi says in the video. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the posts which mentioned that the video was old. Below is a screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an X post by the official handle of Aam Aadmi Party on April 14, 2023. The caption of the post read, "LG ने दिल्ली की मुफ़्त बिजली रोकी‼️ 46 लाख परिवारों, किसानों, वकीलों और 1984 दंगा पीड़ितों को FREE Bijli मिलनी बंद हो जाएगी Delhi Govt की बिजली Subsidy की File LG लेकर बैठ गए हैं, Tata, BSES ने चिट्ठी लिखी—उनके पास सब्सिडी की सूचना नहीं आई तो वो Billing शुरू करेंगे" An English translation of the caption read, "LG stopped free electricity in Delhi‼️ 46 lakh families, farmers, lawyers and 1984 riot victims will stop getting free electricity. LG has taken the file of Delhi Govt's electricity subsidy, Tata, BSES wrote a letter - If they do not get information about subsidy, they will start billing." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk found that this was the complete version of Atishi's speech. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the extended video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp from 0:14 minutes and 0:51 minutes. Atishi can be heard saying that the government needs to cancel the subsidy due to LG's pending decision. In the extended video, Atishi says, "Today I am going to hold a press conference on a very serious issue. An issue which is a topic of concern for 46 lakh families in Delhi. From today, the electricity subsidy for 46 lakh families will be stopped which the government of Arvind Kejriwal gives to the people of Delhi." Further in the video, she says, "This means that from tomorrow, the consumers will not get a subsidy on the electricity bills. So, the people who used to get zero bills, from tomorrow they will get electricity at increased prices, people who used to get 50 per cent subsidy will also get electricity at increased prices." Atishi then elaborates on the reasons behind the subsidy withdrawal. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search and came across a video report published by the Times of India on April 14, 2023. The title of the report read: "Delhiites not to get subsidised electricity bills from tomorrow; 46 lakh families to be impacted". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk found that a year-old video of Atishi was clipped and shared on social media as recent with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, man with Kangana Ranaut in viral photo is not gangster Abu Salem; 2017 photo shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, May 31 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo of actor and BJP leader Kangana Ranaut claiming the man standing with her was gangster Abu Salem. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the man in the photo was a journalist named Mark Manuel. A seven-year-old photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X user shared on May 28 a photo of Kangana Ranaut with a man, claiming that he was gangster Abu Salem. The caption of the post read: "भक्तों की झाँसी की रानी " An English translation of the post read: "Jhansi ki Rani of bhakts". Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several users had shared the same claim. Two such X posts can be found here and here and archive versions of the same can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning, the Desk came across a Facebook post shared by Mark Manuel on September 15, 2017. The post carried the same photo with a long caption. In his post, Manuel mentioned that the photo was taken "at the Korner House in Khar some months ago. It was at a champagne brunch to celebrate Kangana's film 'Simran' that releases today." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk further scanned the profile of Mark Manuel and found the latter works as an Editorial Writer at HuffPost. Here is the link to the profile and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by the Huffpost published on September 24, 2017. The title of the report read, "Kangana Ranaut Should Realise She's Too Talented To Milk Her Personal Life For Attention" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk compared photo of man in the viral picture with one of Abu Salem, and found that the two had no physical or facial resemblance. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a journalist named Mark Manuel, seen in a photo with Kangana, was falsely identified as gangster Abu Salem.

title: PTI Fact Check: Audio clip shared in name of telephonic conversation between AAP MP Swati Maliwal and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee is AI-generated, Claim shared in social media posts is fake
content: New Delhi, June 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A purported recording of an alleged telephonic conversation between AAP MP Swati Maliwal and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was shared on social media with a claim that both of them talked about the assault case she filed against Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal's aide Vibhav Kumar. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral audio clip is AI-generated voice clones of Atishi and Rathee, and was shared on social media with a false claim. On May 13, Swati Maliwal alleged that she was assaulted by Arvind Kejriwal's aide Bibhav Kumar at the Chief Minister's residence in Delhi. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 25 a video of a purported call recording between AAP leader Swati Maliwal and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, in which the former can be heard saying that she was assaulted at the behest of Delhi CM's wife Sunita Kejriwal. The caption of the video read, "दिल्ली स्वाति मालिवाल और ध्रुव राठी का बिडियो हुआ वायरल स्वाति मालिवाल ने ध्रुव राठी को आप के कहने बिडियो नही बनाने को कहा केजरीवाल और सुनिता के कहने पर हुआ पिटाई घ्रूव बिपक्ष के एजेंडे पर बनाता है बिडियो" An English translation of the caption read, "Delhi Swati Maliwal and Dhruv Rathi's video went viral Swati Maliwal asked Dhruv Rathi not to make videos as per your request. Beating happened at the behest of Kejriwal and Sunita Ghruv makes video on opposition's agenda" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk listened to the audio and noticed several discrepancies in it. Also, several words were repeatedly pronounced. Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions of the same can be found here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the posts, claiming that the post was fake and action should be taken against it. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk again listened to the audio closely, and found that discrepancies which suggested that it might be fake or digitally created. At 00:07 and 00:09 seconds, jump-cuts and overlaying of voices of Rathee and Maliwal can be clearly noticed. The Desk then ran the viral video through Itisaar, an AI detection tool developed in collaboration with IIT Jodhpur. The tool confirmed that the audio was AI generated and conclusively fake with a high confidence level. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake AI-generated audio clip was shared with the claim that it was the recording of telephonic conversation between Swati Maliwal and Dhruv Rathee.

title: PTI Fact Check: This 'Amritsar LS seat exit poll' screenshot shared in name of news channel India Today is fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a purported exit poll survey allegedly by a news channel named India Today for Amritsar Lok Sabha seat was shared on social media with the claim that the BJP candidate will win from the prestigious Punjab seat. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the screenshot was fake and the claim shared with the fake screenshot in social media posts was false. The TV Today Group has not released its exit poll data for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections yet following the guidelines by the Election Commission of India. Under Section 126A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, exit polls are regulated to ensure fair conduct. This section prohibits the conduct and dissemination of exit polls between the start of polling and half an hour after the last phase of voting concludes across all states. For the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, media houses and agencies are allowed to release the exit poll data only after 6:30 pm on June 1, after the conclusion of seventh and final phase of voting. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on May 27 a screenshot of a purported exit poll survey by India Today, predicting a vote share lead for the BJP in Amritsar in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. The screenshot was shared with the claim that BJP candidate Taranjit Singh Sandhu was set to win from the Lok Sabha seat. The caption of the post read, "It's @SandhuTaranjitS for Amritsar" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several users had shared the same claim. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post by the official page of India Today on March 7, 2022. The caption of the post read, "The BJP is set to get an impressive vote share of 46 per cent in Uttar Pradesh, according to India Today-Axis My India exit poll. The Samajwadi Party too is expected to improve its share while the BSP may suffer a big loss #IndiaTodayAxisExitPoll #ExitPoll #Elections2022 #DIU" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same template of exit polls as used in the viral photo. Below is a screenshot comparing both: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found an X post by Rahul Kanwal, News Director at India Today. Kanwal called out the viral screenshot as fake. The caption of the post read: "We realise that there's a lot of interest in the results of the @IndiaToday Axis My India exit poll. But please be certain that any 'poll' you see before 6:30 pm on June 1 is fake. It's good to have so much buzz around our poll, but we don't want that there be any confusion as a result. BEWARE FAKE POLLS. See you on June 1 at 5 pm." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk found that a fake screenshot was shared on social media in the name of exit poll survey by India Today.

title: PTI Fact Check: Screenshot of boarding pass claiming Rahul Gandhi booked a flight to Bangkok on June 5 is edited and fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 3 (Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a purported boarding pass of a Vistara flight on June 5, allegedly booked for Bangkok in the name of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, was shared on social media recently. The screenshot of the alleged boarding pass was shared on the day various exit poll surveys predicted a landslide victory for the BJP-led NDA in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo of an unrelated boarding pass was digitally altered and shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The counting of votes for the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls is scheduled to be taken up on June 4. Leaders of the BJPM have been claiming that the Congress-led INDIA bloc with face defeat in the elections, and Rahul Gandhi will go on vacation after the announcement of results. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 1 a photo of a purported boarding pass of a flight to Bangkok on June 5, booked in the name of Rahul Gandhi "Rahul Gandhi running away from India on June 5 to Bangkok," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the photo through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: The same photo was widely shared on X too. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed that the purported boarding pass in the photo mentioned two different flight numbers, suggesting that it might have been digitally altered. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: The Desk then further scanned the Google Lens results, and came across a similar photo, carried in a column on 'Live From A Lounge' – a "digital platform renowned for publishing news and views about aviation, hotels, passenger experience, loyalty programs, travel trends and frequent travel tips for the Global Indian." The headline of the column read: "Onboard Vistara To Singapore: The first Vistara international flight ever!" Here is the link to the column, dated August 7, 2019, and below is a screenshot of the same: "Having flown the first flight of Vistara domestically back in 2015, it was a done deal that I was going to fly them internationally as well on the first flight. Finally, the airline announced international operations in July 2019, and the first international flight was operated between Delhi and Singapore yesterday, on which I flew. For various reasons, Vistara decided to fly the Boeing 737 they acquired recently for the flights to Singapore. One reason is that the A320/Neo in the current fleet of Vistara did not have the ability to operate the 5.5 hour flight to Singapore from Delhi," read a section of the column, written by Ajay Awtaney, the founder and editor of Live From A Lounge. We then compared the two photos, and found striking similarities, suggesting that the photo posted by Ajay was digitally altered. In the next part of investigation, the Desk reach out of Ajay Awtaney via email for his comment on the viral. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated photo was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to Rahul Gandhi.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi celebrating with Congress workers at party office falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha poll results; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 04 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra greeting party workers and celebrating at the party headquarters was shared on social media recently with the claim that it happened a day before the counting of votes for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a year-old video of celebrations at Congress office after Supreme Court suspended Rahul Gandhi's conviction in 'Modi surname' remark case was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to the recently concluded Lok Sabha elections. In 2019, Rahul Gandhi was convicted by a Surat court in a defamation case regarding his 'Modi surname' remark. On August 4, 2023, the Supreme Court suspended Gandhi's conviction, following which the Congress leader was reinstated as Member of Parliament. The Lok Sabha pol results were announced on June 4, in which the BJP-led NDA emerged victorious paving pay for Narendra Modi to take oath as the PM for a third consecutive term. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 3 a video of Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra greeting Congress workers and celebrating at the party headquarters. The caption of the post read, "कांग्रेस पार्टी कार्यालय में आज यानी सोमवार को राहुल गांधी एवं प्रियंका गांधी की मौजूदगी में समर्थकों द्वारा जीत से पहले बांटे गए लड्डू। कल यानी 4 जून को वोटों की गिनती होगी।" An English translation to the post read, "Laddoos were distributed by the supporters before the victory in the presence of Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi in the Congress Party office today i.e. on Monday. Counting of votes will take place tomorrow i.e. on June 4." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Two such videos can be found here and here and their archive versions can be seen here and here respectively. While scanning the results, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of Congress on August 4, 2023. The post carried the same video as was shared in the social media posts. The caption of the post read, "'असत्य पर सत्य की जीत हुई' जय कांग्रेस, विजय कांग्रेस" An English translation of the caption read, "'Truth won over untruth' Jai Congress, Vijay Congress" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Hindu on August 4, 2023. The title of the report read: "Supreme Court stays Rahul Gandhi's conviction in 'Modi surname' remark criminal defamation case" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the Supreme Court on August 4, 2023, stayed the conviction of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi in a criminal defamation case for the 'Modi' surname remark he allegedly made during a political rally in 2019. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to 2023 was shared as recent on social media with false claim

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 photos of Chandrababu Naidu meeting Akhilesh Yadav falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha poll results; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 6 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Some photos of meeting between Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and Telugu Desam Party (TDP) chief N Chandrababu Naidu has been widely shared on social media, with the claim that they recently met to forge a post-poll alliance, following the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo dated back to 2019 from Naidu's visit to Lucknow, which was shared as recent on social media with false claims. Naidu's TDP is part of the BJP-led NDA whereas Yadav's Smaajwadi Party is a partner in the INDIA bloc, led by Congress. With the BJP falling short of the majority mark in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls, it now relies on TDP and Nitish Kumar-led JD(U) to form a coalition government. Claim An Instagram user shared on June 5 a photo of meeting between Samajwadi chief Akhilesh Yadav and TDP chief N Chandrababu Naidu, claiming that they met recently following the announcement of Lok Sabha poll results. The caption of the post read, "BhaktBanerjee be like, Kijiye Meeting Meeting , Kheliye Meeting Meeting..." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that some other photos from the meeting between the two leaders had been shared on social media with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: While scanning the results the Desk came across an X post with a similar photo by the official handle of Akhilesh Yadav on May 18, 2019. The caption of the post read, "It is a pleasure to welcome Hon'ble Chief Minister Shri N Chandrababu Naidu Ji to Lucknow" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the first image in the post was the same as one of the photos shared on social media recently. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the other viral photo through the Google Lens, and came across a report published by Udayavani on May 19, 2019. The title of the report read, "After meeting Rahul, Naidu calls on Akhilesh and Mayawati to consolidate anti-BJP front" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the TDP chief met Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, BSP's Mayawati and SP leader Akhilesh Yadav to discuss the possibility of forming an alliance of all opposition parties, to take on the BJP-led NDA. Subsequently, the Desk found that old photos of meeting Yadav and Naidu were shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of BJP's Navneet Rana crying falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha poll results; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 5 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of BJP leader Navneet Rana crying and being consoled by her husband was recently shared on social media with the claim that she broke down after losing from Amravati seat in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that and old and unrelated video was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 5 a video of BJP leader Navneet Rana crying and being consoled by her husband. The video was shared with the claim that she broke down over her defeat from Amravati seat in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the post read, "इस देश में रहना है तो सबको आदर देना है। ✌️" An English translation of the caption read, "If you want to live in this country, you have to respect everyone." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed the logo of News18 on the vide. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of CNN-News18 on May 5, 2022. The description of the video read: "MP Navneet Rana after being released on bail was rushed to Lilavati Hospital." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: We then conducted another customised keyword search and came across a report by the Hindustan Times published on April 23, 2022. The title of the report read, "Police arrest Rana couple for inciting people" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, MLA Ravi Rana and his wife and Navneet Kaur Rana were arrested by the police in Mumbai on April 23, 2022 after they announced that they will recite the Hanuman Chalisa outside the then-Maharashtra CM Uddhav Thackeray's private residence 'Matoshree' in suburban Bandra, leading to protests by Shiv Sena workers. Subsequently, the Desk found that an old video dating back to 2022 was shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of Yogendra Yadav calling opposition 'useless' falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha poll results
content: New Delhi, June 5 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of activist Yogendra Yadav was shared on social media recently, in which he criticised the opposition, calling it useless. The video was shared with the claim that Yadav was discussing about the recently concluded Lok Sabhs polls, calling it one-sided (in favour of the BJP). In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of an old video of Yadav was shared on social media with false claims. The posts were shared ahead of the announcement of Lok Sabha poll results 2024, in which the BJP-led NDA, despite suffering losses as compared to its 2019 performance, managed to secure majority. Claim An X user shared on June 3 a video of Yogendra Yadav in which was heard criticising the opposition, for not being able to put up a fight against the BJP. The caption of the post read, "Ye to party hi badal liya be 😂😂😂 Kl tk toh Rahul Gandhi ji PM banane jaa rahe the aur bnaa bhaiya rahe the Ab vipkash se moh bhang ho gya hai lagta hai" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several posts carrying the same video with a similar claim. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here, here and here respectively. While going through the comments, the Desk noticed several users mentioning that the viral video was old. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of The Quint on May 19, 2019. The description of the video read: "Reacting to exit polls, Yogendra Yadav said "it is not the people's trust on Modi, but the absence of a reliable face in the Opposition" that could be responsible for the NDA's return in 2019." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that it was the complete version of Yadav's speech. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 02:50 minutes. In the extended video, Yadav can be heard saying: "The big question is, the picture is clear, BJP is leading in this election and I maintain a difference in my hopes and assessments. I and my party, we all believe that if BJP comes into power, it is dangerous for all of us. But thinking this does not mean that one should close their eyes as a pigeon and believe this is not happening." "The truth is that it was a one-sided election, and the opposition was completely useless. After this election, two things came to light, one was that the opposition was completely useless and the media's biased behaviour towards one party. Both the things made this election completely in favour of BJP." In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by NDTV Profit published on May 24, 2019. The title of the report read: "Election Results 2019: Why Yogendra Yadav Thinks Historic Modi Win Is Different From 2014." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of Yogendra Yadav was old and related to the 2019 Lok Sabha poll results.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming BJP won 100 seats with margin of less than 1,000 votes and 30 seats with margin of less than 500 votes are fake
content: New Delhi, June 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared posts claiming the BJP won 30 seats with a margin of 500 votes and 100 seats with margin of 1,000 votes in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls, while raising suspicion on the results of these seats. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the BJP did not win any seat with a margin of less than 500 or even 1,000 votes. The narrowest margin for the BJP was in Odisha's Jajpur where the party candidate won by a margin of 1,587 votes. The social media posts were shared with false claims. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 8 a post claiming that the BJP won 30 seats by a margin of less than 500 votes and another 100 seats by a margin of less than 1,000 votes in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned social media platforms and found that several other users had shared the same claim. Three such Facebook posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archive posts can be seen here , here and here , respectively: The same claim was shared by several users on X too. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively: The Desk then scanned the official website of the Election Commision of India , and found that the BJP did not win any seat with a margin of less than 1,000 votes. The lowest margin for the BJP was in Odisha's Jajpur, where party candidate Rabindra Narayan Behera won by a margin of 1,587 votes. Below is a screenshot showing the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by Deccan Herald. The title of the report read: "Lok Sabha Elections 2024 | Candidates with slimmest victory margin". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The graphical representation also showed that the slimmest victory margin for any BJP candidate was 1,587 in Jajpur, Odisha. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media posts were shared with false claims.

author: Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of TDP supporters burning Chandrababu Naidu's photo falsely linked to 2024 Lok Sabha polls; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 7 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a group of men setting on fire a photo of TDP chief N Chandrababu Naidu was shared on social media, with the claim that people of Andhra Pradesh protested against him for joining the NDA, which is forming the government at the Centre for a third straight term. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video from the runup to the 2024 Andhra Pradesh Assembly elections was shared on social media with false claim. The BJP emerged as the single largest party in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls, and the TDP, with 16 seats in its kitty, has emerged as the biggest alliance partner in the NDA, which is coming back to power for the third straight term at the Centre. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 6 a video of a group of men setting on fire a photo of TDP chief and Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu, and claimed that the people of the state protested against him for joining hands with the BJP following the Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the post read: "Citizens of Andhra Pradesh burning photo frames of Chandrababu Naidu @JaiTDP for supporting @narendramodi. Political experts & leaders foresee that #Modi3.0 will last hardly for 5-6 months or a year maximum." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here, here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here, respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Samayam Telugu on Mar 29, 2024. The description of the video read: "Guntakal TDP workers burned Chandrababu Naidu photo and protest against Gummanur Jayaram" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that this was the extended version of the viral video and noticed striking similarities between them. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The New Indian Express published on Mar 30, 2024. The title of the report read, "Andhra Pradesh: TDP faces strong dissent over choice of candidates in final list" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, after the announcement of TDP candidate Gummanuru Jayaram, the followers of former MLA Jitender Goud reached the party office. They proceeded to throw down chairs, flags, and party-related documents, which they then set on fire to express their resentment towards Naidu's decision. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video was falsely linked to TDP being part of the BJP-led NDA forming government at the Centre.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, man in viral video criticising Ayodhya's Hindus is not from Muslim community; scripted video shared as real on social media
content: New Delhi, June 8 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man wearing a skullcap and criticising Hindus for not voting for PM Modi despite the construction of Ram Mandir in Ayodhya was widely shared on social media. In the video, the man refers himself as a Muslim and refers to Hindus in Ayodhya as "tow-faced". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the man in the viral video was Dhirendra Raghav, a content creator. The scripted video was shared on social media as real with misleading claims. In the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls, the BJP lost the Faizabad Lok Sabha seat, that includes the Assembly seat of Ayodhya. This was a highlight of the polls and also a setback to the BJP, given the fact that the Ram Mandir emerged as a major issue during the runup to the elections. Claim An Instagram user shared on June 5 a video of a man wearing a skullcap and referring himself as a Muslim. He criticised Hindus of Ayodhya and called them 'two-faced' for not voting for PM Modi, despite the construction of Ram Mandir. The caption of the post read, "सुनो अयोध्या वालों इस वीडियो को सुनो उसके बाद चुल्लू पर पानी में डूब जाओ। #अयोध्या #ayodhya #upelection2024" An English translation to the post read, "Listen, people of Ayodhya, listen to this video, after that drown yourself in water. #ayodhya #ayodhya #upelection2024" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the results, the Desk came across an Instagram post carrying the same video, shared on June 5, 2024. The caption of the post read, "मुसलमान बन कर हिंदुओं को गाली देने वाला शख्स असल में खुद हिन्दू है इसका नाम धीरेंद्र राघव है. यह दंगा भड़काने की एक साजिश है इसके ऊपर शख्त से शख्त कार्यवाही की जाए." An English translation of the caption read, "The person who is abusing Hindus by posing as a Muslim is actually a Hindu himself, his name is Dhirendra Raghav. This is a conspiracy to incite riots, strict action should be taken against it." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk found the social media handles of Dhirendra Raghav, in which he mentioned him as an artist. Here are the links to the Instagram and Facebook profiles, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk scanned the entire profile of the latter but did not find the viral video. Further we also checked the account's activity log and found several comments on his recent video. Below is the screenshot of the same In the next part of investigation, the Desk checked the archived version of his Instagram account and found the thumbnail of the now-deleted video. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man posing as a Muslim in the viral video was Dhirendra Raghav, a content creator. A scripted video was shared on social media as real.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of IPS Ashish Kapoor assaulting woman cop shared as recent on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, June 4 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video claiming that it showed IPS officer Ashish Kapoor assaulting a woman police officer who accused him of taking bribe. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video dating back to 2018 was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim An X user shared on June 1 shared a video, claiming that it showed IPS officer Ashish Kapoor assaulting a woman police official for filing a bribery case against him. The caption of post read, "महिला पुलिस ने उगाही का मामला दर्ज कराया तो IPS ने महिला को पीटा। पीटने वाले पुलिस ऑफिसर IPS आशीष कपूर है। "महिला पुलिस पर थप्पड़ बरसाते जांबाज पंजाब पुलिस अधिकारी "आईपीएस आशीष कपूर" की सोशल मीडिया पर जमकर सराहना हो रही है.. वीडियो वायरल है??आपकी क्या राय है!!" An English translation of the caption, "When the woman police registered a case of extortion, the IPS beat the woman. The police officer who beat him is IPS Ashish Kapoor. "The brave Punjab Police officer IPS Ashish Kapoor", who slapped the lady police, is being highly appreciated on social media.. Is the video viral?? What is your opinion!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archive versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such X posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be found here , here and here . On further scanning through Google Lens results, the Desk came across another X post by Gagandeep Singh with a similar video on March 24, 2023. The caption of the post read: "A video of suspended AIG Ashish Kapoor is going viral in which he is seen slapping a woman. This video was presented as evidence in the High Court. The video is said to be from the year 2018, where Ashish Kapoor slapped the woman in Zirakpur police station." Here is the link and archive to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The striking similarities can be noticed in the comparison image below, thereby confirming that the video was same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report Navbharat Times, published on March 18, 2023. The title of the report read, "Punjab News: महिला को थप्पड़ मारते हुए सस्पेंडेड IPS का वीडियो वायरल, एक करोड़ रिश्वत लेने का है आरोप" An English translation of the headline read, "Punjab News: Video of suspended IPS slapping a woman goes viral, accused of taking a bribe of Rs 1 crore." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same According to the report, which stated that the video dated back to 2018, the then AIG Ashish Kapoor, who was posted as Superintendent in Central Jail Amritsar, allegedly assured Poonam Rajan of Kurukshetra, who was on judicial remand, that he would arrange for her bail and acquittal from the court. Kapoor, along with SHO Pawan and ASI Harjinder, received a bribe of Rs 1 crore for this work. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video dating back to 2018 was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, BJP leader Vanathi Srinivasan didn't display 'Go Back Modi' placard during PM's Kanyakumari visit; digitally altered photo shared on social media
content: New Delhi, June 5 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of BJP leader Vanathi Srinivasan and claimed that she held a placard mentioning 'Go Back Modi' during the PM's recent visit to Kanyakumari. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo dating back to 2021 was digitally altered and shared on social media with a false claim. PM Modi undertook a 45-hour-long meditation at the Vivekananda Rock Memorial in Kanyakumari after the conclusion of campaigning for the seventh phase of the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. The criticism invoked sharp criticism from the opposition, which termed it a violation of the silence period under the Model Code of Conduct. Claim A Facebook user shared on May 30 shared a photo of BJP leader Vanathi Srinivasan, claiming that she held a placard mentioning 'Go Back Modi' during the recent visit of PM to Kanyakumari. The caption of the post read, "Trend alert #GoBackModi. Pass it on🔥🔥" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the photo through Google Lens, the Desk found it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: While scanning the results, the Desk came across another X post with the similar photo by the official handle by Vanathi Srinivasan on October 24, 2021. The caption of the post read, "இன்று கோவை ஆதியோகி சிலை முன்பாக 100 கோடி தடுப்பூசி செலுத்தி சாதனை படைத்த பிரதமர் திரு. @narendramodi அவர்களுக்கு நன்றி தெரிவிக்கும் இளைஞர் அணி நிகழ்ச்சியில் மாநில தலைவர் திரு.@annamalai_k @VinojBJP @apmbjp அவர்களுடன் கலந்து கொண்டேன் " An English translation of the caption read, "Prime Minister Shri. @narendramodi State President Shri. @annamalai_k @VinojBJP @apmbjp attended with them #100CroreVaccination" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We then compared the two photos, and found striking similarities, suggesting that the viral photo was digitally altered. Subsequently, the Desk found that an old photo dating back to 2021 was digitally altered and shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Did four Lok Sabha candidates lose by a margin of 19,731 votes? No, screenshot of inaccurate data published by newspaper shared on social media
content: New Delhi, June 10 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a purported screenshot of a Hindi newspaper, which showed that four candidates, including BJP's Navneet Rana, Ajay Teni and Madhavi Latha and Congress' Kanhaiya Kumar, lost by exactly 19,731 votes in their respective constituencies in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a Hindi newspaper had published incorrect data in one of its editions, whose clipping was shared on social media with false claim. Apart from Navneet Rana, all the other candidates highlighted in the clipping lost by a margin of more than 30,000 votes. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 5 shared a screenshot of a Hindi newspaper, according to which four candidates, including BJP's Navneet Rana, Ajay Teni and Madhavi Latha and Congress' Kanhaiya Kumar, lost their respective seats by 19,731 votes each in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the post read, "लोगों को अखबार ध्यान से पढ़ना चाहिए‼️ इसमें चार उम्मीदवार एक समान संख्या के वोटों से जीते हैं और हारे हैं..19731 का आंकड़ा क्या कहता है ?ये संयोग है की प्रयोग ? ईवीएम और चुनाव आयोग की विश्वसनीयता लोगों के बीच बरकरार रखने इस प्रकार की परिणाम का सावधानी से अवलोकन किया जाना चाहिए.. ईवीएम में कोई तो सेंटिंग है! इसलिए मैं बार बार कहता हूं ईवीएम हमेशा के लिए रद्द की ही जानी चाहिए!" An English translation of the post read, "People should read the newspaper carefully‼️ In this, four candidates won and lost by the same number of votes.. What does the figure of 19731 say? Is this a coincidence or an experiment? To maintain the credibility of EVMs and Election Commission among the people, such results should be carefully observed.. There is some center in EVMs! That's why I say again and again that EVMs should be canceled forever!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively: While going through the comments, the Desk noticed several users mentioning that the viral screenshot showed the wrong data. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this the Desk scanned the official website of the Election Commision of India, and found that BJP candidate from Amravati Navneet Rana did lose by 19,731 votes to Congress candidate Balwant Basawant Wankhade. Here is the link to the website, and below is a screenshot of the same: However, we found that BJP's Ajay Teni, who contested against Utkarsh Verma of the Samajwadi Party, was defeated by 34,329 votes in Kheri, Uttar Pradesh. We then scanned results for Madhavi Latha, BJP candidate from Hyderabad who contested against All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) MP Asaduddin Owaisi, and found that she lost by a margin of over 3.38 lakh votes. Congress candidate Kanhaiya Kumar was defeated by BJP's Manoj Tiwari by over 1.38 lakh votes. On further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk found that a clipping of a report similar to the viral screenshot published by the Rajastan Patrika. Here is the link to the e-paper and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the viral screenshot and the e-paper slipping. Below is a combination image, comparing the two: The Desk, however, during its investigation found that the Indore edition of the newspaper had indeed published incorrect data, showing the same vote margin of defeat for all the four candidates. Below is a screenshot of the same: This particular screenshot of the newspaper was shared on social media to make the false claim. In the next part of investigation, we reached out to the editorial department of the Indore Bureau of Rajasthan Patrika. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk found that screenshot of incorrect data published by a newspaper was shared on social media. (Disclaimer: The article was updated after the Desk found in its investigation that the screenshot was not digitally altered, but one of the editions of the newspapers indeed published inaccurate data.)

title: PTI Fact Check: No, UP Govt has not implemented Population Control Bill; 2021 news report shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 11 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video news report was shared on social media recently with the claim that the Yogi Adityanath government in Uttar Pradesh implemented the Population Control Bill in the state. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a 2021 news report, discussing the contours of a proposed draft of the Uttar Pradesh Population Control Bill was shared on social media with a misleading claim. The Bill has not been presented in Legislative Assembly till date. According to a draft of the proposed population control bill, anyone violating two-child policy in Uttar Pradesh will be debarred from contesting local bodies elections, from applying for or getting promotion in government jobs, and receiving any kind of government subsidy. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 8 a video report by Republic Bharat on Uttar Pradesh Population Control Bill and claimed that the Bill had bee implemented in the state. The caption of the video read, "#NDA_का_समीकरण,#YogiAdityanath HUGE: Yogi ji removed all Govt Subsidies and Benefits for any family that has over Two children. They also cannot participate in local elections. Population Control Bill unleashed. No more appeasement, just action." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned social media platforms and found that the same video was shared by several users with similar claims. Three such Facebook and Instagram posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here, here and here, respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Two such videos can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here, respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk noticed the logo of Republic Bharat on the viral video. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by Republic Bharat on Jul 11, 2021. The description of the video read, "Yogi ने बना लिया जनसंख्या नियंत्रण फार्मूला! | देखिए Ye Bharat Ki Baat Hai, Syed Suhail के साथ" An English translation of the description read, "Yogi has created a population control formula! , Watch Yeh Bharat Ki Baat Hai, with Syed Suhail" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and found it to be the extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the two visuals: The Desk watched the video and found that the news anchor was discussing the reported details of the draft of the proposed Bill back then. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report published by the Times of India on July 15, 2021. The title of the report read: "UP's 2-child policy: Is there a need for population control measures in India?" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk checked the official website of the Uttar Pradesh State Law Commission (UPSLC), which mentioned the "Population (Control, Stabilization and Welfare) Along with Draft Bill" report, uploaded in 2021. Here is the link to the website along with the link to the and below is a screenshot of the same: The hyperlink led us to the report by state law commission on the population of UP, along with the draft Bill. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that UP Population Control Bill has not been introduced in the legislative Assembly till date. A 2021 news report discussing the details of the draft of the proposed Bill was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of Kangana Ranaut with superimposed audio shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 12 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of newly elected BJP MP Kangana Ranaut coming out of an airport while a person in the background purportedly asked her, "Which cheek was it?". The question was about the recent incident at Chandigarh Airport, where a CISF woman constable allegedly slapped Kangana. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Ranaut was not confronted with any such question at the airport. An external audio clip was superimposed on the video at a specific timeframe to make it look like a media person regarding the slapgate questioned the actor-turned-politician. The digitally altered video was shared on social media with a false claim. Ranaut was allegedly slapped by a CISF woman constable at the Chandigarh Airport on June 7. The accused later said she was angry with Kangana over the latter's remarks on the farmers' protest against the central government. Claim An X user shared on June 11 a video of Kangana Ranaut coming out of an airport with reporters around her. In the video, a person in the background purportedly questioned her regarding the recent incident where a CISF woman personnel at the Chandigarh Airport assaulted her. The post's caption read, "Ye kya puch rahe ho bhai? Thodi to Maryada Rakhiye." Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that an X user shared the same video with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the results, the Desk came across a June 8 YouTube video uploaded by the official channel Araciyal Dot Com. The description of the video read, "இப்படி நடக்கும்னு நினைச்சிருக்கமாட்டாங்க 😔 | Kangana Ranaut | Bjp" "I never thought it would happen like this 😔 | Kangana Ranaut | BJP," read a rough description translation. Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The desk watched the entire video but did not hear any questions asked, as in the viral video. We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report published by the Times of India on June 7. The report's title read, "Kangana 'Loses Cool' In Delhi After 'Slap' At Chandigarh Airport." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same We then contacted PTI Video reporter Ripunj Tiwary, who was there when Kangana arrived at Delhi Airport. He told the PTI Fact Check Desk that no such questions were asked at Delhi airport and that the BJP MP from Mandi left without answering any media queries. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming 110 candidates from Muslim community elected as MP in 2024 Lok Sabha polls is false; Details inside

The caption of the post read, "110 Muslims MP in the parliament. It is already like a Muslim nation. 20% of the representatives in the Indian parliament are Muslims. This will continue to increase quickly and easily, and that is when India becomes an Islamic republic. If this Trend Continues, then maybe within 20-25+ Years, India will become an ISLAMIC NATION.😭 CONGRATULATIONS to all those Hindus who have Not Voted for the BJP. *Be Ready to GIFT Islamic India to Your Children / Grandchildren. Be Ready for SHARIA LAW. Be Ready for Razakar Like Force Rape & Kill YOUR Family Females Including Your Mothers." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned social media platforms and found several other users shared the same claim. title: PTI Fact Check: No security personnel were killed in Reasi terror attack; 2014 photo from Kabul shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 13 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo of a group of security personnel examining a bus, with the claim that 10 Indian army soldiers were killed in the recent terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Reasi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the attack claimed lives of nine pilgrims, but no security personnel was injured or killed. An old and unrelated photo from Kabul, dating back to July 2014, was shared as recent on social media with false claim. On June 9, terrorists opened fire on a 53-seater bus carrying pilgrims when it was en route to the Mata Vaishno Devi shrine in Katra from the Shiv Khori temple. The bus, ferrying pilgrims from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Delhi, plunged into a deep gorge following the gunfire, killing nine people and injuring 41 others. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 10 a photo of a group of soldiers in examining a bus, with the claim that 10 Indian Army personnel were killed in the recent terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir's Reasi. The caption of the post read, "#BREAKING: Massive News⚠️ A major attack on a bus carrying #IndianArmy soldiers in #Reasi #JammuKashmir, has just been reported. Local police confirm that ten (10) Indian soldiers have been killed. #ไบร์ทเนเน่ #Perletti #QueenOfTears #Pushpa2 #LovelyRunner #MySiblingsRomance #런쥔이왔당 #oriele" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively: The post was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archive versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the results, the Desk came across a video report published by BBC News on July 2, 2014. The title of the report read: "Afghan suicide bomber attacks military bus in Kabul" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video report, the Desk noticed striking similarities between its visuals and the viral photo. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two: According to the report, a suicide bomber killed eight military officers in an attack on an Air Force bus in the Afghan capital Kabul. 13 people, including civilians, were wounded in the attack near Kabul University. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by The Hindu on June 10. The title of the report read, "Reasi bus terror attack: Four from Rajasthan, three from U.P. among nine victims" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The report confirmed that the nine killed and others injured in the attack were all pilgrims from different cities of UP. We then scanned the social media (Facebook and Twitter) handles of Reasi Police, and came across a post, dated June 9. The caption of the post read: "Today a group of terrorist attacked yatri bus coming from Ransoo area of District Reasi. Due to the attack driver of bus lost control and bus fell into the deep gorge near kanda area of Pouni Reasi. Due to the accident, 09 people are feared dead and rest injured. Rescue operation was completed at the earliest and injured have been shifted to nearby hospitals. Senior officer of police and other forces rushed on the spot and area is been cordoned off. Search operation launched." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of same: Subsequently the Desk concluded that no security personnel was injured in the Reasi terror attack. An old and unrelated photo dating back to July 2014 was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video of Annamalai getting emotional on stage is not related to his defeat in LS polls, false claim shared in social media posts
content: New Delhi, June 11 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of BJP Tamil Nadu President K Annamalai and claimed that he got emotional while delivering a speech, after losing from Coimbatore in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video of Annamalai's visit to an old age home was shared on social media with a false claim. Annamalai, who contested from the Coimbatore Lok Sabha constituency, lost the seat to DMK's Ganapathy Rajkumar P by a margin of 1,18,068 votes. Claim An Instagram user shared on June 8 a video of BJP Tamil Nadu President K Annamalai, in which he can be seen controlling his tears while delivering a speech. The user claimed that Annamalai broke down after losing from Coimbatore in the recent Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the post read: "If you are not elected, it's not your loss, it's the loss of the people of your constituency!" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed the logo of 'News18' in the viral video.
