Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of News18 Tamil Nadu on Apr 17, 2024. The description of the video read: "மைக்கை பிடித்து கண் கலங்கிய பாஜக அண்ணாமலை - இறுதியில் எழுந்த அந்த ஒரு கோஷம் | Annamalai Cries" A rough translation of the description read: "BJP Annamalai who held the mic and was confused - that one slogan that arose at the end | Annamalai Cries" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same We then conducted another customised keyword search and came across a report by Asianet News, published on Apr 17, 2024. The title of the report read, "Annamalai: Annamalai who spoke with dismay at the old age home; Seniors consoled in BJP style" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Annamalai visited an old age home in the Palayam area to engage with the elderlies. During his conversation with them, he mentioned, "I look forward to serving as your son," and gradually became emotional. The Desk also came across some photos uploaded by the official X handle of Annamalai on April 17. An English translation of the caption, "Our Honorable Prime Minister of India Mr. @narendramodi has won more than 400 seats and when he takes charge of the Prime Minister again for the third time, the rural areas around Coimbatore and the city will get all the basic facilities of the city to get development, and the central government's plan will go to the people to monitor, ask questions, and our For the future of the children to be better and for them to live in a developed India in the next 25 years, I earnestly request you, your dear brother, your home child, Annamalai, to vote for the lotus symbol in Coimbatore Parliamentary Constituency and win with a large margin of votes " Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from Annamalai's visit to an old age home was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Rahul Gandhi watching PM Modi's swearing-in ceremony' is digitally altered; false claim shared in social media post
content: New Delhi, June 13 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi purportedly watching PM Modi's swearing-in ceremony while travelling in his car was widely shared on social media. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally altered video of Rahul Gandhi was shared on social media with a false claim. Narendra Modi took oath as Prime Minister for a third straight term on June 9 this year after the NAD registered a simple majority in the recently concluded Lok Sabha elections. Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and other politicians attended the oath-taking ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan. Claim An Instagram user shared a video on June 9 of Rahul Gandhi purportedly watching PM Modi's oath-taking ceremony while travelling in his car. The post's caption read, "Meanwhile somewhere on a highway built by Nitin Gadkari #ModiCabinet." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several users shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video uploaded from Rahul Gandhi's official Instagram handle on April 17. The caption of the post read, "भारत की सोच में, भारत की खोज में!" An English translation of the post read, "Thinking of India, searching for India!" Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk noticed striking similarities between the video and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the two visuals: In the next part of the investigation, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that PM Modi was wearing a grey jacket while taking the oath as PM for the second term in 2019. Here is the link to a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of the President of India on May 30, 2019, showing the same: In the recent oath-taking by PM Modi for the third term, he wore a blue jacket, as can be seen in the PTI photo below: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered video of Rahul Gandhi was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Rahul Gandhi didn't apologise for his pre-poll promises; social media posts shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, June 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared posts claiming that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi apologised for his party's promises of Rs 8,500 per month to the poor families, and Rs 1 lakh remuneration (Rs 8,500 per month) for one-year apprenticeship to youths, made during the runup to the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found neither Rahul Gandhi nor his party tendered any apology. Social media posts were shared with a fake claim. During the runup to the Lok Sabha polls, Gandhi announced the Mahalakshmi scheme to provide female heads of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families with Rs 8,500 directly to their account, if voted to power. Gandhi had also announced that every young diploma and degree holder in the country will have the right to apprenticeships in the private and government sectors, for which they will get a stipend of Rs 1 lakh (Rs 8,500 per month). Claim An X user shared on June 11 a post claiming that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi apologised for his party's poll promises of Rs 8,500 per month to poor families and RS 1 lakh salary to youths. The caption of the post read, "Rahul Gandhi has apologised for his poll promises of INR 8,500 per month and 1,00,000 salary per month for youths.Using these lies; he managed to get 99 seats in General Elections 2024.It's a clear case of Electoral Fraud and False promises to misguide voters." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned social media platforms and found several other users shared the same claim. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here , and here , respectively. The post was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive links can be found here , here and here respectively. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any such report backing the viral claim. We also scanned the official social media handles (Twitter and Facebook) of Rahul Gandhi and Congress, but could not find any such post as claimed in the viral posts. Here is the link to Gandhi's X profile, and below is a screenshot of the same: We also scanned the profile activity on Social Blade, a social media analytics website, and found that no recent post was deleted. Below is a screenshot of the same: We also scanned the activity of Congress' official X handle on Social Blade, which confirmed that no post was deleted recently. The Desk also found that the claims made on social media that Gandhi had promised Rs 1 lakh per month to youths was false. The party's manifesto read: "Congress guarantees a new Right to Apprenticeship Act to provide a one year apprenticeship with a private or a public sector company to every diploma holder or college graduate below the age of 25. Apprentices will get ₹ 1 lakh a year. The apprenticeship will impart skills, enhance employability and provide full-time job opportunities for millions of youth." Here is the link to the party's manifesto page, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that neither Congress nor Rahul Gandhi apologised for the promises made during the runup to the Lok Sabha polls.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of Chandrababu Naidu losing his temper in state assembly shared as recent on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Tamil Nadu CM N Chandrababu Naidu appearing to speak angrily in Tamil was shared on social media with the claim that he lost his temper before the oath-taking ceremony of the TDP-led NDA government in the state. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video dating back to 2021 was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. TDP chief Naidu was sworn in as the CM of Andhra Pradesh on June 12, after the TDP-led NDA returned to power in the state. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 11 a video of Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu seemingly speak angrily inside the Assembly and walking off, and claimed that the leader lost his temper before the oath-taking ceremony of the NDA alliance government in the state. The caption of the post read: "Chandra shekar babu nidu huye naraz ab plate gi baji #firozaalamsheikh #reelsinstagram #viral #new #reels #bjp #tdp #chandrababu #naidu #angry #jey #constiution #india #allhuakbar #boycottbjp" Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of V6 News Telugu on November 19, 2021. The description of the video read: "TDP Chief Chandrababu Naidu Sensational Decision In AP Assembly. #ChandrababuNaidu #ChandrababuCries" Here is the link to the video, below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video news report, the Desk noticed striking similarities between its visuals and the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by PTI carried by Firstpost on November 20, 2021. The title of the report read, "Chandrababu Naidu walks out of Assembly in tears, vows to return only after returning to power" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Naidu vowed to step into the Andhra Pradesh Legislative Assembly again only after returning to power. "I have been bearing the insults for the sake of people, but remained calm. Today, they have even targeted my wife. I always lived with honour and for honour. I can take it no more," Chandrababu was quoted as saying. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of Naidu shouting inside the Assembly dating back to 2021 was shared as recent on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 news report and newspaper clipping shared as recent on social media with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 15 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a purported screenshot of a Hindi newspaper, which reported an incident in which a "Muslim mob vandalised Ambedkar's statue and thrashed Dalits". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that screenshot of a 2019 report by Amar Ujala newspaper was shared on social media as recent, with a misleading claim. The screenshot was shared targeting the Samajwadi Party and its poll narrative of PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, and Alpsankhyak), after Akhilesh Yadav's party won 37 out of 80 Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, shocking the BJP-led NDA. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 13 a screenshot of a purported Hindi newspaper report about an incident in which a Muslim mob broke Ambdedkar's statue and assaulted Dalits. The caption of the post read, "PDA" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: The screenshot was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the post mentioned that the report was old and dated back to April 18, 2019. Below is the screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a similar report but with a different title published by Amar Ujala on April 21, 2019. The title of the report read, "अनुसूचित बस्ती में आंबेडकर प्रतिमा तोड़ी, मचाया उत्पात" An English translation of the post read, "Ambedkar statue broken in scheduled colony, created ruckus". While the headline of the digital version of the report was a little different from the news report in the viral screenshot, the report was identically same. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same According to this report, Mahuawa Tola of Karjahan village in Gauribazar, is a settlement of Scheduled Caste community. A young man from another community in the village entered a house and harassed a teenage girl. When the girl raised an alarm, her family members woke up, and the young man fled, issuing threats. The next night, the young man entered the girl's house again. When the family members chased him, he ran away. Shortly thereafter, he returned with dozens of other young men armed with sticks. They thrashed the girl and her family members. When the neighbors heard the noise and gathered, they too were chased and beaten. The rampage continued for about an hour. While leaving, they also vandalized an Ambedkar statue in the settlement. About 20 people, including the girl, her mother, and a disabled person, were injured in the attack. During our investigation, we also found a Jagran report on the incident, published on April 21, 2019. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a screenshot of a five-year-old newspaper report was shared as recent on social media with misleading claims

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped and edited video claiming UP CM Adityanath said 'Muslims have first right on country's resources' shared on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 12 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Uttar Pradesh CM Yogi Adityanath was shared on social media in which he was heard saying that Muslims had the first right on the country's resources. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Adityanath's interview was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Several BJP leaders, including PM Modi, had attributed this alleged statement to former PM Dr Manmohan Singh to attack the Congress during the Lok Sabha poll campaign. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 11 a video of UP CM Yogi Adityanath, in which he can be heard saying that the Muslims have the first right on the resources of the country. The caption of the post read, "वाह उत्तर प्रदेश मे बड़ी हार देख सुर ही बदल गयेजी अब अन्दभक्तों का क्या होगा" An English translation of the caption read, "Wow, after seeing the big defeat in Uttar Pradesh, the tone has changed, now what will happen to the blind devotees" Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archive versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the results, the Desk and came across a YouTube video uploaded by official channel of Bharat Express on Apr 23, 2024. The description of the video read, "CM YOGI का Congress पर हमला, किसके इशारे पर कहा, 'देश के संसाधनों पर पहला अधिकार मुसलमानों का'" An English translation of the description read, "CM YOGI's attack on Congress, on whose example did he say, 'Muslims have the first right on the country's resources'" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk found that the video was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped at the timestamp of 0:38 minutes which made it sound like Yogi said Muslims have the first right on the resources of India. In the extended video, Yogi responds, "During their time (Congress) when one of the members of Congress was PM, Dr Manmohan Singh ji was the Prime Minister of India. On who's directions did he say that the Muslims have the first rights on the resources of India." Adding to this Yogi says, "You want to divide the country in the name of Muslims and non-Muslims, minority and majority? This country has already seen a partition in 1947." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Yogi's interview was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Screenshot of news report on EVM, later termed incorrect, shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 17 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported news report claiming that a relative of Shiv Sena leader Ravindra Waikar was able to unlock EVMs using a mobile phone at a counting centre in Mumbai on June 4, the day Lok Sabha poll results were announced. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check found that the Election Commission refuted the allegations and the screenshot of a factually incorrect news report was shared on social media with a false claim. The Vanrai Police in Mumbai have registered a case against Waikar's brother-in-law for allegedly using a mobile phone at a counting centre in Goregaon (which is part of Waikar's constituency) on June 4, when results of the general elections were announced. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 16 a purported screenshot of a Mid-Day report claiming that a relative of Shiv Sena leader Ravindra Waikar was able to unlock EVMs using a mobile phone. The caption of the post read, "चुनाव आयोग और सुप्रीम कोर्ट कब इसका संज्ञान लेंगे? EVM हटाओ लोकतंत्र बचाओ @ECISVEEP" An English translation of the post read, "When will the Election Commission and the Supreme Court take cognizance of this? Remove EVM and save democracy @ECISVEEP" Here is the link and archive link to the post, below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: The screenshot was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be found here , here and here respectively. We found that the same screenshot was also shared by Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, as he backed the recent remarks on EVMS by Elon Musk. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed the logo of 'Mid-Day' on the viral screenshot. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found the same report published on June 16. While the article stands removed now, the Desk was able to capture an archive version of the same. Here is the link to the archive version of the now-deleted report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident took place at the NESCO vote counting centre in Mumbai North West on June 4, the day Lok Sabha results were announced. Shiv Sena leader Ravindra Waikar and candidate Amol Kirtikar were present at the site. During the counting of votes through the EVM machine,the candidate Amol Kirtikar was ahead but when the votes on the Electronically Transmitted Postal Ballot System (ETPBS) were counted, Kirtikar lagged behind, eventually losing the race to Waikar, the report added.Waikar emerged victorious in the Mumbai North West constituency by a razor-thin margin of just 48 votes. The Desk noticed discrepancies in the headline and the report. We then checked the official website of the Election Commission to check the role of the Electronically Transmitted Postal Ballot System (ETPBS) and how it works. Here is the link to the document and below is a screenshot of the same: Electronically Transmitted Postal Ballot System (ETPBS) is a system that enables the voters to cast their vote through an electronically received postal ballot from their preferred location, which is outside their originally assigned voting constituency unlike the EVM. An election officer can log in from any system to create and send postal ballots. To access the portal the officer needs to provide an OTP received on his registered phone number. After which RO prepares password-protected ballot papers for the constituency and uploads them to the system. The ballot papers are then sent electronically to the voters belonging to the service class. The complete process is secured by way of multiple checks and transmission protocol to ensure safe transmission. Upon receipt of the postal ballot at the counting centres, the returning officer validates the receipt by a series of QR codes with that of the transmitted system. We conducted another customised keywords search on Google and came across a report published by ABP Live on June 16. The title of the report read, "'No OTP Required, EVMs Stand-Alone Devices': Mumbai EC Official Refutes EVM Hacking Claims" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Vandana Suryavanshi, the returning officer of the Mumbai North West Lok Sabha constituency, clarified that data entry and vote counting are two separate processes. An OTP (One Time Password) allows the ARO to access the Encore login system for data entry, but this is unrelated to the vote counting process, which remains independent and unaffected by unauthorised mobile phone use. Furthermore, there is no OTP for unlocking EVMs (Electronic Voting Machines), as they are non-programmable and lack wireless communication capabilities. "The EC's response came in response to the police case against a relative of a Shiv Sena (Ekhnath Shinde) MP Ravindra Waikar for allegedly using a mobile phone within a counting centre," read the summary of the report. Speaking at a press conference, Suryavanshi said the personal mobile phone of one Dinesh Gurav, the data entry operator of Jogeshwari assembly constituency, was found in the hands of an unauthorised person and action is being taken in this regard. "Data entry and vote counting are two different aspects. An OTP enables the ARO to open the encore login system for data entry. The counting process is independent and has nothing to do with unauthorised use of mobile phone, which is an unfortunate incident and is being probed," Suryavanshi added. "Advance technical features and robust administrative safeguards are in place to rule out any possibility of manipulation. Safeguards include conducting everything in the presence of candidates or their agents," she said. The official said neither Waikar or losing candidate Amol Kirtikar of the Shiv Sena (UBT) had sought a recount but verification of invalid postal ballots was demanded and it was done. "The counting ETPBS (electronically transmitted postal ballot system) happens in physical form (postal ballots) and not electronically as is being spread as part of a false narrative. Every counting sheet at every table for ETPBS, EVM and postal ballot counting (including ETPBS) is signed by counting agents after due diligence," Suryavanshi asserted. Further, the Desk also came across a press note issued by the Election Commission of India, stating that the newspaper was spreading false news, which is being used by some leaders to create a false narrative. Below is a screenshot of the same: Then the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a clarification issued by Mid-day regarding the viral report published on June 17. Here is the link to the e-paper and below is a screenshot of the same: During its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk also came a June 17 PTI report, carried by News18, whose headline read: "Newly Elected Mumbai MP Waikar's Kin Booked for Using Phone Inside Counting Centre on June 4". Here is the link to the report "The brother-in-law of newly elected Mumbai North West Lok Sabha MP Ravindra Waikar has been booked for allegedly using a mobile phone at a counting centre on June 4, when results of the general elections were announced, a police official said on Saturday. The Vanrai police station official said the case against Mangesh Pandilkar was registered on Wednesday for his alleged act inside a counting centre in Goregaon, which is part of Waikar's constituency," read a portion of the report. In the next part of investigation, PTI that reached out to Rampyare Rajbhar, senior inspector of Vanrai police station. Rajbhar confirmed the news as "fake", and said that the police were "sending legal notice to Mid-Day and Lokmat as story is fake. We have just taken action under section 188 and investigation is underway". Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot of a factually incorrect Mid-Day report was shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped and pixelated video shared on social media to falsely claim PM Modi ignored handshake from US Prez Joe Biden; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 18 (Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): Multiple social media users shared a pixelated video, claiming that it showed PM Modi ignoring a handshake offered by US President Joe Biden. The timing of social media posts insinuated that this happened recently when the two leaders met at the G7 Summit held in Apulia, Italy. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the person in the video was not Biden but a support staff member guiding PM Modi for his next meeting through a hand gesture. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 16 a video, claiming that it showed PM Modi ignoring a handshake from US President Joe Biden. "बाईडेन से हाथ न मिलाकर मोदी जी ने अमेरिका को उसकी औकात दिखा दी ... हमारे चुनावों में दखल अंदाजी का नतीज़ा तो औकात दिखादी दुनिया के सामने....," read the caption of the post. An English translation of the post read: "By not shaking hands with Biden, Modi ji showed America its worth... The result of interference in our elections will be visible to the world.." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here . The video was widely shared on X (formerly Twitter), too. One such post can be viewed here , and its archived version can be seen here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by Firstpost on June 15. "Hello From Team Melodi" Selfie of PM Modi & Giorgia Meloni Goes Viral | PM Modi at G7 Summit 2024," read the video title. Here is the link to the YouTube video, and below is a screenshot of the same: At the beginning of the video, the Desk noticed the same visuals as in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the two videos: A screenshot from the same video showed that the person in the video was not Joe Biden. The Desk also compared the visuals of the man in the viral video with those of Biden in the event. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google, leading us to an extended version of the same video, uploaded by the official YouTube handle of G7 Italy 2024. At 21:02 minutes timestamp, PM Modi can be seen walking along with the man, who is not Biden but looks like a support staff member. Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the entire video and noticed the same person guided several delegates towards the spot where Italian PM Giorgia Meloni was standing to greet them. Below is a combination image showing the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man seen with PM Modi in the video was not US President Joe Biden. Also, that person – a support staff member – was not offering a handshake to the PM but guiding him with a hand gesture.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 news report of TDP chief Chandrababu Naidu breaking ties with BJP shared as recent with false claim on social media
content: New Delhi, June 19 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An Instagram user shared a purported video report by ABP News, according to which Andra Pradesh CM and TDP chief N Chandrababu Naidu broke alliance with the BJP, over the non-fulfilment of the promise of special state status. The report further claimed that two of the TDP ministers will tender their resignation from the Union Cabinet. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video dating back to March 2018 was shared on social media as recent with false claims. TDP is part of the NDA-led government at the Centre and two of its leaders are ministers in the Union Cabinet, namely Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu and Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani. Claim An Instagram user shared on June 16 a purported video news report by ABP News, which claimed that Andra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu broke alliance with BJP following the Lok Sabha results. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the post mentioning that the news report was 6 years old. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of ABP NEWS on March 7, 2018. The description of the video read, "As per TDP sources, The Chandrababu Naidu is likely to convey the same to Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday morning. Also, all the ministers would also be resigning thereafter." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video report, the Desk noticed striking similarities between its visuals and the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two: We then conducted another customised keyword search and came across a report by India Today, published on March 8, 2018. The title of the report read, "TDP-BJP break up: Why Andhra CM Chandrababu Naidu walked out of Modi govt." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the TDP accused the BJP of reneging on its promise to grant special category status to Andhra Pradesh. Former Finance Minister Arun Jaitley rejected this demand, stating, "We have to think of the country as a whole." He pointed out that there are other states earning less revenue than Andhra Pradesh. However, Jaitley assured that the Centre is ready to provide an equivalent amount of money to Andhra Pradesh as a special package. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted another cutomised keyword search but could not find any such report stating that any such political development took place recently. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old news was shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video clip shared falsely claiming RJD's Tejashwi Yadav was drunk while talking to media; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 19 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed him in an inebriated state. In the video, Yadav criticised the allocation of ministries to Bihar leaders in the Union Cabinet of the NDA-led central government. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the playback speed of the video was slowed down, and the edited video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 13 a video of Tejashwi Yadav commenting on the allocation of ministries to Bihar leaders in the Union Cabinet. The user claimed that Yadav was under the influence of alcohol when making the statement. The caption of the post read, "राजद का सड़क छाप नेता,,, झूम बराबर झूम शराबी " An English translation of the post read, "RJD street raid leader Jhoom Barabar Jhoom Sharabi" Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk noticed the logo of 'Republic Bharat' on the viral video. Taking a cue from this, we came across a YouTube video uploaded by official Republic Bharat on June 11. The description of the video read, "Tejashwi Yadav ने मंत्रालय बंटवारे पर तंज कसते हुए ये क्या कह दिया? " An English translation of the video read, "What did Tejashwi Yadav say while taunting on ministry sharing?" Here is the lin k to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image, showing the same: The Desk watched the video and noticed that the audio playback in it was faster than the viral video. We also found an X post by PTI which shared the similar video on June 10. The caption of the post read, "It is the PM's prerogative to allot ministries but work should happen in all the departments. However, he became the PM because of Bihar but the ministries given to Bihar's leaders shows that they have been short-changed," says RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav (@yadavtejashwi) on Union Cabinet portfolio allocation." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: On watching the video, the Desk found that the playback speed of the viral video was slowed down to make it look like Tejashwi was speaking in an inebriated state.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 report on childbirths in Rohingya camps in Bangladesh falsely shared on social media in India's context; details inside
content: New Delhi, June 20 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users claimed that 60,000 babies were born in Rohingya camps in India within a year. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a 2018 report on expectation of 60,000 childbirths in Rohingya camps in Bangladesh was falsely linked to India and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 17 a post claiming that 60,000 babies have been born in Rohingya camps in India within a year. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same Investigation The Desk scanned social media platforms and found that several other users shared the same claim. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archive versions can be seen here and here , respectively. We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an IANS report published by India TV on February 28, 2018. The title of the report read: "The situation of Rohingya Muslims may get worse, 60,000 children are expected to be born in the camps" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Dr. Poonam Khetrapal, South-East Asian Regional Director of the World Health Organisation (WHO) mentioned that the crisis started on August 25, 2017. The condition of Rohingyas who have reached Bangladesh from Myanmar in large numbers is horrifying. 6,88,000 Rohingyas are living in the refugee camps of Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh, while earlier 2,12,500 Rohingyas have reached Bangladesh. This is the largest population to migrate in such a short period. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search to find the official statistics regarding Rohingya babies born in the refugee camps in Bangladesh. The Desk came across a press release by UNICEF highlighting the conditions and reason for the increased birth rate of Rohingya babies in the refugee camps in Bangladesh. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Further, we scanned the results for the refugees registered with UNHCR India. According to UNHCR, as of 31 January 2022, more than 46,000 refugees and asylum-seekers were registered mainly from Myanmar and Afghanistan. Also, there is no official information about the number of childbirths happening in the Rohingya camps in India. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim of 60,000 births a year in Rohingya camps pertained to Bangladesh, and not India.

author: Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, government has not relaunched Agnipath scheme with another name; fake screenshot shared on social media
content: New Delhi, June 20 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a purported document claiming that Agnipath scheme was relaunched by the name 'Sainik Saman Scheme', with several modifications in it, was recently shared on social media. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that no such changes were made to the Agnipath scheme by the government. A fake screenshot was shared on social media with a false claim. In June 2022, the Centre rolled out the Agnipath recruitment scheme for short-term induction of personnel into the armed forces with an aim to bring down the age profile of the three services. The scheme provides for recruiting youngsters in the age bracket of 17 years and a half to 21 years for a four-year period with a provision to retain 25 per cent of them for 15 more years. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 16 a screenshot of a document claiming that the Agnipath scheme was relaunched as 'Sainik Saman Scheme', along with several modifications. The caption if the post read, "Relaunched Aganipath. Now it's Sainik Saman Scheme take a look on comparison." Here is the link to the post and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively: The post was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed several discrepancies in the viral document. It lacked an official letterhead and was not signed by any government authority. Additionally, the document contained multiple grammatical and spelling errors. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: The Desk then scanned the official website and the social media (Twitter and Facebook) handles of the Ministry of Defence, but could not find any notification regarding the Agnipath scheme. Here is the links to the official website and X handles of the Ministry of Defence. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Indian Express on June 7. The title of the report read: "After Agnipath faces poll fire, JD(U) says 'discuss, remove flaws', Chirag agrees" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, KC Tyagi, a leader of BJP's ally JD(U), urged the government to address the shortcomings of Agniveer scheme. He noted that a section of voters in western Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan were dissatisfied with the Agnipath scheme. Earlier on June 2, Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan said that the implementation of the Agnipath scheme has been one of the major reforms towards maintaining a youthful profile of the three services. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral document was fake and shared on social media with false claim.

author: Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of people breaking glass door at Congress leader Kumari Selja's meeting venue shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 21 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check): A video of Congress leader Kumari Selja was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed people protesting outside her office and breaking the glass door, demanding the Rs 8,500 (per month) promised by the Congress in its manifesto for the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from an unrelated event where the supporters of Congress leader Paramvir Singh alleged that the glass door was locked from inside, and was broken as they tried to gain access to the conference room where Selja was holding a meeting. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. The Congress, in its manifesto for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, announced the Mahalakshmi scheme to provide female heads of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families with Rs 8,500 per month directly to their bank accounts, if voted to power. The party had also promised a Right to Apprenticeship Act to provide a one-year apprenticeship with a private or a public sector company to every diploma holder or college graduate below the age of 25, along with a stipend of Rs 1 lakh per year (Rs 8,500 per month). Claim A Facebook user shared on June 15 a video, claiming that it showed Congress leader Kumari Selja being confronted by the public protesting outside her office over their demand of Rs 8,500 each, as promised by the Congress party in its manifesto for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the video read, "नव निर्वाचित सांसद कुमारी सैलजा जब अपने ऑफिस पहुंची तो 8500 मांगे वाले लोग आ गए हैं* *खटखट पैसे नहीं दिये तो भट्टा भट्ट शुरू हो गयी* *तड़क् तड़क् शीशे टूटने शुरू हो गए" An English translation of video read, "When the newly elected MP Kumari Selja reached her office, people demanding 8500 came to her office* *When the money was not given, they started banging* *The glasses started breaking with a bang" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of Punjab Kesari Haryana on June 13. The description of the video read: "प्रेस कांफ्रेंस में हुआ बवाल, बेकाबू समर्थकों ने तोड़ डाला गेट, और फूट पड़ा कुमारी सैलजा का गुस्सा......ये तस्वीरें टोहाना की हैं, जहां सिरसा लोकसभा सीट पर जीत का परचम लहराने के बाद कुमारी सैलजा प्रेस कांफ्रेंस करने के लिए पहुंचीं थी" An English translation of the description read, "There was chaos in the press conference, uncontrolled supporters broke the gate, and Kumari Selja burst out in anger... These pictures are from Tohana, where Kumari Selja had reached to hold a press conference after winning the Sirsa Lok Sabha seat" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video, as seen below: We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another report published by The Tribune on June 13. The title of the report read: "Stuck door, sloganeering mar Selja's press meet in Tohana" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Haryana Congress MP Kumari Selja visited the Tohana town of Fatehabad district following her victory in the elections. While the leader was addressing a conference in a room at the venue of a workers' meeting. Former Agriculture Minister and Congress leader Paramvir Singh arrived outside the venue, and mediapersons closed the door to prevent disturbances. Meanwhile, Singh and his supporters attempted to enter the room to join the press conference. His supporters knocked persistently on the door, eventually smashing a glass pane, and finally forced the door open. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 3-year-old video of PM Modi's individual meeting with Pope falsely shared in name of recent G7 Summit
content: New Delhi, June 21 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of PM Modi meeting Pope Francis, claiming it was from the recent G7 Summit held in Italy and that the Indian PM was the only world leader invited by the Pope. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video of meeting between PM Modi and the Pope was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. The Pope met all the world leaders who attended the G7 Summit. Claim An X user shared on June 20 a video of PM Modi meeting with the Pope, and claimed that out of all the world leaders at the recent G7 Summit held in Italy, PM Modi was the only leader invited by the Pope for a meeting. The caption of the post read: "The media doesn't show this outreach. Only ModiJi was invited by Pope out of all state heads attending meeting G7 meet at Italy. This is the power of India today. No credit is given to ModiJi by Indian Seculars..." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another X post by the official account of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting which shared the similar video on October 30, 2021. The caption of the post read, "Prime Minister @narendramodi met Pope Francis at the Apostolic Palace in Vatican earlier today." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of PM Modi on October 30, 2021. The description of the video read, "PM Modi meets Pope Francis in the Vatican City" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the extended video, the Desk noticed striking similarities between the visuals of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the two videos: We then conducted another customised keyword search and came across a PTI report carried by The Print on October 30, 2021. The title of the report read: "PM Modi meets Pope Francis at Vatican, invites him to visit India" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, PM Modi met Pope Francis, the head of the Catholic Church at the Vatican in their first-ever one-to-one meeting. The PM was accompanied by National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar. During the visit, PM Modi discussed a wide range of issues aimed at making the planet better by fighting climate change and removing poverty. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search to find about the Pope's meeting with leaders during his Italy visit for the G7 Summit, and came across a report by Vatican News published on June 14. The title of the report read, "Pope Francis meets with world leaders at G7 summit" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Pope Francis held one-on-one meetings with several leaders including US President Joseph Biden, Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, France President Emmanuel Macron and many others. The Pope also addressed a special session on the perils and promises of AI. On further scanning the search results the Desk also came across a photo collage shared by the official Threads handle of Hindustan Times on June 15. The caption of the post read, "In Pictures | Pope Francis became the first pope to address G7 Summit. He met world leaders including Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the G7 venue in Italy. PM Modi also invited him to visit India. Pictures of the Pope with the world leaders are doing rounds on the internet." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Pope met several world leaders at the G7 Summit, and not just PM Modi. An old video dating back to 2021 was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of anti-encroachment drive in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar shared in name of Ayodhya with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 21 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of women crying as a bulldozer seemingly razed structures was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed houses being razed in Ayodhya for the construction of Ram Mandir. The users shared the video, citing this as the reason for BJP's defeat from the Faizabad Lok Sabha constituency. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video of an anti-encroachment drive in Maharashtra's Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to Ayodhya. Ram Mandir emerged as the major poll issue in the Lok Sabha elections, and BJP's defeat in Faizabad Lok Sabha constituency, of which Ayodhya is a part, has been a topic of discussion in the political quarters ever since. Claim An X user shared on June 5 a video in which of women crying and a bulldozer seemingly razing a structure, linking it to Ayodhya and BJP's defeat in Firozabad in the recent Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the post read, "ऐसे कैसे अयोध्या जीत जाते? तुमने देखा नहीं आखों का समंदर होना।" An English translation of the caption read, "How could Ayodhya be won like this? Didn't you see the ocean in the eyes" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Four such posts can be seen here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be viewed here , here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube, too. Three such videos can be viewed here , here and here and its archived version can be seen here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed the watermark of 'jaihindshakeel.khan98' on the viral video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk searched the said handle on Instagram and found the same video, posted in February 2024. We also found that the user – Shakeel Khan – mentioned himself as 'photojournalist at Lokmat Samachar hindi daily'. Here is the link to the profile and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that Khan posted the video with hashtags "#chatrapatisambhajinagar #aurangabad". Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Lokmat Times on February 21, 2024. The title of the report read: "Decades-old 80 feet road expansion sparks fury, 125 houses razed" Here is the link to the report: According to the report, there was an 80-foot road proposed in Cidco's 2001 plan between Mohalla Jhenda Chowk (Mukundwadi-Pundliknagar Railway gate) to Vishranti Chowk. However, implementation remained elusive for over two decades as over 300 houses were constructed on the designated road. A time limit of 72 hours was allotted to vacate the houses. However, citizens did not vacate their homes and were reluctant for cash compensation. On February 21 morning, the municipal team entered Vishwakarma Chowk in heavy police presence. Additional commissioner Saurabh Joshi, Deputy commissioner Mangesh Deore repeatedly explained and asked the citizens to cooperate with the administration. But women residents started protesting against the anti-encroachment drive, pelting stones at police and injuring several officers and municipal employees. The charged atmosphere escalated into clashes, with police resorting to lathi charges and tear gas to control the crowd. Despite assurances of alternative housing under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY), residents remained adamant, refusing to vacate their homes. We then conducted another customised keyword search on Google and found a video report on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of Marathwada Voice News on February 2. The description of video read, "Jai Bhawani Nagar Se Mukundwadi Tak Atikaraman Kya Kaha Dekhiye" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from the video report, the Desk located the Mukundwadi Railway Station on Google Maps. Using the Street View, the Desk noticed the buildings and station entrance were the same as in the YouTube video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of an anti-encroachment drive at Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar in Maharashtra was shared in the name Ayodhya on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, TRAI not to impose fine for dual SIM setup in one phone; charges planned for not using one SIM for extended period
content: New Delhi, June 24 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared posts claiming that the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) was planning to impose a fine on users for using two SIM cards on the same mobile phone. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that TRAI was mulling to impose fines on those who have a second SIM on their phone, but keep it unused or inactive for a long time. The social media posts were shared with misleading claims. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 14 a post claiming that TRAI will impose fine on users for using two SIMs on the same phone. The caption of the post read: "TRAI Plans To Impose Fine for Using Dual SIMs in Same Phone, Say Reports" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned social media platforms and found that several other users had shared the same claim. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The post was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and their archive versions can be found here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Business Standard on June 13. The title of the report read: "Will you be charged for your phone number? Here is what Trai has said" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, on June 6 the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (Trai) proposed introducing fees for mobile and landline numbers, citing that phone numbers represent a "valuable yet finite public resource". The proposal stated that if a subscriber has a dual SIM setup but doesn't use one number for an extended period, TRAI would impose fees and other regulatory measures to ensure that numbering resources are allocated and used efficiently, adapting to the dynamic telecommunications environment in India. A similar report by Economic Times stated that the TRAI was "considering whether to impose penalties on operators, who are holding on to number resources with low utilisation. For instance, a subscriber might have dual SIMs and not use one for a long period, but the operator avoids cancelling the number to retain its user base." Here is the link to the report. We then scanned the official website of TRAI and found a press release along with consulting paper regarding the viral claim. Here is the link to the official website along with the press release and consulting paper : While neither the consultation paper nor the press release mentioned about any charges or fines for people with dual SIMs in their phones, a section in the consultation paper mentioned about special and vanity numbers. "While it is true that a portion of the revenue generated from number sales is contributed as a percentage of the Adjusted Gross Revenue (AGR), however the aforementioned practices can not only lead to inefficient utilization of numbering resources but may also result in hoarding of numbering resources by the service providers. Hence, it may be prudent to consider charging the TSPs with a nominal fee against numbering resource allocated," read the paper. The body further suggested imposing "one-time", or "annual recurring" charges for the underutilised numbers on the TSP, while also imposing "financial disincentives" on TSPs who hold on the deactivated phone numbers without reallocating them. Below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the website, the Desk came across another press release issued on 14 June, to clarify the confusion referred to in the viral claim. "The speculation that TRAI intends to impose charges on customers for holding multiple SIMs/numbering resources is unequivocally false. Such claims are unfounded and serve only to mislead the public," read a portion of the press release. Here is the link to the press release and below is a screenshot of the same: We also checked the official social media handle of TRAI and found the body's response on viral claim. The caption of the June 14 post read, "The speculation that TRAI intends to impose charges on customers for holding multiple SIMs/ numbering resources is unequivocally false. Such claims are unfounded and serve only to mislead the public." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral social media posts were shared with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digvijaya Singh's video of driving away a woman not related to Congress' Rs 8,500 poll promise; Details inside
content: New Delhi, June 24 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of senior Congress leader Digvijaya Singh seemingly driving away a woman was shared on social media with the claim that she had come to ask for Rs 8,500, as promised by the Congress in its manifesto for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video was shared on social media with false claim. The woman reportedly wanted to meet Singh, seeking a party ticket to contest against PM Modi from Varanasi seat in the recently concluded Lok Sabha polls. The Congress, in its manifesto for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, announced the Mahalakshmi scheme to provide female heads of Below Poverty Line (BPL) families with Rs 8,500 per month directly to their bank accounts, if voted to power. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 11 a video of Congress leader Digvijaya Singh seemingly driving away a woman, with the claim that she had come to ask for Rs 8,500 from the leader, as promised by the Congress in its manifesto for the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. The caption of the post read, "जब एक महिला कांग्रेस MP के पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री दिग्विजय सिंह के पास राहुल गांधी के गारंटी कार्ड के खटाखट खटाखट वाले 8500 रू लेने पहुंच गई तो देखो उन्होंने महिला से क्या बर्ताव किया" An English translation of the caption read, "जब एक महिला कांग्रेस MP के पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री दिग्विजय सिंह के पास राहुल गांधी के गारंटी कार्ड के खटाखट खटाखट वाले 8500 रू लेने पहुंच गई तो देखो उन्होंने महिला से क्या बर्ताव किया" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of Live Hindustan on February 21. The description of the video read, "सोशल मीडिया पर एक वीडियो तेजी से वायरल हो रहा है जिसमेंकांग्रेस के दिग्गज नेता दिग्विजय सिंह मध्य प्रदेश के ग्वालियर में एक महिला कार्यकर्ता पर भड़क गए. नाराज दिग्विजय सिंह ने महिला को पागल कहते हुए अपने सुरक्षा गार्डों से उन्हें बाहर निकालने के लिए कहा…" An English translation of the description read, "A video is going viral on social media in which Congress veteran Digvijaya Singh got angry at a woman worker in Gwalior, Madhya Pradesh. Angry Digvijaya Singh called the woman crazy and asked his security guards to throw her out…" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the two videos: We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Hindustan on February 21, 2024. The title of the report read, "'बाहर करो इसको, पागल हो गई है', जब महिला पर भड़के दिग्विजय सिंह; देखें वीडियो" An English translation of the video read, "'Throw her out, she has gone mad', when Digvijaya Singh got angry at the woman; watch the video" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Digvijaya Singh was touring the Gwalior-Chambal region on February 21. While Singh was meeting with party workers, a woman attempted to speak with him but was prevented from doing so by his security. Further, the report identified the woman in the viral video as Dr Leena Sharma. Talking to the media, she said: 'Some people take it lightly, but it does not make any difference. I have no resentment towards Digvijaya Singh. I had come to meet him, he asked me to leave so I will meet him later." Sharma also mentioned that she had come to meet Singh to request a ticket to contest the elections against PM Modi from Varanasi. During its investigation, the Desk also found that the announcement of Mahalakshmi scheme in Congress' manifesto was done in April 2024, whereas the video is from February. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video dating back from before the Lok Sabha elections was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of children consuming alcohol shared as recent with false claim after hooch tragedy in Tamil Nadu
content: New Delhi, June 25 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that it showed a group of children consuming alcohol offered by a man in Tamil Nadu. The video was shared targeting the DMK-led state government in wake of the recent hooch tragedy in Kallakurichi, which claimed 58 lives. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video, dating back to at least 2019, was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. The DMK came to power in Tamil Nadu in 2021. Claim An X user shared on June 22 a video, claiming that it showed of a group of children consuming alcohol in DMK-ruled Tamil Nadu. The caption of the post read, "This is Tamil Nadu. Kids drinking Alcohol under DMK. What to say." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video on Facebook posted by 'Saravanan Vijaya Bharathamak Party Vellore' on September 28, 2019. The caption of the post read, "சிறுவர்களுக்கு மது அருந்த வைக்கும் அதிர்ச்சி காட்சி. எங்கு நடந்தது என்று கண்டுபிடியுங்கள் ஊற்றி கொடுக்கும் நபர் சிறுவர் வன்கொடுமை தடுப்பு சட்டத்தில் கைது செய்யப்பட வேண்டும்" An English translation of the caption read, "A shocking scene where children are made to drink alcohol. Find out where it happened and the person who poured it. Arrest should be made under Prevention of Child Abuse Act." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image, showing the same: The Desk, while scanning the comment section of one of the viral posts, came across an X post by Tamil Nadu government's Fact Check Unit (FCU), stating that "even before 2019, the video was making the rounds on social media". Here is the link to the X post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search and found that the DMK government was formed in Tamil Nadu in May 2021. While we could not establish the exact location and time of the viral video, it was concluded that the video was making the rounds on social media at least since 2019, way before the DMK came to power in Tamil Nadu.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of India's first PM Jawaharlal Nehru's remarks on country's independence shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 25 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru was recently shared on social media in which he was heard saying that he was "not involved in the fight for Independence", and in fact he "opposed it". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Nehru's interview to American TV Host Arnold Michaelis in May 1964 was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 25 a video of former PM Jawaharlal Nehra in which he can be heard saying that he was "not involved in the fight for Independence", and in fact, he "opposed it". The caption of the post read, "दुर्लभ वीडियो... "मैं आज़ादी की लड़ाई में बिल्कुल भी शामिल नहीं था। बल्कि मैंने इसका विरोध किया था।" नेहरू जी" An English translation of the caption read: "Rare video... I was not involved in the freedom struggle at all. Rather, I opposed it." Nehru ji" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Prasar Bharati Archives on May 14, 2019. The description of the video read: "Full video recording of what was perhaps Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru's last significant interview to American TV Host Arnold MichJawaharlal Nehru's last TV Interview - May 1964e his death. Another book by Chandrika Prasad provides a date of 18th May 1964 when the interview was aired in New York, this is barely a few days before the death of Pandit Nehru on 27th May 1964." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the video was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped at 14:50-minute timestamp. In the extended video, the interviewer asked Nehru whether he, along with Mahatma Gandhi and Muhammad Ali Jinnah, was involved in the fight for Independence. To this, Nehru responded: "Mr Jinnah was not involved in the fight for independence at all, in fact he opposed it. The Muslim League was started in 1911, I think. It was started really by the British, encouraged by them so as to create factions, they did succeed to some extent. And ultimately, there came the partition." Subsequently the Desk concluded an edited video of Nehru was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of cop assaulting an elderly man is not from UP; 2022 video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, June 26 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video of a cop assaulting an elderly man at a railway station, and claimed that the incident happened in Uttar Pradesh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from Jabalpur railway station in Madhya Pradesh, dating back to July 2022. The video was shared on social media with false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 23 a video showing a cop assaulting an elderly man at a railway station, claiming that the incident occurred in Uttar Pradesh. The caption of the post read, "Uttar Pradesh is heading towards a Jungle Raaj. Just look at how the Police is beating the old Man mercilessly. Mob lynching, Bulldozer on Homes of Innocent Muslims is common in UP now." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Instagram as well. Two such videos can be viewed here and here and their archive versions can be found here and here respectively. The Desk noticed went through the comment sections of the viral posts and found one of the users mentioning that the viral video was a year old and from Madhya Pradesh. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report by Times Now, published on July 29, 2022. The title of the report read, "Video: Cop Brutally Attacks Elderly Man At Madhya Pradesh Railway Station" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the viral video and the video news report. Below is a combination image showing the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another report published by Times Now on July 29, 2022. The title of the report read, "MP: Cop suspended after video of him brutalising old man at Jabalpur Railway Station went viral" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the cop in the viral video was identified as Anant Sharma and the victim as Gopal Prasad. The incident took place on July 27, 2022 when Gopal Prasad complained to the police that some people abused him at Jabalpur railway station, and the policeman present there attacked him. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that video of an incident that took place at Jabalpur railway station in Madhya Pradesh was falsely linked to Uttar Pradesh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Yusuf Pathan taking oath as MP shared on social media with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 1 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): A video of TMC leader Yusuf Pathan was shared on social media recently with the claim that he raised 'Jai Gujarat' slogan after taking oath as an MP. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Pathan's pledge in the Parliament was taken out of context and shared on social media with a misleading claim. Pathan concluded his oath by saying 'Jai Hind, Jai Bangla, Jai Gujarat', and not just 'Jai Gujarat'. The cricketer-turned politician defeated Congress veteran Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury and BJP's Nirmal Kumar Saha in West Bengal's Baharampur, in the recently held Lok Sabha polls. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 25 a video of TMC leader Yusuf Pathan raising 'Jai Gujarat' slogan while taking oath as an MP. The caption of the post read: "Yusuf Pathan who got elected by the votes of Bengali gave slogan of JAI GUJARAT after oath taking Imagine any BJP MP from Bengal doing this ! Cheap Minister would have tagged him/her as Outsider TMC logic- if you support BJP ,you're outsider; if you oppose BJP, you're our own." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of News18 Bihar Jharkhand on June 25. The caption of the post read: "Parliament Session 2024 : cricketer Yusuf Pathan ने 18वीं लोकसभा के सदस्य के रूप में शपथ ली New Delhi नई दिल्ली : पूर्व क्रिकेटर और तृणमूल कांग्रेस के नेता यूसुफ पठान Trinamool Congress leader Yusuf Pathan ने मंगलवार को 18वीं लोकसभा सत्र में सांसद के रूप में शपथ ली। पठान ने हाल ही में पश्चिम बंगाल के बहरामपुर निर्वाचन क्षेत्र से टीएमसी उम्मीदवार के रूप में लोकसभा चुनाव लड़ा था ." An English translation of the post read: "Parliament Session 2024 : cricketer Yusuf Pathan sworn in as member of 18th Lok Sabha New Delhi New Delhi: Former cricketer and Trinamool Congress leader Yusuf Pathan Trinamool Congress leader Yusuf Pathan on Tuesday took oath as MP in the 18th Lok Sabha session. Pathan recently contested the Lok Sabha elections as a TMC candidate from Baharampur constituency in West Bengal." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the video was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from 0:27-minute timestamp. In the extended video, Pathan, while taking the oath, says: "I, Pathan Yusuf Khan, having been elected a member of the House of People, do swear in the name of God, affirm that I will bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established, that I will uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India and that I will faithfully discharge the duty upon which I am about to enter. Jai Hind, Jai Bangla, Jai Gujarat." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Pathan's pledge was taken out of context and shared on social media with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Is booking train tickets for others a punishable offence? No! Social media posts shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, July 1 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): Multiple social media users shared posts which claimed that as per new regulations of the IRCTC, people could book train tickets only for their blood relatives or those with the same surname. The posts further claimed that booking tickets for friends or others "could lead to a huge fine of Rs 10,000 or a jail term of up to 3 years, or both". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that no such rule was notified by IRCTC and the social media posts were shared with a false claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on June 24 a screenshot which claimed that IRCTC has notified a new booking rule, as per which one could book train tickets only for their blood relatives or those with the same surname. The text on the screenshot further claimed that booking tickets for friends or others "could lead to a huge fine of Rs 10,000 or a jail term of up to 3 years, or both". Here is the link to the post and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: Since some of the viral posts attributed the new rule to Section 143 of the Indian Railways Act, 1989, the Desk conducted a customised Google search for the same. According to the Act, if any person, who is not a railway employee or an authorised agent, and is involved in purchasing or selling of railway tickets, shall be imprisoned for up to three years or fined up to Rs 10,000.
