Here is the link to the document and below is a screenshot of same: The Desk then scanned the official website and the social media (Twitter and Facebook) handles of Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) but could not find any notification regarding the new booking rule. Here is the link to the website: However, while scanning the website, the Desk came across the FAQ section which clearly mentioned that an individual could book tickets for friends and family members. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: We then conducted another customised keyword search on and came across an X post by the official handle of IRCTC issuing a clarification regarding the viral news. The caption of the post read, "The news in circulation on social media about restriction in booking of e-tickets due to different surname is false and misleading." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded the viral posts were fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Virat Kohli did not launch betting app; edited videos using AI voice clone shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several videos of former Indian skipper Virat Kohli recently made rounds on social media with the claim that he launched his own betting app. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Kohli did not launch any such betting app. Deepfake videos with AI-generated voice clone were shared on social media with false claims. The Desk debunked three such videos: Claim 1 A Facebook user shared on June 6 a video of news channel Aaj Tak's anchor Anjana Om Kashyap purportedly reporting about Virat Kohli launching his own mobile application, through which people will get a chance to earn Rs 10,000. The caption of the video read, "2024 में लोकप्रिय खेल 💯100 मिलियन से अधिक भारतीयों द्वारा खेला गया ✅खेलें और बड़ी जीत हासिल करें ✅सुपर मज़ा" An English translation of the caption read, "Popular Game in 2024 💯Played by over 100 Million Indians ✅Play and Win Big ✅Super Fun" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk noticed a lip-sync issue in the viral video. We ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Audi India on February 3, 2022. The description of the video read: "The #AudiQ7 brings its A-game to the road, every time. Great performance marries cutting-edge tech. Experience it in India" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this video and the viral video. Below is a combination image showing the same: Subsequently, the Desk noticed that a portion of this promotional video was digitally altered using superimposed AI-generated audio. Claim 2 A Facebook user shared on June 14 a video in which another anchor can be heard saying that Virat Kohli has launched his own mobile game application where he gives everyone a chance to win. The caption of the post read, "94% खिलाड़ी हर दिन जीतते हैं क्लासिक इंडियन गेम, जीतने के लिए आएं!!!" An English translation of the caption read, "94% of players win every day Classic Indian Game, Come to Win" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation In this video too, the Desk noticed a lip-sync issue. We then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found a YouTube video of a Bangladeshi anchor, who was exactly like the female anchor seen in the video. The video was uploaded by the official channel of Rtv News on December 7, 2023. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image showing the same: We found that the female anchor was not associated with Aaj Tak, but with Bangladesh's Rtv, named Faria Shahreen. The description of the video read, "Rtv Dupurer Songbad | দুপুরের সংবাদ | ০৭ ডিসেম্বর, ২০২৩ | Rtv News" An English translation of the description read, "Rtv Dupurer Songbad | Noon news December 07, 2023 | Rtv News" Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was created by combining two unrelated clips and using superimposed audio. Claim 3 A Facebook user shared on June 13 a video of Aaj Tak anchor, in which she can be heard saying that a single mother from Chennai won lakhs of rupees and became a millionaire with the help of the mobile application launched by cricketer Virat Kohli. The caption of the post read, "2024 में लोकप्रिय खेल 💯100 मिलियन से अधिक भारतीयों द्वारा खेला गया ✅खेलें और बड़ी जीत हासिल करें ✅सुपर मज़ा" An English translation of the caption read, "Popular game in 2024 💯Played by over 100 million Indians ✅Play and win big ✅Super fun" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed lip-sync issue with the viral video. We then ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running the key frames through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Puma in November 2023. The description of the video read, "Virat Kohli recounts never-heard-before stories about his childhood, his slump, his comeback century, what it would mean for him to reach Sachin's record, and how sport has shaped him into the person he is today." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image showing the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the viral videos with the help of 'Itisaar', an AI detection tool developed in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Technology, Jodhpur. The tool confirmed that the audio in the viral videos was AI generated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the videos claiming that Kohli launched online betting apps were digitally altered and created using superimposed AI-generated audio.

title: PTI Fact Check: DeepFake Alert! No, Anant Ambani did not promote any betting app; edited video shared on social media with fake claim
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared videos of Reliance Industries Non-Executive Director Anant Ambani, claiming he promoted an online betting application. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Anant Ambani did not promote any such betting app. A digitally altered video with superimposed audio was shared on social media with false claim. Video 1 A Facebook user shared on May 31 a video of Anant Ambani in which he can be heard saying, "In honor of my wedding I will give one billion rupees to the people of India. You have to download my app and play my favorite game. I will multiply each of your wins by five times and if you lose I will return double your deposit." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed a lip-sync issue in the viral video. We then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of India Today on March 2, 2024. The description of the video read, "Rahul Kanwal LIVE With Anant Ambani | Jab We Met LIVE |Anant Ambani Exclusive Interview |India Today | Vantara | Anant Ambani Interview LIVE: Unmissable Interview With Anant Ambani | Anant Ambani Wedding News LIVE" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image showing the same: We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports to substantiate the viral claim, but did not find any media report related to this. Second video Another Facebook user shared on June 6 a video of Anant Ambani in which he can allegedly be heard talking about making quick money. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: "I Anant Ambani want to tell you the secret of making quick money. There is an incredible game in which you can turn a small amount of money into a huge fortune...." Anant says in the video. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. They always stood by me' #AnantAmbani's speech from the heart as an emotional #MukeshAmbani watches from the audience" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake Alert! These ads of diabetes cure showing Ravish Kumar, Rajat Sharma and Amitabh Bachchan are fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 3 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared purported video reports featuring renowned news anchors and celebs allegedly promoting medicines for diabetes. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that they did not promote any such medicine. Unrelated videos were digitally altered using AI-generated voice clone and shared on social media with false claims. The Desk debunked four such viral claims, as mentioned below: Video 1 A Facebook user shared on June 20 a video of journalist Ravish Kumar in which he can be heard saying, "An Indian doctor has developed a drug that normalises blood sugar in a single dose. He believes in the result so much that he will give you Rs 100 million if you do not cure your diabetes. Read the information on the link given below as the offer expires today." The caption of the post read, "मधुमेह से ठीक होने वाले लोगों की संख्या एक मिलियन तक पहुंच गई है। सिर्फ एक महीने में। दवा का उत्पादन इस तरह की गति के साथ कदम नहीं चल पा रहा है, और ऑर्डरों की संख्या हर मिनट बढ़ रही है। जल्दी कीजिए, आप अभी भी इसे प्राप्त कर सकते हैं।" An English translation of the caption read, "The number of people cured of diabetes has reached one million. In just one month. The production of the drug is not able to keep pace with such a pace, and the number of orders is increasing every minute. Hurry up, you can still get it." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed a lip-sync issue in the viral video. Also, the logo of 'Ravish Kumar Official' was visible on the top right corner of the video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Ravish Kumar Official on October 15, 2023. The description of the video read, "अदाणी समूह पर आई 5 नई रिपोर्ट | 5 new reports on Adani Group" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image showing the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video on X, posted by Ravish Kumar. In the video, Kumar stated that his audio clone was used in the fake advertisement, and also cautioned people against falling pray to such videos. The caption of the post read, "कई दिनों से मधुमेह की दवा के विज्ञापन का वीडियो वायरल हो रहा है जिसमें मुझे प्रचार करते दिखाया गया है। वीडियो लेकर मेरी आवाज़ की नक़ल की गई है। पता चला है कि लोग पाँच पाँच हज़ार तक की दवा ख़रीद रहे हैं। आप झाँसे में न आएँ और दवा न ख़रीदें। मैंने इस दुष्प्रचार को रोकने के लिए एक छोटा वीडियो बनाया है।" An English translation of the caption read, "For several days, a video of a diabetes medicine advertisement is going viral in which I am shown promoting it. My voice has been copied from the video. It has been found that people are buying medicines worth up to Rs 5,000. Do not fall into the trap and do not buy the medicine. I have made a short video to stop this propaganda." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Second Video A Facebook user shared on June 6 a video report by senior journalist and TV anchor Rajat Sharma in which he can be heard saying, "Indian mafia attacked a diabetologist who created a capsule that brings blood sugar levels to normal after one use. This happened because Dr Avinash Mishra is helping citizens to win over diabetes once and for all, almost free of cost. The doctor survived. More than a million citizens of India have already been freed from diabetes, thanks to this remedy. Hurry to get the information on the link given below while it is publicly available." The caption of the post read, "मधुमेह को नष्ट करने वाली नवीनतम दवा आपके शहर में आ गई है! ऑर्डर करने के लिए, वीडियो के नीचे बटन पर क्लिक करें । जल्दी करो, उत्पाद बाहर चल रहा है!" An English translation of the caption read, "The latest drug that will destroy diabetes has arrived in your city! To order, click the button below the video. Hurry up, the product is running out" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk scanned the videos on the official YouTube channel of 'India TV', but could not find any video related to Sharma endorsing any medicine. The Desk then scanned the official social media handles of Sharma and came across a video on his Instagram account, in which he clarified that he had no link to any endorsement video going viral in his name, including those related to medicines. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Since the viral video mentioned one "Dr Avinash Mishra", the Desk took a cue from this and conducted a customised Google search. We came across Facebook posts shared by one Dr Avinash Kumar Mishra in June 2023. In the two posts shared on June 2, 2023 and July 27, 2023, Mishra cautioned people against falling pray for misleading advertisements on diabetes medicine shared in his name. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In a Facebook post made on 2 June 2023, he wrote, "Some people are making fake advertisements of diabetes viral in my name. There is no medicine to cure this disease in two days. It can be controlled by getting treatment." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The July 27 post by Kumar read: "We have not made any kind of claim, that we have discovered any special medicine to cure diabetes completely, some people are doing this kind of propaganda, I have also received some calls, the kind of fake ads are being tricked and money is being extorted by people. Please be careful. We have also filed an FIR against that ad." Third Video Another Facebook user shared on June 20 a video of senior journalist and TV news anchor Rajat Sharma, in which he is heard saying: "For the first time in history, Indian scientists have discovered a cure for diabetes that completely regenerates the stem cells of the pancreas, after which the body starts producing its own insulin. Diabetes completely disappears from the body in just one course of treatment. This morning, a struggle has started in many states of India for a new diabetes drug. People have come out on the streets and are demanding a new drug. The queue for the drug is increasing every minute. The news of the discovery of Indian scientist Avinash Mishra has gone viral on every news channel. This success in the treatment of diabetes has created a sensation all over the world. According to scientists, diabetes will end as a disease in a few years and will not be a threat to humanity…" The caption of the post read, "Today is a day no diabetic patient in India will forget. For the first time in history, scientists have created a chemical compound that destroys diabetes at the cellular level. The number of people completely cured of diabetes has reached one million. Everyone who visits our website by clicking on the 'More Details' button gets this medicine at a subsidized price." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the person in the viral video, who is said to be Avinash Mishra, is actually Dr Atul Gawande. He is working as a professor at the Harvard School of Public Health. Here is the link to his profile and X handle . The Desk further noticed that the latter's photo had been added separately to several frames of the video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of OTV News English on July 5, 2022 . The description of the video read, "WATCH | Full Speech Of President Draupadi Murmu In Parliament House | OTV News" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the video, the Desk noticed striking similarities between visuals shown in the viral video and the YouTube video. Below is a combination image showing the same: Fourth Video A Facebook user shared on June 6 a video of actor Amitabh Bachchan in which he can be heard endorsing a diabetes medicine. The caption of the post read, "अमिताभ ने मधुमेह रोगियों की मदद के लिए एक बड़ी सब्सिडी प्रदान की है। लगभग एक मिलियन लोग "Read More" बटन पर क्लिक करके साइट पर गए हैं और हमेशा के लिए मधुमेह से छुटकारा पा लिया है। जब तक छूट चल रही है, तुरंत साइट पर जाएं। केवल कुछ ही पैकेज बचे हैं।" An English translation of the caption read, "Amitabh has provided a huge subsidy to help diabetic patients. Nearly one million people have visited the site by clicking on the "Read More" button and got rid of diabetes forever. Visit the site immediately while the discount is running. Only a few packages are left." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. While running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of BollywoodCountry in which Bachchan can be seen speaking at the Kolkata International Film Festival. The description of the video uploaded on December 16, 2022 read, "An impressive, star-studded gathering at the inauguration of the 28th Kolkata International Film Festival here on Thursday evening was taken by a bit of surprise, when Bollywood megastar Amitabh Bachchan, usually known for dodging political issues, suddenly referred to issues like "civil liberties" and "freedom of expression"." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the viral video and news report. Below is a screenshot comparing the visuals of the same: In the next part of investigation, the desk scanned all four viral videos through 'Itisaar', an AI detection tool developed in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Technology, Jodhpur. The tool confirmed that the audio in the viral videos was fake and AI generated.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of road flooded with rainwater from Bengaluru falsely shared in name of Delhi; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 2 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of people dragging their vehicles through a flooded road was shared on social media with the claim that it showed the condition of Delhi, following a recent spell of rainfall. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from Bengaluru, dating back to September 2022. It was shared on social media as recent and was falsely linked to Delhi. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 28 a video of people dragging their vehicles through a flooded road, claiming it was from Delhi following a recent spell of rainfall. The caption of the video read, "ये बेवक़ूफ़ दिल्ली की जानता अपने वाहन @ArvindKejriwal जी द्वारा बनाई झील में क्यों ले गये।" An English translation of the caption read, "Why did these idiots take their vehicles to the lake built by @ArvindKejriwal ji, the people of Delhi." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral video which mentioned that the video was old and from Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this the Desk, conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the channel of a social media influencer called The Deshbhakt on September 5, 2022. The description of the video read, "A few hours of rain and India's Silicon City has a new look & identity! Here's Takeshi's Castle and India's very own super-fun Wonderla! " Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the video was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the viral video, we also noticed that the iron sheet alongside the flooded road had BMRCL written on them. Below is a screenshot of the same: On conducting a Google search, we found that BMRCL stood for Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited, popularly known as Namma Metro. We then conducted another customised keyword search and came across a report published by The Indian Express on May 24, 2022. The title of the report read, "Rain on horizon, horrors of 2022 floods on mind, residents of Bengaluru's Mahadevapura zone lament civic apathy" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the breach of the Halanayakanahalli lake caused water to flood the RBD layout, submerging residences and the clubhouse under five feet of water. The area lacks a proper drainage system to manage such a heavy load of rainwater. The residents of the area complained that it had been constructed unscientifically and caused the rainwater to flow back into the layout. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to September 2022 from Bengaluru was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of crowd at 'satsang' in Rajasthan falsely linked to Hathras stampede incident; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 4 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a massive crowd was shared on social media, with users linking it to the recent stampede at a religious congregation in UP's Hathras. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video, dating back to February 2024, from a 'satsang' in Rajasthan's Bharatpur was shared on social media with false claim. A total of 121 people, mostly women, had died after the stampede at self-styled godman Baba Bhole's satsang in Phulrai village of UP's Hathras on July 2. Claim An X user shared on July 2 a video claiming that it showed the huge crowd at the religious congregation in UP's Hathras where a stampede left as many as 121 people dead. The caption of the post read, "वीडियो मे देखे किस तरह #हाथरस मे भोले बाबा सत्संग के बाद भगदड़ मची! इन 122 लोगो की मौत का ज़िम्मेदार कौन?? इतने सारे शवो को देख हार्टअटैक से पुलिसवाले की मौत हो गई! आखिर इन बाबाओ को इतनी भीड़ इकट्ठा करने की छूट किसने दी?? और सुरक्षा का क्या? #Hathras" An English translation of the post read, "Watch the video to see how a stampede broke out after Bhole Baba's satsang in #Hathras! Who is responsible for the death of these 122 people?? A policeman died of a heart attack after seeing so many dead bodies! Who gave these Babas the permission to gather such a huge crowd?? And what about security? #Hathras" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook too. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed that one of the comments on the viral video mentioned that the video was from Roopvas Bharatpur Satsang which took place in January this year. Below is a screenshot of same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named Traveller Sachin on February 9. The description of the video read, "Mangal Divas Roopvas Bharatpur Rajasthan | Narayan Sakar Hari Ke Bhajan | Sataya Ka Sath Rajasthan'' Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the video. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos and striking similarities between them: Taking a cue from this, we located Roopwas town on National Highway 123 in Bharatpur district of Rajasthan. Using the Google Street View, the Desk noticed the building and sign board was the same as in the YouTube video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: The 'satsang' held in Roopwas was of one Narayan Sakar Hari. Notably, the stampede in Hathras also happened during a 'satsang' of preacher Surajpal alias Narayan Sakar Hari alias Bhole Baba. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video dating back to February from a 'satsang' in Rajasthan's Bharatpur was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video from Mathura falsely shared in name of recent stampede in UP's Hathras; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 5 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of overcrowding and stampede-like situation was shared on social media recently with the claim that it was from Hathras, where stampede during a religious congregation left 121 people dead recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an unrelated video of stampede during a pre-Holi event in Mathura was falsely shared in the name of Hathras on social media. A total of 121 people, mostly women, had died after the stampede at self-styled godman Baba Bhole's satsang in Phulrai village of UP's Hathras on July 2. Claim An Instagram user shared on July 2 a video showing a stampede-like situation, claiming to be from Hathras, where the recent stampede incident claimed 121 lives. The caption of the post read, "Death toll reaches 97 in stampede at a religious gathering in India." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several posts carrying the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Two such videos can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel NDTV on March 17. The description of the video read: "A stampede broke out during a pre-Holi event at the revered Shreeji Temple in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura today. The incident resulted in at least six devotees falling unconscious, with injuries reported among the crowd." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the viral video and news report. Below is a screenshot comparing the visuals of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Times Now, published on Mar 18, 2024. The title of the report read, "Stampede At Mathura's Radha Rani Temple During Pre-Holi Event, Several Devotees Injured; Police Deny Reports" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, around 12 devotees got injured on March 17 in a stampede that broke out during a pre-Holi event at the Radha Rani Temple, also known as Shriji Temple, in Uttar Pradesh's Mathura. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of stampede at a pre-Holi event in Mathura was falsely linked to the Hathras stampede incident.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of street vendor's cart being bulldozed not from Andhra Pradesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 7 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed a bulldozer demolishing the cart of a street vendor in Andhra Pradesh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the incident took place in Tambaram, Chennai. The video was falsely shared on social media in the name of Andhra Pradesh. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on June 28 a video of a bulldozer demolishing the cart of a street vendor, claiming it was from Andhra Pradesh. The caption of the post read, "జగనన్న ప్రభుత్వం చిరు వ్యాపారులకు పెట్టుబడి కింద 10,000 ఇస్తూ ఆర్ధికంగా తోడుగా ఉంటే.. ఇప్పటి చంద్రబాబు ప్రభుత్వం అండగా ఉండకపోగా ఏకంగా బుల్డోజర్తో వాళ్ళ జీవనోపాధిపై కొడుతుంది." A rough translation of the caption read: "If the Jagananna government gives 10,000 under investment to the small traders and supports them financially… The current Chandrababu government is not standing by and is hitting their livelihood with a bulldozer." Here is the link and archive link for the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post by the official handle of News Netra uploaded on June 30. The text on the video read: "Tamil Nadu govt. breaks down a small street seller's shop with JCB; Netizens react 'Heartless.'" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the two videos, suggesting that this video was from the same incident, shot from a different angle. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report by India Today, published on June 30. The title of the report read, "Chennai: Crackdown on street vendors, carts destroyed" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the report was related to the same viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: According to the report, the highway department under the Tamil Nadu state government, conducted a road clearance drive on June 15. The officials used an excavator to crush and remove the carts, demount petty shops and stands. The incident has sparked disputes between the owners and officials. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk located the National Institute of Siddha which was visible in the video report on Google maps. Using the Street View, the Desk noticed the buildings and Bank of Baroda ATM were the same as in the video report. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the incident took place in Tambaram, Chennai, and was falsely shared in the name of Andhra Pradesh and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts on arrests by CBI in NEET-UG paper leak case shared with false communal twist
content: New Delhi, July 8 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A Facebook user shared a photo collage of three men, claiming that they were the accused arrested by the CBI in the NEET UG paper leak case. The users shared the collage to point out that "all three accused arrested belonged to Muslim community". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that not just the three persons mentioned in the social media posts, but several others too were arrested in connection with the case. The social media posts were shared with misleading claims, giving them a false communal twist. The CBI has arrested 11 people in connection with the NEET-UG paper leak case so far. On July 9, the agency arrested an aspirant Sunny, who hails from Nalanda, and the father of another candidate Ranjit Kumar, who is from Gaya. NEET-UG is conducted by the NTA for admissions to MBBS, BDS, AYUSH and other related courses in government and private institutions. This year, the exam was conducted on May 5 at 4,750 centres in 571 cities, including 14 abroad. More than 23 lakh candidates had appeared for the test. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 29 a photo collage of three men and claimed that they were arrested by the CBI in connection with the NEET-UG paper leak case. The post was shared to point out that all three arrested were from a particular community. The caption of the post read, "In NEET-UG paper leak case, arrests made by CBI so far : -Md Jamaluddin who was working for Prabhat Khabar -Dr Ehsanul Haq, Principal Oasis school -Imtiaz Alam, Vice Principal Oasis school अब सारे बुद्धिजीवि बिल में घुस जाएंगे" An English translation of the caption read, "In NEET-UG paper leak case, arrests made by CBI so far :-Md Jamaluddin who was working for Prabhat Khabar -Dr Ehsanul Haq, Principal Oasis school -Imtiaz Alam, Vice Principal Oasis school Now all the intellectuals will go inside the hole" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively: The photo was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archive versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. We then conducted a customised keyword on Google and came across a report published by the New Indian Express on June 30. The title of the report read, "Jharkhand journalist arrested; CBI gets custody of 4 accused" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the CBI conducted searches at seven different locations on June 29 and arrested a journalist in Jharkhand. The accused arrested was identified as Jamaluddin Ansari, who worked with a Hindi newspaper in the state. The officials revealed that the latter was allegedly trying to help Principal Ehsanul Haque and Vice-Principal Imtiaz Alam of Oasis School in Hazaribagh. Both of the main accused in the paper leak case were taken into custody on June 29. Further, the CBI investigating teams searched other premises of suspects in Gujarat's Anand, Kheda, Ahmedabad, and Godhra districts respectively. The Gujarat Police had arrested five people, including the principal and the teacher, in connection with the paper leak case. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a PTI report carried by Economic Times on July 1 regarding the updates for the paper leak. The title of the report read, "NEET-UG exam irregularities: CBI arrests private school owner from Godhra" Here is the link to the report: The report stated that on June 30 the CBI arrested Dixit Patel the owner of Jay Jalaram School situated near Godhra in Panchmahal district. The Panchmahal police arrested 5 other accused including vadodara-based education consultant Parshuram Roy, Jay Jalaram School principal Purushottam Sharma, school teacher Tushar Bhatt, and alleged middlemen Vibhor Anand and Arif Vohra. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to check for the names of the accused arrested by CBI and came across a report by The Indian Express published on July 1. The title of the report read, "The names behind the NEET paper 'leak'." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The report mentioned details about the members of the "solver gang" based in Nalanda, Bihar, arrested by the CBI. The report named those arrested by the agency so far, which included Sanjeev Mukhiya, Baldev Kumar, Nitish Kumar, Amit Anand, Nitish Kumar, Amit Anand, Manish Prakash, Ashutosh Kumar, Roshan Kumar, Awadhesh Kumar and Sikander Yadavendu. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that while the three accused mentioned in the photo collage were indeed arrested by the CBI, they were not the only ones held by the agency.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming UP DGP praised Akhilesh Yadav during interview is incorrect; clipped footage of DGP's old video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 8 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of former Uttar Pradesh DGP Devendra Singh Chauhan was shared on social media with the claim that he praised former CM Akhilesh Yadav during an interview for giving a free hand to the state police. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Chauhan's interview, dating back to March 2023, was clipped, taken out of context, and shared on social media with a false claim. He had praised CM Yogi Adityanath, not the former CM, during the interview. Claim An X user shared on July 6 a video of former UP DGP Devendra Singh Chauhan, claiming that it showed him praising former CM and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav for giving a free hand to the state police. The caption of the post read: "आदरणीय अखिलेश यादव जी उत्तर प्रदेश के सबसे बेहतरीन मुख्यमंत्री रहे हैं।" An English translation of the caption read: "Respected Akhilesh Yadav ji has been the best Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Four such posts can be viewed here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of News18 UP Uttarakhand on March 26, 2023. The description of the video read: "Lucknow Adhiveshan 2023 LIVE : DGP DS chauhan के साथ योगी सरकार 2.0 की कानून व्यवस्था पर चर्चा " An English translation of the post read: "Lucknow Adhiveshan 2023 LIVE : Discussion on law and order of Yogi Government 2.0 with DGP DS Chauhan" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination of image comparing the two visuals: While watching the extended video, the Desk noticed that the viral video was clipped at the timestamp of 16:35 minutes. In the extended video, the interviewer questions Chauhan whether he is leaving any benchmark behind. To which Chauhan replied, "I would just like to say that our popular Chief Minister, the most respected Yogi Adityanath ji, I thank him from the bottom of my heart for giving me and my team such an opportunity in which we could serve the public." He further added, "I want to tell you that for the first time as a police officer, I have seen such a Chief Minister who never interferes in our day to day working. Who to catch, who to arrest, who to deploy where, he does not interfere in all this." The later part was clipped and shared on social media while the part where Chauhan mentioned about Yogi Adityanath was omitted. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media was clipped. Chauhan praised Adityanath in the interview, and not Akhilesh Yadav.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, PM Modi did not say 'govt will fight against the poor'; clipped video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video clip of PM Modi's speech in Parliament shared with a claim that he allegedly said 'his government will fight a decisive battle against the poor'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected part of PM Modi's reply to the Motion of Thanks on the President's address was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 3 a video of PM Modi in which he was heard saying that the government will fight a decisive battle against the poor. The caption of the post read, "देश की आयरन लेडी इंदिरा गाँधी जी ने 'ग़रीबी हटाओ' का नारा दिया था, देश के जुमला मैन नरेंद्र मोदी जी ने 'ग़रीबों को हटाओ" का नारा दिया है। आने वाले 5 साल में हमारी सरकार ग़रीबों के ख़िलाफ़ निर्णायक लड़ाई लड़ेगी। — नरेंद्र मोदी" An English translation of the caption read, "The Iron Lady of the country Indira Gandhi gave the slogan of 'Garibi Hatao', The country's Jumla Man Narendra Modi has given the slogan of 'Remove the poor'.In the coming 5 years, our government will fight a decisive battle against the poor. - Narendra Modi" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here . The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such videos can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Narendra Modi on July 3. The description of the video read: "PM Modi's speech during reply to Motion of Thanks in Rajya Sabha" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended video, the Desk noticed that the viral video was clipped at the timestamp of 18:50 minutes. In the extended video, while addressing the Rajya Sabha, PM Modi said, "Respected Chairman Ji, the coming five years are the era of saturation of basic amenities and we want to change the era of saturation of basic amenities into the era of systems, facilities, type of governance required by a common citizen to live a dignified life. Respected Chairman Ji, the coming five years are the decisive battle against poverty." Further correcting himself, PM Modi says, "The coming five years are decisive years of the fight of the poor against poverty and I believe that when the poor stand up with strength to fight against poverty, then the fight of the poor against poverty achieves success and therefore, the coming five years are decisive years of the fight against poverty and this country will emerge victorious in the fight against poverty, I can say this with great confidence on the basis of the experience of the last 10 years." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Shillong Times published on July 3. The title of the report read, "Next 5 years will see decisive fight against poverty: PM Modi lays roadmap of third term" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of PM Modi's speech was clipped and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo shared in social media post claiming Virat Kohli's statue installed at Times Square is fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo claiming Indian cricketer Virat Kohli's statue was installed at famous Times Square during the T20 World Cup tournament in US. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally created photo was shared on social media with false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on June 26 a photo with the claim that cricketer Virat Kohli's statue was installed at America's famous Times Square during the T20 World Cup 2024 The caption of the post read, "अमेरिका के मशहूर टाइम स्क्वायर पर विराट कोहली का स्टैच्यू लगा। दुनिया के पावरप्ले देश ने भी क्रिकेट जगत में विराट के कद को किया स्लाम। " An English translation of the caption read, "Virat Kohli's statue was installed at America's famous Times Square. The world's power play countries also saluted Virat's stature in the cricket world." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results the Desk came across an X post uploaded by the official handle of Duroflex on June 23. The caption of the post read, "Just Unveiled :A larger-than-life statue of Virat Kohli at the iconic Times Square. This King's Duty, we are going global and making history! We're delivering great sleep and great health to Virat Kohli. #GreatSleepGreatHealth #ViratKohli #worldcup #cricket #CGI" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral photo. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: We also noticed that the caption of the post included the hashtag #CGI, which stands for Computer-Generated Imagery, a technology used in computer graphics to create or enhance images for art, printed media, simulators, videos, and video games. On closely watching the video, the Desk noticed that the blimp overhead overlapping with one of the buildings. This is common in videos and images created through AI and computer technology. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: The Desk further conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find if there was any report to corroborate the claim made in the social media posts. We came across a report published by The Indian Express on June 27. The title of the report read: "Top viral videos today: Nita Ambani explores Varanasi before Anant-Radhika wedding, Virat Kohli's statue in NYC and more" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: For the viral photo and video, the report stated: "The viral footage showed a computer-generated golden statue, complete with cricket pads and holding a bat, standing prominently." The Desk also reached out to Duroflex seeking their response on the viral footage. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a computer-generated photo was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of water leakage from overhead area of Air India flight shared as recent on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, July 10 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of water leaking from the overhead area of an aircraft, claiming that the incident happened recently in an Air India flight. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video dating back to November 2023 was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim An X user shared on July 9 a video of water leaking from the overhead area of an aircraft, claiming it was a recent incident that took place in an Air India flight. The caption of the post read, "पेपर लीक , राम मंदिर लीक , ट्रेन लीक , एयरपोर्ट लीक... सरकारी भवन लीक, सरकारी ऑफिस लीक, की शानदार सफल बम्पर उपलब्धि के बाद अब एयरप्लेन लीक....." An English translation of the caption read, "Paper leak, Ram Mandir leak, train leak, airport leak...After the spectacularly successful bumper achievement of government building leak, government office leak, now airplane leak..." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found her e, here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official channel of Pune Pulse on December 1, 2023. The caption of the post read: "Water drips from overhead bins in Air India flight; Airline releases statement soon after statement soon after #AirIndia #leakageinfilght " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities in this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by the Times of India published on December 1, 2023. The title of the report read, "Shocking video of water leakage on Air India flight goes viral." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Air India flight AI169 operating from Gatwick to Amritsar on November 24 had developed a rare occurrence of condensation adjustment issue inside the cabin. The spokesperson of Air India clarified, "Some of our guests seated in the affected rows were promptly relocated to other vacant seats and given the circumstances the cabin crew made every effort to make the guests comfortable. Air India is committed to the safety and comfort of guests on board and we regret this unexpected incident." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to November 2023 was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video of indiscriminate firing on a man in Brazil shared on social media in name of UP's Muzaffarnagar; details inside
content: New Delhi, July 11 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of indiscriminate firing on a man with a claim that the incident happened in Muzaffarnagar of Uttar Pradesh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was captured during an incident of killing in Brazil and it had no links with UP's Muzaffarnagar. The claim with the video shared in many social media posts is misleading. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a man – seemingly painting walls of a room - who was shot multiple times and claimed that the incident happened in UP's Muzaffarnagar. The caption of the post read: "फिल्मी स्टाइल में किया मर्डर सोशल मीडिया पर जमकर हो रहा है वायरल वीडियो मुजफ्फरनगर जिले का बताया जा रहा है" An English translation of the caption read: "Murder done in filmy style, video is going viral on social media, it is being told of Muzaffarnagar district." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Four such posts can be found here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be viewed here , here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video on C uploaded by BAÚ DO RIO OFC on June 30. The caption of the post read: "DOIDEIRA! Criminoso grava vídeo assassinando um homem conhecido como "Olhão" no bairro Novo Aleixo, em Manaus." An English translation of the caption read: "CRAZY! Criminal records video murdering a man known as "Olhão" in the Novo Aleixo neighbourhood, in Manaus" Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities in this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Portuguese news website Diario Manauara published on June 28. The title of the report read, "CV's 'Olhão' is executed by PCC gunman in Manaus" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Lucas Figueiredo Rodrigues also known as 'Olhão' was murdered with 17 shots on the afternoon of June 28 on Penetração 2 street, in the Novo Aleixo neighbourhood, in the north zone of the capital of Amazonas. Olhão had been arrested for drug trafficking multiple times and had an open warrant issued by the court. He was a member of the Comando Vermelho (CV), originally from Rio de Janeiro, and his death was allegedly carried out by the Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), originally from São Paulo. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check whether any such incident took place in Muzaffarnagar district. We came across an X post by the official handle of Muzaffarnagar Police giving a clarification regarding the viral video on July 11. The caption of the post read: "सोशल मीडिया पर एक व्यक्ति की गोली मारकर हत्या करने की वीडियो को थाना नई मण्डी का बताकर वायरल किया जा रहा है जिसका सम्बन्ध जनपद मु0नगर से नहीं है। भ्रामक वीडियो शेयर करने वाले व्यक्ति के विरुद्ध थाना नई मण्डी पर अभियोग पंजीकृत कर विधिक कार्यवाही की जा रही है । CO नईमण्डी की बाईट-" An English translation of the post read: "A video of a person being shot dead is being made viral on social media claiming it to be from Nai Mandi police station which is not related to Muzaffarnagar district. Legal action is being taken by registering a case against the person who shared the misleading video at Nai Mandi police station. Bite of CO Nai Mandi" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that video of an incident that happened in Brazil was falsely shared in the of Muzaffarnagar on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2014 video of Nitish Kumar's protest demanding special status for Bihar shared as recent on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, July 11 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of Nitish Kumar, claiming that the Bihar CM carried out a foot march demanding special category status for the state. The video was shared to suggest that there were differences between BJP and JD(U), the partners of the ruling NDA at the Centre. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to March 2014, when Nitish Kumar, who was the CM of Bihar back then too, led a foot march in Patna, protesting against the special status given to Seemandhra (the southern region of Andhra Pradesh formed after its bifurcation in 2014) by the then UPA government, while demanding the same for Bihar. The video was shared on social media as recent with misleading claims. Claim An X user shared on July 7 a video of Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, claiming that he recently took out a foot march demanding special category status for Bihar. The caption of the post read: "बिहार को विशेष राज्य का दर्जा देने के लिए सीएम नीतीश कुमार ने पैदल मार्च निकाला है! लालू यादव की कही गई बात का असर होने लगा है!! अगस्त भी आने वाला है!!#bihar #nitishkumar #LaluYadav" An English translation of the caption read: "CM Nitish Kumar has taken out a foot march to give special state status to Bihar! What Lalu Yadav said has started having an effect!! August is also coming!! #bihar #nitishkumar #LaluYadav" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived version can be found here and here respectively. On watching the video, the Desk noticed the logo of ABP News. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of ABP NEWS on March 2, 2014. "Nitish Kumar marches to Gandhi Maidan demanding 'special status' to Bihar," read the description of the video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is combination image comparing the visuals of the two: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report published by DNA on March 02, 2014. The title of the report read, "Nitish Kumar marches demanding special status for Bihar" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the Bihar CM led a 6-km foot march from his residence to Gandhi Maidan in Patna. Kumar called for a state-wide shutdown, demanding special status for the state after the UPA government at the Centre granted special category status to the then newly formed Seemandhra. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 10-year-old video of Nitish Kumar was shared as recent on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Accused of making lewd comment on Captain Anshuman Singh's widow on social media not arrested yet; old photo shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 12 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared two photos, claiming that one of them showed the accused who posted lewd comment about Smriti Singh, the widow of Kirti Chakra awardee Captain Anshuman Singh, in Delhi Police custody. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo was of an accused arrested in a snatching case. The photo was shared on social media with a fake claim and false communal twist. Acting on a complaint by the National Commission for Women (NCW), the Delhi Police on July 13 registered an FIR against a social media user for 'lewd and derogatory' remark on Smriti Singh. However, no arrests have been made in the case so far. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 10 a couple of photos, claiming that one of them showed a lewd comment about Smriti Singh, the widow of Kirti Chakra awardee Captain Anshuman Singh, while the other one showed the accused who made the comment, arrested by the Delhi Police. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The photos were widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of DCP Central Delhi on July 6. The caption of the post read, "Mohd Kasim, a proclaimed offender evading trial in a snatching case, has been apprehended by the diligent efforts of team of PS Hauz Qazi staff. This arrest, based on local intelligence and surveillance, highlights the ongoing commitment to justice and community safety. " Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a report by Times of India, published on July 13. The title of the news report read: "Delhi Police files FIR over 'lewd' comments on late Captain Anshuman's widow Smriti Singh". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to check whether an arrest regarding the incident were done and came across a report by Business Standard on July 11. The title of another report by Business Standard read: "NCW demands arrest over 'lewd comment' made on Smriti Singh: What happened?" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, on July 5, Smriti Singh received the Kirti Chakra, awarded posthumously to her late husband, Captain Anshuman Singh. An X user named 'Ahmed K' posted a derogatory comment about Smriti on one of the pictures of her receiving the award at the Rashtrapati Bhawan. National Commission for Women (NCW) took cognisance of the comment, followed by a written letter to Delhi Police for speedy action against the accused. The commission had called for an immediate FIR and stressed the potential penalties, including up to three years in jail and fines. The Desk then checked the official social media handles of National Commission for Women and came across the letter, demanding a strict action against the accused. The caption of the post read, "National Commission for Women (NCW) has identified a lewd and derogatory comment made by Ahmad K. from Delhi on a photo of a Kirt Chakra Captain Anshuman Singh's widow. This act violates Section 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act, 2000.NCW condemns this behavior and urges immediate police action. Hon'ble Chairperson Ms Rekha Sharma @sharmarekha has sent a letter to Delhi commissioner of Police @DelhiPolice @DCPCentralDelhi to arrest the accused and send A detailed report within 3 days.@CyPAD_Delhi" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated photo was shared on social media with a fake claim and false communal twist.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of crowd raising slogans against Rahul Gandhi during his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra shared as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, July 10 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Congress MP and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi was shared on social media with the claim that he was driven away by people with slogans of 'go back' and 'Anyaya Yatra' during his recent visit to strife-torn Manipur. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video from Gandhi's Assam visit in January this year was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. On July 8, Gandhi visited Manipur, his first visit to the strife-torn state after being elected as the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha. During his visit, Gandhi met with people affected in two relief camps and listened to their plight due to ethnic clashes. Claim An X user shared on July 9 a video of Rahul Gandhi, claiming that he was driven away by the locals during his recent visit to Manipur. The caption of the post read, "This is so soothing to watch. Common people of Manipur raised slogans #RahulGoBack They couldn't take him calling "Hindus Himsaks" and his "Vulture tourism". You know later whom will he blame. He will say they are 'BJP Karyakartas'." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Four such posts can be found here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here , here and here respectively. We went through the posts and noticed several comments, which mentioned that the video was old and from Assam. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Amar Ujala on January 23. The description of the video read, "Assam में Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra का फिर विरोध, भीड़ ने लगाए Rahul Gandhi go back के नारे। Congress" An English translation of the description read, "Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra in Assam opposed again, crowd raised slogans of Rahul Gandhi go back. Congress." Here is the link to the YouTube video: The Desk noticed this was the extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a PTI report carried by Deccan Herald on January 22. The title of the report read, "'Anyay Yatra': Crowd raises slogans against Rahul Gandhi outside eatery in Assam's Nagaon Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident took place when Gandhi and some other leaders stopped at the restaurant in Ambagan on way to their night halt in Rupohi, about 10 km from the site. The crowd raised slogans against the MP and also displayed placards with messages such as 'Anyay Yatra' and 'Rakibul go back', referring to Samaguri Congress MLA Rakibul Hussain. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to January from Gandhi's visit to Assam as part of his Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Instagram user Reshma Sebastian falsely shared in name Captain Anshuman Singh's wife Smriti; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 15 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a woman dancing to a Bollywood song, claiming she was Smriti Singh, the wife of martyr and Keerti Chakra awardee Captain Anshuman Singh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman in the viral video was Reshma Sebastian, an Instagram user based in Kerala. Sebastian's reels were falsely shared in name of Smriti Singh. The claim shared in social media posts is false. Smriti Singh has been grabbing the headlines ever since she, along with her mother-in-law, received the posthumous Kirti Chakra for her husband Captain Anshuman Singh, who died in Siachen in July 2023. Captain Singh's parents have demanded a change in the Indian Army's 'Next Of Kin' (NOK) policy. The policy governs the distribution of financial assistance to families when an Army member dies. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 14 a video of a woman dancing to a Bollywood song and claimed she was Smriti Singh, wife of martyr Captain Anshuman Singh. The caption of the post read: "अपने शहीद पति को मिला हुआ शौर्य चक्र और एक करोड़ रुपए लेकर ससुराल छोड़ कर जाने वाली पत्नी को देखिए... अभी महीना भर नहीं हुआ है... ससुराल में शहीद अंशुमन के माता पिता का रो रोकर बुरा हाल है, ये शहीद की आंखिरी निशानी भी वहा से ले आई है, उन्होंने अपने बेटे का सम्मान, कीर्ति चक्र हाथ में लेकर भी नहीं देखा.. कैसी विडम्बना हैं भाग्य की देखिए जिसको फर्क नहीं वो सब पा गईं और मौज में है, और जिनका बेटा गया वो.... @highlight." An English translation of the caption read, "Look at the wife who left her in-laws' house with the Shaurya Chakra awarded to her martyred husband and one crore rupees... Not even a month has passed yet...Martyr Anshuman's parents are in a bad condition crying in their in-laws house, she has also brought the last memento of the martyr from there, they did not see their son honored even with the Kirti Chakra in his hand.. What an irony of fate. Look, the one who doesn't care got everything and is happy, and the one who lost his son... @highlight" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video on Instagram uploaded by the official account of Reshma Sebastian, who is an actress and model by profession. The caption of the post read: "There are songs, but then there is 'this song' " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: While scrolling through the profile, we also found a post issuing a clarification that this is not the account of the wife of martyr Captain Anshuman Singh. The caption of the post read, "There is a limit.." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then compared the pictures of the woman seen in the viral video with the wife of martyr Captain Anshuman Singh. A screenshot of this comparison can be seen here: We also contacted Reshma Sebastian through email regarding the viral video. "This is very unfortunate. Due to this, my personal and professional life is getting affected. I am thinking of taking legal help from the cyber cell in this matter," she said. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman in the viral video was fashion influencer Reshma Sebastian and not Smriti Singh, the wife of martyr Captain Anshuman Singh. The video was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of Bollywood actors Salman Khan and Aishwarya Rai together at Anant Ambani's wedding is digitally altered; claim shared on social media is false
content: New Delhi, July 15 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of Bollywood actor Aishwarya Rai Bachchan with Salman Khan and his sister Arpita was shared on social media recently with the claim that they posed together at the wedding ceremony of Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant, held recently in Mumbai. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally altered photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 13 a purported photo of actor Salman Khan and Aishwariya Rai posing together at Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant's wedding. The caption of the post read: "Aishwarya didn't arrive with the Bachchan family, and now she's having a picture with Salman bhai. This is my multiverse of madness." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users. Two such posts can be viewed here and here archived posts can be found here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on X too. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post by Zoom TV uploaded on July 12. The caption of the post read: "@beingsalmankhan is looking sharp as he arrives with his sister @arpitakhansharma at Anant Ambani and Radhika Merchant's wedding!" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We further scrolled the Instagram page of Zoom TV and found another video showing actor Aishwariya Rai posing with her daughter at the event. The caption of the post read, "Aaradhya is the replica of mommy @aishwaryaraibachchan_arb🥹❤️ mother-daughter duo look their traditional best at Ambani's wedding!" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that Salman Khan attended the event along with his sister Arpita Khan Sharma, while Aishwarya posed with her daughter. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Subsequently, the Desk concluded a digitally altered photo was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of flooded Mumbai road shared as recent on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, July 12 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of vehicles submerged on a flooded road was shared on social media, claiming it showed the condition of Mumbai following the recent spell of incessant rainfall in the city. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of monsoon flooding in Mumbai, dating back to August 2020, was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 10 a video of vehicles submerged on a flooded road, claiming that it was from Mumbai, following a recent spell of rainfall. The caption of the post read: "This is called Masterstroke of Amrit Kaal" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived posts can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video news report published by The Guardian on August 6, 2020. The title of the report read, "Monsoon rains driven by high winds bring flooding misery to Mumbai" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: According to the video report, "heavy overnight rain in Mumbai severely impacted rail and road traffic, as several parts of the city were waterlogged. The weather office also warned civilians about the "possibility of danger to very old buildings and unmaintained structures." Over 30 people died in a building collapse in Bhiwandi, near Mumbai." Taking a cue from the report, we located Cawasji Patel Tank Road in Mumbai. Using the Google Street View, the Desk noticed the building and signboard were the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to August 2020 was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Congress leader Sonia Gandhi shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A monochrome was shared on social media recently with the claim that it showed senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi from her young days, holding a cigarette. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an AI-generated photo was shared on social media as real with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 12 a purported monochrome of a woman holding a cigarette in her hand, suggesting that she was Congress leader Sonia Gandhi. The caption of the post read, "पहचानने वाले को 8500 मिलेंगे खटा खट टका टक" An English translation of the caption read, "The one who identifies will get Rs 8500" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same photo was shared by several other users. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On carefully observing the viral photo, the Desk noticed a watermark at the bottom left with 'Remaker' written on it. On conducting a keyword search on Google, we found that 'Remaker' is an editing tool used for various tasks like changing faces in photos and videos and generating images using artificial intelligence. Below is a screenshot showing the same: The Desk then ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens and found a similar photo uploaded on Tumblr on February 26, 2013. The photo also had a watermark at the bottom right with 'Farzad' written on it. The caption of the photo read, "Ghazale Photographed by Farzad Sarfarazi, 2012." Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the viral image and the original photo. Below is a comparison image comparing the visuals of the two: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally altered photo was shared as real on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of water gushing through roof of Guwahati Airport shared on social media as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, July 16 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that it showed the roof of Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport in Guwahati leaking due to rainfall. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video dating back to March 2024 was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 10 a video claiming that it showed the roof of Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport in Assam leaking due rainfall. The caption of the post read: "थोड़ी सी बारिश के बाद गुवाहाटी अंतरराष्ट्रीय हवाई अड्डे की छत टपकने लगी है? अडानी प्रबंधित इस एयरपोर्ट का एक हिस्सा 3 महीने पहले भी ढह गया था? मोदी जी का मास्टरस्ट्रोक अपने चरम पर है " An English translation of the post read: "The roof of Guwahati International Airport has started leaking after a little rain? A portion of this Adani managed airport had collapsed 3 months ago too? Modi ji's masterstroke is at its best" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video.
