Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the video was old. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a Facebook post by The Assam Tribune on March 31. The caption of the post read: "As Guwahati braces rainfall, Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International (LGBI) Airport witnesses water gushing in through roof. Video Source: X #TheAssamTribune #LGBIAirport #rainfall #guwahati" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by ABP Live on March 31. The title of the report read, "Storm Wreaks Havoc At Guwahati Airport, Video Shows Water Gushing Inside Terminal After Portion Of Roof Collapses" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, heavy rainfall accompanied by a storm wreaked havoc at the Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport in Guwahati on March 31. Due to the sudden downpour, the authorities had to briefly suspend operations and divert six flights to other destinations. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to March 2024 was shared as recent on social media with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of water pipeline bursting in Kerala falsely shared as recent on social media in name of Haryana; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 17 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of water exploding out of a road like a fountain, claiming it to be from Haryana. The video was shared to criticise the BJP-led government in the state, which will go to polls later this year. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video from Kerala, dating back to February 2024, was shared on social media in the name of Haryana with false claim. Claim A Facebook user on July 10 shared a video of water exploding out of a road like, claiming it to be from Haryana. The caption of the video, "चौंकिए मत! ये किसी भूत प्रेत का काम नही है ये है भाजपा का 'विकास' मॉडल है।" An English translation of the caption read, "Don't be shocked! This is not the work of any ghost, this is BJP's 'development' model." Here is the link and archived version of the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived posts can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of 24 News on February 25, 2024. The description of the video read, "കുടിവെള്ള പൈപ്പ് പൊട്ടി നാടാകെ ജലധാര; അപകടം കുന്ദമംഗലം പത്താംമൈലില്‍" An English translation of description read, "Drinking water pipe broke and fountain all over the country; Accident at Kundamangalam Tenth Mile" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is combination comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Asianet News published on February 25, 2024. The title of the report read, "സംഭവം കോഴിക്കോട്, നടുങ്ങി നാട്ടുകാർ, റോഡിൽ പൊടുന്നനെ ഗർത്തം, പിന്നാലെ അഗ്നിപർവത സ്‌ഫോടനം പോലെ ജലപ്രവാഹം!" An English translation of the title read, "The incident happened in Kozhikode, the locals were shocked, there was a sudden pothole on the road, followed by a stream of water like a volcanic eruption!" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident took place around 5:30 pm at the Kundamangalam Pantheerpadam junction. A huge crater formed in the road, causing water to gush out and resulting in a massive traffic jam. Despite being informed, senior officials of the water authority did not reach the spot, leading to protests among the locals. Residents stated that the drinking water pipe had burst six times before this in Pantheerpadam. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to February 2024 from Kerala was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming Rohingya Muslims posed as sadhus in Meerut shared with false communal twist
content: New Delhi, July 17 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was shared on social media claiming to show three Rohingya Muslims caught disguised as sadhus in UP's Meerut. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the three people who were arrested in Meerut were the sadhus from the Nath community. The video was shared on social media with a false communal twist. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of three men, claiming they were actually Rohingya Muslims named Md. Shamim, Altab, and Zubair and accused them of child theft. The caption of the post read, "The public caught 3 Rohingyas roaming around as sadhus in Meerut. The name is Md. Shamim, altab & Zubair . They used to do recce of Hindu localities wearing saffron clothes. The public also accused the three of stealing children." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived posts can be found here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed that watermark of 'Sudarshan Uttar Pradesh' on the viral video. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Sudarshan Uttar Pradesh on July 13. The description of the video read: "Meerut में साधु बनकर घूम रहे 3 लोगो को पब्लिक ने पकड़ा साथ ही लगाया यह आरोप।" An English translation of the video read, "Public caught 3 people roaming around in Meerut posing as sadhus and also made this allegation." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: We then conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Dainik Bhakar on July 12. The title of the report read, "मेरठ में संदिग्ध बताकर पकड़े नाथ समुदाय के साधु:डंडा दिखाकर डराया, पुलिस के पास लेकर पहुंचे लोग, बच्चा चोरी का लगाया आरोप" An English translation of the title read, "Sadhus of Nath community caught as suspects in Meerut: Threatened with a stick, people took him to the police, accused of child theft" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the residents of Prahlad Nagar caught the three sadhus and brought them to the Lisadi Gate Police Station, accusing them of being fake and involved in child theft. Inspector Jitendra Singh of Lisadi Gate Police Station said, "The names of the three are Gaurav, Gopi, and Sunil. All three sadhus are residents of Darwamajiri village, Thana Sadar, Yamunanagar, Haryana. The village head and the local police have confirmed their identity. All three sadhus travel around to earn their livelihood. None of the three has any criminal history." The Desk also came across an X post by the official X handle of Meerut Police issuing a clarification regarding the viral video. The caption of the post read, "थाना लिसाडी गेट क्षेत्र में साधुओ से मारपीट की वायरल वीडियो के सम्बन्ध में पुलिस अधीक्षक नगर मेरठ द्वारा वीडियो बाईट।" An English translation of the caption read, "Video byte by Superintendent of Police, Meerut City, regarding the viral video of assault on sadhus in Police Station Lisadi Gate area." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the three sadhus were not Rohingya Muslims, but belonged to the Nath community.

title: PTI Fact Check: Two old videos from Muzaffarnagar and Venezuela posted in a social media post falsely shared as recent
content: New Delhi, July 18 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a video, which combines two separate clips, showing a group of men from the Muslim community thrashed a biker in the first clip, while the second footage was about some people beheading a person. The social media post was shared with the claim that both incidents happened in India recently. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the first footage in the video was related to an old incident that happened in UP's Muzaffarnagar in 2021, and the other video clip was from an incident that happened in Venezuela in 2018. The old and unrelated clips were combined in one video and shared on social media as recent. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 5 a video, a combination of two clips, that first showed a man being brutally assaulted by a mob, and later a man being beheaded. The video was shared with the claim that it showed a Hindu murdered by a Muslim mob in India. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk fact-checked the two clips in the viral video separately. Here's what we found: Video 1 Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a similar video post on X. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video on X uploaded by Anokhi Satta News Delhi on May 5, 2021. The caption of the post read: "बंगाल हिंसा की आहट अब उत्तरप्रदेश के जनपद मुज़फ्फरनगर में भी, बिजली लाइनमैन पर हमला, हत्या की नीयत से जानवरो की तरह अंदर खीच ले गए अशांतिदूत, भोपा थाना छेत्र के मुस्लिम बाहुल्य गांव सीकरी का हैं मामला, देखिये वीडियो" An English translation of the caption read: "The sound of Bengal violence has now reached Muzaffarnagar district of Uttar Pradesh, an electricity lineman was attacked, the rioters dragged him inside like animals with the intention of killing him, the incident is from Sikri village, a Muslim dominated village in Bhopa police station area, watch the video" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Amar Ujala published on May 5, 2021. Here is the link to the report: According to the report, villagers in Sikri village held Anuj, a lightman, hostage, beating and severely injuring him. The victim reported that Salman, a resident of the same village, arrived with his brother Ayyaz and requested the lineman to change the house cable. When the lineman refused to change the cable without the permission of the Junior Engineer (JE), the brothers became angry. They called their companions Rafi, Khalid, Naz, Aas Mohammad, and Abid, who then dragged Anuj inside a house and beat him up. The police took action and filed a case against Salman, Ayyaz, Rafi, Khalid, Naz, Aas Mohammad, Abid, and an unknown person. Inspector in charge Deepak Chaturvedi stated that a team led by investigating sub-inspector Reshampal Singh arrested five absconding accused: Salman, Ayyaz, Rafi, Naz, and Khalid. They were presented in court and subsequently sent to jail. Hence, the Desk concluded that clip from a three-year-old video from Muzaffarnagar was shared as recent on social media. Video 2 In the next part of the investigation, the Desk again ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a report by Spain-based news website Periodista Digital published on June 19, 2019. The title of the report read, "Las macabras y sangrientas imágenes de la masacre que dejó diez presos decapitados en una cárcel paraguaya" An English translation of the title read, "The macabre and bloody images of the massacre that left ten prisoners beheaded in a Paraguayan prison" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, members of the Primer Comando da Capital, a Brazil-based criminal organization, dismembered an associate of another group within a Paraguayan jail cell resulting in the deaths of 10 inmates and left 15 others injured. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that old and unrelated clips were combined and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Maulana Mahmood Madani's 2022 speech shared on social media with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 19 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind chief Maulana Mahmood Madani, claiming he said "Hindus should leave India if they cannot tolerate their religion". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Madani's speech dating back to May 2022 was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 16 a video of Maulana Mahmood Madani in which he was heard saying that if Hindus could not tolerate their religion, then they should leave India. The caption of the post read, "हमारा मजहब बर्दाश्त नहीं तो हिंदुओं भारत छोड़ दो* *यह आदमी अभी तक जिंदा क्यों है* *इसे तो अब तक मर जाना चाहिए* *यह हरामखोर महमूद मदनी का भतीजा अरशद मदनी है* *यह चाचा-भतीजे देवबंद दारुल उलूम के मुखिया हैं* *जो यूपी-देवबंद में मौजूद है* *सारे आतंक की जड़ यही है*" An English translation of the caption read, "*If our religion is not tolerated then Hindus should leave India* Why is this man still alive? *he should be dead by now* *This bastard is Mahmood Madani's nephew Arshad Madani* *This uncle-nephew are the heads of Deoband Darul Uloom* *Which is present in UP-Deoband* This is the root of all terror" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Four such posts can be found here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here , here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video, uploaded by the official channel of Jamiat Ulama-i-Hind on May 29, 2022. The description of the video read: "Two Days National Governing Body Meeting Jamiat Ulama-I-Hind. 28-29 May Usman Nagar Deoband Presided By: Maulana Mahmood Asad Madani, President Jamiat Ulama-i-Hind 28-29 May 2022 Usman Nagar Deoband" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that the video was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing visuals of the two videos: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from 2:22:25-minute timestamp. In the extended video, Maulana Mahmood Madani can be heard saying, "We (Muslims) are not strangers. We are citizens of this country, and this country is ours, understand well that this is our country. Whatever responsibility we have for this country, we will fulfill it in any situation, Insha Allah. There will be no compromise in it. Our religion is different, our clothes are different, our culture is also different, and our way of eating and drinking is also different and if you cannot tolerate our religion, then go somewhere else." He further added, "People who are heating the market with hatred are in minority. We are already in the majority. You must understand this. For the protection of the country, for the progress of the country, for justice in the country, for the equality of the country, for equal government, Muslims have given and will always give sacrifices." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Maulana Madani's speech was taken out of context and shared on social media on social media with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video of AAP leader Sanjay Singh speaking about Arvind Kejriwal's weight is clipped; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 20 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of AAP leader Sanjay Singh in which he was heard saying that the weight of Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal, lodged in Tihar Jail, "dropped by 8.5 kg, from 70 kg to 81.5 kg". In its investigation, the Desk found a selected portion of Singh's speech was clipped and shared on social media with misleading claim. The complete video showed that while Singh inadvertently mentioned 81.5 kg, he immediately corrected himself and mentioned 61.5 kg. However, that portion of the speech was omitted in the viral video. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 15 a video of AAP leader Sanjay Singh in which he can be heard saying, "When Arvind Kejriwal was arrested on March 21, his weight was 70 kg. And today his weight has dropped by 8.5 kg to 81.5 kg." The caption of the post read, "शिक्षा क्रांति की सबसे ज्यादा जरूरत आम आदमी पार्टी के नेताओं को है जहां उन्हें सिखाया जाए 70-8.5 =81.5 किलो नहीं होता।" An English translation of the post read, "Aam Aadmi Party leaders need an education revolution the most where they are taught that 70-8.5 does not = 81.5 kg." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Aaj Tak on July 13. The description of the video read: "संजय सिंह ( Sanjay Singh ) ने कहा कि अरविंद केजरीवाल ( Arvind Kejriwal ) का वजन 70 किलो से घटकर 61.5 किलो हो गया है. इसके अलावा, उनका शुगर लेवल पांच बार 50 से नीचे गया है, जो गंभीर चिंता का विषय है. जालंधर वेस्ट उपचुनाव में आम आदमी पार्टी के महेंद्र भगत ने 38,000 वोटों से जीत हासिल की है. इन सभी घटनाओं ने भारतीय राजनीति में हलचल मचा दी है और जनता की नजरें इन पर टिकी हुई हैं." An English translation of the description read: "Sanjay Singh said that Arvind Kejriwal's weight has decreased from 70 kg to 61.5 kg. Apart from this, his sugar level has gone below 50 five times, which is a matter of serious concern. Aam Aadmi Party's Mahendra Bhagat has won the Jalandhar West by-election by 38,000 votes. All these events have created a stir in Indian politics and the public's eyes are fixed on them." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found this was the extended version of the viral video. Below is combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the original video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamps of 1:25 to 1:46 minute. In the extended video, Singh can be heard saying, "For your information, I would like to tell you when on March 21 Kejriwal ji got arrested his weight was 70kgs. And as of today his weight has dropped by 8.5 kg to 81.5… 61.5 kg. His weight has dropped from 70 kg to 61.5 kg. His weight has decreased by approximately 8.5 kg since 21 March." Clearly, the inadvertent mistake by Singh was corrected by him immediately after, but that part was omitted and a clipped video was shared on social media to make the misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: X user shared AI-generated photo to falsely claim responsibility for Microsoft global outage; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 21 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a post carrying a photo of him, in which he suggested that he was an employee of CrowdStrike and was responsible for the recent tech outage at Microsoft. Sharing a thread of X posts, the user further suggested that he was fired from the company following the 'glitch'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the user was neither an employee of CrowdStrike, nor he was responsible for the global outage. The video and photo, which showed the logo of CrowdStrike, were AI-generated, which was revealed by the user himself on X. The viral social media post was shared with a fake claim. A defective software update sent by CrowdStrike to its customers disrupted airlines, banks, hospitals and other critical services on July 19, affecting about 8.5 million machines running Microsoft's Windows operating system. The painstaking work of fixing it has often required a company's IT crew to manually delete files on affected machines. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 19 a photo claiming to be an employee of CrowdStrike and stated that he had caused the massive global tech outage at Microsoft. The caption of the post read: "First day at Crowdstrike, pushed a little update and taking the afternoon off " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the same thread, the user shared a video in which he can be heard saying, "It was my first day of work as a new system admin and I was very eager and excited. Let's say I might have actually done a small update in the coding and maybe I shouldn't have done that. But, I got fired. They called me back today and said I really need to come back. However, I am not being called to congratulate me. I am just waiting for my termination documentation…." Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed that the user's hands and fingers were quite different from the shape of his body. A horn-like protrusion was also visible on his head. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: The Desk then checked the video shared by the user and found that there was no bulge on the head of the user and his fingers were also normal. Below is a comparison image comparing the visuals of the two: During our investigation, we found another video on the user's X account, in which he mentioned that the viral image was photoshopped and created with the help of generative AI. Here is the link to the video and below is combination of screenshots of the same: In the video, the user stated that the original photo was from a training session on fake news where he was with some teachers. He edited the same photo using AI and Photoshop, adding childlike hands and a horn-like protrusion on his head. The user also said that he had also made the video claiming that he was fired from his job with the help of AI. The original video was in French language, which was translated into English language with the help of AI. After the video went viral on the internet, the user shared many things related to "learning lessons" from this incident. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a PTI report, which quoted Cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike saying that the issue that has caused major disruptions to companies worldwide was not a security incident or cyberattack. CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz posted on social media platform X that the company "is actively working with customers impacted by a defect found in a single content update for Windows hosts." He said: "This is not a security incident or cyberattack. The issue has been identified, isolated and a fix has been deployed." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the user had shared AI-generated photo and video on social media with fake claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Train accident video from Chile falsely shared in name of India on social media
content: New Delhi, July 21 (Anushka Pandey, Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was shared on social media with the claim that it showed the impact of a recent collision between a Vande Bharat train and the engine of another train. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from an accident in Chile that happened on June 20. The video shared on social media, falsely linking it to India. The video was shared on social media after the recent derailment of Chandigarh-Dibrugarh Express near Gonda Railway Station in UP, in which three passengers lose their lives while 33 others were left injured. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 21 a video, purportedly showing the impact of a collision between a Vande Bharat train and the engine of another train. The caption of the post read, "वंदे भारत चढ़ी इंजन के ऊपर" An English translation of the caption read, "Vande Bharat climbed on top of the engine" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on YouTube as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archived links can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram carousel uploaded by the official handle of CNN Chile on June 20. An English translation of the caption of the post, originally in Spanish, read: "A serious train accident occurred after midnight on Thursday, June 20, at kilometer 26 of Route 5 South, when a freight train and a passenger train that was carrying out speed tests collided head-on, leaving two people dead and nine injured….." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Mirror US on June 20. The title of the report read, "Horror high-speed train collision in Chile leaves at least two dead and nine injured" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a train accident occurred after midnight on Thursday, June 20 when a passenger train, which was heading south, collided with the freight train that was traveling in the opposite direction from the El Teniente mine to the Central Station. The violent crash resulted in the death of two Chileans, aged 43 and 58, who were in the first locomotive of the freight train. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of a train accident in Chile was falsely shared on social media in the name of India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old videos of rain aftermath in Dubai falsely shared on social media in name of Ayodhya; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 22 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video – a combination of two separate clips – in which the first showed a broken road flooded with muddy water and the second clip showed some people crossing a flooded underpass, claiming it to be from UP's Ayodhya. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that old and unrelated videos from Dubai, dating back to April this year and November last year, were combined and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 21 a video - a combination of two separate clips – claiming that it showed the condition of damaged roads and waterlogging in UP's Ayodhya due to rainfall. The caption of the post read, "चंदा दो धंदा लो की एक और परते खुल कर सामने आ गयी है!! प्रभु श्री राम जी ऐसे ना हराया है चंदा चोरो को!! अयोध्या प्रभु श्री राम मंदिर मार्ग" An English translation of the caption read, "Another layer of the give and take donation business has come out in the open!! Lord Shri Ram has not defeated the donation thieves like this!! Ayodhya Lord Shri Ram Mandir Marg " Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk fact-checked the two videos separately. Here's what we found: Video 1 Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the viral video was from Dubai. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report on YouTube uploaded by the official channel New Islamic World on May 10. The description of the video read, "दुबई में आया तूफान और हुई तेज बारिश | Dubai Rain 2024" An English translation of the description read, "Storm and heavy rain in Dubai | Dubai Rain 2024" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is combination image comparing the visuals of the two: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another report by Business Standard, published on April 16. The title of the report read, "Heavy rains: UAE grapples with flood damage, death toll in Oman rises to 18" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, heavy rains lashed the United Arab Emirates, flooding portions of major highways and leaving vehicles abandoned on roadways across Dubai. Meanwhile, the death toll in separate heavy flooding in neighbouring Oman rose to 18 with others still missing as the sultanate prepared for the storm. The rains began overnight, leaving massive ponds on streets as whipping winds disrupted flights at Dubai International Airport. Video 2 In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a Facebook post, dated for November 18, 2023. The caption of the post read: "Dubai after rain" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by NDTV published on November 18, 2023. The title of the report read, "Dubai Roads Flooded After Heavy Rainfall, Thunderstorm" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the roads of Dubai were waterlogged and flooded after heavy rainfall and thunderstorms hit parts of the UAE on November 18. Due to extreme weather conditions, people were advised to avoid beaches and stay indoors. Traffic and flight operations were also affected in the Emirates due the weather. On further investigation, the Desk also came across an X post by the official handle of Ayodhya Police giving a clarification regarding the viral video. The caption of the post read, "कतिपय ट्विटर हैंडल एवं सोशल मीडिया पर प्रसारित असत्य खबर का #Ayodhyapolice खंडन करती है। ट्वीट में दिखाया गया वीडियो अयोध्या का नहीं है। भ्रामक खबर फैलाने वाले व्यक्ति के विरुद्ध अभियोग पंजीकृत किया गया है। #UPPolice" An English translation of the caption read, "#Ayodhyapolice denies the false news being circulated on certain Twitter handles and social media. The video shown in the tweet is not from Ayodhya. A case has been registered against the person who spread the misleading news. #UPPolice" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that old and unrelated clips from Dubai were combined and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of two women beating a saint shared as recent on social media with misleading claims
content: New Delhi, July 23 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of two women beating a man in saffron attire, purportedly a saint. The text plate running on the video claimed that the man in the video was a rapist. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check found an old video dating back to September 2018 was shared as recent on social media with misleading claims. Claim An X user shared on July 21 a video showing two women beating a man in saffron attire. The text plate on the video claimed that the man was a rapist. The caption of the post read: "भगवा वस्त्र में अब संत महात्मा नहीं मिलते...." An English translation of the caption read, "Now, saints and mahatmas are not found wearing saffron clothes..." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Oneindia Hindi on September 28, 2018. The description of the video read: "देहरादून की कचहरी परिसर में एक अजीबोगरीब नजारा देखने को मिला जब कचहरी परिसर में दो महिलाएं एक बाबा की लात-घूसों से पिटाई कर रही थी। यह नजारा देख वहां कई अधिवक्ता एकत्रित हो गए और उन्होंने बाबा को पकड़ लिया। कारण जानने के बाद और लोगों ने भी बाबा की पिटाई शुरु कर दी " An English translation of the description read: "A strange sight was seen in the Kachari complex of Dehradun when two women were beating a Baba with kick-bribes in Kachher campus. Seeing this view, many advocates gathered there and they caught Baba. After knowing the reason and other people also started beating of Baba" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Rajya Sameeksha on September 29, 2018. The title of the report read, "Video: देहरादून में बीच सड़क पर बाबा की धुनाई, महिलाओं ने चप्पलों से जमकर पीटा" An English translation of the title read, "Video: Baba was beaten up in the middle of the road in Dehradun, women beat him with slippers" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the women alleged that Baba had assured them of arranging for their daughter's marriage would be arranged. However, they claimed Baba was forcibly sending their daughters with an unknown person. The women lodged a complaint against Baba, named Dr Advait Ishwasyam, at the Kotwali Police Station. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to September 2018 was shared as recent on social media with misleading claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video of man damaging stone structure of woman is not from France; 2017 video shared on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, July 23 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo of a man disfiguring a stone statue of a woman in France, claiming that he did so because he considered "nudity as sin". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that video of an unrelated incident from Algeria, dating back to 2017, was shared on social media as recent with misleading claim. Claim An X user shared on July 17 a photo of a man disfiguring a stone statue of a woman in France. The caption of the post read, "FRANCE A man destroys the breasts and face of a female statue of a fountain, considering nudity as 'sin' (haram)" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users. Four such posts can be here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report published by Alarabiya News English on December 18, 2017. The title of the report read: "VIDEO: Algerian Salafist vandalizes historical statue of naked woman" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the Ain el Fouara statue, located in the heart of Setif, is placed on top of a fountain built in 1898 by the French sculptor Francis de Saint-Vidal. A Salafist climbed the statue and destroyed it using a hammer and an iron bar, specifically targeting the marble face and chest areas. The Algerian Salafist vandalized the statue as he viewed it as a disgrace and merely a "fetish" depicting a woman stripped of her clothes. Using the Street View, the Desk noticed the structure of the fountain and the statue was the same in the news report. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old incident dating back to 2017 from Algeria was shared as recent on social media as recent with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2015 video of train accident in Mumbai shared on social media as recent with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 24 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a train crashing into barriers and partly mounting the platform was shared on social media, with users suggesting that it was a recent incident that took place in India. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2015 from Mumbai's Churchgate Railway Station, which was shared on social media as recent with misleading claim. The video was shared just days after few coaches of Chandigarh-Dibrugarh Express derailed near Gonda Railway Station in UP, causing three deaths and leaving over 30 people injured. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 23 a video of a train crashing into barriers and partly mounting the platform. The caption of the post read: "रेल मंत्री "अश्विनी वैष्णव" जी ये वीडियो देखिए गजब का वीडियो है! पता ही नहीं चल रहा है स्टेशन है या सर्कस का कोई शो आप बताएं कृपया, भारतीय रेलवे में आखिर क्या चल रहा है? " An English translation of the caption read: "Railway Minister "Ashwini Vaishnav" ji, watch this video, it is an amazing video! It is not clear whether it is a station or a circus show. Please tell us, what is going on in Indian Railways?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of BBC News on June 25, 2015. The description of the video read, "Footage shows a passenger train at Mumbai's Churchgate station overshooting the platform and injuring several people. CCTV footage was released by authorities at Churchgate station showing the moment when the train hit the buffers and partly mounted the platform. Five passengers were injured and train services were disrupted for a while after the crash on Sunday. Railway authorities have blamed "human error" for the incident." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the video news report was related to the same incident, whose video was shared on social media recently. Below is combination image comparing the visuals of the two videos: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Hindustan Times on June 28, 2015. The title of report read: "Panic at Mumbai's Churchgate station as train crashes into dead end" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a local train on June 28, 2015 crashed into the dead end at the Churchgate station in Mumbai, injuring five passengers and disrupting the suburban train services on the Western Railway line. On further investigation, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of the Ministry of Railways giving a clarification regarding the viral video. The caption of the post read, "This is an old video. Please refrain from circulating such videos spreading misinformation." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from Churchgate Railway Station in Mumbai, dating back to 2015, was shared on social media as recent with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Sikh man wearing turban in this viral photo is not General Mohan Singh who participated in WW II; claim in social media post is false
content: New Delhi, July 24 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ); A social media user shared a photo of a Sikh man wearing a turban claiming it's a photo of General Mohan Singh, who fought for Germany in World War II. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the Sikh man in the photo shared in the social media post was Sardar Mohan Singh, who had no connection with any military service or had no involvement in World War II. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. During investigation, the Desk came to know about General Mohan Singh, who was a British Indian Army officer, and he had led the Indian National Army in South East Asia during World War II. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 15 a photo of a man in turban, claiming he was 'Sardar Mohan Singh' who fought for Germany in World War II. The user further claimed that after the war, when Hitler wanted to reward Singh, the latter requested for weapons to liberate India, which were used by the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army). The caption of the post read: "ये हैं सरदार मोहन सिंह, जिन्होने 2nd विश्व युद्ध में जर्मन के लिए लड़ाई लड़ी थी। युद्ध जीतने के बाद हिटलर ने उन्हें इनाम देना चाहा तो सरदार जी ने कहा कि हमें अच्छे से अच्छे हथियार दीजिए, क्योंकि हमें अपने देश को आजाद करवाना है। हिटलर ने फिर उन्हें जो हथियार दिये, वही हथियार आजाद हिन्द फौज ने इस्तेमाल किए और सही मायने मे इस लड़ाई में रंगून में 50 हजार से ज्यादा अंग्रेजी फौज के मारे जाने के बाद ही अंग्रेजो ने भारत छोड़ने का फैसला लिया था। इसमें गाँधी और काँग्रेस का कोई योगदान नहीं था। बाद में इन काँग्रेसियो ने आजादी का सारा credit गाँधी के चरखे को दिया। सरदार मोहन सिंह जैसे महान योद्धा का नाम भारत के इतिहास से गायब कर दिया" An English translation of the caption read, "This is Sardar Mohan Singh, who fought for Germany in the 2nd World War. After winning the war, when Hitler wanted to reward him, Sardar ji said that give us the best weapons, because we have to liberate our country. The weapons that Hitler gave him, the same weapons were used by the Azad Hind Fauj and in reality, in this war, the British decided to leave India only after more than 50 thousand British soldiers were killed in Rangoon. Gandhi and Congress had no contribution in this. Later these Congressmen gave all the credit of independence to Gandhi's spinning wheel. The name of a great warrior like Sardar Mohan Singh disappeared from the history of India." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same photo was shared by several other users. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the Founder's page of the Modern Senior Secondary School in Punjab's Patiala. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the page, the photo featured in it was of Sardar Mohan Singh, who started the school in 1948. "He joined the Imperial Bank of India in 1926, one of the first Indians to do so. However, in early 1944, he resigned from the bank on both principle and policy over the discrimination of Indians in the bank's senior appointments. He then became Managing Director of the State Bank of Patiala from 1944 for a period of nine years." The Desk noticed striking similarities the photo on the page was the same as viral image. Below is a combination image, comparing the two photos: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an article by The Tribune, published on October 8, 2023. The title of the report read: "INA, in words of founder Mohan Singh" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the article, General Mohan Singh, the founder of the Indian National Army (INA), began his military career as a simple soldier and eventually rose to the rank of General. During World War II, after his battalion lost the Battle of Malaya, he proposed raising an army of surrendered Indian soldiers to fight the British with Japanese support. This led to the birth of the INA. Despite initial efforts, the INA, under both Singh and later Subhas Chandra Bose, faced defeats. Mohan Singh noted the Japanese were more interested in using the INA for non-combat functions and propaganda rather than actual combat. In 1943, Bose took over the INA in Singapore, renaming it Azad Hind Fauj. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man in the viral photo was Sardar Mohan Singh, founder of a school in Punjab's Patiala. The post was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Nirmala Sitharaman travelling in Delhi Metro shared on social media as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 25 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman travelling in a metro train was shared on social media recently, with the claim that she used metro for her daily commute to the office. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to May 2024, when Sitharaman took the metro while campaigning in East Delhi during the run-up to 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The video was shared on social media on the day when Sitharaman presented the Union Budget in the Parliament, for a record seventh time. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 23 a video of Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman travelling in a metro train, claiming it was how she commuted daily to her office. The caption of the post read, "She is the current Finance Minister of 4 trillion dollars economy, 5 trillion stock capitalization, 700 billion foreign reserves.She is the Indian Finance Minister Mrs. Nirmala Sitaraman who travels to office by Metro Train every day." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of News Nation on May 17, 2024. The description of the report read, "Nirmala Sitharaman in Delhi Metro: मेट्रो में सफर करने पहुंची निर्मला सीतारमण, फिर देखिए क्या हुआ? लोकसभा चुनाव के बीच वित्त मंत्री निर्मला सीतारमण दिल्ली मेट्रो में नजर आईं. जहां उन्हें देख वहां मौजूद लोग हैरान रह गए और उनके साथ फोटो क्लिक करने लगे ..जिसके बाद जो हुआ उसे देख हर कोई हैरान रह गया.." An English translation of the description read, "Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman was seen in Delhi Metro amid Lok Sabha elections. The people present there were surprised to see him and started clicking photos with him..after which everyone was surprised to see what happened.." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Hindustan Times on May 17. The title of the report read, "Nirmala Sitharaman travels by Delhi Metro, interacts with people| Video" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on May 17 took the Delhi Metro from Laxmi Nagar to reach the venue to campaign for East Delhi BJP candidate Harsh Malhotra. During the journey, she interacted with fellow commuters. On further investigation, the Desk also came across an X post by the official handle of Nirmala Sitharaman Office sharing visuals of her ride in the Delhi Metro. On further investigation, the Desk also came across an X post by the official handle of Nirmala Sitharaman Office sharing visuals of her ride in the Delhi Metro. The caption of the post read: "Smt @nsitharaman travels in Delhi Metro to Laxmi Nagar and interacts with fellow commuters." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of Sitharaman travelling in Delhi Metro was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of Joe Biden with AI-generated voice clone shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 26 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of US President Joe Biden was shared on social media recently with the claim that it showed him making profane remarks about Americans after dropping out of the presidential race. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally altered video of Biden with superimposed AI-generated voice clone was shared on social media with a false claim. The video was shared a day after Biden announced on July 21 that he would withdraw from the 2024 presidential election race, putting the United States into uncharted territory. Biden endorsed Vice President Kamala Harris to be the Democratic nominee. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 22 a video of US President Joe Biden in which he can be heard making profane remarks about Americans. The user claimed that he made the remarks just after dropping out of the presidential race. The caption of the post read: "Breaking Now: President Joe Biden makes his first video address following dropping out of the Presidential race." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk watched the viral video and noticed a lip-sync issue. We then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such videos can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of The White House on July 15. The description of the video read, "President Biden Addresses the Nation" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two: In the original video, Biden was heard speaking, "My fellow Americans, I want to speak to you tonight about the need for us to lower the temperature in our politics and to remember, while we may disagree, we are not enemies. We're neighbors. We're friends, coworkers, citizens. And, most importantly, we are fellow Americans. And we must stand together." He further added, "Yesterday's shooting at Donald Trump's rally in Pennsylvania calls on all of us to take a step back, take stock of where we are, and how we go forward from here. Thankfully, former [President] Trump is not seriously injured.I spoke with him last night. I'm grateful he's doing well. And Jill and I keep him and his family in our prayers. We also extend our deepest condolences to the family of the victim who was killed……….. " On further investigation, the Desk came across an X post shared from the official handle of Biden, in which where the US President announced that he was dropping out of the presidential race for the upcoming November elections. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the Locus AI and Resemble AI , both generative AI voices and robust deepfake audio detection apps. Below are the screenshots of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded a digitally altered video with superimposed audio was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming former Indian cricketer and all-rounder Yuvraj Singh withdrew his retirement is fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 25 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) ; Multiple social media users shared a graphic along with a photo of former Indian cricketer and all-rounder Yuvraj Singh, claiming that he expressed his desire to withdraw his retirement and rejoin the Indian cricket team. This alleged statement surfaced after the India Legends team, captained by Yuvraj Singh, recently won the 'World Championship of Legends' title by defeating Pakistan Legends. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Singh had not made any such statement recently. The former Indian player had expressed his desire to play domestic cricket back in 2020 when he wrote a letter to the then-BCCI President Sourav Ganguly and Secretary Jay Shah. A four-year-old statement was shared on social media as recent, with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 22 a graphic along with a photo of former Indian cricket team all-rounder Yuvraj Singh, claiming that he expressed his desire to withdraw his retirement and rejoin the Indian cricket team. The caption of the post read, "युवराज सिंह ने कहा कि मैं रिटायरमेंट वापस लेकर भारतीय टीम से जुड़ना चाहता हूं क्योंकि, मुझे लगता है मेरे अंदर अभी बहुत क्रिकेट बचा हुआ है और मैं बेहतर करूंसद " An English caption translation read, "Yuvraj Singh said that I want to take back my retirement and join the Indian team because I feel I still have a lot of cricket left in me, and I want to do better." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same photo was shared by another user on Facebook as well. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not find any recent statements by Yuvraj Singh. We also checked Singh's social media handles (Facebook and Twitter) but did not find any announcements. On searching further on Google, we found a report published by Dainik Bhaskar in September 2020. The title of the report read, "युवराज क्रिकेट में वापसी चाहते हैं:रिटायरमेंट के एक साल बाद बीसीसीआई को चिट्‌ठी लिखकर मांगी इजाजत, पंजाब के लिए घरेलू क्रिकेट में खेल सकते हैं" An English title translation read, "Yuvraj wants to return to cricket: One year after retirement, he wrote a letter to BCCI seeking permission to play domestic cricket for Punjab." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found a PTI report from Business Today published on September 20, 2020. The report's title read, "Yuvraj Singh decides to end his retirement; writes to BCCI chief Sourav Ganguly." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Yuvraj Singh had decided to come out of retirement at the Punjab Cricket Association's (PCA) request. Singh mentioned that PCA Secretary Puneet Bali was the first person to offer him the opportunity to come out of retirement for the benefit of Punjab cricket. Bali had told 'PTI' then that Yuvraj Singh had written a letter to BCCI President Sourav Ganguly. During the investigation, the desk also found another PTI report carried by Indian Express on 3 November 2021. In this report, citing Yuvraj Singh's social media post, it was said that Yuvraj Singh can return to the playing field again. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted PTI's Bureau Chief (Sports) Poonam Mehra. She told the desk that this claim starts going viral on social media every 6-8 months. There is no truth in it. At the same time, the PTI Sports Desk also contacted Yuvraj Singh regarding the viral claim, to which he laughed. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral statement about Yuvraj Singh withdrawing his retirement and rejoining the Indian cricket team was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Yeti Airlines plane crash falsely shared as recent on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 26 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ); An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video showing a mid-air tilted plane before a crash, claiming it to be from the recent Saurya Airlines crash at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found an old video dating back to January 2023 from a plane crash of Yeti Airlines that was shared recently on social media with false claims. A Saurya Airlines aircraft crashed during takeoff at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. The incident occurred on July 24 at around 11:00 AM. The flight was bound for Pokhara, with 19 people on board, including aircrew. According to reports, 18 people were killed in the accident. Claim An X user shared on July 24 a video of a mid-air tilted plane before a crash, claiming it to be from the recent Saurya Airlines crash at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. The caption of the post read, "Plane crashes during takeoff in Nepal, killing at least 18. #Nepal #Kathmandu #Planecrash" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Hindustan Times on January 15, 2023. The video's description read, "The terrifying moments of a plane crash in Nepal were captured on video. The viral video of Yeti Airlines with 72 people on board showed that the twin-engine ATR aircraft lost balance mid-air and hit the ground. It can also be seen staggering through mid-air just seconds before landing at the newly built Pokhara International Airport. Watch this video to know more." Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another INDIA TV report published on January 16, 2023. The title of the report read, "Nepal plane crash Updates: Flight with 72-onboard crashes on runway at Pokhara International Airport, 68 dead." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, around 68 people died after a 72-seater Yeti Airlines plane crashed on the runway at Pokhara International Airport in Nepal on January 15. The plane was going to Pokhara from Kathmandu. A total of 68 passengers and four crew members were on board the Yeti Airlines aircraft that crashed between the old airport and the Pokhara International Airport. There were 5 Indians among 15 foreign passengers onboard the Yeti Airlines flight. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from a 2023 Yeti Airlines plane crash was shared on social media as recent, with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2015 video of kids crossing a river on a cable trolley to attend school from Nepal falsely shared in the name of India; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 29 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ); Several social media users shared a video showing a group of children in uniform and carrying bags, crossing a river in a cable trolley to reach school, targeting the government.In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dates back to 2015 and is from Nepal. An old video was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to India. The Kanwar Yatra, which began on July 22 with the start of the month of Sawan, has been making headlines. The government has implemented robust food, security, and lodging arrangements for the Kanwariyas along the Yatra route. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 28 a video of a group of children wearing blue uniforms and bags crossing the river sitting in a cable trolley targeting the government. The caption of post read, "सरकार ने जितनी ताकत कावड़ यात्रा पर लगाई है काश कि थोड़ा सा ध्यान इन स्कूल जाते बच्चों के रास्ते के लिए भी दे देते।" An English translation of the caption read, "The government has put so much effort in Kavad Yatra, I wish it would have paid a little attention to the path of these school going children as well." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results the Desk came across a Youtube video uploaded by the official channel of FreeDocumentary on September 6, 2015. The description of the video read, "Most Dangerous Ways To School | NEPAL | Free Documentary" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: According to the description of the video, in the mountain village of Kumpur, located in Nepal, nearly half of which lies over 4,000 meters above sea level, children face a challenging journey to attend school in the valley. While the village was self-sufficient 50 years ago, now children frequently travel to the city, crossing a dangerous river. Kumpur, spread across 18 farms on Dhap Mountain, is a remote community where families have lived for thousands of years, herding cattle without modern amenities. Despite the constant danger and isolation, parents send their children to school daily, believing in the promise of education. Subsequently the Desk concluded an old video dating back to 2015 from Nepal was shared as recent on social media falsely linking to India.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 news report of an edited newspaper clipping shared as recent on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, July 29 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ); Multiple social media users shared a purported screenshot of a Hindi newspaper which reported an incident in which a "Muslim youth was caught opening fish plates on a track." In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the headline and sub-headline of the viral screenshot were edited and the incident dates back to 2018. The viral screenshot was shared as recent on social media with false claim. The purported screenshot was shared on social media soon after the recent derailment of Chandigarh-Dibrugarh Express near Gonda Railway Station in UP, in which three passengers lost their lives while 33 others were left injured. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 24 a screenshot of a Hindi newspaper reporting an incident where a "Muslim youth was caught opening fish plates on a track." The caption of the post read, "देश में लगातार हो रहे रेल और बस हादसे सामान्य और सिर्फ हादसे नही हैं | लगातार तीसरी बार हिंदुओं के प्रति भाव रखने वाली सरकार के सत्ता में आने के बाद रेल हादसों में इतनी तेजी आई है जो सोचनीय है | अब पटरी की फिश खोलते हुए जो मुगल पकड़ा गया है अगर यह पकड़ा नही जाता और अपनी योजना में सफल होता तो ना जाने कितने परिवार अनाथ होते |और कांग्रेसी तत्व अंतराष्ट्रीय स्तर पर देश की सत्ता को बदनाम करने के लिए हर जोर प्रयास करते" An English translation of the caption read, "The rail and bus accidents occurring continuously in the country are not normal and just accidents. After the pro-Hindu government came to power for the third time in a row, the number of railway accidents has increased so much that it is a matter of concern. If the Mughal who was caught while opening the fish track had not been caught and had been successful in his plan, then who knows how many families would have become orphans? And Congress elements make every effort to defame the country's power at the international level." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation We the viral screenshot was run through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: The screenshot was also widely shared on Facebook. Three such posts can be found here , here , and here , and their archive versions can be found here , here , and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report published by Nayi Duniya on January 20, 2018. The title of the report read, "फिश प्लेट खोलते धरा गया युवक, पलटने से बची देहरादून एक्सप्रेस" An English translation of the title read, "A young man was caught opening a fish plate, Dehradun Express was saved from overturning." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a young man was opening a fish plate from the railway track near Ghaziabad's Muradnagar railway station when three youths caught him, beat him up, and handed him over to the station master. The youth was identified as Fukran Ali, a resident of Bulandshahr. When he removed the fish plate, the Dehradun Express would arrive on the same track shortly afterwards. Muradpur GRP officer Krishan Kumar stated that the accused claimed to be a drug addict who was removing nuts and bolts from the railway tracks to buy liquor. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google. I came across the Ghaziabad edition of Amar Ujala, dated 20 January 2018, and found the original news published in it. The title of the original report read, "किशोरों की सूझबूझ से बचा बड़ा रेल हादसा" An English translation of the title read, "A major railway accident was averted due to the presence of mind of teenagers." Here is the link to the report: The Desk found discrepancies in the original and the viral news reports. Below is a combination image comparing the headlines of the two: According to the report, a major railway accident was averted due to the quick actions of three teenagers identified as Shiva (16), Tushar (15), and Sachin (14), residents of Dayanand Colony, noticed a youth from Bulandshahr removing a fish plate from the Delhi-Meerut railway track and throwing it into the bushes. The teenagers caught a young man named Furkan and handed him to the police. The station master, Gaurav Singh, informed the authorities, and the Dehradun Express was halted at 8:59 a.m. After the fish plate was replaced, the train resumed its journey at 9:46 a.m. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an edited screenshot of a six-year-old newspaper report was shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video showing woman's body in a suitcase shared as recent on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 30 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video showing a woman's body kept in a suitcase, claiming that a Muslim man killed his Hindu girlfriend in a recent incident. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was dated back to 2022, when a man named Gulsher alias Gulbez killed his girlfriend Ramsha in Piran Kaliyar in Haridwar, Uttarakhand. An old video was shared recently on social media with a communal twist. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 28 a video showing a dead girl's body kept in a suitcase, claiming that a Muslim man killed his Hindu girlfriend. The caption of the post read, "इसका अब्दुल तो अलग था इसलिए सुटकेस मे डालकर लाया......." An English translation of the post read, "His Abdul was different, so I brought it in the suitcase….." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by V Ashish Nautiyal, who uploaded the same video on March 25, 2022. The caption of the post read, "नोट- सेंसिटिव कंटेंट पिरान करीयर में लव जिहाद। अपनी प्रेमिका काजल की हत्या कर सूटकेस में लाश को कलियर गेस्ट हाउस से ठिकाने लगाने जा रहा ज्वालापुर का गुलशेर। डिटेल्स @thelaatanews पर कुछ देर में" An English translation of the caption reads, "Note- Sensitive content I love Jihad in Piran's career. Gulsher of Jwalapur is going to dispose of his girlfriend Kajal's body in a suitcase from Kaliyar Guest House after killing her.Details on @thelaatanews in some time." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by News18 published on March 26, 2022. The title of the report read, "कलियर हत्याकांड: सूटकेस में मिली लड़की की लाश, लड़के ने पहले कहानी गढ़ी फिर किया हत्या की वजह का खुलासा" An English translation of the title read, "Kaliyar murder case: Girl's body found in a suitcase, boy first made up a story and then revealed the reason for the murder." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Gulsher, also known as Gulbez, called his girlfriend Ramsha to a guest house in Piran Kaliyar. During the police interrogation, he confessed that they had been in a long-term relationship, and he had been pressuring her to marry him. However, when she refused, he devised a plan and lured her to the guest house, where he suffocated her with a pillow and killed her. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from an incident dating back to 2022 was shared recently on social media with a communal twist.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, deadline for filing income tax returns has not been extended beyond July 31; unrelated advisory shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, July 31 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared screenshot of a purported notice issued by the government claiming that the deadline for filing income tax returns was extended till August 31. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that no such deadline extension was announced by the Income Tax Department. An unrelated advisory issued by the Office of the Press Registrar General of India was misconstrued and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 31 a screenshot of a notice to claim that the central government had extended the deadline for filing income tax returns till August 31. The caption of the post read, "ITR भरने की अंतिम तिथि बढ़ाई गई... अब नई अंतिम तिथि 31 अगस्त की गई.." An English translation of the caption read, "Last date for filing ITR extended... Now the new last date is 31st August..." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively: The post was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here, here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by the Mint published on July 31, 2024. The title of the report read, "ITR Filing FY 2023-24 Last Date: Why are income taxpayers expecting a deadline extension beyond July 31" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the All-India Federation of Tax Practitioners (AIFTP) formally requested the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to extend the deadline for filing income tax returns for the assessment year 2024-25 to August 31 due to technical glitches with the income tax website. However, the Income Tax Department clarified that the deadline for filing ITRs for FY 2023-24 remains July 31, with no extension granted. The report quoted the Income Tax Department "addressing a false social media announcement claiming the ITR filing deadline had been extended to August 31. They clarified that the deadline for filing ITRs for FY 2023-24 remains July 31, with no extension granted. Taxpayers are advised to file their ITRs as soon as possible to avoid penalties or notices." In the next part of the investigation, the Desk noticed that the viral screenshot mentioned that the "Advisory No. 19 of 2024" was issued by the Deputy Press Registrar General and was a continuation to a previous advisory. Taking a cue from this, the Desk again conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across the Press Registrar General of India's portal and found the previous notice on the website. Here is the link to the website and initial circular and below is a screenshot of the same: On further investigating, the Desk found two follow-up circulars issued after the initial notice. The link for the two can be found here and here and below are the screenshots of the same: According to the initial circular, publishers whose periodicals are registered with Office of the Press Registrar General of India (PRGI) are advised to file the Annual Statement online through the Press Sewa Portal. The initial deadline for filing was set for 31 May 2024. But later, two additional circulars were issued for the extension of the deadline for filing the annual statement. The deadline for the same has now been extended to August 31. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the deadline for ITR remains July 31. The viral circular was issued for the publishers registered with PRGI.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Bollywood singer Kumar Sanu didn't sing a song for ex-Pak PM Imran Khan; digitally altered video shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, August 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed Bollywood singer Kumar Sanu singing a song at a concert related to the release of jailed former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of Sanu's concert in Brisbane, held in May this year, was digitally altered with superimposed AI-generated voice clone, and shared on social media with a false claim. Khan has been in jail since last August facing dozens of charges ranging from corruption to leaking state secrets. Claim A Facebook user shared on July 26 a video of Bollywood singer Kumar Sanu singing a song at a concert related to the release of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan. The caption of the post read: "Imran Khan Wazir E Azam Banayenge Naya Pakistan ko Wapas le aaenge" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official Kumar Sanu Classics on May 18. The description of the video read, "Kumar Sanu Live in Concert Brisbane Australia New Zealand Tour 2024."
