Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found this was the extended version on the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended video, the Desk noticed the viral video was clipped at the timestamp of 1:22:20 minutes. In the extended video, Sanu can be heard singing several Bollywood songs. However, in the entire concert he cannot be heard singing any song on Imran Khan. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the Locus.Ai , video detection tool. Below is a screenshot of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Sanu did not sing any song related to the release of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of flooding in China's Guangdong falsely shared in name of Kerala's Wayanad; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A timelapse video of a house getting inundated by floodwater was recently shared on social media with the claim that it was from Kerala's Wayanad, where rainfall-triggered landslides have caused havoc claiming hundreds of lives. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video from China's Guangdong province, dating back to June 2024, was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. As many as 190 people have died and over 200 are missing in the massive landslides that hit Wayanad district earlier this week. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 31 a timelapse video claiming that it showed a house drowning with floodwaters in Kerala's Wayanad. The caption of the post read, "shocking flood video footage from Wayanad." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here, here and here, and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across X post by the official handle of The Epoch Times, which uploaded the same video on June 24. The caption of the post read, "2024年6月16日,梅州市平远县黄田村黄田水库突然泄洪,监控拍下平远县樟演村一处院子被淹没的过程,显示当地水位在3小时内爆长两米。当局宣布,截至6月21日15时,梅州市平远县强降雨灾害共造成38人死亡、2人失联。" An English translation of the caption read, "On June 16, 2024, the Huangtian Reservoir in Huangtian Village, Pingyuan County, Meizhou City suddenly released floodwaters. Surveillance cameras captured the process of a yard in Zhangyan Village, Pingyuan County being flooded, showing that the local water level rose by two meters in three hours. The authorities announced that as of 15:00 on June 21, the heavy rainfall disaster in Pingyuan County, Meizhou City, caused a total of 38 deaths and 2 people missing." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: The Desk also closely watched the video and noticed that the date of recording the video at the top left corner was mentioned as June 16, 2024. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: Meanwhile, on further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk came across an article by a Chinese web portal named Sohcradio. The headline of the article, which used screenshots of the same viral video, read in English: "A shocking man-made tragedy! Heavy rains wreaked havoc in nine provinces of China and floods continued for days. Video of Meizhou flood discharge reveals that Xinjiang is so hot that it melts." Here is the link to the article and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by NBC News on June 21. The title of the video report read, "Historic flooding in southern China kills 47, with more floods feared" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, at least 47 people died due to severe downpours in southern China's Guangdong province, leading to historic flooding and landslides, state media reported on June 21. State broadcaster CCTV announced that an additional 38 fatalities were confirmed in a county under Meizhou city's jurisdiction, adding to the previously reported nine deaths elsewhere in Meizhou. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from China's Guangdong province was shared on social media in the name of India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Selected part of Nitin Gadkari's speech in Parliament about toll tax shared on social media with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Aug 2 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users purportedly shared a video of Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari speaking in the Parliament, and claimed that he announced that people living within 60 km of a toll booth could cross it without paying any fee, just by showing their Aadhar card. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Gadkari's speech in the Lok Sabha, dating back to March 2022, was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 29 a video of Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari, claiming he announced that people living within 60 km of a toll booth could cross it without paying any fee, just by showing their Aadhar card. The caption of the post read: "आपके घर से 60 किमी के भीतर किसी भी टोल बूथ पर कोई टोल शुल्क देय नहीं है। इसके लिए आपको अपने आधार कार्ड का उपयोग करना होगा। @nitin_gadkari यह केंद्र सरकार का आदेश है। " An English translation of the caption read, "There is no toll fee payable at any toll booth within 60 km from your home. You have to use your Aadhaar card for this.@nitin_gadkari This is the order of the Central Government." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of Office of Nitin Gadkari, Minister of Road Transport & Highways, dating back to March 22, 2022. The caption of the post read, "All toll collecting points which are within 60 km of each other on the National Highways will be closed in the next three months. : Union Minister Shri @nitin_gadkari ji" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another video on YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Doordarshan National on March 22, 2022. The description of the video read, "Minister Nitin Gadkari 's reply on discussion on Demands for Grants under the control of the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways 2022-23 in #LokSabha" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found this was the extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended video, the Desk noticed that the viral video was clipped at the timestamp of 21:40 minutes. In the extended video, while addressing the Lok Sabha, Gadkari said, "Shree Nivas Patil ji suggested those who have an Aadhar card and there is a toll nearby, should get a pass. So, I accept the suggestion; wherever these tolls are made and people of that area face difficulty, people will get a pass based on their Aadhar cards." He further adds, "The second thing is that there is no toll within 60 km, and still it is open in some places. Today I assure the Parliament that this is wrong and illegal. After this, within 3 months, if there is more than one toll booth within 60 km, it will be closed." The Desk found Gadkari did not talk about the radius of 60 km from home. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the official website Ministry of Road Transport and Highways to check about the toll tax exemption policies. Here is the link to the website and the document and below is a screenshot of the same: According to Rule 11 of The National Highways Fee (Determination of Rates and Collection) Rules, 2008, exemption from toll tax can be granted if the house is within a 20 km radius of the toll plaza. The applicant needs to submit their documents, and after verification, they will receive the exemption. Subsequently, the Desk concluded a selected portion of Gadkari's speech dating back to March 2022, was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts falsely claimed Sri Lankan cricketer Muttiah Muralitharan danced to Bollywood song in viral video; details inside
content: New Delhi, August 2 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man dancing to a Bollywood song was shared on social media with the claim that the dancer was former Sri Lankan cricketer Muttiah Muralitharan. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the dancer in the viral video was Indian choreographer Kiran Jopale. His video was falsely shared in the name of Muralitharan by users in multiple social media posts. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video of a man, alongside two women, dancing to a Bollywood song and claimed that he was former Sri Lankan cricketer Muttiah Muralitharan. The caption of the post read: "Muralitharan's got some sick moves dayumnnn" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook. Three such posts can be found here, here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named MrKiranJ on July 25. The description of the video read, "TAUBA TAUBA" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing visuals of the two videos: The Desk further scanned the YouTube channel and found that the man in the video was Kiran Jopale, with over 1 million subscribers. Jopale had shared several others of his dance videos on the channel. Here is the link to his YouTube channel and below is a screenshot of his profile. We also scanned his Instagram account, where the same video was uploaded by him on July 22. The caption of the post read, "CAN'T GET OVER WITH THIS VIBE🧿 THANK SO MUCH BANGALORE @dance.inn.bangalore FOR SUCH A MEMORABLE DAY♥️ LOTS OF LOVE @team.kiranj @manasa.jk__ @laharsharma_29" Here is the link to the profile and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also compared the man in the viral video with Muttiah Muralitharan. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man in the viral video was an Indian dancer and choreographer named Kiran Jopale, and not Muttiah Muralitharan.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2 months old video of Palghar woman's murder shared on social media with false claim and communal twist
content: New Delhi, August 3 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video and claimed the footage was of a Muslim man, who killed a Hindu girl. The video showed a man, with what seemed like a spanner in his hand, standing near the body of a woman on the street. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was related to an incident that took place in Maharashtra's Palghar in June 2024, where a woman named Aarti Yadav was killed by her ex-boyfriend Rohit Yadav. The video of the incident was shared on social media as recent with a false claim and with communal twist. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on July 25 a video of a man standing near the body of a woman, with what looked like a spanner in his hand. The user claimed that the man was a Muslim who had killed the woman, who was a Hindu. The caption of the post read: "One more love jihad One more Hindu daughter dead One more case file only One more Muslim jihadi will live his life as ghar Jamai in jail " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by a user named Indian Observer, shared on June 18. The user claimed that the incident took place in Maharashtra's Vasai. The caption of the post read, "#SHOCKINGVISUALS : A man brutally kills his lover in the middle of the road with Spanner in Vasai, Asks 'Kyun Kiya Aisa Mere Saath'. The motive behind the assault was reportedly a recent breakup after a two-year relationship. #Mumbai #Vasai #Murder #Crime #MumbaiMurder" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Hindustan Times on June 19. The title of the report read: "29-year-old man arrested for battering girlfriend to death with spanner on busy Vasai road" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the accused, identified as Rohit Yadav, followed his girlfriend, Aarti Yadav, to work, intercepting her in the middle of the road. He assaulted her with a heavy spanner and continued to hit her until she collapsed motionless on the road. Rohit and Aarti, both residents of Nalasopara, had been in a relationship for the past six years. Aarti worked in a factory in Vasai East, while Rohit, who was unemployed, became upset after seeing her talking to male colleagues. The police stated that Yadav was booked under Section 302 (murder) of the Indian Penal Code. In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the Maharashtra Police website and accessed the FIR filed in the case. Here is the link to the FIR and below is a screenshot of the same: The FIR clearly stated that the lone accused in the case was Rohit Shriramnivas Yadav. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of the incident was shared on social media with a false communal twist.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming athlete Avinash Sable secured India's first gold medal at Paris Olympics are fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 5 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared posts claiming that track and field athlete Avinash Sable secured the first gold medal the country in the ongoing Paris Olympics. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that India is yet to win a gold medal in the event. The social media posts were shared with fake claim. India has so far won three bronze medals in the Paris Olympics. Sable will be seen action in the Men's 3000 m Steeplechase later today. Claim An Instagram user shared on August 3 a post claiming that Avinash Sable secured India's first gold medal in the Paris Olympics 2024. The caption of the post read, "पेरिस ओलंपिक भारत का पहला गोल्ड मेडल 🥇🥇👌✅" An English translation of the caption read, "Paris Olympics: India's first gold medal" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Business Standard published on August 5. According to the report, Sable will represent India in the Men's 3000 m Steeplechase event on August 5. The title of the report read, "Paris Olympics 2024: India schedule on August 5, live time (IST), streaming" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found a complete schedule of events for Day 10 on the official website of Paris Olympics 2024. According to the report, Avinash Mukund Sable will represent India in the men's 3000 m steeplechase run at 10:34 PM on August 5. Below is a screenshot of the schedule: In the next step of investigation, the Desk scanned the official website of Paris Olympics 2024 and found the medal tally of India, along with the names of winners. The title the report read, "Paris 2024 Olympics medal tally: Indian winners from every sport - full list and table" Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: Manu Bhaker won the first medal for India at the Paris 2024 Olympics, securing a bronze and becoming the first Indian woman shooter to win an Olympic medal. She made history again by becoming the first Indian to win two medals at a single Olympics, after clinching a Mixed Team 10m Air Pistol bronze with Sarabjot Singh. Additionally, Swapnil Kusale won a bronze medal in the Men's 50m rifle 3 positions event. Subsequently, the Desk concluded India has not won any gold medal so far in the ongoing Paris Olympics.

title: PTI Fact Check: Four-year-old video of road caving in near a tunnel in Turkey falsely shared on social media in name of India; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 5 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a road caving in near a tunnel, with the captions insinuating that it was from India. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video from Ordu, Turkey, dating back to July 2023, was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 3 a video showing a road caving in near a tunnel, claiming to be from India. The caption of the post read, "Anything and everything he's ever built is crumbling right before our eyes... Soon we'll be back where we were in 2014..." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the viral video was from Turkey. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of World Events News on Jul 23, 2023. The description of the video read, "In this short video, you'll see a shocking moment when a major road collapse and landslide occurs in Ordu, Turkey. Be sure to watch to the end to see the incredible aftermath!" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by a Turkish news portal Alanya Postasi published on July 12, 2023. The title of the report read, "Tünel çıkışı yol çöktü! Bakan bir daha baktı" An English translation of the title read, "The road at the tunnel exit collapsed! The minister looked again" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the landslides occurred on July 11 due to heavy rain along the Ordu leg of the Black Sea-Mediterranean Road, indirectly affecting 50 provinces. The heavy water flow caused the culverts of the Çağlayan Stream in the Darıcabaşı Tunnel area on the Mesudiye district border to collapse, disrupting transportation from Ordu to the Mediterranean. Subsequently, the Desk concluded an old video dating back to July 2023 from Ordu, Turkey was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2001 photo of landslide in El Salvador falsely shared as recent in the name of Wayanad; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 5 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo, claiming that it showed a large area of land washed off in the recent landslides in Kerala's Wayanad. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo of a landslide that occurred in El Salvador in 2001 was shared as recent on social media with a false claim. The devastating landslides in Kerala's Wayanad on July 30 have killed more than 300 people and injured over 200 others, according to government officials. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 1 a photo, claiming that it showed a large area of land washed away in the recent landslide in Wayanad. The caption of the post read, "#WayanadLandslide Today Wayanad , tomorrow it may be Tamilnadu- Nilgiris or Kanyakumari, stop blasting rocks for your personal gain in Western ghats!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report published by NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) on February 13, 2006. The Desk noticed that the feature image in the article was the same as the viral photo. The description on the website read, "Gridding the Risks of Natural Disasters" Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption of the photo read: "The 2001 ElSalvador earthquake-induced landslide, located in a neighbourhood near Santa Tecla, El Salvador, buried numerous homes under tons of earth. The Hotspots report identified El Salvador as being at high risk for landslides, earthquakes, floods, and cyclones. Photograph by Edwin L. Harp/Courtesy USGS." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another report by The Guardian, published on January 15, 2001. The title of the report read, "El Salvador earthquake" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a landslide devastated the town of Santa Tecla, near San Salvador, following an earthquake that measured 7.6 on the Richter scale. The aerial view revealed extensive destruction caused by the massive landslide. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old photo of a landslide in El Salvador, dating back to 2001, was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Four-year-old photos from landslide in Idukki shared as recent on social media in the name of Wayanad; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Ever since devastating landslides hit Kerala's Wayanad on July 30, social media has been abuzz with photo and videos claiming they are related to the recent calamity. The PTI Fact Check Desk found four such photos and a video shared with the claim that they showed the aftermath of landslides in Wayanad. In its investigation, the Desk found that two of the photos were from a 2020 landslide that occurred in Kerala's Idukki district 2020. The old and unrelated photos were shared on social media with a false claim. The devastating landslide in Kerala's Wayanad on July 30 killed at least 308 people and injured over 200, according to government officials. The number of casualties is feared to rise, as 240 people are still missing and many are believed to be trapped under the debris. The Desk fact-check four photos and a video shared in the name of Wayanad. Here's what we found: Photo 1 A Facebook user shared on July 30 a photo of NDRF officials carrying out a rescue operation after a landslide claiming to be from Wayanad. The caption of the post read, "बेहद दुःखद खबर केरल से भीषण बारिश से लैंडस्लाइड, मलबे में दबे 100 से ज्यादा लोग, 8 लोगों की मौत। हे भोलेनाथ बाबा वहाँ के लोगो का रक्षा करे। #Wayanad#WayanadLandslide" An English translation of the caption read, "Very sad news from Kerala Landslide due to heavy rains, more than 100 people buried under the debris, 8 people died.Oh Bholenath Baba, please protect the people there. #Wayanad#WayanadLandslide" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and came across a PTI report carried by Business Standard on August 9, 2020. The title of the report read, "Kerala landslide: Toll rises to 26; search on to locate missing persons" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that the feature image of the news report was the same as the viral image. Below is a combination image comparing the two: According to the report, around 20 houses of tea estate workers in the high-range Idukki district of Kerala were destroyed due to a massive landslide on August 8, 2020. Approximately 65 estate workers were killed when an avalanche crashed down on the tea plantation workers in the Kanan Devan Hills of Idukki district. Photo 2 A Facebook user shared on July 30 a photo of a car struck by a landslide, claiming it to be from Wayanad. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and came across a report by Asianet News published on July 30, 2024. The title of the report read, "Wayanad में बर्बादी के वीडियो, Landslides ने तहस नहस की जिंदगी" An English translation of the title read, "Videos of devastation in Wayanad, landslides destroyed lives" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral photo. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Photo 3 An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a photo of a rescue operation of a landslide in front of a tea plantation, claiming to be Wayanad. The caption of the post read, "Massive #landslides hit Kerala's #Wayanad district. Pray for Wayanad " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We ran the photo through Google Lens and came across a report by Hindustan Times published on August 8, 2020. The title of the report read, "Photos: Landslide in Idukki kills 15 people, NDRF teams rushed" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the feature image of the news report was the same as the viral photo. Below is a combination image comparing the two photos: According to the report, debris remained scattered on the ground after a landslide in Idukki on August 7. Concurrently, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a red alert for Idukki on the same day, predicting extremely heavy rainfall of over 20 centimeters in the coming days. Photo 4 A Facebook user shared on July 30 a photo of a person's hand caught under the debris after a landslide in Wayanad. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Further while investigating, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google lens and came across a report by News12 India Malayalam published on July 30, 2024. The title of the report read, "വയനാട്ടിലെ മേപ്പാടി മുണ്ടക്കൈയിലും ചുരല്‍മലയിലും ഉണ്ടായ വന്‍ ഉരുള്‍പൊട്ടലില്‍ മരണ സംഖ്യ ഉയരുന്നു. ഇന്നലെ രാത്രി 2 മണിക്കാണ് ആദ്യ അപകടം നടന്നത്." An English translation of the title read, "Death toll rises in massive landslides at Meppadi Mundakai and Churalmala in Wayanad. The first accident happened at 2 o'clock last night." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral photo. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: According to the report, heavy rains in the southern coastal state of Kerala triggered landslides in the hills of Wayanad district, sending torrents of mud, water, and tumbling boulders downhill, sweeping people to their deaths. Although the bodies were found in the Chaliyar river, the landslide occurred in a residential area, trapping many people and likely causing numerous fatalities. In Mundakai alone, around 300 families were affected by the landslides. Video 1 An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video showing a car trapped amidst a landslide caused by heavy rain in Wayanad. The caption of the post read, "बेहद दुःखद खबर केरल से भीषण बारिश से लैंडस्लाइड, मलबे में दबे 100 से ज्यादा लोग, 8 लोगों की मौत। हे भोलेनाथ बाबा वहाँ के लोगो का रक्षा करे। #Wayanad#WayanadLandslide" An English translation of the caption read, "Very sad news from Kerala Landslide due to heavy rains, more than 100 people buried under the debris, 8 people died. Oh Bholenath Baba, please protect the people there. #Wayanad#WayanadLandslide" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation We then ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of The Indian Express which uploaded a similar video on July 30. The caption of the post read, "At least 50 people have died after massive landslides ravaged Wayanad, Kerala. "The ground shook violently, and within seconds, everything was gone," said a resident who narrowly escaped. "We heard a thunderous noise and then saw our neighbours' house being swallowed by the earth," another survivor recounted, his voice trembling. Villagers are speaking of their terror and loss, with many saying, "We watched helplessly as our homes were swept away."" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Republic World published on July 30. The title of the report read, "Wayanad Landslide: Video Captures Massive Destruction; Houses, Vehicles & Roads Washed Away" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a bridge connecting Chooralmala to Mundakkai and Attamala collapsed after landslides in the hills of Wayanad district. One car and a jeep can be seen stuck amid uprooted trees and rapidly flowing water. This collapse isolated the two places and hindered rescue personnel from reaching trapped families. The rescue and relief operations, coordinated by the Army, NDRF, SDRF, and civil administration, are underway at multiple locations, ensuring the quick evacuation of stranded people and the provision of basic amenities and medical assistance. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that two photos were related to a landslide that occurred in Idukki district 2020, where as the remaining two photos and a video were indeed related to the recent landslide in Wayanad.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 videos of protesters storming former Sri Lanka President's residence falsely shared as recent in name of Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 6 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Soon after news of Sheikh Hasina resigning as Bangladesh PM and left the country, social media has been abuzz with videos, claiming they showed protesters lying on her bed and enjoying in her private swimming pool after storming into the former PM's residence in Dhaka. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the videos dated back to July 2022 when protesters stormed the then Sri Lankan President Gotabaya Rajapaksa's house in Colombo, when the country went through an economic and subsequent political turmoil. Old and unrelated videos were shared on social media as recent with false claims. On August 5, Hasina, 76, resigned as prime minister of Bangladesh and left the country amid unprecedented mass protests against her government. She later arrived in India on her way to London. Video 1 A Facebook user shared on August 5 a video, claiming that it showed protesters lying on the bed of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina at her residence in Dhaka. The caption of the post read, "Scenes from Sheikh Hasina's bedroom" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a report by Hindustan Times published on July 10, 2022. The title of the report read, "President's house or tourist spot? Sri Lanka protesters relax in bedrooms, work out in gym | Watch" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, protesters stormed Sri Lankan President Gotabaya Rajapaksa's house after he resigned from his position. On July 10, 2022, the premises virtually turned into a new picnic spot, with people strolling through the balconies, relaxing in the bedrooms, working out in the gym, and dining in the kitchen. The same photo featured in a photo gallery, published by India Times on July 12, 2022, whose headline read: "These pictures show how Sri Lanka protesters enjoy the luxuries of the Presidential palace." Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: Video 2 An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 5 a video, claiming that it showed protesters enjoying in the private pool at former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina's residence. The caption of the post read, "People of Bangladesh bathing in Sheikh Hasina Wajid's swimming pool" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation While watching the viral video the Desk noticed the super running on the video that read: 'Sri Lanka Crisis. Protesters storm President Rajapaksa's residence'. Below is a screenshot of the same: We then ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of The Telegraph on July 9, 2022. The description of the video read, "Sri Lanka's President Gotabaya Rajapaksa fled his official residence in Colombo shortly before protesters gathered to demand his resignation and stormed the compound." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that old videos dating back to 2022 from Sri Lanka were shared as recent on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated videos shared on social media to falsely claim Indian Army entered Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 7 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : Amid the ongoing protests and political turmoil in Bangladesh, two videos were shared on social media with claims that they showed Indian Army personnel entering the crisis-hit country to suppress the protests. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that old and unrelated videos were shared on social media with false claims. On August 5, Sheikh Hasina fled Bangladesh shortly after resigning as the PM, in wake of the violent protests against her government, which claimed over 300 lives. Hasina landed in Delhi in a military helicopter, and later left for London, where she is reportedly seeking asylum. The Desk debunked both videos categorically. Here's what we found: Video 1 A Facebook user shared on July 20 a video, claiming that it showed Indian Army vehicles entering into Bangladesh via West Bengal border. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was posted by a Facebook user on June 23, 2022. The user posted the video along with an emotional note for the Indian Army. Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that the government had not made any announcement regarding sending Indian Army troops to Bangladesh. During our investigation, we found a statement issued by the Ministry of External Affairs on July 21, regarding the return of students in wake of the protests in the neighbouring country. Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: Video 2 An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 6 a video, claiming that it showed a group of Indian Army personnel at an airport in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "ইন্ডিয়ান সেনাবাহিনী বাংলাদেশের এয়ারপোর্টে কেন..?" An English translation of the caption read, "Why is the Indian army at the Bangladesh airport..?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same; Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the personnel in the viral video were from APBN. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across the official Facebook page of Airport Armed Police Battalion. We then scanned the profile and found several photos of the personnel in uniform. Here is the link to the profile and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the uniform looked similar to what the personnel wore in the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the two: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that old and unrelated videos were shared on social media as recent, falsely linking them to the ongoing crisis in Bangladesh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of public hanging of a Awami League leader in Bangladesh shared on social media with false communal narrative
content: New Delhi, August 8 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed an elderly Hindu man lynched and publicly hanged by Jamaat-e-Islami, one of the largest Islamic parties in crisis-hit Bangladesh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the man in the video was Shahidul Islam Hiran, chairman of Porahati Union Parishad in Bangladesh. The viral post was shared on social media with a false claim and communal twist. According to a report in PTI, there has been a spike in crime against the minority Hindu community and the destruction of Hindu temples in Bangladesh following the ouster of the Sheikh Hasina-led government earlier this month. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 6 a video and claimed that it showed an elderly Hindu man being lynched and publicly hanged by extremists raising religious slogans in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "Heartbreaking 💔 An old Hindu man is lynched and hanged on a statue by terrorists of Jamaat-e-Islami in Bangladesh. IsIamists were seen raising AIIah-Hu-Akbar slogans around him... #SaveBangladeshiHindus" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here, here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the man in the viral video was an Awami League worker and not a Hindu. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Dhaka Post on August 5. The title of the report read, "গুলি করেও বাঁচতে পারলেন না আলোচিত হিরণ চেয়ারম্যান" A rough English translation of the title referred to the killing of one 'Hiran chairman'. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Jhenaidah Sadar Upazila Awami League General Secretary Shahidul Islam Hiron and his driver Akter Hossain were killed by miscreants who hacked and burned them at Hiron's home. Hiron's body was later found hung in Piara Chattar. Additionally, two agitators died while setting fire to a former Chhatra League leader's house in Kaliganj upazila. These incidents, which injured several people, occurred on August 5 in Jhenaidah town and Dhakale Para. On further scanning the search results, the Desk also came across a YouTube video uploaded by a user named Hazrat Ahammad on August 6, which claimed to show the public hanging of Hiron. The description of the video read, "ঝিনাইদহ জেলা হরিনাকুন্ড আমলীগ নেতা হিরন কে মেরে ফেলা হয়েছে ঝিনাইদহ পায়রা চত্বরে তার লাশ টাঙ্গানো" An English translation to the description read, "Jhenaidah District Harinakund Amlig leader Hiron was killed and his body was hanged in Jhenaidah pigeon square." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to locate Piara Chattar and came across a photo uploaded by Wikimedia Commons. The title of the photo read, "Payra chattar, jhenaidah" Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the YouTube video. Below is a combination of comparing the visuals of the two: Subsequently, it was concluded that the deceased in the viral video was not a Hindu. The social media posts were shared with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old Protest video from Bangladesh misleadingly shared with false communal claims on social media
content: New Delhi, August 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a girl with her hands and legs tied and mouth taped was circulated on social media, with the claim that it depicted the massacre of Hindus in violence-stricken Bangladesh. However, PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that the video was actually part of a protest at Jagannath University in Dhaka against a student suicide. The unrelated and outdated video was falsely presented as recent, with a misleading communal narrative. The video was shared amid reports of increased violence against minority Hindus and attacks on Hindu temples in Bangladesh. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 7 a video of a girl, with the hands and feet tied and her mouth taped, claiming she was a Hindu captured in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "हिंदु लड़की को इस तरह से बंदी बनाया जा रहा है बांग्लादेश में हिंदुओं का नरसंहार किया जा रहा है बांग्लादेशी हिंदुओं के लिए प्रार्थना करें … और भारत सरकार चुप चाप देख रही है @DrSJaishankar @RSSorg @PMOIndia#SaveBangladeshiHindus #Bangladesh #Hindus #" An English translation of the caption read, "Hindu girl is being held captive like this Hindus are being massacred in Bangladesh Pray for Bangladeshi Hindus… And Indian government is watching silently @DrSJaishankar @RSSorg @PMOIndia" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post uploaded by a page named 'JnU Short Stories' on July 26. The caption of the post read, "আপনাদের গুজবের কারণে মেয়েটা আজ ট্রমার মধ্য দিয়ে জীবন পার করছে। মেয়েটি জগন্নাথ বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় ২০২১-২২ শিক্ষাবর্ষের একজন সাধারণ ছাত্রী। এই ভিডিওটি কিছুদিন আগে অবন্তিকা আত্মহ*ত্যার প্রতিবাদ স্বরূপ পথ নাটকের দৃশ্যপট! কিন্তু কিছু মানুষ ভিডিওটিকে বর্তমান আন্দোলনের সময়কার উল্লেখসহ মেয়েটিকে ছাত্রলীগের নেত্রী হিসাবে উপস্থাপন করে ছড়িয়ে দেয় ফেসবুকে যা মুহুর্তে ভাইরাল হয়ে যায়। মেয়েটি এসব দেখে ট্রমার মধ্য দিয়ে জীবন পার করছে। আজ যদি মেয়েটিও অবন্তিকার মতো আত্মহ*ত্যার পথ বেচে নেয় তার দায়ভার কে নিবে?মেয়েটির পাশে দাড়ান সবাই, যেখানেই এই ভিডিওটি দেখবেন কমেন্টে প্রতিবাদ সহ রিপোর্ট করবেন। যত পারি এই পোস্টটা শেয়ার করে এই গুজবকে বন্ধ করি প্লিজ! " An English translation of the post read, "The girl is going through trauma today because of your rumours. The girl is a regular student of Jagannath University in the academic year 2021-22. This video is the scene of the path play as a protest against Avantika's suicide a few days ago! But some people shared the video on Facebook, presenting the girl as a leader of the Chhatra League with references to the current agitation period, which went viral instantly. The girl is going through the trauma of seeing this. Today, if the girl commits suicide like Avantika, who will take her responsibility? Everyone stand by the girl, wherever you see this video, report it with protest in the comments. Please share this post as much as possible to stop this rumour!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Ajker Patrika on July 27. Here is the link to the report According to the report, following the suicide of a student named Fairuz Avantika, students at Jagannath University organised various forms of protest, including dramas, silent plays, and torch processions, to demand justice against those who allegedly instigated the suicide. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of 'SOMOY TV' on March 18, 2024. A rough translation of the title of video read: "Oppressed Avantika returned to Jagannath campus! | Abantika | Jagannath University | Student Protest". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: At 1:04 minutes, the Desk noticed that a girl wearing the same attire as the viral video. Below is a combination image, comparing the two visuals: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that video from a student protest at Jagannath University in Dhaka was shared on social media with a false communal angle.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old Photo of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina crying misleadingly shared as recent from India: Details Inside
content: New Delhi, August 9 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo circulating on social media claims to show former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina in tears after arriving in India amid violent protests in her country. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that the image is actually from her visit to a vandalised metro station in Bangladesh on July 25. The photo was inaccurately shared on social media with a false claim. Hasina, on August 5, fled the country after resigning as Bangladesh PM. This came after hundreds of people were killed in a crackdown on demonstrations that began as protests against job quotas and swelled into a movement demanding her downfall. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 5 a photo of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina, claiming that it showed her crying after landing in India. The caption of the post read, "Bullet Breaking,- 1st picture of Ex Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina after she reaches India after Coup by Bangladesh Army. Seen crying in this pic." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and came across a BBC report, published on July 26. The title of the report read, "Scorn as Bangladesh PM weeps at train station damage" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the then Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina visited the vandalised metro rail station at Mirpur 10 on July 25 morning. She inspected various parts of the station, which had been severely damaged during the recent student protests calling for reform of the public service quota system. Metro rail services were suspended on July 18 due to the ongoing demonstrations by students demanding quota reform in public service. On further scanning the search results, we came across another report published by AFP on July 25. The title of the report read, "BANGLADESH - UNREST - STUDENTS" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded the viral photo predated the events stated in the social media posts.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated photos from mass protests in Myanmar and China falsely shared as recent in name of Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 10 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): In the aftermath of the violent protests and political unrest in Bangladesh, several photos were circulated on social media, including three images claimed to be recent depictions of protesters armed with self-defense gear. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that these photos were old and unrelated, and were shared with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 4 three photos, claiming that they showed protesters in Bangladesh equipped with self-defence gear. The caption of the post read, "Some Self defence equipment. আমার ভাইয়ে রেডি খেলার জন্য!শুভকামনা রইলো সবার জন্য" An English translation of the caption read, "Some self defense equipment. Ready to play my brother! Good luck to all" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same; Investigation The Desk fact-checked all three photos categorically and here's what it found: Photo 1 The Desk ran the first photo in the post through Google Lens, and came found that the same photo was carried in a news report, published by Wyoming Public Media on March 3, 2021. The title of the report read: "At Least 18 Killed In Another Bloody Day For Myanmar" Here is the link and archive link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, protesters blocked the road against the military coup in Myanmar's Mandalay. It further stated that at least 18 people were reportedly killed, and eight journalists have also reportedly been arrested while covering the protests. was one among the deadliest in Myanmar since the coup. Photo 2 We ran the second photo through Google Lens and found that another Facebook user had the shared the same pic on August 4. The caption of the post read, "Some Self defence equipment. আমার ভাইয়ে রেডি খেলার জন্য! শুভকামনা রইলো সবার জন্য সবাইকে জানিয়ে দেন, কেউ যেন খালি হাতে না আসে৷ পতাকার সাথে রড, বাঁশ নিয়ে আসতে হবে৷" An English translation of the caption read, "Some self defense equipment. My brother is ready to play! Good luck to all He informed everyone that no one should come empty-handed Rod, bamboo should be brought along with the flag" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is s screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report published by The New York Times on April 17, 2021, which had carried the same photo. The title of the report read, "Myanmar's Protesters Face Down the Military With Slingshots and Rocks" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption of the photo read: "Protesters using slingshots during a protest in Yangon, Myanmar, last month." Photo 3 The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and came across a Facebook user shared on August 4, which carried the same photo of a man wearing tear-gas protective gear. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same photo on the website of Shutterstock Images, uploaded on August 24, 2019. The description of the photo read: "Protesters take part in an anti-government march in Hong Kong, China" Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Daily Mail published on August 24, 2019. The title of the report read, "Hong Kong protests turn violent again as police in riot gear brandishing batons fire tear gas and charge huge crowd of protesters who respond with barrage of stones, bottles and bamboo poles" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The caption of the photo read: "Protesters take part in an anti-government march in Kwun Tong, Hong Kong on August 24. Hong Kong has been engulfed in protests since early June". Subsequently, the Desk concluded that old photos and unrelated photos were shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, viral photo doesn't show house of cricketer Liton Das being set ablaze in Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 8 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared two photos – one of Bangladeshi cricketer Liton Das and the other of a house set on fire – and claimed that the house of the cricketer, who is a Hindu by faith, was set ablaze by 'Islamists' amid the ongoing violent protests in the country. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the house in the photo was of former Bangladesh cricketer and Awami League MP Mashrafe Bin Mortaza, and not Liton Das. The post was shared on social media with a false claim and communal twist. The claim comes in wake of the reported spike in attacks on minority Hindus and Hindu temples in the neighbouring country, which has been marred by violent protests against the Sheikh Hasina-led government and political turmoil lately. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 5 photos showing a house on fire and Bangladesh cricketer Litton Das with Hindu idols, claiming that Das's house was set ablaze amidst the protests in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "He is Liton Das, a Bangladeshi cricketer. He is a national Hero of Bangladesh.His house was set on fire by Islamists. This is the condition of an elite Hindu of Bangladesh. Just imagine the condition of common Hindus. #SaveBangladeshiHindus" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The photo was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by Himanshu Pareek, a sports journalist, shared on August 5. The caption of the post read: "Former cricketer Mashrafe Murtaza's house has been SET ON FIRE in Bangladesh by the protesters." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Firstpost, published on August 6. The title of the report read: "Watch: Former Bangladesh captain Mashrafe Morataza's house set on fire by protestors" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, vandals attacked and set Mortaza's house on fire after the Prime Minister left the country following widespread student protests. Mashrafe Mortaza, a Member of Parliament from the Narail-2 constituency in Khulna division, won his seat as an Awami League candidate led by Sheikh Hasina in the general elections in 2024. The incident was also reported by Dhaka Tribune on August 5. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by Prothom Alo, a Bangladeshi newspaper. The video, uploaded on August 5 showed agitators setting ablaze the house of Mortaza in Narail. Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that house on fire seen in the video was of former cricketer and Awami League MP Mashrafe Bin Mortaza, and not former cricketer Liton Das.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old 2022 Video of Solapur train derailment misleadingly circulated as recent incident on social media
content: New Delhi, August 10 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a derailed train in a field near the railway tracks was shared on social media with a misleading claim that the event recently occurred in Bhiwani, Haryana. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that the video actually dates back to September 2022 and is from Solapur, Maharashtra. Despite this, the video went viral after a recent derailment involving an engine and a wagon on the Rewari-Bhiwani section of the Bikaner division in Bhiwani district. Although no one was injured, the incident caused temporary disruption on the line late at night. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 8 a video of a train derailed and having entered a nearby field and claimed that the incident happened recently in Haryana's Bhiwani. The caption of the post read, "हरियाणा में भिवानी स्टेशन के पास ट्रेन पटरी से उतर खेत में घुस गई। रेल मंत्री "रील मंत्री" बने हुए हैं। लापरवाही चरम पर है। किसी की कोई जवाबदेही नहीं। जनता लाचार और बेबस है।" An English translation of the caption read: "A train derailed near Bhiwani station in Haryana and entered a field. The railway minister has become a "Reel Minister". Negligence is at its peak. No one is accountable. The public is helpless and powerless." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a similar video on YouTube, uploaded by the official channel of NEWS9 Live on August 8, 2024. The description of the video read: "In Bhiwani, Haryana, a goods train derailed and left the tracks, causing it to enter a field. This incident led to the short termination of 8 trains and changes in the routes of many others. Watch the viral video capturing the aftermath of the derailment and the impact on train services." Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The found the video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of ABP Majha on Sep 4, 2022 . The description of the video read, "Freight Train Accident in Solapur : मालगाडी रुळावरुन घसरुन थेट शेतात, करमाळ्यातील घटना" An English translation of the description read, "Freight Train Accident in Solapur: A freight train derailed directly into a farm, incident in Karmala" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. The combination image below, comparing the visuals of the two videos, shows that number mentioned on the coach was likely the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by the Times of India on September 5, 2022. The title of the report read, "Pune-bound freight train derails at Kem in Solapur district; no injuries reported" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a Pune-bound goods train carrying cement derailed along the loop line at Kem village in Karmala tehsil of Solapur district around 2:30 am on September 4. The train, which had departed from Solapur, saw its engine and several wagons go off the tracks. Preliminary inspections by railway officials suggest that brake failure may have been the cause of the derailment and no casualties were observed in the accident. On further investigation, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of Divisional Railway Manager (DRM), Solapur giving a clarification on the viral video. The caption of the post, dated August 8 read, "आज सोलापूर मण्डल पर ऐसी कोई घटना नहीं घटित हुई है। यह २०२२ की घटना है। कृपया ऐसी भ्रामक पोस्ट ना डाले। इनसे भारतीय रेल्वे के १२ लाख कर्मियों का हौसला कम ना करे।" An English translation of the caption read, "No such incident has happened in Solapur division today. This is an incident from 2022. Please do not post such misleading posts. Do not demoralize the 12 lakh employees of Indian Railways by doing this." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to September 2022 was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Vandalised Rabindranath Tagore statue from 2023 resurfaces on social media with false recent incident claim
content: New Delhi, August 7 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a vandalised statue of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore recently went viral on social media platforms, falsely claimed to depict a recent incident in violence-hit Bangladesh. However, PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that the photo actually dates back to an event at Dhaka University in 2023. The old image was misleadingly shared as a current event. Violence-hit Bangladesh is reeling under a major political crisis, triggered in mid-July over a controversial quota system rule. The violence began on July 16, after clashes broke out between the protesting student activists at Dhaka University and supporters of the ruling Awami League Party. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 7 a photo of a vandalised statue of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore and claimed that the incident happened in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "Desecrated & decapitated - the composer of #Bangladesh's national anthem! Homage to Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore on his death anniversary today…." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by English Loktej, published on February 19, 2023. The title of the report read: "Head found of Tagore sculpture that 'disappeared' from Dhaka University" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "The dismatled head of a sculpture of Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore, that was removed from the campus of Dhaka University, has been found by some passersby at the premises of the ongoing 'Amar Ekushe' Book Fair here, Shimul Kumbhkaar, leader of Bangladesh Chhatra Union, Dhaka University, told IANS on Saturday," read a section of the report. "On Thursday, Dhaka University (DU) authorities had reportedly removed the statue of Tagore, which the university students constructed next to the Raju Memorial sculpture. The students built the symbolic sculpture of Tagore on Tuesday to protest against the recent banning and censorship of books at the 'Amar Ekushe' Book Fair," it added. On further investigation, the Desk came across another report by the Dhaka Tribune, published on Feb 18, 2024. The title of the report read: "Rabindranath sculpture returns at DU (Dhaka University)." The report carried several photos of the statue, including the one shared on social media recently. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded an old and unrelated photo was falsely linked to the ongoing violence in Bangladesh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of student protesters tying up Chhatra League Leaders at Dhaka College misrepresented with false communal narrative on social media
content: New Delhi, August 11 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media shows two women tied to a pillar and being verbally abused, accompanied by claims that they are Hindu victims in Bangladesh. Some users further alleged that the women were held captive and sold by Muslims amidst violence in the country. However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the incident occurred at Begum Badrunnessa Government Women's College in Dhaka, where student protesters had tied up members of the Chhatra League in opposition to the quota reform movement. The video was falsely portrayed with a communal narrative on social media. In the context of ongoing violence and political instability following the ousting of the Sheikh Hasina-led government on August 5, reports have surfaced about increased attacks on the minority Hindu community and the destruction of Hindu temples in Bangladesh. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 7 a video, suggesting that it showed Hindu women being tied up to a pillar in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "देख लो हिंदूओं... बहुत प्यार है ना तुम्हें भाईचारा से मुग़लों ने क्या क्या किया नहीं पता , कोई नी वो इतिहास है अब तो समझो, देखों और सुनो अंधे मत बनो जागों प्यारे जागों " An English translation of the caption read, "Look Hindus... you love brotherhood a lot, don't you?You don't know what the Mughals did, it's history. Now understand, see and listen, don't be blind. Wake up dear, wake up." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Four such posts can be found here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here, here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by Dhaka Age on July 17. The description of the video read, "বদরুন্নেসা কলেজ ছাত্রলীগ নেত্রীদের বেঁধে রাখলেন শিক্ষার্থীরা, মুহূর্তেই ভাইরাল" An English translation of the description read, "Badrunnesa College Chhatra League leaders tied up by students, instantly viral" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that this was the same as viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Bangladesh news portal Priyo, published on July 17. The title of the report read, "ছাত্রলীগ কর্মীদের বেঁধে রাখলেন শিক্ষার্থীরা, করালেন কান ধরে ওঠবস" An English translation of the title read, "The students tied the BCL workers, made them sit by their ears" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident occurred on Wednesday, July 17, around 2 PM, in the residential dormitory of Begum Badrunnessa Government Women's College. During the altercation, a group of students tied two Bangladesh Chhatra League (BCL) workers to a pillar using black rope, while others were made to sit with their ears held as punishment. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the event predated Hasina's resignation as PM and the video of the unrelated incident was shared on social media with a false communal angle.

title: PTI Fact Check: Misleading video claims Hindus killed in Bangladesh violence; fact check reveals footage from electrocution incident during Rath Yatra
content: New Delhi, August 12 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) ; A video showing several people lying on the road, seemingly dead or injured, was recently circulated on social media with claims that they were Hindus killed in violence-stricken Bangladesh after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's resignation. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that the video, which dates back to July, actually depicts a tragic incident in Bogra, Bangladesh, where people died from electrocution during Jagannath Dev's Rath Yatra. The video was misleadingly shared with a false communal narrative. The video surfaced amid reports of increased attacks on the minority Hindu community and the destruction of Hindu temples in Bangladesh following the ouster of the Sheikh Hasina-led government earlier this month. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 9 a video of several people lying on the road, and claimed they were Hindus killed in violence in crisis-hit Bangladesh. The caption of the post read: "#SaveHindusInBangladesh" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such claims can be found here and here and their archived claims can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk the scanned the comments on the viral posts and came across a user claiming the video to be from an old incident that happened during Rath Yatra. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official chan2nel of Desh TV News on July 7. The description of the video read, "5 people died due to electrocution during Rath Yatra in Bogra Bogra Rath Yatra | Desh TV News" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two; On further investigation, the Desk came across a report published by Bangla News 24, published on June 7, 2024. The title of the report, originally in Bangla, read: "Five dead, 25 injured due to electrocution during Rath Yatra in Bogra". The Desk noticed that the feature image of the article was the same as one of the visuals in the viral video. Below is a combination image, showing the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by Dhaka Tribune, published on July 7. The title of the report read, "Electrocution leaves 5 dead during Ratha Yatra in Bogra" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the accident occurred during the Ratha Yatra in Bogra's Seujgari area on July 7. Witnesses, including the chariot driver Govinda, stated that the event began around 5 pm at the Iskcon temple in Seujgari, attracting a large crowd. Some participants rode in the chariot while others walked alongside, holding the ropes. About 15 minutes into the procession, as the chariot reached Seujgari Amtala, its metal dome made contact with a high-voltage overhead wire, causing it to catch fire. The accident led to the electrocution and injury of approximately 50 people, with five losing their lives. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false communal narrative.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming India purchased 28 islands from Maldives are fake: Details inside
content: New Delhi, Aug 15 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check): Multiple social media users recently shared posts claiming India purchased 28 islands from the Maldives, and stated that it was the result of PM Modi's visit to Lakshwadeep Islands. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the inauguration of India-funded water and sanitation project in 28 Maldivian islands was misconstrued and shared on social media with a false claim. The social media claims were made in wake of External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar handing over a significant water and sanitation project to Maldives, valued at approximately Rs 923 crore, which will benefit 28 islands, covering seven percent of the archipelago's population. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 12 a post claiming that India purchased 28 islands from Maldives. The caption of the post read: "India bought 28 islands from Maldives. Maldives handover its 28 Islands to India. President Muizzu himself signed the agreement.The magic of 50 meters walk on Lakshadweep beach and one tweet. Rest the team at MEA managed.Work in silence and let ur work shout LOUD" Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The post was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check the veracity of the claim. While we could not find any such report on India "buying islands from Maldives", the search led us to a PTI report carried by India Today on August 13. The title of the report read: "Jaishankar launches Maldives' largest India-funded sanitation project". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar was on a three-day official visit to Maldives where he handed over a massive water and sanitation project worth USD 110 million funding from India to 28 islands covering seven per cent of the population of the archipelagic nation. On further investigation, the Desk came across a press release by the Ministry of External Affairs on August 11. The title of the report read: "Visit of External Affairs Minister to Maldives (August 09-11, 2024)" Here is the link to the press release and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across an X post by the official handle of Dr S Jaishankar, carrying a broadcast link of the virtual inauguration of Water and Sanitation Projects on August 10. The caption of the post read, "Virtual inauguration of Water and Sanitation Projects in 28 Islands of Maldives." Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: We also checked the official social media handles of the President of Maldives Dr Mohamed Muizzu and came across a post expressing his gratitude towards the Indian government. The caption of the post read, "It was a pleasure to meet @DrSJaishankar today and join him in the official handover of water and sewerage projects in 28 islands of the Maldives. I thank the Government of India, especially Prime Minister @narendramodi for always supporting the Maldives. Our enduring partnership continues to strengthen, bringing our nations closer through cooperation in security, development, and cultural exchange. Together, we build a brighter, more prosperous future for the region." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We then conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find reports related to the purchased 28 islands from the Maldives and came across a report by CNBC TV18 published on August 13. The title of the report read, "MEA calls out 'fake' social media posts claiming Maldives handed over 28 islands to India" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the controversy surfaced following External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar's recent three-day visit to the Maldives. During this period, several social media users falsely claimed that India had "purchased" 28 islands from the Maldives, alleging that an agreement was signed by President Muizzu. The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) has since clarified that these claims are baseless and misleading, stressing that no such agreement exists between the two countries. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that social media posts regarding "India buying 28 islands from Maldives" were fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: Misleading video of Chhatra League woman leader harassed by protesters circulates on social media with false communal claims; Fact Check Inside
content: New Delhi, August 13 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video showing a woman being forced to do sit-ups by a group of protesters has been circulating on social media with the false claim that she was a Hindu targeted in the unrest in Bangladesh. Some posts even alleged that she was raped and killed by the mob.
