However, a PTI Fact Check investigation revealed that the woman is Sagorika Akhter, a Chhatra League leader from Eden Women's College. The video, shared as recent, was falsely portrayed with communal overtones. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 9 a video of a Hindu woman crying and being forced to do sit-ups by a mob. The post further claimed that the woman was stripped, raped, and burned alive while religious slogans in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "भयावह ये हैं बांग्लादेश की ज्योतिका बसु-चटर्जी। एक ऐसी महिला जिन्होंने एक मानवतावादी संगठन चलाते हुए हिंदू मुस्लिम सभी की शिक्षा और स्वास्थ्य पर अथक प्रयास किया। धर्म जाति भूलाकर उन्होंने गरीब महिलाओं की हरसंभव मदद की। लेकिन जैसे ही दंगे शुरू हुए, कट्टरपंथी पुरुष और महिलाएं सब कुछ भूल गए - मैडम ज्योतिका से उठक-बैठक कराई गई। - इसके बाद बीस लोगों ने उन्हें निर्वस्त्र कर रेप किया। - फिर धार्मिक नारे लगाकर उन्हें जिंदा जला दिया। ज्योतिका के भाई ने इसका लाईव वीडियो बनाकर भारत सरकार से मदद मांगी और बहन ज्योतिका की कहानी बताई. बाद में उसे भी जिंदा जला दिया गया!" An English translation of the caption read, "Horrifying This is Jyotika Basu-Chatterjee from Bangladesh. A woman who ran a humanitarian organization and tirelessly worked for the education and health of all Hindus and Muslims. She helped poor women in every possible way, regardless of religion and caste.But as soon as the riots started, the fundamentalist men and women forgot everything. - Madam Jyotika was made to do sit-ups. - After this, twenty people raped her after stripping her naked. - Then she was burnt alive while chanting religious slogans. Jyotika's brother made a live video of this and asked for help from the Indian government and told his sister Jyotika's story. Later, he too was burnt alive!" Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post shared by Mahdy Hasan Talha, a sports journalist from Bangladesh, on July 17. The caption of the post read: "পালাতে চেয়েছিলেন ইডেন মহিলা কলেজ ছাত্রলীগের নেত্রী সাগরিকা আক্তার, কিন্তু সাধারণ শিক্ষার্থীরা তাকে আটকে কান ধরে উঠবস করিয়েছেন।" A rough translation of the caption in English read: "Sagarika Akhter, leader of Eden Women's College Chhatra League, wanted to escape, but ordinary students caught her and made her sit by her ear." Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the girl in the video was the same as the one seen in the viral social media posts. Below is a combination image showing the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an X post shared a user named Shohanur Rahman. The user mentioned an article, calling it out for falsely identifying the woman in the video as Jyotika Basu. "She is Sagarika Akhter, a Muslim and a female Chhatra League leader from Eden Women's College. This video and incident is from July 17. She is not Jyotika Basu, as mentioned in your fabricated story. She was punished for standing against students and torturing them using political power. RW propaganda handles are continuing to spread anti-Bangladesh communal propaganda," read his X post, shared on August 10. Here is the link to the post. On further investigation, the Desk came across a report published by Barta 24 on July 29. The report carried a photo of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina meeting Akhter. The title of the report read, "প্রধানমন্ত্রীকে নির্যাতনের বর্ণনা দিতে গিয়ে কাঁদলেন ছাত্রলীগ নেত্রী" An English translation of the title read, "Chhatra League leader cried while describing the torture to the Prime Minister" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, on July 29, the then Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina met with leaders and activists who were injured and tortured in attacks at various colleges and universities. During the meeting, one of the leaders (Akhter) broke down in tears while recounting the horrific torture experienced during the quota reform movement. In the next part of investigation, the Desk tried to verify the claims made around the woman's alleged rape and murder, but could not find any report substantiating the claim. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman in the viral video was Sagorika Akhter, a Muslim leader of the Chhatra League from Eden Women's College. An old video was shared on social media with communal twist.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming Olympic medallists Neeraj Chopra and Manu Bhaker getting married are fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 14 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): As Manu Bhaker and Neeraj Chopra grabbed the limelight on social media with their Olympic medal victories, several users went on to claim that the two were all set to get married. The rumours emanated from videos of Bhaker and Chopra chatting with each other, and another one of Chopra having a conversation with Bhaker's mother during the recently concluded Paris Olympics. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the claims made on social media were mere false rumours. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 12 photos of Olympic medallists Neeraj Chopra and Manu Bhaker, claiming that the two were getting married. The caption of the post read, "ओलंपिक मेडलिस्ट नीरज चोपड़ा व मनु भाकर दोनों का अपने माता-पिता की मौजूदगी में रिश्ता तय! पवित्र बंधन में बंधने के लिए उज्ज्वल भविष्य की अनन्त शुभकामनाएं! सूत्र के हवाले से ख़बर।" An English translation of the caption read, "Olympic medalists Neeraj Chopra and Manu Bhaker's marriage was fixed in the presence of their parents! Best wishes for a bright future for tying this sacred knot! News from the source." Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned social media platforms and found that the set of photos Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. During the investigation, the Desk came across a report published by Hindustan Times on August 13. The title of the report read: "Manu Bhaker's father clears the air as fans link her with Neeraj Chopra: 'She's too young'" Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: "Following the viral memes and posts, Manu Bhaker's father, Ram Kishan Bhaker, has opened up, sharing that she is "still too young" and they are "not thinking of her marriage"," read a section of the report. The report further quoted Manu Bhaker's father Ram Kishan Bhaker telling Dainik Bhaskar: "Manu is still very young. She is not even of marriageable age. Not even thinking about it right now." While commenting on the viral video showing his wife and Neeraj Chopra, Ram Kishan said: "Manu's mother considers Neeraj like her son". On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another report by NDTV Sports, which quoted Manu herself rejecting the speculations. Here is the link to the report titled 'Manu Bhaker Breaks Silence On Viral Video With Neeraj Chopra. Says, "During Events..."', and below is a screenshot of the same: "I don't know much about it. I was not there when this happened. But since 2018 we have been meeting on the sidelines of events. We don't have that much interaction otherwise. During events we talk a little. But there is no truth to the rumours that is going around," Bhaker was quoted as saying in the report, in response to a query regarding the speculations. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the social media posts were shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Pakistan's Independence Day celebration in Canada digitally altered and falsely linked to Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): In wake of violent protests and ensuing political turmoil in Bangladesh, a video was shared on social media with the claim that it showed people waving Pakistan flags and chanting pro-Pakistan slogans in the country. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an unrelated video of Pakistan's Independence Day celebration in Canada in August 2023 was digitally altered and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 8 a video showing people waving Pakistan flags and chanting pro-Pakistan slogans in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "Real Face of Students Movement in Bangladesh: Bengali Muslims with Pakistani flags chanting "Direct Action"" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named Salman official on August 15, 2023. The title of the video read, "Pakistan Independence day celebration||2023|| Canada||Gerrard St" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a cutomised keyword search and came across several other videos on YouTube from the same event. Two such videos can be seen here and here respectively. While watching one of these videos, the Desk noted striking similarities suggesting that they were from the same event as the viral video. A combination image below shows the same two women as can be seen in the viral video: In the next step of investigation, the Desk closely watched the viral videos as well as those showing visuals of Pakistan's Independence Day celebrations in Canada. We noticed several shops seen in the background, such as Lahore Tikka House and Desi Burger, and on geolocating them, we found them to be on Gerrard Street in Toronto, Canada. Below are the screenshots showing the same: One DJ Mian also posted a video on Instagram on August 25, 2023, from the same event. "Abhi Toh Party Shuru Hui Hai #djmian #fyp #beatofthenorth #gerrard #pakistanindependenceday #pakistan #blockparty," read the caption of the video post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: While it was confirmed that the video was from Canada and not Bangladesh, the Desk tried to ascertain the truth behind the slogans in the viral video. We watched several videos from the same event but could not find any Bangla slogans being raised. So, we reached out to one of PTI reporters with a fair knowledge of Bangla, who confirmed to us that the slogans were against former Bangladesh PM Khaleda Zia, asking her to go to Pakistan. On conducting another customised keyword search, the Desk came across a 2018 video on YouTube in which the same slogan was used. The headline of the video, originally in Bangla, read: "Khaleda of Pakistan go back to Pakistan." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video from Pakistan Independence Day celebrations in Canada, dating back to August 2023, was digitally altered to superimpose an unrelated Bangla slogan to it, and it was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show Vinesh Phogat breaking down after her disqualification at Paris Olympics: Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Indian wrestler Vinesh Phogat was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed her breaking down after her disqualification from the women's 50kg freestyle final at the recently concluded Paris Olympics. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old and unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. On August 14, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) rejected Vinesh Phogat's appeal against her disqualification from the 50 kg category final at the Paris Olympics. Phogat was disqualified for being 100 grams overweight during the second weigh-in on the morning of her gold-medal match. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 10 a video of Indian wrestler Vinesh Phogat breaking into tears and claimed that it was from after disqualification at the recently concluded Paris Olympics. The caption of the post read: "See and feel that unlucky time when @Phogat_Vinesh was disqualified at the Olympics so called "100gm" overweight rules " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Four such posts can be found here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed the watermark of 'nnis' on the viral video. Taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an extended version of the video on the official channel of N1 Media Consultancy Private Limited. The description of the video read, "Vinesh Phogat showing why she is the 'Queen Bee'" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended video, the Desk noticed a banner with the logo of 'SAI' (Sports Authority of India) and Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports-Patiala written on it. Below is screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk further scanned Google Lens search results and came across an X post by the official handle of nnis Sports sharing the same video on March 12, 2024. The caption of the post read, "Vinesh Phogat got emotional after winning the 50kg final, securing her berth for the Asian and World Olympics Qualifiers!" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We then conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find reports related to the latter's reaction after her disqualification at the Paris Olympics and came across a report by Hindustan Times published on August 16. The title of the report read, "Vinesh Phogat's heartbreaking first reaction to CAS dismissing her plea for joint silver at Paris Olympics" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Vinesh Phogat made history by becoming the first Indian woman to reach an Olympic final in wrestling, defeating Cuba's Yusneylis Guzman in the semi-final. However, she was unexpectedly disqualified from the gold medal match after being found 100 grams overweight during the weigh-in the following morning. On August 14, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) dismissed her appeal for a joint silver medal. Following this decision, Vinesh shared her first public reaction, posting a photo on Instagram of herself lying on the mat with her hands on her head, without adding a caption. Here is the link to the Instagram post Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to March 2024 was shared as recent, falsely linking it to her disqualification at the Paris Olympics.

author: Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Amitabh Bachchan Did Not Voice Video Discussing Indian Hindus; AI-Generated Audio Misleadingly Attributed to Actor
content: New Delhi, August 17 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media, featuring various visuals and a voiceover urging Indian Hindus to unite, has been falsely attributed to Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan. PTI Fact Check's investigation revealed that the video was digitally manipulated, with AI-generated audio superimposed over the original content, leading to the false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 12 a video with the claim that Bollywood star Amitabh Bachchan voiced it to urge Indian Hindus to unite. The caption of the post read, "अमिताभ बच्चन की आवाज मे, बहुत सुंदर तथ्य पेश किया है, चलो कम से कम बुढ़ापे मे समझ आया इस बच्चन को..👆🫵हिंदूओं समझ जाओ और ईकठ्ठा हो जाओ.." An English translation of the caption read, "In the voice of Amitabh Bachchan, very beautiful facts have been presented, at least this Bachchan understood this in his old age..👆🫵Hindus understand and unite.." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The Desk then noticed the logo of Google with 'Appu Patel BJP' written inside it. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a Facebook profile with the name 'Appu Patel BJP', that had shared several videos with the same logo, as the viral one. Here is the link to the profile and below is a screenshot of the same: While we couldn't find the viral video on the profile, we found several videos made in similar style using edited visuals and audio. Two such videos can be seen here and here . In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the TrueMedia and Resemble AI , both generative AI voices and robust deepfake audio detection apps. Below are the screenshots of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated audio was superimposed on the edited video, which was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2017 video of Virat Kohli condemning violence against women edited and shared in name of Kolkata doctor case
content: New Delhi, August 20 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Indian cricketer Virat Kohli was circulated on social media with the false claim that it captured his remarks on the rape-murder of a trainee doctor at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital in Kolkata. PTI Fact Check's investigation revealed that the video was actually from 2017, where Kohli spoke against a mass molestation incident in Bengaluru. The video was edited and shared with a misleading narrative amidst the ongoing outrage over the tragic Kolkata case. The video was shared on social media amid the nationwide outrage over the alleged rape and murder of a medic at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital and the chilling details of the incident which came to light later. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 18 a video of cricketer Virat Kohli condemning the violence against women following Kolkata doctor rape and murder case. The caption of the post read, "Listen What Virat Kohli Is Telling About Dr ****** Cas And The Society We Live In" Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. While further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a thread of videos, shared by Kohli on X on January 6, 2017. The caption of the post read, "This country should be safe & equal for all. Women shouldn't be treated differently. Let's stand together & put an end to such pathetic acts" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and noticed that it was same as the one shared on social media recently. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: In this original video, Kohli can be heard saying, "Guys what happened in Bangalore, is really really disturbing. To see something like that happen to those girls and for the people to watch it and not do anything about it I think it is a cowardly act. Those people have no right to call themselves men. I have only one question. If something like that happened God forbid to someone in your family, would you stand and watch or would you help? That's my only question. And I think these things are allowed to happen and people stand there and watch these things happen and they are fine with it because they think its absolutely fine for something like that to happen to a girl just because she's wearing short clothes. It's her life, it's her decision, it's her choice for men to accept that it's an opportunity for us to do something like this and get away with it and people in power who try to defend it, its absolutely horrible. I think as a society, the fact that these things are certain…… " Following this, the cricketer shared another video with the caption, "Change your thinking and the world will change around you." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Here he further adds, "the fact that these things are in..certain people's heads acceptable to a certain degree. It's disturbing and shocking and I'm aff.. and ashamed, ashamed to be a part of that society. I think we need to change our thinking. We need to treat men and women in the same way and be respectful and treat women with compassion and as I said put yourself in that situation and think what if we were the family members of those girls, how would we feel about it..Jai Hind!" The Desk noticed the former skipper talked about an incident in Bangalore and nowhere mentioned about the recent Kolkata rape and murder incident. Meanwhile, in the viral video, words like "what happened in Bengaluru", "those girls" were omitted. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Financial Express on January 6, 2017. The title of the report read, "Bengaluru mass molestation: Virat Kohli lashes out, says ashamed to be part of society" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, eyewitnesses recounted that on the night of December 31, women were molested, groped, and subjected to lewd remarks by miscreants in a posh area, despite claims that 1,500 police personnel had been deployed to control the crowds. In response to the incident, Virat Kohli condemned both the molesters and the politicians, expressing his shame at being part of a society that condoned such acts of perversion. Kohli voiced his outrage through his Twitter handle, posting videos in which he emphasized that men and women are equals. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video from 2017, where Virat Kohli spoke about a mass molestation incident in Bengaluru on New Year's Eve, was edited and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of man refusing to install national flag at his shop shared on social media as real incident with false communal narrative
content: New Delhi, August 21 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video which showed a group of men trying to install the national flag at a shop, while the shopkeeper, seen wearing a skullcap, appeared to resist the installation. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the man was Ritik Kataria, a content creator, and selected portion of a scripted video was shared as a real incident on social media with a misleading communal narrative. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 18 a video of a man wearing a skullcap resisting installation of the national flag at the shop. The user insinuated that the man was a Muslim. The caption of the post read, "भगवा तो दूर की बात अब इन्हें तिरंगा भी नहीं चाहिए ?" An English translation of the caption read, "Forget about saffron, they don't even want the tricolour now?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here, here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The description of the video read, "तिरंगे को लगाने पर हुआ हिन्दू मुस्लिम का झगड़ा तिरंगे को लगाने पर हुआ हिन्दू मुस्लिम का झगड़ा।" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended version of the video, the Desk found that the group attempts to force the man in the skullcap to install the flag at his shop, which he repeatedly refuses, leading to a scuffle. A policeman then arrives and questions the man about his refusal to install the flag. The shopkeeper explains that the national flag should be installed at a height so that it can be looked up to with respect. The video concludes with a message promoting brotherhood and nationalism. Further, the Desk found the social media handles (Facebook and Instagram) of Ritik Kataria, in which he mentioned him as an actor. Here are the links to the Instagram and Facebook profiles, and below is a screenshot of the same: While further scanning, the Desk found that Kataria had shared the same video on his Instagram page on August 15. The caption of the video read, "happy independence day to all, may god bless you all with power and peace with only good vibes 🇮🇳🙏🥳❤️ jai hind dosto #ritikkataria #amarkataria apni sawtantrta ka istemaal smbhal kr kre 🙏🇮🇳🍣🥧😊 #bagaborder" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Ritik Kataria who clarified that the video was uploaded in the month of August in 2023 to spread the message of brotherhood and harmony. He further told PTI that 'YouTube Shorts' of the same video were shared recently and as an actor he intends to spread motivation and will continue to make more such videos in the future. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a scripted video was shared as real on social media with a misleading communal narrative.

title: PTI Fact Check: This video of naga sadhus not related to protest against attacks on Hindus in Bangladesh; false claim shared on social media
content: New Delhi, August 21 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media claims to show Naga Sadhus marching on the streets with swords and tridents in protest against alleged violence targeting minority Hindus in Bangladesh. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation has revealed that this video is misleading. The footage, which dates back to March 2021, was actually recorded in Haridwar and is now being falsely presented as a recent protest. Recent reports indicate a significant increase in crimes against the minority Hindu community and the destruction of Hindu temples in Bangladesh following the recent ouster of the Sheikh Hasina-led government. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 12 a video of Naga Sadhus marching on a street with swords and tridents, and claimed that they were protesting against the violence on minority Hindus in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "बांग्लादेशी हिंदुओं की रक्षा में उतरे हमारे नागा साधु.. बांग्लादेश कुच करने की दी चेतावनी....." An English translation of the caption read, "Our Naga Sadhus came to the rescue of Bangladeshi Hindus..warned of marching to Bangladesh....." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named Naveen Binjola on March 13, 2021. The description of the video read, "first sahi sanan Naga baba 2021 mahakumbh Haridwar...." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: We came across another YouTube video uploaded by a channel named 'Paryatan Sathi Trips' on April 7, 2021. The title of the video read: "हरिद्वार कुंभ 2021 | शाही स्नान | नागा साधु | Paryatansathi". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the video and noticed that the viral clip was taken from 00:32-minute timestamp. Below is a combination image showing the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video posted by a Facebook page named Haridwar Live on March 11, 2021. The caption of the post read, "In Haridwar : Naga Sadhu going towards Har Ki Pauri to take first royal bath of Maha Kumbh 2021." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Hindustan Time published on March 11, 2021. The title of the report read, "Mahakumbh's 1st Shahi Snan witnesses mega rush, over 3 mn pilgrims take holy dip" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, over 3 million pilgrims took a dip in the Ganga on the occasion of Mahashivratri in Haridwar during the first Shahi Snan (royal bath). The Shri Panch Dashnam Juna Akhada was the first to take the holy dip, with the central attraction being the chariot of Acharya Mahamandaleshwar Swami Avdeshanand Maharaj, accompanied by hundreds of Naga ascetics. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from Mahakumbh in Haridwar, dating back to March 2021, was shared as recent on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Did Pannun stage attack on himself in US? No, viral screenshot of Washington Post report is FAKE
content: New Delhi, August 22 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported article by The Washington Post, which claimed that US-based separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun had staged an attack on himself to implicate India. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that no such article was published by The Washington Post. A fake and digitally altered screenshot was shared on social media with false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 20 a screenshot of a purported article by The Washington Post, which claimed that the US-based separatist leader Gurpatwant Singh Pannun staged an attack on himself to implicate India. The caption of the post read, "Why are we not talking about this?! After 1 year of investigation, the US found Pannu faked an attack on himself to implicate India." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that it was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively: The screenshot was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across another article, published by The Washington Post on April 29. The title of the article read, "An assassination plot on American soil reveals a darker side of Modi's India" Here is the link to the article and below is a screenshot of the same: "In reports that have been closely held within the American government, U.S. intelligence agencies have assessed that the operation targeting Pannun was approved by the RAW chief at the time, Samant Goel. That finding is consistent with accounts provided to The Washington Post by former senior Indian security officials who had knowledge of the operation and said Goel was under extreme pressure to eliminate the alleged threat of Sikh extremists overseas. U.S. spy agencies have more tentatively assessed that Modi's national security adviser, Ajit Doval, was probably aware of RAW's plans to kill Sikh activists, but officials emphasized that no smoking gun proof has emerged," read a section of the report by The Washington Post. The Desk compared the screenshot with the original report, which suggested that the latter was digitally altered to create the fake screenshot: On the contrary, the summary mentioned in the viral screenshot read: "In reports that have been closely held within the American government, U.S. intelligence agencies have assessed that Pannun could have staged attacked on himself. After one year of probe no Indian angle have been found yet to reach a conclusion that India was involved in the attack." In the next part of investigation, the Desk came across an X post by the official account of Gerry Shih, India Bureau Chief of Washington Post, where he termed the viral screenshot as "photoshopped". He also shared link to the original article on August 21. The title of the report read, "The viral post below is photoshopped, NOT a @washingtonpost story. Unfortunately, it already has 3.2K retweets—another Wednesday for the Indian social media disinfo factory. Fortunately, you can read the real story w this gift link and help share it: https://wapo.st/3XcitNO" Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to The Washington Post via email, seeking their comment on the viral screenshot. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot shared on social media in the name of Washington Post was fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: This letter about CBI withdrawing from Kolkata rape-murder case investigation is FAKE; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 22 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared screenshot of a purported letter from one 'Dr Akash Nag', claiming to be the DIG and Joint Director at the Crime Branch in Kolkata, which requested the Home Ministry to withdraw from investigating the Kolkata doctor's rape-murder case due to "political manipulation and social influence." The alleged letter was shared with the claim that the CBI had withdrawn itself from the probe into the case, which has triggered a nationwide uproar. The PTI Fact Check Desk, however, found in its investigation that a fake and fabricated letter was shared on social media with a false claim. The investigation revealed that there was no official with the said name and designation working with the central probe agency, as claimed in the viral screenshot. Last week, the CBI took over from Kolkata Police the investigation into the rape and killing of a post-graduate medic at Kolkata's RG Kar Medical College and Hospital following a directive from the Calcutta High Court. On August 22, the central agency submitted a status report of the investigation before the Supreme Court. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 20 a screenshot of a purported letter from one 'Dr Akash Nag', claiming to be DIG and Joint Director at the Crime Branch in Kolkata, requesting the Home Ministry to withdraw from the investigation into the rape and murder of a trainee doctor at Kolkata's RG Kar Medical College and Hospital due to "political manipulation and social influence". The user claimed that The caption of the post read, "@HMOIndia Sir, Request Home ministry to provide proper security guards to Seema Pahuja madam. In Bengal the whole adm in the hands of TMC goons. They threatened Dr Akash Nag and withdrawn. See the letter" Here is the link and archive link t o the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed discrepancy in the name mentioned on the letter. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a press release by the CBI issuing a clarification regarding the viral letter. The title of the press release read, "Clarification Regarding a Fake Letter About CBI Investigation of a Case Related to Rape and Murder of Trainee Doctor" Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by CBI, carrying the same clarification regarding the viral letter as in the press release. The caption of the post read: "Clarification Regarding a Fake Letter About CBI Investigation of a Case Related to Rape and Murder of Trainee Doctor" Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the official websites of Kolkata Police , West Bengal CID and CBI , but could not find the details of any official by the name of Dr Akash Nag. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the alleged letter shared on social media was fake. The CBI had not sought withdrawal from investigation into the Kolkata medic's rape and murder.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, KL Rahul did not announcement retirement through an Instagram story, fake post shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, August 23 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of an Instagram story allegedly posted by Indian cricketer KL Rahul, announcing his retirement from professional cricket. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Rahul did not make any formal announcement regarding his retirement. The post circulating on social media is fake and was shared with a false claim. The caption of the post read, "This is unexpected 🥲 Kl Rahul announced his retirement from professional Cricket #cricket #klrahul #roaminglife🎪" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here , and their archived versions can be found here , here and here , respectively. The post was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here and here and their archived version can be found here and here respectively. The Desk then scanned the Instagram handle of the cricketer and found a story with "I have an announcement to make, stay tuned...." written on it uploaded on August 22. Here is the link and archive link to the story and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk scrolled further but did not find anything regarding his retirement. We also checked the account's activity log on Social Blade, a social media analytics website, and found that no post was deleted recently. Below is a screenshot showing the same: In the next part of the investigation, the PTI Sports Bureau contacted a long term associate of KL Rahul to know the truth behind the claim in the social media post. The associate dismissed the rumors stating, "Social media has many pranksters, can't take all these seriously. Isn't it? His focus is on the Duleep Trophy." The associate dismissed the rumors circulating on social media. Additionally, PTI contacted Rahul's coach, Samuel Jayaraj, who stated, "I don't know what is happening on social media. He is focused on his game," further refuting the claims. title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show Virat Kohli commenting on Kolkata rape-murder case; AI-generated audio overlaid on 2022 video

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Dhaka University professor being forced to resign during recent students protests shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 25 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was shared on social media with the claim that it showed a Hindu professor at a college in Dhaka was forced to recite verses from the Quran and then resign by members of the Jamaat-e-Islami student organisation. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the man in the video was Professor Dr Abdul Bashir, Dean of the Faculty of Arts at Dhaka University, who was forced to resign following the students' protest. The video was shared on social media with a false communal narrative. The viral video emerged amid the reported spike in violence against the minority Hindu community in crisis-hit Bangladesh following the ouster of Sheikh Hasina-led government earlier this month. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 19 a video with the claim that it showed a Hindu professor at Dhaka College being forced to recite the Quran and then resign by members of the Jamaat-e-Islami student organisation. The caption of the post read, "ढाका कॉलेज के एक हिंदू प्रोफेसर का इस्तीफा जमाते इस्लामी के छात्र संगठन ने बेहद अजीब तरीके से लिया पहले हिंदू प्रोफेसर को कुरान की तिलावत सुनाई गई यानी कुरान की आयतें सुनाई गई और उसके बाद उनका इस्तीफा लिया गया". An English translation of the caption read, "The resignation of a Hindu professor of Dhaka College was taken in a very strange manner by the student organization of Jamaat-e-Islami. First, the Hindu professor was made to recite the Quran, i.e., verses from the Quran were recited and then his resignation was taken." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same; Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video. Four such posts can be found here , here , here and here and their archived versions can be viewed here , here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Dhaka Post on August 19. The description of the video read: "পদত্যাগ করলেন ঢাবির কলা অনুষদের ডিন আবদুল বাছির | DU | Dhaka Post" An English translation of the description read: "Abdul Bachir, Dean of Arts Faculty of DU, resigned D.U Dhaka Post" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is combination image comparing visuals of the two: The Desk also came across an X post by a Bangladeshi content creator named Nazmus Sajid Chowdhury, who shared photos from the same incident. The caption of the post read: "During his tenure as the Dean of the Faculty of Arts at Dhaka University, he banned students from organizing Quran recitation events at Historic Bottola Premises and issued show-cause notices to those involved. Today, students forced Abdul Basir to resign, and afterward, they bid him farewell by playing the very Quran recitation he once tried to suppress and offered prayers in his office. What a scene!" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Dhaka Tribune on August 19. The title of the report read, "DU Faculty of Arts dean resigns amid student protests" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, AB Jubayer, co-coordinator of the anti-discrimination student movement, accused Prof. Dr. Abdul Bashir of being involved in attacks on Dhaka University students and of previously attempting to punish students who participated in a Quran recitation program on campus during Ramadan. Jubayer criticized Prof. Bashir as a supporter of autocracy and a provocateur, arguing that he was unfit to hold a significant position such as the Dean of the Faculty of Arts. In response to the protest, students escorted Prof Bashir from his room on the third floor of the Arts Building to the Dean's office around 12 PM, where he drafted his resignation letter on the official letterhead of the Faculty of Arts. Following his resignation, a recitation from the Holy Qur'an was held, and a prayer was offered for peace and discipline at Dhaka University and across the country. Subsequently, the Desk concluded the video of a professor at Dhaka University being forced to recite verses of the Quran and resign. The video was shared with a false communal narrative.

title: PTI Fact Check: Viral report claiming WHO ordered governments to prepare for mpox 'mega lockdowns' is FAKE
content: New Delhi, August 26 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported report by The People's Voice claiming that the World Health Organisation (WHO) ordered governments to prepare for 'mega lockdowns' in wake of Monkeypox. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that no such guidelines were issued by the WHO. The claim made in the article was fake. On August 14, WHO Director General Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus announced mpox outbreak a public health emergency of international concern. Most of the mpox cases have been reported across west, central, and east African countries, along with some in Pakistan and Thailand. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 16 a screenshot of a report stating the WHO has directed governments to prepare for 'mega lockdowns' in wake of spike of Monkeypox cases. The caption of the post read, "Will you be "Locked Down"? The World Health Organization (WHO) has ordered government's to prepare to initiate tough new lockdowns due to the "strong likelihood" that the new monkeypox strain will become a deadly pandemic. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here , and their archived versions can be found here and here , respectively. The post was widely shared on Twitter too. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here respectively. The Desk then conducted a keyword search on Google and came across the said report, whose screenshot was shared on social media. The title of the report, dated August 15, read: "WHO Orders Govt's To Prepare for 'Mega Lockdowns' Due to 'Deadly Monkeypox' Strain" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "The World Health Organization (WHO) has ordered government's to prepare to initiate tough new lockdowns due to the "strong likelihood" that the new monkeypox strain will become a deadly pandemic," read a section of the report. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any other report backing the claim made in the viral article. Had it been the case, the news would have grabbed headline across the globe. We couldn't find any social media post on this by the organisation either. In the next part of investigation, we checked the official page of the WHO and came across a press release published on August 14. The title of the release read, "WHO Director-General declares mpox outbreak a public health emergency of international concern" Here is the link to the release and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the release, "WHO Director-General Dr. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, acting on the advice of an IHR Emergency Committee of independent experts, convened earlier to review data from WHO and the affected countries. The committee expressed concern about the potential for the virus to spread further across Africa and potentially beyond the continent." Committee Chair Professor Dimie Ogoina stated, "The current upsurge of mpox in parts of Africa, along with the spread of a new sexually transmissible strain of the monkeypox virus, is an emergency, not only for Africa, but for the entire globe. Mpox, originating in Africa, was neglected there, and later caused a global outbreak in 2022. It is time to act decisively to prevent history from repeating itself." The report nowhere made any mention of the WHO chief warning governments with lockdowns. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to gather details regarding the virus and came across a report by the WHO published on April 18, 2023. Here is the link to the report. As per the report, Mpox (monkeypox) is an infectious disease caused by the monkeypox virus, characterised by a painful rash, swollen lymph nodes, and fever. While most people fully recover, some may experience severe illness. The virus is transmitted through direct contact with infectious skin lesions, including those in the mouth or on the genitals. Symptoms typically begin within a week of exposure, though they can appear anytime between 1 to 21 days after contact. The illness usually lasts 2–4 weeks but may persist longer in individuals with weakened immune systems. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the WHO had not directed governments to impose lockdowns to contain mpox outbreak.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated video of Rajdeep Sardesai shared on social media, falsely linking it to Kolkata rape-murder case
content: New Delhi, August 25 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video of journalist Rajdeep Sardesai, claiming that he refused to acknowledge the horrific rape and murder of a trainee doctor in Kolkata, during a recent TV panel discussion. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old remark by Sardesai, clipped from a news debate dating back to 2023, was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 13 a video of senior journalist Rajdeep Sardesai, claiming that he refused to acknowledge the recent Kolkata rape and murder of a trainee doctor during a panel discussion. The caption of the post read, "Rajdeep "Dalal" Sardesai was lecturing on roits that follow rapes of women in UP and other BJP ruled states but when shown mirror on recent incident on bengal, he conveniently avoids it by saying it's the only state with women chief minister!." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the viral video was old. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of The Lallantop on August 5, 2023. The description of the video read, "PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi पर क्‍या बातें हुईं कि तालियां बज उठीं? Netanagri 200 Episode। Saurabh Dwivedi" An English translation of the description read, "What happened to PM Modi,Rahul Gandhi that got applause? Netanagri 200 Episode. Saurabh Dwivedi" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed this was the original video, from where the viral video was clipped. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended video, the Desk found that the viral video was clipped from the timestamp of 3:36:35-minutes. During the panel discussion, one of the participants from the audience raised a question related to crimes against women during political and communal violence, to which Sardesai replied by giving examples from Manipur. Further, the participant added, "I have seen it in Gujarat, in Mumbai during 1992-1993, and in Muzaffarnagar in 2012. Whenever riots happen, we always hear stories of rape and gang rape. What is the reason for this?" As he continued his speech, fellow panellist and senior journalist Rahul Shrivastava intervened, questioning why he omitted West Bengal when referencing states where atrocities against women have occurred. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Sardesai's remarks during a panel discussion dating back to 2023 was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to the rape and murder of a trainee doctor in Kolkata.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of mob vandalising a bus in Surat shared as recent on social media with misleading claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 27 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video showing several men wearing skull caps, purportedly from the Muslim community, vandalising a bus during a protest was shared on social media, with users claiming it was from a recent incident. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video from Surat, dating back to 2019 was misleadingly shared as a recent event. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video showing a group of people wearing skull caps vandalising a bus and smashing its windows with stones. The caption of the post read, ""जिहादी" अर्थव्यवस्था में "योगदान" करते हुये।" An English translation of the post read, ""Contributing" to the "Jihadi" economy." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video. Two such posts can be found here and here and can be viewed here and here r espectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Two such videos can be seen here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Divyang News Channel on July 5, 2019. The description of the video read, "Surat l Police fire tear gas shells as rally against mob lynching incidents turns violent l Divyang News" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Times of India on Jul 6, 2019. The title of the report read, "Surat: Rally against mob lynching turns violent" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the Versatile Minorities Forum (VMF) was granted permission to hold a rally from Dargah to Makkai Pool in Nanpura. However, a section of the crowd moved ahead and ignored police requests to return. Some individuals began throwing stones at the police, prompting the authorities to fire tear gas shells and one round in the air to disperse them, as claimed by the police. The mob also targeted a city bus near the restaurant, shattering its windows, and damaged another bus at a different location. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to July 2019 from Surat was shared as recent on social media with misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Andhra shared in name of Tripura dam with false claim that water gushing out of it caused floods in Bangladesh
content: New Delhi, August 26 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) A video of water gushing out of a dam was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed the Dambu Hydroelectric Power Project in Tripura, and was responsible for floods in Bangladesh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an unrelated video showing Srisailam Reservoir Dam in Andhra Pradesh was shared on social media with a false claim. Rainfall-triggered floods in eastern Bangladesh have claimed dozens of lives recently and left millions of people affected. In the flood-hit districts of Bangladesh, some have blamed it on the water released from the Dumbur Dam in Tripura. However, India has denied opening the sluicegates. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 21 a video of water gushing out of a dam, claiming it was Dambu ​​Hydroelectric Power Project in Tripura. The caption of the post read, "Status of Dambu ​​Hydroelectric Power Project or Dambu ​​Gate in Tripura, India. May Allah protect us from this terrible situation" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report published by ETV Bharat on July 30. The title of the report read: "WATCH: Srisailam Reservoir Dam Gates Opened Due to Heavy Inflows from Upper Reaches" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the same: "About 1.35 lakh cusecs was released into Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir. The Srisailam Reservoir is flooded due to heavy rains in the upper areas. As the flood flow rose, the authorities lifted five gates. Each gate is raised by 10 feet and the water is released.Water is being released to Nagarjunasagar dam through the spillway. On the other hand, 4.27 lakh cusecs of flood water are coming to Srisailam reservoir from Jurala and Sunkesula dam. A large number of tourists come to see this beautiful scene," stated the report. Following this, the Desk also came across an X post by the official handle of the Ministry of External Affairs issuing a clarification regarding the viral claim on August 22. The caption of the post read, "Flood situation in Bangladesh not due to release of waters from Indian dam on Gumti River, Tripura" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also found a link to the press release by the ministry issued on the same day. Here is the link to the release. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from Srisailam Reservoir Dam from Andhra Pradesh was falsely identified as Dumbur Dam in Tripura.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 photo of people offering prayers in chest-deep water in Bangladesh misleadingly shared as recent linking it to recent floods; Details inside
content: New Delhi, August 28 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of people from the Muslim community offering namaz in chest-deep water was shared on social media with the claim that it was from Bangladesh, where rain-triggered floods have affected several parts. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an unrelated photo from Bangladesh, dating back to 2021, was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Rain-triggered floods in several parts of eastern Bangladesh have claimed over a dozen lives and left millions of people misplaced. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 27 a photo of people from the Muslim community praying in chest-deep water, and claimed that it was related to the ongoing flood situation in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "इस समय बांग्लादेश में आई भयानक बाढ़ से हाल बेहाल। कर्म का फल मिलता है पर इतनी जल्दी मिलता है ये पहली बार देख रहा हूँ.." An English translation of the post read: "At this time, Bangladesh is in a terrible state due to the terrible floods.One gets the fruits of his deeds, but I am seeing it so quickly for the first time." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a webpage on the official website of International Photo Awards, that carried the same photo on October 8, 2021. The title of the photo read, "Pray for mercy" Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: "This picture was taken from Satkhira, Bangladesh which is low-lying coastal region nearby word largest mangrove forest " Sundarban". People living here have to perform their prayer with the water equal to the knee or chest and the prayers should be offered with the water equal to the throat so that almighty Allah protects them from this danger. But after few days they lost this mosque due to strong current of extreme high tidal water. Although they are none responsible for these consequences of global warming and climate change," read the description of the photo. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an Instagram profile of Sharwar Hussain who shared the same photo September 19, 2023. The caption of the post read, "Pray for mercy by Sharwar Hussain @sharwarhussain | @iphotoawards 2022 - Best of Show⠀ This photo was taken in Satkhira, Bangladesh, a low-coastal region near the world's largest mangrove forest, "Sundarban". People pray for Allah's protection against extremely high tides. ⠀ ⠀ Pray for mercy by Sharwar Hussain | International Photography Awards 2022 - Best of Show⠀ ⠀ This picture was taken in Satkhira, Bangladesh, a low-lying coastal region near the world's largest mangrove forest "Sundarban". People are praying for Allah's protection against the extremely high tides." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a three-year-old photo was falsely linked to the ongoing flood situation in Bangladesh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Visakhapatnam falsely shared in name of Kolkata rape-murder victim and her father; Details Inside
content: New Delhi, August 29 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media claimed to show hospital staff at Kolkata's RG Kar Medical College and Hospital applauding with folded hands as the father of the deceased trainee doctor, who was raped and murdered, passed through the corridor with her body. However, PTI Fact Check, in its investigation, found that the video was from an unrelated incident in Visakhapatnam in June this year. The video was shot when the hospital staff applauded the father, a resident of Rajasthan's Jalore, who decided to donate the organs of his son who died in an accident. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 21 a video showing medically personnel at a hospital lined up with folded hands along a corridor as they bid farewell to the deceased Kolkata rape-murder incident and also applauded her braveheart father. The caption of the post read, "ये हिम्मत है उस पिता की जो मर के भी जिंदा है😥 महादेव जी ये पिता को ये लड़ाई लड़ने की शक्ति दे🙏🏼" An English translation of the caption read, "This is the courage of that father who is alive even after death😥 Mahadev ji give this father the strength to fight this battle🙏🏼" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the viral video showed the staff paying respect to someone who donated their body organs. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report published by News 18 Hindi on June 2. The title of the report read, "मरने के बाद भी अमर हो गया इस पिता का लाल, एक्सीडेंट में गई जान, तो बेटे का कर दिया देहदान" An English translation of the title read, "This father's son became immortal even after death, when his son died in an accident, he donated his body" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Vipin Mehta, a resident of Jalore Fateh Royal Colony, died in a road accident in Visakhapatnam. After this, Vipin's father Praveen Mehta donated his son's body. After the father's decision, 300 members of the hospital that treated Vipin gave a guard of honor to Vipin Mehta's body and sent off the body from the hospital for donation." stated an English translation of the report. Following this the Desk also came across another report by Dainik Bhaskar published in May with the title, "Son died in an accident, father donated his organs: 300 doctors, nursing staff and employees present in the hospital gave guard of honour" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Vipin Mehta, a resident of Jalore Fateh Royal Colony, tragically lost his life in a road accident while returning home on his bike in Visakhapatnam. After his passing, Vipin's father, Praveen Mehta, decided to donate his son's organs. In response to this, around 300 members of the hospital staff, who had been involved in Vipin's care, respectfully bid farewell to the deceased. Subsequently, the Desk concluded an old and unrelated video was shared on social media falsely linking to the Kolkata rape and murder case.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 Malaysia video of boy thrashing a girl shared on social media with false communal narrative
content: New Delhi, August 30 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video with the claim that it showed a Muslim boy mercilessly slapping, kicking and beating with slipper a Hindu girl. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old and unrelated video was shared as recent on social media with a false communal narrative. According to reports, the video showed a boy assaulting his sister in Malaysia in October 2022 for allegedly leaving their sick mother alone in the home to meet her friend. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on August 29 a video, claiming that it showed a Muslim mercilessly assaulting a Hindu girl, calling it a case of "love jihad". The caption of the post read, "मित्रो इसी को बोलते है लव जेहाद, आप देख सकते है सेक्यूलर हरामखोर हिन्दुओं की बेटी अपने जेहादि आशिक अब्दुल से कितना प्यार से मार खा रही हैं, सूटकेस में भी कल पैक हो जाएगी परतुं आशिकी खत्म नही होना चाहिए," An English translation of the caption read: "Friends, this is called love jihad. You can see how lovingly the daughter of secular bastard Hindus is getting beaten up by her jihadi lover Abdul. She will be packed in a suitcase tomorrow but the love should not end." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such videos can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post by the official handle of Utusan Malaysia on October 31, 2022. The caption of the post read, "Harap PDRM cepat ambil tindakan terhadap pelaku." An English translation of the caption read, "Please PDRM take immediate action against the culprit." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: We than ran a keyword search on Google and found that PDRM was the short form for Royal Malaysia Police. We then conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Malaysian news portal Wau Post on November 1, 2022. The title of the report read, "Teenaged boy kicks & beats-up sister violently after she allegedly left their bedridden mum home alone to go out" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Some netizens have even claimed that the young girl was in fact the teenage-boy's sister, and that he was angered by how she had snuck out to meet a boy instead of taking care of their bedridden and sick mother who was in hospital. However, neither the claim nor the location and time of the incident can be ascertained at this point." stated the report. The Desk came across another report by News Nestia, a Malaysian news website published on November 1, 2022. The title of the report read, "Boy slaps & kicks sister repeatedly with full force, allegedly for leaving bedridden sick mother to meet a 'male dude'" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same According to the report, an 18-second video was shared on Twitter on October 30, where a teenage boy repeatedly striking a girl on the head with full force three times before viciously kicking her in the torso. After the video went viral, Kota Kinabalu District Police Chief, Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zaidi Abdullah, urged those with knowledge of the incident to come forward and assist in the investigation, as no police report had yet been filed regarding the matter. The Kinabalu District Police Chief had also released a statement on Facebook regarding the incident on October 31, 2022. Here is the link to the Facebook post and below is a screenshot of the same: "ON 30/10/22 A VIDEO OF A TEENAGE FEMALE PUNCHED AND KICKED BY A MALE TEENAGE WHICH WAS SAID TO HAVE HAPPENED AT A SHOPPING CENTER IN KOTA KINABALU DISTRICT HAS GONE VIRAL. THE POLICE HAVE NOT RECEIVED ANY POLICE REPORT REGARDING THE INCIDENT AND HAVE NOT BEEN ABLE TO CONFIRM THAT THE INCIDENT HAPPENED IN KOTA KINABALU DISTRICT OR VICE VERSA. HOWEVER, THE POLICE ARE CARRYING OUT AN INVESTIGATION REGARDING THE VIRAL VIDEO AND HAVE INSTRUCTED ALL ELEMENTS INCLUDING THE POLICE CHIEF OF THE STATION IN THIS DISTRICT TO GET INFORMATION ABOUT THE INCIDENT, LOCATION AND PERPETRATOR. THE POLICE ALSO REQUESTS THE COOPERATION OF ALL PARTIES TO APPEAR AND PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT THE INCIDENT TO ENABLE THE POLICE TO CARRY OUT THE INVESTIGATION AND ARRESTS THE PERPETRATORS," read an English translation of the post, originally in Malay. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated incident dating back to at least 2022 was shared as recent with a false communal narrative.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old RSS foot march video from Kerala shared in name of Haryana with false context; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Aug 31 (Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed foot march by RSS workers in Haryana, which is scheduled to go to polls in September 2024. The users who shared the video also claimed that the RSS, considered as the ideological parent organisation of the BJP, was working on war-footing in the poll-bound state. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old video of RSS march in Kerala's Malappuram on the occasion of Vijayadashami, was shared as recent on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video claiming that it showed RSS workers carrying out a foot march in Haryana ahead of the state going to polls. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. Some Facebook users also shared screenshots of X posts, which had carried the same video. Two such posts can be seen here and here and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post, shared by an Instagram handle named RSS Kerala on October 7, 2022, which carried the same video as the one shared in social media posts. "Tanur , Malappuram district of KERALA.....where the Malabar riot where occurred against the HINDUS during 1921....." read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: A Facebook handle named Vishwa Samvad Kendra – Kokan shared the same video on October 7, 2022. "Vijaya Dashami Path Sanchalan at Malappuram #RSS #RSSVijayadashami2022 Friends of RSS," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the post: Taking a cue on the location of the place – Tanur, Malappuram, Kerala – we geolocated the same location on Google Maps. We found the same location on Google Maps as seen in the viral video. Below is a combination image, showing the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of RSS rally in Kerala was shared as recent, falsely linking it to the upcoming Haryana Assembly polls.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Pakistan's Karachi shared with false claim of children damaging railway tracks in India
content: New Delhi, Sep 2 (Anushka Pandey / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): In the wake of the recent train derailments in the country, a video showing some children on a railway track was shared on social media. Users claimed that the footage was from India and that the children were tampering with the tracks. However, when the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the viral claim, it found that the video was not from India but from Karachi, Pakistan. Social media users are sharing this old video from Pakistan with false claims, presenting it as if it was from India. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video on August 30 showing children playing with a spanner on a railway track, seemingly attempting to sabotage it. The caption of the post read, "#TrainAccident ये मासूम बच्चे ट्रेन की पटरी पर क्या कर रहे हैं ? कौन सिखा रहा है इन्हें ये सब ? बच्चों को मोहरा बनाकर ट्रेन डिरेल कराने की साजिश है?? बस मोदी सरकार को टारगेट करने के लिए विपक्ष किसी भी हद तक..." An English translation of the caption read, "#TrainAccident What are these innocent children doing on the railway track? Who is teaching them all this? Is there a conspiracy to derail the train by using children as pawns?? The opposition will only target the Modi government to any extent..." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other X users shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was also widely shared on Facebook. Three such posts can be found here , here , and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here , and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by a Pakistan channel named CCTV World on December 6, 2023. The video's description read, "Sartaj Khan Railway Phatak Boat Basin Gulshan e Sikandarabad tapu site." Here is the link to the video , and below is a screenshot of the same: Following this, the Desk came across a similar video posted by a Pakistani Trains Facebook page, uploaded on December 5, 2023. "Sir Taj Khan Phatak boat basin checkpoint steals the valuables of railway lines very often. PS boat basin is requested to take this action." read an English translation of the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: After the matter came to light, Karachi Pakistan's Media Cell-DIG South Zone caught the children stealing goods from Boat Basin Railway Gate and brought them to the police station. Later, after the parents assured them, the children were handed over to their parents.
