The caption of the post read, " بوٹ بیسن چوکی کے قریب سرتاج خان پھاٹک ریلوے لائن سے پٹری کے نٹ بولٹ چوری کی ویڈیو کا معاملہ۔ ڈی آئی جی ساؤتھ کی ہدایت پر ایس ایچ او بوٹ بیسن نے کاروائی کرتے ہوۓ ریلوے پھاٹک سے سامان چوری کرنے والے نو عمر بچوں کو تھانے لایا گیا۔ بچے چونکہ چھوٹے ہیں اس بنا پر بچوں کے والدین کو تھانے بلایا گیا۔ جنہیں بچوں کی چوری سے متعلق آگاہ کرتے ہوۓ تنبیہ کی گئی کے اپنے بچوں کا دھیان رکھیں اور انکی روز مرہ کی غیر معمولی سرگرمیوں پر کڑی نظر رکھیں۔ والدین کی طرف سے یقین دھانی کرائے جانے پر بچوں کو والدین کے حوالے کردیا گ" An English translation of the post read, "Video case of theft of track nut bolts from Sartaj Khan Phatak railway line near Boot Basin Chowki. Under the direction of DIG South, SHO Bot Besan took action and brought the juveniles who stole goods from the railway gate to the police station. As the children were small, the parents of the children were called to the police station. Those who have been warned about child abduction should keep an eye on their children and keep a close eye on their unusual daily activities. The children will be handed over to the parents after the parents give the assurance." Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to December 2023 from Karachi, Pakistan, was shared as recent, falsely linking to India with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Pakistan involving threats to electricity employees over power theft falsely shared as an incident from India
content: New Delhi, Aug 3 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video recently circulated on social media depicted a man, who appeared to be from a minority community wearing a skullcap, admitting to stealing electricity and threatening violence if his service is cut. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claim in the social media post and found that the video was not recent and not from India either. It was an old clip from July 2020 in Karachi, Pakistan, and was misrepresented on social media with false claims in the Indian context. Claim On September 2, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video showing a man in a skullcap, suggesting he is from a minority community, admitting to electricity theft and threatening to kill if his connection is interrupted. The caption of the video read, "बिजली चोरी करूंगा !! मीटर नही लगने दूंगा...आपको जंक्शन बॉक्स चेक करने नही दूंगानहींं मानूंगा!! मरूंगा या मारूंगा।।।। ये तालिबान तो देश के भीतर ही पैदा हो रहा है... भारत की चाहे पुलिस हो या किसी भी विभाग के सरकारी कर्मचारी इनके सामने भीगी बिल्ली बन जाते हैं देखिए कितनी इज्जत से बात कर रहा है यही बात यदि कोई हिंदू बोलता तब इन सरकारी कर्मचारियों के अंदर न जाने कहां से सुपरमैन की आत्मा घुस जाती है और वह उस हिंदू को पीट-पीटकर अधमरा कर देते हैं" An English translation of the caption read, "I will steal electricity!! I will not let the meter be installed... I will not let you check the junction box I will not agree!! I will either die or be killed. This Taliban is being born within the country itself... Whether it is the police of India or the government employees of any department, they become like a wet cat in front of them, see how respectfully they are talking If a Hindu had said the same thing, then God knows from where the soul of Superman enters these government employees and they beat that Hindu to death" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other X users shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was also widely shared on Facebook. Three such posts can be found here , here , and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here , and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by the official handle of Trends Pakistan on July 28, 2020. The caption of the post read, "مروں گا یا ماروں گا لیکن کنڈا نہیں اتارنے دوں گا۔ کراچی کا شہری" An English translation of the caption read, "I will die or kill, but I will not let go of Kanda. A citizen of Karachi" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Following this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Pakistani news website Siasat published on July 28, 2020. The title of the report read, "مروں گا یا ماروں گا لیکن کنڈا نہیں اتارنے دوں گا ۔ کراچی کا شہری" An English translation of the title read, "I will die or kill, but I will not let go. A citizen of Karachi" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the viral video was of an incident in Karachi, Pakistan. The person seen shouting in the video was caught committing electricity theft but, instead of admitting his wrongdoing, started threatening the government employees who had come for questioning. We also found the same video posted by the official X handle of K-Electric, Pakistan's largest power utility. The video shows the engineer featured in the viral clip, clarifying the situation and providing context for the incident. The caption of the post dated for July 27, 2020 read, "Watch this man caught red handed! #ChoriAurSeenaZori" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: ​ Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to July 2020 from Karachi, Pakistan, was shared as recent on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video from PM Modi's 2023 US visit falsely shared as recent in the name of Ukraine; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 5 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of PM Modi meeting and greeting supporters at an airport was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it was from his recent visit to war-torn Ukraine. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was from PM Modi's visit to the United States in June 2023. The video was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. On August 23, PM Modi visited Ukraine at the invitation of President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. His visit to the war-torn country came nearly 45 days after his official visit to Russia in the first half of July this year. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 24 a video of PM Modi meeting and greeting people at an airport and claimed that it was from his recent visit to Ukraine. The caption of the post read: "modi in Ukrainian पूरा वीडियो देखो अगर सीना चौड़ा ना हो जाए तो कहना। एक बार देखो। मोदी के गाड़ी से उतरने से पहले कैसे ब्लैक कमान्डोस ने फील्ड सजाई। है विश्व के किसी भी देश के नेता की छाती में इतना दम जहां दो देशों के बीच युद्ध चल रहा हो और वहां खुले में जाकर अपने समर्थकों का अभिवादन स्वीकार कर सकें।" An English translation of the caption read: "modi in Ukrainian Watch the full video, if your chest doesn't swell with pride then tell me. Watch once. How the Black Commandos set up the field before Modi got off the car.Does any leader of any country in the world have the courage to go out in the open and accept the greetings of his supporters when a war is going on between two countries?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was also widely shared on Facebook. Three such posts can be found here, here , and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here , and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report published by the Times of India on June 20, 2023. The description of the video read: "PM Modi lands in New York; receives warm welcome as crucial state visit to the US commences." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by CNBC TV18 on June 21, 2023. The title of the report read, "Modi US visit | Indian community embraces PM with 'Modi-Modi' chants, vibrant Garba dance; watch video" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the Indian diaspora enthusiastically chanted PM Modi's name as he landed at New York's JFK Airport on June 20. The primary purpose of his visit was to commemorate the International Day of Yoga at the United Nations Headquarters and to engage in bilateral discussions with President Joe Biden in Washington, D.C. In the next part of the investigation, we conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find reports related to PM's recent visit to Ukraine. We came across a report published by the Economic Times on August 23. The title of the report stated, "PM Modi's Ukraine Visit: Inside Rail Force One, the lavish train crossing war-hit regions." Here is the link to the report. According to the report, PM Modi, after concluding his Poland visit, arrived in Kyiv on August 23 "via a secure and distinct mode of transport—Ukraine's 'Rail Force One'." "This 20-hour train ride from Poland through the conflict-ridden areas of Ukraine highlighted the exceptional measures required for diplomatic engagements in a nation where conventional travel routes have been significantly disrupted due to war," the report added. The Desk also came across a video report by Republic World, published on August 23, whose headline read: "PM Modi Arrives In Kyiv, Ukraine Aboard Rail Force One, Receives Grand Welcome." Here is the link to the YouTube video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video of PM Modi's visit to the United States in June 2023 was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to his Ukraine visit.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Cristiano Ronaldo did not say he is 'better football player' than Lionel Messi; AI-generated audio overlaid on 2019 video
content: New Delhi, September 4 (Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of football legends Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi seated together in an event. In the video, Ronaldo can purportedly be heard saying that "he is more handsome and a better football player" than Messi. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of Messi and Ronaldo, dating back to 2019, was digitally altered using superimposed AI-generated audio and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 11 a video of football legends Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, in which Ronaldo can be heard saying that he is "more handsome and a better football player." The caption of the post read, "Cristiano Ronaldo 263 I'm more handsome and better than Leo Messi" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk noticed a lip-sync issue with the viral video. We then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be viewed here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of TNT Sports on August August 29, 2019. The description of the video read, "Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi sat next to each other at the #UCLDraw, and the Juventus great revealed he wants to spend private time with the Argentine. " Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed this was an original version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended video, the Desk found the interviewer saying: "We noticed that you both have been talking alot, do you miss him?" To this Ronaldo replies, "I was, because we shared the stage for 15 years, me and him. I don't know if it has ever happened in football that same two guys at the same stage all the time. So it is not easy and of course we have a good relationship where we have not had dinner together yet. But I hope in future and of course I miss playing in Spain and we have that battle we had in the last 15 years. He pushes me and I push him as well so it's good to be part of this kind of football…". The Desk heard the entire conversation, but did not come across any such statement by Ronaldo as can be heard in the viral video. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through the TrueMedia and Resemble AI , both generative AI voices and robust deepfake audio detection apps. Below are the screenshots of the results: As can be seen in the results above, both the software suggested that the audio in the video was fake or AI-generated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video, dating back to August 2019, was digitally altered using superimposed AI-generated audio to falsely claim that Ronaldo mentioned himself a "better player" than Messi.

author: Anushka Pandey/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: This opinion poll graphic claiming Congress leading in Haryana Elections is edited and fake
content: New Delhi, September 6 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A graphic circulating on social media, purportedly from an opinion poll conducted by 'Republic TV-Matrize,' claimed to predict the outcome of the upcoming Haryana Assembly elections. According to the shared graphic, the BJP was projected to secure 26-36 seats in the 90-member assembly, while Congress was expected to win 35-40 seats, and the Aam Aadmi Party 15-20 seats. However, after investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that no such opinion poll, as claimed in the social media post, was officially released by the 'Republic TV-Matrize.' The edited opinion poll graphic was shared in social media post with false claim. The Haryana Assembly election, comprising 90 seats, is scheduled for October 5, with the vote count taking place on October 8, when the final results will determine the new state legislature. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 31 a screenshot of an alleged opinion poll by 'Republic TV-Matrize' on the upcoming Haryana Assembly polls, projecting the BJP to secure 26-36 seats, Congress 35-40 seats and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) 15-20 seats in the 90-member state assembly. The caption of the post read, "हम सर्वे में नहीं सीधा सरकार में आते है। हरियाणा की जनता की राजनैतिक समझ को हल्के में लेने की गलती नहीं करनी चाहिए । ये सत्ता परिवर्तन की लड़ाई है और परिवर्तन कभी पुरानी पार्टी नहीं लाती। Dr. Sandeep Pathak" An English translation of the caption read, "We do not come into power through surveys but directly come into power. One should not make the mistake of underestimating the political understanding of the people of Haryana. This is a fight for change of power and change is never brought about by an old party. Dr. Sandeep Pathak" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same graphic with similar claims. Four such posts can be found here , here , here and here their archived versions can be seen here , here , here and here respectively. We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if Republic TV or Matrize had released any such opinion poll on Haryana polls. However, we could not find any such graphic as shared in the viral post, or any other post regarding any opinion poll on Haryana. Further, the Desk scanned the official social media handles of 'Republic TV' and 'Matrize News Communications' but did not find any related post. Click here , here and here to see the social media handles. While scanning through the profile, the Desk found Matrize News Communications, a public opinion and market research survey company, conducted an opinion poll for the news channel Times Now in the month of August. This survey predicted that the BJP alliance would get 37-42 seats, Congress 33-38 seats, Jannayak Janata Party (JJP) 03-08 seats and others 07-12 seats in the Haryana assembly elections. Further Times Now has also shared this survey on its 'X' (formerly Twitter) handle and YouTube channel, which can be viewed by clicking here and here . In the next phase of investigation, the Desk reverse searched the viral screenshot and found a template similar to the viral graphic in a report published on ETV Bharat's website on June 1, 2024. This graphic was used for the exit poll of the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The title of the report read, "हरियाणा में बीजेपी के लिए बुरी ख़बर...एग्जिट पोल के मुताबिक नहीं कर पा रही क्लीन स्वीप...इतने सीटों का हो रहा नुकसान - HARYANA EXIT POLL 2024 LIVE" An English translation of the title read, "Bad news for BJP in Haryana... According to the exit poll, it is not able to do a clean sweep... it is losing so many seats - HARYANA EXIT POLL 2024 LIVE" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same The Desk noticed striking similarities between the two graphics, suggesting that the original one was digitally altered to create the viral graphic. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that no such opinion poll was released by 'Republic TV-Matrize' or any of them. A fake graphic was shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of a man assaulted over extramarital affair shared as recent on social media with false communal narrative
content: New Delhi, September 4 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a man being brutally beaten by sticks in full public view was recently shared on social media with the claim that he was assaulted for allegedly converting from Hinduism to Christianity. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old video from Telangana, where the man was beaten from being allegedly involved in an extramarital affair. The unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false communal narrative. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 2 a video of a man being brutally beaten with sticks, allegedly for converting from Hinduism to Christianity The caption of the post read, "Is leaving Hinduism and converting into other religion crime in this country? This man was brutally beaten by mobs just because he left Hindusim and converted himself into Christian" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post sharing the same video on July 4, 2022. The caption of the post read, "WARNING: Disturbing Visuals Begari Naresh, a SC boy was dragged from his house and mercilessly thrashed with sticks in Sangareddy, Telangana.Such a callous act. We demand strict action against the goons. Stop casteism." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Mooknayak published on July 6, 2022. The title of the report read, "तेलंगानाः दलित युवक की पिटाई का वीडियो वायरल, मामला दर्ज" An English translation of the caption read, "Telangana: Video of Dalit youth being beaten up goes viral, case registered" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, B Naresh, a Dalit youth from Chilmamidi, was allegedly involved in an affair with a woman from another community. Despite warnings from the villagers to stay apart the two were reportedly caught in a compromising situation, leading Naresh to flee after pushing the woman's husband. The following day, the woman's husband and relatives called Naresh for a discussion. When Naresh arrived with his family, they were attacked by the woman's husband, her relatives, and a group of villagers using sticks. Further the Desk also came across another report published by Telangana Today on July 4. The title of the report read, "Man attacked over extra-marital affair in Sangareddy." Here is the link to the report https://telanganatoday.com/man-attacked-over-extra-marital-affair-in-sangareddy The report stated that Begari Naresh was brutally assaulted with sticks in Chelemamidi village, Jharasangam Mandal, after being accused of having an extramarital affair with a woman from another community. Naresh was rushed to Area Hospital Zaheerabad by some villagers after he lost consciousness. Following this, a complaint was filed by his parents, and the Jharasangam Police registered a case against 11 individuals, with the investigation led by DSP Zaheerabad, Raghu. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video related to an incident from Telangana in 2022 where a man was beaten by locals over an alleged extramarital affair.

author: Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of madrasa students helping flood victims in Bangladesh falsely shared on social media in name of Gujarat
content: New Delhi, September 7 (Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): At a time when several parts of Gujarat are facing the challenge of rain-triggered floods, a video was shared on social media with the claim that it showed Muslim men rescuing flood-hit people while risking their own lives in Jamnagar. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a video of some students providing relief material to flood victims in Bangladesh was falsely shared in the name of Jamnagar, Gujarat. Heavy downpours in Gujarat since the last week of August have claimed more than four dozen lives and left thousands of people misplaced. Claim An X user shared on September 5 a video claiming that it showed Muslim men swimming in floodwaters and providing relief material to flood-hit people and rescuing them in Gujarat. "Thousands of people are stuck in their homes without food and water due to torrential rains and floods in Gujarat. In such a difficult situation, students of religious schools are providing food and water to the people without caring about their lives," read a rough translation of the post, originally in Urdu. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by a Facebook user with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post. On further scanning the search results, we came across an Instagram post by a Bangladeshi user named Ahmed Daiyan. The post, shared on August 25, carried the same video. "Floods continue after India opened dam in Tripura without any warnings to Bangladesh. Thousands of people are still stuck in different parts without any food or drinking water," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, we came across an extended version of the viral video, which was shared by a Facebook page named 'সুপ্রভাত বইঘর - Suprovath Boighor'. According to information available on the Facebook page, the viral video is from Fulgazi Upazila of Feni district of Bangladesh, where madrasa students provided food and water to flood victims amid heavy waterlogging. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The same video was shared by a YouTube channel as well. Here is the link to the video, whose headline stated that it was from Bangladesh. Furthermore, the Desk while watching the viral video noticed a board in Bangla. Below is a screenshot of the same: The Bangla board in English means 'Buro Bangladesh', which is an NGO of Bangladesh. The name board of the same NGO was published by a media report. Here is the link to that report and below is a screenshot of the same: A comparison of both the images turned out to be quite similar, as can be seen below: Bangladesh-based BanglaVision News also uploaded an extended version of the video, stating that the men seen assisting people in the video were madrasa students. Here is the link to the video: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of people assisting flood victims in Bangladesh was falsely shared in the name of Gujarat.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2022 video of Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar meeting Lalu Yadav shared as recent on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, September 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was shared on social media showing Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar smilingly meeting Rashtriya Janata Dal President Lalu Prasad Yadav, purportedly from a recent event. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dates back to 2022, when Nitish Kumar was part of the Grand Alliance and had visited Lalu Yadav's residence for a meeting. An old video was shared on social media with false claim. On September 3 Nitish Kumar met Tejashwi Yadav regarding the appointment of an Information Commissioner at the Chief Secretariat in Patna, Bihar. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 6 a video showing Bihar CM Nitish Kumar smilingly meeting Rashtriya Janata Dal President Lalu Prasad Yadav. The caption of the post read, "बिहार में खेला होने की संभावनाएं बढ़ती जा रही हैं। आज नीतिश कुमार जी और लालू यादव जी के आवास पर मुलाकात करने पहुंचे। 3-4 दिन के अंदर नीतिश जी और तेजस्वी जी की ये दूसरी मुलाकात है।" An English translation of the post read, "The chances of a game being played in Bihar are increasing. Today I visited Nitish Kumar ji and Lalu Yadav ji's residence to meet. This is the second meeting between Nitish ji and Tejaswi ji within 3-4 days." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video on YouTube uploaded by the official channel of OTV News on September 5, 2022. The description of the video read, "Bihar CM Nitish Kumar meets Ex-CM Lalu Prasad Yadav in Patna" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Zee News on September 5, 2022. The title of the report read, "Bihar CM Nitish Kumar meets Lalu Yadav ahead of Delhi visit, to meet Oppn leaders including Rahul Gandhi" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same According to the report , Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar met Rashtriya Janata Dal President Lalu Prasad at his residence at 10, Circular Road. The Chief Minister was welcomed by Deputy Chief Minister Tejashwi Yadav. Following this the Desk found Tejashwi Yadav also shared pictures of Lalu-Nitish meeting on social media platform 'X' (formerly Twitter) on 5 September 2022. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We then conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find reports related to the appointment of Information Commissioner in the Chief Secretariat and came across a report by Dainik Jagran published on September 5. The title of the report read, "नीतीश-तेजस्वी की मीटिंग के बाद अटकलों का बाजार गर्म, डायरेक्ट पटना पहुंच रहे जेपी नड्डा; खेला होगा?" An English translation of the report read, "After Nitish-Tejaswi's meeting, speculations are rife, JP Nadda is reaching Patna directly; could this have been a game?" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Nitish Kumar and Tejashwi Yadav met in the Chief Secretariat regarding the appointment of the Information Commissioner. This meeting lasted for 30 minutes. After the meeting, political activities intensified from Patna to Delhi." stated the report. According to the report published on , Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar met Rashtriya Janata Dal President Lalu Prasad at his residence at 10, Circular Road. The Chief Minister was welcomed by Deputy Chief Minister Tejashwi Yadav. Read the full report by clicking here . Tejashwi Yadav also shared pictures of Lalu-Nitish meeting on social media platform 'X' (formerly Twitter) on 5 September 2022, which can be seen by clicking here . When the desk did a Google search with the help of relevant keywords to know about the latest developments, we found a report published on the website of Dainik Jagran. The report states that Nitish Kumar and Tejashwi Yadav met on 3 September 2024 regarding the appointment of Information Commissioner in the Chief Secretariat. This meeting lasted for 30 minutes. Read the full report by clicking here . During the investigation, we also found a statement of Tejashwi Yadav on the 'X' handle of 'Press Trust of India' (PTI). Responding to media questions after meeting Chief Minister Nitish Kumar, he said, "I have talked to him (Chief Minister Nitish Kumar) about Schedule 9... He said the matter is in court." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to 2022 was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This LIC circular announcing withdrawal of all insurance plans by September 30 is FAKE
content: New Delhi, September 8 (Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a purported notice issued by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) which claimed that the organisation will withdraw all its insurance products and plans for revision by September 30, 2024. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the LIC had issued any such notice. A fake notification was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 31 an alleged notice issued by the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), which stated that the organisation was withdrawing all its insurance products and plans for revision by September 30, 2024. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The same screenshot of the alleged notification was shared by several X users as well. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. To verify the claim made in social media posts, the Desk scanned the official website of LIC (https://licindia.in/) but did not find any notification or press release stating that it was withdrawing all its insurance products and plans. The Desk went through the social media handles ( X and Facebook ) of LIC but did not find any such notification as shared on social media. Meanwhile, we found that LIC had shared a post by PIB India on X, which stated, "A notice allegedly issued by LIC is doing the rounds on social media & claims that it is going to withdraw all insurance products/plans for revision on 30 September 2024. No such notice has been issued by @LICIndiaForever." Click here to view the post. On closely seeing the screenshot shared in social media posts, the Desk noticed some discrepancies. For instance, the notice was not dated. Also, there were some grammatical and spelling errors as highlighted below: However, while scanning the website, we found that the LIC does withdraw some insurance plans each year, and introduces new products that better meet customer needs. Here is the link and below is a screenshot for the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a fake notification was shared on social media in the name of LIC.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video of woman being molested is not from Manipur; 2017 video from Andhra Pradesh shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, September 10 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that it showed molestation of a woman from the Kuki community by a Hindu man in violence-hit Manipur. However, the PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the video was from an incident that happened in Andhra Pradesh in 2017. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The video was shared on social media amid a fresh round of violence in Manipur which included drone and missile attacks, claiming at least eight lives. More than 200 people have been killed and thousands rendered homeless in ethnic strife between Imphal Valley-based Meiteis and adjoining hills-based Kukis since May last year. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 7 a video allegedly showing harassment of a woman from the Kuki community by a Hindu man in Manipur. The caption of the post read: "#ManipurVoilence in India a Hindu is trying to rape a university student in the Bush. The girl is from a Christian minority called the kukis. This all happens under the supervision of the state government. But the government refrains to take action against such rapists. " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such claims can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of TV9 Telugu Live on September 26, 2017. The description of the video read: "Rape attempt on girl filmed and uploaded on Social Media| Kanigiri | Prakasam district - TV9" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the visuals in the video news report were the same as the viral video. We then came across another report published by News18 on September 26, 2017, relating to the same incident The title of the report, "Andhra Police Arrest 3 Youth Who Molested a Girl, Filmed it" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident happened in August in Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh. The police took suo moto cognisance of the matter, registered a case, and arrested the accused. It was stated by the police that the girl had been in a relationship with the accused, and when the situation deteriorated, she decided to end the relationship. Another report published by The News Minute on September 26, 2017, identified the accused as Sai, Karthik, and Pawan, who molested the girl. Andhra Pradesh Women's Commission Chairperson Nannapaneni Rajakumar, along with Satya Yesu Babu, Prakasam's Superintendent of Police, assured that the government would cover the expenses of the girl's education and relocate her to either Ongole or Guntur. Here is the link to the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from Andhra Pradesh, dating back to 2017, was shared as recent falsely linking to Manipur.

title: PTI Fact Check: Myanmar video of helicopter being shot down falsely shared in name of Manipur; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 11 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video circulating on social media falsely claimed that an Indian helicopter was recently shot down in Manipur. The PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that the footage was from Myanmar and it had nothing to do with recent incidents in Manipur. The misleading video emerged amid renewed violence in Manipur, where drone and missile attacks have claimed at least eight lives. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 7 a video of a fighter helicopter being shot down, and claimed that the incident happened recently in Manipur. The caption of the post read, "#Breaking The #indian fighter helicopter shot down by freedom fighter in #Manipur" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Two such videos can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the viral video showed the Kachin Independence Army (KIA) shooting down a Myanmar military junta helicopter using MANPADS. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the channel Conflict Live on September 6. The description of the video read, "Kachin Independence Army (KIA) shoots down a Mi-24 of the #Myanmar Air Force using MANPADS" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The visuals confirmed that this was the same as the viral video. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post sharing the same video by the official handle of Resonant News on September 6. The caption of the post read: "Myanmar Rebels shoot down a Military helicopter A recent video shows Kachin Independence Army (KIA) shooting down Myanmar's military junta helicopter with MANPADS. Its not clear when exactly the incident took place. The video has been published today." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also came across the same video uploaded by the official handle of Alerta Noticias UKR 24, a Ukrainian News Page, on September 6. The caption of the post read, "#Myanmar ( #Burma ) 🇲🇲 : El Ejército de la Independencia ( #KIA ) derribó un helicóptero de la Junta. El grupo utilizó un MANPADS FN-6 (Feinu-6) muy raro de fabricación china 🇨🇳 ) para destruir el helicóptero." An English translation to the caption read, "#Myanmar ( #Burma ) 🇲🇲 : The #KIA ( #Independence Army ) shot down a junta helicopter. The group used a very rare Chinese-made FN-6 (Feinu-6) MANPADS 🇨🇳 ) to destroy the helicopter." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from Myanmar was falsely shared on social media in the name of Manipur.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of drone attack from Myanmar falsely shared in name of Manipur; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 11 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Amid the fresh round of violence and protests in Manipur, a video was shared on social media with the claim that it captured the members of Kuki community launching drone attacks on Meitei settlements in the unrest-hit northeastern state. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old video from Myanmar, dating back to last year, was falsely shared in the name of Manipur. The video shared on social media had no connection with the recent drone attacks in Manipur. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 6 a video showing two men operating drones and claimed that they were members of Kuki community launching bomb attacks on Meitei settlements in Manipur. The caption of the post read, "Video leak oirakpa ngarang gi koutruk ta KUKI singna drone sijinnaraga yumda bomb thadarakpgid" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived posts can be found here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel on Mandalay Free Press - MFP on June 2. 2023. The title of the post read, "အရာတော်နယ်ထဲ ရွာစဉ်ပတ်မွှေ အကြမ်းဖက်နေတဲ့ စစ်အုပ်စုကို ဗုံးထုတိုက်ခိုက်" An English translation of the title read, "A bomb attack on a military group that is doing violence around the village" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: "In Sagaing Region's Ertao Township, the killers roamed the villages relying on weapons. robbery Ayadaw Bone Naing - ABN PDF reports that two armed groups were killed when they attacked the military group that was burning on May 31st when they were entering the village of Wa Tan," read the description of the video. On the afternoon of May 31st, the military group that was entering the village of Watan in Ertao Township was attacked by the Monywa District Battalion (19). Ayadaw Bone Naing: ABN PDF, MRTF Guerrilla Force AMT Guerrilla Force Sae Nyo Guerrilla Force Reflective PDF He said that a battle with that military group took place for more than half an hour at 8:00 p.m., as well as a drone and bomb attack in cooperation with the Patti Nyaung Guerrilla Forces," it added. lc Taking a cue from this, the Desk came across a report by a report published by Myanmar Now on April 17, 2023. The title of the report read, "Myanmar regime says eight killed in Thingyan drone attack on Pyu Saw Htee village" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Myanmar's military regime stated that eight people, including five children, were killed in a drone attack on a Thingyan water festival pavilion in Kywel Pon village, Sagaing Region, on April 13 . The attack took place around 5:40 pm on the first day of the Burmese New Year holiday and left 30 others injured.Bombs were dropped on a pavilion set up in a football field near the village school, with local sources confirming the casualties and the damage caused by the attack. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk located the War Tan Village of Myanmar on Google Earth. Below is a combination image comparing the surrounding of the two: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from Myanmar was shared as recent on social media, falsely linking it to Manipur.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Akhilesh Yadav didn't jump gate to avoid media queries about rape-accused in recent Kannauj case; old, unrelated video shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, September 13 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed him jumping over a gate to avoid media queries on the alleged involvement of former party leader Nawab Singh Yadav in the Kannauj rape case. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to 2023, when Akhilesh Yadav climbed the gate of the Jai Prakash Narayan Interpretation Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow to pay tribute to the late socialist leader, after being denied entry by the police. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Nawab Singh Yadav, a former aide to Samajwadi Party leader Dimple Yadav, was arrested on August 12 under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the POCSO Act and was remanded to 14-day judicial custody for allegedly raping a minor. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 11 a video of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav jumping over a gate, and claimed that he did so to avoid media questions about rape-accused Nawab Singh Yadav. The caption of the post read: "Yesterday, after the DNA test confirmed that Samajwadi Party leader Nabab Singh Yadav had raped a minor girl, reporters from various channels surrounded *Akhilesh Yadav.* When Akhilesh Yadav was unable to answer, he was forced to jump from the gate and run away!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived version can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video from the incident shared by the official handle of PTI on October 11, 2023. The caption of the post read, "VIDEO | Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav climbs a wall while trying to enter Jai Prakash Narayan International Center in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. The officials had reportedly denied permission to the party workers, citing the construction work at the centre." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across a YouTube video report uploaded by the official channel of Mirror Now on October 11, 2023. The description of the video read, "Akhilesh Yadav Climbs Compound Wall After Denied Entry | Drama At Convention Centre | Mirror Now" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across a report published by LiveMint on October 11, 2023. "Akhilesh Yadav climbs boundary wall after being stopped from garlanding JP Narayan, warns of 'total revolution' | Watch" read the title of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, on the anniversary of socialist leader JP Narayan, Samajwadi Party President Akhilesh Yadav was compelled to climb the boundary wall of the Jayaprakash Narayan Interpretation Centre (JPNIC) in Lucknow. Yadav criticised the authorities for locking the gates, accusing them of deliberately preventing him from garlanding the bust of Jayaprakash Narayan. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video dating back to 2023 was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of boy beaten by mob for stabbing a girl in West Bengal shared on social media with false communal narrative; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a Muslim man being beaten by a mob, after he stabbed a Hindu girl in West Bengal for rejecting his proposal. The video also showed the girl covered in blood. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the boy had stabbed the girl, allegedly after she slapped him for making lewd remarks against her. Both the accused and victim were Hindus and the video was shared on social media with a false communal narrative. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 8 a video of a group of men thrashing a boy and claimed that the latter was a Muslim who had stabbed a Hindu girl for refusing his advances in West Bengal. The caption of the post read, "ఒక్క ముస్లిం యువకుడు పట్టపగలు హిందూ అమ్మాయిని ఎలా పొడిచాడో చూడండి!! *మమతా రాజ్ ఆధ్వర్యంలో హిందువులు సురక్షితంగా లేరు!* షాకింగ్!! WBలో పరిస్థితి భయంకరంగా ఉంది. త్వరలో కోల్‌కతా మరియు ఇతర పొరుగు రాష్ట్రాలకు కూడా వ్యాపిస్తుంది, ఇక్కడ BD/మయన్మార్ నుండి చొరబడిన ముస్లింలు బెంగాల్ నుండి పెయిడ్ ఆధార్/ఓటర్ ID/ మరియు రేషన్ కార్డ్‌లతో నెట్టివేయబడుతున్నారు కాబట్టి మరిన్ని చూడటానికి TMC ఓటు వేయండి!" An English translation of the post read: "Watch how a Muslim youth stabbed a Hindu girl in broad daylight!! *Hindus are not safe under Mamata Raj!* Shocking!! The situation in WB is dire. Soon will spread to Kolkata and other neighboring states too, where infiltrating Muslims from BD/Myanmar are being pushed from Bengal with paid aadhaar/voter ID/ and ration cards so vote TMC to see more!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be seen here and here and their archived versions can be found here and here respectively. We then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by the Times of India on September 5. The title of the report read, "Spurned, youth stabs girl thrice on Belgharia road, mom injured too" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: As can be seen above, the photo in the article was the same as the visuals from the viral video. According to the report, a 14-year-old girl was brutally attacked by a youth in broad daylight in Belgharia, Kolkata. The incident occurred in the afternoon of September 4 when the girl was walking on the road when the attacker, Abhijit Dutta, made a lewd comment towards the girl, which prompted her to slap him in response. Enraged by this, Dutta attacked the girl with a sharp weapon, inflicting deep injuries on her shoulders, neck, and head. The girl's mother, who rushed to her daughter's aid, was also injured in the attack. The injured girl was immediately taken to a private hospital off EM Bypass, where she underwent emergency surgery. Following this, the Desk came across an X (formerly Twitter) post by the Barrackpore Police issuing an update on the incident dated for September 5. The caption of the post read, "With reference to the incident under Belgharia PS jurisdiction, a girl who was attacked by a person with a sharp edged weapon (দা ), a specific case under proper sections of law has been registered. Police arrested one accused person and all proper legal actions are being taken." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We then checked the official website of Barrackpore Police Commissionerate and found the FIR copy which confirmed the name of the accused as Abhijit Dutta. Below is a screenshot of the FIR copy, that makes it clear that both the accused and victim were Hindus. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the accused and the victim belonged to the same community and the video was shared on social media with a false communal narrative.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 photo of Sheikh Hasina shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to India
content: New Delhi, September 12 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of Bangladesh former PM Sheikh Hasina seemingly enjoying a feast was shared on social media with the claim that it was a recent one after she fled to India, following the political turmoil in her country. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the photo, originally taken after an award ceremony in Bangladesh's Mirzapur in 2019, was falsely circulated as a recent photo from India. Hasina, on August 5, fled Bangladesh after resigning as PM. The same day, she landed at a military base near Delhi following her chaotic exit from the violence-hit country. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 7 a photo of Bangladesh's former PM Sheikh Hasina, claiming that it showed her enjoying a feast during her continued presence in India. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that several other X users had shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report published by Bangladesh's news portal Ittefaq on March 15, 2019. The title of the report read: "কুমুদিনী পরিবারে ৩১ পদের খাবার খেলেন প্রধানমন্ত্রী" An English translation to the post read: "The Prime Minister ate a 31-course meal at Kumudini's family" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina attended the commemoration and award ceremony of Martyr Danveer Randa Prasad Saha at Bharateshwari Homes, Kumudini Complex, Mirzapur. After the ceremony, the Prime Minister was impressed by the hospitality of the Kumudini family. Younger sister Sheikh Rehena was with her. The Kumudini family hosted a 31-course Bengali meal for the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister had food in a brass plate and water in a brass glass," stated the report. The report further mentioned that according to an old tradition of the Kumudini family, they host guests with an elaborate variety of food. Notably, former President of India Pranab Mukherjee was also hosted by this family during a previous visit. Following this, the Desk also came across another report from the same event published by Sangbad Pratidin on March 15, 2019. "Hasina is overwhelmed with hospitality, decorated in 31 steps in bronze vessels" read an English translation of the post. Here is the link to the report: According to the report, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina attended the commemoration and award ceremony of Martyr Danveer Ranadaprasad Saha at Bharateshwari Homes, located within the Kumudini Complex in Mirzapur. Following the event, the Prime Minister was impressed by the hospitality extended by the Kumudini family. The lunch menu consisted of an array of 31 traditional dishes, including rice, dal, various fish bhartas, vegetables, fish, meat, polao, korma, along with snacks such as muri murki, various pithas, and kebabs. The meal concluded with curd and pies as desserts which were served in copper plates. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated photo of Hasina was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Jammu and Kashmir BJP did not ask its workers to attend MP Engineer Rashid's welcome rally; viral press release is FAKE
content: New Delhi, September 15 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a screenshot of an alleged press release by Jammu and Kashmir BJP, which directed party workers to "attend the welcome rally of Abdul Rashid Sheikh (Engineer Rashid)". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the BJP's state unit had not issued any such press release or directive to its workers. A fake screenshot was shared on social media with a false claim. Abdul Rashid Sheikh, who was lodged in Tihar Jail since 2019 in connection with a terror funding case, had been granted interim bail till October 2 to campaign for the upcoming Assembly polls in Jammu and Kashmir. Reacting to Rashid's release, National Conference and PDP – the two major regional parties of the state – called him a 'BJP proxy', an allegation dismissed by the Baramulla MP. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 11 a screenshot of a press release, supposedly issued by the Jammu and Kashmir BJP, claiming that party workers were directed to attend a welcome rally for Abdul Rashid Sheikh, popularly known as Engineer Rashid. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same graphic with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by Inam Un Nab, shared on September 11. The caption of the post, carrying the same screenshot, read: "The NC and PDP have sunk to new lows in their desperation to undermine Er Rashid's growing support. Their latest tactic of spreading malicious falsehoods is a disgrace to political integrity. These parties are now nothing more than purveyors of deceit. Their actions reveal their deep-seated fear and utter lack of principles. It's appalling to witness such hypocrisy and moral bankruptcy from so-called leaders." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by Deccan Herald on September 11. The title of the report read, "J&K BJP chief terms 'fake' an order asking supporters to welcome Engineer Rashid in Kashmir Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across an X post by the official account of Jammu & Kashmir BJP President Ravinder Raina, in which he shared the viral screenshot, calling it a 'fake letter'. The caption of the post read "Political propaganda by frustrated opposition. This fake letter is being circulated in Kashmir Valley, this is nothing but a political Propaganda by frustrated Opposition. No such order issued from my office. I have requested @ECISVEEP to register FIR in the political fraud." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, the Google Lens results took us to a Facebook post, shared by the official page of Jammu & Kashmir BJP on November 2, 2021. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between the two graphics, suggesting that the original one was digitally altered to create the viral screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that no such press release was issued by BJP.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of abduction of two girls in Egypt shared in name of Bengaluru with false communal spin; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of two men purportedly abducting two young girls in an elevator was recently shared on social media, claiming the Hindu girls were kidnapped by Muslim men recently in Bengaluru, capital city of Karnataka. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old and unrelated video from Cairo in Egypt was shared in the name of Bengaluru in India with a false communal narrative. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 12 a video of two men abducting two young girls in an elevator, and claimed that it showed Hindu girls being kidnapped by Muslim men in Bengaluru, Karnataka. The caption of the post read, "Karnataka, Bangalore - See how Jihadis are kidnapping Hindu girls in the lift by making them smell chloroform. They make the girls unconscious in the lift and put them straight in the car parked in the car parking and leave. The girls and women who are kidnapped are never traced!!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other X users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report published by UAE-based news portal Al Bawaba on December 20, 2023. The title of the report read: "Video: 2 girls drugged, kidnapped inside elevator Egypt" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, two men hurried into the elevator, carrying towels laced with a drug. They swiftly covered the mouths and noses of the two Egyptian girls, causing them to faint before being carried out of the elevator. Some individuals claimed that one of the men involved in the kidnapping was the girls' father. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Al-Masry Al-Youm published on December 21, 2023. The title of the report read, "فاصيل جديدة.. «الداخلية» تشرح بالفيديو قصة القبض على المتهمين بخطف طفلتين داخل مصعد" An English translation of the title read, "New details.. "Interior" explains in a video the story of the arrest of the accused of kidnapping two girls inside an elevator" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the mother of the two girls, a resident of Nasr City, filed a complaint with the authorities, alleging that her ex-husband, an accountant working abroad, along with two other men, had forcibly taken one of their daughters. She explained that the family had been embroiled in disputes since their separation, during which the girls had lived with their father until 2022. The mother further stated that she had obtained legal custody of both daughters following the separation. Following this we also came across another report published by Al Arabiya on December 23, 2023. "I want my sister" .. The" girl in the elevator video confronts the accused of kidnapping her sister" read an English translation of the report. Here is the link to the report. The report revealed that the father of the two girls had, with the help of his two friends, carried out the kidnapping as seen in the video footage. It was found that on the same day of the incident, he had left the country with one of his daughters through Cairo International Airport, with her own will. The two friends were arrested— one of whom appeared in the video alongside the father, while the other was the driver of the car used in the kidnapping. Upon questioning, both individuals confessed their involvement, stating that they had committed the crime in collaboration with the father in exchange for a sum of money. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video dating back to 2023 from Cairo, Egypt was falsely shared in the name of India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Unrelated videos of Owaisi offering namaz and woman reciting bhajan on airplanes shared on social media with false communal spin
content: New Delhi, September 17 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared two videos, claiming that one of them showed a Muslim man, seemingly AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi, offering 'namaz' on board a flight, while the other one showed a woman singing bhajan in response to the man's prayer. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video from two separate incidents and were shared together on social media with a false communal narrative. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 10 two videos, claiming that one showed a man offering namaz in an airplane while the other showed a woman reciting bhajan in response to the man's prayer. The caption of the post read, "A Muslim person doing Namaz by sitting on his own seat & this lady got triggered & started doing this Just imagine the amount of Toxicity & Intolerance filled in her. This is what Modi has done to Hindus in 10 years." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first scanned social media platforms and found that several other users had shared the same videos with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here, here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The videos were widely shared on X as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The Desk debunked the claim by investigating the two videos categorically. Here's what we found: Video 1 The Desk ran the first video of a man, seemingly AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi, offering 'namaz' on a flight, through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Hyderabad News Urdu on August 26, 2019. The description of the video read, "Asaduddin Owaisi Performed Namaz in Plane During Traveling" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Further, we also came across a Facebook page named The Gulbarga Mirror, which shared the same video on August 28, 2019. "AIMIM PARTY PRESIDENT BR ASADUDDIN OWAISI OFFERING NAMAZ IN FLIGHT" read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post. Video 2 In the next phase of investigation, the Desk ran the other video, of a woman singing bhajan on flight, through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a similar video uploaded on X by a handle named 'Drunk Journalist' on March 31, 2024. The caption of the post read, "This is okay and permitted." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching, the Desk noticed this was similar to the viral video but we noticed it did not have the voiceover as the viral one. We also found that the same user replied to one of the viral posts on X stating that this video had no connection with the man offering namaz on the flight. The caption of the post read, "This video has nothing to do with Namaz. This is an old video where this woman just sang her Bhajan and it has nothing to do with Muslims or Namaaz. Randomly post some crap and people go wild." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk came across a YouTube video, which was an extended version of the viral video. The video was shared on March 8 by a channel named 'SAI ki beti Nisha Shivdasani Nisha Shivdasani.' In the video, the woman can be heard introducing herself as Nisha Shivdasani and wishes the flight passengers on the occasion of International Women's Day, which is celebrated across the world on March 8. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The video was captioned, "happy international Women's day 2024 | Nisha Shivdasani | Indigoairline thank you." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that two unrelated videos from different incidents were shared on social media with a false communal twist.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated footage falsely shared on social media in name of Manipur protests; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Amid the recent round of violence and protests in Manipur, a video of a sea of people waving flags and banners and raising slogans was shared on social media recently, with users claiming it was a recent footage from Manipur, where people had taken to the streets to demand "freedom from India". However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was AI-generated, which was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 11 a video, claiming it showed a sea of people raising slogans and waving banners in Manipur to demand "freedom from India". The caption of the post read, "#BREAKINGNEWS The situation in Manipur has significantly worsened, with no coverage from Indianın media. Frustration is mounting, as thousands of people have taken to the streets demanding freedom fron India. #India #Indian #Modi #Manipur" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post by the username Manab Jyoti Gogoi sharing a similar video on February 1. The caption of the post read, "MANIPUR WANTS PEACE All images are AI Generated... #manipur #peace #stop #killings #rally #imphal #public" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk scanned the user's Instagram account and found that he had shared several such AI-generated videos. Here is the link to the profile and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through the Hive Moderation , a generative AI voice and robust deepfake audio detection application. Below is a screenshot of the result of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated video was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: This press release claiming Adani Group bribed and threated Kenyan officials is FAKE; details inside
content: New Delhi, September 18 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of an alleged press release by Adani Group, titled "denouncing baseless accusations and threats", has been widely shared on social media. The purported press release not only admits to have paid bribes for securing projects in Kenya, but also threatens to "reveal the names of government shareholders who have benefited from our investments". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral screenshot was fake and was shared with a false claim. No such press release was issued by the Adani Group. Kenya Aviation Workers Union recently protested against the Adani Group's planned deal to take over Kenya's main international airport, calling the deal "opaque" and warning it could result in job losses. The protest ended after they were assured by the government that the plan will only proceed with the union's approval. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 16 a screenshot of an alleged press release by Adani Group, which not only admitted to bribing the officials for securing a project in Kenya, but also threatened to "reveal the names of government shareholders who have benefited from our investments" if the protests in the country continued. The caption of the post read, "पहले तो @gautam_adani रिश्वत देकर पॉलिसी फ़ैसले अपने हक़ में करवाता है, और बाद में "रिश्वतों के खुलासे" की धमकी देकर दोबारा बाँह मरोड़ता है। इंडिया में भी यही फार्मूला है इसका, दोनों पार्टियों के नेताओं / सारे अफ़सरों के साथ। हर पार्टी के बड़े नेता जेब में हैं इसके। (@AdaniOnline इस लैटर की सत्यता पर सफ़ाई दे)" An English translation of the caption read, "First @gautam_adani bribes the other person to get the policy decisions in his favour, and then twists his arm again by threatening to "expose the bribes".The formula is same in India too, with the leaders/officers of both the parties.Big leaders of every party are in his pocket. ( @AdaniOnline Clarify the authenticity of this letter)" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same screenshot with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the viral screenshot was fake. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the official website and social media handles of the Adani Group and found an X post issuing a clarification regarding the viral screenshot dated September 16, calling it fake. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Further, the Desk found a link to the official press release issued by the organisation regarding the same. "Media Statement on Fake Press Releases" read the title of the release dated for September 16. Here is the link to the press release and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the release, several fake press releases, including one titled "Adani Group Denounces Baseless Accusations and Threats," have been shared with the aim of misleading the public about the group's activities in Kenya. The Adani Group firmly denied issuing any such statements, clarifying that neither the company nor its subsidiaries have released press communications related to their presence in the country. The group condemned the circulation of these fake releases, urging the public to dismiss them entirely. In response to this misleading campaign, the Adani Group stated that it would pursue legal action against individuals involved in spreading false information. Further the Desk noticed several discrepancies between the official release and the viral screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing the two: The Desk found the logo in the viral screenshot was placed on the left side whereas the original release has the logo on the right-hand side of the screenshot. We also noticed a mismatch in the date format of both the releases. In the next phase of the investigation the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find report related to the protests in Kenya and came across a report by Aljazeera published on September 11. The title of the report read, "Kenya airport workers strike over takeover bid by India's Adani Group" Here is the link to the report: According to the report, the Kenyan government announced a build-and-operate agreement with the Indian conglomerate Adani Group to renovate Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA), including the construction of an additional runway and terminal. The Kenya Airport Workers Union, led protests against the deal, arguing that it would result in job losses and deteriorate employment conditions. Several critics raised concerns that the agreement would deny taxpayers future profits from JKIA, which contributes over 5 percent of Kenya's gross domestic product (GDP) through its freight and passenger fees. Meanwhile, another report by Business Today, dated September 12, stated that the workers' union ended the strike after they were assured by the government that the plan will only proceed with the union's approval. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot shared on social media in the name of Adani Group was fake.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 photo shared as recent on social media with false claim in connection with IIT-BHU gangrape case; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 5 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a photo claiming that it showed three accused in the IIT-BHU gangrape case cutting cake and celebrating with "people of a particular party" after their release on bail. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a photo dating back to 2021 was shared on social media with a false claim. Only two of the three accused have been released on bail whereas the third accused, who can be seen in the viral photo, is still in jail. The three accused – Anand alias Abhishek Chauhan, Kunal Pandey and Saksham Patel – allegedly raped a woman student of IIT-BHU when she had come out of her hostel with a friend on the night of November 1, 2023, according to the complaint lodged in the matter. Only two of the accused – Anand alias Abhishek Chauhan and Kunal Pandey – have been released on bail. The other accused, Saksham Patel, has not yet been granted bail; his bail application is set to be reviewed on September 14, 2024. The viral photo features BJP MLA from Varanasi Cantt, Saurabh Srivastava, along with Saksham Patel, who is still in jail. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 1 a photo claiming that it showed all the three accused in the IIT-BHU gangrape case cutting cake and celebrating after being released on bail. The caption of the post read, "When the gangrape accused of IIT BHU student came out on bail, Then their family members and people of a particular party welcomed them by cutting a cake. Only those wearing black caps can welcome rapists like this. When the gangrape accused of IIT #black_cap_tainted_thoughts" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that several other users shared it with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report with the same photo published by Aaj Tak on September 1. The title of the report read, "IIT-BHU: गैंगरेप के आरोपियों को केक लगा रहे BJP विधायक, वायरल तस्वीर की सच्चाई खुद MLA ने बताई!" An English translation of the title read, "IIT-BHU: BJP MLA applying cake to gangrape accused, MLA himself revealed the truth of the viral picture!" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "A photo of both of them is also going viral on social media. In which BJP MLA from Varanasi Cantt Assembly Saurabh Srivastava is celebrating his birthday with both the accused Kunal Pandey and Abhishek Chauhan who have got bail," stated the report. "The BJP MLA is also seen applying cake on the face of accused Abhishek Chauhan with his own hands. However, when the BJP MLA was contacted over the phone to know his side in this matter, he said that this photo is about 5 years old. He said that it can also be seen that the photo is from the Corona period. Because he is wearing a mask," it added.
