Taking a cue from this, the Desk scanned the social media handles of BJP MLA Saurabh Srivastava and came across the same viral photo uploaded on July 12, 2021. The caption of the post read, "भाजपा के महानगर उपाध्यक्ष श्री मधुकर चित्रांश जी व युवा कार्यकर्ता श्री सक्षम सिंह पटेल को जन्मदिवस की हार्दिक शुभकामनाएं..." An English translation of the caption read, "Happy Birthday to BJP's Metropolitan Vice President Mr. Madhukar Chitransh and young activist Mr. Saksham Singh Patel..." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk looked for photos of the three accused. The combination images below highlight that the viral image shows two of the three accused in the gangrape case, whereas the third person in photo is BJP MLA Saurabh Srivastava. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a photo dated back to 2021 and showed only two of the three accused in the IIT-BHU gangrape case. The third person – BJP MLA from Varanasi Cantt. – was wrongly identified as one of the accused.

title: PTI Fact Check: Protest video from Venezuela falsely shared on social media in name of Delhi; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 17 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed people running on the streets of Delhi in panic following a cloudburst. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an unrelated video of stampede during protest over a disputed election in South America's Venezuela was falsely shared as a recent incident from Delhi, India. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 13 a video of people running on a street in chaos, and claimed that it was from Delhi following a cloudburst. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an Instagram post shared by Venezuela En La Mira, handle with over 4 lakh followers. The caption of the post, dated July 30, read: "Protesta en Puerto La Cruz, estado Anzoátegui, contra el fraude de Maduro.Por Monitoreamos. #VenezuelaEnLaMira #Venezuela #Noticias #Elnacionalweb #Pais #Venezolanos #Instagram #Viral" An English translation of the caption read, "Protest in Puerto La Cruz, Anzoátegui state, against Maduro's fraud. By Monitoreamos. #VenezuelaEnLaMira #Venezuela #News #Elnacionalweb #Country #Venezuelans #Instagram #Viral" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found the photo carried in the post strikingly similar to the visuals of the viral video. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk looked at the clear version of the video and noticed 'CCR'. On searching for the same on Google Maps, we were able to locate the place as Centro Commercial Regina Mall , in Puerto La Cruz, Venezuela. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report published by CNN on July 31. The title of the report read, "Venezuela is wracked with protests and election uncertainty. Here's what to know" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, The National Electoral Council (CNE) officially declared President Nicolas Maduro the winner on July 27, with 80% of ballots counted. It said Maduro had won 51.2% of the votes, while Edmundo Gonzalez received 44.2%. Following this the opposition claimed their candidate, Gonzalez, received more than twice the votes of Maduro, but the election authorities announced Maduro as the winner. International observers called the election unfair, while the government labelled the protests an attempted rebellion. Subsequently the Desk concluded that an unrelated video from stampede during protest in Venezuela was shared as a recent incident from Delhi, India.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of elderly man 'molesting a woman' shared as real incident from Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 19 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of an elderly man allegedly molesting a burqa-clad woman was circulated on social media with the claim that the incident recently happened in Bangladesh. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that it was a scripted video originally posted by a Bangladesh-based content creator, Azizul Haque Morad, and was shared as an actual incident on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X (former Twitter) user shared on September 16 a video, claiming that it showed an elderly man molesting a burqa-clad woman in Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "वीडियो में गंदी-गंदी गालियां थी तो म्यूट कर दिया बांग्लादेश का वीडियो है बुजुर्ग की उम्र देखीये और बाद में जब उसे जब लड़की ने दो तमाचे मारे तब बुजुर्ग कह रहे हैं कि मैं जल्दी में था तो गलती से हाथ लग गया था" An English translation of the caption read, "There were abusive words in the video, so it was muted. This is a video from Bangladesh; look at the age of the old man And later, when the girl slapped him twice, the old man said that I was in a hurry and it touched me by mistake." Here is the link and archive link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other Facebook users shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a Facebook post by 'Azizul 2.0', shared on September 12. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same video as the viral one. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: The desk then scanned the user's Facebook profile and found several videos with the same bearded man shared on the profile. Here is the link to the profile, and below is a screenshot of the same: While reviewing the profile, the Desk noticed some videos were tagged to another account with a similar username. Further investigation revealed that the user used another account named Azizul Haque Morad, which had a bio identifying him as a "Video Creator." Additionally, the Desk found that the phone number listed on the profile started with Bangladesh's country code. Below is the link to the other account and a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk tried to contact Morad to clarify the video. The story will be updated as and when a response is received. Our investigation revealed that a scripted video was shared on social media as a real incident with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, CPI(M) leader Sitaram Yechury was not a Christian; social media posts shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, September 18 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo of people paying last respects to CPI(M) leader Sitaram Yechury was recently shared on social media to claim that he was a Christian since his body was placed in a coffin-like wooden box, which is commonly associated with Christian funerals. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false as Yechury was born in a Telugu-speaking Brahmin family, and never changed his religion. In fact, Yechury himself stated that he was an atheist. The social media posts were shared with a false communal claim. The mortal remains of Yechury, who passed away at AIIMS Delhi on September 12, were donated to the hospital authorities for medical research after being kept at the party office in the national capital for people to pay their tributes. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 15 a photo of people paying tributes to Sitaram Yechury with his mortal remains kept in a coffin-like wooden box. The user shared the photo to claim that the late leader was a Christian. The caption of the post read, "Name: Sitaram Yechuri Religion: Christian Imagine how many people he had fooled with his Hindu name while being a rice bag all along." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same graphic with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here, here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be viewed here , here and here and their archived here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report by The New Indian Express, published on September 14, which carried the same photo. The title of the report read: "Political leaders, diplomats pay last respects to Sitaram Yechury" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, leaders from various political parties, diplomats, and party volunteers gathered on September 14 at the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPM) headquarters in New Delhi to pay their final respects to the party's general secretary, Sitaram Yechury. Later that evening, Yechury's body was donated to AIIMS for medical research, in the presence of his family members and members of the party's polit bureau. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video of Yechury's Rajya Sabha speech in 2017, uploaded on the official channel of The Print. The title of video read: "When CPI(M)'s Sitaram Yechury Recalled His Political Stint In His Farewell Speech In Rajya Sabha." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: During his speech in Rajya Sabha, the late Marxist leader can be heard saying, "I was born in the Madras General Hospital now called Chennai to a Telugu-speaking Brahmin family. My grandfather being a judge…goes to Guntur, so we shifted there in 1954, I was born in 1952. We shifted to Hyderabad in 1956. My school education is in an Islamic culture that was prevalent in Hyderabad under the Nizam rule in the early days of independence in 56….. Then I came to Delhi, studied here. I am married to a person whose father is a Sufi of the Islamic order, and whose surname is Chisti… Her mother is a Rajput but a Mysorean Rajput who migrated there in the 8th century AD. We're now in the 21st Century…I am from a south Indian Brahmin family married to this lady, what will my son be known as, sir?… There's nothing that can describe my son rather than being an Indian." Following this, we also came across an X post by Yechury criticising a statement of former Union Minister Ravi Shankar Prasad on April 22, 2017. The caption of the post read, "Indians who are Hindus, Muslims, Christians, Sikhs or Atheists (like me) are all Indian citizens. #NotCharity #Constitution" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across a report by Hindustan Times published on October 14, 2018with the title, "Don't wear Lenin on my sleeve: Yechury on Communism, the Emergency and more." Here is the link to the report: According to the interview, "'I was named Sitaramarao, after my grandfather, but I dropped the caste appendage and carried on with my name. So Sitaram it has remained. In any case as Shakespeare said what is in a name?" During the investigation, we found that the viral image, along with other visuals, were posted by Jawaharlal Nehru University Student's Union (JNUSU) on X. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: It may be worth mentioning here that Yechury had completed his post-graduation from JNU. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by Business Standard on September 15. The title of the report read, "Amid chants of Lal Salaam, Yechury's body handed over to AIIMS for research" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The report stated that wrapped in the red flag of the CPI(M), the body of party veteran Sitaram Yechury was handed over to AIIMS authorities for medical research. The ceremony took place amid chants of "Lal Salaam," as supporters and party members paid their final respects. Subsequently, the Desk concluded the photo was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this photo doesn't show AIIMS Delhi doctors paying tributes to Sitaram Yechury; 2016 photo from China shared as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Sep 19 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A photo recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed doctors at AIIMS Delhi paying their last respects to CPI(M) leader Sitaram Yechury, who breathed his last at the hospital earlier this month, by bowing before his body. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an unrelated photo from China's Hefei, dating back to 2016, which showed doctors paying respects to a fellow doctor, whose family donated his organs after his death, was shared on social media as recent from India with a false claim. The body of Yechury, who passed away at AIIMS Delhi following a prolonged illness on September 12, was donated to the hospital authorities for medical research. Claim A Facebook user shared a photo on September 17 and claimed that it showed doctors at AIIMS Delhi paying their last respects to Sitaram Yechury, who breathed his last at the hospital on September 12. The caption of the post read: "Doctors at Delhi AIIMS pay their last respects to an organ donor. The name of the organ donor is Sitaram Yechury." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same graphic with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The photo was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk found a similar photo uploaded on Facebook by the official page of China based news portal CGTN September 30, 2016. The caption of the post read, "Chinese doctor dies while volunteering in Tibet, donates his organs Zhao Ju, a 41-year-old doctor from east China's Anhui Province, volunteered to work in Shannan, Tibet Autonomous Region with a group of other doctors two months ago. But partway through his service he began to suffer headaches and dizziness - he was found to have a brain aneurysm, the rupture of which led to his death. Zhao's family respected his noble last wishes and donated his kidneys, liver and corneas. "My son was a doctor, he used to heal the wounded and rescue the dying and he would always do his best for the betterment of others," said Zhao's father. Fellow doctors were pictured paying their respects to Zhao with deep bows at a hospital in Hefei City, the capital of Anhui Province. And netizens were quick to pay tribute online to a man who showed such selfless devotion to helping others." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by the English-language website of China News Service by September 30, 2016. The title of the report read, "On duty doctor dies in Tibet, donates all usable organs (1/3)" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Doctors and nurses bow to the body of Zhao Ju at a hospital in Hefei City, the capital of East China's Anhui Province, Sept. 29, 2016. Zhao volunteered to join a team of doctors sent to work in Shannan, Tibet Autonomous Region in July as part of the province's assistance program. The 41-year-old suffered symptoms of headache and dizziness a few days after arriving in Shannan, and was later found to have a ruptured aneurysm in his head. Zhao died on Sept. 22 and donated his body parts. " stated the report. In the next phase of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a PTI report carried by Business Standard on September 15. According to the report, Yechury's body was handed over to AIIMS Delhi for education and research purpose. The title of the report read, "The title of the report read, "Amid chants of Lal Salaam, Yechury's body handed over to AIIMS for research" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The report stated that wrapped in the red flag of the CPI(M), the body of party veteran Sitaram Yechury was handed over to AIIMS authorities for medical research. The ceremony took place amid chants of "Lal Salaam," as supporters and party members paid their final respects. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old photo dating back to September, 2016 from China was shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Decade-old photo of road with potholes from Prayagraj shared as recent on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, September 20 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Several incidents of potholes and roads caving in during this Monsoon season have been reported recently. Amid this, a photo of a pothole-ridden road with a partially overturned truck has been shared on social media with users blaming the central government for the poor condition of roads. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image has been circulated online since at least 2012 and is reportedly from Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. The old photo was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 16 a photo of a pothole-ridden road with a partially overturned truck, and criticised the BJP-led central government for the alleged poor condition of roads. The caption of the post read, "Our roads are deliberately designed to keep drivers alert ! Thank you #Gadkari" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that a similar photo was shared on Facebook as well. The caption of the post read, "Our roads are deliberately designed to keep drivers alert ! Thank you #NitinGadkari ji #ModiHaiTohMumkinHai #ModiDisasterForIndia" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar photo shared on the official page of Alfa College of Engineering & Technology, Allagadda on July 23, 2012. The caption of the post read, "I call this peoples mistake not governments, corruption free government is peoples responisbility, How many of you agree dear engineers!" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, we also came across the same photo shared by Times Photos on April 30, 2015, stating that it was from Prayagraj. The caption of the photo read, "No Road Left: When it rains in India, the roads get very damaged. But this road in Allahabad got damaged to the next level! " Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: During our investigation, we also came an AFP Fact Check report carried by The Express Tribune in October 2019, which clarified that the photo was from Prayagraj, and not Peshawar, Pakistan. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo was at least 12 years old and was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Newspaper screenshot claiming Congress General Secretary KC Venugopal made statement about ending reservations is edited and fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 21 (Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A screenshot of a Hindi newspaper was shared on social media by many users, claiming Congress General Secretary K C Venugopal made a statement about ending (caste-based) reservations. Social media users shared the newspaper screenshot to target the Congress party for its stand on reservation policy. PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the viral claim and found it to be fake. The investigation revealed that K.C. Venugopal did not make any such statement about ending reservations. Congress General Secretary Dr. Vineet Punia called the viral claim fake. Claim On September 20, a user on the social media platform 'X' (formerly Twitter) posted a newspaper clipping, saying, "Congress is the root of unrest and casteism in the country. As long as Congress exists, attacks on reservations will continue. If Congress is destroyed, reservations will flourish." The post's link , archive link , and screenshot can be seen here. Another social media user shared the newspaper clipping and wrote, "Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was right: Congress was anti-Dalit, is anti-Dalit, and will remain anti-SC/ST. Just look, Congress leaders themselves are saying that Congress's biggest goal is to end reservations in India." The post's link , archive link , and screenshot can be seen here. Investigation To verify the viral claim, the desk first carefully examined the newspaper and found that it was labeled "Aapki Awaaz." Upon searching, we did not find any credible newspaper by this name. Continuing the investigation, the desk tried to find media reports related to the viral statement using relevant keywords. If a Congress leader had made such a statement against reservations, it would have been reported in the media, but we did not find any credible media report related to his statement. During the investigation, we found KC Venugopal's most recent statement on reservations in a report published on the ABP News website. In it, Congress General Secretary KC Venugopal accused the BJP of defaming Rahul Gandhi. He said that the agenda being pushed by the BJP would not benefit them. After Rahul Gandhi's statement on reservations in Washington, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha came under BJP's attack, following which Congress General Secretary defended Rahul Gandhi and targeted the BJP. Read the full report here . Finally, the desk contacted Congress General Secretary Dr. Vineet Punia, who called the viral claim fake, saying, "Our leader did not make any such statement. This is false propaganda by our political opponents." PTI Fact Check's investigation so far makes it clear that the fake statement attributed to K.C. Venugopal is going viral on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 video of molestation and assault on woman in Bihar's Saran shared as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, September 20 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video showing some men molesting a woman sitting on the back of a motorcycle, pulling her saree and beating her with a stick has been shared on social media, with users claiming it to be a recent incident from Bihar. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that while the footage was from Bihar's Saran, the incident actually took place in 2021. The video was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 19 a video showing a group of men molesting a woman sitting on the back of a motorcycle, pulling her saree and beating her with a stick, and claimed that it was a recent footage from Bihar. The caption of the post read, "ये वीभत्स दृश्य और महिला के प्रति घृणित कार्य बिहार में हो रहा बताया जा रहा है! भाजपा सरकार है और इसे ही भाजपा नेता रामराज्य कहते होंगे?" An English translation of the caption read, "These gruesome scenes and disgusting acts against women are said to be happening in Bihar! There is a BJP government and BJP leaders must be calling this Ramrajya?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded on the official channel of Live Hindustan on October 6, 2021. The description of the post read, "Bihar: छपरा में चिल्लाती रही महिला, साड़ी खींचते रहे मनचले, Video viral होने के बाद चार गिरफ्तार" An English translation of the description read, "Bihar: In Chhapra, the woman kept screaming while the miscreants kept pulling her sari, four arrested after the video went viral" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Navbharat Times on October 6, 2021. The title of the report read, "Chhapra Viral Video : पकड़े गए छपरा के वायरल वीडियो में दिख रहे दरिंदे, बिहार में 'गिद्ध कल्चर' कबतक?" An English translation of the title read, ""Chhapra Viral Video: The beasts seen in the viral video of Chhapra have been caught, till when will the 'vulture culture' continue in Bihar?" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident occurred in Laxman Chor area under Dariyapur Police Station limits, where the victim and her friend were passing through a forested area when their motorcycle suddenly stopped. At that moment, 4-5 boys attacked the woman, attempting to disrobe her. Some of the attackers touched her inappropriately, while others pulled at her saree as she screamed for help, still sitting on the bike. One of the boys recorded the assault on camera. The man accompanying the woman managed to start the motorcycle and fled the scene. The police have since arrested four suspects — Rakesh Kumar, Arvind Kumar, Nitish Kumar, and Amod Kumar. However, two other accused, Guddu Rai and Dharmendra Kumar, were absconding (back then). The Desk also came across an X post by Saran District Administration, giving an update regarding the incident on October 6, 2021. The caption of the post read, "सारण पुलिस द्वारा वायरल वीडियो की सूचना प्राप्त होने के 8 घंटे के अंदर घटनास्थल का सत्यापन कर सभी 6 अभियुक्तों की पहचान कर ली गई है।वायरल वीडियो में शामिल 4 अभियुक्तों को गिरफ्तार कर लिया गया है,शेष अभियुक्तों की गिरफ्तारी शीघ्र ही संभावित है।" An English translation of the caption read, "Within 8 hours of receiving information about the viral video, Saran Police verified the scene of the incident and identified all the 6 accused. 4 accused involved in the viral video have been arrested, the arrest of the remaining accused is likely soon.@nildeoreIAS" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Hence, it was clear from our investigation that the video shared as a recent incident from Bihar actually dated back to October 2021.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of an actor dancing at RG Kar protest site in Kolkata shared on social media claiming her to be a doctor; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 21 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a woman dancing on a street and claimed that she was one of the doctors protesting in Kolkata over the RG Kar rape-murder case. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the woman was Bengali actor Mokksha Sengupta, who performed the 'Kalli Nrutyam' as part of protest against the case in Jadavpur's Santoshpur area, and not a doctor. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. The junior doctors at Kolkata's RG Kar Medical College and Hospital protested for over a month, which was called off on September 21 following their meeting with West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee, where they presented their charter of demands and were given assurance over the same. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 20 a video of a woman dancing on the street, claiming she was a doctor protesting in Kolkata against the rape and murder at RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. The caption of the post read, "ममता बनर्जी के विरोध के स्वर बढ़ते जा रहे है ।RG KAR अस्पताल की घटना के विरोध में कल डाक्टरों ने फिर प्रदर्शन किया । माँ काली के संहार करने वाले रूप में ये नृत्य एक डाक्टर कर रही है । ममता बनर्जी का सिंहासन जल्द उखड़ेगा" An English translation of the post read, "Voices of opposition against Mamata Banerjee are increasing. Yesterday, doctors again protested against the incident at RG KAR Hospital. A doctor is performing this dance in the form of Maa Kali who is the destroyer. Mamata Banerjee's throne will soon be toppled." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other users shared the same video. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived version can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded on X post by a handle named Prasu on September 19. The caption of the post read, "Actress Mokksha 👏👏 🙏" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised Google search and came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Tollywood News Raja on September 19, 2024. The description of the video read, "Actress Mokksha Powerful Bhadrakali Dance Performance For Kolkata Doctor Protest | Mokksha Sengupta" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: The Desk then scanned the social media handles (Facebook and Instagram) of Mokksha, which confirmed that the woman in the viral video was her. Here are the links for the Facebook and Instagram handles and below are the screenshots of the same: We also found a report published by India Today published on September 16 mentioning about the viral video and Mokksha. "Meet actor Mokksha whose street dance at Kolkata protest has gone viral," read the title of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "When I first heard about the crime, I was in Hyderabad for a film release and was unaware of the situation. As soon as I learnt about this heinous act in Kolkata, I returned to my city to protest. I felt compelled to act because I am a sensitive person. As an artist, I chose street performance as my form of protest. I dedicated my time to participating in various protests, using my art to voice the concerns of the common people, standing as a representative of the city's residents," stated Mokksha in the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman in the viral video was a Bengali actor, and not a doctor.

title: PTI Fact Check: Bangladesh video of men vandalising toll plaza shared in name of India; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 23 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed Muslim men vandalising a toll plaza in India after they were asked to pay toll fee. However, the PTI Fact Check found that the video was from an incident that happened in Bangladesh, which was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 23 a video showing a group of men wearing skull caps, seemingly from the Muslim community, vandalising a toll plaza in India after being asked to pay toll fee. The caption of the post read, "Demography is Destiny! Poor toll booth guy doesn't understand that the skull cap is the toll free pass provided by the Secular government. We are heading to Gazva E Hind..…" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on X as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of SOMOY TV on September 18. The description of the video read, "Arguing with the toll collector, at one point a young man broke the barricade stopping the vehicles. The CCTV footage of the incident at the Kuril Toll Plaza of the elevated expressway in the capital has been spread through social media. The authorities informed the police but no action was taken." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk found that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report News Post BD published on September 18. The title of the report read, "এক্সপ্রেসওয়ের টোল প্লাজার কর্মীদের মারধর, তদন্তে পুলিশ" An English translation of the title read, "Expressway toll plaza workers beaten up, police investigating" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the incident occurred at the Kuril Toll Plaza at around 9:48 am on Wednesday, September 18. CCTV footage revealed that a medium-sized pickup truck, carrying several passengers, stopped at the toll plaza on the Dhaka Elevated Expressway. Upon noticing the extra passengers, the toll plaza attendant refused to collect the toll fee. In response, one of the individuals in the pickup truck broke the toll plaza barrier. Several others then exited the vehicle and assaulted the toll plaza workers. Following the altercation, the pickup truck proceeded onto the elevated expressway with its passengers. The Desk came across another report published by Dhaka Tribune published on September 18. "Elevated Expressway's Kuril toll plaza vandalized centring pickup van crossing" read the title of the report. Here is the link to the report: The report stated the incident occurred at the Kuril Toll Plaza on the Dhaka Elevated Expressway when a pickup truck, carrying 30-40 passengers, attempted to bypass regulations prohibiting certain vehicles like pickup vans, motorcycles and rickshaws from using the expressway due to safety concerns. The toll plaza attendant refused to accept the toll, leading one individual to break the barrier, while others assaulted the staff. The project director of the Elevated Expressway, AHM Akhtar confirmed the incident and emphasised the safety risks posed by such vehicles. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was from Bangladesh, not India.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Bangladesh Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus did not announce his retirement; digitally altered video with AI-generated audio shared on social media
content: New Delhi, September 23 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bangladesh Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus was recently shared on social media in which he was heard announcing his resignation and handing over power to Pinaki Bhattacharyya. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of Yunus' speech was digitally altered using superimposed audio and shared on social media with false claim. Nobel Laureate Muhammad Yunus was sworn in as the chief adviser of Bangladesh's interim government on August 6, a day after Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled the country following a violent crackdown on a student-led uprising. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 13 a video showing Bangladesh Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus announcing his resignation and handing over power to Pinaki Bhattacharyya. The caption of the post read, "প্রধান উপদেষ্টা পদত্যাগ করেছেন....... এবং কাকে ক্ষমতা দিয়েছেন সেটা মনোযোগ দিয়ে শুনুন।" An English translation of the caption read, "Chief Adviser Resigns And listen carefully to whom you have given power." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the video and first noticed a lip-sync issue with the viral video. We then ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of EKHON TV on September 11. The description of the video read, "জাতির উদ্দেশে প্রধান উপদেষ্টা ড. ইউনূস-এর সম্পূর্ণ বক্তব্য | Dr. Yunus Speech | Interim Government" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the same: While listening to the extended video, the Desk found that Yunus did not make any announcements regarding his retirement. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through TrueMedia and Resemble AI , both generative AI voices and robust deepfake audio detection apps, both suggesting presence of AI-generated audio. Below are the screenshots of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Yunus' speech was digitally altered with superimposed audio and shared on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of attack on stage play artiste in Odisha shared on social media with misleading communal narrative; Details inside
content: New Delhi, September 24 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video with the claim that it showed a Muslim man delivering a hate speech in which he said that he will "convert all Hindus to Islam" and later being attacked by a Hindu man in retaliation. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video of an incident during a stage play in Odisha was shared on social media with a misleading claim. The man making the communal remark was actually an artiste who was attacked by a person from the audience. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 17 a video and claimed that it showed a Muslim man on stage saying that he will "convert all Hindus to Islam", and later being beaten by a Hindu man for his remarks. The caption of the post read, "A peaceful was giving speech against Hindus A single Hindu man went on stage and gave him a GPL in front of peaceful fringe mob" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found several other Facebook users shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that the viral video showed a drama scene from a play in Odisha. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a video report published by Kalinga TV on September 11. The title of the report read, "Audience beat up Jatra artist on stage in Sambalpur, watch" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Following this, the Desk came across another report published by Odisha TV published on September 11. The title of the report read, "Too real to handle: Jatra villains thrashed by audience for devilish acting in Odisha's Sambalpur" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, during a performance of the Jatra party Swarna Mahal's play 'Swami Pain Pachhe Narkaku Jibi', a young man from the audience climbed onto the stage and began assaulting one of the performers. Later it was found that the artistes performed so well that the audience could not resist and a youth went to the stage and attacked an artist on the dialogue of conversion of religion. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of an incident during a stage play in Odisha was shared on social media with a misleading claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video does not show meteorite fall in Rajasthan; VFX video shared on social media as real
content: New Delhi, September 25 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a recent incident of meteorite falling on land in Rajasthan. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was digitally created using VFX technology, which was falsely shared on social media as a real celestial event. Claim An Instagram user shared on September 18 a video and claimed that it showed a meteorite falling on land in Rajasthan. The caption of the video read, "राजस्थान के सांचोर शहर में तेज धमाके के साथ बमनुमा आकार की चीज आसमान से आकर गिरी और जमीन में एक फुट तक धंस गई. इस धमाके की आवाज 2 किमी दूर तक सुनाई दी. इस चीज को कोई उल्का पिंड बता रहा है, कोई मोर्टार, कोई बम तो कोई जहाज का टूटा हुआ हिस्सा. बहरहाल, यह चीज अब पुलिस के कब्जे में है और जांच जारी है.पूरी जानकारी के लिए ये वीडियो देखें" An English translation of the caption read, "In Rajasthan's Sanchore city, a bomb-like object fell from the sky with a loud explosion and got buried one foot deep in the ground. The sound of this explosion was heard up to 2 km away. Some are calling this object a meteorite, some a mortar, some a bomb and some a broken part of an airplane. Anyway, this object is now in the possession of the police and investigation is going on. Watch this video for complete information." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel Unreal VFX on November 3, 2023. The description of the video read, "In this video i made some crash scenes with #adobe #aftereffects and you can see what happened if falled #meteor to #earth I put very nice vfx and sfx in this video. Thank you for watching. " Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was same as the video, as can also be seen in the combination image below: The Desk then scanned the YouTube channel and found several such videos, which were made using the VFX technology. We also scanned the user's Instagram account and found that several such videos made using VFX technology were shared there too. Here are the links to the user's Instagram handle and YouTube channel and below are screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google but did not come across any report to substantiate the claim of any recent dropping of meteorite in Rajasthan. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a digitally created video was shared on social media as real with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Arvind Kejriwal criticising 'one nation, one election' proposal shared on social media as recent
content: New Delhi, September 25 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): After the Union Cabinet approved the proposal for 'one nation, one election' earlier this month, as recommended by a panel headed by former president Ram Nath Kovind, a video of AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal criticising the proposal was shared on social media, claiming the remarks were made recently. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a year-old video of the then Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 19 a video showing AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal criticising the "One Nation, One Election" proposal. The caption of the post read, "#दिल्ली के पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री अरविंद केजरीवाल ने वन नेशन वन इलेक्शन पर बोला जमकर हमलाl सुनिए क्या कहा दिल्ली के पूर्व मुख्यमंत्री अरविंद केजरीवाल ने |" An English translation of the caption read, "#Former Chief Minister of Delhi Arvind Kejriwal launched a scathing attack on One Nation One Election. Listen to what former Chief Minister of Delhi Arvind Kejriwal said." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video on Twitter with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and her e and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Aam Aadmi Party on September 18, 2023. The description of the video read, "Madhya Pradesh के Rewa में महारैली | Arvind Kejriwal की Latest Fiery Speech 🔥| AAP Madhya Pradesh" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Economic Times on September 18, 2023. The title of the report read, "Arvind Kejriwal opposes simultaneous polls, demands 'one nation, one education' system" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Kejriwal opposed the concept of 'one nation, one election' and stated that it allows the political parties to interact regularly with the electors. He further added that the country needs 'one nation, one education (equal education for all) and 'one nation, one treatment' (rich or poor, equal treatment for all). Following this, we came across a PTI report carried by The Print published on September 18, 2023. "Kejriwal opposes simultaneous polls, demands 'one nation, one education' system" read the title of the report. Here is the link to the report: "If this concept of one nation, one election is implemented, then political party leaders will roam around London, Paris and other places abroad for four-and-a-half years and will come to you just before elections. The AAP believes elections should be held every month and instead of one nation, one election, one nation, one education and one nation, one treatment system should be implemented in the country" stated Kejriwal during a rally in Rewa. In the next phase of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to check if Kejriwal recently made any remark on the 'one nation, one election' proposal. However, we could not find any substantial report on the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video was shared as recent on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show destruction by Hezbollah missiles in Israel; 2015 video from China shared with false claim
content: New Delhi, September 28 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and Lebanon's Hezbollah group, that has escalated after the killing of Hezbollah chief Hassan Nasrallah, a video has gone viral on social media, with users claiming that it showed the destruction caused by Hezbollah's guided missiles at what looks like a factory, in Israel. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video dated back to 2015 showing explosion at a chemical factory in China. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 24 a video, claiming that it showed the destruction caused by guided missiles of Hezbollah in Israel. The caption of the post read, "#Hezbollah Hits Israeli Base By Guided Missiles And Causes Comlete Destruction. Hezbollah #Israel" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived posts can be found here and here respectively. content: New Delhi, September 29 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that it showed a Muslim flower seller spitting on garlands outside a temple in India. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was from Pakistan, and was shared on social media with a false and communal claim. Claim An Instagram user shared on September 23 a video of a boy drinking water and then spitting on a flower garland, with claims that the boy was from the Muslim community and sold flowers outside a temple in India. The caption of the post read, "Before Buying Flowers For Pooja /Temple Please Check The Vendor हम ऐसे ही इन लोगों के खिलाफ आवाज उठाते रहेंगे ।। और आपसे निवेदन है अगर आप भी हमारे साथ हो और आवाज उठाना चाहते हो तो हमें फॉलो करके सहायता करें ।। निवेदन है फॉलो कर लिजिए - @thehinduclan #jayshreeram #bharat #bhartiyasena #hindu" An English translation of the caption read, "Before Buying Flowers For Pooja /Temple Please Check The Vendor We will continue to raise our voice against these people. And we request you that if you are also with us and want to raise your voice then please help us by following us. We request you to follow us - @thehinduclan #jayshreeram #bharat #bhartiyasena #hindu" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video on Twitter with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Twitter as well. The description of the video read, "Yeh technology pakistan se bahar ni jana chaiyee 🤪🤪" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show Jr NTR's effigy burnt by fans; accidental fire incident shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, October 1 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed fans burning the effigy of actor Nandamuri Taraka Rama Rao Jr., popularly known by the initialism Jr NTR, outside a theatre in Hyderabad over poor performance of his Telugu-language action-drama film, Devara. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was related to an incident where a cut-out of Jr NTR caught fire after fans set off firecrackers to celebrate the release of Devara. The video of the incident was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 27 a video showing an effigy of Jr. NTR on fire, claiming that it was set ablaze by his fans outside a Hyderabad theatre due to the poor ratings of his movie Devara. The caption of the post read: "Fans Burning NTR Cutout Outside Hyderabad Theatre after the Initial Poor Ratings & Bad Talk for the Movie #Devara !" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived links can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded on Twitter by the official handle of Deccan Chronicle on September 27. The caption of the post read, "In an unexpected turn of events, a huge cut out of Jr NTR caught fire due to firecrackers set off by excited fans during a massive celebrations at #Sudarshan theatre near RTC X roads in #Hyderabad on Friday. The mishap occurred during the celebrations of #Devara: Part 1 where hundreds of fans had gathered to mark the occasion." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Times of India on September 27. The title of the report read, "'Devara' Incident: Jr NTR's Cut-Out Set on Fire Outside Hyderabad Theatre" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a cut-out of Jr NTR caught fire after fans set off firecrackers to celebrate the release of Devara, starring Janhvi Kapoor, Saif Ali Khan, and Jr NTR. Local authorities and the fire brigade responded swiftly to extinguish the flames, and no injuries were reported in the incident. Following this the Desk also came across a report published by Hindustan Times on September 27. "Jr NTR's cutout catches fire at a theatre in Hyderabad on Devara Part 1 release day; fans click pictures" read the title of the report. Here is the link to the report: "At the Sudarshan 35 MM theatre at RTC X Roads in Hyderabad, Jr NTR's fans had put up a massive cutout of the actor and garlanded it. They also burst firecrackers, as is the norm in Telugu states during big releases like this. However, the celebrations took an unexpected turn when the cutout caught fire and went up in flames." stated the report. During its investigation, the Desk also found that Devara – 1 was released on September 27, the same day the video started making rounds on social media and when the incident actually took place outside a theatre in Hyderabad. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showed a cut-out of the actor catching fire accidentally.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Randeep Hooda's Swatantrya Veer Savarkar is not India's 'official entry' for Oscars 2025; Details inside
content: New Delhi, October 2 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A poster of actor Randeep Hooda-starrer film 'Swatantrya Veer Savarkar' was recently shared on social media with users claiming that the film was selected as one of India's official entries to the 97th Oscar Awards. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that Kiran Rao's 'Laapataa Ladies' was India's 'official entry' for the Oscars. The poster was shared on social media with a false claim. However, it is worth mentioning that the Randeep Hooda-starrer film may have been submitted for the Oscars individually, but Laapataa Ladies was India's only official entry for the Academy Awards, picked by the FFI. The Kiran Rao-directed movie was one chosen out of a list of 29 films from different languages, such as Hindi, Tamil, and Malayalam, among others. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 1 a poster of actor Randeep Hooda's starrer Swatantrya Veer Savarkar's, claiming that the movie was nominated as one of India's entries for the Oscars 2025. The caption of the post read, "The Film Federation of India has selected Swatantrya Veer Savarkar as one of the official entries from India for the Oscars 2024. Producers Anand Pandit, Sandeep Singh, and Randeep Hooda are overjoyed by this recognition and shared their excitement. #SwatantryaVeerSavarkar #RandeepHooda #India #Oscars2024 #Oscars #Explore #Bollywood #Viral" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same screenshot with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The post was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an Instagram post by the official handle of Sandeep Singh, producer of the movie shared a similar poster on September 24. The caption of the post read, "Honored and humbled! Our film SwatantryaVeer Savarkar has officially been submitted for the Oscars. Thank You FILM FEDERATION OF INDIA for this remarkable appreciation. This journey has been incredible, and we are immensely grateful to everyone who has supported us along the way. #WhoKilledHisStory" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The post mentioned that the film has been "officially submitted" for the Oscars and did not mention that it selected as India's official entry by FFI. This was the post, which led to the confusion. Following this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Times of India published on September 26. The title of the report read, "FFI President laughs off Veer Savarkar's makers' claim that the Randeep Hooda starrer has been 'officially' submitted to the Oscars" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "They (the makers of Savarkar) have given some wrong communication. I am going to release a statement about it as well. Only Laapataa Ladies has been sent for Oscars from India officially." stated Ravi Kottakara, FFI President. Meanwhile, a report by Hindustan Times stated that as per the rules of the Academy Awards, there can only be one 'official' entry from each country but filmmakers can submit their films as independent entries as well, which might have been the case with 'Swatantrya Veer Savarkar'. For instance, SS Rajamouli's blockbuster RRR and Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Gangubai Kathiawadi have been submitted independently in the past. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search to find reports related to Oscar nominated movies for 2025 and came across a PTI report carried by The New Indian Express published on September 23. The title of the report read, "'Laapataa Ladies' picked as India's entry for Oscars" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a 13-member selection committee headed by Assamese director Jahnu Barua unanimously decided on Laapataa Ladies, produced by Aamir Khan and Rao, for reckoning in the best international film category at the Academy Awards. Besides Laapataa Ladies, Hindi film Srikanth, Tamil movies Vaazhai and Thangalaan and Malayalam film Ullozhukku were among the top five in the 29-title list. Meanwhile, a report by Deadline, a popular American entertainment news website, listed the country-wise submission for the best international feature film category in the Oscars. We found it listing 'Laapataa Ladies' as the official entry for India. Here is the link to the article titled 'Oscars: Here Are This Year's Submissions For Best International Feature Film – Updated With China, Vietnam & More', and below is a screenshot of the same: The Film Federation of India officially announced 'Laapataa Ladies' as India's official entry for Oscars 2025 among a competitive pool of 29 films. Some of the formal enteries were Payal Kapadia's Cannes winner 'All We Imagine As Light', Anand Ekarshi's National Award-winning 'Aattam', and Sandeep Reddy Vanga's controversial blockbuster 'Animal'. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Laapataa Ladies was India's official entry for the Academy Awards, as stated by the FFI president.

title: PTI Fact Check: 7-year- old video of Jyotiraditya Scindia criticising Bajrang Dal shared as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, October 2 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia criticising the Bajrang Dal and accusing its member Balram of receiving funds from Pakistani spy agency ISI. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to February 2017, when Scindia was a Congress member. The seven-year-old video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 30 a video showing Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia criticising the Bajrang Dal. The caption of the post read, "लगता है सिंधिया जी का बीजेपी में दिन भर गया है" An English translation of the caption said, "Looks like Scindia ji's day in BJP is over" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video on Twitter with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Indian National Congress on February 17, 2017. The description of the video read, "AICC Press Briefing by Jyotiraditya Madhavrao Scindia at Congress HQ, February 17, 2017" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: In the next part of investigation, the Desk came across a report published by Amar Ujala on February 18, 2017. "BJP has become an ISI certified party: Congress" read an English translation of the title. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "ATS has exposed the ISI network in Madhya Pradesh. ATS has arrested 11 people with telecommunication equipment equipped with ultra-modern technology on the charges of espionage. They used to provide information related to the army and country, movement, photos etc. to the Pakistan intelligence agency," stated the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google to find reports related to Scindia's association with BJP and came across a report published by NDTV on March 11, 2020. The title of the report read, "Jyotiraditya Scindia Joins BJP, Says Congress No Longer The Party It Was" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Jyotiraditya Scindia officially joined the BJP on March 11, 2020 a day after resigning from the Congress, and was named the party's Rajya Sabha candidate from Madhya Pradesh. Notably, Scindia made the decision to leave the Congress on the 75th birth anniversary of his father, Madhavrao Scindia. His induction into the BJP took place at the party headquarters in the presence of BJP President JP Nadda. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Scindia made the statement in February 2017, and not recently.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Bangladeshi actress, heckled for celebrating Sheikh Hasina's birthday, shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, October 3 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a woman on a rickshaw being heckled by some boys was recently shared on social media with users claiming that she was an American, who was harassed in Bangladesh for not wearing hijab. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The incident has sparked outrage and raised questions about freedom of expression." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across another report by Daily Inqilab, reporting the incident. The title of the report read, "শেখ হাসিনার জন্মদিনের কেক কাটতে টিএসসিতে নায়িকা, নেটিজেনদের ক্ষোভ" An English translation of the title read, "Actress in TSC to cut Sheikh Hasina's birthday cake, anger of netizens" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "My leader's name is Jannetri Sheikh Hasina. I came to TSC to cut my leader's birthday cake. Because she was dishonored in this place on Saturday. I have come to honor her where she has been dishonored. I want to tell those who said that my leader has committed corruption that it is not actually corruption, it is love. Sheikh Hasina has developed the country to keep the people of the country well. She has done many things that cannot be said," the report quoted Mishti as saying. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman in the viral video was Bangladeshi actor and model Mishti Subas, and not an American tourist.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, this video doesn't show Israeli PM Netanyahu rushing for safety amid Iranian missile attack; 2021 footage shared on social media as recent
content: New Delhi, October 3 (Anushka Pandey/ Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): After Iran's recent ballistic missile attack on Israel caused few casualties, a video of Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu was shared on social media with users claiming that it showed him running towards a bunked for shelter. The caption of the post read, "The moment of Netanyahu's escape😆🤣" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other users had shared the same video with similar claims. \ Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar photo shared by the official X handle of Benjamin Netanyahu on December 14, 2021. The caption of the post read, "אני תמיד גאה לרוץ בשבילכם. 🇮🇱💪🏻 צולם לפני חצי שעה בכנסת" A rough translation of the post read: "I am always proud to run for you. 🇮🇱💪🏻 It was taken half an hour ago in the Knesset" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of Netanyahu dating back to 2021 was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of assault on policeman in UP's Ghaziabad falsely shared as recent in name of Karnataka; Details inside
content: New Delhi, October 4 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that it showed a Muslim woman and men assaulting a policeman after the latter issued them a challan in Karnataka. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an unrelated video from Ghaziabad, dating back to August 2018, was shared on social media as recent with a false claim and communal twist. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 2 a video showing a Muslim woman and a group of men started hitting a policeman after they were asked to pay challan in Karnataka. The caption of the post read, "🧐👇🏼Karnataka News.. When the police issued a challan, the Muslims beat them. This is a direct challenge to the law. This video tells what will happen in India in the future, who will rule the country and how everyone's future will be. 🤔😱😱" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. After refusing to provide the token, the bank official declined to proceed with the process, leading to an argument. The official then called the policeman stationed at the branch. In response, Imran summoned his family members, and during the altercation, his sister allegedly began beating the policeman with slippers. Following this, we also came across an X post by the official handle of Police Commissionerate Ghaziabad, shared on August 27, 2018. title: PTI Fact Check: No, WHO has not issued advisory on milk adulteration in India; viral newspaper clipping is fake
content: New Delhi, October 4 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a newspaper clipping claiming that the World Health Organisation (WHO) had issued a warning of 87 per cent of Indians being at the risk of cancer by 2025 due to consumption of adulterated milk. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that no such advisory was issued by the WHO. The viral screenshot was fake and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on September 30 a newspaper clipping claiming that the World Health Organisation (WHO) issued a warning stating that 87 per cent of Indians were at the risk of having cancer by 2025 due to consumption of adulterated milk. The caption of the post read, "मिलावटी दूध ..." An English translation of the caption read, "adulterated milk" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same screenshot with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a report published by Dainik Bhaskar on September 20, 2018. The title of the report read, "चौंकाने वाला खुलासा : रोज सुबह दूध नहीं, जहर पी रहे हैं आप... क्योंकि देश में बिकने वाला 68.7 फीसदी दूध निकला नकली; WHO ने भी जारी की चेतावनी" An English translation of the title read, "Shocking revelation: You are drinking poison every morning instead of milk... because 68.7% of the milk sold in the country is fake; WHO has also issued a warning" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "68.7 percent of milk and milk products sold in the country are adulterated. Animal Welfare Board member Mohan Singh Ahluwalia confirmed this and said that 89 percent of the products have one or two types of adulteration. The shocking thing is that till 31 March 2018, the total production of milk in the country was recorded at 14.68 crore litres per day, while the per capita consumption of milk in the country is 480 grams per day. There is a direct gap of 68 percent in this. Apart from the southern states, more cases of adulteration of milk have been reported in the northern states, " stated the report. Following this, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google to find reports related to WHO's advisory and came across a press note release by the organisation issuing a clarification regarding the viral screenshot. The title of the release read, "Clarification: No WHO Advisory on Milk Contamination" Here is the link to the release and below is a screenshot of the same: We found that the release clearly mentioned that WHO did not issue any advisory to the Government of India on the issue of adulteration of milk/milk products. Meanwhile, we came across a PDF file of Lok Sabha proceedings dating back to November 2019 when the claim had resonated in the Parliament. The then Union Health Minister Dr Harsh Vardhan, replying to a Parliament member's question on reports of WHO warning on adulterated milk, said that the global agency had issued no such advisory to the Government of India. Here is the link to the then-health minister's response to the question in Lok Sabha on November 22, 2019, and below is a screenshot of the same: In response to the question, the Harsh Vardhan also refuted the claim stating that, ""The Nationwide Milk Safety and Quality Survey conducted by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) in 2018 revealed that only 7% (456 out of a total of 6,432 samples) had contaminants (antibiotics, pesticides and aflatoxin M1) that make milk unsafe for consumption. Further, only 12 out of 6,432 samples had adulterants that affected milk safety. These 12 samples include six samples adulterated with hydrogen peroxide, three samples adulterated with detergents, two samples adulterated with urea, and one sample was found to have neutraliser," he stated in the Parliament." Here is the screenshot of the response in the Parliament: We also came across a press release issued by the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying d stating the WHO did not issue any such advisory to the government and the department along with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is taking all possible steps to help supply of safe and good quality milk to the consumers across the country Here is the link to the press release and below is a screenshot of the same: The PTI Fact Check Desk had the same claim when it was shared on social media in February 2023. Here is the link to find the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that no such advisory was issued by the WHO for the Indian Government.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of boy attempting to molest a girl shared on social media as a real incident; Details inside
