title: PTI Fact Check: Video of boat overloaded with passengers capsizing in Congo falsely attributed to Goa; Details inside
content: New Delhi, October 7 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video showing a boat overloaded with passengers capsizing into a waterbody was widely circulated on social media, with a claim that the tragic incident occurred in Goa in India. The post further claimed that 23 bodies were recovered, 40 people rescued, and 64 others remained missing. However, a PTI Fact Check investigation revealed that the video was actually from Lake Kivu in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where an overcrowded boat capsized earlier this month, resulting in the loss of 78 lives. The video was shared online with the false claim linking the incident to India's Goa. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 6 a video of an overcrowded boat capsizing in a water body, and claimed that the incident happened in Goa. The caption of the post read, "Very sad news 😲Goa accident today 23 bdies recovered 40 people rescued ang 64 missing great of the boat owners in overloading over confidence of travellers to very sad 😭🙏" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of Firstpost on October 4. The title of the video read, "78 Dead After Boat Capsizes in DR Congo's Lake Kivu | Firstpost Africa "A tragic boat accident on Lake Kivu in the Democratic Republic of Congo claimed 78 lives, highlighting the persistent dangers faced by those travelling on overcrowded and unsafe vessels in Africa. Just days before, another sinking off Djibouti took dozens more lives. While similar tragedies in the region often go unnoticed, the world recently watched with intense interest as a luxury yacht carrying billionaires sank off Italy. This disparity in attention underscores the haunting reality that lives lost in Africa frequently receive little more than a passing mention," read the description of the video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Guardian on October 4. The title of the report read, "At least 78 dead and dozens missing after ferry disaster in DR Congo" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, on the morning of October 3, a boat carrying approximately 278 passengers, named MV Merdy, capsized just a few hundred meters from the shore of Lake Kivu in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Jean-Jacques Purisi, the governor of South Kivu province, confirmed that the death toll has risen to 78. He further added that rescue operations are still ongoing and at least three more days will be needed to determine the final number of casualties. We also came across an X post shared by the official account Goa Police giving a clarification on the viral video on October 5. The caption of the post read, "Official Clarification: A video circulating on social media claims a boat capsized near Goa's shores. This is false. The incident occurred in Goma, Congo, Africa. Please refrain from sharing unverified news. — Goa Police" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of a boat capsizing incident from Congo, Africa was falsely shared on social media in the name of Goa.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped, edited video shared with false claim that Bangladeshi activist threatened Hindus to leave country; Details inside
content: New Delhi, October 8 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed a Muslim man in Bangladesh issuing a public threat to Hindus, asking them to leave the country within seven days. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that a clipped portion of Bangladeshi activist Saifuddin Mohammad Amdad's speech was shared on social media with a false claim and communal narrative. Amdad was actually threatening the remaining supporters and members of the Awami League in Bangladesh. The video has been shared on social media amid the spike in incidents of violence against Hindu minorities in Bangladesh amid the unrest that ensued in the country following the collapse of the Awami League government led by Sheikh Hasina in August this year. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on September 30 a video of a man addressing the public appearing to threaten individuals with claims that Muslim leaders in Bangladesh were urging Hindus to leave the country. The caption of the read, "Hindus are being given an ultimatum to leave the country within 7 days in #Bangladesh . Saying, "Your fathers are gone, your aunts are scared, you too go away."" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Twitter users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded on Facebook by a user named Md Junaid Abdullah on September 28. The caption of the post read, "জুলাই জুলাই বিপ্লবের শহীদ পরিবার ও যোদ্ধাদের নিয়ে স্মৃতিচারণ ও সাংস্কৃতিক সন্ধ্যায় সাইফুদ্দিন মোহাম্মদ এমদাদ ভাইয়ার ঐতিহাসিক জ্বালাময় বক্তব্য স্থান :শিরিষ তলা, সি আর বি, চট্টগ্রাম। আয়োজনে: @বিকিরণ চট্টগ্রাম মহানগর #সি_আর_বি #জুলাই_বিপ্লব #বাংলাদেশ #চট্টগ্রাম #mdjunaidabdullah Amdad Babu - এমদাদ বাবু Babu Amdad Junaid Abdullah" An English translation of the caption read, "Saifuddin Mohammad Emdad Bhaiya's historical fiery speech at the commemoration and cultural evening about the martyred families and fighters of the July Revolution. Place: Shirish Tala, CRB, Chittagong. Organized by: @Bikiran Chittagong Mahanagar #CR_B #July_Revolution #Bangladesh #Chittagong #mdjunaidabdullah Amdad Babu - Amdad Babu Babu Amdad Junaid Abdullah" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed this was the extended version of the viral video. While watching the video we found that the viral video was clipped at the timestamp of 5:56-minutes. At the timestamp of 4:36-minute Emdad can be heard saying, "I want to know, why are the friends of dictatorship roaming around in the alleys of Chittagong? I want the answer. Where is the administration, where is my state, where is the power given to my army, why are they not using the power?" He further continues, "We must raise again, we must march again, we must raise slogans again, I don't want to resist the protest again, I want to see those murderers in jail, I want to see them in jail, I want them to be tried.. Don't take the words from the front, I want to warn them for their trial if we have to take to the streets again. We will take to the streets again. They are still plotting. Do you know whether they are called Hindus or minorities? Sometimes they call Chittagong Press Club. What do they say of Chittagong Press Club, leaders of leaders, so-called journalists?" "I want you not to make excuses, hide your shame, flee from the country, break the truth, break the truth, your fathers are broken, your grandfathers are broken, Sheikh Hasina is broken. I gave you a week ultimatum then I'll see you as long as I live I'll see you then " stated Emdad while concluding. During the entire speech Saifuddin can be heard talking about supporters of Awami League and former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. The latter spoke about the supporters of Awami League under the disguise of Hindus, minorities and Chittagong Press Club. Following this, we also came across a Facebook post shared by the username Babu Amdad on October 4 giving a clarification regarding the viral video. The caption of the post read, "Many RW Indians handles, and Indian media shared a video claiming that "Hindus are being given an ultimatum to leave the country within 7 days in Bangladesh," which is FALSE. The statement was not against Hindus; it was against the previous regime/government and its associates who attacked on protesters. The man speaking in the video is Saifuddin Mohammad Emdad, aka Emdad Babu, who actively participated in the anti-discrimination movement in July and lost vision in one of his eyes due to a police bullet. He delivered this speech at a program titled "July Remembrance and Cultural Evening," organized by a social organization named 'Bikiron' in Chittagong. Emdad made his statements about the one-week ultimatum while addressing those who attacked students during the movement. If you listen to his entire speech, it's clear that he was targeting the previous Awami League government and its associates, not Hindus. (Listen his full speech here : youtu.be/UkECUoCjlVM?si…) For example, at one point in his speech, he says, "Until now, the henchmen of the autocracy have been roaming the streets of Chittagong. I want to know why they are still walking free. How do they have so much courage? They, armed, have shot at the student community of Chittagong at Bahaddarhat and New Market. Why are they still openly walking around?" This clearly indicates that his speech was against those associated with the Awami League who attacked rotestors. Why did he mention the word 'Hindu'? Bangladeshi can easily understand the context of this clipped part. Initially, after the interim government took office, there was a protest by Anser, a paramilitary auxiliary force, in front of the interim government head office. Instead of helping the government restore law and order during the massive floods in Bangladesh, they came to protest. As a result, people termed them 'Anser League,' saying that Awami League came in the form of Anser. Then, the very next day, there was a protest by rickshaw pullers, and they were also termed the same because they were creating tension. It became a phenomenon—whoever protested was termed the same. Because, they hadn't protested in the last 15 years, but during that time of law collapse, they came to protest. There was also a 'Hindu protest,' and in reference to this phenomenon, Emdad mentioned that the Awami League came in the form of 'Hindus' which may created communal tensions . If you notice, he also talked about journalists and others who appeared in the form of AL; it is a figurative term." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Bangladeshi activist Saifuddin Mohammad Amdad's speech was clipped and shared on social media with false communal narrative.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of a boy hitting his mother for not letting him use smartphone shared as real incident on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, October 8 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video recently went viral on social media with users claiming that it showed a child hitting his mother on head with a bat after she scolded her for using mobile phone. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a scripted video was shared on social media as a real incident with a false claim. The caption of the post read, "छोटे बच्चों को मोबाइल देने का नतीजा देखो कैसे इस बच्चे ने अपनी ही मां की जान ले ली।" An English translation of the caption read, "See the result of giving mobile phones to small children, how this child killed his own mother." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that several other Twitter users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video shared by a Facebook user Yogesh Deoda on October 2. The caption of the post read, "This May Happen In Any Family..! 😲😲 Thank you for watching! Disclaimer: Please be aware that this page features scripted dramas and parodies as well. This short film is not for entertainment & is for educational purposes only! Characters in this video are entertainment and educational purpose. #education Yogesh Deoda" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: While watching the extended video, the Desk noticed at the timestamp of 3:02-minutes a 'Disclaimer' flashes in between the video. Below is screenshot of the same: "This Reel Life Vido footage published only for the purpose of educating the public by making them understand how the real-world situations will be. and picturized to educate public. Characters in this video are entertainment and education purpose" read the disclaimer. Following this, we also came across a Facebook page named 'IdeasFactory', with 557K followers, which shared similar scripted CCTV footages which were presented as real incidents. While scanning the page we came across a video with similar background setup as in the viral video. Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted the owner of the page, who confirmed that the video was made to spread awareness and to educate parents regarding their kids' smartphone addiction. Our investigation revealed that a scripted video was shared on social media as a real incident with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of damaged roof of under-construction parking area at Ratnagiri Railway Station shared on social media with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, October 9 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed a newly installed roof and cladding at Ratnagiri Railway Station damaged due to rains. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the video actually showed damaged roof and cladding at an under-construction parking area outside Ratnagiri Railway Station. The video was shared on social media with a misleading claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 7 a video of a newly installed roof and cladding, claiming that it was from Ratnagiri railway station, which was damaged by heavy rainfall. The caption of the post read: "Gone with the wind.. Ratnagiri Railway Station in Maharashtra.." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Twitter users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here, here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came a report published by CNBC TV 18 on October 7, which carried visuals to those of the viral video. The title of the report read, "WATCH | Ratnagiri railway station roof damaged by storms just months after installation" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "This structure, located at the west entrance of the railway station, was part of an ongoing beautification project managed by the state public works department. Work on the project is still incomplete, raising concerns about its durability," stated the report. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals carried in the news report to those of the viral video: Following this, we also came across an X post shared by the official handle of Konkan Railway giving a clarification on the viral video on October 7. The caption of the post read, "This is a misleading information. The station building is intact and there is No Impact on Train Operations. The video shown is of under construction parking area being developed by PWD , Maharashtra. @RailMinIndia" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Further we came across a PTI report carried by Deccan Herald on October 8, whose headline read: "Viral video: Roof damaged by rains part of parking lot, not Ratnagiri station, say Konkan Railway officials" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "A newly installed roof and cladding damaged due to rains were part of a upcoming parking lot and wasn't the roof of the Ratnagiri railway station in Maharashtra, officials said on Monday," read a section of the report. It further quoted a Konkan Railway spokesperson clarifying that the viral video showed the parking area outside the railway station, which was built by PWD Maharashtra, as part of the beautification project. "The video depicts the parking area outside Ratnagiri station which is in progress and currently undertaken by PWD-Maharashtra and has no impact on train operations. Train operations are fully functional." The KR spokesperson said Maharashtra PWD is developing a garden, concourse and parking area in Ratnagiri station complex 150-200 meters away from the station building. Kindly refrain from spreading misleading information," the spokesperson was quoted as saying. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video showed the parking area of the railway station which is still under construction.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Deepender Hooda breaking into tears shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to Haryana Assembly polls
content: New Delhi, October 10 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda in tears was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he broke down after the Congress party's defeat in the recently concluded Haryana Assembly elections. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to June 2024 when Hooda cried out of joy after emerging victorious from Rohtak in the Lok Sabha polls. The old and unrelated video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Defying exit poll predictions, the BJP emerged victorious in the recently concluded Haryana Assembly polls to form the government for a record third straight term. The Congress remained a distant second with 37 seats. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 8 a video of Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda, claiming that it showed him in tears after Congress' defeat in Haryana Assembly elections. The caption of the post read, "Deepender Hooda got emotional 🥹💔 This man worked Tirelessly for the party. This man Efforts will be unforgettable 👏🏻 Well Fought My Leader @DeependerSHooda Ji ✋🏻🔥 Whatever the circumstances may be always with you Forever and Ever. #HaryanaElectionResults" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Twitter users had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well.Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. The Desk noticed one of the comments on the viral post, which claimed that it was from after the Lok Sabha elections. Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named Karnal Breaking News on June 4. The description of the video read, "भीड़ देखकर दीपेंद्र हुड्डा की आंखों में आए आंसू , 3 लाख से ऊपर वोटों से जीते दीपेंद्र हुड्डा , बोले तैयारी करो Haryana में आ रही Congress की सरकार" An English translation of the caption read, "Seeing the crowd, tears came in Deepender Hooda's eyes, Deepender Hooda won by more than 3 lakh votes, he said, get ready, Congress government is coming to Haryana" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Following this, we also came across a report published by DNA on June 5. "Deepender Singh Hooda Emotional: Deepender Singh Hooda's tears flowed after the victory, workers also became emotional" read an English translation of the title. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, Deepender Singh Hooda became emotional after winning more than 3 lakh votes in the Lok Sabha election. In the Lok Sabha elections 2019, he lost from Rohtak by a narrow margin of 7 thousand votes. After this victory, a huge crowd of workers gathered at his house which made the Congress leader emotional. Subsequently, the Desk concluded an old video dating back to June 2024 was shared on social media as recent with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of former PM Manmohan Singh 'endorsing' online investment app falsely shared on social media
content: New Delhi, Oct 7 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : A video was widely shared on social media showing former prime minister Dr Manmohan Singh endorsing an online investment app, in which he was heard saying that the app ensured "exceptional success in any financial market." However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old video dating back to 2019 was digitally altered using AI-generated superimposed audio and shared on social media with false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on August 21 a video showing former Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh endorsing an online investment app. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk watched the viral video and noticed a lip-sync issue. We then ran the video through the InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded on September 1, 2019. The description of the video read, "Former PM Manmohan Singh said the state of India's economy is 'deeply worrying'. He said, "The state of the economy today is deeply worrying. The last quarter's GDP growth rate of 5% signals that we are in the midst of a prolonged slowdown. India has the potential to grow at a much faster rate but all-round mismanagement by the Modi government has resulted in this slow down." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the viral video was taken from this video, as can be seen from the comparison of visuals of the two shared below: While watching the video, the Desk noticed Singh talking about India's economy, GDP and criticising the Narendra Modi government for its mismanagement, but nowhere made any mention of any online investment app. In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the video through TrueMedia and Resemble AI , both generative AI voices and deepfake audio detection apps. Both the apps suggested the presence of AI-generated audio. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of Dr Manmohan Singh dating back to 2019 was digitally altered and shared on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of boy vandalising idols at Hindu temple in Bangladesh shared on social media as recent with misleading claim
content: New Delhi, Oct 11 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed a Muslim boy vandalising Hindu idols in a temple in Dohar upazila of Dhaka, Bangladesh and also abusing and threatening minority Hindus. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that while the video was from Dohar, the incident happened in June 2023. The video of over a year-old incident was shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. The video was shared on social media amid the reported spike in crimes against minority Hindus in Bangladesh and the attacks on Hindu temples in the unrest-hit country following the sudden collapse of Sheikh Hasina-led government on August 5. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 6 a video of a boy vandalising Hindu idols and making derogatory remarks against Hindus, and claimed that the miscreant was Mohammad Siddiqui who attacked the Jayapara Durga Temple in Dhaka. The caption of the post read, "मोहम्मद सिद्दीकी नाम के एक कट्टरपंथी ने ढाका के दोहर उपजिला में जयपारा दुर्गा मंदिर पर हमला किया। मंदिर पर हमले के बाद मदरसा चरमपंथी ने सभी हिंदुओं को मारने की धमकी भी दी।" An English translation of the caption read, "A radical named Mohammad Siddiqui attacked the Jayapara Durga Temple in Dohar Upazila of Dhaka. After the attack on the temple, the madrasa extremists also threatened to kill all Hindus." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Twitter users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The video was widely shared on Facebook as well. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived posts can be viewed here, here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video shared on Facebook by a user named Ashish Chandragupt on June 23, 2023. The caption of the post read, "A terrorist named MD Siddique attacked the Jaipara Durga temple in Dhaka's Dohar Upazila. The Madrasah extremist threatened to slaughter all Hindus after the temple attack. #SaveBangladeshiHindus #HindusUnderAttack" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by a Bangladesh news portal Naya Alo published on June 22, 2023. The title of the report, when roughly translated to English, read: "Idol vandalism in Doha; Detention 1 " Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, a man named Mohammad Siddiqui forcibly entered the temple by breaking the lock with an iron rod. He then vandalised six Durga idols with the rod and started making derogatory remarks. The locals nabbed the young man and handed him over to the police. Following this, we came across another report by Daily Amar Somoy published on June 23, 2023. "Vandalism of temple idols in Doha, arrest 01" read an English translation of the title. Here is the link to the report. "Salim, a local resident, said Md Siddique, son of Abdul Rahman of Batia village, is a drug addict. He was released from rehab a few days ago. Nitai Karmakar, President of Dakshin Joypara Daspara Ekta Jubo Sangh Durga Mandir said, "Today at around 4 pm, our temple was vandalised by Md. Siddique, son of Abdur Rahman of Batia village. He broke the lock of the temple with a rod and smashed five-six idols and broke their arms, legs and heads. While fleeing from the temple, the people of the area chased him and took him to the police station. Siddique is currently detained at the police station. He also said that the boy has mental problems. But we have no communal problem here"," stated the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded an old video dating back to 2023 from Dohar upazila of Dhaka was shared on social media as recent.

title: PTI Fact Check: Murder of Muslim man by his cousins in Bangladesh shared on social media with false communal narrative; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Oct 12 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a body lying in pool of blood, and claimed that he was a Hindu killed in full public view in Bangladesh's Narsingdi. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was shared with a false communal narrative. The deceased was one Hanif Miya, who was allegedly killed by his maternal cousins Nadeem and Naeem. The video was shared on social media amid the reported spike in crime against minority Hindus in Bangladesh since the collapse of the Sheikh Hasina-led government on August 5. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 2 a video of a body lying in a pool of blood and claimed that he was a Hindu killed in full public view in Narsingdi, Bangladesh. The caption of the post read, "Another Hindu was killed by slitting his throat in front of everyone at the Eidgah gate of Kauria Para in Narsingdi district of Bangladesh. @UNHumanRightsis sleeping. If not we, who will raise the voice for Bangladeshi Hindus ? #SaveBangladeshiHindus" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Twitter users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official handle of Sorejomin Barta on October 7. The description of the video read, "নরসিংদী শহরে পূর্ব শত্রুতার জেরে হানিফ নামে এক যুবককে জবাই করে হত্যা। Narsingdi |Sorejomin Barta" An English translation of the description read, "A young man named Hanif was slaughtered due to previous enmity in Narsingdi town. Narsingdi | Sorejomin Barta" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: While watching the Youtube video, the Desk noticed the background building was similar to the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by RTV Bangladesh on October 2. The title of the report read, "A young man named Hanif was slaughtered due to previous enmity" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the deceased Hanif Mia was murdered in front of Kauria Para Municipal Eidgah in broad daylight, at around 2.30 pm on October 1. The relatives of the deceased alleged that family dispute with Hanif's maternal uncle Habu Mia was the reason of the murder. Following this, the Desk came across another report published by Bangladesh Bulletin on October 9. "In Narsingdi, one person was killed due to previous enmity" read an English translation of the title. Here is the link to the report: "Kaushar Mia, the cousin of the deceased, said that Hanif's younger brother Babu had hacked his uncle Habu Mia to death a month and a half ago. At that time Habu's sons Naeem and Nadeem vowed to kill his father's killer within 40 days while burying his father. We believe Naeem and Nadeem killed Hanif today.Narsingdi detective police officer in-charge SM Kamruzzaman said that the murder was organised due to previous enmity" stated a rough English translation of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the body shown in the video was of Hanif, who was killed by his maternal cousins, and not any Hindu.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old and unrelated videos of Samajwadi Party's Kamal Akhtar and Raja Chaturvedi combined and shared on social media as recent with false claim
content: New Delhi, Oct 13 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Samajwadi Party leader Kamal Akhtar has been widely shared on social media, with users claiming that it first showed him boasting about his influence over the state and later got beaten up by the police for challenging the administration. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that two old and unrelated videos were combined and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 2 a video and claimed that it first Samajwadi Party leader Kamal Akhtar boasting about his influence over the state and the later part showed him being beaten up by the police for his statement. The caption of the post read, "सपा नेता "कमाल अख्तर" यूपी के "प्रशासन" को धमकी दे रहा था यूपी पुलिस ने उनकी "औकात" दिखा दी। फिर से सपा नेता की गुंडागर्दी का वीडियो वायरल, यह हो क्या रहा है? #follower" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first scanned social media platforms and found that several other users had shared the same videos with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk debunked the claim by investigating the two videos separately. Here's what we found: Video 1 The Desk ran the first video of Samajwadi Party leader Kamal Akhtar through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of ABP Ganga on April 9, 2021. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: "Samajwadi Party's national secretary and former cabinet minister Kamal Akhtar has given a controversial statement in Amroha. In a public meeting, he said that no IAS-IPS officer of Uttar Pradesh has the courage to refuse any work of Kamal Akhtar. He gave this statement in a meeting regarding Panchayat elections. BJP has retaliated on his statement," read an English translation of the description of the video. This made it clear that the first footage in the viral video was three years old. Video 2 In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the other video, of the man getting thrashed by the police, through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found a similar video uploaded on YouTube by a user Santosh Chaturvedi on April 25, 2011. The description of the video read, "SAMAJWADI PARTY LEADER RAJA CHATURVEDI 21 FEB 2011 AT VIDHAN SABHA U.P." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by The Indian Express on February 23, 2011. The title of the report, "MLAs were dragged out of the House by BSP goons: SP" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, the Samajwadi Party "alleged that the ruling Bahujan Samaj Party had unleashed goondas for forcible eviction of its MLAs from the state Assembly late Monday night when they were protesting against the abrupt adjournment of the House and passage of a bill paving the way for indirect election of mayors and presidents of various municipalities in the state." We then compared the photos of Kamal Akhtar and Raja Chaturvedi with the man in the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the same: It was clear that the man seen in the second footage was Raja Chaturvedi, and not Kamal Akhtar. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that two old and unrelated videos were clubbed and shared on social media with false claim

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming India became a permanent member of UNSC with veto power are FAKE
content: New Delhi, Oct 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Since PM Modi's recent visit to New York for the 79th UN General Assembly session, multiple social media users have shared posts claiming that India secured a permanent seat on the UN Security Council with veto power. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that India has not yet been granted permanent membership in the UNSC with veto power. The social media posts were shared with a fake claim. Currently, only five countries — China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom, and the United States — are permanent members of the UNSC, and only these permanent members have veto power. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 2 a video of PM Modi claiming India had been granted permanent membership in the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) with veto power. The caption of the post read, "बधाई " भारत को मिला विटो पावर " विश्व के 180 देशो ने किया भारत का समर्थन , चायना का विरोध पडा ठंडा, भारत का दशको पुराना सपना हुवा पूरा। ये है - मोदी के भारत कि सुपर पावर । 🚩 मोदी है तो ही मुमकिन है।" An English translation of the post read, "Congratulations "India got veto power" 180 countries of the world supported India, China's protest cooled down, India's decades old dream came true. This is - Modi's India's super power. 🚩 It is possible only if Modi is there." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Facebook users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. The video was widely shared on Twitter as well. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here and their archived versions can be found here , here and here respectively. We then scanned the official website of the United Nations and found that only five countries are members of its Security Council, and only these countries have veto power. They are China, France, Russian Federation, the United Kingdom and the United States, namely. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: Furthermore, the Security Council consists of 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms by the General Assembly. The Desk also scanned the official website of the Ministry of External Affairs to find reports regarding India's membership in UNSC but did not find anything to substantiate the viral claim. Here is the link to the website In the next part of the investigation, we conducted a customised keyword search on Google to understand the importance of veto power and came across the official website of the United Nation Security Council describing the same. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: The website stated that 'veto power' is a special voting power granted to the five permanent member states by the UN Security Council that if any one of the five permanent members cast a negative vote in the 15-member Security Council, the resolution or decision would not be approved. In September this year, ahead of the 79th UNGA Session, the United States reaffirmed its support for a permanent seat for India and endorsed text-based negotiations to reform the UN Security Council, which has been stalled due to disagreements among a few countries. The US also reaffirmed its support for permanent Security Council seats for India, Japan, and Germany. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that India is not yet a permanent member of the UN Security Council. Social media posts were shared with a fake claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2020 video of Salman Khan released during COVID-19 lockdown falsely shared with claim that he threatened Lawrence Bishnoi
content: New Delhi, Oct 15 (Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of Bollywood actor Salman Khan has been widely shared on social media with users claiming it was a video released by him for jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi. The video started making rounds just days after the killing of NCP leader Baba Siddique, who is considered a close friend of Khan. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a selection portion of an unrelated video, dating back to April 2020, was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Back then, Khan had released the video message for people violating lockdown guidelines during the COVID-19 pandemic. The Mumbai Police suspects Siddique was killed at the behest of Bishnoi after a purported Facebook post surfaced claiming "Jo Salman Khan aur Dawood gang ki help karega apna hisab-kitab laga ke rakhna (whoever helps Salman Khan and the Dawood gang, keep your accounts in order)". Police said they were verifying the social media post in which an alleged member of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang has taken responsibility for the murder of Siddique. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 15 a video of Salman Khan, and claimed that it was a video message released by the actor, issuing a threat to jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi. "ये सन्देश जरूर सुना जाये…" read the caption of the post. An English translation of the same read: "This message should be listened to…" Meanwhile, the text plate running on the video read: "After all this happened, Salman Khan threatened Lawrence Bishnoi." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by another X user. The posts can be seen here , and its archived version can be seen here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by channel named 'World of Clips' on April 19, 2020. The caption of the video read: "Salman Khan gave an emotional message to the people regarding the lockdown." The Desk listened to the 9:36-minute video carefully and found that Salman Khan's message was for those who were violating the lockdown guidelines imposed during COVID-19 pandemic. At 8:35 minutes, Salman Khan says, "Maan liya hai, Bade takatwar ho aap... Bade bahadur ho aap.. Itne bahadur, itne takatwar ho aap ki aap apne pariwar walon ko kandha doge, unki arthi uthaoge... Itna jigar hai aap mein..." (I agree, you are very strong… you are very brave… You are so brave, so strong that you will give shoulder to your family members, you will carry their bier… you have so much courage… (sic.)). Salman further says, "Everything has two aspects, this too has two aspects, one aspect is that we all stay, the other aspect is that no one stays… You decide and everyone should thank the police force, the doctors, the nurses and the people who work in the banks… and be careful that this does not spread further…." Click here to watch the full video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found this video of Salman Khan on the official YouTube channel of Sansad TV. The caption of the video read, "Actor Salman Khan gave a strong message to those violating lockdown guidelines." Click here to watch the full video. Khan had also shared this video on his Instagram account on April 15, 2020. Here is the link to the post. Since the murder of Baba Siddique, in which the name of Lawrence Bishnoi gang has emerged, the security at the residence of Salman Khan's residence has been beefed up. Khan, along with several other Bollywood celebs, had close friendship with Siddique. Bishnoi gang had done recce of Salman Khan's farm house several times. In January 2024, two people also tried to forcibly enter Salman's farm house in Panvel. In April this year, two men on a bike opened fire outside Salman Khan's residence in Mumbai's Bandra. Mumbai Police claimed that the shooters were hired by Lawrence Bishnoi's gang, who had allegedly conspired to kill the actor. Bishnoi had openly threatened Khan in connection with the blackbuck poaching case. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected part of an old and unrelated video of Salman Khan was shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2023 video of Ratan Tata receiving 'Udyog Ratna' award shared on social media as recent with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Oct 15 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of late industrialist and Tata Group Chairman Emeritus Ratan Tata being felicitated by Maharashtra CM Eknath Shinde has been widely shared on social media with users claiming it to be his last public appearance before his demise on October 9. Maharashtra Deputy CMs Devendra Fadnavis and Ajit Pawar were also seen in the video. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old and unrelated video of Tata receiving 'Udyog Ratna' was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim Multiple news outlets shared a video of Maharashtra CM Eknath Shinde felicitating industrialist Ratan Tata, claiming it was the latter's last public appearance before his demise on October 9. The video shared by NDTV Profit , ANI , DNA , Zee News and News 24 can be seen here, here, here, here and here, and their archived versions can be seen here , here , here , here and here respectively. Investigation On further scanning the Google Lens results, the Desk found a similar video uploaded on YouTube by the official channel of The Tribune on August 19, 2023. The description of the video read, "Maharashtra Government on August 19 honoured prestigious 'Udyog Ratna Award' to industrialist Ratan Tata. The award was conferred to Ratan Tata at his residence in presence of CM Eknath Shinde and deputy CMs Devendra Fadnavis and Ajit Pawar. CM Shinde also thanked the industrialist for accepting the award " Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was the same as the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by India Today on August 19, 2023. The title of the report read, "Ratan Tata conferred Maharashtra's first Udyog Ratna award" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Tata Group chairman, Ratan Tatan was honoured with the Udyog Ratna award at his home in Mumbai by Maharashtra Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and Deputy Chief Ministers Ajit Pawar and Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday. The Maharashtra government introduced the prestigious Udyog Ratna award this year and Tata was the first person to receive the award," read a section of the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk scanned the social media handles of late Ratan Tata to verify about his public appearance before the demise and came across an X post in which the late industrialist shared about Tata group's investment for the treatment for cancer care in Assam dated for March 20. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Following this, we came across an Instagram post by cricketing legend Sachin Tendulkar, shared on May 21, 2024, where Ratan Tata can be seen sitting next to him. The caption of the post read, "A Memorable Conversation. Last Sunday was memorable, as I had the opportunity to spend time with Mr. Tata. We shared stories and insights about our mutual love for automobiles, our commitment to giving back to society, passion for wildlife conservation, and affection for our furry friends 🐕. Conversations like these are invaluable and remind us of the joy and impact our passions can bring to our lives. It's a day I will remember with a smile always." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, an Instagram post by NDTV carried a footage of Tata casting his vote in the Lok Sabha polls in Mumbai's Colaba on May 20. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded an old video of Ratan Tata dating back to August 2023 was shared as recent on social media with false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of a boy on bicycle misleadingly shared as young Ratan Tata: Details Inside
content: New Delhi, Oct 16 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A monochrome photo of a boy riding a bicycle was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed late industrialist Ratan Tata in his youth. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a digitally altered AI-generated photo was shared on social media as real with false claim. Former Tata Group chairperson Ratan Tata passed away on October 9 at Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital at the age of 86. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 10 a monochrome photo of a boy riding a bicycle, claiming that it showed late industrialist Ratan Tata in his youth. The caption of the photo read, "A young #RatanTataSir going to work 🥹❤️" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens, and found that several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here, here and here respectively. The same photo was also shared by several news portals such as News 18 , MensXP and India Times . The archived versions of the same can be seen here , here and here , respectively. The Desk then went through the comment section of the viral post and noticed several users claiming that the photo was AI-generated. Below are the screenshots of two such comments: Following this, we took a closer look at the viral photo and noticed several discrepancies such as the people in the background with distorted faces. Below is a screenshot highlighting the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk ran the photo through TrueMedia and Hive Moderation , both generative AI image and video detection tools. Both the apps yielded results suggesting that the photo was created using generative AI, with Hive Moderation stating that the photo was 99.6 per cent AI-generated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of a boy riding a bicycle did not show a young Ratan Tata, but was AI-generated.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of vandalised Goddess Durga idol in Hyderabad shared on social media with false communal narrative; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Oct 14 (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a vandalised idol of Goddess Durga and claimed that it was destroyed by Muslims at the Nampally Exhibition Grounds in Hyderabad. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the vandal, identified as one Krishnaiah Goud, who was "mentally unsound". According to the police, he inadvertently committed the act while looking for food or some money. The video was shared on social media with false communal narrative. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 11 a video of a vandalised idol of Goddess Durga and claimed that it was destroyed by Muslims at the Nampally Exhibition Grounds in Hyderabad. The caption of the post read: "Outrageous! Maa Durga idol vandalized in Hyderabad… and no, not in Pakistani Hyderabad, but Indian Hyderabad. Where's the justice? 😡" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other Twitter users had shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of India Today on October 11. The description of the video read, "In a shocking incident, unidentified miscreants vandalised the idol of Goddess Durga at the Nampally exhibition grounds in Hyderabad. The idol was part of the annual Devi Sharan and Navratri celebrations. The Begum Bazaar Police, along with several Hindu devotees and organisations, have reached the site of the incident. ACT Chandrashekhar is overseeing the situation on the ground. A case has been registered and the Begum Bazaar Police are investigating the matter. #goddessdurga #idolvandalised #navratri #itwebvideos #hyderabad " Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried by The Telegraph on October 12. The title of the report read, "Mentally unsound man arrested for vandalising idol in Telangana" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "A mentally unsound man was arrested for allegedly vandalising the idol of Goddess Durga in a pandal at the exhibition ground here and there was no communal angle in the incident, " stated the police in the report. Meanwhile we also came across another report published by Telangana Today on October 11. "Hyderabad: Police crack case of Durga idol vandalism, nab one" read the title of the report. Here is the link to the report According to the report, Central Zone DCP Akshansh Yadav, in a press release, confirmed that Krishnaiah Goud, who suffers from a mental condition, became angry when he couldn't find food at the pandal and vandalised the idol and damaged the pandal. The Begum Bazaar police have registered cases against Goud for the vandalism and also against the pandal organisers for not following proper procedures in setting up the event. Subsequently, the Desk concluded a "mentally unsound" man Krishnaiah Goud who vandalised the idol while searching for food at the pandal, and no communal narrative was involved in the incident.

author: Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Old, edited video of Salman Khan with AI-generated superimposed audio shared with false claim that he threatened Lawrence Bishnoi
content: New Delhi, Oct 21 (Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video of Salman Khan was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed him threatening jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi, whose gang has been repeatedly giving death threats to the Bollywood actor. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an old and unrelated video of Salman Khan was digitally altered with AI-generated superimposed audio and shared on social media with a false claim. The video was shared following the killing of NCP leader Baba Siddique, whose responsibility has been reportedly claimed by the Bishnoi gang. Since Siddique was considered a close friend of Khan, the latter's security has also been beefed up since then. Claim A Facebook user shared a video in which Salman Khan was heard addressing Lawrence Bishnoi and saying that he cannot can't do anything to him, and that Lawrence was no one whom he should apologise to. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation : The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video was widely shared on YouTube. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) to two such videos: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video where Salman Khan was seen in conversation with his brother Arbaaz Khan. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the shirt wore by Khan and the background were similar to those in the viral video. The Desk noticed that the YouTube video mentioned "Credit: QU Play". Taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised keyword search and came across the original video, which was uploaded on July 21, 2021. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk watched the entire video and found that nowhere did Salman made any mention of Lawrence Bishnoi. In the next phase of investigation, the Desk ran the viral video through True Media, a generative AI image and video detection tool. The tool suggested substantial evidence of the audio being AI-generated. Below are the screenshots of the results from both the software. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video of Khan was digitally altered using superimposed AI-generated audio.

title: PTI Fact Check: Jaipur video of car burning on flyover falsely shared on social media in name of Mumbai; details inside
content: New Delhi, 16 Oct (Anushka Pandey / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video of a car engulfed in flames sloping down a flyover was shared on social media, with users claiming that the incident took place on the Western Express Highway near Malad East in Mumbai. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was from an incident that took place on the Ajmer Road of Jaipur, Rajasthan, which was falsely shared on social media in the name of Mumbai. Claim An Facebook user shared on October 14 a video of a car engulfed in flames sloping down a highway, and claimed that it was from a recent incident that took place on the Western Express Highway near Malad East, Mumbai. The caption of the post read, "Incident on the Western Express Highway near Malad East, Mumbai. A car catches flame and starts rolling down the slope towards curious bystanders who stopped to see a car burn. To satisfy your curiosity, this was most likely caused due to a short circuit and was not an electric vehicle. Shared by team Raw " Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the video was shared across social media platforms with similar claims. Three such posts can be found here , here and here and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video uploaded on Facebook by the official page ET NOW on October 13. The caption of the video read: "A dramatic incident unfolded in Jaipur when an unmanned, blazing car careened down the elevated Ajmer Road towards Sudarshanpura Pulia. The vehicle, engulfed in flames, collided with a parked motorcycle and forced other motorists to frantically evade its path. The fiery journey ended when the car crashed into a road divider. Miraculously, despite heavy traffic, no injuries were reported. Viral videos captured the terrifying moments as motorcyclists abandoned their bikes and fled to safety. The car's owner was identified as Jitendra Jangid, a resident of Mansarovar's Journalist Colony." Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed striking similarities between this and the viral video. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the two: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Times of India on October 13. The title of the report read, "Panic grips Jaipur as burning car sans driver speeds through traffic" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "The car was being driven by Jitendra Jangid, a resident of Divya Darshan Apartment in the Journalist Colony of Mansarovar. According to police, the car was descending the elevated road when Jitendra noticed smoke coming from the car's air conditioning. Concerned, he called his brother, who advised him to check under the bonnet. After stepping out and opening the bonnet, Jitendra discovered that the engine caught fire." stated the report. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk closely looked at the Facebook video and noticed the signboard with 'I love Vegas' written on it. On searching for the same on Google Maps, we were able to locate the Grand Anukampa Hotel on Ajmer Road, Rajasthan. Subsequently, the Desk concluded the video of the car engulfed in fire was from Jaipur, not Mumbai.

author: Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of temple vandalised over financial dispute in Andhra Pradesh shared on social media with false communal narrative
content: New Delhi, Oct 23 (Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed a Hanuman temple recently vandalised in Mulakalacheruvu village of Andhra Pradesh's Chittoor district, insinuating that it was done by members of Muslim community. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video showed Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple in Andhra Pradesh's Annamayya district, that was reportedly desecrated by a Hindu priest of another temple over a financial dispute. The video was shared on social media with a false communal narrative. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 16 a video, claiming that it showed a Hanuman temple vandalised in Andhra Pradesh's Chittoor district, further suggesting that it was done members of Muslim community. "Another day, another Hindu temple vandalised. Heartbreaking This time in AndhraPradesh. Some miscreants vandalised Hanuman Temple in Molakalacheruvu, Chittoor DT, Andhra Pradesh. Izlamist jihadis in Telangana. #ConversionMafia in AP are rampant and destroying peace," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several others social media users with similar claims. Three such posts can be here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an October 16 report by Times of India, which carried a photo same as visuals from the viral video. The headline of the story read: "Unidentified miscreants damage temple walls in Andhra Pradesh". Here is the link to the news report and below is a screenshot of the same: Below is a combination image which makes it clear that the report is related to the same incident as the viral video. The report quoted Annamayya Superintendent of Police B Krishna Rao as telling PTI that the police suspected the "involvement of treasure hunters or rival groups connected to the temple". The report also carried an October 16 X post by PTI, which was an extended version of the video footage posted on social media. "VIDEO | Andhra Pradesh: Unidentified miscreants allegedly vandalised 'Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy Temple' in #Chittoor district," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: A follow-up report by Telangana Today on October 18, quoted police stating that Harinath Yadav, a priest from another temple in the same district, along with five others, vandalised the Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple. "District Superintendent of Police V. Vidyasagar Naidu said Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple's priest had differences with Harinath Yadav, priest of Kanugunda Swamy temple over sharing of the temple income. Harinath Yadav wanted to take Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple under his control to get its income but priest Vidyasagar did not agree," read a section of the report. "Angry over this, Harinath planned to blow up the temple thinking that this would force the priest to run away from the place. As per his plan, the accused spread a rumour that there is a treasure trove under Abhaya Anjaneya Swamy temple. A week ago, he procured some explosives from two persons in Sri Sathya Sai district but failed in the attempt to blow up the temple. Accused Harinath later took the help of five others to damage the temple structure with shovels, hammers, chisels and other objects," it added. During the investigation, the Desk also found a Facebook post shared by Annamayya District Police on October 17, in which it provided details of the case. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that there was no communal angle in the case and the video was shared with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2018 video of a woman publicly assaulted in UP shared as recent on social media with false communal claim
content: New Delhi, Oct 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : A video of a man brutally assaulting a saree-clad woman tied to a tree with a large crowd surrounding them was recently shared on social media with users claiming that the man was a Muslim, who was punishing his wife under Sharia or Islamic religious laws. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to March 2018 and showed a Hindu woman being publicly flogged by her husband following a kangaroo court order in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr, which found her guilty of adultery. The video was shared on social media as recent with a false communal narrative. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on October 21 a video,, claiming that it showed a Muslim man mercilessly beating his wife to punish her under Sharia or Islamic religious laws. "Under Sharia law, if a woman is raped, it's considered sex outside of marriage, and she is to be punished. In most Sharia countries, women are stoned to death if they report they were raped. So the one in the video got 'lucky' for only being flogged," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the video was shared by several other social media users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across an X post shared on March 22, 2018, which carried a photo same as the visuals of the viral video. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: "Here's what is happening in the most progressive of all Indian states, #UttarPradesh. A village kangaroo court orders tying a woman to a tree and flogging her for allegedly eloping with a neighbour. Village Launga, district Bulandshahr," he wrote in the caption of the post. In a thread post, the user shared the video of the incident, same as the one share on social media recently. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across multiple media reports dating back to March 2018, which stated that the incident happened in the Launga village of Bulandshahr district. A report by India Today, published on March 23, 2018, was titled 'Caught on camera: Husband flogs wife in public on panchayat's orders to 'teach her a lesson' for eloping'. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The India Today quoted mentioned a report by Hindustan Times , which quoted Bulandshahr SP Praveen Ranjan Singh saying that "former pradhan Shersingh, his son Shravan, and woman's husband, Shaudan Singh, have been arrested and raids are underway to arrest other accused." Police said that the panchayat came up with the punishment of flogging because they wanted to "teach a lesson to the woman", the report added. Another report by News18 Hindi, also published on March 23, 2018, stated: "A video of a woman being beaten up in Bulandshahr went viral. On Friday, the police arrested three accused including the husband and village head Sher Singh in the case of tying a married woman to a tree in front of the panchayat and brutally beating her on suspicion of illicit relations in village Launga of Thana Syana area. At present, the police are conducting raids in search of the remaining accused." Here is the link to the report: In the next part of investigation, the Desk managed to access the FIR copy of the case, from which it became clear that the victim woman was also a Hindu. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that video dated back to 2018 and was shared on social media with a false communal narrative.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of structures razed in anti-encroachment drive falsely linked to administrative action after Bahraich violence
content: New Delhi, Oct 25 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : Following the death of a person in the violence that broke out in Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich on October 13, a video has been widely shared on social media with users claiming that it showed demolished houses of the violence accused, bulldozed by the Yogi Adityanath-led state government. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that while the video was from Bahraich, it predated the incident of violence in the city and was shared on social media with a false claim and communal twist. The video showed the structures demolished by the authorities in an anti-encroachment drive as per court orders. Violence broke out in Bahraich's Maharajganj area on October 13 allegedly over loud music being played outside a place of worship during a Durga Puja immersion procession. Ram Gopal Mishra, 22, part of the passing group, died of a gunshot wound in the ensuing violence. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 20 a video of demolished structures in an area and claimed that they were bulldozed houses of the Bahraich violence accused. "Bahraich Turns Into Ground Zero for Justice—Yogi Unleashes His Wrath! CM Yogi Adityanath is bringing the heat in Bahraich! No more safe havens for criminals and rioters—he's turning the district into a no-nonsense zone. With bulldozer justice in full effect, Yogi Ji is delivering swift action, proving that law and order come first. The message is loud and clear—there's no room for chaos in Uttar Pradesh under Yogi's leadership!" read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes from it. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared by several users across social media platforms with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across an Instagram post shared on September 26, which carried the same video. "Wazirganj 😭😭 | Apna Wazirganj | Bahraich #wazirganj #bahraich #apnawazirgang," read the caption of the post. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a PTI report carried by Deccan Herald on September 26, 2024. "23 structures razed in Bahraich at HC order; illegal constructions bulldozed in Kannauj, Fatehpur," read the headline of the news report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: A video report by TV9 showed visuals from the anti-encroachment drive carried out in Bahraich on September 25 following a court order, amid heavy police presence. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: During its investigation, the Desk also came across an X post by Bahraich Police, in which it refuted the claims made in the viral social media posts. "प्रदर्शित विज़ुअल एक कोर्ट द्वारा आदेशित एंटी एंक्रोचमेंट ड्राइव के हैं जो कि जनपद बहराइच के फखरपुर क्षेत्र में दिनांक 25.09.24 को चली थी न कि विगत दिनों घटित महराजगंज की घटना का है । भ्रामक पोस्ट से सौहार्द और कानून व्यवस्था बिगाड़ने के विरुद्ध विधिक कार्यवाही अमल में लाई जाएगी।" read the post. An English translation of the post read: "The visuals shown are of a court-ordered anti-encroachment drive that was carried out in the Fakharpur area of Bahraich district on 25.09.24 and not of the incident that happened in Maharajganj a few days ago. Legal action will be taken against those who disturb the harmony and law and order by making misleading posts." Here is the link to the October 19 X post by Bahraich Police and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media predated the incident of violence in Bahraich.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old, unrelated video falsely shared in name of Cyclone Dana impact in Odisha; details inside
content: New Delhi, Oct 27 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : A widely was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed the impact of the landfall of Cyclone Dana in Odisha's coastal region. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the footage showed Cyclone Tauktae's effect in Kanyakumari way back in May 2021. The over three-year-old video was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to Cyclone Dana. Severe cyclonic storm Dana struck the eastern coast in the early hours of October 25, triggering torrential rain and high-speed winds that uprooted trees and electric poles, and caused significant damage to infrastructure and crops in Odisha and West Bengal. While no casualty was reported in Odisha, West Bengal has so far reported four deaths linked to the storm. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 25 a video claiming that it showed the impact of the landfall of Cyclone Dana. "Landfall Of Cyclone 'Dana' At Bhitorkonika,Odisha," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running of the keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared across social media platforms with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video, uploaded on May 18, 2021, which was the same as the viral footage. The caption of the video read: "Cyclone Tauktae effect." Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The same video was uploaded by another YouTube channel on May 15, 2021 and claimed to show the impact of Cyclone Tauktae in Kanyakumari. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Reliance Jio, in its X post, also shared a video in June 2021, which included visuals seen in the viral footage. Here is the link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same: While the Desk could not further establish the exact time and location of the video, it was clear that the footage was dates back to at least May 2021, and is not related to the recent Cyclone Dana.

author: Deepak Chaudhary/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 video of IUML flags in rally shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's nomination filing in Wayanad
content: New Delhi, Oct 28 (Deepak Chaudhary/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a crowd chanting slogans and waving green flags was recently shared on social media, with users claiming it was from a rally organised in support of Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra during her nomination filing in Wayanad. The users further claimed that the green flags seen in the video were Pakistan's national flag. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to at least June 2019, and was reportedly from a rally organised by Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) workers and supporters. Moreover, the green flags seen in the video were not Pakistani, but of IUML. The video was shared on social media as recent, falsely linking it to Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's nomination filing. The by-election for Wayanad Lok Sabha seat became necessary after Rahul Gandhi, who won the Lok Sabha polls from there and Rae Bareli constituency, decided to vacate Wayanad. Voting in Wayanad will be held on November 13. Claim: A Facebook user shared on October 24 a video claiming that it showed visuals from a rally in support of Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, ahead of her filing nomination from Wayanad. The caption of the post read, "बेगम प्रियंका खातून ने Sorry प्रियंका वाड्रा ने लाहौर से पर्चा भरा, Sorry वायनाड से पर्चा भरा साला, प्रियंका वाड्रा के समर्थन में रैली की वीडियो देखकर यकीन ही न हुआ कि पर्चा भारत के वायनाड से भरा गया है.. न तिरंगा न कॉंग्रेसी झंडा सिर्फ और सिर्फ इस्लामिक भीड़ के हाथ हरा झंडा✍️" A rough English translation of the caption read: "Begum Priyanka Khatoon Sorry Priyanka Vadra Filed the nomination from Lahore, sorry filed the nomination from Wayanad. After watching the video of the rally in support of Priyanka Vadra, I could not believe that the nomination was filed from Wayanad, India.
