Neither the tricolour nor the Congress flag Green flag only and only in the hands of Islamic mob✍️" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared recently by several other social media users with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here respectively. Meanwhile, several social media posts from April 2024 carried the same video with a different claim linking it to Rahul Gandhi's filing of nomination for the Lok Sabha elections held earlier this year. It may be worth mentioning here that the former Congress President contested the Lok Sabha polls from two seats - Wayanad and Amethi - and emerged victorious in both. Later, he decided to retain the Amethi seat, prompting bypolls on the Wayanad seat. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived version can be viewed here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across the same video but shared on YouTube, dating back to June 10, 2019. The video mentioned the Kerala-based political party IUML in the caption. Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk compared the official flag of IUML with the ones seen in the video and found that they were the same. Below is a combination image comparing the flag seen in the video with the flag of IUML and the national flag of Pakistan: In the next part of investigation, the Desk noticed that signboards containing the names of some shops were visible in the video. One such sign read 'Aramana Silks'. Taking a cue from this, the Desk geo-located the video to MG Road in Kasaragod, Kerala with the help of Google Maps. Below is a combination image comparing the two visuals: Following this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across several news articles stating that the IUML was part of an alliance with Congress during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. Congress had fielded Rajmohan Unnithan from the Kasaragod constituency, who ended up winning the seat. Here is the link and the archive link to a news report published by The Indian Express and below is a screenshot of the same: Here is the link and the archive link to an article published by the Hindu and below is a screenshot of the same: On carefully listening to the slogans raised in the video, one can also notice his name being mentioned near 0:22 timestamp, which further corroborates that this rally was organised in his support in Kasaragod. The Desk, however, could not establish the exact date and time of the video, but ascertained that it at least dated back to 2019. Subsequently, it was concluded the video shared on social media was old and unrelated. Earlier too, false claims have been made on social media regarding the IUML and its flag. PTI Fact Check debunked one such claim in April this year in the run-up to Lok Sabha polls. ( Click here to read the fact-check report ).

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Pakistan-based social media posts falsely claimed Home Minister Amit Shah's name put on Interpol's 'wanted list'; details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 2 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple Pakistan-based social media users shared a graphic carrying the photo of Amit Shah, and claimed that the Interpol had added the Union Home Minister's name to its 'wanted list' for allegedly approving attacks on 'Canadian Sikh nationals'. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that no such notice was issued by the Interpol. A fake graphic card was shared on social media with a false claim. The claim went viral amid India's strained diplomatic ties with Canada, and the latter's Deputy Foreign Affairs Minister David Morrison recently alleging that Shah ordered a campaign of violence, intimidation and intelligence-gathering targeting Sikh separatists inside Canada. New Delhi has vehemently rejected the references made by Morrison about Shah and warned that such "absurd and baseless" allegations will have serious consequences for bilateral ties. Claim A Pakistan-based Facebook page named 'Khaber.tv' shared on November 1 a graphic card and claimed that the Interpol had issued a wanted notice against Union Home Minister Amit Shah for allegedly approving a series of attacks on Sikh separatists on Canadian soil. "Credible sources have informed that Indian Home Minister Amit Shah has recently been added to Interpol's wanted list. Shah is in hot waters after Canada's Deputy Foreign Minister accused him of authorizing killing operations against Canadian Sikh nationals," read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the viral graphic card through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other users with the same claim. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here , here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any credible report corroborating the viral claim. Had any such development taken place, it would have grabbed the headlines in both national and global media. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk searched Interpol's official website using the keyword 'Amit Shah' across pages but could not find any information about the global agency issuing any such notice. Here is the link to the official website of Interpol and below is a screenshot of the same: During its investigation, the Desk came across a report by Hindustan Times, published on November 2, whose headline read: "India dismisses Canada's allegation against home minister Amit Shah as 'absurd'." Here is the link to the report: We also reached out to the BJP and the concerned ministry for their comments on the viral claim. The story shall be updated as and when a response is received. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral graphic card on the alleged Interpol notice is fake.

author: Deepak Chaudhary/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Narayana Murthy, Sudha Murty did not launch any investment programme; digitally altered video shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, Nov 3 (Deepak Chaudhary / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): The PTI Fact Check WhatsApp number recently received a video of Infosys co-founder Narayana Murthy and Rajya Sabha MP Sudha Murty addressing an audience. In the video, they can be heard 'promoting a new automated investment software they have launched'. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that a selected portion of their dialogue from a media event held earlier this year was digitally altered using superimposed audio with a false claim. Claim A user shared a video with the PTI Fact Check WhatsApp number that showed Infosys co-founder Narayana Murthy and Rajya Sabha MP Sudha Murty addressing an audience. Both can be heard promoting a new automated investment software they have launched. They claim that if a user deposits an initial amount of ₹22,000 with them, they will be able to earn ₹18,00,500 by the end of the month. Here is the Google Drive link to the video, and below are screenshots of the same: Investigation To start the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded by the official channel of India Today Conclave on March 15, 2024. The title of the video read, "India Today Conclave 2024: Sudha & Narayana Murthy Exclusive |Fascinating Journey of Infosys Couple" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that this was an extended version of the video shared on the PTI Fact Check WhatsApp number, as can be seen from the comparison of visuals of the two shared below: While listening to the extended video, the Desk found that Narayana Murthy and Sudha Murty spoke about various things, ranging from their married life to setting up Infosys, but nowhere did they mention the alleged 'automated investment software'. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through TrueMedia and Resemble AI , both generative AI voices and deepfake detection apps. Both the apps suggested the presence of AI-generated media. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Narayana Murthy and Sudha Murty's dialogue from a media event in March 2024 was digitally altered using superimposed audio and shared with a false claim. Earlier, too, false claims were made on social media regarding the launch of new investment apps and schemes that promise unrealistic returns using the faces and voices of Narayana Murthy and Sudha Murty. PTI Fact Check debunked one such claim in September this year. ( Click here to read the fact-check report. )

author: Deepak Chaudhary/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming to show Donald Trump's first X post after getting re-elected as US President is fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 6 (Deepak Chaudhary / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a huge crowd celebrating in front of a big screen inside a hall was recently shared on social media, with the user claiming it was in reaction to Donald Trump's first post on X (earlier Twitter) after getting re-elected as the US President. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation revealed that an old video from Bristol, UK, was digitally altered and shared with the false claim on social media. ​ Donald Trump on November 6, won the US presidency for a second term in one of the greatest political comebacks in American history, cruising past his Democratic rival Kamala Harris. Claim An X user shared on November 6 a video claiming that it showed visuals of a crowd celebrating Donald Trump's first X post after getting re-elected as the US President. The caption of the post read, "First tweet of Shri Donald Trump after re-elected as President 😂😂😂" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation To start the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded on June 17, 2016. The title of the video read, "Fans at Ashton Gate Stadium, Bristol, celebrate England winner against Wales at Euro 2016". Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the YouTube video was similar to the one shared on social media recently, as can be seen from the comparison of visuals of the two shared below: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk went through the official X account of Donald Trump to verify if he had posted anything similar to the claim. The Desk found that till the time of this story being filed, no such post had been made by his X account. Subsequently, it was concluded that the video shared on social media was digitally altered and fake.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited photo of Delhi autorickshaws displaying anti-Kejriwal quote shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Nov 5 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a photo of two autorickshaws with a Hindi text on their back cover, which translated to 'we will oust Arvind Kejriwal'. The photo was shared in the context of the Assembly polls, scheduled to be held in Delhi early next year. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an edited photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on October 30 a photo of two autorickshaws with a Hindi text on their back cover, which translated to 'we will oust Arvind Kejriwal'. "दिल्लीवालों ने ठाना है, केजरीवाल को भगाना है !" read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other social media users with similar claim. One such post and archived version can be seen here. We found that the same photo was also shared by Delhi BJP. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, we found that the original photo was uploaded on Wikimedia Commons by Subhashish Panigrahi on April 9, 2013. The text in the original photo did not read as what seen in the viral image. Instead, it read: "Ayush Gupta Akansha, ghar kab aaoge." Here is the link to the original photo and below is a combination image, comparing it with the viral one, which makes it clear that the photo has been edited. Notably, the same photo was edited and used with a different text by Fevicol for an advertisement in February 2018. Here is the link to the Facebook post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated photo was digitally altered and shared on social media as recent.

author: Deepak Chaudhary/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No 'Modi Modi' chants were made during Donald Trump's victory speech; claim made in social media posts is false
content: New Delhi, Nov 7 (Deepak Chaudhary / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Donald Trump's address following his victory in the US presidential elections has gone viral on social media with several users claiming that the crowd present during Trump's speech was chanting 'Modi Modi' in support of the Indian Prime Minister. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the crowd chanted 'Bobby Bobby' slogan, and not 'Modi Modi', during Trump's victory speech. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Trump referred to Robert F. Kennedy Junior as 'Bobby' in his speech. Kennedy, the son of former US Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy, was one of the presidential candidates who later dropped out of the race and endorsed Trump. On November 6, Trump won the polls in one of the greatest political comebacks in American history, cruising past his Democratic rival Kamala Harris. Claim: An X (formerly Twitter) account named 'Kreately Media' shared on November 6 a video claiming that chants of "Modi Modi" were raised during Donald Trump's victory speech following his win in the US presidential elections. The caption of the post read, "Trump के देश में Modi का जलवा" A rough English translation of the caption read: "Modi's influence in Trump's country" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The video was also shared by Rajya Sabha MP and West Bengal BJP's Chief Spokesperson Samik Bhattacharya, among others. However, he later deleted the post. Here is the archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation: The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video uploaded on November 6, 2024, by the channel 'FOX 9 Minneapolis-St. Paul'. The title of the video read, "Trump says Robert Kennedy Jr. will 'make America healthy again'" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: At around the 00:12 seconds mark, Trump mentions Robert Kennedy Jr., saying, "He is going to help make America healthy again…", to which the crowd responds by chanting "Bobby Bobby." Trump smiles and says, "He is a great guy and he really means it, he wants to do some things and we are going to let him do it." Throughout the video, Trump refers to Robert Kennedy Jr. as 'Bobby.' In the next part of the investigation, the Desk found the complete transcript of Trump's victory speech on 'The Nightly' website, where it was mentioned that the crowd chanted "Bobby Bobby" during that part of the speech. Here is the link to the transcription and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Trump's victory speech, where chants of "Bobby Bobby" were made by the crowd, was shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2016 video of Donald Trump calling himself 'big fan of Hindus and India' misleadingly shared as recent after he elected US President again
content: New Delhi, Nov 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : Following the victory of Donald Trump in the recently concluded US presidential polls, a video of him has been widely shared on social media in which he says that he is a "big fan of Hindu and a big fan of India". The users shared the video, claiming it was a recent clip from after Trump's victory. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a 2016 video was being shared on social media as recent with a misleading claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 6 a video of Donald Trump praising Hindus and India and claimed that it was a recent clip from after his victory in the US presidential polls. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by another Facebook user. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a video report by Republic World, uploaded on November 7, whose headline read: "'Big Fan Of Hindu & India' Will Counter Radical Islamism; Trump's Old Video Goes Viral | Donald Trump". The Desk watched the video and found the same viral clip from 00:59-minute timestamp. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The description of the video read: "An old video of Donald Trump from 2016 resurfacing after his 2016 presidential victory has sparked renewed attention on social media. The video, which reflects Trump's rhetoric during the election campaign, has gained traction as people revisit his words in the context of his time in office." Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Indian Express, published on October 16, 2016. The headline of the report read: "Donald Trump's quotes on India: Narendra Modi is a great man, I am a fan of Hindus". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, we found the full video of Trump's speech at the fundraiser organised for him – the then Republican presidential nominee – by Republican Hindu Coalition in Edison, New Jersey. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded the viral remarks of Trump on Hindus and India were made in 2016.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fabricated social media post shared on social media to falsely claim Joe Biden mocked Kamala Harris after her poll defeat
content: New Delhi, Nov 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : Following Donald Trump's historic return as the President of the United States, multiple social media users shared a screenshot of a purported X post by former President Joe Biden in which he took a dig at the presidential candidate Kamala Harris after she suffered defeat. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that a screenshot of a fabricated post was shared on social media with a false claim. On November 6, Trump won the US presidential election for a second term, handing a shock defeat to Harris, in one of the most remarkable comebacks in American electoral history after he was evicted from power four years back. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 7 a screenshot of a purported X post by Joe Biden, taking a dig at US presidential candidate Kamala Harris after she suffered defeat at the hands of Trump. "That's what you get for kicking me out of the race, you ****** *****," read the supposed X post. The caption of the Facebook post read: "Joe Biden's first real tweet in the last 4 years that wasn't tweeted by one of his assistants." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same screenshot was shared by several other social media users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk went through the official X handle of Biden but did not find any such post. Biden shared three posts after the announcement of US presidential poll results, in which he praised Harris for her campaign. Below are the screenshots of the three posts: The Desk also checked the account's activity on Social Blade, a social media analytics website, which confirmed that no X post was deleted recently. Below is a screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, the Desk noticed several discrepancies in the viral screenshots, which are highlighted in the image below. The date and time format is different from the usuals X posts. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the screenshot shared on social media was of a fabricated X post.

title: PTI Fact Check: X post from Donald Trump's parody account calling 'Rahul Gandhi a Soros agent' reshared as real by social media users
content: New Delhi, Nov 8 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : Several social media users shared a screenshot of an alleged response from Donald Trump to a post by Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on X, in which Gandhi congratulated Trump on winning the U.S. presidential election. In the supposed response, Trump referred to Gandhi as an "Indian Soros agent." However, an investigation by the PTI Fact Check Desk revealed that the response actually came from a parody account impersonating Trump. The social media posts were therefore shared with a false claim. On November 7, Gandhi, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, wrote to US President-elect Trump, congratulating him on his victory and wishing him success on his second term. In the letter, Gandhi expressed confidence that the two nations would further deepen cooperation in areas of mutual interest. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 9 a screenshot of a purported response by Donald Trump on Rahul Gandhi's X post congratulating the former on his US presidential poll victory. "Donald Trump responded to Rahul Gandhi in a twitter..." read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral screenshot through Google Lens and found that it was shared another Facebook user with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We then went through the official X account of Trump, which goes by the name '@realDonaldTrump', but could not find any such any such post or response made to Rahul Gandhi. In the next part of investigation, the Desk noticed that the response was made from an account with the username '@thedonaldtrumph', and the name mentioned as 'Donald J. Trump Parody'. Below is a screenshot of the bio of the account, from which the response was shared. The bio mentioned that it was a fan account managed by one Ashwini Shrivastava. We scanned the user's account and found that he had shared a post on November 6, which read: "Hello, everyone! How are my replies from @thedonaldtrumph to Narendra Modi,Rahul Gandhi, @JustinTrudeau & Khalistanis?Some people are claiming this account @thedonaldtrumph is run by the BJP IT Cell, but I'm definitely not part of the IT Cell. Yet, I think I've done more damage to RaGa and Trudeau than any IT Cell could." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We also found the X post by Rahul Gandhi, in which he congratulated Trump on his election victory. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the response to Rahul Gandhi, going viral in the name of Donald Trump, was actually shared from a parody account.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of green flag at Ajit Pawar and Nawab Malik's rally misrepresented as Pakistani flag; details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 11 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A photo circulating on social media shows a green flag with a white crescent and star, accompanied by claims that it represents the Pakistani flag displayed at a rally held by NCP leaders Ajit Pawar and Nawab Malik in Mumbai. The image was shared by many social media users amid heightened political activity in Maharashtra as campaigns ramp up for the upcoming November 20 Assembly elections. However, PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation reveals that the claim is false. The flag in question is similar to an Islamic religious symbol, not a Pakistani flag. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 9 a photo of a green flag with a white crescent and star, claiming that it was a Pakistani flag seen at the rally of NCP chief Ajit Pawar and party leader Nawab Malik in Mumbai. "फडनीस देवेंद्रजी, तुमच्या मित्रपक्षाच्या रॅलीत हा कुठला झेंडा आहे?" read the caption of the post, which roughly translates to, "Fadnavis Devendraji, which flag is this at your allies' rally?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other users with the same claim. Three such posts can be seen here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. On further scanning the results, the Desk came across a Facebook post by Nawab Malik shared on November 8, which carried the same photo. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: "Maharashtra's strong leadership is National President of Rashtravadi Congress Party and Maharashtra's beloved Deputy Chief Minister. No. @a Ajit Pawar Dada's Mankhurd Shivaji Nagar," read the caption of the post, in which Deputy CM Ajit Pawar can be seen campaigning for Malik and his daughter, standing on either side of him. On closely watching the viral image, the Desk noticed that the green flag in question had a white crescent and a star surrounded by several small smaller stars. On the other hand, the Pakistani flag showed a green field with a white vertical stripe on the left side, and a single crescent and star in the remaining green portion. Below is a combination image, comparing the viral flag photo with that of Pakistan, as available on photo stock website Alamy. However, the flag in the viral photo bore striking similarities to the Islamic religious flag. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: We also came across a report on the rally from which the photo went viral. "Maharashtra Assembly Elections 2024 | Ajit Pawar takes out road show in support of Nawab Malik, Sana Malik," read the headline of the Deccan Herald report, published on November 7. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image did not show Pakistani national flag, but an Islamic religious flag at the poll rally of Ajit Pawar and Nawab Malik.

author: Deepak Chaudhary/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Nitin Gadkari's speech shared to falsely claim he made objectionable remarks on PM Modi; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 13 (Deepak Chaudhary/Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of Union Minister and BJP leader Nitin Gadkari speaking at a rally was recently shared on social media, with users claiming he said "he would kick PM Modi". The PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. In the video, Gadkari said that he would kick any politician who talks about caste (to get votes), but did not name any particular individual or party. A selected portion of the speech was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on November 8 a video of Union Minister Nitin Gadkari speaking at a rally, claiming that he made objectionable remarks against PM Modi. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation: The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other social media users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across the full video of the speech uploaded on Nitin Gadkari's official YouTube channel. It was a YouTube Live, which was streamed on his channel on November 7, 2024. The title of the video read, "📍Nagpur | Live from Inauguration of BJP🪷 Election Office of North Nagpur Assembly Constituency" Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: On watching the video carefully, the Desk found that the viral clip shared on social media was taken from 17:13 timestamp onwards. The Desk then listened to his full speech to verify the claim shared in the viral social media posts, but did not find him making any mention of PM Modi or any other individual, when he said that he would kick anyone who talks about caste. Here is a transcript of the part of the speech where he talked about caste: "मैं तो बहुत साफ़ हूँ, डरता नहीं हूँ किसी से. यह नेता लोग जो होते हैं जो काम पर चुन कर नहीं आते वो जात की बात करते हैं आकर.... मैं फलाना जाती च। ... हमारे पास कोई जाती नहीं है, मैं कहता हूँ जो करे जात की बात, उसको कसके मारूंगा लात. मैं नागपुर का हूँ और नागपुर की जनता मेरा परिवार है. जो मुझे वोट देगा उसका भी काम करूँगा, नहीं देगा उसका भी करूँगा। मुझे वोट नहीं मिलने से फरक नहीं पड़ता।" A rough English translation of the transcript reads, "I am very clean, I am not afraid of anyone. These politicians who are not elected for their work, come and talk about caste… I am from such and such caste… We do not have any caste, I say whoever talks about caste, I will kick him hard. I am from Nagpur and the people of Nagpur are my family. I will work for those who vote for me, and I will also work for those who do not vote for me. It does not matter to me if I do not get votes." He then proceeded to talk about the health facilities he and his party members have provided to the people. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Gadkari's speech was shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Deepak Chaudhary/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, Sunil Mittal, Mukesh Ambani did not launch any investment programme; digitally altered video shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, Nov 18 (Deepak Chaudhary / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Fake advertisements luring people with promises of abnormally high returns on stock market investments are being widely shared across social media platforms. The PTI Fact Check Desk received one such video on WhatsApp, with a request to verify its authenticity. The video showed Bharti Enterprises founder Sunil Mittal and Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani promoting a 'new automated investment platform that they have launched'. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a selected portion of their speeches at a tech conference in 2022 were digitally altered using superimposed AI-generated audio, and shared on social media with a false claim. Claim PTI Fact Check received a video on its WhatsApp number +91-8130503759 that showed Bharti Enterprises founder Sunil Mittal and Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani promoting a 'new automated investment software', allegedly launched by them. They were heard saying if a user deposits an initial amount of Rs 22,000, they will be able to earn Rs 19,00,000 by the end of the month. Here is the Google Drive link to the video, and below are screenshots of the same: Investigation: To start the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. After running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube live video streamed by the official channel of PM Narendra Modi on October 1, 2022. The title of the video read, "PM Modi inaugurates 6th India Mobile Congress at Pragati Maidan, New Delhi" Here is the link to the video, and below is a screenshot of the same: The video was a live stream of the 6th edition of India Mobile Congress 2022, a tech conference, where both Mittal and Ambani addressed the audience. It was an extended version of the video shared on the PTI Fact Check WhatsApp number, as can be seen from the comparison of visuals of the two shared below: While listening to the original video, the Desk found that Sunil Mittal and Mukesh Ambani spoke about the launch of 5G in India but nowhere did they mention the alleged 'automated investment platform'. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk ran the video through TrueMedia , a generative AI voice and deepfake detection app. The app suggested the presence of AI-generated media. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a selected portion of Sunil Mittal and Mukesh Ambani's speeches from a tech conference in October 2022 was digitally altered using superimposed AI-generated audio and shared with a false claim.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video of Rajat Sharma reporting news of Dr Bimal Chhajer's death is fake and created using AI; details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video of a purported news report by senior journalist and TV news anchor Rajat Sharma on the alleged death of Dr Bimal Chhajer, a cardiologist who spoke against pharmaceutical companies, in a car explosion. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was created by combining old and unrelated clips and overlaying it with AI-generated audio. The doctored video was shared on social media with a fake claim. The Desk categorically investigated the three clips used in the video. Below is a detailed report of what we found in our investigation: Claim A Facebook user shared a video of a purported news report by senior journalist and TV news anchor Rajat Sharma, in which he talked about the death of Dr Bimal Chhajer, a cardiologist, in a car explosion. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running few of those keyframes through Google Lens, we found that the same video was shared across social media platforms with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk then closely watched the video and noticed lip-sync issue across the 1-minute clip, which suggested that the original audio of the clips used in the video may have been altered. Taking a cue from this, the Desk decided to verify the authenticity of all the three clips separately. Here's what we found: Video 1 The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes showing Rajat Sharma through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube livestream posted on the official channel of IndiaTV on October 2. The video showed Sharma in the same attire in the same background as the viral video. The title of the video, when translated to English read: "Aaj Ki Baat Live: Israel declares... will take revenge... will choose the time and method ourselves | Israel Iran War Update." Here is the link to the video and below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the two videos: The Desk watched the entire video, but nowhere did we find Sharma making any mention of Dr Chhajer. Video 2 We ran another keyframe through Google Lens to find the source of the police statement and came across an X post by All India Radio News, shared on September 28, in which Inspector General of Police Kashmir Range, VK Birdi shared information about an encounter between security forces and terrorists in Kulgam district. The Desk noticed that this was the same video as shown in the viral clip, except that the audio was different, which was altered in the recent clip. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a combination image showing that it's the same video. Video 3 For the third clip of Dr Chhajer in the viral video, the Desk ran another keyframe through Google Lens and came across a YouTube video, uploaded on a verified channel named 'GetsetflySCIENCE by Gaurav Thakur' on July 20, 2024. The title of the video read: "Do This to CLEAN Cholesterol in 3 Months | Prevent Heart Attack - Dr. Bimal Chhajer | GT Show" Here is the link to the video and below is a combination image, which shows Dr Chhajer wearing the same outfit and sitting in the same background as the viral clip. The Desk watched this video but could not find Dr Chhajer mentioning anywhere about receiving any death threats. We also came across a video where Dr Chhajer himself stated that the viral video claiming about his death in a car explosion was fake. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk passed the video through Deepfakes Analysis Unit , which confirmed that "synthetic audio was used to fabricate the video.". "The audio content in each of the videos is different from that in the doctored video. However, the clothing, backdrop, and body language of the subjects in these videos and their respective segments in the doctored video are identical. The logos and supers visible in the original videos are absent in the doctored video. The frames in the manipulated clips are more zoomed in," the DAU's analysis stated. We also ran the video under TrueMedia, an AI detection tool, which stated that there was substantial evidence of manipulation. Below are the screenshots of the result: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media was doctored and made using AI-generated voice clones.

author: Deepak Chaudhary/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of Amit Shah shared to falsely claim he insulted BJP leaders Babulal Marandi and Champai Soren; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 16 (Deepak Chaudhary / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing Assembly polls in Jharkhand, a video of Union Home Minister Amit Shah addressing a rally was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that he insulted BJP leaders Babulal Marandi and Champai Soren. The PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that Shah's use of the word '–ji' (used with names to show respect) was clipped out, and the edited video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim: Congress leader Supriya Shrinate shared a video on Facebook on November 10, claiming that Union Minister and senior BJP leader Amit Shah insulted party leaders Babulal Marandi and Champai Soren. The caption of the post read, "इतना अपमान! सिर्फ़ क्योंकि जिनको बुला रहे हैं वह आदिवासी हैं आदिवासियों से इतनी चिढ़ क्यों है आपको अमित शाह?" A rough English translation of the caption read: "Such an insult! Just because the people you are calling are tribals Amit Shah, why are you so irritated with the tribals?" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation: The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other social media users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across the full video of the speech uploaded on BJP's official YouTube channel. It was a YouTube Live, which was streamed on the channel on November 3, 2024. The title of the video read, "LIVE: HM Shri Amit Shah addresses public meeting in Ghatshila, Jharkhand" Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: On watching the video carefully, the Desk found that the viral clip shared on social media was taken from the 27:34-minute timestamp. The Desk noticed that Shah addressed both Babulal Marandi and Champai Soren respectfully throughout his speech. He regularly used the suffix '–ji' (Babulalji and Champaiji) with their names to show respect and also asked the audience to vote for them in the ongoing Jharkhand Assembly elections. Upon comparison of the two videos, we found that the use of '–ji' before their names was edited out in the viral video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an edited video of Shah's speech was shared on social media with a false claim.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: No, RBI did not issue Rs 7 coin to honour MS Dhoni; photo shared on social media is fake
content: New Delhi, Nov 17 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : A photo of a gold-coloured Rs 7 coin featuring skipper Mahendra Singh Dhoni was recently shared on social media with users claiming that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was issuing the coin to honour the former Indian skipper for his contributions to Indian cricket. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the image was originally shared by a satirical page and the RBI had not made any such announcement. The social media posts were shared with a fake claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 13 a photo of both sides of a gold-coloured Rs 7 coin featuring Mahendra Singh Dhoni and claimed that the RBI was issuing the coin to honour the former Indian skipper. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found that several other users had shared the same image with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the official website of RBI, but did not find any such announcement as claimed in the viral posts. We found the latest list of coins in circulation, but did not find any mention of Rs 7 coin. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the page: In the next part of investigation, the Desk checked the list of coins in circulation on the official website of Security Printing & Minting Corporation of India Limited (SPMCIL), but did not find any mention of Rs 7 coin there either. Here is the link to the website and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also scanned the list of commemorative coins but it did not include Dhoni's name. Here is the link to the list. In the next part of investigation, the Desk found that the same photo was shared by an Instagram handle named '@thetathyanews' on November 3. The caption of the post mentioned that the information was not real news and was a satire intended for entertainment purposes. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photo of Rs 7 coin shared on social media was fake.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Video from 'Pushpa 2' trailer launch event falsely shared as crowd at Maha Vikas Aghadi rally in Mumbai; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : Amid the ongoing Assembly polls in Maharashtra, a video was shared on social media with users claiming it showed a massive crowd gathered at a meeting of the Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA), at the Bandra Kurla Complex (BKC) in Mumbai. However, the PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the video was from the trailer launch event of the film 'Pushpa 2: The Rule', starring Indian actor Allu Arjun, which will release on December 5. Maharashtra voted in single phase on November 20 and the votes will be counted along with Jharkhand on November 23. Claim A Facebook user shared a November 18 a video and claimed that it showed the massive crowd gathered at a meeting of the Maha Vikas Aghadi at the BKC in Mumbai. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other users with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a YouTube video, streamed live on November 17, 2024. The video, uploaded by movie promotional agency YouWe Media was titled: "Pushpa 2 - The Rule Massive Trailer Launch Event LIVE". The video featured visuals similar to the viral footage, confirming it showed the same event. Below is a combination image highlighting the same: The viral video from 9 to 23 seconds, of the camera moving from rear to the front, can be seen at 6:44 and 6:54 timestamps in the extended part of the video. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Indian Express published on November 18, which featured similar visuals from the trailer launch event of 'Pushpa 2'. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "The highly-anticipated trailer of Pushpa 2: The Rule was launched on Sunday in Patna, Bihar. The grand event turned into a massive fan frenzy as thousands of gathered at Gandhi Maidan to catch a glimpse of Allu Arjun and Rashmika Mandanna," read a portion of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video was from the launch event of trailer of Allu Arjun-starrer 'Pushpa 2', held at Gandhi Maidan in Patna.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming land area owned by Waqf Board in India is more than that of Pakistan are fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 13 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a post which claimed that the total area of properties owned by Waqf Board in India is more than the total land area of Pakistan. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false as the total area of Pakistan is around 232 times larger than the area of properties owned by Waqf Board in India. Claim A Facebook user on November 6 shared a post, which claimed that the total land area of Pakistan was 8.81 lakh square kilometre whereas the total area of properties owned by Waqf Board in India was 9.40 lakh square kilometre. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned social media platforms using specific keywords and found that the same claim was shared by several other users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised Google search and came across an explainer of the Waqf Amendment Bill 2024, posted on the official website of Press Information Bureau (PIB) on September 13, 2024. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the explainer, the Waqf Boards control 8.7 lakh properties spanning 9.4 lakh acres across India with an estimated value of 1.2 lakh crores. As can be noticed, 9.4 lakh is in acres, not square kilometre, as claimed in the viral posts. On converting, we found that the total area of properties comtrolled by Waqf Boards across India is 3804.04 sq km. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across the official website of Central Investigation Agency (CIA), which mentioned Pakistan's land area to be 770,875 sq km. Here is the link to the webpage and below is a screenshot of the same: This means that the total area of Pakistan is nearly 202 times larger than the total area of land controlled by Waqf Boards in India. Hence, the viral claim is false.

author: Abhinav Gupta/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated image of Gautam Adani shared on social media to falsely claim his arrest amid indictment in US; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 22 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A day after industrialist Gautam Adani's indictment in the United States of America for alleged fraud and bribery, a photo went viral on social media which showed the Adani Group founder held by US security personnel. The PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that an AI-generated image was falsely shared on social media as a real one. Adani, India's second-richest man, and seven others, including his nephew Sagar Adani, have been charged by the US Department of Justice with paying bribes to unidentified officials of state governments in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha to buy expensive solar power, potentially earning more than USD 2 billion in profit over 20 years. Unconfirmed media reports have also claimed that an arrest warrant has been issued against the industrialist. Claim A Facebook user shared the photo on November 21 and claimed that Adania had been arrested. "And if I may ask.. Did Zakayo had to wait for so long to cansel this Adani deal?? He should be prosecuted alongside this conman…" read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that several other users had shared the same image across social media platforms with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk took a closer look on the viral image and noticed several discrepancies, suggesting that it was not real. While one of the security personnel can be seen with abnormal looking six fingers, some faces in the background are deformed. The image below highlights the same: Taking a cue from this, we ran the image through True Media, a generative AI voice and deepfake detection app. The software suggested strong presence of AI-generated media, making it clearer that the viral photo was fake. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and did not find any credible report on Adani's arrest. We, however, came across some reports which stated that an arrest warrant was issued against him in New York. Here is the link to a report by The Indian Express , published on November 23, whose headline read: "Arrest warrant issued against Gautam Adani in New York for alleged bribery: What this means, what happens next." "A Reuters report said arrest warrants were issued in the United States for Gautam Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani, after a grand jury in New York indicted the business tycoon and seven others on charges of bribery of $265 million (around Rs 2,029 crore) on Wednesday (November 20)," read a section of the report. Meanwhile, a report by India Today stated that "an arrest warrant against Gautam Adani was unsealed in a New York court last month after the billionaire industrialist was indicted on charges of bribery and fraud." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an AI-generated photo was shared on social media, which users misinterpreted as a real image.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Atishi did not allege sexual assault on Arvind Kejriwal in Tihar Jail; X post from parody account shared on social media as real
content: New Delhi, Nov 21 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): With the Assembly polls in Delhi nearing, political parties have stepped up their campaigns. Meanwhile, multiple social media users recently shared a screenshot of an alleged X post by Delhi CM Atishi stating that the people of Delhi will respond to the BJP by defeating it for the "atrocities and sexual assault done on Arvind Kejriwal in Tihar Jail". In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the X post was shared from a parody account, not Atishi's official account. The screenshot was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 17 a screenshot of a purported X post by Delhi CM Atishi, alleging that Arvind Kejriwal was sexually assaulted in Tihar Jail. "भाई का यौन शोषण भी हुआ है इसकी तो में कड़े शब्दों में निंदा करता हूँ," read the post. An English translation of the post read: "Brother has also been sexually exploited, I strongly condemn it." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned the official X account of Atishi but did not find any such post We then reverse-searched the image in the viral post and found that the viral X post had originated from a parody account, '@atishi_maarlena'. Here is the link and archive link to the post shared on November 12 and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the X name of the user was mentioned as 'Dr. Atishi || AAP || CM, Delhi 2024 || Parody ||,' a verified handle. The username of the account was mentioned as '@atishi_maarlena'. Also, the bio of the X account read: "Parody || No Endorsements || Tweets's can't be legally challenged || Tweets are just for Fun and Satire || Not affiliated to anyone || Fan Account of Atishi ||." On investigating further, the Desk found that the photo used in the viral post was taken from a press conference held by AAP leaders Atishi and Sanjay Singh in February 2023. The press conference was held after the MCD meeting was adjourned for the third consecutive time without electing a mayor. Here is the link to the event video, and below is a combination image showing that the photo in the viral post was taken from the same event. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral post was shared from a parody account, not the real X account of Delhi CM Atishi.

title: PTI Fact Check: Congress worker posing with Rahul Gandhi falsely identified as American evangelist's wife on social media; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Nov 25 (Abhinav Gupta /Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : A photo of a woman posing with Congress MP Rahul Gandhi was recently shared on social media with users claiming she was she was the wife of American evangelist Daniel Stephen Courney. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman was Anusha Pullaiah, a Karnataka Congress member, and she is not Courney's wife. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Courney is accused of carrying of religious conversion-related activities under the pretext of doing social service. While he is married to an Indian woman named Anusha, she is not the one seen in the viral image. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 22 a photo of a posing with Congress MP Rahul Gandhi and claimed that she was Anusha, wife of American evangelist Daniel Stephen Courney. "Is INC A Religious Conversion Cult? Meet Anusha (@AnushaS25), wife of Daniel Stephen Courney, the kingpin of religious conversion racket who has been converting thousands of Hindus into Christianity every year. Anusha is Secretary of Karnataka Pradesh Youth Congress Committee and specializes in running election war-rooms of Indian National Congress. With this documented evidence, can't we say - INC is actually involved in numerous crimes being a religious conversion cult? Please ask Antonio Albina Maino, Raul Vinci and Bianca to prove this photo wrong," the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the post: Investigation The Desk reverse searched the viral image and found that the same photo was shared by several other users with similar claims. One such post can be seen here , and its archived version can be seen here , respectively: The Desk noticed that the user Salah Uddin Shoaib Choudhury, identified himself as Editor at Bangladeshi outlet named 'Blitz'. On scanning his profile, we found that Choudhury had shared the same photo (as seen in the inset in the viral image) in October as well, comparing it with a photo of Courney and his wife to claim that she was the same woman. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On investigating further, the Desk found an X post by Anusha in which she rejected the claims made by the user by sharing her letter and an FIR copy that she has filed against her photos being misidentified. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In her bio, Anusha mentioned herself as "Secretary @IYCKarnataka Research, specialising in running election Warrooms for @INCIndia". The Desk noticed that her profile photo was the same as the one shared in viral posts. Below is a screenshot of her X profile: On scanning her profile, we found that she had shared the same photo in a post on June 4, 2024. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to Congress spokesperson and party's General Secretary in Karnataka, Lavanya Ballal, who vehemently rubbished the claim, calling it fake. Anusha was neither married not associated to Courney. "It is unfortunate that a 'young girl' is subjected to all this and treated like this. It is in unfortunate times that we are living in, where someone puts out something on social media, and many believe in such things. Where is this going...? Some people are making their living out of fake news...trust factor is eroding because of fake news...." she told PTI. The Desk also scanned the Facebook profile of Daniel Stephen Courney and found that his wife Anusha was a different woman. Below is a combination image of Courney's wife Anusha and Anusha, the Congress worker. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Karnataka Congress worker Anusha was falsely identified as the wife of American evangelist Daniel Stephen Courney.

title: PTI Fact Check: Satire article claiming Elon Musk's CNN deal falsely shared on social media as real news
content: New Delhi, Nov 26 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : Social media has recently been abuzz with the claim that tech entrepreneur and X owner Elon Musk was buying US broadcaster CNN for USD 3 billion. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be fake. The claim seemingly originated from a satire article, which was shared by social media users as a news report. Claim A Facebook page shared on November 10 a post claiming that Elon Musk had agreed to buy CNN at USD 3 billion dollars. The caption of the post read: "Elon Musk Agrees to $3 Billion to Buy CNN. Elon Musk Reportedly Eyeing CNN Acquisition: "'ll Fix the Media, One Network at a Time" 💪 love it!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk scanned social media handles using customised keywords and found that several other Facebook users had shared the same claim. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but did find any genuine report confirming the claim made in social media posts. Taking a cue from this, the Desk searched on Google the caption used in the viral posts, and found that an article with the same headline, on the website SpaceXMania. Here is the link to the article published on October 18, 2024 and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk noticed that the article was posted under the Satire category, as can also be seen mentioned in the screenshot above. The Desk then scanned the website and found its 'About Us' page mentioning that it provides the "freshest fake news, some sassy analysis, and a good dose of satire" focused on Musk. Here is the link to the webpage and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk also noticed that the satire website had separate categories named Elon Musk, SpaceX, NASA, Tesla and Satire. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a satire article was shared on social media as real news

title: PTI Fact Check: No travel ban imposed on Adani, Amit Shah or Doval by US or Canada; social media posts shared with fake claim
content: New Delhi, Nov 28 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : Amid the ongoing row over the indictment of businessman Gautam Adani in the United States of America for alleged fraud and bribery, several social media users recently shared posts claiming that he, along with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval, was not allowed to visit Canada and US, as the two countries had imposed travel restrictions on all three. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the claim shared on social media was fake. None of the two countries has imposed any travel restrictions on Shah, Doval or Adani. The posts have been shared in context of two recent developments – first is Adani's indictment and second is the recent diplomatic faceoff between India and Canada following Prime Minister Justin Trudeau's allegations in September last year of a "potential" involvement of Indian agents in Khalistan extremist Hardeep Singh Nijjar's killing. New Delhi rejected Trudeau's charges as "absurd". Claim A Facebook user shared on November 22 a post claiming that industrialist Gautam Adani and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval were banned from travelling to the United States while Canada had imposed travel ban on Union Home Minister Amit Shah. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found that similar claims were shared by several other users across social media platforms. One such user on X shared a purported screenshot of a news report published by India Herald Group on Dailyhunt, whose headline read: "Modi's close aide Adani, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval can't travel to US or Canada." Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Another user on Facebook shared a link to an article published on 'India Herald' with the same headline as stated in other posts. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: It seemed that the viral claim stemmed from the Indian Herald article, which did not quote any official to support the claim. In the next part of investigation, the Desk scanned the U.S. State Department's website for references to Amit Shah. We found the transcription of a press briefing held on October 30, 2024, in which spokesperson Matthew Miller replied to accusations made by Canada against Shah. Here is the link to the website and Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk further scanned the US State Department's website but did not find any news related to any travel ban imposed on Shah. The latest travel ban issued by the US was issued on October 9, 2024, against former Ecuadorian leaders Rafael Vicente Correa Delgado and Jorge David Glas Espinel for corruption and abuse of power. Similarly, the latest mention of Ajit Doval on the website was in a July 2023 press briefing. Below is a screenshot regarding the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google but did not find any report related to and travel ban on Adani in US or Canada. During our investigation, we came across a report by The Indian Express, published on November 23. The headline of the report read: "After MEA rebuff, Canada rejects report: 'no evidence linking PM, Jaishankar, NSA'." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "In a significant move indicating an attempt to dial down tensions between Ottawa and Delhi, Canadian National Security Advisor Nathalie G Drouin, contradicting a report in The Globe and Mail daily, has said the government of Canada "has not stated, nor is it aware of evidence linking" Prime Minister Narendra Modi, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar and NSA Ajit Doval to "the serious criminal activity" in Canada — a reference to the killing of Khalistan separatist Hardeep Singh Nijjar last year," read a section of the report. Regarding the claim about Adani, the Desk found that the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York had filed charges against Adani for alleged bribery. Here is the link to a press release issued by US Department of Justice on November 20, titled: "Billionaire Chairman of Conglomerate and Seven Other Senior Business Executives Indicted in Connection With Scheme to Pay Hundreds of Millions of Dollars in Bribes and Conceal Bribery Scheme From U.S. Investors." We also came across a November 22 report by The Indian Express, which quoted a Reuters report stating that "arrest warrants were issued in the United States for Gautam Adani and his nephew Sagar Adani, after a grand jury in New York indicted the business tycoon and seven others on charges of bribery of $265 million (around Rs 2,029 crore) on Wednesday (November 20)." Here is the link to the report. We again reviewed the US State Department website, but did not find any information regarding a travel ban on Adani. Hence, the claim of travel ban on Adani is misleading since the charges levelled against him are being investigated. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that no such travel ban was imposed on Shah or Doval as claimed in social media posts.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Fake X account of Sheikh Hasina falsely shares old photo of her with daughter Saima as recent; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the recent incidents of violence against minority Hindus in Bangladesh, a photo of country's former PM Sheikh Hasina enjoying a meal with her daughter Saima Wazed was recently shared on X (formerly Twitter), purportedly from the former's handle. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old photo was shared from an imposter account, falsely insinuating that it was a recent image. The photo was originally shared by Saima on X in June this year. On August 5, the Sheikh Hasina-led government was overthrown following months of protests by the country's youth. Since the fallout of the government, there has been a sharp spike in incidents of violence against minority Hindus in the crisis-hit country. Claim An X handle, claiming to be of former Bangladesh PM Sheikh Hasina, shared on December 3 a picture wherein she can be seen enjoying a meal with her daughter and World Health Organisation (WHO) South Asia Regional Director Saima Wazed. The post was captioned, "We mother and daughter are eating together," suggesting a speculation for the viewers that the post had been of recent times. "In your country, our Hindu brothers and sisters are being killed, our temples are being raided, our sisters' honor is being looted, and you are eating together here. Hey, talk about it, raise the issue at the international level, take it to our country's Prime Minister, talk to our Defence Minister," one of the social media users criticizing the former leader commented on her post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral image through Google and came across an X post by Saima Wazed, shared on June 9 this year, which featured the same photo. "A quick bite with Ma, ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's inauguration in Delhi later today," she had captioned the post back then. Here's the original link , archive link and screenshot of the post shared by Saima Wazed. We also found a news report by Times of India based on the photo, which was published on the same day, i.e. June 9, 2024. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted multiple keyword searches on Google, but did not find any authentic or verified X account of Sheikh Hasina. The Desk then scanned the account from which the image was posted, and found that it was created in November 2024. Below is a screenshot, highlighting the same: We also clicked the link mentioned in the bio of the account, which led us to a portal related to domain purchase. Below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, it was concluded that an old photo of Sheikh Hasina enjoying a meal with her daughter was recently shared from an imposter account of the former Bangladesh PM.

title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video showing old man marrying minor girl shared on social media as real incident; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 3 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : A video recently shared on social media claims to show a 76-year-old Muslim man having man married a 12-year-old girl. Sharing the video, users claimed that the man was Rozob Ali, who married the girl named Sakina Bibi. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that a scripted video was shared on social media with a false claim and communal spin. Claim An Instagram user shared on November 22 a video, claiming that it showed 76-year-old Rozob Ali who married a 12-year-old girl named Sakina Bibi. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared across social media platforms with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across the same video uploaded on YouTube by one 'MB TV' channel on September 26, 2024. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk checked the 'About' section of the channel, which clearly mentioned: "Entertainment Channel Enjoy And Share. Please Like , Comments Share and Subscribe My Channel." Below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk checked other videos posted by the channel and found that the same girl, as seen in the viral video, had featured in other videos too, which looked scripted. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: The same video was also posted by a Facebook page named 'Disha Media' on September 29, 2024. Here is the link and archive link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The 'Intro' section of the page read: "This is official page of "Disha Media". This page is made for entertainment, education, inspiration purpose. For more update, please follow our page." Below is a screenshot of the same: Hence, it was concluded that a scripted video was shared as a real incident on social media, with a false communal claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video of Champai Soren shared on social media as recent to falsely claim he wanted to rejoin JMM; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 03 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : A video of BJP leader Champai Soren praising Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it was a recent video and that he wanted to return to the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, his former party. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that an old video from the time when Hemant Soren was with the JMM and was serving as Jharkhand CM following Hemant Soren's arrest by the Enforcement Directorate. The video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Champai Soren, a long-time associate of JMM leader Shibu Soren, resigned from JMM to join the BJP earlier this year. He contested the Jharkhand Assembly elections from Seraikela seat, from which he has been winning since 1991. He won by a margin of over 20,000 votes. The JMM-led grand alliance, however, won the elections with Hemant Soren continuing as the CM. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 1 a video of BJP leader Champai Soren talking about Rahul Gandhi's Bharat Jodo Yatra and praising Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren, and claimed that he wanted to return to the JMM. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes of the viral video. On running of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that the same video was shared by several other social media users with the same claim. One such post can be seen here and its archived version can be viewed here . On further scanning the search results, the Desk found that the video was originally posted on the X account of a news agency on February 2 this year, when Soren was sworn in as the CM of Jharkhand after the arrest of Hemant Soren by the ED. The original video can be seen here . In the video, Champai talks about meeting Hemant Soren in jail and refers to him as leader of the party, JMM. He also talked about Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra, which was taken out from Manipur to Mumbai between January and March this year. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Hindu, published on February 3. The headline of the report read: "Champai Soren sworn in as Jharkhand CM; ex-CM Hemant Soren remanded to five days of ED custody." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk noticed that the event of his oath-taking happened on February 2, and as can be seen in the photo above, he was wearing the same attire as seen in the viral video. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: We also came across an X post by Soren, in which he termed the rumours of him going back to JMM as false, while calling out the viral video. "Some misleading rumours are being spread about me on social media as part of an agenda by making an old video viral. This was done at the time of elections also. Please avoid such false rumours," read the X post, originally in Hindi. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video shared on social media was old and unrelated.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally edited video of actor Pankaj Tripathi talking about online fraud shared with false claim that he criticised BJP; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid the charged political atmosphere in the national capital ahead of the upcoming assembly elections, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on December 5 shared a video in a social media post featuring Bollywood actor Pankaj Tripathi claiming he criticised Bharatiya Janata Party. In the video, Tripathi appeared to caution voters against trusting promises made by the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and found the video to be digitally altered. The original clip, dated September 23, featured Tripathi discussing UPI fraud, not commenting on the BJP or the elections. The manipulated version, released shortly before the February 2025 assembly polls, falsely attributed political statements to the actor. Claim An X post by the AAP's Rajasthan unit and several other handles features a video starring Bollywood actor Pankaj Tripathi. In the video, he purportedly speaks about how even a peanut seller (the character he features in the viral video) is not a fool to vote for the BJP, as they know that if the latter is voted to power, they will evade with the government money. 'I sell peanuts, not my brain. Check this message shared by the BJP, which highlights that if they are voted to power, they will bring development. But do you think I don't know anything? Here, if I vote for the BJP, they will evade the government money. I am a peanut seller, not a fool. Remember, if the BJP tempts you, mention that 'I am not a fool,' Pankaj Tripathi's statement in the video mentioned (approx. translation). Here's the link, archive link, and SS of the video posted by the AAP. Here's the link , archive link , and SS of the video posted by the AAP. Investigation: To start the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk ran a keyframe of the video through Google Lens and came across several links of reports that got us to the original video, and it found a Facebook post shared by a Unified Payments Interface (UPI) social media account published on September 23. In the video, which appears to be the same as the one shared by AAP social media handles, except for a few changes, Pankaj Tripathi, featuring a Moongfaliwala, talked about the UPI-related frauds, not the BJP. He also talked about how everyone needs to be careful about the same. Also, in the video, when Tripathi shows his phone screen, it reads, "Winner. Congrats! You have won a lottery of Rs 25,00,000! To claim your prize, click the link below." In the viral clip, however, the same is altered with the BJP's symbol and the text: "Vote for BJP." Here is the link and the screenshot of the photo shared by UPI. Further, in next part of the investigation, the Desk also obtained a few media articles, which state that the UPI launched a UPI safety awareness campaign, "Main Moorkh Nahi Hoon", earlier in September, and the video featuring Pankaj Tripathi was made as part of the campaign only. Here is the link and the screenshot of the news article posted by a news website Economic Times. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video posted by the AAP on its regional social media unit was altered, and Pankaj Tripathi did not talk about voting against the BJP. The video was originally made as part of a UPI safety awareness campaign, 'Mai Murkh Nahin Hoon'.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video of aircraft with woolen jacket created for clothing brand ad shared as real with false claim; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 5 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media user shared a video, allegedly shot in Alaska, showing an aircraft covered in a puffer jacket making its way to the runway. The user claimed the plane was covered in a jacket to protect it from extreme temperatures of -60 degrees Celsius in Alaska. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video of the aircraft with a woolen jacket on it was an AI-generated video created as part of a promotion for the Australian clothing brand Decjuba. The claim in the social media post was false. Claim A viral social media post containing a video claimed that amid the extreme weather conditions in Alaska, where the temperatures can drop to (-29°C to -34°C) (on average), an aircraft there is also wearing a warm winter jacket so that the engines do not get stiff due to the cold.
