"Custom jackets, also known as engine covers or aircraft covers, are designed to protect planes from frigid temperatures in Alaskan airports, often reaching -60°C (-80°F) or lower. Custom jackets play a vital role in protecting aircraft from Alaska's extreme cold, ensuring safe and efficient operations," the accompanying text from the viral video stated. Here is the link and archive link to the viral social media post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation: The PTI Fact Check Desk conducted multiple keyword searches on Google to start the investigation. It came across several posts that led to articles and YouTube links about the same video. One of the significant pieces of information the Desk obtained in its investigation was a YouTube video posted by Creativa, the company responsible for producing the advertisement. In its description, the company mentioned that the video generated was for an ad campaign for the Australian clothing brand DECJUBA, designed to showcase their new D-LUXE Basics puffer collection. Further, Creativa's post also mentioned that the video under review is a virtual outdoor (FOOH) advertisement. "FOOH (Fake Out of Home) involves producing content that mimics real-world out-of-home advertising, such as billboards, posters, or installations. The twist? These are digitally created and designed to look as if they're happening on the streets. This digital content is then shared online to capture audience attention as if it were unfolding life in public spaces," the company stated. Here is the link , the archive link of the post by the company, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk also found a LinkedIn post shared by Hero, an Australia-based advertising company, and learned that Hero and Creativa generated the AI-powered video featuring an aircraft 'wearing a puffer jacket' at Melbourne airport. Based on the information posted by the company, the investigation got the backing that the video was not real but a virtual advertisement generated through 3D animation. "To put comments to rest, we can confirm that whilst the stunt is very convincing thanks to 3D animation, rendering, and a little creativity, the stylish puffers are currently only available in human-sized measurements," the company stated. Here is the link , the archive link of the post by the company, and below is a screenshot of the same: In addition, the Desk also searched various news reports about the development and found an article by the UK-based media portal Independent, which also debunked the video featuring an aircraft with a puffer jacket as not real. The claim on the media portal was published on December 3, 2024. Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video showing an aircraft wearing a puffer jacket allegedly to protect its engine from the freezing cold of Alaska is, in fact, an AI-generated promotional video for Australian brand Decjuba.

title: PTI Fact Check: Old video from Hathras stampede falsely shared on social media in name of anti-minority violence in Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 6 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Amid the rising incidents of atrocities against the minority community in Bangladesh, a video recently went viral on social media, claiming that it showed how Hindu women were raped and murdered in Bangladesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was shared on social media with a false claim and showed victims of a stampede in Uttar Pradesh's Hathras in July this year. On July 2, thousands of people, mostly from disadvantaged sections of society, gathered in Hathras to listen to a 'godman' preach. As he left the venue, they ran out to catch a final glimpse of him and knelt down to collect the mud on which he had walked. A stampede broke out, killing 121 people, most of whom were women. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 5 a video, claiming that it showed Hindu women who were raped and murdered by people from the Muslim community in Bangladesh. Here's the link , archive link , and the screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran a keyframe of the video through Google Lens and found that a similar video showing women's bodies was uploaded on YouTube on July 2, 2024, which looked somewhat similar to the viral video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The title of the video stated that it was from Hathras, where 122 people had died in a stampede. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found an Instagram post with the same video as the viral post. The caption of the July 5 post also stated that it was from Hathras. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: We also came across a news report by the Times of India on the incident posted on July 10, 2024. The feature image of the article was the same as the visuals shown in the viral video Here's the link and screenshot of the news article by the Times of India. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video was falsely shared in the name of violence against Hindus in Bangladesh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Khandwa fire incident falsely shared on social media in name of Ajmer Dargah protests
content: New Delhi, Dec 07 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Days after a local court ordered a survey of Rajasthan's Ajmer Sharif Dargah in response to a plea claiming it was built over a Hindu temple, a video allegedly linked to the development went viral on social media. The video was shared with claims that members of the Hindu community, who held a protest march over the ongoing controversy, were injured in a fire that erupted accidentally. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk investigated and debunked the claim. It found that the viral video showing a torch procession was not related to Ajmer but was originally from Khandwa, Madhya Pradesh. According to authorities, the torch procession is an annual event in Madhya Pradesh's Khandwa, held in memory of three individuals killed by members of the banned Students' Islamic Movement of India (SIMI) in 2009. This year, during the event's conclusion at Ghantaghar, an accidental mishap occurred when participants were placing their torches down, causing nearby torches to ignite suddenly. Several attendees, including women, children, and men, suffered burns, primarily on their hands, faces, and legs. Claim A recently shared video on social media shows many people holding torches. Users have purportedly claimed that the video was shot during a Hindu protest march held over the controversy surrounding the Dargah of Khwaja Moin-ud-din Chishti. The user who shared the video mentioned that during the protest only, a fire broke out, engulfing the people under it. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the viral video shared across several social media platforms. Investigation In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk extracted keyframes and performed a Google reverse image search. Through the same, it came across a YouTube video posted by a media organisation, NDTV. The keyframes the desk used match the visuals posted by the news portal, which mentioned that the same is from the accident site in Madhya Pradesh's Khandwa. Here's the link and the screenshot of the video posted by NDTV on December 1, 2024. In the next part of the investigation, the desk also conducted multiple keyword searches on X and found a video by the news channel Mirror Now on November 29. The video circulated in the viral post matches the one posted by the news channel. The description of the video mentioned by the news channel read, "Mishap during torch procession in Madhya Pradesh's Khandwa." Here's the link and screenshot of the video posted by the Mirror Now news channel on November 29. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Madhya Pradesh fire tragedy video was falsely shared in the name of the protests held by the Hindu community people over the controversy surrounding Ajmer Sharif Dargah, wherein they also suffered burn injuries.

title: PTI Fact Check: Edited video of TMC MP Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar shared on social media with false claim that she schooled Amit Shah in Parliament
content: New Delhi, Dec 07 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Amid the ongoing Winter Session of Parliament, a video featuring Union Home Minister Amit Shah and All India Trinamool Congress MP Dr. Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar was shared on social media, claiming the TMC MP lashed out at the Home Minister over the issue of GST during the Parliament proceedings. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video was shared on social media with a false claim and was made by editing two different videos, thus misleading the context. Significantly, the video of the TMC MP's speech from Parliament dates back to August 2022. Then, she spoke over the issue of high LPG costs during the debate on price rise in Lok Sabha. Meanwhile, the short clip of the Union Home Minister was taken and edited from his statement in Rajya Sabha over the attack on the convoy of AIMIM MP Asaduddin Owaisi on February 7, 2022. Claim The video featuring TMC MP Dr Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar and Union Home Minister Amit Shah was shared across several social media handles. Claims suggest that the TMC MP schooled Amit Shah in the Parliament on the issue of GST. The video also shows Ghosh reprimanding Amit Shah and asking him to sit down (the visuals followed the same in the viral video). Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk extracted keyframes and performed a Google reverse image search. Through the same, it came across a YouTube video posted by Sansad TV on August 1, 2022. The video holds the complete speech of the TMC MP, as well as a portion circulating on social media, where the latter reprimanded the MPs from other parties who tried to raise an argument during her speech over the price rise in the Parliament. Nowhere had the Union Home Minister Amit Shah appeared in the video, which was against the viral claim. Here's the link and screenshot of the video posted by Sansad TV. Further, in the next part of the investigation, the Desk extracted keyframes and performed a reverse image search. This time, the team used the keyframe from Amit Shah's viral segment. This search again led us to a video uploaded on Sansad TV's YouTube channel on February 7, 2022. The description of the same stated that Union Home Minister Amit Shah made a statement in Rajya Sabha over the attack on the convoy of AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi back in the year 2022. Here's the link and screenshot of the video posted by Sansad TV. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was edited. Users are sharing the altered video, which was made after combining two videos of the proceedings, with a false claim. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that this was not the first time the same video had gone viral on social media. Earlier, the PTI Fact Check Team had debunked all the false claims surrounding the video. Here's the link to the PTI fact-check article.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of cow slaughter from Manipur falsely linked to Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's Wayanad poll victory; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 09 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Days after Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra won the Lok Sabha bypoll from Wayanad, a video was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that a local party leader there killed a cow to celebrate the leader's sweeping electoral victory. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the claim was false. The video was found to be at least six months old and is from Manipur, not Wayanad. It is pertinent to note that the false claim was shared on social media soon after Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on November 23 registered a mammoth victory from the Wayanad Lok Sabha seat. She defeated CPI candidate Satyan Mokeri by a huge margin of 410,931 votes. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 28 a video, claiming that it showed the media-in-charge of Kerala Congress, Mohammed Mujahid Islam, sacrificing a cow by shooting it in the head to celebrate Priyanka Gandhi's victory in Wayanad Lok Sabha bypoll. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the same post. Investigation The Desk ran of the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and came across an X post, dated May 7, 2024, which carried the same video. The caption of the post stated that the incident happened in Manipur and that the person opening fire on the cow was a "Kuki militant". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In response to the post, animal rights organisation PETA also responded on May 7, 2024, that its "Cruelty Response Team is working with Manipur Police's Cyber Crime Cell to confirm the details with respect to the location of the crime." Here's the link and the screenshot of the post by PETA India. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a news report by The Free Press Journal on May 7, 2024. The report mentioned that the incident occurred in Manipur and led to a public outcry demanding strong action to be taken against the perpetrator. Here's the link and screenshot of the news report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video from Manipur was falsely linked to Priyanka Gandhi Vadra's bypoll victory in Wayanad.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Bangladesh student clash falsely shared with communal spin; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Amid the reports of a rise in cases of atrocities against the Hindu minorities in Bangladesh, a social media post was shared with a claim that a student (Hindu) was beaten to death at Dhaka's Dr Mahbubur Rahman Mollah College. The video attached, along with the viral posts, showed a mob attacking a student with sticks, thus triggering speculation of a communal angle to the incident. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The video was about the violent clashes that broke out between student groups from three colleges in Bangladesh last month. Claim An Instagram user shared on December 4 a video where a group of students armed with sticks thrashed a Hindu student in Bangladesh. The Hindu student was said to be beaten to death by the mob. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the viral post. Investigation The Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and came across a YouTube video posted by a local news channel (bdnews24.com) on November 25. The description of the video then read, "The incident is the attack on the students of Dr. Mahbubur Rahman Mollah College by the students of Government Shaheed Suhrawardy College and Kabi Nazrul Government College." Here's the link and screenshot of the video posted by the Bangladesh news channel. Further, in the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across several news reports published around the incident. According to the news report published by the Bangladesh-based news portal, The Daily Star, on November 25, 2024, the incident is of a violent clash that broke out between students of Government Shaheed Suhrawardy College, Kabi Nazrul Government College, and Dr Mahbubur Rahman Mollah College. Around 100 people were also injured in the hours-long violence, according to the media reports. Here's the link and the screenshot of the news article posted by a Bangladesh-based daily. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim circulated along the video that a Hindu student was beaten to death on the streets in Bangladesh is false. The incident captured in the video is of a violent clash that broke out between student groups over the death of another person earlier last month.

title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of famous Japanese bridge falsely shared claiming it's located in Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich
content: New Delhi, Dec 10 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/ Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): An image of a steep bridge was shared on social media platforms with a claim that it was of a bridge constructed in Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich district. However, through the investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim circulated with the photo to be false. The investigation revealed the bridge is not located in India but is from Japan, named the 'Eshima Ohashi Bridge'. According to data from Japan's government, the Eshima Ohashi is a large, steeply sloped bridge that spans Lake Nakaumi to connect Matsue in Shimane Prefecture and Sakaiminato in Tottori Prefecture. Claim An image was circulated on different social platforms, claiming the bridge with a unique design was constructed on Dargah Road in Uttar Pradesh's Bahraich district. The users posted the picture with the caption, "Unique picture of the bridge on Dargah Road in the Bahraich district of Uttar Pradesh." Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the image the social media user posted. Investigation The Desk ran the keyframe of the viral image through Google Lens and came across an article by the UK-based news portal Daily Star dated May 07, 2015. The article's feature image was the same as the one we had seen in the viral post. Here's the link and screenshot of the news article posted by Daily Star. Further, in the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a website featuring exclusive details about the famous Japanese bridge. The website (Shimane Japan) stated, 'At its highest point, the bridge reaches a height of approximately 45m and is Japan's largest girder bridge made of concrete.' Here's the link and the screenshot of the website. Also compare the viral image circulating with a false claim with that of an original image of the bridge. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image is not from Bahraich but is of Japan's famous Eshima Grand Bridge.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered photo falsely claims Aishwarya Rai Bachchan's second marriage; social media post debunked as baseless
content: New Delhi, Dec 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A social media post recently went viral, alleging that Bollywood actor Aishwarya Rai Bachchan had entered into a second marriage with London-based businessman Vatche Manoukian. The post further claimed that this marriage followed her alleged divorce from her husband, actor Abhishek Bachchan. The user shared photos allegedly depicting Aishwarya Rai Bachchan with the businessman to support this claim. However, after a thorough investigation, the PTI Fact Check desk found that the images had been digitally altered. The original photos only featured Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and her husband, Abhishek Bachchan. The claim was deemed entirely false and misleading, with no basis in fact. Claim A social media post shared Bollywood actor Aishwarya Rai Bachchan's images with a London-based businessman, Vatche Manoukian, claiming that both of them got married. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk extracted keyframes and performed a Google reverse image search. Through the same, we came across a post made by an account called Celebo. The handle is known for publishing news, photos, videos, and reels of Bollywood celebrities. Significantly, the post contains an exact image of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan with her husband, Abhishek Bachchan, taken earlier. However, we noticed that the same image was altered in the viral post to match London-based businessman Vatche Manoukian's post. Here's the link and screenshot of the post. The Desk also compared the viral image with that of the original image. It is clearly visible that the original image has been tampered with. See the screenshot of the comparison here. Further, in the next part of the investigation, the Desk again did reverse image search on the other purportedly shared image of Aishwarya Rai Bachchan with Manoukian. Similarly, in the first case, this image of Bollywood actor Aishwarya Rai Bachchan was also found to be altered. During further search we came to know that the original image dates back to 2016, when Aishwarya Rai Bachchan had attended the pre-wedding bash of Isheta Salgaocar, the niece of Indian industrialist Mukesh Ambani, with her husband Abhishek Bachchan. The image of the star couple entering the party was published by media portal Firstpost in 2016. Here's the link and screenshot of the image published by the news portal. Subsequently, the desk concluded that the photos shared by a social media handle featuring Aishwarya Rai Bachchan and the London-based businessman Vatche Manoukian were digitally altered.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media post claiming Canada declared India a 'terror sponsoring state' is FAKE; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 11 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Following the recent diplomatic standoff between Canada and India, several social media users recently claimed that Ottawa had declared New Delhi a terrorism-sponsoring state. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be false. No such announcement has been made by Canadian authorities. However, it is pertinent to mention here that amid the deteriorating diplomatic ties, Canada recently named India in a list of cyberthreat adversaries, suggesting that state-sponsored actors could be spying against it. India was named after China, Russia, Iran and North Korea in the National Cyber Threat Assessment 2025-2026 (NCTA 2025-2026) report. Claim A Facebook user claimed on November 6 that Canada had officially declared India as a "terrorism-sponsoring state for the first time". Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post shared by the user. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but did not find any authentic report confirming the claim made in social media post. Had any such development taken place, it would have grabbed the headlines across global media, particularly the two countries. We then scanned the Public Safety Canada, an official government website, which mentioned the list of 'terrorist entities', but did not find India's name on it. Here is the link to the page and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then scanned the social media handles of Canadian PM and country's external affairs department , but did not find any such announcement made regarding India. In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to Canada's External Affairs Ministry via email. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. During its investigation, the Desk came across a PTI report carried by the Deccan Herald on November 2, 2024. The headline of the report read: "Another example of Canadian strategy to 'attack India': MEA on India being listed among cyberthreat 'state adversaries'." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "India on Saturday slammed Canada for naming it in the list of countries considered cyber threat "adversaries", describing the "categorisation" as another example of the Canadian strategy to "attack" the country," read a section of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim of Canada declaring India as a terror sponsoring country was false.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming about petitioner's son and 'survey official' in Ajmer Sharif Dargah case are FAKE
content: New Delhi, Dec 12 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : A civil court in Ajmer last month issued notices to the Ajmer Dargah Committee, Union Ministry of Minority Affairs and the Archaeological Survey of India, after a petition was filed, claiming that the Dargah was originally a Shiva temple. The petition, filed by Vishnu Gupta, the national president of Hindu Sena, sought a survey of the Ajmer Sharif Dargah. Meanwhile, several social media users claimed that the son of petitioner Vishnu Gupta was diagnosed with cancer after the petition. At the same time, some other social media users claimed that the officer 'surveying' the Ajmer Dargah suffered a heart attack. The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated both these claims and found them to be completely fake and fabricated. Claim A Facebook user claimed that the son of Vishnu Gupta, the petitioner who sought a survey of Ajmer Sharif Dargah, was diagnosed with cancer. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Meanwhile, another Facebook user shared a post claiming that the official conducting the survey on the Dargah had suffered from heart attack. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same : Investigation The Desk investigated both the claims separately. Here's what we found: We conducted customised keyword search on Google regarding the claim of petitioner's son being diagnosed with cancer, but did not find any authentic report supporting it. The Desk, however, came across an X post by Vishnu Gupta, in which he refuted the viral claim and called it fake. "Some people with Jihadi terrorist mentality are spreading the news on social media that the son of the person who filed a case against Ajmer Dargah has cancer! All these news is false and with the blessings of Mahadev, our family is healthy. Soon, we will perform Abhishek and Puja on Mahadev in Sanatani Ajmer Sankat Mochan Mahadev Temple!" read the December 11 post. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Regarding the claim that the official conducting survey at the dargah had suffered heart attack, the Desk conducted a separate keyword search on Google, but did not come across any report, backing the viral claim. We, however, came across a news report by ETV Bharat on December 9, whose headline read: "अजमेर दरगाह विवाद : अंजुमन कमेटी ने कहा- शान-ओ-शौकत से मनाया जाएगा उर्स". An English translation of the headline read: "Ajmer Dargah controversy: Anjuman Committee said - Urs will be celebrated with great pomp and show". Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: The report quoted Anjuman Committee Secretary Syed Sarwar Chishti refuting rumours of survey being conducted at the 12th century mosque Adhai Din Ka Jhonpra. In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted Chishti, who told PTI that no such survey was done in Ajmer Dargah recently. Chishti said that the last survey in Ajmer Dargah was done in 1949 and that was only for administrative purposes. The desk also contacted police inspector Narendra Jakhar of Dargah Police Station in Ajmer. He told PTI that no survey was being done or recently done at the Ajmer Dargah, nor has any officer suffered a heart attack. The next hearing in the court regarding this matter will be on December 20. Here is the link to a report by ETV Bharat. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim of a survey at Ajmer Dargah is fake, and so is the claim regarding the petitioner's son suffering heart attack.

author: Sajan Kumar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Deepfake Alert! Digitally altered videos shared to falsely claim Rajat Sharma, Ravish Kumar and Dr Rahil Chaudhary endorsed solutions to eye-related problems
content: New Delhi, Dec 12 (Sajan Kumar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple videos claiming to offer solutions for eye-related problems through a special drink have recently gone viral on social media. These videos, presented as news reports, feature prominent names such as journalists Rajat Sharma, Ravish Kumar, and eye specialist Dr Rahil Chaudhary, allegedly endorsing the drink's ability to provide relief from eye issues within just 48 hours. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that they did not promote any such medicine. Unrelated videos were digitally altered using AI-generated voice clone and shared on social media with false claims. Claim A Facebook page named 'Best Health' shared on December 6 a purported video of journalist Rajat Sharma in which he can be heard saying that an eye specialist can provide 100 percent relief from eye-related issues within just 48 hours. The caption of the post read, "क्या आप हमेशा के लिए दृष्टि संबंधी समस्याओं से छुटकारा पाना चाहते हैं? भारत सरकार के इस चिकित्सा कार्यक्रम में तुरंत पंजीकरण करें और केवल 14 दिनों में अपनी दृष्टि पुनः प्राप्त करें!" An English translation of the caption read, "Do you want to permanently get rid of vision-related problems? Register now for this medical program by the Government of India and restore your vision in just 14 days!" Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The same user shared another video on Facebook with similar claims. This time, journalist Ravish Kumar can be seen promoting a special drink said to cure eye problems. Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk closely analysed both videos and noticed that the same script had been used in each and there was a lip-sync issue in the viral video. Also, the multiple pronunciation errors raised doubts about the authenticity of the video. The desk further ran both videos under TrueMedia, an AI detection tool, which stated that there was 'substantial evidence of manipulation'. Below are the links ( here and here ) and screenshots of the result : On December 4, India TV Chairman and Editor-in-Chief Rajat Sharma shared a video on social media platform X and clarified that he has not endorsed any medication in connection with such videos. The caption of the post read, "आजकल नकली दवाईयां बेचने वाले मेरे कई फेक वीडियो पोस्ट करते हैं। ये डीपफेक हैं, फर्जी हैं। ये लोग मेरे वीडियो इस्तेमाल करते हैं, उन पर एआई से मेरी जैसी आवाज लगाते हैं। लेकिन वो आवाज मेरी नहीं है। मैं कोई दवाई नहीं बेचता। किसी डायबिटीज की दवा को, किसी वजन घटाने की दवा को, किसी घुटनों के दर्द की दवा को प्रचारित नहीं करता। ये सारे वीडियो झूठे हैं। इन पर विश्वास न करें।" An English translation of the caption read, "These days, fake videos of me promoting medicines are being posted by those selling counterfeit drugs. These are deepfakes and completely false. They use my videos and overlay an AI-generated voice that sounds like mine, but it is not my voice. I do not sell any medicines or endorse treatments for diabetes, weight loss, or joint pain. All these videos are fake. Do not trust them." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Following Rajat Sharma's X post, a news report was also published on the IndiaTV website. This makes it clear that Rajat Sharma has not endorsed any medication for relieving eye-related problems. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same : On further scanning, the Desk came across a video on Facebook, posted by Ravish Kumar. In the video, Kumar stated that his audio clone was used in the fake advertisement, and also cautioned people against falling prey to such videos. He clarified that he had not endorsed any medication. On December 4, 2023, he wrote, "I have not advertised any medicine, not even for diabetes. For several days, a deep fake version of my voice has been used. If anyone has purchased medicine due to such an advertisement, they should throw it away immediately and never consume it." He further added, "The company that imitates someone's voice to sell medicine is selling fake products. Diabetes is a disease that requires discipline. It is not controlled by divine grace. Many take advantage of your weakness in this way. Consult a proper doctor and pay attention to your health." The original caption of the post read, "मैंने किसी दवा का विज्ञापन नहीं किया है। मधुमेह की दवा का भी नहीं किया। कई दिनों से मेरी आवाज का डीपफेक वर्जन तैयार किया गया है। अगर किसी ने ऐसे विज्ञापन के फेर में दवा खरीदी है तो अभी तुरंत फेंक दें। कभी सेवन न करें। जो कंपनी किसी की आवाज की नकल कर दवा बेच रही है वह नकली दवा ही बेचगी। मधुमेह एक बीमारी है। यह आपसे अनुशासन मांगती है। दैवी कृपा से नियंत्रित नहीं होती। आपकी इस कमजोरी का फायदा उठा कर कई लोग इस तरह की चपत लगा जाते हैं। किसी ढंग के डॉक्टर से दिखाया करें और सेहत पर ध्यान दें।" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: He also posted a video on Instagram on December 7, 2023, clarifying that he had not endorsed any medication. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Since the viral video also features eye specialist Dr. Rahil Chaudhary. The desk conducted a reverse image search on this frame, and found the original video on YouTuber Ranveer Allahbadia's channel. In the video, both were discussing eye-related issues. However, throughout the conversation, Chaudhary did not make any claims as presented in the viral video. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that these prominent names, such as journalists Rajat Sharma, Ravish Kumar, and eye specialist Dr. Rahil Chaudhary, did not promote any such medicine. Unrelated videos were digitally altered using AI-generated voice clones and shared on social media with false claims.

title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photo of Arvind Kejriwal with Elon Musk shared on social media as real with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Ahead of the Assembly polls in Delhi, a purported photo of Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal with tech mogul and CEO of X (formerly Twitter) Elon Musk has been widely shared on social media with users claiming that the two met recently during the latter's Delhi visit, and discussed the educational and healthcare reforms in the national capital. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that no such meeting had taken place. An AI-generated image was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 13 a photo of AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Tesla Motors CEO Elon Musk, claiming that the two met recently in the national capital. Here is the link , archived link and screenshot of the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other social media users with the same claim. Here's the link , archived link , and the screenshot of one such X post. The Desk then ran a customised keyword search on Google but could not find any report regarding such any meeting between Kejriwal and Musk in Delhi. In fact, we could not find any previous report either of any meeting between the two. We closely watched the image and noticed several discrepancies, which suggested that it may be fake or AI-generated. For instance, fingers of the two look disfigured or abnormal, along with blurred faces in the background. Below is a photo highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through True Media and Hive Moderation, both AI detection tools, which suggested substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below are the screenshots of the results: The Desk also noticed '@RisingPiku' watermark at the bottom of the viral image. A customised keyword search for the same keyword led us to an X handle with the same name. The description on the user's profile read, "AI Enthusiast | X Content Creator | Stock Market | The first person to use AI in political campaigns." Here's the link and the screenshot of the profile: We scanned the handle and found that the user had shared the same photo with identical claim on December 13 and later in the thread, the user himself mentioned that it was generated using AI. Here's the link and screenshot of the post shared by the user. Subsequently, it was concluded that the photograph of Arvind Kejriwal with Elon Musk was fake.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video from Bihar's Purnea falsely shared in name of Hindu family's murder in Bangladesh; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 15 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A disturbing video depicting three deceased children and a woman was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed a Hindu family, which was murdered by Muslims in Bangladesh. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the video was of an unrelated incident that took place in Bihar's Purnea, where a woman reportedly killed her three children before committing suicide. The clip was shared on social media with a false claim. Last week, Bangladesh confirmed 88 incidents of communal violence against minorities, mostly Hindus, following the removal of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina in August. The announcement came a day after Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri highlighted "regrettable incidents" of attacks on minorities and expressed India's concerns regarding their safety and welfare during meetings with Bangladeshi officials. Claim An X user shared on December 10 a video depicting three deceased children and a woman, and claimed that they were murdered by people from a particular community in Giripur, Bangladesh. Here's the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: (Note: Disturbing visuals) Investigation In its investigation, the Desk ran the keyframes from the viral video through Google Lens and came across a YouTube video uploaded by a channel named 'City News' on November 7. The title of the video, which carried visuals similar to the viral clip, read: "छठ के खरना में एक घर से मिली माँ-बेटी समेत 4 की लाशें". An English translation of the title read: "Dead bodies of 4 including mother and daughter found in a house during Chhath's Kharna". Here's the link and screenshot of the YouTube video posted by the channel. In the next part of investigation, the Desk performed a customised keyword search and found several media reports on the incident. According to a report by ETV Bharat, the video was from Bihar's Purnea district, where a mentally unstable woman on November 6 killed her three children before committing suicide. Here's the link and screenshot of the news article posted by ETV Bharat. Times of India also reported the incident on November 7. Here is the link to the report titled "Woman, 3 children found hanging in Bihar's Purnia dist". Here is the link to the report. "Bodies of a woman and her three children were found hanging at her home at Kilpara village under Rauta police station of Purnia district on Wednesday. The woman allegedly had some mental issues and prima facie the incident appears to be that of a suicide, police said," read a section of the report. "Police said the deceased were identified as Babita Devi (32) and her three kids—Riya (8), Suraj (5), and Sujeet (3). The woman's husband, Ravi Sharma, was not at home during the time of the incident," it added. In the last phase of investigation, we reached out to Rauta Police Station's Station House Officer (SHO) Gyan Ranjan, who confirmed that the incident happened in Kilpara village in Purnea district. Subsequently, it was concluded that the video was from Bihar, not Bangladesh.

title: PTI Fact Check: Hindu idols unearthed in Karnataka falsely linked to mosque survey in UP's Sambhal; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Weeks after violent clashes over a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid in Uttar Pradesh' Sambhal claimed four lives, several social media users recently shared a collage claiming that it featured images of Hindu idols and artefacts found during the survey of the mosque. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the three of the four idols in the collage were those found in Karnataka in February this year, whereas the fourth image was taken from a shopping website. The collage of unrelated images was shared on social media with a false claim. Four people were killed after violence erupted in Sambhal last month during protests by the Muslim community against the survey of the mosque which was ordered by a court after a petition claimed that it was the site of the Harihar temple and sought permission to worship there. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 8 a collage of four images, claiming that 1,500-year-old idols, including Shivling, two idols of Lord Vishnu, and a Sudarshan Chakra, were unearthed during a survey of a mosque in Uttar Pradesh's Sambhal district. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the social media post. Investigation The Desk ran the four images separately through Google Lens and came across a news report by NDTV, on February 7, 2024. The news article featured a 1,000-year-old Vishnu idol and the Shivling recovered by the authorities in Karnataka's Raichur district during construction of a bridge. These images exactly matched two of the idols in the collage. Here's the link and screenshot of the news article posted on February 7, 2024. Below is a combination image, which shows that two of the idols in the viral collage are the same as those featured in the news report. To corroborate the details, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a PTI report carried by Hindustan Times in February 2024. The report confirmed that the idols were discovered near the Krishna River in Karnataka, and its feature image matches the ones in the viral collage. Here's the link and the screenshot of the article posted by Hindustan Times. Below is a combination image, which shows that the images featuring in the news report are the same as those in the viral collage. To trace the fourth image in the collage, depicting a Sudarshan Chakra, the Desk ran it through Google Lens and found the same image on shopping portal Indiamart. The artefact on sale was titled "Material: Brass Sudarshanachakra Kalasham, Temple." Here's the link to the webpage and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that three idols in the collage were discovered in Karnataka, while the fourth image came from a shopping website. The claim that these idols were found during a mosque survey in Sambhal, Uttar Pradesh, is false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Digitally altered video of spiritual content creator Abhinav Arora shared to falsely claim he was attacked by bull
content: New Delhi, Dec 18 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared video claiming that it showed 10-year-old spiritual content creator Abhinav Arora being attacked by a bull, while he was giving a sermon. The PTI Fact Check found in its investigation that the video was digitally altered using AI and was shared on social media with a false claim. The original video does not show Arora being attacked by the bull standing behind him. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 14 a video that showed 10-year-old spiritual content creator Abhinav Arora being attacked by a bull. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation To verify the authenticity of the viral video, the PTI Fact Check Desk scaned Abhinav Arora's Instagram account, with 948k followers and 2,990 posts. Here's the link to his Instagram account, and below is a screenshot of the same. On scanning his account, we found a video published on November 8 that matched the viral video's thumbnail and setting. In the video, Arora was seen completing his sermon without any interruption or attack by the bull standing behind. Here's the link to the original video and below is a screenshot of the same. Moreover, going through the investigation, the desk found multiple indications of the video clip of Arora to be digitally altered. For example, the desk found the part of the video clip to be more pixelated than the original version. Below is the screenshot of the comparison indicated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through True Media, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is the screenshot of the result. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of Abhinav Arora was digitally altered using AI.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of South Korean overbridge falsely shared as that of national highway in Jammu and Kashmir
content: New Delhi, Dec 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of an overbridge was recently shared on social media with users claiming it to be the 'Jammu and Kashmir National Highway' in India. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that it was the Yeongdong Hongseong Bridge/Yeongdong Expressway in the Gangwon-do Province of South Korea. The photo was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on November 29 a photo of an overbridge and claimed that it was the Jammu and Kashmir National Highway. "Beautiful view of Jammu National Highway India!!" read the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the image through Google Lens and found that it was shared by several other social media users, attributing it to numerous countries over the years, frequently being referred to as one of their most favoured tourist locations. The claims widely range from it being located in Pakistan, Nepal and Indonesia. A post was shared on 'X' (formerly known as Twitter) on October 14, 2020 claiming the bridge to be in Pakistan, a road connecting Haripur and Thakot. Here is the link and archive link . Below is the screenshot of the same. New Spotlight, a news magazine of Nepal, posted an article on June 22, 2022 with the feature image similar to the one in the viral post. Here is the link and archive link to the article and below is a screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a Korean commercial site, 'Woojung 365', which sells expressway coupon. The text, when translated to English, read: "Yeongdong Hongseong Bridge", and the photo featured the same overbridge. Here is the link and archive link to the webpage, and below is a screenshot of the same. We also came across a YouTube video uploaded by a Korean company named Meritz, on June 1, 2021. The Desk watched the video and found at 2:56 minutes that the visual was similar to the photo shared on social media. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk looked for the Yeongdong Expressway on Google Maps and found that the Street View of the map was similar to that of the viral image. Below is the screenshot of the Google Maps location. Below is a screenshot of the Street view: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral image was of Yeongdong Hongseong Bridge of South Korea, and not from Jammu and Kashmir.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo and videos from incidents dating back to 2022 and 2023 combined and falsely linked to man mocking cow
content: New Delhi, Dec 17 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared a video of a man sitting in a car and mocking a cow standing nearby, followed by visuals showing a purportedly injured man being dragged by the police, and saying 'cow is our mother'. The video also included a photo of a man sitting on the floor, with police personnel standing behind him. The users sharing the video claimed that a Muslim man was punished by the police for mocking the cow. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral video was a combination of two videos and a photo from unrelated incidents dating back 2022 and 2023, which was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user recently shared a video, claiming that it showed a Muslim man mocking a cow, and how he was thrashed by the police for that. "Eid hai, bach ke. Eid hai, Eid. As-salamu alaykum," says the man in the video. In the later part of it, he can be seen being dragged by the police and saying, "Cow is our Mother." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk reverse searched the keyframes of the video and found that the same video was posted by another Facebook user on November 7, 2024. "Abdul Bhai forgot that he is in Uttar Pradesh," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk then ran the keyframes of the first clip through Google Lens and found that the same video was shared by an Instagram user on October 12, who called for action against the man seen mocking the cow in the video. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: The Desk scanned the comment section and found a user claiming that the man in the video was a Hindu, named Nakul. Another user who shared the shared the video on September 19, also mentioned a screenshot of an Instagram account that had originally shared the cow-mocking video. The account, which goes by the username "@n___nakul_", stands deleted. Here is the link to the Instagram post, and below is a screenshot of the video which shows the Instagram profile of the now-deleted account of the accused. We also ran the image of the man and the cop standing behind through Google Lens and found the same photo featured in a Hindustan Times report published on July 1, 2023. According to the report, a case was filed against nine persons out of which two were arrested for allegedly throwing meat near a Hanuman temple on Gurugram-Faridabad Road. The image of a man and a police officer, as seen in the viral clip, is a cropped version of the same image. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image, comparing the photo in the viral clip with the photo in the news report. In the next part of investigation, the Desk through Google Lens a keyframe of the clip in which the man says "cow is our mother", and came across a video report by News18 UP Uttarakhand, uploaded on YouTube on October 28, 2022. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: The incident was also covered by Aaj Tak on October 28, 2022. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same Subsequently, it is clear that the photo and videos are from separate incidents that took place in 2022 and 2023.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: This video showing 'Hindu women rescued from Muslim man's house' is scripted; shared on social media with false communal claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with users claiming that it showed two people allegedly rescuing Hindu girls from a Muslim man's house. The video showed the girls crying and covered in bruises, who were allegedly kept in a cupboard after being abducted. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a scripted video was shared on social media as real with a false communal claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 15 a video, claiming that it showed several Hindu women being rescued from a Muslim man's house. The video was shared with the caption, "Muslim boys kidnap Hindu girls." Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and came across a YouTube video posted by a channel named 'Naveen Jangra' on February 12, 2023. The content in the video was the same as the viral clip. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the YouTube video. Below is a combination image, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as that of the YouTube channel. The Desk watched the video and found that it contains a disclaimer at the 22-second mark stating it should be consumed for "entertainment purpose only". Here's the screenshot of the disclaimer posted in the video. Further, to corroborate the details, the Desk also scanned through other videos uploaded on the YouTube channels and found many scripted videos like the viral clip. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was scripted and was shared as a real incident, with a false communal claim.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: 2-year-old video from Udaipur falsely shared as recent in name of gang war incident in Jaipur tunnel
content: New Delhi, Dec 19 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared a video claiming that a gang war broke out inside Jaipur's 'Ghat Ki Guni' tunnel. The video showed a mob attacking a few individuals and allegedly firing shots in the air. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the viral video is neither from Jaipur nor is related to any recent incident. The video is of a clash that broke out inside Chirwa Tunnel in Udaipur back in the year 2022. Claim An Instagram user shared on December 15 a video, claiming that it showed footage of a gang war that broke out inside Jaipur's 'Ghat Ki Guni' tunnel. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and came across a YouTube video published by a channel named 'News 18 Virals' on March 5, 2022. The content in the video was the same as the viral clip. However, its YouTube title stated that the video is of Udaipur's Chirwa tunnel and not of Jaipur, where more than half a dozen youths created a ruckus. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the Youtube video posted by the channel. Below is a combination image, which shows that the content in the viral video is the same as that of the YouTube channel. To corroborate the details, the Desk made a customized keyword search and found a report published around the development by the Rajasthan vertical of the Zee News portal. According to the news report also, the incident dates back to March 2022, when some youths created a ruckus in the Chirwa tunnel located at the Udaipur Nathdwara National Highway. Here's the link and screenshot of the news report published. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk through customized keyword search found a social media post made by the official handle of the Jaipur Police. In a post on X (formerly Twitter), the Jaipur Police had back stated that, "The video is not of the Ghat Ki Guni tunnel; no such incident has occurred in Jaipur." Here's the link and screenshot of the post made by the Jaipur Police. Meanwhile, regarding the development, the Udaipur police back in the year 2022 had also issued a statement. Then, in a post on X (formerly Twitter), the Udaipur Police vehemently dismissed if any firing incident had occurred in the tunnel. However, it was mentioned that further investigation into the viral video was underway. Here's the link and screenshot of the social media post by the Udaipur Police. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral incident of the clashes that broke out inside a tunnel in Rajasthan is of Udaipur. The claim that a gang war broke out inside the 'Ghat Ki Guni' tunnel in Jaipur is misleading.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming Pride Flags permanently banned at FIFA Club World Cup 2025 are fake
content: New Delhi, Dec 18 (Kaushiki Goel/ Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A photo has been viral on several social media platforms claiming that Pride Flags have been forever banned at FIFA Club World Cup 2025. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that it was originally shared by a website 'SPACEXMANIA' in their 'Satire' category and no such information was found on the official website of FIFA. The photo was shared with a false claim on various websites. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 8, 2024 a collage of two pictures where in one of the pictures a man is seen holding the Pride Flag, while the other picture was that of a MetLife stadium, in New Jersey. "BREAKING: Pride Flags Baппed Forever At FIFA Clυb World Cυp 2025 – 'No More Woke Pride'," the post read. Here is the link and archive link . Below is the screenshot of the same. Another post was shared on Threads 6 days ago with the similar caption as the above facebook post. Here is the link and archive link . Below is the screenshot of the same. Another Facebook post read "Soccer finally does something worth watching". This post was shared on December 12, 2024. Here is the link and archive link . Below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a website named 'SPACEXMANIA' that had uploaded an article on November 15, 2024 in the Satire category about the supposed ban. "MLS stadium issues permanent ban on pride flags for FIFA Club World Cup 2025," the headline read. Here is the link to the article. Below is the screenshot of same. Furthermore, the Desk also reached out to the Media Team of FIFA via email. "Please note that there is no validity to this report you mention. The source is a satirical site, which clearly states at the bottom of the story that it is not true," said Will Shand, the Media Relations Officer, FIFA. When we looked through the official website and pages of the FIFA no data was found to corroborate the claims. The official document containing all the information about the tournament- qualified teams, groups, fixtures, competition format, hosts, tickets, etc was also scanned but there was no mention of the Pride Flags being banned. Here is the link . Below is the screenshot of the same. In the next part of the investigation the official social media handles were checked and FIFA's website and press releases were also studied but no such announcements were published by them. Here is the link to FIFA's social media pages: Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/fifa/ 'X' (formerly known as twitter): https://x.com/fifacom Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/fifa/ YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@fifa/streams Official website: https://www.fifa.com/en Press release: https://inside.fifa.com/about-fifa/organisation/media/all-media-releases The FIFA Club World Cup 2025 has been scheduled to be held in the US between June and July in the following year. The 2034 FIFA World CUP will be held in South Africa. The BRICS News on December 18 tweeted, "Saudi Arabia says LGBTQ fans are "safe and welcome" at the 2034 FIFA World Cup." "England's Football Association said it had received assurances from Saudi Arabia that LGBTQ fans would be "safe and welcome" at the 2034 World Cup, explaining its support for the successful bid from the Gulf state," the tweet further read. Here is the link . Below is the screenshot of the tweet. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral post was misleading and does not hold any substance.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming 'One Nation One Election' Bill got Lok Sabha nod are false; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 19 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Amid the ongoing buzz and debate over the bills for simultaneous polls in India, several social media users recently shared posts claiming that the One Nation One Election Bill was passed in the Lok Sabha. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. While the text on the photo shared in the viral social media posts rightly mentioned that 269 votes were cast in favour of the bills and 198 against them, the bills were not passed in the Lok Sabha. The two bills –The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 and The Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024 – that lay down the mechanism to hold simultaneous elections in the country were introduced in Lok Sabha on Tuesday. Later, the government referred One Nation One Election (ONOE) bills to Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) after a fiery debate in the Parliament in which the opposition termed the move "dictatorial". Claim A Facebook user shared on December 17, a photo from the inside of the parliament claiming that the 'One Nation, One Election' Bill passed in Lok Sabha with 269 votes. "MODI 3.0: Turning commitments into Reality.The #OneNationOneElection Bill passes in Lok Sabha with 269 votes," the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found that the Lok Sabha did not pass the "One Nation, One Election" Bill on December 17, 2024. Instead, in order to accomplish "One Nation, One Election," the Lok Sabha voted a motion with a simple majority for the two bills- "The Constitution 129th Amendment Bill 2024" and "The Union Territories Laws Amendment Bill 2024." The Desk came across a PTI report carried by Kashmir Observer on December 17, whose headline read: "One Nation One Election bills introduced in Lok Sabha; opposition terms move 'dictatorial'". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk came across an NDTV report, published on Dec 17, whose headline read: '31 Members, 90-Day Term: What We Know About 'One Nation, One Poll' Committee'. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Live Law also published an article on December 17. "Centre Introduces Bills In Lok Sabha For 'One Nation One Election'; Law Minister Agrees For Examination By Joint Parliamentary Committee," the headline read. Here is the link to the report. In the next part of the investigation, we went through the parliamentary proceedings from December 17, 2024, where it is clearly mentioned that the two Bills were introduced, and not passed in the Lok Sabha. Here is the link to the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs website and below is a screenshot of the same: Here are the links for the 'The Constitution 129th Amendment Bill 2024' and 'The Union Territories Laws Amendment Bill 2024,' introduced in the Lok Sabha – https://sansad.in/getFile/BillsTexts/LSBillTexts/Asintroduced/const%20amdt1217202425225PM.pdf?source=legislation , https://sansad.in/getFile/BillsTexts/LSBillTexts/Asintroduced/ut1217202425100PM.pdf?source=legislation Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the Lok Sabha did not pass the 'One Nation, One Election' bills. Instead, the two bills for simultaneous polls were introduced in the Lok Sabha and later referred to the JPC.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Did South Africa remove passport requirement for Nigerian travellers? No, President Ramaphosa's speech misinterpreted and misleadingly shared on social media
content: New Delhi, Dec 20 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Amidst the tensions between South Africa and Nigeria, a video recently went viral on social media, claiming that South Africa's President Cyril Ramaphosa announced that Nigerian tourists won't need to submit their passports for visa. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigationRamaphosa's speech was misinterpreted and wasshared on social media with a misleading claim. The President was talking about the online VISA process, which requires uploading a certified passport copy rather than a physical one — upon approval, the physical document still needs to be presented. The process was rolled out in 2019 and includes more than 30 countries, not just Nigeria. Claim An 'X' (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 3 a clipping of South African President Matamela Cyril Ramaphosa at the South Africa and Nigeria Bi-National Commission, claiming that Nigerian travellers would not need to submit their passports for a visa. "South Africa to ease visa rules to boost trade with Nigeria. President Cyril Ramaphosa announced efforts to introduce a simplified five-year multiple-entry visa for Nigerian tourists, removing the requirement to submit passports. He also stressed the importance of enhancing trade, stating, we want Nigerian products on South African shelves," read the post. Here is the link and archive link . Below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran one of the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and came across another Facebook post, which carried a purported press release along with a photo of Ramaphosa with Nigerian President Bola Tinubu. Here is the link and archive link . Below is the screenshot of the same. The Desk foremost looked for the official press briefing of President Cyril Ramaphosa and came across the original video that was uploaded on the YouTube channel 'The Presidency of the Republic of South Africa' on December 3, 2024. The Desk watched the video and at 4:51 minutes, in which the President said, "Our efforts to create a favourable environment include our simplified visa process for Nigerian business people to travel to South Africa. Qualifying Nigerian business people can be granted a five-year multiple entry VISA". At an event attended by the Nigerian counterpart Bola Tinubu, he further added, "In addition, tourists from Nigeria are now able to apply for a visa without even submitting a passport." Here is the link Below is the screenshot of the same. The day following the incident, South Africa's president issued a statement clarifying the remarks in response to the public outcry. "Prospective travellers can apply for their visas without submitting their passports along with their applications – at the time of application, they are only required to submit certified copies of the biopage of their passports, and their actual passports should also be availed during the application process for verification and confirmation," read the statement. It further read, "Once a visa has been approved, they are required to submit their passports for the process to be completed and for the visa to be affixed in the passport." Here is the link to the press release issued by the South African President, whose headline read: "Statement On Simplified Visa Process For Nigerian Visitors". Below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across an article from Business Day. "South Africa e-visa fully operational in Nigeria, says Ndlovu," the headline read. Here is the link . Below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk found that South African President Cyril Ramaphosa's speech was misinterpreted and that he was talking about the online VISA process.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming name change of JNU to Dr BR Ambedkar University are fake; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared posts claiming that the name of Jawaharlal Nehru University in Delhi was changed to Dr BR Ambedkar University. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the claim was fake. No such announcement was made by the Ministry of Education. The viral posts came amid the political slugfest that erupted after Home Minister Amit Shah's statement on BR Ambedkar in the Rajya Sabha during a debate on the 75th year of the adoption of the Indian Constitution. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 19 a post, claiming that Jawaharlal Nehru University was renamed to Dr BR Ambedkar University. The caption read: "Big Breaking BJP changed the name of Jawaharlal Nehru University to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar University" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found no information regarding the viral claims being circulated on social media. However, the Desk came across a PTI report carried by The Economic Times on Feb 18, 2021, whose headline read: "No proposal for JNU name change: Ramesh Pokhriyal Nishank" The statement came when the then BJP General Secretary CT Ravi had proposed in 2020 a name change of the JNU after Swami Vivekananda. On this, the then Union Education Minister Ramesh Pokhriyal had stated that there was no proposal to change JNU's name. Here is the link to the article and below is a screenshot of the same. Additionally, the Desk went through the website of Ministry of Education and official X handle of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, but we couldn't find any information about JNU's name change. https://www.education.gov.in/ https://x.com/dpradhanbjp The Desk also cross-checked on for any announcements or press releases on JNU's website, but nothing substantial was found. Here is the link to the website. In the next part of investigation, the Desk reached out to the senior officials of JNU, who categorially rejected the claim made in social media posts. "This is completely false and there is no truth to it. Neither the Centre nor the Ministry has ever proposed changing the name of JNU. Such rumours, often spread by unverified accounts, should not be given any importance as they are intended to stir controversy around JNU," said a senior varsity official on condition of anonymity. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim made in social media posts was fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Starbucks to quit Indian market? No, claim made in social media is false
content: New Delhi, Dec 21 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiplesocial media users recently claimed that Starbucks, the international coffeehouse chain,was about to exit the Indian market. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be fake. The claim originated from reports suggesting that the company was planning to exit the Indian market amid high operating costs and low profitability in the country. Starbucks entered India in 2012 through a partnership with Tata Consumer Products. Claim A Facebook page shared on December 19 a post claiming that Starbucks was about to exit the Indian market. The caption of the post read: "Starbucks to Exit India" Here is the link and archive link to the post. Below is a screenshot of the same. An X (formerly Twitter) user had also shared a post on December 19, along with the screenshot of an article published by 'The Philox'. The caption of the post as well as the headline of the purported article read, "Starbucks to exit India due to high costs, bad taste, and mounting losses". Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found the article published in The Philox. After a thorough read, the news piece did not consist of quotes or official statements neither from Starbucks nor from TATA Consumer Products. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. Taking cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by Hindustan Times, which quoted Tata Consumer Products refuting the claim. The headline read: "Starbucks is not exiting India: Tata Consumer denies 'baseless' report of coffee chain quitting country". Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: "Starbucks is fully committed to the Indian market. Any statements suggesting otherwise are false. TATA Starbucks currently operates more than 470 stores in 76 cities across India, which continues to be a key growth market for Starbucks globally," said Starbucks as quoted by Hindstan Times in the report. The report further quoted TCPL denying the possibility of exiting India in a letter titled "Clarification on News Article Titled - Starbucks to Exit India Due to High Costs, Bad Taste, and Mounting Losses." In the next part of the investigation,we went through National Stock Exchange's (NSE) website and found the press statement released on December 19, 2024. Here is the link to NSE's website The statement read: 'The Company would like to state that the information in the said article is baseless' Here is the link and below is the screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Starbucks was not quitting the Indian market.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated video claiming Rahul Gandhi broke coconuts with his hand shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 22 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Amid reports of an investigation of the claim that Congress leader Rahul Gandhi allegedly pushed and injured BJP MPs during a reported scuffle in Parliament, a video has gone viral on social media that claims Gandhi broke over 140 coconuts in seconds. Social media users linked the video to the Parliament scuffle, speculating about the potential impact on BJP MPs if the allegation against the Congress leader was true. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video shared in the social media was AI-generated. The original footage, posted on the official Guinness World Records YouTube channel on December 20, 2017, features Abheesh P. Dominic from Kerala breaking 122 coconuts to set a world record. Claim A Facebook user on December 21 shared a video of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, where he was seen breaking over 140 coconuts with one hand in a matter of a few seconds. Linking it to the assault allegations in Parliament, the user captioned Gandhi's video with a dig at BJP MPs, stating, "What if they (BJP MPs) had really been pushed?" Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the keyframes of the viral video through Google Lens and came across a report published by SAMYAM TAMIL, a Tamil news brand from Times Internet, on December 10, 2019. The video attached in the news report matched the viral video's background and setting, except to a matter that instead of Rahul Gandhi, who was seen breaking open the coconuts with one hand, another man had been featured. Significantly, the news report was titled, "25 seconds...A young man breaks 140 coconuts!' Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the news report. Moreover, going through the investigation, the desk found multiple indications of the video clip of Rahul Gandhi to be digitally altered. For example, the Desk found the part of Rahul Gandhi in the video clip to be more forcefully added than the original version. Below is the screenshot of the comparison indicated. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the image through True Media, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below is the screenshot of the result. Further, to trace the original video, featuring a man breaking a record number of coconuts, the desk made a customized keyword search on Google and found out about a report published by the official website of the Guinness World Record on December 20, 2017. The report featured the same man as seen in the video published by the SAMYAM TAMIL news portal. According to the same, the man has been identified as Abheesh P. Dominic, who broke open 122 coconuts to beat the previous record of 118 that had stood since 2011. Here's the link and screenshot of the report published by Guinness World Record. Further, the YouTube link of the development, which has also been attached to the report, showed Abheesh P. Dominic scripting another world record by breaking over 122 coconuts with one hand. Here's the link and screenshot of the post. Subsequently, the desk concluded that the viral video of Rahul Gandhi was digitally altered using AI.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: AI-generated photos of Sania Mirza with Mohammed Shami shared on social media with a false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 23 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check): Two purported photos of Indian tennis star Sania Mirza with cricketer Mohammed Shami recently went viral, with the claim that they were clicked in Dubai and to insinuate that the two were in a relationship. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photos shared on social media were fake; AI-generated photos were shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 21 two purported photos of Sania Mirza and Mohammed Shami, and claimed that they were clicked in Dubai. The post insinuated that the two were in a relationship. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photos through Google Lens and found that they were shared by several other social media users as well. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of one such Instagram post. The Desk then ran a customized keyword search on Google but could not find any authentic report carrying the viral images. In the next part of investigation, the Desk closely watched the viral images and noticed several discrepancies, which suggested that it may be fake or AI-generated. For instance, the faces of the two in the viral image looked forcefully added. Below is a photo highlighting the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the combination of photos through True Media, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below are the screenshots of the results: During our investigation, we also came across a report by Hindustan Times, where Shami refuted the rumours about his supposed marriage to Sania Mirza. Here's the link to the news report and below is a screenshot of the same. "It is weird and done purposely for some lame fun. But what can be done? If I open my phone, then I could see those memes. But I would only like to say I think that memes are made for fun, but if they are related to someone's life, then you must think about it and then share such things. These people share from unverified pages and get away by saying anything and everything," the report quoted Shami as saying. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photos of Sania Mirza and Mohammed Shami shared on social media to claim they were in a relationship are fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Pratyush Ranjan
title: PTI Fact Check: Videos of 2020 Beirut Port explosion falsely shared in name of recent LPG tanker-truck crash in Jaipur
content: New Delhi, Dec 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Pratyush Ranjan, PTI Fact Check ): Several social media users shared videos of explosions and their aftermath, claiming they were from Jaipur, where an LPG tanker collided with a truck while making a U-turn on the Jaipur-Ajmer highway on December 20, 2024.
