However, after investigating the matter, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the videos circulating on social media actually showed a chemical explosion that occurred at the Beirut Port in 2020. On August 4, 2020, a massive explosion rocked Beirut's port, resulting in the loss of over 150 lives, and the recent LPG tanketr-truck crash near Bhankrota on the Jaipur-Ajmer highway on December 20, 2024, claimed the lives of more than 10 people. Claim An Instagram account shared a post on December 22, claiming that the video shows visuals of the Jaipur tanker collision. The video had 2,46,937 likes. Here is the link and archive link , and the screenshot is below. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found several other users had shared visuals claiming it to be from Jaipur-Ajmer highway incident site. The same links can be seen here and here , and their archived link can be found here and here , respectively. On commencing the investigation the Desk using InVid tool conducted a reverse image search of the keyframes of the video and discovered several news stories that featured the same images from the viral video. A report from The Guardian published four years ago shows several pictures of the blast that hit Beirut dock. Here is the link , and below is the screenshot. It also consists of visuals of the viral video being circulated as the Jaipur LPG tanker-trck crash. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found another article published in The Telegraph featuring similar video clips. Here is the link , and below is the screenshot of the article. The Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found a YouTube video posted by Sky News four years ago, showing the Beirut blast's raw footage. Here is the link , and below is the screenshot. To corroborate the details, the Desk reviewed various news articles by several media houses and came across one such piece by the Times of India, which consisted of a montage of videos from the deadly attack in the capital of Lebanon. Here is the link , and below is the screenshot. In the subsequent part of the investigation, analysing a Facebook post put out on December 21, using the InVid tool conducted a reverse image search of the keyframes of the video. A news article by Mirror published on August 5, 2020 was foud. The Headline read: "Beirut explosion: Horrifying videos capture moment deadly blast smashes into cars and people." Here is the link , and below is the screenshot. Below is a combination image comparing the photo in the viral clip with the real one. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the visuals of the Beirut blast were shared from different places and angles than those of the Jaipur, where an LPG tanker collided with a truck while making a U-turn on the Jaipur-Ajmer highway on Dec 20.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2019 Amul ad digitally altered and shared on social media to falsely claim it mocked Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi
content: New Delhi, Dec 23 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A photo of a purported advertisement banner of Amul was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it featured cartoons depicting Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and mocked the Congress party. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that an old advertisement by Amul was digitally altered to create the viral image, which was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 17 a photo of a purported billboard ad by Amul, claiming that it featured Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra to mock Congress party. "Top class Advt with real meaning what happened and is happening," read the caption of the post. The Hindi text on the banner translated to: "Grandfather ate, grandmother ate, father ate, mother ate and sister you also eat and call brother-in-law." It is used to take a dig at the Gandhi family insinuating the alleged corruption by the family members. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. In the next part of investigation, the Desk performed a customised keyword search and came across an advertisement shared by the company on its X (formerly Twitter) accounton January 24, 2019. Back then, the company had actually run an ad regarding Priyanka Gandhi's entry into mainstream politics when she was appointed as the general secretary of the Congress UP East. It featured cartoons of Priyanka Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, but no slogan was mentioned on it. Here is the link and archive link to Amul's ad, and below is its screenshot. Below is a combination image, comparing the photo in the viral clip with the photo in the news report. Furthermore, we found that the same edited photo had gone viral in 2019 and the company had termed it "fake". "Dear Sir, It is a fake post. Amul has not released this Topical. The original topical is shared below" Here is the link and archive link , and below is the screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old advertisement by Amul was digitally altered and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Pakistani woman being thrashed shared on social media giving it communal spin; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A video of a woman being thrashed outside a court was recently shared on social media with claims that she was a Hindu woman beaten by Muslim lawyers in Pakistan. According to the post, the woman was attacked for trying to highlight in court that local police were refusing to register a case against the kidnappers and rapists of her minor sister. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the woman was a Pakistani national, identified as Amrit Shahzadi. According to Pakistan's local daily, Dawn, she visited a court in Shakargarh in October 2019 in connection with a land dispute. But a group of people, including lawyers, thrashed her and her cousin Abdul Qayyum for pursuing the case. The claim in social media post was false. Claim An X user shared on December 21 a video of a woman being thrashed by Muslim lawyers outside a local court in Pakistan. The caption of the post identifies the woman as a Hindu who was kicked and punched by Muslim lawyers as she tried to draw the attention of the court towards the fact that Pakistani police are not registering a case against the kidnappers and rapists of her minor sister. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk uploaded the video in the InVid tool and found several keyframes of the video. Continuing the investigation, we searched for the details of the keyframes through Google Lens and found some news articles published on the clash incident. According to the Times of India news website, the incident reportedly took place at Shakargarh in Pakistan in 2019, where a woman identified as Amrat Shahzadi had appeared in a court for a hearing; however, she was attacked by a lawyer there. The lawyer, too, in their defence, had alleged that the woman attacked them first. Here's the link and screenshot of the post. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found an article published by Dawn, Pakistan's daily news outlet in 2019. The news report identified the woman as Amrit Shahzadi, a resident of Shahpur Bhangu village in Pakistan. In its report, the Dawn mentioned that Shahzadi and his brother Abdul Qayyum visited a court in Shakargarh concerning a land dispute case but were thrashed there by a group of people, including lawyers, for pursuing it. Here's the link and screenshot of Dawn's news article. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Pakistan's Shakargarh court incident, where lawyers thrashed a woman outside a court for reportedly pursuing a land dispute case, was falsely shared with a communal spin.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of clash between two groups at Bangladesh's Baitul Mukarram mosque shared on social media with false claim; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming that it showed a tussle between two groups of Tablighi Jamaat members, that allegedly broke out over "who would perform Halala with a Bangladeshi woman". It was further claimed that one group supported India's Tablighi Jamaat chief Maulana Saad, while the other backed Maulana Tariq Jameel, the chief of Pakistani Tablighi Jamaat. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be false. The video was actually of clashes that broke out between followers of the former and current Khatibs of Bangladesh's national mosque, Baitul Mukarram, on September 20, 2024. The old video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 21 a video, claiming that it showed a fight between two groups of Tablighi Jamaat, one from India and the other from Pakistan, over who would perform Halala with a Bangladeshi woman. "A total of 12 people have died so far in the incident," it claimed. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an Instagram post by 'Briefly by NEWJ', which was shared on September 21, 2024. We found that the post carried the same video as shared on social media. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the video. According to the details published by NEWJ, "The video showed a violent clash broke out at Dhaka's Mukarram National Mosque, leaving at least 50 people injured. The confrontation occurred between followers of the mosque's former Khatib, Mufti Ruhul Amin, and current Khatib, Mufti Waliur Rahman Khan, during Friday's sermon." Below is also a combination image, which shows that the video shared on social media was the same as the one shared by NEWJ in September 2024. To further corroborate the details, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a news report by Bangladeshi daily, The Dhaka Tribune, on September 20, 2024. The report confirmed that before Friday prayers, a violent clash erupted between followers of the current and former Khatibs of the mosque, resulting in a scuffle and damage to property. A total of 50 people also suffered injuries in the incident. Here's the link and screenshot of the news article published by Dhaka Tribune. "According to sources, the current Khatib, Mufti Waliur Rahman Khan, was delivering a sermon when the former Khatib, Mufti Ruhul Amin, arrived at the mosque with his followers and attempted to take the microphone. This led to a confrontation between the followers of both Khatibs, resulting in physical altercations. Several people were injured, and many worshippers were disturbed by the chaos, prompting some to leave the mosque," read a section of the report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old and unrelated video from Bangladesh was shared on social media as recent with a false communal claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: Clipped video of Kejriwal's 2012 speech shared on social media to falsely claim that he mocked Constitution and its makers
content: New Delhi, Dec 24 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ) : Amid the ongoing political debate over the Constitution and Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar, a video of Aam Aadmi Party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal recently was recently shared on social media with users claiming that he insulted the Constitution and its makers. In the viral clip, Kejriwal can be heard saying, "We were sitting... someone said whoever wrote the Constitution must have been drunk while doing it." However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found that a clipped video from his speech dating back to 2012 was taken out of context and shared on social media with a false claim. In the original video, Kejriwal was actually criticising the internal constitution of the Congress party, and not that of India. The video went viral on social media amid the ongoing opposition uproar over Union Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks on Ambedkar during his speech on the Constitution in the recently concluded Winter Session of the Parliament. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 24 a video of AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal and claimed that he disrespected the Constitution and its makers in it. "आम आदमी पार्टी के मुखिया का ये मुस्कान भरा वीडियो मिला..जिसको सुनकर हर कोई ऐसे बहुरूपिये का असली रंग देख पायेगा! (Found this smiling video of the Aam Aadmi Party chief... after listening to which everyone will be able to see the true colours of such an impostor!)," read the caption of the post. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Notably, the video was majorly shared by BJP leaders and several others associated with the party, including party MP Manoj Tiwari. Here are the links ( here and here ) and archive links ( here and here ) to two posts, and below are screenshots of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by AAP Rajasthan spokesperson Devender Yadav, who replied to one of the users who shared the viral video. Yadav shared a longer, unedited version of Kejriwal's statement. "कांग्रेस के समर्थन में उतरे भाजपाई. ये है पूरा असली विडियो! बाबा साहब के भक्त अरविंद केजरीवालजी ने कहा था "कांग्रेस का संविधान जिसने लिखा, उसने दारू पीकर लिखा होगा" भाजपा वाले उसे काटकर फर्जी वीडियो चला रहे है। @PunjabPoliceIndसबके खिलाफ कार्रवाई करेगी।झूठनहीं,सचफैलाओ," read the post by Yadav. An English translation of the post read: "BJP members came out in support of Congress.This is the real video!Daba Saheb's devotee Arvind Kejriwal had said "The one who wrote the constitution of Congress must have written it after drinking alcohol"BJP people are cutting it and running a fake video.@PunjabPoliceInd. Will take action against everyone.Spread the truth, not lies." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the extended video, Kejriwal was heard saying: "I have read the constitution of all political parties. The constitution of the Congress Party says that no Congress worker will consume alcohol... We were sitting... Somebody said whoever wrote the constitution must have done it after drinking alcohol." In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across the 17-minute-long original video, uploaded to the official YouTube channel of the Aam Aadmi Party on December 3, 2012. According to the video's description, Kejriwal made this speech at Raj Ghat in New Delhi on November 25, 2012. Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: The complete remark can be heard at 4:35-minute timestamp. We found that Kejriwal delivered the speech a day before the official launch of Aam Aadmi Party on November 26, 2012. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a 12-year-old speech of Kejriwal was clipped and shared on social media with a false claim.

title: PTI Fact Check: No, Cristiano Ronaldo has not converted to Islam; AI-generated photos shared on social media with fake claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 24 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared several photos, claiming that they showed star football player Cristiano Ronaldo with his alleged wife Georgina Rodriguez. The users also claimed Ronaldo had converted to Islam and the photos were from their visit to Haram Sharif in Mecca, where they offered namaz. In its investigation, however, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photos shared on social media were fake. AI-generated photos were shared as real with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 21 multiple photos of legendary football player Cristiano Ronaldo along with his alleged wife, Georgina Rodriguez. In the post, which has garnered over 247.5k views so far, the user claimed that the former had accepted Islam and offered namaz with Rodriguez at Haram Sharif in Mecca. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the viral photos through Google Lens and found that they were shared by several other social media users as well. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of one such Facebook post. The Desk then ran a customized keyword search on Google, but could not find any authentic report on the viral images or on the claim that Ronaldo had accepted Islam. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk closely watched the viral images and noticed several discrepancies, which suggested that they may be fake or AI-generated. For instance, the fingers of Ronaldo look disfigured or abnormal, along with blurred faces in the background. Below is a photo highlighting the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk ran the combination of photos through True Media, an AI detection tool, which suggested a substantial presence of AI-generated or deepfake content. Below are the screenshots of the results: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the photos of Cristiano Ronaldo along with Georgina Rodriguez shared on social media were fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Tirumala Tirupati Temple's replica falsely shared on social media as visuals of original temple's sanctum sanctorum; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 24 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video recently shared on social media claimed to show the inside visuals from the Tirumala Tirupati temple in Andhra Pradesh. The users shared the video claiming that it was shot during the Covid period. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. The video actually showed the replica of the famous temple. Notably, pilgrims are prohibited from taking any electronic items into the temple as part of the strict security measures. These include mobile phones and cameras. Claim A Facebook usershared on December 21 a video, claiming that it showed the inside visuals from the Tirupati temple (Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple) in Andhra Pradesh's Tirupati district. The caption read: "Tirupathi Perumal's unseen complete live Ekantha Darshan. Do visit. Real video shoot at Thirupati Temple in corona time see & feel happy. May God bless you all" Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an article published by The Hindu on June 13, 2016, whose headline read: "Replica of Tirumala temple in disarray" Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. "A replica of the Sri Venkateswara temple at Tirumala, commissioned to serve as a model for film shootings and TV programmes, lies in a shambles at Alipiri. The model of the temple (namoonaaalayam) has rather become an eyesore in the otherwise pristine locality at the foot of the Tirumala hills," read the article. The cover photo of the news piece was similar to that from the viral video. Below is a combining image of the same. Taking cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across a video shared by a Facebook user, which carried visuals similar to those seen in the viral video. The caption of the Facebook post shared by a user - 'Trip Tirupati' which garnered around 28k views, read: "Srivari Namuna Aalayam (Tirumala Replica Temple) at Tirupati near Alipiri." Here is the link and archive link of the video. Below is a combination image, comparing the visuals of the viral video with the one posted on YouTube. Here is another combination image of the viral video and YouTube video. In the subsequent part of the investigation, we performed a keyword search on YouTube that landed us on a video posted by National Geographic India, dated 13 July 2023. The title of the video read: "The Replica Temple? | Inside Tirumala Tirupati | National Geographic" CEO, Sri Venkateswara Bhakthi Channel, Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams, AV Narasimha Rao had extensively talked about the formation of the replica temple and how the devotees can benefit from it. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. According to the information by National Geographic India, the NamoonaAlayam, meaning "replica temple", is a replica of the original Tirumala constructed in 2008 for those devotees who are unable to reach the real idol. The Desk also scanned the official website of TTD and found a press release on the replica of the temple. It was published on September 15, 2015. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. Taking cue from the fact that pilgrims are prohibited from bringing electronic devices inside, the Desk performed a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by The Times of India, published in 2020. The headline of the article read: "TTD chairman clarifies no video taken inside sanctum sanctorum at Tirumala temple" Additionally, on reading the article further it came to our knowledge that similar videos of the 'NamoonaAlayam' (replica temple) were shared back then, to which the Chairman of TTD clarified that no video was allowed to be taken inside the sanctum sanctorum of the Lord Venkateswara temple, and underlined that the purported videos were circulated by mischief mongers on social media platforms. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the article. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was of a replica temple, and not the real Lord Venkateswara temple itself.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photos from Karnataka Assembly shared on social media to falsely claim that Ambedkar's photo was placed on opposition benches in Parliament; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 25 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a post claiming that Dr BR Ambedkar's photo was placed on opposition leaders' seats in the Parliament as a form of protest against Union Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks. The viral posts came amid the political slugfest that erupted with Shah's remarks on BR Ambedkar in the Rajya Sabha during a debate on the 75th year of the adoption of the Indian Constitution. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found in its investigation that the claim was false as the viral photos were from the Karnataka Assembly, and not the Parliament. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user 'Luv Datta #INC' shared on December 19 a post claiming that Dr BR Ambedkar's photoswere places on every opposition member's bench in the Rajya Sabha. "Baba Sahab Ambedkar's photo on each & every Opposition bench in Rajya Sabha. Jai Bheem" Here is the link and archive link , and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk used ran the viral photos through Google Lens and found that several other users had shared the same photo with similar claims. The links to two such posts can be found here and here , and the archive links of the same can be viewed here and here . In the next part of investigation, the Desk performed a customised keyword search and came across news reports published by Hindustan Times, One India and The News Minute, regarding the viral photos. The headline of the Hindustan Times report dated December 19, read: "Ambedkar photos on benches, chants in the air: Karnataka Assembly erupts over Amit Shah's remarks" Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. The links for the other two articles can be viewed here and here The Desk then went through the official X handle of Karnataka Congress and came across a post shared on December 19. The post carried the same photos as shared in the viral social media posts. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Below is the combination image, show the difference in the settings depicted in the viral photo to that of the Rajya Sabha. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that photos from Karnataka Legislative Assembly were falsely shared as visuals from inside the Parliament.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Telangana Police did not announce any discount on pending traffic challans in Dec 2024; viral social media claim is false
content: New Delhi, Dec 25 (Kaushiki Goel/ Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users recently shared posts claiming that Telangana Police had announced special discount to help citizens clear their pending traffic challans. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that neither Telangana Police nor Hyderabad Traffic Police had made any such announcement, and the claim shared on social media was fake. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 24 a post, claiming that Telangana Police have given a big discount on pending traffic challans to help the citizens. Moreover, it mentioned that the offer was valid from December 26 to January 10 and also provided a link to the website for clearing the challans online. The caption of the post read: "The Telangana police have announced a special discount to help citizens clear their pending traffic challans. Citizens are encouraged to make use of this opportunity: Two-Wheelers: 80% discount on pending fines. For instance, if the fine is ₹700, you only need to pay ₹140. Cars (Private): 60% discount. If the fine is ₹2000, you will pay ₹800. This offer is valid from December 26 to January 10. Citizens can clear their challans online through the official website: echallan.tspolice.gov.in," Here is the link and archive link and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk ran the viral photo through Google Lens and found that another user had shared the photo with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link of the same. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but did not find any authentic report backing the claim. However, on further scanning the search results, we came across news reports from December last year, which mentioned that Telangana Police had announced similar discount offer back then. One such report was published by WION in December 2023, whose headline read: "Telangana offers up to 90% discount on traffic challans for violators, here is how to avail" Here is the link and archive link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same. The article read: "Under the scheme, those with pending unpaid challans or fines can avail of up to 90 per cent discounts. People can get their fines cleared from the E-challan website from December 26 till January 10, 2024, officials were quoted as saying by the Hindustan Times." Additionally, even Business Standard had put out an article, whose headline read: "90% discount on pending traffic challans in this state: Details here" Here is link and archive link to the article. In the subsequent part of the investigation, we also scanned the official websites and came across a post on X (formerly known as Twitter) by Hyderabad Traffic Police. They categorically mentioned that a fake message was going viral regarding discount on pending traffic challans. The caption read: "A Fake message, discount on pendingTraffic challans getting viral in social media. It's a request to Netizen's/Citizen's, Don't believe such messages and Do not spread rumors without a valid proof." Here is the link and archive link , and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that neither Telangana Police nor Telangana Hyderabad Police had recently announced any discount for citizens on pending traffic challans.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming three Indian diplomats killed in attack in Afghanistan's Jalalabad are fake
content: New Delhi, Dec 25 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared posts claiming that three high-ranking Indian diplomats were killed in an attack on Indian consulate vehicle in Afghanistan's Jalalabad on December 24. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be false. In fact, an Afghan national working at the Indian consulate in Jalalabad sustained injuries when unidentified persons opened fire at his vehicle the same day. Notably, India had long closed operations at the Indian consulate in Jalalabad post the fall of the Ashraf Ghani government. Only a number of local staffers are presently working at the mission. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on December 24 claimed that three high-ranking Indian diplomats were killed in an attack in Afghanistan's Jalalabad. The post has garnered over 20k views so far. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation On running the viral screenshot through Google Lens, the Desk found that similar claim was shared by several other social media users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Below is the screenshot of one such post by a user on X (formerly Twitter). In the next part of investigation, the Desk carried out a customised keyword search on Google, but could not find any authentic news report, substantiating the viral claim. However, the search results led us to a PTI report carried by The Print on December 24, whose headline read: "Afghan staffer at Indian consulate in Jalalabad injured in attack". Here is the link to the post: "An Afghan national working at the Indian consulate in Jalalabad sustained injuries on Tuesday when unidentified persons opened fire at his vehicle, people familiar with the matter said," read a section of the report. It further stated that India had closed operations at the consulate around three-and-a-half years back but a number of local staffers were working at the mission. On further scanning the search results, we came across another report on the incident by Hindustan Times. Here's the link and screenshot of the news report. None of the reports mentioned anything about any casualty or any Indian official suffering injuries in the attack. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim of three Indian officials being killed in an attack in Afghanistan's Jalalabad was fake.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Photo of PM Modi attending Christmas celebrations at Union Minister George Kurian's residence falsely shared claiming event celebrated in Parliament
content: New Delhi, Dec 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A photo of PM Modi was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed him participating in Christmas celebrations in the Parliament premises. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be misleading since the photo was from the Christmas festivities at the residence of Union Minister George Kurian, and not in the premises of the Parliament. Claim A Facebook user named 'Epuru Subbarao' shared on December 20 a post claiming that PM Modi celebrated Christmas in the Parliament premises. The caption of the post read: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi garu in Christmas celebrations in Parliament premises…" Here is link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found that another user had shared the same image with a similar claim. Here is the link and archive link to the post: The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by India Today, published on December 20, whose headline read: "PM Modi joins Christmas celebrations at Union Minister's home. See pics" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same. The Desk went through the report and found that the same photo was carried in it. Below is a screenshot of the same: We also found an X post by Press Trust of India on December 19. The caption of the post read: "PM Modi attends Christmas celebrations at the residence of Union Minister George Kurian in Delhi." Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. In fact, the same photo, along with others from the same event, was shared by PM Modi from his official X handle on December 19. The caption of the post read: "Attended the Christmas celebrations at the residence of Union Minister Shri George Kurian Ji. Also interacted with eminent members of the Christian community." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a photo of PM Modi celebrating Christmas at the residence of Union Minister George Kurian was misleadingly shared in the name of Parliament premises.

title: PTI Fact Check: This social media post about religious identity of management and trust members at Tirupati Balaji, Siddivinayak temples is absolutely false; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): According to a recent claim shared by several social media users, the chairman of the Tirupati Balaji temple committee was a Christian while 44 other members were from the Muslim community. The claim further stated that Salim, a Muslim, was one of the trustees of the Siddhivinayak Temple in Mumbai. The PTI Fact Check Desk categorically investigated the claims made in the social media posts and found them to be fake. Neither the Tirupati Balaji temple trust has a Christian chairman, nor it has any Muslims member. Likewise, none of the trustees of the Siddivinayak Temple is a Muslim. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 19 a post claiming that the chairman of the Tirupati Balaji temple committee was a Christian whereas 44 other members were from the Muslim community. The post further claimed that Salim, a Muslim, was one of the trustees of the Siddivinayak Temple in Mumbai. Here's is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation The Desk categorically investigated the claims made in the above-mentioned social media post and here's what it found: The Desk first carried out a customised keyword search on Google and found that similar claims around the Tirupati Balaji temple committee chairman have been making rounds on social media since at least 2020. Here is the link to one such post and the archived version of the same can be seen here. Below is a screenshot of the post: Claim 1 –Tirupati Balai temple committee chairman Chandrashekhar Reddy is a Christian. To investigate the claim, the Desk first scanned the official website of Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams Trust Board, which manages several shrines, including the Tirumala Venkateswara Temple in Andhra Pradesh, popularly known as the Tirupati Balaji temple. The website mentioned the chairman of the temple trust board as BR Naidu. Below is a screenshot of the same: We also conducted a customised keyword search to check if any 'Chandrashekhar Reddy' had served as the chairman of the temple board, but could not find any report backing the claim. We, however, found that similar rumours were spread in 2018 about the then TTD Trust Board chairman Putta Sudhakar Yadav, following which he had clarified that he was not a Christian. Here is the link to an April 2018 report by The Hindu, whose headline read: "I am not a Christian, says new TTD chief." Below is a screenshot of the same: Further, amid the recent controversy over the alleged use of animal fat in the preparation of 'laddoo prasadam' at the Sri Venkateswara Swamy Temple in Tirupati, similar allegations were levelled against former temple board chairman YV Subba Reddy. The same claim had gone viral in 2019 as well. Here are the links ( Link 1 , Link 2 ) and archive links ( Link 1 , Link 2 ) to two such posts, one from September 2024 and the other from 2018. Below are the screenshots of the same: Reddy had himself refuted the claim and retweeted a post, which carried his poll affidavit, clearly mentioning that his full name was Yarram Venkata Subba Reddy, and not Yehova Vincent Subba Reddy. Here is the link to the X post, and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk contacted the TTD Trust Board to provide a list of people who served as the chairman of the trust. The article will be updated as and when a response is received. Claim 2 - 44 members of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams Trust Board are Muslims Along with BR Naidu, the TTD Trust Board website mentioned the names of 26 members appointed, but none of them were Muslims. Here's the link to the webpage mentioning the list of people serving at the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams Trust Board. During our investigation, we also came across an India Today report, published on November 1, 2024. The headline of the report read: "TTD chairman BR Naidu announces Hindu-only staff policy in Tirumala." Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Claim 3 - Person identified as Salim serves on the Board of Trustees of Shree Siddhivinayak Temple The desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across a list on the temple's website that mentioned the names of the Board of Trustees. After carefully scanning the list, the desk concluded that no individual named Salim is present in the Board of Trustees. Here's the link and screenshot of the list. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claims made regarding management and trust members of Tirupati Balaji Temple and Siddivinayak Temple were false.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: No, former US President Bill Clinton didn't attend PV Sindhu's wedding reception; Tamil actor Ajith's video was shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, December 26 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed former US President Bill Clinton attending the wedding festivities of star Indian shuttler PV Sindhu and Hyderabad-based Executive Director at Posidex Technologies, Venkata Datta Sai. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that person claimed to be Clinton was actually Tamil actor Ajith Kumar. The video was from Sindhu's wedding reception held in Hyderabad on December 24. Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu embarked on a new journey in life as she tied the knot with entrepreneur Venkata Datta Sai in a private ceremony in Udaipur on December 22. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 24 a video claiming that it showed former US President Bill Clinton attending PV Sindhu and Venkata Datta Sai's wedding in Hyderabad. The post has garnered over 751k views so far. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found an Instagram video posted by entertainment website 'Pinkvilla South', on December 25. The video matched the viral clip and was captioned as "Thala Ajith and his family join the celebrations at PV Sindhu and Venkat's reception." Reportedly, the Tamil superstar is widely referred to as Thala by his fans. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the video posted by Pinkvilla South. In the next part of investigation, the Desk made a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report by the India Today, which confirmed that the person in the viral video was Tamil superstar Ajith Kumar. According to India Today report, published on December 25, "Ajith Kumar, his wife Shalini, and their two children, Anoushka and Aadvik, attended the wedding reception of badminton player PV Sindhu in Hyderabad on December 24." Here's the link and screenshot of the report published by the India Today news website. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the man in the video, claimed to be former US President Bill Clinton, was actually Tamil actor Ajith.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Indonesian mosque engulfed in fire falsely shared on social media in name of India; Details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 26 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : A video was recently shared on social media with the claim that it showed a mosque set on fire in India. The video showed people running around the structure engulfed in fire and some filming the incident. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found the claim to be false. The mosque in the video was in Indonesia, and not India. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 15 a post claiming that a mosque was set on fire in India. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across another social media post, which carried the same video with similar claim. The link of the post can be viewed here and the archive link can be found here. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google, but did not find any substantial report corroborating the claim that the mosque was in India. However, on further scanning the search results, we came across a Facebook post that carried several pictures, which were strikingly similar to the visuals of the viral video. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: A rough translation of the post in English read: "A great fire broke out in the Central Market, Luwuk, Banggai, Sunday, December 8, 2024 morning. This location is reportedly that in the near future a Mall will be built, even the Disperindag party is said to have done socialization to the residents of the site that has the last remaining pieces." Below is a combination image, highlighting the similarities between the viral video and the photos from the Dec 8 Facebook post. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found that the Central Market, Luwuk, was located in Indonesia. Another customised keyword search on Google led the Desk to an article published by Tribun Palu – an Indonesian news portal – on December 8.The headline of the report read: "LuwukBanggai Central Market Mosque Also Engulfed by Fire, Dozens of Traders' Stalls Leveled to the Ground" Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same: "A major fire hit Luwuk Central Market ,Banggai Regency , Central Sulawesi, Sunday (8/12/2024) morning.The fire reportedly started from a trader's stall next to the Central Market Mosque. The flames spread quickly, destroying the mosque and dozens of stalls around it," read a section of the report. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the viral video to that of the photo featured in the Indonesia news report. The next part of the investigation the Desk scanned Tribun Palu's YouTube using customised keyword search and found a video posted by them on December 8, which showed similar visuals of the mosque as displayed in the viral video. Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same. Below is a combination image comparing the visuals of the viral video to the visualsof the YouTube video. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video was from Indonesia, and not India.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of Colombian woman stuck under sliding doors of bus station falsely shared in name of India, Pakistan; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a video claiming it showed an Indian immigrant stuck at an entry gate while trying to travel without a ticket in London. Meanwhile, some users claimed that the person was a Pakistani immigrant. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to January this year and was from Colombia's capital Bogotá. A woman got trapped while attempting to crawl under a glass entrance gate at a Transmilenio hub. (TransMilenio is a bus rapid transit (BRT) system that serves Bogotá, the capital of Colombia, and Soacha, a neighbouring city.) The old video was shared on social media as a recent incident, falsely linking it to India and Pakistan. Claim An X (formerly known as twitter) user - 'Shahinur' shared on December 25 a post claiming that an Indian immigrant named Panam Singh was stuck at an entry gate trying to travel without a ticket in London. The caption of the post read: "An Indian immigrant, #PanamSingh, was stuck at the entry gate while trying to travel without a ticket in #London." Here is the link and archive link to the X post and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across several other social media posts, which carried the same video,where some users claimed it to be from India and others claimed it to be from Pakistan. One such post can be seen here and its archived version can be viewed here . Below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this,the Desk conducted a keyword search on Google and found an article published by Daily Mail in January 2024, whose headline read: "Embarrassed Colombian woman tries evading 75 CENT transit fare by sneaking under gate and gets TRAPPED by sliding doors" Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that neither the incident happened in London, nor the person in the video was an Indian or Pakistani.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts claiming Israeli forces killed Brigadier General Amitabh Jha are fake; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 27 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users recently shared posts claiming that Indian Brigadier General Amitabh Jha, serving as Acting Force Commander of UNDOF (United Nations Disengagement Observer Force) in the Golan Heights, was killed by the Israeli forces. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk, in its investigation, found the claim to be false. According to the statement released by the Indian Army, Brigadier Amitabh Jha, who was deployed on a UN mission as Deputy Force Commander in UNDOC, passed away due to 'medical reasons' on December 23. The social media posts claiming that Brigadier General Amitabh Jha was killed by Israeli forces are fake. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user on December 26 shared a photo of Brigadier General Amitabh Jha, claiming that he was killed by Israeli forces while serving with the United Nations Disengagement Observer Force (UNDOF) at Golan Heights. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk conducted a customised keyword search and found that similar claim was shared by several other social media users. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archived versions can be viewed here and here , respectively. Below is the screenshot of one such post by a user on X (formerly Twitter). In the next part of investigation, the Desk carried out a customised keyword search on Google and came across a report carried out by the India Today on December 24, which, while quoting Indian Army officials, claimed that Brigadier Jha died due to medical reasons. Here's the link and screenshot of the news report carried by India Today. Below is also the link and screenshot of the social media post by the Indian Army, which had stated that Brigadier Jha passed due to medical reasons. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the claim of Indian Brigadier General Amitabh Jha being killed by Israeli forces is fake. Brigadier Jha passed away due to medical reasons.

title: PTI Fact Check: 2011 video of tiger atop elephant in Uttarakhand falsely shared as recent incident from Bihar
content: New Delhi, December 27 (Sajan Kumar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a 30-second video clip showing a tiger, along with two people, sitting on an elephant. The viral clip showed the two men sitting atop the elephant, twisting the tiger's ear and pulling its head upwards, while the tiger remained calm. Many media outlets and social media users shared this video, claiming it to be from Bihar. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the video dated back to January 2011 and was from Uttarakhand. The video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. Claim : An X (formerly Twitter) user, 'Guru', shared a video on December 24, showing two people sitting on an elephant and pulling a tiger's ears and head, and claimed it top be from Bihar. The post has garnered over 996k views so far. The caption of the post read, "इ बिहार है बाबू यहां उड़ती चिड़िया को भी हल्दी लगा देते हैं! ऐसे अदभुद नजारे बिहार में ही देखने को मिल सकते है!" An English translation of the post read: "This is Bihar, babu. Here even flying birds are given turmeric! Such amazing sights can only be seen in Bihar!". Here is the link and archive link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Investigation: Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several media outlets had shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be found here and here and their archived versions can be seen here and here respectively. On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across a similar video uploaded by an Instagram page named 'wildtrails.in' on May 9, 2024. The caption claimed that the footage was from Sundarkhal, Uttarakhand. The caption of the post read, "In 2011, Sunderkhal, Uttarakhand, witnessed a reign of terror as a tiger claimed six lives. Driven by instinctual urges and likely prompted by an injury, the majestic beast turned Man-Eater, instilling fear among locals. Authorities launched a relentless pursuit to capture the notorious tiger. Finally subdued, it was paraded atop an elephant for public viewing, its once fearsome demeanor now subdued…" Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Instagram Page, 'tigerdiaries', also shared the same video on June 15, 2024, and mentioned the incident's location as Uttarakhand. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: On further scanning the search results, the Desk came across an X post by an Indian Forest Service (IFS) Officer Praveen Kaswan, who replied to one of the users who had shared the viral video. "It's an old video of 2011 from Ramnagar of Uttrakhand. The tiger killed 6 people and later hunted down by authorities. It was transported on elephant, maybe vehicles were not able to go to the place," read the post by Kaswan. Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and came across news reports published by India Today and Times of India, published on January 28, 2011. According to reports, the incident occurred in the Ramnagar division of Uttarakhand. Here is the link ( here and here ) to the news report and below is a screenshot of the same: Subsequently, the Desk concluded that an old video from Uttarakhand was shared as a recent incident from Bihar with a false claim.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: 2021 photo of former PM Manmohan Singh falsely shared on social media as his last picture from Delhi's AIIMS; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 27 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Following the tragic demise of Dr Manmohan Singh on December 26, several social media users shared a photo, claiming it was the last picture of the former PM that showed him bedridden. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the photo dated back to October 2021 when Singh was admitted to Delhi AIIMS after suffering from fever, reportedly dengue. The three-year-old photo was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. 92-year-old Singh breathed his last at Delhi's AIIMS on Thursday night. He served as the prime minister of India twice, from 2004 to 2014. Singh had retired from the Rajya Sabha earlier this year after a 33-year-long service in the House. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user, named 'Raju Verma', shared on December 26 a photo, claiming it was the last picture offormer PM Dr Manmohan Singh before his demise on December 26. The caption, originally in Hindi, translated to: "Last photo of Manmohan Singh ji. Salute to such a great personality who took the sinking economic condition of the country to new heights." Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found an uncropped version of the picture posted by 'NBT Dilli' on X in October 2021. The photo showed the then Union Health Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and a doctor standing beside him. The caption of the post read: "Union Health Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya arrived to meet former Prime Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh admitted in AIIMS." Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same. Taking a cue from this, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came acrossa PTI report, carried by Business Today published on October 14, 2021, whose headline read: "Union Health Minister Mansukh Mandaviya meets Manmohan Singh at AIIMS" Here is the link and below is the screenshot of the same article: On further scanning the search results, we also found a video report by The Tribune uploaded on YouTube three years ago. The title of the report read: "Union Health Minister Mansukh Mandaviya meets Manmohan Singh at AIIMS, enquires about his health" Here is the link to the video and below is a screenshot of the same: In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search and came across an X post by Mandaviya, shared on October 14, 2021, in which he informed about visiting Manmohan Singh at AIIMS. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: During its investigation, the Desk also came across a report by Dainik Bhaskar, published on October 16, 2021. The report was on the controversy that erupted back then over the photos from Mandaviya's visit to AIIMS to meet Manmohan Singh. The former PM's daughter Daman Singh had expressed her anger on the photo being made public. Here is the link to the report titled, "Manmohan Singh's daughter got angry at Mandaviya: When the picture of her father lying on the hospital bed was made public, she said - My parents are not zoo animals". Below is a screenshot of the same: The report quoted Daman Singh as saying, "My mother had refused to take the photo. My father is undergoing treatment for dengue at AIIMS. His condition is stable but his immunity is low. We have banned visitors due to the risk of infection. It was nice to have the Health Minister visit and express his concern. However, my parents were in no position to be photographed at that time. My mother insisted that the photographer should leave the room but she was completely ignored. She was very upset about this." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that viral photoactually dated back to October 2021, when Singh was admitted to Delhi AIIMS.

title: PTI Fact Check: Video of stray dog attack on Jalandhar woman falsely shared in name of UP's Agra; details inside
content: New Delhi, December 28 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): A video was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed an elderly woman being attacked by a pack of stray dogs in Agra's Idgah Colony area. The video, apparently a CCTV footage, showed a woman being attacked by 7-8 stray dogs, who dragged her across the street while she struggled to rescue herself. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the viral video was from Jalandhar, not Agra. The 65-year-old woman was attacked by stray dogs on her way back from gurdwara. The video was falsely shared on social media in the name of Agra. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 25 a video claiming that it showed an attack on an elderly woman by a pack of 7-8 stray dogs in Uttar Pradesh's Agra. The user mentioned, "The pack of dogs fiercely attacked an elderly woman who works as a house help and was passing through the area in Agra's Idgah colony area." Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across an India Today report, published on December 16, which stated that the incident happened in Punjab's Jalandhar. Here's the link and screenshot of the news report. According to the news report, a 65-year-old woman suffered serious injuries when a pack of seven to eight stray dogs attacked and bit her on a deserted road. The woman was walking alone and returning from a gurdwara at the time of the incident, which was captured on CCTV. On further scanning the search results, we came across an X post by Agra Police, where it stated that the video was from Jalandhar, and not Agra. Here's the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same. Since the India Today report mentioned 'inputs from Devinder Kumar', the Desk contacted the Jalandhar-based reporter, who confirmed that the incident took place in his city. "The incident took place near Doordarshan Enclave Phase-2 located near Satguru Kabir Chowk. There are more than 25 dog bite marks on the elderly woman's body. She also suffered a head injury, and was rushed to the Civil Hospital," he told PTI. "The victim's husband said that a young man sitting on the roof of his house saw it from a distance and he reached the spot and chased away the dogs," he added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the video of stray dog attack on an elderly woman was from Jalandhar, not Agra.

author: Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Video of passenger ferry capsizing in Congo in October 2024 falsely attributed to recent Mumbai boat accident; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ): A video of a passenger boat capsizing in a waterbody was recently shared on social media, with users claiming that it showed the recent incident in which a passenger boat traveling from Alibaug to the Gateway of India sank into the sea. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the video was actually of an accident that occurred in Lake Kivu in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo in October this year. An overcrowded boat there capsized, resulting in the death of 78 people. The old and unrelated video was falsely shared on social media as recent in the name of with the false claim that the incident occurred in Mumbai. Meanwhile, it is pertinent to note that the video went viral on social media after a Navy boat rammed into the tourist ferry on way to the Elephanta Island from the Gateway of India in Mumbai on December 18, leaving as many as 14 people dead. Claim A Facebook user shared on December 21 a video of an overcrowded boat capsizing in a water body. The users claimed that the video was of the recent incident in which 14 people were killed after an Indian Navy boat rammed into the tourist ferry – 'Neel Kamal' – on way to the Elephanta Island from the Gateway of India in Mumbai. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk conducted a customized keyword search and found that a similar claim was shared by several other social media users. Two such posts can be seen here and here & its archived versions can be viewed here and here respectively. Below is the screenshot of one such post by a user on Facebook. In the next part of the investigation, the desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video published by the official channel of Firstpost on October 4. The title of the video mentioned, "78 Dead After Boat Capsizes in DR Congo's Lake Kivu | Firstpost Africa." Below is the link and screenshot of the YouTube video published by the news portal. The Desk noticed striking similarities between the two videos, suggesting that this was the same as the viral clip. Below is a combination image, highlighting the same: To corroborate the details, the Desk conducted another customised keyword search on Google and came across a report published by Reuters on October 4. The title of the report read: "78 drown after boat capsizes in Congo's Lake Kivu, provincial governor says." Here is the link to the report, and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, "At least 78 people drowned when a boat carrying 278 passengers capsized in Lake Kivu in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo on Thursday, a provincial governor said." Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a video of a boat capsizing incident from Congo, Africa, was falsely shared on social media in the name of the Mumbai.

title: PTI Fact Check: Year-old video of Nitish Kumar shared on social media to falsely claim he resigned as Bihar CM and quit NDA; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 30 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar / Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Amid the alleged political rumblings in Bihar, a video of Chief Minister Nitish Kumar was recently shared on social media with users claiming that he had once again shifted his political allegiance. The clip from a news report showed him speaking to media after resigning as the CM and saying that he had moved out of the 'Mahagathbandhan'. Users shared the video to insinuate that the JD(U) chief had moved out of the NDA, once again. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a year-old video was shared on social media as recent with a false claim. The video dated back to when Kumar had moved out of the grand alliance led by RJD in January this year, ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, and formed government with the BJP. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 28 a video of Nitish Kumar speaking to media after resigning as Bihar CM and moving out of the ruling alliance in the state. The user shared the video to claim that the JD(U) chief had severed ties with the BJP, with which his party was in power in alliance in Bihar. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation The Desk ran the viral video through InVid Tool Search and found several keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across a YouTube video published by Times of India on January 28. The YouTube video matched the viral clip, and its description stated, "Nitish Kumar, Chief Minister of Bihar and President of the JD(U), resigned from his position after a meeting with JD(U) MLAs." Below is the link and screenshot of the video posted by Times of India. According to the Times of India report, Nitish Kumar resigned as the Chief Minister of Bihar after breaking away from the 'Mahagatbandhan' government it had formed in the state with the support of RJD. In the next part of investigation, the Desk conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a similar report by India Today, dated January 28. The report elaborated over Nitish Kumar's first reaction to the media after quitting the Mahagatbandhan government, which comprised JD(U), RJD, and Congress. Here's the link and screenshot of the news report. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral video of Nitish Kumar resigning as Bihar CM dated back to January 2024.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Scripted video of policemen helping a woman vegetable seller falsely shared on social media as real incident; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Multiple social media users shared a video, claiming that it showed two policemen helping a vegetable seller by freeing her dress caught under a car tyre. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that a scripted video was shared on social media as a real incident with a false claim. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user shared on December 21 a video of two policemen helping a vegetable seller free her dress from under a car. The caption of the post read: "Great job by the Indian police, big salute to them" Here is the link and archive link and below is the screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk first ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk came across another social media post, which carried the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and and the archive link can be found here and here , respectively. On further scanning the search results, we came across a Facebook post by a user 'Sanjjanaa Galrani'. The user shared a 6:32-minute video on April 12, whose caption read: "This Will Teach Us A Life Lesson..!" Towards the end, a disclaimer running on the video read: "This Reel Life Video footage published only for the purpose of educating the public by making them understand how the real world situations will be and picturized to educate the public. Characters in this video are entertainment and education purpose." Here is the link to the post and below is a screenshot of the same: Taking a cue from this, we conducted a customised keyword search and came across a similar YouTube video by '3RD Eye', uploaded on April 19 this year, whose title read: "Who Is Correct..? See What This Car Owner Did to The Poor Vegitable Seller | #lifelesson". Here is the link and below is a screenshot of the same: The disclaimer in the description read: "Thank you for watching! Please be aware that this Channel features scripted dramas and parodies of Aware People in Different Situations. This Channel Brings Social Awareness Videos. These short films are for entertainment purposes only!" Subsequently, the Desk concluded that a scripted video was falsely shared as a real incident.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: Kuwaiti yoga practitioner's photo with PM Modi misrepresented as Queen of Kuwait; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 30 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : Soon after PM Modi concluded his two-day visit to Kuwait, multiple social media users shared a photo of PM Modi interacting with a woman and claimed that she was the Queen of Kuwait and was dressed without a hijab. In its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found that the woman in the photo was a yoga practitioner who started the first licensed yoga studio in Kuwait. The image was shared on social media with a false claim. During his recent two-day visit to Kuwait, the first by any Indian PM after 43 years, PM Modi met Shaikha A J Al-Sabah, a yoga practitioner and founder of the first licensed yoga studio in Kuwait, Daratma. According to a statement by PMO India, they discussed ways to further popularise yoga, especially among the youth. Claim A Facebook user shared a picture on December 26 claiming that during his recent visit to Kuwait, PM Modi met with the country's queen, who was dressed without a Hijab. The caption, initially translated into Hindi, reads: "She is the Queen of Kuwait! She looks like a leader of a European country! No burqa, no hijab; this is the mark of being real. In India, burqa and hijab are required for college and office use." Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same. Investigation The Desk ran the photo through Google Lens and found that multiple other users shared the same picture with a similar caption. The links to the posts can be viewed here and here , and their archive versions can be found here and here , respectively. The Desk then conducted a customised keyword search on Google and found a PTI report from NDTV on December 22. The report featured the same picture as that being circulated on social media. The report headline read: "PM Modi Meets Yoga Practitioner, Other Influencers In Kuwait." Here is the link , and below is the screenshot of the same: The report read: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Shaikha AJ Al-Sabah, an avid yoga practitioner and founder of the first licensed yoga studio 'Daratma' in Kuwait, and other influencers from the Gulf country." PM Modi shared the photo from his official X handle on December 22, whose caption read: "Met HH Shaikha AJ Al-Sabah in Kuwait. She has distinguished herself for her passion for Yoga and fitness. She has established her own Yoga and wellness studio, which is quite popular in Kuwait. We talked about ways to make Yoga more popular among the youth." Here is the link and archive link , and below is the screenshot. The search results further led us to an Instagram post by the Ministry of External Affairs, which carried the same photo. Here is the link to the post, and below is a screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the woman sitting with PM Modi in the photo was not the queen of Kuwait but a yoga practitioner.

title: PTI Fact Check: LinkedIn post, reports claiming athlete Parag Patil, now working as a cab driver, was an Olympian are misleading
content: New Delhi, Dec 30 (Abhinav Gupta / Pratyush Ranjan PTI Fact Check ): A rare yet concerning case of misinformation has emerged from a LinkedIn post, leading many users on the social media platforms to like and share and several news portals to publish an inspiring but misleading story. This story is based on a post by entrepreneur Aaryan Singh Kushwah about his encounter with a cab driver, Parag Patil, whom he described as a decorated Olympian. Kushwah claimed in his post that Patil had represented India on the global stage, winning two gold, 11 silver, and three bronze medals. However, he also noted that Patil was now struggling financially and working as a cab driver to support his family. The PTI Fact Check Desk investigated the claims made in the LinkedIn post and subsequent articles. It was found that Patil had never represented India at the Olympic Games. Instead, he participated in the World Senior Games and other biennial events. Nonetheless, the articles, relying on Kushwah's post, created the impression that Patil's medals were from Olympic events. While Patil's accomplishments are undoubtedly admirable, PTI Fact Check emphasises the importance of understanding the distinction. This case underscores how misleading headlines can contribute to the spread of misinformation. Claim Kushwah's LinkedIn post, which has now garnered close to 500 likes, mentioned that "my Ola driver is an Olympian", and that he never returned without a medal each time when he represented India internationally. "2 golds, 11 silvers, 3 bronze," the post read. Here is the link and archive link to the post, and below is a screenshot of the same: Based on this LinkedIn post, several media outlets published the story of Patil, which clearly suggested that the latter was an Olympian and that his medals were from Olympic events. Three such articles can be read here , here and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here and here , respectively. Investigation The Desk found that Kushwah, in his LinkedIn post, had tagged Patil's LinkedIn profile, where he mentioned himself as 'Parag Patil Senior Olympian'. We scanned the profile and found that he had mentioned all his achievements. Notably, nowhere had he mentioned about winning or participating in any Olympic event. Here is the link to Patil's LinkedIn profile and below is a screenshot of the same: We conducted customised keyword search to find details of each of the sports events mentioned by Patil, and found that they were organised for athletes over a certain age, and had no association with International Olympic Committee or were anywhere connected to the Olympic Games. The Desk also tried to find whether Patil had ever participated in any Olympic event, but could not find any substantiating report on the same. During the investigation, however, we came across a report by The Indian Express, published on October 24, 2019. "Track athlete who bagged 5 medals at international event struggles for funds," read the headline of the report. Here is the link to the report and below is a screenshot of the same: According to the report, "Parag Patil, a Chinchwad-based track and field athlete, had bagged four silver medals and one bronze at the Australian Masters Games 2019 in Adelaide, held between October 5 to October 12." "A Senior Olympian, Patil started his journey as an athlete 30 years ago at the school and college levels. Thereafter, he pursued it professionally and went on to win 12 international medals between 2010 and 2018. After the Australian Master's Games 2019, his total medal tally comes to 17: two gold, 11 silver and four bronze medals. Currently, he also holds the second position in triple jump, third rank in long jump and fifth in the 100-metre categories in the World Master's Ranking in Asia," it added. In the next part of investigation, the Desk spoke to Poonam Mehra, Chief of Bureau (Sports) at PTI, seeking details regarding the viral LinkedIn post and the related news reports. "It is not Olympics, it is something called the World Senior Games… It's a biennial thing which happens mostly in the United States… It is completely informal to call it senior Olympics, it's misleading and wrong, because Olympics is a trademark of IOC. So, it's a completely misleading claim," she said. This makes it clear that while Parag won accolades at several biennial events across the globe, he neither participated nor won any medal in any Olympic event. However, the headlines of the articles on his story tend to suggest otherwise, with the potential of misinforming the readers.

author: Kaushiki Goel/Abhinav Gupta
title: PTI Fact Check: FM Nirmala Sitharaman's statement on GST on used cars was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claim
content: New Delhi, Dec 31 (Kaushiki Goel / Abhinav Gupta, PTI Fact Check ) : After the 55th GST Council meeting introduced several changes to the GST framework, several social media users criticised the recommendation of a taxation hike on used cars and shared a clip of Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's address claiming that individuals will have to pay 18 per cent GST on the difference between the car's original purchase price and its resale price. Some users also claimed that GST would be charged even when a seller incurs a loss. However, the PTI Fact Check Desk's investigation found that the announcement by the finance minister was taken out of context and shared on social media with false claims. PTI quoted sources as saying that a registered person or firm will have to pay GST on selling an old or used vehicle only if the seller or the firm has earned a margin profit, with the selling price higher than the depreciation-adjusted cost price of the vehicle. If an individual sells an old or used car to another individual, GST would not be applicable. Claim An X (formerly Twitter) user named 'Ankit Mayank' shared a post on December 23 on the revised GST on selling old and used vehicles that garnered 1.9 million views. The caption of the post read: "I bought a car in 2014 for ₹6 lakhs. If I sell it today, I will get ₹1 lakh. As per new rules, I will have to pay 18% GST on the margin (₹6 lakhs - ₹1 lakh = ₹5 lakhs). So after selling the car, - I will get ₹10k, - Modi Govt will get ₹90k. RIP, middle class." Here is the link and archive link , and the screenshot is below. Investigation Several other social media users also shared the same video with similar claims. Two such posts can be seen here and here , and their archive versions can be viewed here and here . The Desk categorically investigated the claims made in the above-mentioned social media post, and here's what it found: Claim 1: Individuals selling their used cars would be taxed at 18% on the profit, i.e. the difference between the car's original purchase price and its resale price. To investigate the claim, the Desk watched FM Nirmala Sitharaman's official press conference on December 21, 2024, in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Here is the link , and below is a screenshot. At 25:30 minutes, Sitharaman said: "We want to promote EVs. The GST council is in favour of EVs. Nobody is stopping people from buying EVs. However, if an individual sells used EVs to others, there is no GST. But if a company has bought an EV or a regular registered used car seller who buys EVs, does some propping up in it and adds value in it, then sells it, it was felt by states and many others also that the EV market is not so saturated as yet and that used cars will come. Therefore, the used car category includes electric, petrol, and diesel cars...This 18% GST will be levied on the margin value of the purchase and resale prices of any used cars. So it is on the margin, not the entire amount the car has been sold." The Desk also came across a PIB press release on the announcement, issued on December 21. Here is the link to the release, and below is a screenshot of the same: The press release mentioned: "To increase the GST rate from 12% to 18 % on sale of all old and used vehicles, including EVs other than those specified at 18% -Sale of old and used petrol vehicles of engine capacity of 1200 cc or more & of length of 4000 mm or more; diesel vehicles of engine capacity of 1500 cc or more & of length of 4000 mm and SUVs.[Note: GST is applicable only on the Value that represents the Margin of the Supplier, that is, the difference between the Purchase price and Selling price (depreciated value if depreciation is claimed) and not on the value of the vehicle. Also, it is not applicable in case of unregistered persons.]" This means that the 18 per cent GST would not be applicable if an individual sells old and used cars to another individual. The Council has now made the rate uniform at 18 per cent for all second-hand vehicles, including EVs. Earlier, GST on old and used vehicles (other than specific high-capacity petrol and diesel vehicles) was set at 12 per cent. For high-capacity petrol vehicles (engine capacity of 1200 cc or more and length exceeding 4000 mm), diesel vehicles (engine capacity of 1500 cc or more and length exceeding 4000 mm), and SUVs, the rate is already 18 per cent.
