In the next part of the investigation, the Desk contacted Prof. Gourav Vallabh, Chartered Accountant and Company Secretary, who explained that individuals selling used users to others were not liable to pay the 18 per cent GST on the margin. "If I, as an individual, sell the car to another individual, neither Gourav Vallabh nor the individual has to pay the 18% GST. A company that does business with used cars sells a car and is liable to pay GST only on the margin. This means that if that company buys a car for Rs 10 lakh and sells it at Rs 12 lakh, the margin accounts for Rs 2 lakh. The GST will be applicable on that Rs 2 lakh margin. Individuals buying and selling used cars do not have to pay GST. If the company buys a car for Rs 10 lakh and sells it for Rs 8 lakh, the company does not have to pay GST on the loss margin," he told PTI. The Desk also contacted Suranjali Tandon, an Associate Professor at the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy, who further explained the change in the GST framework for user cars. "The application of GST on resale of cars was previously also different, as per the vehicle types and the person selling the car. Different categories of people reselling exist - individual to individual, business selling to others, or businesses and dealerships. So far, as long as there is a transaction between dealership or business, this GST arises, which will be applicable on the margin between purchase and sale price..." Tandon told PTI Fact Check. Multiple news portals published articles explaining the confusion over who is liable to pay the 18 per cent GST. Two such reports by Business Today and Times of India can be read here and here . The article by CNBC TV 18 categorically mentions: "Only registered persons, such as businesses involved in the purchase and selling of old and used vehicles, etc., are liable to pay GST." Claim 2: 18 per cent GST will be charged even when a seller incurs a loss Here is the link and archive link to the claim. As per Rule 32(5) of the CGST Rules, 2017, "where a taxable supply is provided by a person dealing in buying and selling of second-hand goods i.e. used goods as such or after such minor processing which does not change the nature of the goods and where no input tax credit has been availed on the purchase of such goods, the value of supply shall be the difference between the selling price and the purchase price and where the value of such supply is negative, it shall be ignored." Here is the link , and below is the screenshot. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman's address following the 55th GST Council Meeting was misinterpreted and shared with false claims regarding selling used cars on social media.

title: PTI Fact Check: Social media posts falsely claim man travelled 250 km hiding between wheels of train; details inside
content: New Delhi, Dec 31 (Vaidehi Jahagirdar/Abhinav Gupta PTI Fact Check ): Multiple social media users shared a video claiming it showed a man who allegedly travelled 250 km without a ticket hiding between the wheels of a train. Users also claimed that he was spotted by railway officials when the train travelling from Itarsi to Jabalpur reached its final destination. However, in its investigation, the PTI Fact Check Desk found the claim to be false. The Railways clarified that it was impossible for anyone to travel hiding between the wheels. The video was shared on social media with a false claim. Claim On December 27, an X (formerly Twitter) user shared a video claiming to show a person who travelled 250 km by hiding between the wheels of a train. Here's the link , archive link , and screenshot of the post. Investigation Starting the investigation, the Desk ran the video through InVid Tool Search and found a few keyframes. On running one of the keyframes through Google Lens, the Desk found that several other social media users had too shared the same video with similar claims. Three such posts can be seen here , here , and here , and their archived versions can be seen here , here , and here , respectively. In the next part of the investigation, the Desk carried out a customised keyword search on Google and came across a PTI report carried out by The Hindu on December 28. The report quoted a Railway Ministry official as stating that the claim of a man travelling 250 km hiding on the train's wheel axle was 'fake' and 'misleading.' Here's the link to the news article carried out by 'The Hindu.' Below is the screenshot of the same. "These reports are completely fake and baseless," said the Railway Ministry official. "The person was hiding near the wheel axle when the train was not moving. It is practically impossible for anyone to hide on the wheelset of a moving train as it moves along with the wheels," Dilip Kumar, Executive Director, Information and Publicity, Railway Board, said. "Some news organisations and social media influencers picked it up and made it viral without verifying its authenticity," he added. Subsequently, the Desk concluded that the viral claim about a man travelling 250 km from Itarsi to Jabalpur while sitting on the axle of a wheel of a Pune-Danapur Express train was false.
